ap:252683.body:
Reference: 38627 / FSP 006 / 2027
UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic position in Community Health
Main campus: Brussels Woluwe
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
The Brussels Woluwe campus offers a unique living environment, conveniently located and easily accessible, on the outskirts of Brussels. The site hosts the five research institutes and three out of the four faculties on the Health Sciences Sector, as well as an academic hospital, the Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc. The multiple interactions between those entities make the campus a very attractive hub for students and researchers in the field of health sciences.
Post description
Within the Faculty of Public Health (FSP) and the Institute of Health and Society (IRSS), Health Science Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

You will primarily teach in the field of community health, with a focus on the analysis of social determinants, participation, and dynamics of cooperation. The community approach integrates global health concepts, community diagnosis and project planning. The teaching responsibilities will also include courses in health promotion, notably strategies and core values with an emphasis on reducing social health inequalities. You will teach in the Master's programs of the Faculty, and also supervise Master’s dissertations.
Research

You will develop your own research activies, including leading research projects in the field of community health. Your activities will focus on intervention strategies within community health and health promotion, with a particular emphasis on reducing social health inequalities. Your activities could include an analysis of the social, cultural and environmental determinants influencing the health of populations, and mobilize qualitative, quantitative or mixed methods. Your activities may also involve a commitment to co-constructing actions and their evaluation with local stakeholders, with the aim to strengthening the autonomy and the empowerment of communities. These activities will incorporate a sustainable approach that is attentive to social justice in health.
You will be responsible for the supervision of PhD theses.
In addition …

Once tenured, you will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee, or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
You will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Public Health, Health Sciences, Psychology, or Humanities and Social Sciences.
You are a healthcare professional in the medical or paramedical field; you have experience of fieldwork as a professional or researcher and are sensitive to societal issues and community health challenges.
Experience

You have a proven track record in university teaching, with evidence where possible by formal evaluations. Your scientific experience is demonstrated by publications of international standing.
You have supplemented this with an extended stay or significant experience abroad, outside the institution that awarded your doctorate.
Skills

You are comfortable working as part of a team of academics and integrate research results into your teaching. You are capable of conducting high-level scientific research, from obtaining funding to team management. You are creative, open to pedagogical innovation and multidisciplinary.
You can communicate in French and English. If this is not the case, you undertake to acquire a command of these two languages within two years of taking up your position. Knowledge of other languages is an asset.
What we offer
Tenure after positive assessment of the probationary period – typically four years. This type of career entitles you to a public sector pension.

Appointment as lecturer or professor according to your previous academic experience, as determined by the Rectoral Council.

Teaching load capped at 90 hours for a full-time tenure-track position, and 150 hours once tenured.

An attractive and progressive salary according to seniority and the promotion process.

A start date of 1 September 2027 at the earliest.

An integrated leadership and management training programme, including a range of pedagogical, linguistic and other training courses.

Benefits including transport, family, culture, commercial, etc.

Official policy that supports equal opportunities and promotes diversity within academic and all other categories of staff.

Specific emphasis on a work-life balance.

Practical Information
Application deadline: 5 November 2026 at noon (UTC+1 Time Zone)
Starting date: September 1st 2027
Location:
Health Science Sector
(FSP) (https://uclouvain.be/en/faculties/FSP)
(IRSS) (https://uclouvain.be/en/research-institutes/IRSS)
Need more information?
Questions about this position:
Prof. Sophie Thunus, Dean FSP – [email protected]
Prof. Sandy Tubeuf, President IRSS – [email protected]
Questions about the procedure:
Madam Céline Brauns, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Questions about online application:
Madam Andreea Chiriac, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Interested?
Applications must be submitted exclusively via UCLouvain’s online recruitment system; submissions through other channels will not be considered.
Full details regarding the application procedure are available at: https://www.uclouvain.be/en/careers/submit-your-application
Applications must include one single PDF file containing the following documents:
a cover letter (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a detailed and up‑to‑date curriculum vitae (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a copy of the official doctoral degree certificate;
a complete publication list, including a summary of three recent and significant publications;
a teaching statement;
a research statement presenting the proposed research programme for the next five years.

Shortlisted candidates invited for an interview will subsequently be asked to provide:
a PhD project proposal, with a view to the possible recruitment of a doctoral candidate during the first year of appointment;
three to five letters of reference, submitted directly by referees according to the instructions provided by the University.

Elle intègre les enjeux de la crise écologique dans les formations et développe de nombreux projets locaux (ferme universitaire, campus durables). Université numérique, l'UCLouvain s’implique dans la science et l’éducation ouvertes et forme les enseignants aux pratiques pédagogiques innovantes (Louvain Learning Lab). Vous enseignerez principalement dans le domaine de la santé communautaire, en ce compris l'analyse des déterminants sociaux, de la participation et des dynamiques de coopération. L'approche communautaire intègre les concepts de santé globale, le diagnostic communautaire et la planification de projets. La charge d'enseignement comprend aussi des cours en promotion de la santé, qui couvrent les stratégies et valeurs fondamentales, en mettant l'accent sur la réduction des inégalités sociales de la santé. Vous assurerez vos enseignements dans les programmes de master de la faculté, et vous dirigerez également des mémoires de master.
Recherche

Vous développerez vos activités de recherche, y compris l’animation de programmes de recherche, dans le domaine de la santé communautaire. Vos activités porteront plus particulièrement sur les stratégies d'intervention communautaire et de promotion de santé, en visant notamment à réduire les inégalités sociales de santé.
Vos activités pourraient inclure une analyse des déterminants sociaux, culturels et environnementaux influençant la santé des populations, et mobiliser des méthodes qualitatives, quantitatives ou mixtes. Vos activités pourraient également impliquer un engagement dans des démarches de co-construction des actions et de leurs évaluations avec les acteurs locaux, afin de renforcer l'autonomie et le pouvoir d'agir des communautés. Elles intégreront une approche durable et attentive à la justice sociale en santé.
Vous assurerez la supervision de thèses de doctorat.

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en Sciences de la santé publique, Sciences de la santé, en Psychologie ou en Sciences humaines et Sociales.
Vous êtes professionnel·le de la santé dans le domaine médical ou paramédical; vous avez une expérience du terrain comme professionnel·le ou comme chercheur·euse, et une sensibilité aux problématiques sociétales et aux enjeux de santé communautaire.

Vous êtes capable de mener des recherches scientifiques de haut niveau, de l’obtention des fonds jusqu’à la gestion de l’équipe. ap:252685.body:
Reference: 38628 / FASB 008 / 2027
UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic in Human Biology and Neurobiology
Main campus: Brussels Woluwe
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
The Brussels Woluwe campus offers a unique living environment, conveniently located and easily accessible, on the outskirts of Brussels. The site hosts the five research institutes and three out of the four faculties on the Health Sciences Sector, as well as an academic hospital, the Cliniques universitaires Saint-Luc. The multiple interactions between those entities make the campus a very attractive hub for students and researchers in the field of health sciences.
Post description
Within the Faculty of Pharmacy and Biomedical Sciences (FASB) and the Institute of NeuroScience (IoNS), Health Science Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

You will teach primarily mainly in the fields of biology, neurobiology and neuroscience across Bachelor's and Master's level courses offered by the faculty, and will be expected to supervise Master’s theses.
Research

You will develop and lead research programmes in the field of neuroscience, with a focus on the mechanistic aspects of brain function and associated pathologies. You will be responsible for the supervision of PhD theses. In addition, the role involves academic leadership of the Neuroscience track, encompassing thesis evaluation and internship supervision.
In addition …

Once tenured, you will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee, or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
You will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Biomedical Sciences, Pharmacy, Medicine, Biology or in a domain that can be considered as equivalent.
Experience

You have a proven track record in university teaching, with evidence where possible by formal evaluations. Your scientific experience is demonstrated by publications of international standing.
You have supplemented this with an extended stay or significant experience abroad, outside the institution that awarded your doctorate.
Skills

You are comfortable working as part of a team of academics and integrate research results into your teaching. You are capable of conducting high-level scientific research, from obtaining funding to team management. You are creative, open to pedagogical innovation and multidisciplinary.
You can communicate in French and English. If this is not the case, you undertake to acquire a command of these two languages within two years of taking up your position. Knowledge of other languages is an asset.
What we offer
Tenure after positive assessment of the probationary period – typically four years. This type of career entitles you to a public sector pension.

Appointment as lecturer or professor according to your previous academic experience, as determined by the Rectoral Council.

Teaching load capped at 90 hours for a full-time tenure-track position, and 150 hours once tenured.

An attractive and progressive salary according to seniority and the promotion process.

A start date of 1 September 2027 at the earliest.

An integrated leadership and management training programme, including a range of pedagogical, linguistic and other training courses.

Benefits including transport, family, culture, commercial, etc.

Official policy that supports equal opportunities and promotes diversity within academic and all other categories of staff.

Specific emphasis on a work-life balance.

Practical Information
Application deadline: 5 November 2026 at noon (UTC+1 Time Zone)
Starting date: September 1st 2027
Location:
Health Science Sector
(FASB) (https://uclouvain.be/en/faculties/FASB)
(IONS) (https://uclouvain.be/en/research-institutes/IONS)
Need more information?
Questions about this position:
Prof. Raphaël Frédérick, Dean FASB – [email protected]
Prof. Pascal Kienlen-Campard, President IONS – [email protected]
Questions about the procedure:
Madam Céline Brauns, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Questions about online application:
Madam Andreea Chiriac, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Interested?
Applications must be submitted exclusively via UCLouvain’s online recruitment system; submissions through other channels will not be considered.
Full details regarding the application procedure are available at: https://www.uclouvain.be/en/careers/submit-your-application
Applications must include one single PDF file containing the following documents:
a cover letter (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a detailed and up‑to‑date curriculum vitae (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a copy of the official doctoral degree certificate;
a complete publication list, including a summary of three recent and significant publications;
a teaching statement;
a research statement presenting the proposed research programme for the next five years.

Shortlisted candidates invited for an interview will subsequently be asked to provide:
a PhD project proposal, with a view to the possible recruitment of a doctoral candidate during the first year of appointment;
three to five letters of reference, submitted directly by referees according to the instructions provided by the University.

Vous serez ouverts aux techniques et méthodes de développement émergentes. Vous assurerez vos enseignements dans les bacheliers en sciences informatiques à Charleroi et à Louvain-la-Neuve, dans le diplôme de bachelier ingénieur civil et les diplômes de master en ingénieur civil informatique, en sciences informatiques, en science des données, en cybersécurité à Louvain-la-Neuve. Les cours de bachelier sont donnés principalement en français, ceux de master exclusivement en anglais. Vous y dirigerez également des mémoires de master.
Recherche

Vous développerez vos activités de recherche, y compris l’animation de programmes de recherche, dans le domaine des sciences du logiciel, comme par exemple:
Les méthodes de conception de logiciels;
Les langages et systèmes de programmation;
La fiabilité du logiciel;
La gestion et l'interrogation de grandes masses de données.

Les candidat·es de niveau exceptionnel dont les recherches s'inscrivent dans d'autres thématiques complémentaires à l'expertise en informatique présente au sein de l'institut, pourront également être considéré·es.
Il est attendu que vous visiez à mettre sur pied des activités de recherche sur le site de Charleroi. Une préférence pourra être accordée à des candidat·es qui développent des applications transdisciplinaires et qui sont complémentaires des recherches actuellement réalisées au sein de l'institut ICTEAM. Une expérience en développement de logiciels sera considérée comme un atout.
Vous assurerez la supervision de thèses de doctorat.
Et encore...

Vous assumerez, une fois confirmé·e (« tenured »), différentes activités de services et responsabilités au sein de l’institution, telles qu’un rôle dans les commissions de programme, dans les jurys d’études ou des responsabilités de gestion au sein de la faculté ou de l’institut de recherche.
Vous contribuerez également aux services à la société, notamment dans les domaines économique, social, culturel ou de la coopération au développement. Enfin, vous assurerez, par des activités de recherche et d’enseignement, la visibilité internationale de l’université.
Qui cherchons-nous?
Votre parcours

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat. Vous l’avez complété par un séjour d'étude prolongé à l'étranger ou une expérience significative hors de votre institution d'origine.
Votre expérience

Vous disposez d’une pratique avérée en enseignement universitaire, attestée si possible par des évaluations formelles. Votre expérience scientifique est démontrée par des publications de niveau international.
Vos compétences

Vous travaillez aisément en équipe d’enseignant·es et vous intégrez les résultats des recherches dans vos enseignements. Vous êtes capable de mener des recherches scientifiques de haut niveau, de l’obtention des fonds jusqu’à la gestion de l’équipe. Vous faites preuve de créativité, d’ouverture à l’innovation pédagogique et à la pluridisciplinarité.
Vous communiquez en français et en anglais. Si ce n’est pas le cas, vous vous engagez à acquérir la maîtrise de ces deux langues dans un délai de deux ans après la prise de fonction. La connaissance d’autres langues est un atout.
Nous vous offrons
Une nomination définitive au cadre académique après évaluation positive de la période probatoire d’une durée habituelle de 4 ans. Ce type de carrière donne droit à une pension du secteur public;
Une nomination au grade de chargé·e de cours ou de professeur·e en fonction de votre expérience académique antérieure, appréciée souverainement par le Conseil rectoral;
Une charge d’enseignement plafonnée à un maximum de 90h pour un temps plein avant confirmation (en «tenured-track») contre 150h en «tenured»;
Une rémunération attractive et évolutive en fonction de l’ancienneté et du processus de promotion;
Un démarrage de vos fonctions au plus tôt le 1er septembre 2027;
Un parcours de formation intégré en leadership et management et un éventail de formations pédagogiques, linguistiques et autres;
Divers avantages: transport, famille, culture, commerces, etc.;
Une politique du personnel soutenant l’égalité des chances et la diversité au sein de la carrière académique comme dans toutes les autres catégories de personnel;
Une attention particulière portée à la conciliation vie privée – vie professionnelle.

https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/candidature-aca.html

Reference: 38702 / DRT 042 / 2027
UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic position in Law, Transition and Economic Governance
Main campus: Louvain-la-Neuve
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
Post description
Within the Faculty of Law and Criminology (DRT) and the Institute for Interdisciplinary Research in Legal and Criminology Sciences (JUR-I), Social Sciences and Humanities Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

You will teach mainly in the field of the economic governance and regulation of economic activity in democracies (for example, courses on corporate regulation and sustainable development, public economic law, banking law, business and tax law, or media law). You will also be expected to supervise Master’s theses and to teach various courses managed by the faculty. In addition, you will be required to teach an introductory course in law, possibly within another faculty.
Research

You will develop your research activities, including the lead of research programmes in the field of transition, economic governance and regulation and democracy. You will be responsible for the supervision of PhD theses.
In addition …

Once tenured, you will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
You will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Legal Sciences.
Experience

You have a proven track record in university teaching, with evidence where possible by formal evaluations. Your scientific experience is demonstrated by publications of international standing.
You have supplemented this with an extended stay or significant experience abroad, outside the institution that awarded your doctorate.
Practical experience (gained in ministerial departments, within a government body, a public institution, a court or a law firm, or through work as an expert in various public or private entities) is an asset, as is a practical understanding of the dynamics of Belgian and European governance (particularly through professional experience)
Skills

You are comfortable working as part of a team of academics and integrate research results into your teaching. You are capable of conducting high-level scientific research, from obtaining funding to team management. You are creative, open to pedagogical innovation and multidisciplinary. Given your knowledge, skills, and methodological approach to legal research, you are well-positioned to bridge the gap between public law and economic law in a broad sense. You have conducted interdisciplinary and/or theoretical research that demonstrates an understanding of the economic dynamics involved in the transition.
You can communicate in French and English. If this is not the case, you undertake to acquire a command of these two languages within two years of taking up your position. Knowledge of other languages, such as, in particular, Dutch, is an asset.
What we offer
Tenure after positive assessment of the probationary period – typically four years. This type of career entitles you to a public sector pension.

Appointment as lecturer or professor according to your previous academic experience, as determined by the Rectoral Council.

Teaching load capped at 90 hours for a full-time tenure-track position, and 150 hours once tenured.

An attractive and progressive salary according to seniority and the promotion process.

A start date of 1 September 2027 at the earliest.

An integrated leadership and management training programme, including a range of pedagogical, linguistic and other training courses.

Benefits including transport, family, culture, commercial, etc.

Official policy that supports equal opportunities and promotes diversity within academic and all other categories of staff.

Specific emphasis on a work-life balance.

Practical Information
Application deadline: 5 November 2026 at noon (UTC+1 Time Zone)
Starting date: September 1st 2027
Location:
Social Sciences and Humanities Sector
(DRT) (https://uclouvain.be/en/faculties/DRT)
(JURI) (https://uclouvain.be/en/research-institutes/JURI)
Need more information?
Questions about this position:
Prof. Edoardo Traversa, Dean DRT – [email protected]
Prof. Sylvie Sarolea, President JURI – [email protected]
Questions about the procedure:
Madam Céline Brauns, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Questions about online application:
Madam Andreea Chiriac, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Interested?
Applications must be submitted exclusively via UCLouvain’s online recruitment system; submissions through other channels will not be considered.
Full details regarding the application procedure are available at: https://www.uclouvain.be/en/careers/submit-your-application
Applications must include one single PDF file containing the following documents:
a cover letter (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a detailed and up‑to‑date curriculum vitae (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a copy of the official doctoral degree certificate;
a complete publication list, including a summary of three recent and significant publications;
a teaching statement;
a research statement presenting the proposed research programme for the next five years.

Shortlisted candidates invited for an interview will subsequently be asked to provide:
a PhD project proposal, with a view to the possible recruitment of a doctoral candidate during the first year of appointment;
three to five letters of reference, submitted directly by referees according to the instructions provided by the University.

L'UCLouvain est la première université belge francophone et est aussi largement reconnue à l'international. Université complète implantée au cœur de l’Europe depuis 1425, elle rassemble près de 40.000 étudiantes et étudiants et 6 000 membres du personnel répartis sur 9 campus, à Bruxelles et en Wallonie. Elle intègre les enjeux de la crise écologique dans les formations et développe de nombreux projets locaux (ferme universitaire, campus durables). Université numérique, l'UCLouvain s’implique dans la science et l’éducation ouvertes et forme les enseignants aux pratiques pédagogiques innovantes (Louvain Learning Lab). Grâce à 2 parcs scientifiques, la recherche bénéficie d’interaction avec 250 entreprises et 3 incubateurs, au cœur d’une région animée par l’innovation technologique.

Ces partenariats se concrétisent à travers de nombreux accords d’échange, l’engagement fort dans l’alliance européenne Circle U. et dans le réseau The Guild, et l’accueil d’une large communauté de chercheuses et chercheurs internationaux, facilité par le Louvain Welcome Desk.

Enseignement

Vous enseignerez principalement dans le domaine de la gouvernance de l’activité économique et de la démocratie (par exemple des cours en matière de régulation des entreprises et développement durable, droit public de l’économie, droit bancaire, droit fiscal et de l’entreprise, droit des médias). Recherche

Et encore...

Vous contribuerez également aux services à la société, notamment dans les domaines économique, social, culturel ou de la coopération au développement. Enfin, vous assurerez, par des activités de recherche et d’enseignement, la visibilité internationale de l’université.
Qui cherchons-nous?
Votre parcours

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en sciences juridiques.
Votre expérience

Vous disposez d’une pratique avérée en enseignement universitaire, attestée si possible par des évaluations formelles. Votre expérience scientifique est démontrée par des publications de niveau international.
Vous l’avez complétée par un séjour prolongé ou une expérience significative à l’étranger, effectué hors de l’institution qui a délivré votre doctorat.
Une expérience dans la pratique (auprès de cabinets ministériels, au sein d’une administration, d’une institution publique, d’une juridiction ou d’un cabinet d’avocat, ou par des interventions au titre d’expert.e dans différentes entités publiques ou privées) est un atout, tout comme une connaissance pratique des dynamiques de la gouvernance belge et européenne (notamment à travers une expérience professionnelle).
Vos compétences

Vous travaillez aisément en équipe d’enseignant·es et vous intégrez les résultats des recherches dans vos enseignements. Vous êtes capable de mener des recherches scientifiques de haut niveau, de l’obtention des fonds jusqu’à la gestion de l’équipe. Vous faites preuve de créativité, d’ouverture à l’innovation pédagogique et à la pluridisciplinarité. Vous êtes susceptible, par vos connaissances et compétences et votre positionnement méthodologique dans la recherche en droit, de jeter des ponts entre le droit public et le droit économique au sens large. Vous avez développé des recherches interdisciplinaires et/ou théoriques, qui démontrent une connaissance des dynamiques économiques relatives à la transition.
Vous communiquez en français et en anglais. Si ce n’est pas le cas, vous vous engagez à acquérir la maîtrise de ces deux langues dans un délai de deux ans après la prise de fonction. La connaissance d’autres langues, comme en particulier le néerlandais, est un atout.

Reference: 38704 / LSM 011 / 2027
UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic position in Quantitative Finance : Innovation and Transition
Main campus:
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
Post description
Within the Louvain School of Management (LSM) and the Louvain Institute of Data Analysis and Modeling in economics and statistics (LIDAM), Social Sciences and Humanities Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

You will teach mainly in the AFIN field (accounting and finance) within the Louvain School of Management (LSM). You will teach in the various study cycles managed by the faculty. You will also supervise master's theses. You may be required to teach courses outside your direct area of expertise (e.g. general management courses, or courses of a quantitative nature) and, to a lesser extent, on campuses other than that linked to your main assignment, and on a staggered timetable. The teaching load is delivered in English and French at the bachelor's and master's levels, across the two campuses of the faculty, located in Louvain-la-Neuve and Mons. Overall, your presence will help to expand the capacity for supervising dissertations and diversify teaching approaches, whilst ensuring a stronger interdisciplinary presence.
Research

You will develop your research activities, including leading research programs, in the field of finance, studied using data-driven and quantitative approaches.  With this in mind, you will explore the concepts of innovation and transition in a very broad sense: technological innovations, including AI, and other innovations in the field of financial engineering on the one hand; and transition in the environmental, social and governance sense on the other. You will play an active role within the Louvain Institute for Data Analysis and Modeling (LIDAM) and the Louvain Finance (LFIN Pole) by participating in various events (seminars, workshops, etc.). You will also supervise Ph.D. theses.
In addition …

Once tenured, you will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee, or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
You will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Management, Economics or Finance or in another field (engineering, statistics, actuarial science, etc.) but have worked on financial applications. As part of your research, you have worked with modern quantitative analysis tools. Fields of application of particular relevance to us include – but are not limited to: AI and machine learning, data science, fintech, energy, climate and environment.
Experience

You have experience of teaching at university level, preferably supported by formal assessment. If not, you have teaching skills (presentations to audiences of various sizes). Your research experience is evidenced by international publications. You have a good network of scientific collaborators in different countries, as evidenced by publications or research partnerships (academic and/or with the associative or private sector). Ideally, you have completed a significant stay or experience abroad, outside the institution where you obtained your PhD.
Skills

You are comfortable working as part of a team of academics and integrate research results into your teaching. You are capable of conducting high-level scientific research, from obtaining funding to team management. You are creative, open to pedagogical innovation and multidisciplinary. You are familiar with modern tools in the field of statistics, econometrics and data analysis in general.
You can communicate in French and English. If this is not the case, you undertake to acquire a command of these two languages within two years of taking up your position. Knowledge of other languages is an asset.
What we offer

Référence du poste: 38704 / LSM 011 / 2027
L'UCLouvain recherche
Un·e académique à temps plein en Finance quantitative : innovation et transition
Campus principal: Louvain-la-Neuve
À propos de nous
L'UCLouvain est la première université belge francophone et est aussi largement reconnue à l'international. Université complète implantée au cœur de l’Europe depuis 1425, elle rassemble près de 40.000 étudiantes et étudiants et 6 000 membres du personnel répartis sur 9 campus, à Bruxelles et en Wallonie. L’UCLouvain est un acteur majeur de transition vers une société durable. Elle intègre les enjeux de la crise écologique dans les formations et développe de nombreux projets locaux (ferme universitaire, campus durables). Université numérique, l'UCLouvain s’implique dans la science et l’éducation ouvertes et forme les enseignants aux pratiques pédagogiques innovantes (Louvain Learning Lab). Ces partenariats se concrétisent à travers de nombreux accords d’échange, l’engagement fort dans l’alliance européenne Circle U. et dans le réseau The Guild, et l’accueil d’une large communauté de chercheuses et chercheurs internationaux, facilité par le Louvain Welcome Desk.
L’Université a une politique du personnel basée sur cinq binômes de valeurs qui constituent des piliers fondamentaux du mode de fonctionnement et de la façon de travailler et de vivre ensemble au sein de l’Université : https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
La fonction
Au sein de la Louvain School of Management (LSM) et du Louvain Institute of Data Analysis and Modeling in economics and statistics (LIDAM), Secteur des sciences humaines, cette fonction comprend des activités d’enseignement, de recherche et de services à la communauté:
Enseignement

Vous enseignerez principalement dans le domaine d'enseignement AFIN (comptabilité et finance) au sein de la Louvain School of Management (LSM). Vous assurerez vos enseignements dans les divers cycles d’études gérés par la faculté. Vous y dirigerez également des mémoires de master. Vous pourriez être amené·e à enseigner des cours en dehors de votre domaine d’expertise directe (par exemple des cours généralistes en gestion, ou de nature quantitative) ainsi que, dans une moindre mesure, sur d’autres campus que celui lié à votre affectation principale et en horaire décalé. Ce poste comprend une charge d'enseignement dispensée en anglais et en français aux niveaux bachelier (licence) et master, sur les deux campus de la faculté, situés à Louvain-la-Neuve et à Mons. Votre présence contribuera à renforcer les capacités d'encadrement de mémoires et à diversifier les approches pédagogiques, tout en assurant une présence interdisciplinaire plus marquée.
Recherche

Vous développerez vos activités de recherche, y compris l’animation de programmes de recherche, dans le domaine de la finance environnementale et climatique étudié à l’aide d’approches quantitatives. Dans cette optique, vous aborderez les concepts d'innovation et de transition dans leur acception la plus large : d'une part, les innovations technologiques, notamment l'intelligence artificielle, et d'autres innovations dans le domaine de l'ingénierie financière ; d'autre part, la transition au sens environnemental, social et de gouvernance. Vous prendrez une part active au sein du Louvain Institute for Data Analysis and Modeling (LIDAM) et du pôle de recherche Louvain Finance (LFIN), en participant aux différents événements organisés (séminaires, workshops, etc). Vous assurerez la supervision de thèses de doctorat.
Et encore...

Vous assumerez, une fois confirmé·e (« tenured »), différentes activités de services et responsabilités au sein de l’institution, telles qu’un rôle dans les commissions de programme, dans les jurys d’études ou des responsabilités de gestion au sein de la faculté ou de l’institut de recherche.
Vous contribuerez également aux services à la société, notamment dans les domaines économique, social, culturel ou de la coopération au développement. Enfin, vous assurerez, par des activités de recherche et d’enseignement, la visibilité internationale de l’université.
Qui cherchons-nous?
Votre parcours

Vous êtes titulaire d’un doctorat en gestion, économie ou finance ou dans un autre domaine (ingénierie, énergie, statistiques, etc) mais ayant travaillé sur des applications liées au domaine de la finance. Dans le cadre de vos recherches, vous avez manipulé des outils modernes d’analyse quantitative. Les domaines d'application qui nous intéressent particulièrement comprennent, entre autres : l'intelligence artificielle et l'apprentissage automatique, la science des données, la fintech, l'énergie, le climat et l'environnement.
Votre expérience

Vous disposez d’une pratique en enseignement universitaire, attestée si possible par des évaluations formelles. A défaut, vous avez une aptitude dans le domaine pédagogique (présentations devant des audiences de tailles diverses). Votre expérience en recherche est démontrée par des publications de niveau international. Vous bénéficiez d’un bon réseau de collaborateurs scientifiques dans différents pays, attesté par des publications ou des partenariats de recherche (académique et/ou avec le monde associatif ou privé).
Idéalement, vous l’avez complétée par un séjour ou une expérience significative à l’étranger, effectué hors de l’institution qui a délivré votre doctorat.
Vos compétences

Vous travaillez aisément en équipe d’enseignant·es et vous intégrez les résultats des recherches dans vos enseignements. Vous êtes capable de mener des recherches scientifiques de haut niveau, de l’obtention des fonds jusqu’à la gestion de l’équipe. Vous faites preuve de créativité, d’ouverture à l’innovation pédagogique et à la pluridisciplinarité. Vous maitrisez des outils modernes dans le domaine des statistiques, de l’économétrie, et en analyse de données de manière générale.
Vous communiquez en français et en anglais. Si ce n’est pas le cas, vous vous engagez à acquérir la maîtrise de ces deux langues dans un délai de deux ans après la prise de fonction. La connaissance d’autres langues est un atout.
Nous vous offrons
Une nomination définitive au cadre académique après évaluation positive de la période probatoire d’une durée habituelle de 4 ans. Ce type de carrière donne droit à une pension du secteur public;
Une nomination au grade de chargé·e de cours ou de professeur·e en fonction de votre expérience académique antérieure, appréciée souverainement par le Conseil rectoral;
Une charge d’enseignement plafonnée à un maximum de 90h pour un temps plein avant confirmation (en «tenured-track») contre 150h en «tenured»;
Une rémunération attractive et évolutive en fonction de l’ancienneté et du processus de promotion;
Un démarrage de vos fonctions au plus tôt le 1er septembre 2027;
Un parcours de formation intégré en leadership et management et un éventail de formations pédagogiques, linguistiques et autres;
Divers avantages: transport, famille, culture, commerces, etc.;
Une politique du personnel soutenant l’égalité des chances et la diversité au sein de la carrière académique comme dans toutes les autres catégories de personnel;
Une attention particulière portée à la conciliation vie privée – vie professionnelle.

Informations pratiques
Date limite de candidature: 5 novembre 2026 à midi (12h) (fuseau horaire UTC+1)
Entrée en fonction: le 1er septembre 2027
Localisation:
Secteur des sciences humaines
Louvain School of Management (LSM) (https://uclouvain.be/fr/facultes/LSM)
Louvain Institute of Data Analysis and Modeling in economics and statistics (IDAM) (https://uclouvain.be/fr/instituts-recherche/IDAM)
Besoin de plus d’informations?
Des questions sur la fonction ?
Prof. Matthieu de Nanteuil, Doyen LSM – [email protected]
Prof. Catherine Legrand, Présidente IDAM – [email protected]
Des questions sur la procédure ?
Mme Céline Brauns – Cabinet de la Rectrice - [email protected]
Des questions sur le dépôt de votre dossier online ?
Mme Andreea Chiriac – Cabinet de la Rectrice – [email protected]
Intéressé·e?
Les candidatures doivent être introduites exclusivement via l’outil de recrutement en ligne de l’UCLouvain ; celles transmises par d’autres canaux ne seront pas prises en considération.
Les modalités complètes de constitution du dossier sont disponibles à l’adresse suivante:
https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/candidature-aca.html
Pour être recevable, le dossier de candidature doit comprendre un fichier PDF unique, contenant les documents suivants:
une lettre de motivation (à inclure également dans votre profil candidat);
un curriculum vitae détaillé et à jour (à inclure également dans votre profil candidat);
une copie du diplôme officiel de doctorat;
la liste complète de vos publications, accompagnée d’un résumé de trois publications récentes et significatives;
un projet pédagogique, présentant votre vision et vos méthodes d’enseignement;
une stratégie de recherche, décrivant votre programme de recherche envisagé sur cinq ans.

Les candidat·es présélectionné·es et invité·es à une audition seront ultérieurement invité·es à fournir:
un projet de thèse de doctorat, en vue de l’éventuel engagement d’un·e doctorant·e dès la première année de la nomination;
trois à cinq lettres de recommandation, à transmettre directement par les personnes de référence selon les modalités qui leur seront communiquées.

UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic position in Common Law, Comparative Law and Legal Culture
Main campus: Saint-Louis - Bruxelles
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
The Saint-Louis Campus Brussels (until recently known as the Université Saint-Louis - Brussels) is characterised by its specialisation in the humanities, its pioneering experience with staggered timetables, successful initiatives promoting multilingualism over the past 30 years, and the specialisation and influence of its centres and research institute, IRIS-L, in a number of specialist fields. This approach is part of a commitment to promoting interdisciplinarity in relevant fields, a culture of community and human relations across all the site’s activities, and a resolute openness to the economic, social, cultural and religious diversity that characterises the BrusselsCapital Region, which serves as both the primary seat of the European Union’s institutions and the capital of the State.
Post description
Within the Faculty of Law Saint-Louis and the Institut de recherche interdisciplinaire Saint-Louis, Social Sciences and Humanities Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

You will be responsible for delivering daytime lectures in English. These will mainly cover common law and comparative law, for the bilingual French-English Bachelor of Law and the Bachelor of Droit-Rechten-Laws (a joint degree with KU Leuven), in blocks 1 and 2. The Common Law course will not be limited to English and US law and will incorporate other legal cultures. You will also be responsible for teaching legal theory (in block 3).
Where necessary, and where possible, teaching in the humanities may be added to your portfolio.
These courses will form part of our Manifesto for Legal Education ( https://doi.org/10.3917/riej.076.0169)
Research

You will be based at the IRIS-L Institute (which brings together the research units at the Saint-Louis campus in Brussels) and will play an active role in one of the Faculty of Law’s research centres (in private, public, criminal or environmental law, etc.  depending on your main areas of research). You will participate in and initiate collaborative projects within this centre. During your career, you will supervise PhD theses there and seek to secure external funding, particularly from the FRS-FNRS, the Federal Science Policy Office, the Brussels-Capital Region and the European Union, to carry out new projects.
You will also need to demonstrate an ability to develop collaborative projects with other research centres, in particular the Interdisciplinary Seminar on Legal Studies (SIEJ – https://siej.uclouvain.be/)
In addition …

Once tenured, you will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee, or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
You will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Law or Legal Science, or possibly in another relevant discipline, and have the necessary legal training for the post advertised here (such as a postgraduate degree or an LLM).
Experience

You have a proven track record in university teaching, with evidence where possible by formal evaluations.
Skills

Teaching skills
You must demonstrate significant experience in public speaking.
You will also have a high-quality, innovative teaching programme that promotes student inclusion and participation, as well as dialogue with the legal profession and with disciplines outside the field of law.
If you are shortlisted during the first phase of the application assessment, you will have the opportunity to demonstrate your skills and teaching proposal during a lesson on Common Law or comparative law, delivered in English and in the presence of the recruitment panel.
Experience of university teaching is a significant advantage. Ideally, this experience will have been gained with a variety of audiences (large lecture theatres and small groups, for example).
Academic expertise
You must have completed a doctoral thesis in law, the excellence of which is attested to, amongst other things, by the examination report.
You must also be able to demonstrate a significant number of academic publications in law, in edited volumes and Belgian or international peer-reviewed journals. You must be able to work effectively within a teaching team and integrate research findings into your teaching.
You are capable of conducting high-level scientific research, from securing funding to managing a team. You demonstrate creativity and an openness to pedagogical innovation and to multi- or interdisciplinary approaches (such as the humanities).
The following are considered significant assets:
international experience;
the publication of one or more monographs and/or edited volumes;
the ability to combine different disciplinary fields and an appreciation of multi- or interdisciplinarity;
having undertaken research visits to institutions other than the one where the thesis was completed;
conducting research with an interdisciplinary focus and working with colleagues from other disciplines;
the organisation of one or more international seminars and/or conferences;
having secured external funding;
having close ties with certain journals and learned societies in the field of Common Law or comparative law;
one or more community roles demonstrating a commitment to serving society through previous projects and research activities;
the ability to participate, in French, in faculty activities, or a commitment to acquire this ability towards confirmation.

Language skills
You must have a perfect command (C2 level) of English. If this proficiency is not demonstrated by at least two years’ university study in the language in question, it must be certified by an external assessment.
You must also have a very good command of French (C1 level) or commit to acquiring it with a view to confirmation.
What we offer
Tenure after positive assessment of the probationary period – typically four years. This type of career entitles you to a public sector pension.

Appointment as lecturer or professor according to your previous academic experience, as determined by the Rectoral Council.

Teaching load capped at 90 hours for a full-time tenure-track position, and 150 hours once tenured.

An attractive and progressive salary according to seniority and the promotion process.

A start date of 1 September 2027 at the earliest.

An integrated leadership and management training programme, including a range of pedagogical, linguistic and other training courses.

Benefits including transport, family, culture, commercial, etc.

Official policy that supports equal opportunities and promotes diversity within academic and all other categories of staff.

Specific emphasis on a work-life balance.

Starting date: September 1st 2027

Vous disposez d’une pratique avérée en enseignement universitaire, attestée si possible par des évaluations formelles. Votre expérience scientifique est démontrée par des publications de niveau international.
Vos compétences

Compétences pédagogiques
Vous devez témoigner d’une expérience significative de prise de parole en public.
Vous aurez également un projet pédagogique de qualité et innovant, qui vise l’inclusion et la participation des étudiant·e·s mais aussi le dialogue avec la pratique et avec des disciplines extra-juridiques.
En cas de sélection lors de la première phase d’évaluation des candidatures, vous aurez l’occasion de démontrer votre compétences et votre projet pédagogique lors d’une leçon en Common Law ou en droit comparé dispensée en anglais et en présence de la commission de recrutement.
Une expérience d’enseignement universitaire constitue un atout appréciable. Idéalement, cette expérience sera acquise auprès de publics différents (grands amphithéâtres et petits groupes par exemple).
Compétences scientifiques
Vous devez avoir réalisé une thèse de doctorat en droit dont l’excellence est attestée, entre autres, par le rapport de soutenance.
Vous devez aussi pouvoir faire état d’un nombre significatif de publications scientifiques en droit, dans des ouvrages collectifs et des revues belges ou internationales, soumis au peer-review.
Vous devez travailler aisément en équipe d’enseignant·es et intégrer les résultats des recherches dans vos enseignements. Vous êtes capable de mener des recherches scientifiques de haut niveau, de l’obtention des fonds jusqu’à la gestion de l’équipe. Vous faites preuve de créativité, d’ouverture à l’innovation pédagogique et à la pluri– ou l’interdisciplinarité (humanities par exemple).
Constituent des atouts appréciables :
une expérience internationale ;
la publication d’une ou plusieurs monographies et/ou ouvrages collectifs ;
l’aptitude à brasser des champs disciplinaires différents et le sens de la pluri– ou l’interdisciplinarité;
l’accomplissement de séjours de recherche dans des établissements autres que celui au sein duquel la thèse a été réalisée
l’accomplissement de recherches avec une orientation interdisciplinaire et le travail avec des collègues issus d’autres disciplines ;
l’organisation d’un ou plusieurs séminaires et/ou colloques internationaux ;
l’obtention de financements extérieurs ;
des liens privilégiés avec certaines revues et sociétés savantes dans le domaine de la Common Law ou du droit comparé;
un ou plusieurs engagements associatifs au service de la société par ses projets et activités de recherche antérieurs;
une capacité à participer, en français, aux activités de la faculté, ou vous engager à l’acquérir en vue de la confirmation.

Compétences linguistiques
Vous devez avoir une parfaite maîtrise (niveau C2) de l’anglais. Cette compétence, si elle n’est pas attestée par une formation universitaire d’au moins deux ans suivie dans la langue concernée, devra être certifiée par un indicateur extérieur
Vous devez avoir aussi une très bonne maîtrise du français (niveau C1) ou vous engager à l’acquérir en vue de la confirmation.
Nous vous offrons
Une nomination définitive au cadre académique après évaluation positive de la période probatoire d’une durée habituelle de 4 ans. Ce type de carrière donne droit à une pension du secteur public;
Une nomination au grade de chargé·e de cours ou de professeur·e en fonction de votre expérience académique antérieure, appréciée souverainement par le Conseil rectoral;
Une charge d’enseignement plafonnée à un maximum de 90h pour un temps plein avant confirmation (en «tenured-track») contre 150h en «tenured»;
Une rémunération attractive et évolutive en fonction de l’ancienneté et du processus de promotion;
Un démarrage de vos fonctions au plus tôt le 1er septembre 2027;
Un parcours de formation intégré en leadership et management et un éventail de formations pédagogiques, linguistiques et autres;
Divers avantages: transport, famille, culture, commerces, etc.;
Une politique du personnel soutenant l’égalité des chances et la diversité au sein de la carrière académique comme dans toutes les autres catégories de personnel;
Une attention particulière portée à la conciliation vie privée – vie professionnelle.

https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/candidature-aca.html

une lettre de motivation (à inclure également dans votre profil candidat);

Reference: 38690 / LSM 067 / 2027
UCLouvain seeks to recruit
A full-time academic position in Optimization and Learning for Data-Driven Decision systems
Main campus: Louvain-la-Neuve
About us
UCLouvain is the leading French-speaking university in Belgium and is also widely recognised internationally. Founded in the heart of Europe in 1425, the university brings together 40,000 students and 6,000 staff members on nine campuses in Brussels and Wallonia. Research and education activities are organised in 20 faculties, 23 research institutes, 5 learning centres and 18 libraries. UCLouvain also has two university hospitals.
UCLouvain is a major player in the transition to a sustainable society. The challenges of the ecological crisis are integrated into courses and the university develops numerous local projects (such as a university farm and sustainable campuses). As a digital university, UCLouvain is involved in open science and education, and trains academics in innovative teaching practices through its Louvain Learning Lab. Thanks to two science parks, the university’s research benefits from interaction with 250 companies and 3 incubators, which is fuelled further by being at the centre of a region driven by technological innovation.
UCLouvain has a strong tradition of international collaboration in both teaching and research. These partnerships take shape through numerous exchange agreements, its firm commitment to the European alliance Circle U. and the network The Guild, as well as the welcoming of a large community of international researchers, supported by the Louvain Welcome Desk.
The University's staff policy is based on five pairs of values which are fundamental pillars of the way the University operates, works and lives together: https://uclouvain.be/fr/emploi/politique-personnel.html
Post description
Within the Louvain School of Management (LSM) and the Louvain Institute of Data Analysis and Modeling in economics and statistics (LIDAM), Social Sciences and Humanities Sector, this position will include the following teaching, research and community service duties:
Teaching

To develop, in future managers, high-levels skills in coding, optimization, and learning-based decision methodologie, the current course portfolio includes programming, operations research, artificial intelligence, and quantitative decision making. The teaching load is delivered in English and French at the bachelor's and master's levels, across the two campuses of the Louvain School of Management (LSM), located in Louvain-la-Neuve and Mons. Overall, your presence will help to expand the capacity for supervising dissertations and diversify teaching approaches, whilst ensuring a stronger interdisciplinary presence.
Research

To develop a strong and internationally visible research agenda centered on mathematical optimization and its integration with data science and machine learning for decision systems, research areas of interest include advanced optimization methods (linear, integer, stochastic, robust, distributionally robust, and chance-constrained); predictive and prescriptive analytics bridging forecasting and decision-making; learning-integrated decision frameworks (predict-then-optimize, decision-focused learning, reinforcement learning); and algorithmic decision models combining mathematical programming with AI techniques.
The successful candidate is expected to play an active role within the Louvain Institute for Data Analysis and Modeling (LIDAM), and more specifically in the Center for Operations Research and Econometrics (CORE), by participating in academic events, publishing in leading journals in operations research,  mathematical programming and machine learning, supervising doctoral students, and actively collaborating with researchers from the Center for Operations Research and Econometrics (CORE), and more generally from the Louvain Institute for Data Analysis and Modeling (LIDAM), as well as those from the Institute of Information and Communication Technologies, Electronics, and Applied Mathematics (ICTEAM).
In addition …

Once tenured, the successful candidate will carry out various service activities and responsibilities within the institution, such as being a member of a programme committee or examination committee or having management responsibilities within the faculty or research institute.
The successful candidate will also contribute to serving society, particularly in the economic, social, cultural or development cooperation fields. Finally, you will ensure, through research and teaching activities, the university’s international visibility.
Who we’re looking for
Education

You have a PhD in Operations Research, Applied Mathematics, Systems Engineering, Computer Science, Management Engineering, or a closely related quantitative field.
Experience

You have a proven track record in university teaching, with evidence where possible by formal evaluations. You can demonstrate a strong and independent research track record, with publications in leading international journals, or clear potential to publish, in operations research, mathematical programming, learning-based optimization, or machine learning. You have a strong core identity rooted in mathematical programming and operations research. Experience in securing competitive research funding and supervising doctoral students will be considered a strong asset.
Skills

You will bring expertise in the theory, algorithms, and modeling frameworks of mathematical optimization, with a research identity centered on advancing the methodological foundations of decision systems. You are able to make original contributions to optimization methods, whether in integer and stochastic programming, robust and distributionally robust optimization, or the principled integration of learning and optimization through frameworks such as predict-then-optimize, decision-focused learning, or reinforcement learning for sequential decision-making, and you are motivated by the challenge of building a unified methodological bridge between mathematical programming and modern data science. Specific experience in data-driven and learning-driven approaches to modeling and optimization will be considered as a strong asset.
You will be expected to become an active and contributing member of the research community of CORE and, more broadly, of LIDAM, enriching its methodological culture through contributions that advance the algorithmic and theoretical foundations of optimization and its integration with machine learning and AI.
You can communicate in French and English. If this is not the case, you undertake to acquire a command of these two languages within two years of taking up your position. Knowledge of other languages is an asset.
What we offer
Tenure after positive assessment of the probationary period – typically four years. This type of career entitles you to a public sector pension.

Appointment as lecturer or professor according to your previous academic experience, as determined by the Rectoral Council.

Teaching load capped at 90 hours for a full-time tenure-track position, and 150 hours once tenured.

An attractive and progressive salary according to seniority and the promotion process.

A start date of 1 September 2027 at the earliest.

An integrated leadership and management training programme, including a range of pedagogical, linguistic and other training courses.

Benefits including transport, family, culture, commercial, etc.

Official policy that supports equal opportunities and promotes diversity within academic and all other categories of staff.

Specific emphasis on a work-life balance.

Practical Information
Application deadline: 5 November 2026 at noon (UTC+1 Time Zone)
Starting date: September 1st 2027
Location:
Social Sciences and Humanities Sector
(LSM) (https://uclouvain.be/en/faculties/LSM)
(IDAM) (https://uclouvain.be/en/research-institutes/IDAM)
Need more information?
Questions about this position:
Prof. Matthieu de Nanteuil, Dean LSM – [email protected]
Prof. Catherine Legrand, President IDAM – [email protected]
Questions about the procedure:
Madam Céline Brauns, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Questions about online application:
Madam Andreea Chiriac, Rector’s Office,  [email protected]
Interested?
Applications must be submitted exclusively via UCLouvain’s online recruitment system; submissions through other channels will not be considered.
Full details regarding the application procedure are available at: https://www.uclouvain.be/en/careers/submit-your-application
Applications must include one single PDF file containing the following documents:
a cover letter (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a detailed and up‑to‑date curriculum vitae (to be included in the single PDF as well as in your candidate profile);
a copy of the official doctoral degree certificate;
a complete publication list, including a summary of three recent and significant publications;
a teaching statement;
a research statement presenting the proposed research programme for the next five years.

Shortlisted candidates invited for an interview will subsequently be asked to provide:
a PhD project proposal, with a view to the possible recruitment of a doctoral candidate during the first year of appointment;
three to five letters of reference, submitted directly by referees according to the instructions provided by the University.
