ap:253176.body:
Turun ihmistieteiden tutkijakollegiumissa (Turku Institute for Advanced Studies, TIAS) on haettavana neljä  (4) kollegiumtutkijan  kolmivuotista tehtävää ajalle 1.9.2027–31.8.2030.
TIAS-tutkijat valitaan kansainvälisen haun kautta. Haku on avoin kaikille hakijoille, joiden tutkimusprojektit sijoittuvat TIASin viiden perustajatiedekunnan tieteenaloille (humanistiset tieteet, kasvatustieteet, kauppatieteet, oikeustieteet, yhteiskuntatieteet).   Tutkijat valitaan akateemisten ansioiden perusteella.
Tehtävänkuvaus
TIAS-tutkijan päätehtävä on toteuttaa kansainvälisesti korkeatasoinen kolmivuotinen tutkimusprojekti ja levittää projektin tuloksia laajasti ja monipuolisesti eri tahoille. Tutkijoiden oletetaan myös antavan panoksensa TIAS-yhteisön toimintaan esimerkiksi osallistumalla ja esittämällä tutkimustaan TIAS-tapaamisissa, järjestämällä TIAS-tapahtumia ja tekemällä tieteidenvälistä yhteistyötä TIAS-kollegoidensa kanssa.
Tehtävät sijoittuvat Turun yliopiston kampuksille ja valittujen tutkijoiden on asuttava Suomessa. TIAS-tapaamisten lisäksi tutkijoiden oletetaan käyvän kampuksella säännöllisesti. TIAS-tutkijat sijoittuvat tiedekuntien laitoksiin ja ovat samalla osa aktiivista TIAS-tutkijayhteisöä.
Etsimämme henkilö
Kollegiumtutkijalta edellytetään tohtorin tutkintoa, jonka suorittamisesta on kulunut hakuajan päättyessä enintään 12 vuotta. Vakituisessa professorin tehtävässä olevat eivät voi hakea kollegiumtutkijan tehtävää.
Menestyksekäs julkaisutoiminta ja muu tieteellinen työ sekä merkittävä aktiivisuus ja osallistuminen kansainvälisiin akateemisiin verkostoihin tohtorintutkinnon suorittamisen jälkeen ovat edellytyksiä kollegiumtutkijan tehtävään nimittämiselle. Hakijoilta odotetaan kunnianhimoisia tutkimussuunnitelmia, joiden tavoitteena on uusi tieteellinen läpimurto.
TIAS tukee Turun yliopiston tutkimusstrategiaa. Hakijoiden tulee ilmoittaa, mihin Turun yliopiston laitokseen/yksikköön he toivoisivat sijoittuvansa, sekä kuvata, mihin laitoksen tutkimusalueista hakijan tutkimus kiinnittyy. Hakijoiden on myös kuvattava, miten heidän tutkimuksensa liittyy yhteen tai useampaan Turun yliopiston monitieteiseen teemaan ja vahvuusalaan sekä miksi he haluavat olla osa TIAS-yhteisöä.
TIAS-tutkijat valitaan korkeatasoisten akateemisten ansioiden perusteella.   Ulkoisia arvioijia pyydetään antamaan arviot (asteikolla 1–6) (i) hakijan aikaisemmista akateemisista saavutuksista suhteessa uravaiheeseen, (ii) tutkimussuunnitelman laadusta ja toteutettavuudesta kolmessa vuodessa, (iii) tutkimuksen teoreettisesta ja metodologisesta viitekehyksestä sekä (iv) suunnitelluista julkaisuista ja muista tuotoksista. Lisäksi heitä pyydetään antamaan (v) kokonaisarvio hakemuksesta. Arvioijia pyydetään myös kommentoimaan tutkimussuunnitelman eettisiä näkökohtia. TIAS-johtokunta valitsee tutkijat ulkoisten arvioiden perusteella.
Tarjoamme
TIAS edistää tutkijanuran alku- ja keskivaiheilla olevien huippututkijoiden urakehitystä tarjoamalla kolmivuotisen rahoituksen ja mahdollisuuden toteuttaa itsenäisesti suunniteltu tutkimusprojekti.
TIAS-tutkijoilla on tutkimustyön lisäksi vain vähän muita työvelvoitteita. Kaikilla TIAS-tutkijoilla on mahdollisuus osallistua Turun yliopiston opetustoimintaan. Opetustehtävät voivat olla enintään 5 % tutkijan vuosittaisesta 1 612 tunnin työajasta. Lisäksi tutkijat voivat käyttää toisen 5 % kokonaistyöajastaan muihin akateemisiin ja hallinnollisiin tehtäviin
Lue lisää meistä  Tervetuloa meille töihin  -sivulta, jossa lisää siitä, mitä yliopisto tarjoaa työntekijälleen.
Euroopan komissio on myöntänyt Turun yliopistolle oikeuden käyttää erinomaisen työnantajan  HR Excellence in Research laatuleimaa  merkkinä yliopiston sitoutumisesta tutkijoiden aseman ja työolosuhteiden jatkuvaan kehittämiseen Tutkijoiden eurooppalaisen peruskirjan tavoitteiden mukaisesti.
Turun yliopisto sijoittuu kansainvälisissä yliopistorankingeissa erittäin hyvin ja on useilla aloilla maailman yliopistojen parhaimmiston joukossa. Korkealaatuinen perustutkimus, monitieteinen tutkimusprofiili sekä tiivis yhteistyö tutkimusinfrastruktuureiden osalta luovat pohjan kansainväliselle huippututkimukselle. Lue lisää sijoittumisestamme kansainvälisissä yliopistorankingeissa.
Turun yliopistossa on useita korkeatasoisia huippututkimuksen edellyttämiä tutkimusinfrastruktuureja. Katso lista Turun yliopiston tutkimusinfrastruktuureista ja lue lisää yritysyhteistyötä tukevista palvelututkimuksesta ja infrastruktuureista .
Palkkaus ja koeaika
Kollegiumtutkijan palkkaus määräytyy yliopistojen palkkausjärjestelmän mukaisesti. Tehtäväkohtainen palkkaus on määritelty siten, että palkkaus vastaa työsuhteeseen otettaessa vaativuustason 7 ja henkilökohtaisen suoriutumisen osuuden 17 % euromääräistä palkkausta (tällä hetkellä 5295 €/kk). Tutkijan henkilökohtaisen suoriutumisen kehittyminen voidaan työsuhteen aikana ottaa huomioon palkkauksen määrittelyssä.
Tehtävässä noudatetaan kuuden kuukauden koeaikaa.
Hakuohjeet
Luethan ensin  yksityiskohtaiset hakuohjeet TIASin verkkosivuilla  (sisältää ohjeet tarvittavista hakuasiakirjoista).
Hakemukset tulee jättää  viimeistään 13.11.2026 (klo 16:00)  sähköisen rekrytointijärjestelmämme kautta.
Lisätietoja antaa
Lisätietoja TIASista verkkosivuilla .
Hakuinfo järjestetään maanantaina 28.9.2026 klo 14.00–16.00. Huomaathan, että hakuinfossa käydään läpi sekä TIAS-tutkijahaku (tutkijatohtorit ja kollegiumtutkijat) että TIES2 MSCA COFUND Fellowship -haku . TIASin johtaja esittelee haun ja arviointiprosessin sekä vastaa kysymyksiin. Esitysdiat päivitetään verkkosivuille tilaisuuden jälkeen.  Ilmoittaudu hakuinfoon saadaksesi osallistumislinkin.
Kysymyksiä hausta voi lähettää myös osoitteeseen [email protected] .

Turun ihmistieteiden tutkijakollegium  (Turku Institute for Advanced Studies, TIAS) on humanistisen tiedekunnan, kasvatustieteiden tiedekunnan, oikeustieteellisen tiedekunnan, Kauppakorkeakoulun ja yhteiskuntatieteellisen tiedekunnan yhteinen kollegium. Turun yliopisto on 25 000 opiskelijan ja työntekijän innostava ja kansainvälinen akateeminen yhteisö. Rakennamme kestävää tulevaisuutta monitieteisellä tutkimuksella, koulutuksella ja yhteistyöllä. Job description
In this EngD project, you will develop an AI model that automatically detects underground infrastructure in GPR radargrams and estimates its depth. The project builds on the growing availability of high-quality GPR data collected at the University of Twente’s Utility Mapping Site (UMS), a unique test environment for utility mapping technologies.
Current machine learning models and their training data are limited in size, comprehensiveness, and realism – resulting in partial automation with limited performance. This constrains their usefulness in real-world conditions. Your challenge is to develop and validate machine learning models using systematically collected and accurately annotated GPR datasets. By combining geospatial data, subsurface sensing, and AI, you will contribute to the next generation of utility mapping technologies and support safer excavation practices.
Your environment
This project is part of the ZoARG|ReDUCE programme, a collaborative initiative aimed at minimizing excavation damage to underground infrastructure in the Netherlands. You will work within a multidisciplinary environment that includes:
The University of Twente’s Departments of Civil Engineering and Management (CEM) and Applied Earth Sciences (AES)
The Utility Mapping Site (UMS) at the UT FieldLab
Industry collaborators involved in the ZoARG programme

Analyse existing GPR interpretation methods, machine learning techniques, and relevant software tools
Explore and evaluate AI approaches for automated utility characterization
Prepare, preprocess, and manage large GPR datasets collected at the Utility Mapping Site
Design, develop, train, and validate machine learning models for interpreting GPR radargrams
Compare developed models with existing approaches reported in literature and commercial software solutions
Work in close partnership with infrastructure owners, contractors, technology providers, and researchers engaged in the ZoARG programme
Report findings and translate results into practical recommendations for measurement practice and technology evaluation

Your profile
A Master’s degree or equivalent experience in Civil Engineering, Geomatics, Computer Science, Data Science, or a related field
Experience with machine learning, data analytics, or computer vision techniques
Programming experience in Python and familiarity with machine learning frameworks such as PyTorch, TensorFlow, or similar tools
Curiosity about geospatial data, remote sensing, subsurface sensing, or utility mapping applications;
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills
The ability to work independently and collaborate effectively with academic and industrial partners
Excellent communication skills and proficiency in English

Two-year full-time EngD position, where scientific and research domains are combined optimally with education and practical implementation of innovative design
Full status as an employee at the UT, including pension and health care benefits
A tailor-made post-master build programme that has an educational component (40%) as well as a design project (60%)
A gross monthly salary of €3173
An annual holiday allowance of 8% of the gross annual salary, and an annual year-end bonus of 8.3%
Minimum of 29 holidays per year in case of full-time employment

ap:253210.body:
You will be embedded in the research unit Occupational & Organisational Psychology and Professional Learning (O2L) at the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, KU Leuven (https://ppw.kuleuven.be/o2l/english). O2L brings together researchers working on work, organizational behavior, and professional learning, and offers a collaborative environment with active seminar series, methodological support and international collaborations.

Within O2L, you will work in the interdisciplinary research group of this project, jointly supervised by Prof. dr. Jeroen Stouten (Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, KU Leuven) and Prof. dr. Katleen De Stobbeleir (Vlerick Business School). Jeroen Stouten is Professor of Organizational Psychology and studies leadership and organizational change. Katleen De Stobbeleir is Professor of Leadership at Vlerick Business School and KU Leuven, where she directs the Centre for Excellence in Leading Adaptive Organisations; her research focuses on adaptive leadership, coaching, feedback processes and proactivity at work. This dual affiliation gives you access to both a strong psychological research tradition and a business school network with close ties to practice.

Website unit

Project

Leaders play a crucial role in helping their employees grow, not only in performance but also in knowledge and skills. Yet we know surprisingly little about how leaders actually do this. What concrete strategies do they use to guide and develop employees? And why does one leader's approach work better than another's?

This PhD research digs into the heart of that question. We examine the mechanisms and behaviors through which leaders shape employee development, from providing growth opportunities and feedback to creating a climate in which learning feels natural. By making these strategies visible and measurable, we aim to contribute to a renewed understanding of leadership that is both theoretically relevant and practically applicable.

We are looking to fill two PhD positions for curious, ambitious candidates with a passion for organizational psychology and leadership research. The two positions are methodologically complementary: one focuses on quantitative work (survey and experimental designs, multilevel and longitudinal analysis), the other on qualitative work (interviews, observation, and case-based designs). Both candidates work on the same overarching question and collaborate closely, in an inspiring research environment where the two approaches inform each other.

Profile

Holds (or will soon obtain) a Master's degree in Psychology, or another relevant discipline.

A strong academic record, with at least a distinction (or equivalent) in the Master's degree.

Strong interest in scientific research, and in leadership and organizational psychology topics.

Solid methodological training, with depth in the approach of the position applied for: For the quantitative position, a strong affinity for quantitative methods and statistics (e.g., multilevel analysis, SEM); for the qualitative position, a strong affinity for qualitative methods (e.g., interviewing, thematic and case-based analysis). Familiarity with the other approach is an asset.

Independent and flexible, with good organizational and time-management skills.

Strong collaboration and communication skills within a research team.

Excellent written and verbal skills in English.

Motivated to invest in further training, in both theory and research methods.

Motivated to publish research in high-quality international scientific journals and to present findings at international conferences.

Interested in teaching and supervising students.

Committed to obtaining a PhD within the four-year appointment.

Offer

Two fully funded and full-time PhD scholarships for one year, renewable up to four years upon positive evaluation.

A research budget for data collection, conferences, and training.

Starting date: from January 2027, subject to approval by the doctoral committee

Throughout your doctoral training, you will be encouraged to publish in leading international journals, present your work at international conferences, collaborate with renowned researchers, and build an international scientific network.

A research affiliation with Vlerick Business School, giving you access to its faculty, research infrastructure and corporate network.

KU Leuven offers a competitive PhD salary and benefits, access to excellent research facilities, extensive training opportunities, and a vibrant international academic community in the historic city of Leuven.

KU Leuven offers a wide range of company benefits https://www.kuleuven.be/personeel/jobsite/en/management-and-professionals/management-and-professionals-information#working-conditions

Interested?

Your application should contain the following elements:

(1) a motivation letter (max. two pages), stating whether you are applying for the quantitative or the qualitative position or for both

(2) a curriculum vitae

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Jeroen Stouten, mail: [email protected] or Prof. dr. Katleen De Stobbeleir, mail: [email protected]

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. ap:253211.body:
This proposed PhD research will be carried out in the Additive Manufacturing (AM) team at the Department of Mechanical Engineering from KU Leuven.

KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a center of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. The university caters to over 60,000 students from more than 140 countries. KU Leuven's three doctoral schools provide internationally oriented PhD tracks for more than 4,000 doctoral students. KU Leuven and affiliated knowledge institutes provide fertile ground for innovation and high-tech entrepreneurship in the Leuven region. This favourable climate for knowledge-driven innovation makes the Leuven region an attractive location for many high-tech companies.

KU Leuven website: https://www.kuleuven.be/english/kuleuven/

AM team linkedIn: https://www.linkedin.com/company/amkul

AM team website:

Website unit

Project

KU Leuven seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded, four-year international doctoral position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) project TURBO-IMPACT (TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology ; Website: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350).

The TurboImpact project, funded by Horizon Europe – MSCA-DN, tackles challenges in designing, optimizing, selecting materials, and manufacturing small-scale turbomachinery for applications in heat pumps, fuel cells, organic Rankine cycles, or gas turbines. This project develops robust system and component design methods, an integrated manufacturing platform, and multi-material joining techniques to efficiently produce small-scale turbomachinery.

In that large EU project, This PhD researcher (DC7) will work at KU Leuven and focus on increasing the fundamental understanding of multi-metal Laser Powder Bed Fusion (LPBF) additive manufacturing for small-scale turbomachinery. Metals with high temperature-resistance will be targeted with special focus on the relation between material characteristics, LPBF process parameters, and resulting mechanical performance.

The doctoral candidate will:

Use and extend beyond state-of-the-art equipment available in Leuven and investigate 1D and 3D powder deposition strategies inside LPBF equipment

Design and validate a multi-physical digital model to predict ideal LPBF parameters and scanning strategies with focus on the interface regions

Study the influence of local laser remelting on surface properties, porosity and general interface quality

Investigate the relationship between material, process, and final properties

The project includes potential international secondments at DTU (Prof. G. Bissacco, Denmark) and Amnovis (Dr. R. Wauthle, Belgium).

The researcher is supervised by Prof. Brecht Van Hooreweder (www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/en/person/00059721), director of Leuven.AM and head of the AM team. The AM team currently counts >25 researchers and is pioneering in metal AM since 1990. More information on the website (www.mech.kuleuven.be/en/research/am/) or linkedIn (www.linkedin.com/company/amkul).

Profile

• I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics and performed above average in comparison to my peers. I am not in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.

• I am proficient in written and spoken English.

• During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some basic experience with the basic physical principles of additive manufacturing and/or with the basic principles of manufacturing and mechanical behavior of materials or I have a profound interest in these topics.

• I demonstrate a strong sense of initiative and responsibility, while also being an effective and collaborative team player.

• Based on interactions and discussions with my supervisors and the colleagues in my team, I set up and update a plan of approach for the upcoming 1 to 3 months to work towards my research goals. I work with a sufficient degree of independence to follow my plan and achieve the goals. I indicate timely when deviations of the plan are required, if goals cannot be met or if I want to discuss intermediate results or issues.

• In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors who steer the direction of my research.

• I feel comfortable to work as a team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and be inspired by my colleagues.

Special requirements:

In accordance with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network regulations:

Applicants must comply with the MSCA Mobility Rule. At the time of recruitment, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the hiring Country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment.

Applicants must be doctoral candidates (i.e., not already hold a doctoral degree) and be eligible under the MSCA Doctoral Network rules at the time of recruitment.

Short stays such as holidays, compulsory national service, or time spent as part of a refugee procedure are not considered.

Applicants must have a two-year master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing Engineering, Computer Science, Data Science, Software Engineering, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Offer

Successful candidates will:

be enrolled in the KU Leuven PhD programme,

conduct research in a stimulating international environment with access to state-of-the-art facilities and supervision by recognised experts,

participate in local and network-wide training activities aimed at advancing scientific knowledge and transferable skills,

attend workshops and international conferences relevant to their research topic,

undertake secondments of approximately 4–6 months at other network or associated partner institutions.

receive further doctoral training for PhD candidates in the framework of the KU Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School (https://set.kuleuven.be/phd), known for its strong focus on both future scientists and scientifically trained professionals who will valorise their doctoral expertise and competences in a non-academic context.

Assessment:

Recruitment will be carried out and monitored in full accordance with the principles of the European Charter for Researchers, the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, and the Doctoral Network mobility rules. The process will follow an open, transparent, merit-based, impartial, and equitable procedure, tailored to each individual DC position. Promising candidates will undergo a series of interviews with the PI, the Supervisory Team, and the Recruitment Committee.

Please note that this position is part of a consortium involving several partner universities. By submitting your application, you consent to your personal data, CV and motivation letter being shared with and accessible to the relevant members of the consortium for the purposes of the recruitment and selection process

Salary and appointment terms:

Successful candidates will receive a comprehensive financial package in line with the rules for Doctoral Candidates (DCs) in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. Employment will be provided by the recruiting organisation and will include mobility and family allowances (where applicable), together with full social security coverage.

Doctoral Candidates will benefit from a competitive salary, paid leave (in accordance with institutional regulations), and access to national social security schemes. The employment starts on 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

Interested?

Follow the KU Leuven job application tool and enclose:

1. full CV – mandatory

2. motivation letter – mandatory

3. full list of credits and grades of both BSc and MSc degrees (as well as their transcription to English if possible) – mandatory(when you haven’t finished your degree yet, just provide us with the partial list of already available credits and grades)

4. proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, …) -if available

5. two reference letters - if available

6. an English version of your MSc or PhD thesis, or of a recent publication or assignment - if available

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Brecht Van Hooreweder, mail: [email protected] .

The IB is currently seeking an experienced individual to take on the role of Deputy Examiner Responsible (DER)  for its Tibetan A: Literature  course.
The International Baccalaureate® (IB) is a non-profit educational foundation offering four programmes of international education that develop the intellectual, personal, emotional and social skills needed to live, learn and work in a rapidly globalizing world. We strive to develop students who will build a better world through intercultural understanding and respect.
One of the characteristics of the IB's Diploma Programme is that students are required to study, as one of six subjects that constitute the diploma, one of three ‘Language A’ courses, each designed to develop high social, aesthetic and cultural literacy, as well as communication skills. The language A: literature course introduces students to the analysis of literary texts. It is the course through which the IB’s policy of mother-tongue entitlement is delivered. The course is automatically available in 55 languages and available by special request and may be studied in any language with a sufficiently developed written literature.
The duties of DER include the setting and marking of examinations and determining final grades of students.
Outline information about this role, as well as the application form and recruitment policy can be found at:  IB Deputy Examiner Responsible - International Baccalaureate®
Please note that this position is part-time, involves no relocation, and is usually undertaken in addition to existing work commitments.
You must:
have a degree or equivalent in the subject (or a related subject) for which you are applying,
have a minimum of one year’s experience teaching the subject (or a related subject) for which they are applying to students of: 16 to 18 years of age (DP)

be native speaker/fluent in English and Italian in order to write reports and mark students’ written and spoken responses.

ap:253225.body:
The Leibniz Institute for Educational Media | Georg Eckert Institute (GEI) is pleased to announce the Call for Applications for the 2028 Georg Arnhold Senior Fellow for Education for Sustainable Peace.
The principal objectives of the Georg Arnhold Program are (i) to bridge the gap between theory and practice in the field of peace education by bringing together scholars and practitioners, (ii) to respond to the need for decolonial approaches to peace education research and practice, (iii) and with its publications, to render findings and experiences freely available via open access publishing.
The Georg Arnhold Program is run by the Leibniz Institute for Educational Media | Georg Eckert Institute (GEI) in Brunswick, Germany. The GEI conducts research into the production, content and appropriation of educational media for schools in their socio-cultural, political, economic and historical contexts.
The fellowship aims to promote education for sustainable peace with a particular focus on educational media and curricula at secondary-school level in all regions of the world. Candidates should make clear in their application how their project responds to the objectives listed above.
The fellowship, which includes a research stay of six months at the GEI in Germany, offers outstanding and experienced individuals in the field of peace education the opportunity to focus on a research – or practice – related project. The project should focus on educational media of all kinds.
The Fellowship is endowed with
a monthly stipend of 3,300 EUR for a fellowship period of six months (in exceptional cases a shorter time frame can also be arranged, the minimum period being three months) at the Leibniz Institute for Educational Media ǀ GEI in Brunswick, Germany
return economy airfare to Germany
and support with administrative matters and publication work provided by the program coordinators

Eligibility
Applications are welcomed from outstanding scholars in the humanities, political and social sciences or education, with a project firmly located in the field of peace education. We also welcome applications from distinguished practitioners in the field of peace education with high-level international experience, for example in NGO management.
Scholarly applicants are required to hold a PhD and practitioner applicants are required to demonstrate at least five years of advanced professional achievement in their field. Pracademics should combine scholarly excellence with hands-on practice and grassroots work.
Obligations of the Fellowship Holder
The Georg Arnhold Senior Fellow shall complete a project in the area of education for sustainable peace, preferably with a focus on educational media or curriculum development.
The Fellowship holder is expected to take responsibility for the intellectual and conceptual design of the annual conference of the Georg Arnhold Program in collaboration with the coordinator of the Georg Arnhold Program.
They shall also present their project at the GEI’s research colloquium.
The Senior Fellow is expected to spend their fellowship period at the Leibniz Institute for Educational Media ǀ GEI in Brunswick, Germany, and to participate in the daily working life of the institute. The working language will be English.
The outcomes of the fellow’s project should be published no later than one year after the termination of the Fellowship. The output from the fellowship holder’s work should preferably be policy papers, educational materials, research papers, or a larger publication.
Candidates are responsible for obtaining a passport and visa, should the latter be required, as well as for arranging their own health and liability insurance for the duration of their stay in Germany.

The Fellowship offers
Use of the GEI’s international library of educational media (such as school textbooks, curricula and digital educational resources for schools) as a resource center, and the opportunity to explore the role textbooks and other educational media play in processes of peace and reconciliation but also in exacerbating inequities and conflict.
Mentoring by/discussions with GEI experts and the opportunity to present at GEI research colloquia.
Use of “The Basement” (experimental digital media lab at GEI with focus on games learning, VR, robotics, creative pedagogies, etc.) for own research.
Access to a broad network of scholars and practitioners working at the cross-section of peace education and educational media research.
Open Access fees for direct project outputs will be covered where possible.

Application and Selection Procedure
The application and selection process consist of five steps:
Online Application: Please complete the online application form. You will be asked to describe your project by answering some guiding questions about its objectives, the research gap you intend to address, your project's methodological and theoretical framework, and the expected outcomes. Before you start, it is therefore recommended to have short and longer written descriptions ready. Please also consult our AI-use policy before beginning.
Pre-selection by the Leibniz Institute for Educational Media | Georg Eckert Institute (GEI): The initial pre-selection of eligible candidates and suitable projects involves a multi-stage selection process at the GEI by academic experts of the institute. Up to 10 applications will be then forwarded to the Academic Advisory Board of the Georg Arnhold Program.
Shortlisting by the Academic Advisory Board of the Georg Arnhold Program: The Advisory Board will select the top three candidates for the final selection step.
Submission of full proposals by the shortlisted candidates: The three shortlisted top candidates will be invited to submit a full application (including a short CV and a list of publications) and a detailed project proposal via email. The full proposal should be no longer than 25 pages, including references and evidence of the impact they have made in the area of peace education (e. g. oft-cited publications, project websites, success stories, etc.). Each of the three shortlisted candidates, of which one will be selected, will be invited to an online interview with the Academic Advisory Board of the Georg Arnhold Program.
Selection Criteria: The principal criteria for the Board’s decision will be (i) the candidate’s expertise, experience and innovation as a practitioner or researcher, (ii) the overall quality of the project and the proposed output, (iii) the alignment of the project with the objectives of the Georg Arnhold Program (see above), (iv) and the candidate’s motivation to benefit from the stay at the Institute specifically.
Start of the Fellowship
The successful candidate can begin their fellowship in January 2028 at the earliest.

Doctoral Position for Synthetic Biology-Inspired Therapies
A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of the ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position in pioneering projects developing synthetic biology-inspired human therapies.

The D-BSSE is the first truly interdisciplinary research department, uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in material science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley, a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life science industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background
Advancing the Frontiers of Cell-based therapies and Synthetic Biology

Our group applies state-of-the-art synthetic biology principles to engineer human cells and create next-generation cell-based therapies targeting cancer as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune and infectious diseases. Leveraging innovative platforms such as novel biosensors, gene switches, genetic closed-loop circuits, and chemical structures that interface with and actuate cellular activities, we design programmable cellular implants and devices for therapeutic applications. By integrating fundamental discoveries with translational development, we aim to shape the future of biomedical innovation.

Job description

PhD projects will combine molecular engineering, cell programming, and chemical–biological interfacing to engineer human cells using synthetic gene circuits and biosensing platforms, develop novel biosensing systems for real-time monitoring of cellular states, create genetic architectures for precise therapeutic protein regulation, and translate these research advances into programmable cellular implant prototypes

Projects will be highly interdisciplinary, fostering close collaboration with molecular biologists, bioengineers, and clinical researchers to accelerate translation into clinically relevant therapies

Profile

We are seeking highly motivated applicants eager to bridge basic and translational research in cell biology and synthetic biology

Candidates should have strong skills in molecular and cell biology techniques, including cultivation and engineering of primary human cells and mammalian cell lines

Experience with in vivo techniques, as well as completion of an accredited course in laboratory animal science (FELASA / LTK or equivalent), would be an asset

We welcome applicants with an outstanding academic record and who are enthusiastic about building a career in academia, industrial R&D, or biotechnology entrepreneurship

We offer

Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

We are actively committed to a sustainable and climate-neutral university

You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

CV

Complete academic transcripts

A list of publications

A motivation letter

Two letters of recommendation

A brief research plan (1 page)

Further information about the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering, can be found on our  website  or in our published work . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Professor Martin Fussenegger,  [email protected] (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

Doctoral Position in Advanced Bioelectronic & Electrical Conversion Research
A World-Class Research Environment at the Nexus of Biology, Engineering, and Physical Sciences

The Biotechnology and Bioengineering group led by Prof. Dr. Martin Fussenegger at the Department of Biosystems Science and Engineering (D-BSSE) of ETH Zurich in Basel invites exceptional candidates to apply for a PhD position in pioneering projects at the intersection of synthetic biology, nanotechnology, and bioelectronics.

The D-BSSE is ETH Zurich's first truly interdisciplinary research department uniting theoretical and experimental biology with advanced bioengineering and fostering close collaborations with leaders in materials science, physics, and chemistry to drive transformative advances in systems biology, biotechnology, and synthetic biology. Situated in Basel, Switzerland, at the heart of the BioValley, a tri-national region that hosts 40% of the global life sciences industry and numerous major pharmaceutical companies, the D-BSSE offers a unique environment for high-impact translational research with unparalleled access to academic and industrial expertise.

Project background
Advancing the Frontiers of Bioelectronics and Synthetic Biology

Our group integrates state-of-the-art synthetic biology with advanced nanotechnology, and electrogenetic interfaces to engineer human cells for next generation bioelectronic medicine, designing programmable cells that respond to electrical, electromagnetic, acoustic and biochemical cues to achieve wireless, real-time control of therapeutic protein expression and metabolic regulation. Leveraging innovative platforms such as direct-current-actuated regulation, electromagnetic programming of wireless expression, and closed-loop systems, we aim to translate these technologies into clinically relevant, minimally invasive therapies for cancer, as well as metabolic, neurodegenerative, autoimmune, and infectious diseases.

PhD projects will combine catalyst engineering, computational simulation, bioelectrode device fabrication, and electrical engineering to develop bioelectronic interfaces enabling closed-loop programming of cellular behaviour and real-time monitoring of metabolic activity

There will also be opportunities to design novel bioelectronic implants and develop specialized control software

About the SnT
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The  Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust ( SnT ) at the University of Luxembourg is a leading international research and innovation centre in secure, reliable and trustworthy ICT systems and services.
We play an instrumental role in Europe by fueling innovation through research partnerships with industry, boosting R&D investments leading to economic growth, and attracting highly qualified talent. We look for researchers from diverse academic backgrounds to contribute to our projects in areas such as: Network Security, Information Assurance, Model-driven Security, Cloud Computing, Cryptography, Satellite Systems, Vehicular Networks, and ICT Services & Applications.
Your role
Support project management activities
Track milestones and deliverables
Coordinate timelines across teams
Manage documentation
Help ensure projects stay on scope and on schedule

The successful candidate will become a member of the Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust within the Interdisciplinary Research in SEDAN Team under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Radu STATE at the University of Luxembourg.
We're looking for an R&D Specialist to help shape and deliver our research agenda. You'll work closely with researchers and stakeholders to define new research projects - scoping objectives, identifying methodologies, and assessing feasibility and impact - then take an active role in executing them, from data collection and experimentation to analysis and reporting.
Beyond the technical work, you'll act as a bridge between the scientific and operational sides of R&D, keeping projects moving while maintaining research rigor.
Your profile
Comfortable working across the full project lifecycle - from initial concept to final delivery
Strong organizational skills
Scientific curiosity
Ability to communicate clearly with both technical and non-technical stakeholders

Language requirements:

The University of Luxembourg is set in a multilingual and multicultural context. The person hired on this position must be proficient in English and either French or German. The University encourages its staff to learn the other language and provides access to language courses to this end.
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae, including: For each degree received or currently enrolled in, the degree, institution name, city, and country, and date (or expected date) of graduation
Title and short summary of final thesis
List of publications (if any)
Name, affiliation, and contact details of at least two recommenders
If available, link to GitHub repository including completed open-source projects

Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken
Cover letter

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
The University of Luxembourg is committed to achieving gender parity among its staff. Should candidates present equivalent profiles, preference will be given to female candidates in all departments where gender parity is not yet achieved.

Description de l'offre d'emploi
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne , c’est s’engager dans une institution où la science et l’innovation bâtissent un avenir plus durable. Une école d’excellence où chacun a l’opportunité de révéler son plein potentiel et de contribuer à relever les défis de demain.
Classée parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs en France et reconnue mondialement, notre école, membre de l’Institut Mines-Télécom, forme les talents de demain tout en contribuant activement à relever les grands défis industriels, numériques et environnementaux. Avec nous, vous intégrez une communauté de 500 collaborateurs, 2500 étudiants, et participez à un projet ambitieux : conjuguer excellence académique, recherche d’avant-garde et impact sociétal positif.
L’Institut Mines-Télécom fédère les grandes écoles françaises autour des défis industriels majeurs, numériques, énergétiques et écologiques. Avec ses 8 Grandes Écoles publiques et 2 écoles filiales, il est le premier institut public dédié aux ingénieurs et managers. Ensemble, nous imaginons et construisons un avenir durable, en formant les acteurs qui façonneront les transitions de demain.
🎯 Ce que nous attendons de vous
En tant que Concepteur(trice) de Systèmes Etirables Autonomes , vous êtes au cœur de nos missions en formation, recherche et innovation affecté au département électronique flexible. Au sein de ce département vous conjuguez passion scientifique et goût pour l’innovation.
Au sein du Centre Microélectronique de Provence, le département FEL mène ses recherches dans le domaine de l'électronique flexible et étirable, pour des applications dédiées aux objets "wearable" et au « monitoring » environnemental. La conception de systèmes complets, du capteur au module de de communication, en fonction des contraintes énergétiques et environnementales est un élément essentiel permettant la réalisation de prototypes compatibles avec les cas d'usages étudiés.
Vous aurez pour mission principale, à partir du savoir-faire du département de développer l'expertise électronique dans le domaine des objets autonomes / autoalimentés pour le monitoring environnemental ( Projet Hydrademo ) et des interfaces "wearable" pour la perception augmentée( Projet flexeo3D ). Par ailleurs, vous contribuerez au développement de modules de formation en mastère spécialisé, dans le cadre du programme EDU4chip
Vous accompagnez le développement de systèmes autonomes dans le cadre de différents projets du département
Vous contribuez au montage à la dispense d'un module d ’enseignement en conception de systèmes autonomes (25h) à destination des étudiants du mastère spécialisé « Concepteur de Circuits Microélectroniques »
Vous assurez la conception et la réalisation des interfaces spécifiques capteurs et énergie pour nos démonstrateurs systèmes
Vous participez à la réalisation de prototypes innovants et à leur test en étroite collaboration avec nos équipes de recherche

Votre capacité à travailler en mode projet et à faire dialoguer enseignement, recherche et application concrète sera essentielle pour réussir.
Pré-requis du poste
🔍 Ce que nous recherchons
Vous êtes titulaire d’un :
Titulaire d’un Diplôme de doctorat ou d’ingénieur ou équivalent en électronique
Junior accepté : oui si expérience pertinente lors des stages

En outre, vous possédez :
Une expérience dans le développement de systèmes à microcontrôleurs
Une expérience pratique de la conception et de la réalisation des cartes électroniques
De bonnes connaissances en électronique analogique
La connaissance de procédés d’intégration électronique sur support flexible serait un plus

Vos atouts supplémentaires :
Votre sens pratique et votre esprit « maker »
Votre capacité à évoluer dans un environnement collaboratif de recherche et développement
Votre autonomie et votre sens de l’initiative

🌍 Pourquoi rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne ?
Nous accompagnons chacun de nos collaborateurs sur le chemin de l’excellence, avec la conviction qu’ensemble, nous pouvons avoir un impact durable et significatif sur notre monde.
Rejoindre Mines Saint-Étienne, c’est l’opportunité de trouver :
Un environnement stimulant : des moyens expérimentaux de pointe, un réseau international solide (T.I.M.E., EULIST) et des campus à taille humaine avec un environnement urbain
Un impact réel : des projets de recherche contractuelle à hauteur de 11 M€/an, majoritairement avec des partenaires industriels, un centre de culture scientifique la Rotonde qui s’engage depuis 25 ans dans la médiation des sciences avec plus de 50 000 visiteurs/an
Une qualité de vie incomparable : 49 jours de congés et RTT, télétravail partiel, prise en charge des transports en commun à 75 %, soutien financier au covoiturage et au vélo et un baromètre social où 83 % des collaborateurs plébiscitent la qualité de vie au travail

Construisons un avenir plus durable, à travers la science, l’ingénierie, et des projets qui font sens.

ap:253281.body:
This proposed PhD research will be carried out in the Laser Manufacturing Group at the Department of Mechanical Engineering of KU Leuven.

KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a centre of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. The university caters to over 60,000 students from more than 140 countries. KU Leuven's three doctoral schools provide internationally oriented PhD tracks for more than 4,000 doctoral students. KU Leuven and affiliated knowledge institutes provide fertile ground for innovation and high-tech entrepreneurship in the Leuven region. This favourable climate for knowledge-driven innovation makes the Leuven region an attractive location for many high-tech companies.

KU Leuven website: www.kuleuven.be/english/kuleuven

Laser Manufacturing Group linkedIn: www.linkedin.com/company/ku-leuven-laser-micromanufacturing

Laser Manufacturing Group website:

Website unit

Project

KU Leuven seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded international doctoral position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Networks (MSCA-DN) project TURBO-IMPACT ( TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology; Website: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350 ).

The TURBO-IMPACT project, funded by Horizon Europe – MSCA-DN, tackles challenges in designing, optimizing, selecting materials, and manufacturing small-scale turbomachinery for applications in heat pumps, fuel cells, organic Rankine cycles, or gas turbines. This project develops robust system and component design methods, an integrated manufacturing platform, and multi-material joining techniques to efficiently produce small-scale turbomachinery.

In this large EU project, this PhD researcher (DC9) will work at KU Leuven and focus on improving laser machining of ceramic materials for the fabrication of advanced surface features. The goal is to better understand and control the manufacturing process so that small, precise, and reliable structures can be produced efficiently. These developments will contribute to the project's broader objective of developing 3D laser processing strategies for aerodynamic bearings with enhanced tribological performance.

The doctoral candidate will:

Leverage and extend KU Leuven’s state-of-the-art ultrashort-pulse laser micromachining facilities to develop crack-free laser texturing strategies for ceramic materials.

Establish predictive models linking laser processing conditions to feature geometry and crack formation in ceramic materials.

Develop high-precision laser texturing approaches for complex 3D ceramic components.

Study the relationship between laser-generated surface textures and the performance of bonded ceramic-ceramic and ceramic-metal interfaces.

The research is supervised by Prof. Sylvie Castagne ( www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/en/person/00114469 ), head of the Laser Manufacturing Group ( www.mech.kuleuven.be/en/research/Femto ).

Profile

You have a master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing or Materials Engineering, Photonics, Physics or related field with strong interest in technology, and performed above average in comparison to your peers. You are not in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment.

You are proficient in written and spoken English.

During your studies or prior professional activities, you have gathered some experience related to the basic physical principles of laser material processing and/or to the fundamental principles of manufacturing and mechanical behaviour of materials or you have a profound interest in these topics.

Ideally you have experience with either COMSOL, ANSYS or another CAE simulation software.

You are highly precise and detail-oriented, consistently delivering accurate and thorough work.

You demonstrate a strong sense of initiative and responsibility, while also being an effective and collaborative team player.

You are willing to travel between the university of Leuven (BE), and other consortium partner locations. This includes secondments to Neuchâtel (CH, 2 months), Jena (DE, 1 month) and Padova (IT, 1 month), as well as to our industrial partner in Belgium (BE, 2 months).

Special requirements:

In accordance with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network regulations:

Applicants must comply with the MSCA Mobility Rule. At the time of recruitment, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the hiring country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment.

Applicants must be doctoral candidates (i.e., not already hold a doctoral degree) and be eligible under the MSCA Doctoral Network rules at the time of recruitment.

Short stays such as holidays, compulsory national service, or time spent as part of a refugee procedure are not considered.

Applicants must have a two-year master's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Manufacturing or Materials Engineering, Photonics, Physics or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Offer

Successful candidates will:

Be enrolled in the KU Leuven PhD programme.

Conduct research in a stimulating international environment with access to state-of-the-art facilities and supervision by recognised experts.

Participate in local and network-wide training activities aimed at advancing scientific knowledge and transferable skills.

Attend workshops and international conferences relevant to their research topic.

Undertake secondments of approximately 6 months at other network or associated partner institutions.

Receive further doctoral training for PhD candidates in the framework of the KU Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School ( https://set.kuleuven.be/phd ), known for its strong focus on both future scientists and scientifically trained professionals who will valorise their doctoral expertise and competences in a non-academic context.

Assessment:

Recruitment will be carried out and monitored in full accordance with the principles of the European Charter for Researchers, the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, and the Doctoral Network mobility rules. The process will follow an open, transparent, merit-based, impartial, and equitable procedure, tailored to each individual DC position. Promising candidates will undergo a series of interviews with the PI, the Supervisory Team, and the Recruitment Committee.

Please note that this position is part of a consortium involving several partner universities. By submitting your application, you consent to your personal data, CV and motivation letter being shared with and accessible to the relevant members of the consortium for the purposes of the recruitment and selection process.

Salary and appointment terms:

Successful candidates will receive a comprehensive financial package in line with the rules for Doctoral Candidates (DCs) in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. Employment will be provided by the recruiting organisation and will include mobility and family allowances (where applicable), together with full social security coverage.

Doctoral Candidates will benefit from a competitive salary, paid leave (in accordance with institutional regulations), and access to national social security schemes. The employment starts on 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

Interested?

Follow the KU Leuven job application tool and enclose:

full CV – mandatory

motivation letter – mandatory

full list of credits and grades of both BSc and MSc degrees (as well as their transcription to English if possible) – mandatory (if you have not finished your degree yet, just provide us with the partial list of already available credits and grades)

proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, …) – if available

two reference letters – if available

an English version of your MSc thesis, or of a recent publication or assignment – if available

For more information please contact Prof. Sylvie Castagne, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

ap:253287.body:
Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitos hakee tutkijatohtoria, evolutiivinen ympäristöbiologia,  1.12.2026   alkaen tai mahdollisimman pian sen jälkeen kahden vuoden määräajaksi.
Etsimme kokenutta postdoc-tutkijaa, joka on erityisen kiinnostunut evoluutioekologiasta, integroivasta biologiasta ja ympäristötieteistä. Katso tarkemmat tiedot englanninkielisestä hakuilmoituksesta .
Etsimämme henkilö
Tutkijatohtorin kelpoisuusvaatimuksista ja kielitaidosta määrätään  yliopiston johtosäännössä ja kielitaito-ohjeistuksissa . Tutkijatohtoreilla tulee olla tohtorin tutkinto suoritettuna ennen tehtävässä aloittamista. Tehtävissä edellytetään hyvää englannin kielen taitoa ja eduksi katsotaan kyky antaa opetusta englannin kielellä. Tehtävää täytettäessä käytetään kuuden kuukauden koeaikaa.
Tarjoamme
Tule osaksi innostavaa ja lämminhenkistä yhteisöämme!
Jyväskylän yliopistossa olet arvostettu yliopistoyhteisön jäsen. Teemme merkityksellistä työtä ja vaalimme sivistystä. Monitieteisessä yliopistossamme saat mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa kansainväliseen tutkimukseen ja laadukkaaseen akateemiseen koulutukseen. Meille jokaisen hyvinvointi on tärkeää, ja tarjoamme kampuksella sekä sen läheisyydessä erinomaiset puitteet aktiiviseen ja hyvinvoivaan elämäntapaan.
Palkkaus perustuu tehtävien vaativuuteen ja henkilökohtaiseen työstä suoriutumiseen yliopistojen palkkausjärjestelmän mukaisesti. Tutkijatohtorin tehtäväkohtainen palkanosa määräytyy opetus- ja tutkimushenkilöstön tehtävien vaativuustason 5–6 mukaan. Palkkasi on noin 3600–4800 euroa kuukaudessa riippuen aiemmasta osaamisestasi ja kokemuksestasi.
Tarjoamme hyvät työolosuhteet tutkijoille ja noudatamme Tutkijanuran ja -aseman kehittämisen ( HRS4R ) periaatteita. Human Resources Strategy for Researchers (HRS4R) -työ perustuu Euroopan komission julkaisemaan Tutkijoiden eurooppalaisen peruskirjan arvoihin ja säännöstöön tutkijoiden työhönotosta (englanninkielinen lyhenne Charter & Code). Jyväskylän yliopisto on sitoutunut tasapuolisuuteen, johdonmukaisuuteen ja läpinäkyvyyteen valintapäätöksissä ja noudattaa vastuullisen tutkijanarvioinnin kansallisia suosituksia . Jyväskylän yliopisto on sitoutunut vastuullisen tutkijanarvioinnin DORA-julistukseen ja noudattamaan CoARA -periaatteita.
Hakeminen
Haussa edellytetään, että ORCID‑profiilisi ( https://orcid.org ) on ajan tasalla ja julkaisusi näkyvät julkisina (Set visibility: Everyone).
Hakemuksiin tulee liittää pdf-muodossa:
Ansioluettelo (CV), joka laaditaan hyvää tieteellistä käytäntöä noudattaen sekä ottaen huomioon mahdollisuuksien mukaan ansioluettelomalli (ks.  TENK:n ohje ).
Lyhyt vapaamuotoinen hakemuskirje (enintään 2 sivua) sisältäen tutkimusintressisi, uratavoitteesi ja aiemman kokemuksesi sekä ansiosi suhteessa tämän tehtävän pätevyyteen.
Numeroitu julkaisuluettelo Suomen Akatemian mallin mukaan  kaikista niistä tieteellisistä ja muista julkaisuista, joilla hakija haluaa osoittaa kelpoisuutensa ja ansionsa tehtävään.
Tutkintotodistus (korkein tutkinto).

Odotamme hakemustasi rekrytointijärjestelmäämme viimeistään 2.11.2026.
Lisätietoja antaa professori Katja Räsänen, [email protected] .
Hakemusprosessimme on läpinäkyvä, ammattimainen ja kansainvälinen. Tiedotamme hakijoita avoimesti prosessin edistymisestä sen eri vaiheissa. Arvostamme tasa-arvoa ja monimuotoisuutta työyhteisössämme ja kannustamme kelpoisuuden täyttäviä hakijoita hakemaan tehtäviä.

Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitos

Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitoksen   tutkimus keskittyy kolmeen ydinalueeseen: evoluutiobiologiaan, luonnonvaroihin ja ympäristöön sekä biologiseen nanotieteeseen. Yhteisö on erittäin kansainvälinen, ja sen jäsenet edustavat yli 30 kansallisuutta. Laitoksen päärakennus, Ambiotica, on olennainen osa Jyväskylän yliopiston Ylistönrinteen matematiikan ja luonnontieteiden tutkimuskeskusta,  johon kuuluvat myös kemian ja fysiikan laitokset sekä nanotiedekeskus. Ambioticassa on huipputason biotieteiden laboratoriot ja kokeelliset tilat monenlaisiin biologisiin ja kemiallisiin analyyseihin sekä erittäin motivoitunut laboratoriohenkilökunta. Lisäksi Konneveden tutkimusasema tarjoaa mahdollisuuksia laajamittaisiin, ekologisesti merkityksellisiin kokeisiin ja kenttätutkimuksiin sekä paikan työpajoille ja kenttäkursseille luonnonkauniissa ympäristössä.
Jyväskylän yliopiston 2800 asiantuntijan ja 14 500 opiskelijan ihmisläheisestä yhteisöstä jokaisen on helppo löytää paikkansa. Meille on tärkeää, että yhteisömme jäsenet voivat hyvin ja heillä on mahdollisuudet kasvaa ja kehittyä. Kaunis puistokampuksemme sijaitsee Jyväskylän keskustassa. Yliopistona olemme savuton ja tuoksuton työpaikka, joka on Keski-Suomen kolmanneksi suurin työnantaja.

Puhelin:
(014) 260 1211

Sähköposti:
[email protected]

Sijainti: Seminaarinkatu 15

Hakulomaketta ei voi tallentaa luonnoksena. Työhakemuksen täyttämiseen on kuitenkin aikaa 6 tuntia ennen aikakatkaisua. Lähettämisen jälkeen voit palata muokkaamaan hakemusta sähköpostitse saamasi linkin kautta hakuajan päättymiseen asti.

ap:253292.body:
Doctoral Student in Design and Analysis of Human-AI Systems
The Decision Sciences and Analytics group, led by Prof. Tu Ni at ETH Zürich is seeking a doctoral student to study the design and analysis of human-AI systems. This position focuses on the development of AI systems with an emphasis on understanding and reshaping the role of human. The study context is broad, such as AI for clinical or legal decisions, AI for learning and education, etc. The research is mainly theoretical, but will be related to empirical study like field/lab experiments when necessary.

Job description

Analyze AI systems where the decision is often high-stake or with long-term impact

Design AI systems that lead to efficient and reliable outcomes

Write high-quality papers and publish on top-tier OM journals

Work with external organizations to evaluate the methods if needed

In addition to research activities, they will contribute to lab responsibilities (e.g. teaching, advising master thesis)

Profile

Hold (or will have completed at the time of appointment) a Master’s degree in applied mathematics, economics, operations, or a closely related field

Excellent academic records and is motivated to produce high-quality, policy-relevant research

Have excellent analytical and modeling skills: optimization, mechanism design, etc

Have excellent verbal and written communication skills

Have industrial experience in AI deployment is a plus

We offer

The starting date is negotiable, but hopefully in six months

The position is initially offered for 18 months, with the prospect of extension for four- to five-year duration of the doctorate, subject to satisfactory progress

We offer the opportunity to pursue a high-quality PhD at a renowned institution and to work in a dynamic and collaborative research environment

Gross salary will be in accordance with the regulatons of ETH Zurich

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents :

A letter of motivation that includes an explanation why you are interested in doing a PhD and fit for the position (within one page)

A resume/CV

Complete academic record with undergraduate and graduate courses and grades

Arrange at least two references and provide the contact information

Further information about our Department can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Tu Ni,  [email protected]  (no applications or unsolicited outreach).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:253298.body:
Employment 1.0 FTE
Gross monthly salary € 3,204 - € 4,051
Required background Research University Degree
Organizational unit Nijmegen School of Management
Application deadline 08 November 2026
What could reparations for colonialism look like? As a PhD candidate, you will explore this urgent question, using participatory and creative research methods to foreground the experiences and expectations of Indo and Indonesian communities affected by colonialism.
Recent developments like the Rhodes Must Fall movement have highlighted the need to address historical injustices and global inequalities, but responses so far have often been superficial. Apologies, like the apologies the Dutch government offered to the Moluccan population in the Netherlands last summer, are often made, but more material forms of redress are slow to follow or remain absent altogether. Current scholarly debates in relation to historical injustices concern the potential and scope of reparations, which are often prioritised by survivors but politically sensitive. So far there is no consensus or empirical data on how reparations could address colonial legacies.
This important question will guide your PhD research in the NWO-funded project ‘Decolonising Reparations: Transforming the Legacies of Colonialism’, led by Dr Sanne Weber, Assistant Professor at the Department of Political Science. You will use participatory and creative research methods to investigate the impact of colonialism on affected communities within Indonesia and the Indonesian diaspora in the Netherlands, as well as what these communities expect from reparations for colonialism.
You will work together with participants on co-produced multimedia products about the potential role of reparations in addressing historical grievances. In addition, you will conduct interviews with a wider group of stakeholders and a vignette study with the broader population in Indonesia. You will receive training on participatory and creative approaches by the Principal Investigator. Strong knowledge of qualitative research methodologies and familiarity with participatory research approaches are an asset.
During your PhD, you will collaborate with the PI and a postdoctoral researcher who will focus on Belgium and the Great Lakes Region of Central Africa. By comparing these case studies and triangulating the diverse methods, the project will enable a better understanding of potential forms of reparations for colonialism. In this way, the project aims to contribute to the decolonisation of reparative justice theory to address the legacies of colonialism committed by Western Europe.
Your duties and responsibilities include:
Developing a concrete and feasible research project fitting the overarching theme and resulting in the defence of an article-based PhD thesis at the end of the 4th year.
Setting up and carrying out in-depth and independent participatory fieldwork.
Authoring and co-authoring publications with other team members.
Participating in conferences, workshops, seminars and other scholarly activities.
Being part of the research team and contributing to the overall organisation and strategy of the team and the project.
Being an active member of the Department of Political Science and the Centre for International Conflict Analysis and Management.
As part of your PhD position, you will also contribute to teaching (max 5%) and will have the opportunity to work on components of your University Teaching Qualification (BKO) portfolio.

Your supervision team will consist of Dr Sanne Weber (main substantive PhD supervisor) and Dr. Haley Swedlund.
Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate .
Does this sound like you?
Required:
You hold a Master’s degree in political science or another relevant discipline, such as conflict studies, anthropology or development studies.
You have a proven substantive research interest in issues of justice, including transitional, reparative and social justice, historical and ongoing injustice, reparations and redress, and theories of justice, decolonisation and intersectionality.
You are trained in qualitative research and analysis methods. You have experience with conducting fieldwork, collecting and analysing qualitative data, ideally in relation to the theme of this project.
You are familiar with Indonesia as you are from Indonesia or the Indo community, have worked or lived there, or have spent an extended period there.
You are willing to conduct several months of in-depth fieldwork in Indonesia.
You have a proven excellent command of written academic English.
You have experience with planning, taking initiative, organising events and presenting your work to a wider audience.

Desired:
You are trained in participatory and/or arts-based research methodologies.
You have experience working with communities at a local level and have a good command of Bahasa or another relevant local language.
You have proficiency in Dutch.
You have experience with basic quantitative methods of research and analysis.

What we offer you
We will give you a temporary employment contract (1.0 FTE) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract).
You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 in the fourth year ( salary scale P ).
You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus.
You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20.

Additional employment conditions
Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes.
Where you will be working
The Department of Political Science examines the complexity and interconnectedness of contemporary politics with a focus on legitimacy and institutional change. The department consists of four chair groups: Peace and Conflict Studies, Political Theory, Comparative Political Science and International Relations. Together, they oﬀer Bachelor’s and Master’s degree programmes in Political Science.
You will be part of the Peace and Conflict Studies chair group (Centre for International Conflict Analysis and Management, CICAM). This chair group is particularly strong in qualitative methodology and fieldwork-based research. Major research topics include land conflict, transitional justice, rebel governance and migration, as well as the politics of aid. Many of the group’s members are active in interdisciplinary Hot Spots and research collaborations across the Nijmegen School of Management and beyond.
Nijmegen School of Management
At Nijmegen School of Management , one of the seven faculties within Radboud University in the Netherlands, we have a clear aim: we enable students, institutions and companies, social actors, and governments to play their part in the transformations towards a sustainable society through high-quality scientific research and education. With more than 4,500 curious students and more than 450 dedicated employees, we form a dynamic community.
Our mission ‘Responsible governance for sustainable societies’ is driven by the ambition to make a difference in the world. At Nijmegen School of Management, we understand management as a broad concept referring to the collective and organised pursuit (responsible governance) of a better world (sustainable societies). We study and teach management at the level of public and private organisations. In this context, we examine how to balance economic, ecological, and social values in a sustainable way. This aim is in line with Radboud University's mission to contribute through teaching and research to a ‘free, healthy world with equal opportunities for all’.
At Nijmegen School of Management, academic research and teaching are carried out in following areas: Business Administration, Economics and Business Economics, Political Science, Public Administration, Human Geography, Spatial Planning, and Environment. Our approach to teaching and research is evolving from multidisciplinarity, where we study societal challenges from different disciplinary backgrounds, to interdisciplinarity (integrating disciplinary perspectives for synergy) and transdisciplinarity (involving non-academic stakeholders).
The United Nations' Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) are an important source of inspiration for our work. Our work focuses on the themes Social economy, Resilient society and Sustainable environment . At Nijmegen School of Management, we have our eyes on the world of the future, in which sustainability and responsibility are central values. Together we are creating a better world for everyone.
Radboud University
At Radboud University, we aim to make an impact through our work. We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. We advocate for an inclusive community and welcome employees with diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives.
If you want to learn more about working at Radboud University, follow our Instagram account and read stories from our colleagues.
Is this the job for you?
You can apply only via the button below. Address your letter of application to Sanne Weber. In the application form, you will find which documents you need to include with your application. We look forward to receiving your application.
The first interviews will take place in the week of 30 November. If you are invited for the second interview, in the week of 14 December, you will be asked to prepare a short research proposal. You will preferably start your employment on 1 March 2027.
We can imagine you're curious about our application procedure . It describes what you can expect during the application procedure and how we handle your personal data and internal and external candidates.
Application deadline 08 November 2026
We would like to recruit our new colleague ourselves. Acquisition in response to this vacancy will not be appreciated.
Want to know more about this position?
Dr S.C. Weber (Sanne)
[email protected]
