ap:253301.body:
As a TEM Application Expert –you’ll help us develop and fine-tune innovative processes for tomorrow’s chips. We go smaller than you’ve ever seen!
What you will do
You will be a member of the TEM operations team within the FAB. This team is responsible for both in-line and off-line electron microscopy inspections. These inspections play a crucial role throughout the technology development cycle, providing wafer-level characterization of processes and materials used in both More-than-Moore applications (such as MEMS, actuators, and sensors) and Core semiconductor technologies (including SRAM, MRAM, and 3D integration).
At the heart of our innovation is imec’s state-of-the-art pilot line, one of the world’s most advanced semiconductor R&D environments. In this experimental production facility, we develop and validate next-generation semiconductor manufacturing processes before transferring them to leading international chip manufacturers. By providing our customers with the knowledge and technologies needed to meet increasingly demanding requirements, we help drive innovation across the semiconductor industry.
To achieve this, we rely on our high-tech cleanroom facilities and advanced characterization capabilities. We are currently looking for a highly skilled TEM Application Expert with a strong background in Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM) and semiconductor materials characterization.
The ideal candidate will have either a PhD in a relevant field or 5+ years of hands-on experience in TEM applications and workflow optimization. In this role you will have the following key responsibilities:
You are a technical expert in TEM sample preparation and inspection, with deep knowledge of the current capabilities and limitations of TEM tools, especially as applied to advanced semiconductor materials and structures.
You will design, develop, and optimize automation recipes for TEM sample preparation and inspection workflows, ensuring high reproducibility, throughput, and quality.
You actively collaborate with cross-functional teams including application specialists, lab assistants, and operations managers to ensure smooth execution and continuous improvement of TEM services.
You are a co-owner of departmental targets, contributing to strategic goals such as throughput, quality, and innovation.
You ensure high-quality and efficient intake of first-time requests, translating customer needs into actionable and well-documented workflows.
You serve as the primary point of contact for evaluating and validating documented customer requests, ensuring technical feasibility and alignment with available capabilities.
You proactively identify efficiency bottlenecks and quality risks, and take initiative to implement corrective actions or propose process improvements.
You stay up to date with emerging TEM technologies, automation tools, and semiconductor characterization techniques, and integrate relevant advancements into recipe development..

You will work in a dynamic multidisciplinary and multicultural environment in close cooperation with researchers, hardware and process engineers, industry assignees, tool suppliers, device- and process experts.
What we do for you
We offer you the opportunity to join one of the world’s premier research centers in nanotechnology at its headquarters in Leuven, Belgium. With your talent, passion and expertise, you’ll become part of a team that makes the impossible possible. Together, we shape the technology that will define the society of tomorrow.
We are committed to being an inclusive employer and proud of our open, multicultural, and informal working environment with ample possibilities to take initiative and show responsibility. We commit to supporting and guiding you in this process; not only with words but also with tangible actions. Through imec.academy, 'our corporate university', we actively invest in your development to further your technical and personal growth.
We are aware that your valuable contribution makes imec a top player in its field. Your energy and commitment are therefore appreciated by means of a market appropriate salary with many fringe benefits.
Who you are
You have a PhD and/ or master’s degree with relevant experience in science/engineering
Experience in the field of microscopy and/or semiconductor process is very important
You have a strong interest in programming/automation, which is a significant advantage
You can plan and organize your work on your own
You can work in a fast-paced setting, multi-task and prioritize assignments.
You have good communication and organizational skills
You are assertive and a good team player
You will work in an alternating shift regime (early / late) and 1 out of 4 weekends
You are a a communicative team player with a fluent knowledge of English

IMEC and its affiliates will not accept unsolicited resumes from any source other than directly from a candidate. IMEC will consider unsolicited referrals and/or resumes submitted by vendors such as search firms, staffing agencies, professional recruiters, fee-based referral services and recruiting agencies (hereafter “Agency”) to have been referred by the Agency free of charge. IMEC will not pay a fee to any Agency that does not have a prior written agreement with IMEC, validated by its HR department, in place regarding a specific job opening and allowing to submit resumes.

ap:253302.body:
The PhD research will be carried out in the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy team at the Department of Materials Engineering of KU Leuven.

KU Leuven (University of Leuven) has been a center of learning for nearly six centuries since 1425, making it one of the oldest and most renowned universities in Europe. Today, it is Belgium’s highest ranked university (QS 2025 : 60), ranked among the top 4% universities in the world and consistently ranked in the top 10 most innovative universities in Europe. The university caters to over 60,000 students from more than 140 countries. KU Leuven's three doctoral schools provide internationally oriented PhD tracks for more than 4,000 doctoral students. KU Leuven and affiliated knowledge institutes provide fertile ground for innovation and high-tech entrepreneurship in the Leuven region. This favorable climate for knowledge-driven innovation makes the Leuven region an attractive location for many high-tech companies.

KU Leuven website: https://www.kuleuven.be/english/kuleuven/

Website unit

Project

KU Leuven seeks a highly motivated PhD candidate for a fully funded, four-year international doctoral position within the Marie Sklodowska-Curie Doctoral Network (MSCA-DN) project TURBO-IMPACT (TURBOmachinery Innovative Manufacturing, Processing, Analysis, Characterization, and Topology ; Website: https://cordis.europa.eu/project/id/101311350).

The TurboImpact project, funded by Horizon Europe – MSCA-DN, tackles challenges in designing, optimizing, selecting materials, and manufacturing small-scale turbomachinery for applications in heat pumps, fuel cells, organic Rankine cycles, or gas turbines. This project develops robust system and component design methods, an integrated manufacturing platform, and multi-material joining techniques to efficiently produce small-scale turbomachinery.

In this EU project, this PhD researcher (DC8) will focus on the complete indirect DLP/SLA additive manufacturing route for silicon nitride turbomachinery components. This involves the development of a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry, optimization of DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components such as impellers, and the post-printing debinding and sintering process to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components. The AM parts will be microstructurally, mechanically and geometrically characterized. Simple geometries will be used for the evaluation of joining and machining performances, whereas the complex near-net-shaped components will be applied in turbomachinery.

The doctoral candidate will:

Develop a UV-curable Si3N4 slurry and optimize DLP/SLA printing strategies for reference parts and complex components

Realize post-printing debinding and sintering processes to obtain fully dense complex near-net-shaped ceramic components

Elucidate the processing – microstructure – mechanical properties – geometrical accuracy correlations.

The project includes potential international secondments at EPFL (Switzerland), Admatec Additive Solutions (The Netherlands) and IFW (Germany).

The researcher is supervised by Prof. Jozef Vleugels (https://www.kuleuven.be/wieiswie/nl/person/00006337), head of the Functional Materials Division (FUNMAT) and coordinator of the Advanced Ceramics and Powder Metallurgy research group at the Department of Materials Engineering. The research group has a long track record (>35 years) on the powder metallurgical development, processing and characterisaton of ceramics, cermets, metcers and metals. More information on the website (https://www.mtm.kuleuven.be/english/research/siem/ACPM)

Profile

I have a two-year master degree in Materials Science, Materials Engineering, or an equivalent master degree.

I am proficient in written and spoken English.

During my courses, master thesis or prior professional activities, I have gathered basic experience on the processing of ceramics, additive manufacturing, microstructural and mechanical characterization or I have a profound interest in these topics.

I demonstrate a strong sense of initiative and responsibility, while also being an effective and collaborative team player.

I am very motivated and obtained good grades (minimum distinction level)

I feel comfortable to work as a team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and be inspired by my colleagues.

Special requirements: In accordance with the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network regulations:

Applicants must comply with the MSCA Mobility Rule. At the time of recruitment, candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the hiring Country for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment.

Applicants must be doctoral candidates (i.e., not already hold a doctoral degree) and be eligible under the MSCA Doctoral Network rules at the time of recruitment

Short stays such as holidays, compulsory national service, or time spent as part of a refugee procedure are not considered.

Applicants must have a two-year master's degree in Materials Engineering, Materials Science, or an equivalent master degree, or a similar degree with an academic level equivalent to a two-year master's degree.

Offer

Successful candidates will:

Be enrolled in the KU Leuven PhD programme,

Conduct research in a stimulating international environment with access to state-of-the-art facilities and supervision by recognised experts

Participate in local and network-wide training activities aimed at advancing scientific knowledge and transferable skills,

Attend workshops and international conferences relevant to their research topic,

Undertake secondments of approximately 4–6 months at other network or associated partner institutions.

Receive further doctoral training for PhD candidates in the framework of the KU Leuven Arenberg Doctoral School (https://set.kuleuven.be/phd), known for its strong focus on both future scientists and scientifically trained professionals who will valorise their doctoral expertise and competences in a non-academic context.

Assessment:

Recruitment will be carried out and monitored in full accordance with the principles of the European Charter for Researchers, the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers, and the Doctoral Network mobility rules. The process will follow an open, transparent, merit-based, impartial, and equitable procedure, tailored to each individual DC position. Promising candidates will undergo a series of interviews with the PI, the Supervisory Team, and the Recruitment Committee.

Please note that this position is part of a consortium involving several partner universities. By submitting your application, you consent to your personal data, CV and motivation letter being shared with and accessible to the relevant members of the consortium for the purposes of the recruitment and selection process.

Salary and appointment terms:

Successful candidates will receive a comprehensive financial package in line with the rules for Doctoral Candidates (DCs) in a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. Employment will be provided by the recruiting organisation and will include mobility and family allowances (where applicable), together with full social security coverage.

Doctoral Candidates will benefit from a competitive salary, paid leave (in accordance with institutional regulations), and access to national social security schemes. The employment starts on 1 February 2027 or according to mutual agreement. The position is a full-time position.

Interested?

For more information please contact Prof. dr. ir. Jef Vleugels, mail: [email protected] .

Follow the KU Leuven job application tool and enclose:

Full CV – mandatory

Motivation letter – mandatory

Full list of credits and grades of both BSc and MSc degrees (as well as their transcription to English if possible) – mandatory (when you have not finished your degree yet, just provide us with the partial list of already available credits and grades)

Proof of English proficiency (TOEFL, IELTS, …) - if available

Two reference letters - if available

An English version of your MSc thesis, or of a recent publication or assignment - if available

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

ap:253324.body:
The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles.
We are now looking for a
Biostatistician
to join us in the  Research Unit of Clinical Medicine for a fixed-term position lasting until 31 December 2029 .
You will be based with the Lifecourse Medicine and Birth Cohort Research Group at the Clinical Medicine Research Unit. Our mission in the research group is to understand how exposures early in life, from the fetal period onwards, affect health and well-being during the life course, up to the next generation, and to use this information to advance lifelong health and well-being. We are in particular interested in adult and next-generation outcomes of people born preterm or small for gestational age in high and low resource settings.
In our research we use various types of data including whole-population data from national social and healthcare registers from Finland and other Nordic countries and data from clinically studied children and adults in high and low resource settings, including detailed physiological measurements and omics data.
About the job
As a biostatistician, you will
Be responsible for data management including data cleaning, harmonisation and documentation and preparation of analysis datasets of diverse data types such as social and healthcare register data, data from physiological and biochemical measurements, omics data or data collected by wearables. This work is conducted in close connection with other group members, much of it in data secure remote access environments including Findata Kapseli, Statistics Finland Fiona Centre for Scientific Computing CS Desktop or corresponding Nordic environments. The job may include visits to the Nordic and other collaborators' institutions.
Contribute to the design of data management solutions to maximise work efficacy and data security.
Handle data access and ethics committee applications and other regulatory requirements of use of data.
Contribute to research and statistical analysis plans together with other research group members, conduct statistical analyses according to these plans and document their results and methodologies used.
Provide advice and take part in training of other group members on data management and data analysis.
Take part in other related activities of the research group.
Actively train to learn new statistical analysis and data management methods.
Depending on the interest and experience of the successful applicant, the job may also include a more active role in developing scientific research questions and writing scientific papers.

What we offer
Working in one of the globally leading teams studying lifelong outcomes of preterm birth and related traits.
Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture, and well-being, and flexible multi-location and remote work opportunities. Read more about other staff benefits.
Work-life balance.
Development and career options of the big organisation.
Work that matters! Read more about working with us.
Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu !

Who are you?
In order to succeed and enjoy the position, we require from you:
A Masters degree in a relevant field including, but not limited to, statistics, mathematics, or bioinformatics.
Fluency in written and spoken English
Very good familiarity with at least one commonly used statistical software and ability to support and work with group members working with different statistical software.
Experience in data management and statistical analysis in research using large quantitative datasets.
Good communication and work organisation skills .

We also appreciate
A doctoral degree.
Finnish language skills. The working language of the research group is English, but documentation including that of the data regulatory authorities may be in Finnish.
Scientific contributions including scientific publications.

The final job description will be shaped according to the skills and interests of the successful candidate.
Salary
The position is fixed term starting from 1.12.2026 (or as agreed) until 31.12.2029.
The salary will be based on the levels MV08-MV09 of the demand level chart for other expert and support staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50 % of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 3300-4200 EUR per month (before taxes), depending on experience. A trial period of 6 months is applied to the position.
How to apply?
Interested? If yes, please apply by 1.11.2026 through our recruitment system. Please attach a
Cover letter
CV
Brief description (maximum one page), in your own words, why you apply and how you meet the requirements of this position .

The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. Interviews will be held during the latter half of October. The selection process may include more than one interview and a suitability assessment. The shortlisted candidates are also asked to submit their diplomas, and their references will be contacted. All applicants will be notified during the selection process.
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders, and linguistic, cultural, or minority groups.
Contact Information
If you have any further questions, please contact Professor Eero Kajantie, [email protected] , Tel +358 50 473 9438.

Faculty of Arts and Humanities
Doctoral Position (f/m/x) – History of Computing in Brazil
ERC Consolidator Grant “WIRED“ | Department of History | Professor Gerstenberger
We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

The ERC-funded project “Wired History. Computers, Humans, and the Making of Latin American Futures, 1950s–2000s” [WIRED], led by Professor Dr Debora Gerstenberger in the Department of History, investigates how people and digital technologies have shaped future-oriented projects and institutions in Latin America since the mid-20th century. Combining approaches from the history of computing, Science and Technology Studies (STS), and social, political, economic, and cultural history, the project explores diverse practices of future-making and their material and social impacts.
We invite applications for a Doctoral Researcher to study the development of university-level computer science education in Brazil during the 1960s and 1970s. The position is part of a collaborative research environment and entails close cooperation with the Principal Investigator, a postdoctoral researcher, a project manager, and another doctoral researcher.
YOUR TASKS
Conduct independent research on the history of computer science education and the development of computer science programs at Brazilian universities and, where relevant, other institutions of higher education
Complete a monograph based on this research
Contribute at least one chapter to a co-authored project monograph jointly developed by all four researchers on the team
Carry out archival research at relevant institutions and locations in Brazil and internationally
Actively participate in research group activities (e.g. reading groups, workshops, and joint publications)
Present research at international conferences and workshops
Publish articles in peer-reviewed journals
Contribute to the organization of project activities (e.g. workshops, guest visits, website maintenance, and social media)

YOUR PROFILE
MA in History or a closely related discipline (e.g. Social/Cultural Anthropology, Cultural Studies, Media Studies)
MA dissertation with excellent marks and demonstrated research potential
Expertise in or strong interest in archival research
Expertise in or strong interest in the history of computing, history of technology, Science and Technology Studies (STS), and/or Latin American history
Excellent proficiency in English and Portuguese; willingness to learn German is an advantage
Willingness to undertake extended research stays in Brazil
Strong organizational and communication skills
Ability to work both independently and collaboratively on an international research team

WE OFFER
Excellent research conditions within a dynamic and innovative team
A diverse working environment with equal opportunities
Support in balancing work and family life
Extensive advanced training opportunities
Occupational health management offers
Flexible working time models

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz – LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation and identity.
The position is available from 15 February 2027 on a part-time basis (25,89 hours per week). The doctoral position is to be filled for a fixed term until 14 February 2031. If the applicant meets the relevant wage requirements and personal qualifications, the salary is based on remuneration group 13 TV-L of the pay scale for the German public sector.
Please apply online with proof of the required qualifications and include a cover letter explaining your motivation and suitability to participate in the research group, as well as a CV, a writing sample (MA thesis or recent article), a list of publications (if applicable) and copies of certificates without a photo under: https://jobportal.uni-koeln.de.
Please also provide the names of two referees who can be contacted via email or telephone.
The reference number is Wiss2609-08. The application deadline is 04 November 2026. Interviews will take place in November or December 2026.
For further inquiries, please contact Professor Dr Debora Gerstenberger ( [email protected] ) and take a look at our FAQs.

Teaser Tekst

Vanwege het vertrek van een collega zijn we op zoek naar een nieuwe supportmedewerker onderwijsapplicaties bij SEEDS, de Science Teacher Support Desk.

Dit ga je doen

Je wordt lid van het team Science E-learning and Educational Development Support (oftewel SEEDS), de Teacher Support Desk van de Faculteit Wiskunde en Natuurwetenschappen (FWN).
Een greep uit jouw werkzaamheden:
Beantwoorden van technische vragen van docenten over onderwijsapplicaties

Docenten en onderwijskundige collega's uit het team adviseren over het gebruik van onderwijsapplicaties, als schakel tussen didactiek en techniek
Facultair (toegangs)beheer van digitale onderwijs- en toetssystemen, zoals Ans en Brightspace

Aanmaken en beheren van gastaccounts

Hier ga je werken

SEEDS ondersteunt docenten van FWN bij didactische uitdagingen en technische vragen zodat docenten zo goed mogelijk onderwijs kunnen geven. We adviseren over werkvormen en onderwijsapplicaties die helpen bij die werkvormen. Daarnaast verzorgen we het functioneel beheer van onderwijsapplicaties en helpen we docenten met opnames en livestreams van colleges. Voor studenten van onze faculteit bouwen en onderhouden we een platform waarop ze zelfstandig kunnen werken aan hun academische vaardigheden.
SEEDS is onderdeel van de afdeling Science Onderwijs- en Studentenzaken (SOSZ). SOSZ ondersteunt en faciliteert de onderwijsorganisatie van de gehele faculteit. Zie voor meer informatie onze  facultaire website .
Je werkt nauw samen met de teams Science Functioneel Beheer en Science Studentenadministratie en de opleidingscoördinatoren binnen de faculteit.

Nieuwsgierigheid en passie voor onderwijs en de wetenschap is wat onze mensen verbindt: we willen weten, begrijpen, duiden en creëren. Onze missie is het verzorgen van excellent onderwijs en onderzoek vanuit de volle breedte van de bètawetenschappen waarmee we bijdragen aan oplossingen voor grote maatschappelijke uitdagingen. Onze acht instituten, van wiskunde, informatica, sterrenkunde, natuurkunde, scheikunde en biofarmaceutische wetenschappen tot aan biologie en milieuwetenschappen vormen samen met het Lorentz Center en de Hortus botanicus de ruggengraat van onze faculteit en zijn sterk met elkaar verbonden.

We werken in een veilige, stimulerende en internationale omgeving waar met plezier en passie wordt gewerkt en gestudeerd en waar het leggen van verbindingen en samenwerken, binnen én buiten de faculteit vanzelfsprekend is. Bij de faculteit werken meer dan 2700 medewerkers en er studeren ruim 6000 studenten in negen bachelor-, en vijftien masteropleidingen. We zijn gesitueerd in het hart van het Bio Science Park, één van Europa’s grootste scienceparken, waar universiteit en bedrijfsleven elkaar ontmoeten.

Dit breng je mee

In dit team zoeken we iemand die zelfstandig aan de slag kan. Elke functie is anders dus er is in het begin aandacht voor inwerken. Mochten bepaalde werkzaamheden nieuw zijn voor je, dan kijken we samen wat je nodig hebt en stellen hiervoor een ontwikkelplan op. Deze functie past bij jou als je je herkent in de volgende punten:
Je hebt affiniteit met het (ondersteunen van) onderwijs.
Ervaring met Brightspace, Ans en/of Feedbackfruits is een pre.
Je bent proactief en hebt een dienstverlenende instelling.
Je werkt zorgvuldig en bent doortastend.
Je hebt oog voor detail en kunt snel schakelen.
Je bent vaardig in het schriftelijk en mondeling communiceren in het Nederlands en Engels.

Herken je jezelf volledig in dit profiel óf voldoe jij niet aan alle eisen maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren!

Dit bieden we je

Jouw werkplek is op de Faculteit Wiskunde en Natuurwetenschappen van de Universiteit Leiden, waar we met de hele afdeling SOSZ op één gang werken in het levendige Gorlaeusgebouw. We lunchen vaak samen of maken een lunchwandeling over het Leiden Bio Science Park.

We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
Een arbeidsovereenkomst voor de duur van één jaar met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband. De overeenkomst valt onder de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten;

Een salaris tussen €3202 - €4159,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (Schaal 07);

Vakantietoeslag (8%), een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%) en een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het ABP;

Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.

Flexibele werkduur: standaard heb je minimaal 29 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime werkweek van 38 uur; je kunt daarnaast extra verlof opbouwen door bijvoorbeeld fulltime 40 uur per week te werken en zo 96 extra verlofuren op te bouwen óf door 96 verlofuren in te leveren en een werkweek van 36 uur te werken;

Ruime keuze in secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden; zo is het bespreekbaar om voor een sabbatical of betaald ouderschapsverlof te kiezen. Binnen ons keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden kunnen vrije dagen en/of salaris ingezet worden voor bijvoorbeeld een voordelig sportabonnement en fietsregeling;

Als de werkzaamheden het toelaten kun je in overleg enkele dagdelen per week thuiswerken;

Een thuiswerkvergoeding (dag- en internetvergoeding) en aandacht voor goede werkplekken, daarnaast krijg je een laptop van de universiteit tot je beschikking.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier:  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Direct solliciteren? Klik dan op de sollicitatiebutton.

Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met Anne-Martine Gielis, teamleider Science Teacher Support Desk, [email protected] . Solliciteren kan tot en met 2 november 2026.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Bij onderlinge afweging van kandidaten, geldt bij gelijke geschiktheid een voorkeur voor interne kandidaten, vrouwen, werknemers met een arbeidsbeperking en werknemers met een migratieachtergrond.

Je woont en bent officieel ingeschreven als inwoner van Nederland of bent bereid te verhuizen zodra je de functie aanvaardt.
Een pre-employment screening (referenties, diploma’s, VOG) kan onderdeel uitmaken van de selectieprocedure.

Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Mocht je ons toch cv’s toesturen dan kunnen daar geen rechten aan worden ontleend. #LI-Hybrid

ap:253363.body:
The PhD specialisation in Marketing focuses on developing doctoral students’ theoretical knowledge and methodological skills required to become successful researchers. We welcome applications from students with a strong background in disciplines such as business, economics, psychology, and statistics.
The Department of Marketing is a strong research department with researchers publishing at the highest international level (e.g., Journal of Consumer Research, Journal of Marketing, Journal of Marketing Research, and Marketing Science). The department is also highly international and has a strong presence at the top conferences in the field globally. The department’s doctoral students are successful and have been placed at high quality international universities and business schools, such as Bayes Business School, Grenoble Ecole de Management, Nanyang Technological University, and University of Groningen.
Eligible applicants must have completed a Master of Science degree with thesis work, a research masters/M. Phil degree, or a comparable degree relevant for the specialisation in Marketing by the early summer of 2027. An MBA degree does not fulfil the requirements for admission. Final year Master of Science students are encouraged to apply.
Accepted applicants will be offered close supervision and follow-up by the research faculty.
The four-year scholarship is set according to the Norwegian State Salary Scale and currently pays NOK 623,200 annually (will be adjusted in 2027). The position normally offers membership in BI's collective pension scheme. The scholarships require 25% of the teaching responsibilities of a full-time professor position. PhD candidates will have their place of work at BI Norwegian Business School in Oslo, Norway.
All documentation that is requested is listed in this announcement text. Please read the announcement text carefully. If you have additional questions, that are not covered by the text, you can contact [email protected] or the academic department. Please note that at BI we are unable to pre-assess qualifications, convert grades, or provide guidance on how to strengthen an application before it is submitted. Applications are assessed by the relevant PhD Evaluation Committee as part of the formal recruitment process. More information can also be found on the Department's  website .
You are required to upload the following with your application:
Certificate of a Master of Science degree or equivalent, including transcripts of grades. Certificate of a Bachelor’s degree or equivalent, including transcript of grades. Please note that BI requires a two year master program and average grades of B and up to be eligible .
A Diploma Supplement or a similar document describing in detail the study and grade system and the rights for further studies associated with the obtained degree. Other relevant certificates and transcripts
An original project proposal (5-10 pages including topic, proposed method, schedule). If generative AI is used to generate any text this needs to be clearly stated and cited.
CV
Letters of recommendations from relevant employers/professors/supervisors providing evidence of your skills as a researcher (a minimum of 2 letters). Letters can be send to [email protected]
Certificates from previously completed courses at the doctoral level, if requesting approval of these for the PhD programme at BI Norwegian Business School (see section 2 in our PhD Regulations). If you have taken any courses at PhD level please complete the following form (maximum 18 ECTS).
A complete list of all publications and/or other documented relevant activities
Signed verification document. Template to be found here: Verification document
Applicants must take either TOEFL or IELTS. The minimum standards for test scores acceptable for admission are: TOEFL – a total score of 575 points for the written test or 233 for the computer-based version or 90 points on the internet-based test
IELTS – a score of 6.5

Exemptions are made for applicants:
whose native language is English
who have two years or more of higher education where the language of instruction was English
from a country which is a member of the EU/EEA and/or the Council of Europe/UNESCO-Cepes, who have English as the first foreign language taken over a period of at least 7 years in primary school, secondary school and upper secondary education.

Under certain circumstances, applicants may request a waiver for the TOEFL or IELTS when applying for admission. To request a TOEFL/IELTS waiver, the applicant must submit a waiver form .
TOEFL / IETLS scores must be from within the last two years. The codes for BI Norwegian Business School are as follows: GMAT 0529, TOEFL 0529, GRE 7365. For IELTS we accept copies as long as the TRF number is visible.
Please note that all documents must be uploaded in the electronic application platform. Documents cannot be submitted by e-mail. Furthermore, note that any documents forwarded after the application deadline will not be considered. Exceptions will only be made for students who are completing their master’s degree in 2027 and do not have a final certificate when applying. Please note that you will not be able to revise your application once it has been submitted.
Candidates may, at a later stage, be asked to forward further information and/or be called in for an interview.
Candidates who are accepted for the programme, must provide a more detailed progress plan with milestones and courses for the four years of study.
Application deadline: December 1st, 2026. Start of the PhD study is August 2027.

ap:253370.body:
The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles.
We are now looking for a
Doctoral Researcher
to join us, Global Change and Biotic Interactions Ecology -group, for the Research Council of Finland-funded project “ Mechanisms of Plant Biodiversity Change ”, both led by Prof. Anu Eskelinen ( Eskelinen Research Group | Global Change and Biotic Interaction Ecology ).
Description of the project
We are looking for a highly motivated and research-oriented person to carry out doctoral
research addressing the mechanisms of plant biodiversity change. In this project, we investigate
what are the roles of mechanisms related to spatial context, dispersal in space and time, biotic
interactions (competition, herbivory) and intraspecific trait change in driving heterogeneous
responses of plant biodiversity to different global change factors (e.g., climate warming, nutrient
enrichment). We aim for a more holistic understanding of plant biodiversity change in the
Anthropocene, being able to provide answers to questions: how, why and where plant
biodiversity changes. The specific research questions can relate, for example, to (1) the role of
temporal dispersal via soil seed banks as a diversity maintaining mechanism under multiple
global changes, (2) the role of intraspecific trait change in modifying the effects of climatic and
other global changes on plant biodiversity, and (3) relative and interactive roles of spatial context
(i.e., connectivity and habitat size), dispersal and herbivory in mediating plant biodiversity
response to global changes. A suitable combination of these questions/ideas will be developed
together with the project leader. We use already existing data (ready to be analyzed) and will also
collect new data from two unique, existing long-term experimental systems to address these
research questions.
Your tasks
As a Doctoral Researcher, you will conduct research in the “Mechanisms of Plant Biodiversity
Change” project described above and complete a doctoral degree and studies studies at the
University of Oulu Graduate School. Your specific tasks are:
Collecting new data on plant communities (field, greenhouse and laboratory work),
including organizing and planning the work
Conducting plant trait measurements
Conducting statistical analyses on new and already existing research data from long-term
field experiments
Writing manuscripts (2-3) and publishing the research findings in high-quality
international peer-reviewed journals under the guidance/supervision of your mentor and
in collaboration with other researchers
Participating national and international conferences and workshops, when relevant
Teaching in BSc/MSc level courses and co-supervising master's students and interns.
Being an active member of the working group

Although the position will be based at the Ecology and Genetics Research Unit in Oulu, the
doctoral researcher will also collaborate with an international researcher team from, for example, the University of Helsinki, Finland and the University of California, Davis, USA. There may also be research visit(s) to these collabortors’ groups.
Qualification requirements for the Doctoral researcher position
MSc in plant community ecology or equivalent field
Strong motivation, curiosity, and enthusiasm towards ecological research and to pursue
doctoral studies
Experience and interest in some of the following: plant biodiversity research, experimental
research, global change research, trait-based plant ecology
Excellent statistical skills with software R
Ability to travel and do field work, experience in field work
Good grassland plant identification skills and ability to quickly learn new species
Knowledge of grassland ecosystems (e.g., temperate, tundra)
Excellent written and spoken English
Good communication and teamwork skills, ability to work in an international team
Driver’s licence is needed or willingness to acquire one
See also the requirements of the University of Oulu Graduate School (UniOGS)

Assessment of the applicants will be based on, acknowledging the content of the job, 1) overall fit to the above profile, 2) scientific publications (if applicable), 3) motivation, 4) previous work experience, 5) national and international mobility and networking skills, and 5) other academic activities and merits.
What we offer
A three-year, full-time Doctoral Researcher position in an ambitious project
Opportunities for national and international collaboration, conference participation, co-
authored publications and research mobility if relevant to your doctoral project
You will become a part of a highly enthusiastic and talented research group that is
working on globally significant research areas
Possibility for a flexible combination of presence work and remote work (this can be
negotiated, depending on the situation of the applicant and project demands)
Full benefits provided by the University of Oulu to university employees, including free
time corresponding to holidays and free occupational health care services. The successful
candidate will receive also benefits provided by the Finnish government to residents, for
example possibility to obtain access to the national healthcare system, tax benefits for
employees with children, and high-quality affordable childcare services.
Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture, and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits here.
Our Buddy Programme and Spouse Network support you and your close ones in settling into Oulu.
We have an HR Excellence in Research -quality label, which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers.
Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us.
Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, an excellent education system, and a competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu.

Salary
The position is fixed-term for three (3) years as of February 1, 2027 or as soon as possible
thereafter. The start date is flexible and can be negotiated.
The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research
staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance
will be paid (a maximum of 50 % of the job-specific component). The typical starting gross salary
will be approx. 2600-3000 € per month (before taxes). As the doctoral research progresses, there
is salary progression in accordance with the University salary system.
A trial period of 6 months is applied to the position.
How to apply?
Interested? If yes, please apply by November 15, 2026 (23:59 Finnish local time, UTC +3)
through our recruitment system. Only applications sent via the online system will be considered.
The application should be written in English and include the following:
1. A motivation letter (max. 2 pages) summarizing the applicant’s professional experience,
and expertise, research interests and motivation, and describing why the applicant is
interested in this position. The motivation letter should also include contact information
of two senior/experienced researchers who may be asked to give a statement on the
shortlisted candidates.
2. CV , following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity
3. List of publications , if applicable, following the guidelines of the Research Council of
Finland
4. A copy of the relevant degree certificate or diploma ; if the qualifying degree is not yet
complete, please describe your expected completion date
The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-
site or remote interview. The refernces of the shortlisted candidates will also contacted. All
applicants will be notified during the selection process.
We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, including people of different ages, genders,
languages, cultures, and minority communities.
Contact Information
For further information, please contact Professor Anu Eskelinen (anu.eskelinen(at)oulu.fi)

ap:253381.body:
About the position
A 100 % position is available at the University of Agder (UiA), Faculty of Engineering and Science  as a PhD Research Fellow in Terrestrial Ecology, affiliated to the Department of Natural Sciences , for a period of three years. The position is located at Campus Kristiansand.
The starting date is negotiable with the Faculty.
Responsibilities
The position is in evolutionary ecology and centres on a fundamental question: how do natural populations respond when humans impose strong and sustained new selection pressures? Evolution depends on the genetic variation already present in populations, yet strong selection can rapidly reshape that variation. Understanding what variation persists, how populations evolve, and why responses differ among populations is important both for explaining diversity in nature and for predicting the evolutionary consequences of human intervention.
The PhD project will exploit a globally unique opportunity to observe this process unfolding across real agricultural landscapes in the context of crop protection. In parts of Brazil, living biological control agents have been deployed against agricultural pests for decades, creating landscapes in which pest populations have experienced contrasting histories of sustained selection. By combining field sampling with laboratory experiments and statistical modelling to quantify genetic variation in complex traits, the candidate will test whether these contrasting histories have driven the evolution of resistance or other life-history shifts in crop pests, and what determines the magnitude of these responses. The project therefore connects fundamental questions about genetic variation and adaptation with an urgent applied challenge: predicting the evolutionary sustainability of biological control. Extended research stays in Brazil will be central to the project, including close collaboration with academic and industry partners, alongside opportunities for research visits and collaboration in Scotland and elsewhere within a wider international network.
The candidate will join a growing collaborative research environment at UiA focused on robust inference about ecological and evolutionary change in human-influenced systems. Researchers work with complex data from diverse marine and terrestrial study systems to examine how historical conditions, environmental change, human interventions, and observation processes affect ecological and evolutionary dynamics and the conclusions drawn from them. The collaboration brings together complementary expertise in observational, experimental, molecular, and quantitative approaches to ecological and evolutionary research.
Required qualifications
A completed Master's degree in evolutionary biology, ecology, entomology, agricultural biology, or a closely related field. Candidates in the final stages of completing their Master's degree may also apply.
A strong academic background relevant to the project.
Experience analysing biological data using R or a comparable programming environment.
Excellent written and spoken English. English will be the primary language for supervision and day-to-day research activities.

Criteria for positions as PhD Research Fellow  (in Norwegian).
A prerequisite for employment is that the candidate is admitted to UiA’s PhD programme in Engineering and Science at the Faculty of Engineering and Science.
Desired qualifications
Strong candidates will typically bring several of the qualifications below, although we recognise that relevant experience may take different forms and do not expect applicants to meet every criterion.
Experience in relevant areas, such as evolutionary ecology, statistical quantitative genetics, experimental evolution, host–enemy interactions, entomology, plant–insect interactions, plant defence, or biological control
Experience undertaking laboratory research on insects or other organisms
Experience with advanced statistical modelling, particularly Bayesian and/or hierarchical models
A track record of scientific writing, demonstrated through theses, manuscripts, reports, publications, or other research outputs.
Knowledge of Portuguese, or to a lesser extent Spanish, will be an advantage for fieldwork and collaboration during extended research stays in Brazil.
Knowledge of Norwegian or another Scandinavian language is an advantage for participation in the wider academic and social environment at UiA.

Personal qualities
Ability to work independently, take initiative, and organise research effectively.
Strong collaborative skills and willingness to contribute to a supportive research environment.
Motivation and preparedness for extended international research stays, particularly in Brazil, and for working across different academic, cultural, and linguistic environments.
Intellectual curiosity and enthusiasm for combining empirical biology with quantitative approaches.

Personal qualities and suitability for the position will be emphasised.
We offer
professional development in a large, exciting and socially influential organisation
a positive, inclusive and diverse working environment
modern facilities and a comprehensive set of welfare offers
membership of the  Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund

More about working at UiA.
The position is remunerated according to the State Salary Scale, salary plan 17.515, code 1017 PhD Research Fellow, NOK 550 800 gross salary per year. A compulsory pension contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund is deducted from the pay according to current statutory provisions.
General information
UiA is an open and inclusive university. We believe that diversity enriches the workplace and makes us better. We, therefore, encourage qualified candidates to apply for the position independent of gender, age, cultural background, disability or an incomplete CV.
The successful applicant will have rights and obligations in accordance with the current regulations for the position, and organisational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities of the position must be expected. The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning the acts relating to  Control of Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology .
Appointment is made by the University of Agder’s Appointments Committee for Teaching and Research Positions. A  background check  may be conducted to verify information that appears in available documents. Background checks are always done with the applicant's consent, and employment in the position requires an approved background check. Relevant applicants will receive further information.
Short-listed applicants will be invited for interview. With the applicant’s permission, UiA will also conduct a reference check before appointment. Read more about the  employment process .
In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act § 25 (2), applicants may request that they are not identified in the open list of applicants. The University, however, reserves the right to publish the names of applicants. Applicants will be advised of the University’s intention to exercise this right.
Application
The application and any necessary information about education and experience (including diplomas and certificates) are to be sent electronically. Use the link "Apply for this job" .
The following documentation must be uploaded electronically:
Certificates with grades
Master’s thesis. Candidates who have not yet completed their Master’s degree should instead submit a current draft of the thesis, or another substantial piece of scientific writing if a thesis draft is not yet available
Contact details for references
Academic publications (including any preprint or in press manuscripts) and other relevant research outputs, if applicable, including a list of these
Statement of research interests and motivation (maximum 2 pages). Applicants should describe their research interests and relevant experience, explain why this PhD project interests them, and identify one or two research questions arising from the advertised project that they find particularly interesting and briefly explain why.
Any other relevant documentation

The applicant is fully responsible for submitting complete digital documentation before the closing date. All documentation must be available in a Scandinavian language or English.
Application deadline: 05.11.26
Contact
For questions about the position:
Associate Professor Luc Bussière, mobile +47 453 98 325, e-mail  [email protected]

For questions about the application process:
HR-Advisor, Linda H. Kristiansen, tel. +47 38 14 11 88, e-mail:  [email protected]

Creating knowledge together
When people who are committed come together to further knowledge, anything is possible.
The University of Agder combines the unique warmth and charm of Southern Norway with first-class scientific, technological and artistic expertise.
Would you like to work with us to create better solutions to our shared challenges?
University of Agder
Universitetet i Agder har over 1500 ansatte og nesten 14 000 studenter. Det gjør oss til en av Sørlandets største arbeidsplasser. Våre ansatte forsker, underviser og formidler kunnskap fra alle sine fagområder.

ap:253412.body:
The IB is currently seeking an experienced individual to take on the role of Deputy Examiner Responsible (DER) for its Lao A: Literature course.
The International Baccalaureate® (IB) is a non-profit educational foundation offering four programmes of international education that develop the intellectual, personal, emotional and social skills needed to live, learn and work in a rapidly globalizing world. We strive to develop students who will build a better world through intercultural understanding and respect.
One of the characteristics of the IB's Diploma Programme is that students are required to study, as one of six subjects that constitute the diploma, one of three ‘Language A’ courses, each designed to develop high social, aesthetic and cultural literacy, as well as communication skills. The language A: literature course introduces students to the analysis of literary texts. It is the course through which the IB’s policy of mother-tongue entitlement is delivered. The course is automatically available in 55 languages and available by special request and may be studied in any language with a sufficiently developed written literature.
The duties of DER include the setting and marking of examinations and determining final grades of students.
Outline information about this role, as well as the application form and recruitment policy can be found at: IB Deputy Examiner Responsible - International Baccalaureate®
Please note that this position is part-time, involves no relocation, and is usually undertaken in addition to existing work commitments.
You must:
have a degree or equivalent in the subject (or a related subject) for which you are applying,
have a minimum of one year’s experience teaching the subject (or a related subject) for which they are applying to students of: 16 to 18 years of age (DP)

be native speaker/fluent in English and Lao in order to write reports and mark students’ written and spoken responses.
ap:253412.employer_blurb: The IB is more than its educational programmes and certificates. At our heart we are motivated by a mission to create a better world through education.
ap:253412.summary: Part-time role setting/marking Lao A: Literature exams and awarding final grades. Requires degree, 1+ yr teaching 16–18, fluent Lao & English.

The IB is currently seeking an experienced individual to take on the role of Deputy Examiner Responsible (DER) for its Lithuanian A: Literature: Literature course.
The International Baccalaureate® (IB) is a non-profit educational foundation offering four programmes of international education that develop the intellectual, personal, emotional and social skills needed to live, learn and work in a rapidly globalizing world. We strive to develop students who will build a better world through intercultural understanding and respect.
One of the characteristics of the IB's Diploma Programme is that students are required to study, as one of six subjects that constitute the diploma, one of three ‘Language A’ courses, each designed to develop high social, aesthetic and cultural literacy, as well as communication skills. The language A: literature course introduces students to the analysis of literary texts. It is the course through which the IB’s policy of mother-tongue entitlement is delivered. The course is automatically available in 55 languages and available by special request and may be studied in any language with a sufficiently developed written literature.
The duties of DER include the setting and marking of examinations and determining final grades of students.
Outline information about this role, as well as the application form and recruitment policy can be found at: IB Deputy Examiner Responsible - International Baccalaureate®
Please note that this position is part-time, involves no relocation, and is usually undertaken in addition to existing work commitments.
You must:
have a degree or equivalent in the subject (or a related subject) for which you are applying,
have a minimum of one year’s experience teaching the subject (or a related subject) for which they are applying to students of: 16 to 18 years of age (DP)

be native speaker/fluent in English and Lithuanian in order to write reports and mark students’ written and spoken responses.

ap:253431.body:
Doctoral position in cognitive and moral heuristics in lay people’s reactions to climate change adaptation
We are looking for a motivated doctoral student who is interested in applying psychological concepts and methodologies to environmental topics. The position is available starting January 2027.

Project background
While climate change mitigation (e.g., reduction of greenhouse gas emissions) remains important, it is also clear that societies need to adapt to the unavoidable hazards associated with climate change. The recent heat waves in Europe and the health and economical damages they caused, exemplify that adaptation measures are not yet sufficiently in place.

Heuristics (mental shortcuts) can bias people’s risk perceptions and affect moral considerations. As such they can influence people’s private adaptation behaviors and their perceptions of technologies that could help societies to deal better with the consequences of climate change. By influencing regulations, they can also impact the exposure of vulnerable groups to hazards, such as heat.

The aim of this doctoral thesis is to gain insights in how cognitive and moral heuristics influence the effective implementation of climate change adaptation measures.

Job description

Conceptualization and conduction of empirical studies (quantitative or qualitative designs are possible)

Writing manuscripts and publishing studies in scientific journals

Dissemination of research results (e.g., at conferences)

Supervising bachelor and master students

Supporting lectures

Profile

Master’s degree in psychology, environmental science, or social sciences

Knowledge and first experiences with descriptive and inferential statistics

Advanced German and English skills

Ability to think conceptually and work independently

Strong interest in research and methodologies from psychology and social sciences

We offer

Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

Letter of Motivation

CV

Copy of your transcript of records (Bachelor and Master)

Copy of your master's diploma

Employment references, if available

Further information about our research group can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Bruno Etter, +41 44 633 84 62 or [email protected] (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:253432.body:
BI Norwegian Business School is one of Europe's largest educational institutions, with over 20.000 students. As Norway's leading business school, BI builds on a unique tradition of combining academic rigour and professional relevance. Our programmes range from bachelor's to master's and PhD programmes. BI is also known for its many customized executive education programmes.
BI boasts some of Europe's leading academic departments within the fields of economics, finance, strategy, marketing, management and data science. As an employee at BI Norwegian Business School you will meet exciting challenges in an engaging and international environment, with over 800 colleagues who continuously push the frontiers of knowledge.
PhD Candidates in Economics
BI Norwegian Business School offers a four-year Ph.D. Programme with specialization in Economics, which trains students to engage in high quality scientific research, making use of economic theory and state of the art econometric methods. The Department of Economics has a strong research-oriented faculty working within microeconomic theory, macroeconomics, econometrics, labour economics, natural resource and energy economics, political economics, industrial organization, and international and development economics. The department hosts five research centres; Centre for Monetary Economics (CME), Centre for Research in Economics and Management (CREAM), Centre for Applied Macro and Petroleum Economics (CAMP), Centre for Experimental Studies and Research (CESAR), and Centre for Applied and Theoretical Econometrics (CATE).
The doctoral programme is an important element in the department's research excellence strategy and in BI's vision to become one of the leading research business schools in Europe. The selected candidates will join a group of talented and ambitious PhD candidates at the department that work in close collaboration with faculty members. PhD students are expected to participate actively in research seminars and workshops. The place of work will be at BI Norwegian Business School in Oslo.
A PhD from BI can be a gateway to prestigious academic positions at universities and research institutions around the world. We encourage and support our candidates in the international job market. Recent graduates of BI's PhD specialization in economics have been hired by, among others, Sciences Po, University of Chicago, Harvard Business School, Católica Lisbon School of Business & Economics, King’s College London, University of Oslo and Research Division of Norges Bank .
Eligible applicants must have completed a Master of Science degree with thesis work, a Research Masters/M.Phil degree, or a comparable degree relevant for the specialization in Economics by the time the programme starts in early autumn of 2026, with a grade point average of B or higher. An MBA degree does not fulfill the requirements for admission. The four-year scholarship is set according to the Norwegian State Salary Scale, and currently pays NOK 623,200 (this will be adjusted).The position normally offers membership in BI's collective pension scheme. The scholarship involves 25% work obligation. BI Norwegian Business School is an equal opportunity employer. We encourage women to apply for the positions.
Applications must be submitted electronically by using the "Send Application" button on the right-hand side of this announcement. Paper or e-mail applications will not be accepted. You are required to submit the following electronically together with your application:
Background Information:
A short personal statement describing your research interests and potential research projects. Please also include BI Department of Economics faculty members that you may be interested in working closely with should you be admitted to the PhD program. The list of our faculty members can be found here .
Curriculum Vitae (CV).
We do not require full research proposals for concrete projects (while applications to other departments may do).

Letters of Recommendation:
We require a minimum of two (preferably three) letters of recommendation from people that can comment on your research potential. These should be emailed directly to us by the letter writers rather than uploaded by you. However, you must include the names of your letter writers in your application. Please arrange with the people submitting recommendation letters to email their recommendations to [email protected]   by the application deadline .

Academic Transcripts:
Certificate of a Master of Science degree or equivalent, including transcript of grades.
Certificate of a Bachelor degree or equivalent, including transcript of grades.
A Diploma Supplement or a similar document describing in detail the study and grade system associated with the obtained degree.
Signed transcript verification document ( to be found here ) . (Please note that this document should be uploaded with your application and not sent to your university. We will use the document to request an official transcript if you are considered for admission to the program and check for any discrepancy with the transcript you uploaded.)

Test Scores:
GRE General/GMAT test score: All applicants, except those who hold a master's degree from an institution inside the European Economic Area/the European Union or Switzerland, must submit results from GMAT or the GRE General test. Note that we need scores for the Verbal, Quantitative and Analytical Writing sections of the GRE General or GMAT to consider your application. Incomplete sections or partial scores are not sufficient to consider your application.
TOEFL/IELTS test score: Applicants whose native language is not English must take either TOEFL or IELTS. To be considered for admission, applicants must have a minimum TOEFL score of 575 (written test)/233 (computer-based test)/90 (internet-based test) or a IELTS score of 6.5. In some cases, applicants can request a waiver from TOEFL/IELTS by submitting a waiver form ( found here ) together with the application. As a general rule, exemptions are made for applicants: who have two years or more of higher education where the language of instruction was English.
from a country which is a member of the EU/EEA and/or the Council of Europe/UNESCO-Cepes who have English as the first foreign language taken over a period of at least 7 years in primary school, secondary school and upper secondary education.

We accept scanned copies of test scores. TOEFL/IELTS scores must be from within the last two years. For scanned IELTS scores, the TRF number must be visible. In case of sending official score reports from the test center, you can use the following codes for BI Norwegian Business School: TOEFL/GMAT: 0529.
GRE: 7365.

Additional documents:
In addition, you may upload the following documents: A writing sample that documents relevant research activities (e.g. a Master's thesis or academic paper).

Certificates from previously completed courses at the doctoral level, if requesting approval of these for the PhD programme at BI Norwegian Business School (see section 2 in our PhD Regulations). If you have taken any courses at PhD level please complete the following form (maximum 18 ECTS).

All documents, apart from the recommendation letters, must be uploaded in the electronic application and may not be submitted by e-mail or on paper. Furthermore, note that any documents forwarded after the application deadline will not be considered. Exceptions will only be made for students who are completing their master's degree in 2026 and do not have a final certificate when applying. Please note that you will not be able to revise your application once it has been submitted.
Candidates may, at a later stage, be asked to forward further information and/or be called in for an interview. Candidates who are admitted to the programme must provide a more detailed progress plan with milestones and courses for the four years of study.
Additional information about the doctoral programme and admission requirements can be obtained from the doctoral administration at BI Norwegian Business School. E-mail: [email protected] .

ap:253436.body:
Let’s shape the future - University of Antwerp
The University of Antwerp is a dynamic, forward-thinking, European university. We offer an innovative academic education to more than 20 000 students, conduct pioneering scientific research, and play an important service-providing role in society. We are one of the largest, most international, and most innovative employers in the region. With more than 6 000 employees from 100 different countries, we are helping to build tomorrow's world every day. Through top scientific research, we push back boundaries and set a course for the future – a future that you can help to shape.
The Department of Electromechanical Engineering Technology (research group Cosys-Lab), in the Faculty of Applied Engineering, is looking for a full-time (100%) doctoral scholarship holder in the field of mathematical modelling and optimal design of mechatronic systems.
Position
You will actively work on the preparation and defence of a PhD thesis in the field of mathematical modelling and optimal design of mechatronic systems. You will research the next generation of automatic generation of mechanisms and the optimization of their performance. This movie provides a general introduction to the machine design research within Cosys-Lab. You will draw up a research plan and corresponding research methods in consultation with your supervisor(s) and undertake the necessary administration for a smooth PhD process.
You will conduct the research efficiently and to an appropriate standard, possibly abroad, and compete for funding for general or specific costs.
You will report progress to your supervisor(s) and committees. Moreover, you will present your research at scientific conferences.
You will defend your thesis publicly and aim for publication in the scientific press.

You will make a supporting, scientific contribution to existing research projects or lines of research within your own doctoral research.
You will compete for internal or external predoctoral funding.
In addition to project-based research, you will also be responsible for a limited range of support tasks related to teaching and/or valorisation within our department.

Profile
You hold a master's degree in mechanical engineering, mathematical engineering, physics, applied math, or similar, or you will have obtained it by the time of appointment.
You can provide evidence of excellent study results.
You have a strong mathematical foundation and demonstrable affinity with mathematical modelling and optimization (e.g. linear/geometric algebra, numerical optimization) applied to an engineering problem, preferably in your master's thesis. Prior exposure to (projective) geometric algebra is a plus but not expected - willingness to master new mathematical formalisms is what matters.
You have a good knowledge of English, both oral and written (preferably C1).
Your teaching competencies are in line with the University of Antwerp’s educational vision .
Your research qualities are in line with the faculty and university research policies .
You act with attention to quality, integrity, creativity, and cooperation.
You combine strong independent working skills with an excellent collaborative mindset.

What we offer
We offer a doctoral scholarship for a period of at least one year. Following a positive evaluation and available funding, the scholarship can be renewed for another period (max three years).
We offer the opportunity to take part in academic activities within the scope of your work, as well as the opportunity to further develop yourself through training and education.
The planned start period is January - March 2027 (or as soon as possible after that date).
Your monthly scholarship amount is calculated according to the scholarship amounts for doctoral scholarship holders.
You will receive ecocheques and a bicycle allowance or a full reimbursement of public transport costs for commuting.
As a doctoral researcher, you will have access to a wide and varied range of courses and an educational credit through the Antwerp Doctoral School .
You will do most of your work at Campus Groenenborger (2020 Antwerp, Belgium) in a dynamic and stimulating working environment.
Find out more about working at the University of Antwerp here .

Want to apply?
You can apply for this vacancy through the University of Antwerp’s online job application platform up to and including 2 November 2026 (by midnight Brussels time). Click on the 'Apply' button and complete the online application form. Be sure to include the following attachments: a motivation letter
your academic CV

The selection committee reviews all applications as soon as possible after the application deadline. As soon as a decision is made, we will notify you. If you are still eligible after the pre-selection, you will be informed about the possible next step(s) in the selection procedure. Please reserve the following date and time in your calendar: 10 November 2026 between 14:00 and 16:00 Brussels time, and 12 November 2026 between 13:00 and 15:00 Brussels time.
If you have any questions about the online application form, please check the frequently asked questions or send an email to [email protected] . If you have any questions about the job itself, please contact Professor Stijn Derammelaere – [email protected] .

The University of Antwerp received the European Commission’s HR Excellence in Research Award for its HR policy. We are a sustainable, family-friendly organisation which invests in its employees’ growth. We encourage diversity  and attach great importance to an inclusive working environment and equal opportunities, regardless of gender identity, disability, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual orientation or age. We encourage people from diverse backgrounds and with diverse characteristics to apply.
