ap:253611.body:
Doctoral Researcher Position in Sustainable Supply Chain Management
The Supply Chain Management Group (Prof. Dr. Stephan Wagner) at the Department of Management, Technology, and Economics at ETH Zurich invites applications for a PhD student / doctoral researcher position in Sustainable Supply Chain Management. The Supply Chain Management Group at ETH Zurich provides an inspiring, team-oriented research environment with a dynamic and international group of researchers. Our team has a strong track record of publishing in leading operations and supply chain management journals. The position offers close supervision and collaboration with leading faculty and senior researchers, as well as access to ETH Zurich’s excellent research infrastructure and strong international network of collaborators.

Job description
Companies are increasingly expected to manage social sustainability issues within their supply chains. Several countries (e.g., France, Germany, Norway) have implemented supply chain due diligence regulations aimed at ending modern slavery and unsafe working conditions. However, such issues continue to occur within global supply chains. In this context, the successful candidate will conduct doctoral research using quantitative and qualitative research methods, including engagement with industry partners and analysis of secondary data. The candidate will be part of a research project led by Dr. Christian Wagner and Prof. Dr. Stephan Wagner.

Further responsibilities include supervising master’s theses, assisting with teaching, and participating in community outreach. Ideal candidates should be interested in and willing to write research-oriented papers for scholarly journals, academic proceedings, and practitioner journals. The dissertation is expected to consist of three high-quality papers intended for submission to top-tier journals.

Profile
We expect an excellent master's degree in Industrial Engineering, Economics, Business Administration, or a related field, as well as excellent written and oral skills in English and, ideally, German. A high level of motivation for academic research is required. A strong background in empirical methods and data analysis using statistical or econometric techniques is necessary. Candidates with primarily analytical backgrounds and/or interests will not be considered. Candidates should demonstrate strong teamwork and social skills, as well as independence, proactivity, and exemplary organizational and project management abilities. Additionally, candidates should feel comfortable taking a leading role in research meetings with project partners and actively networking at conferences.

We offer

Become part of our ambitious and team-oriented Supply Chain Management Group

Benefit from close supervision and collaboration with our international research partners

Attend international academic conferences and present your work

Benefit from ETH Zurich’s excellent research infrastructure, course offerings, and career development programs

Enjoy  numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare , a competitive salary, and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your application. Please submit the following documents as a single merged PDF using only the ETH Zurich online portal. Title the document with your last and first name, as well as the application date (e.g., 20261022_lastname_firstname_application). Arrange the documents in the following order:

Cover letter with a specific statement of your motivation for the position

CV

Name and contact information of two references

University transcripts and other reference letters

Representative published research work (e.g., papers, thesis chapters)

Further information about the Supply Chain Management Group can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Christian Wagner, [email protected] , (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

The application deadline is November 30, 2026. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis, and early submission is therefore encouraged.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

Project description
Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering
Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed alongside humans to carry out complex coordinated tasks. In these settings, autonomous systems must handle strict spatial and temporal constraints while adapting in real time to supervisory commands, unexpected obstacles, and environmental disturbances. Enabling trustworthy human–robot collaboration calls for new mathematical foundations and computational tools that unify decision-making, planning, and control.
We are seeking an exceptional doctoral student to conduct research at the intersection of game theory and control for multi-agent autonomous systems. The position is part of the Digital Futures project Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy via Hybrid Games .  The work will span both mathematical foundations of hybrid games and the design of computationally tractable controllers for deployment on real robotic platforms.
The research will address:
Hybrid dynamic games under temporal logic task specifications;
Game-theoretic modelling of human–robot interaction;
Experimental validation on multi-robot and underwater robotic platforms;

Supervision: Assistant Prof. Giuseppe Belgioioso and Prof. Dimos Dimarogonas are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge

In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.

A strong background in optimization and automatic control is required. Familiarity with game theory, hybrid systems, MPC, or formal methods will be advantageous. Proficiency in programming, and any prior hands-on experience with robotic platforms, will also be beneficial.
Selected candidates must be able to provide contact information to at least one academic or professional reference. The candidate must be able to demonstrate high motivation for doctoral studies.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with many employee benefits and monthly salary according to KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement . Read more about Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden .
Union representatives
Contact information for   union representatives.
Doctoral Student’s network (Students’ union on KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
Contact information for   PhD chapter .
To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled language requirements (see above) . Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be certified .
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge. (max 2 pages).
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (max 1 page).
Representative publications or reports (e.g., master thesis).
Name of at least one academic or professional reference.

Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
Other information
For information about processing of personal data in the recruitment process.
It may be the case that a position at KTH is classified as a security-sensitive role in accordance with the Protective Security Act (2018:585). If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.

ap:253629.body:
Projektbeskrivning
Forskarutbildningsämne:  Elektro- och systemteknik
Autonoma system används i allt högre grad tillsammans med människor för att utföra komplexa, samordnade uppgifter. I dessa miljöer måste autonoma system hantera strikta rumsliga och tidsmässiga begränsningar, samtidigt som de i realtid anpassar sig till övergripande kommandon, oväntade hinder och störningar i omgivningen. Att möjliggöra ett tillförlitligt samarbete mellan människa och robot kräver nya matematiska grunder och beräkningsverktyg som förenar beslutsfattande, planering och styrning.
Vi söker en exceptionellt skicklig doktorand för att bedriva forskning i gränssnittet mellan spelteori, hybridsystem och reglerteknik för autonoma fleragentsystem. Tjänsten ingår i flaggskeppsprojektet ” Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy via Hybrid Games ” inom ramen för Digital Futures. Arbetet kommer att omfatta både matematiska grunder för hybridspel och utformning av beräkningsmässigt hanterbara reglersystem för implementering på fysiska robotplattformar.
Forskningen kommer att behandla:
Hybriddynamiska spel under uppgiftsspecifikationer baserade på temporallogik;
Spelteoretisk modellering av interaktion mellan människa och robot;
Experimentell validering på plattformar för multirobotsystem och undervattensrobotik;

Handledning: Biträdande lektor Giuseppe Belgioioso och professor Dimos Dimarogonas föreslås handleda doktoranden. Beslut tas vid antagning
Behörighet för antagning
För att bli antagen till forskarutbildning (kap 7 39 § högskoleförordningen) krävs att den sökande har grundläggande behörighet:
avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå, eller
fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

Utöver ovanstående  finns också ett obligatoriskt krav på engelska motsvarande Engelska B/6 .
Urval
För att lyckas med dina doktorandstudier på KTH behöver du vara målinriktad och ihärdig i ditt arbete. Vid urval av de sökande bedöms förmågan att:
självständigt driva sitt arbete framåt,
kunna samarbeta med andra,
ha ett professionellt förhållningssätt och
analysera och arbeta med komplexa frågor.

En stark bakgrund i de matematiska verktyg som är nödvändiga för projektet, särskilt inom optimering och reglerteori, krävs. Kunskap om spelteori, hybrida system eller multiagentsystem, modellprediktiv reglering eller formella metoder är meriterande. Eftersom projektet innefattar både numeriskt och experimentellt arbete är kompetens inom programmering och numerisk simulering, samt eventuell praktisk erfarenhet av robotplattformar, också värdefull.
Utvalda kandidater måste kunna lämna kontaktuppgifter till minst en akademisk eller professionell referens. Kandidaten måste kunna visa hög motivation för doktorandstudier.
Efter behörighetskraven kommer stor vikt läggas vid personliga egenskaper.
Målexamen: Doktorsexamen
Information om antagning och anställning
Endast den som antagits till forskarutbildning får anställas som doktorand. Den sammanlagda anställningstiden får inte vara längre än vad som motsvarar utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid under fyra år. En anställd doktorand kan i begränsad omfattning (högst 20 %) utföra vissa arbetsuppgifter inom t.ex. utbildning och administration. En ny anställning som doktorand gäller för högst ett år, anställningen får därefter förnyas med högst två år i taget.
Som doktorand får du del av KTH:s anställningsförmåner och har en månadslön enligt KTH:s avtal för doktorandlöner . Läs mer om Forskarstudier vid KTH | KTH | Sweden.

Ansökan

Ansökan ska ha följande innehåll

Om så är fallet för just denna anställning görs en säkerhetsprövning av sökande i enlighet med säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) efter samtycke. I dessa fall är en förutsättning för anställning att sökande blir godkänd efter säkerhetsprövning.
Vi undanber oss direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av platsannonser.

Bli en del av KTH

KTH formar framtiden genom utbildning, forskning och innovation. Som ett ledande internationellt tekniskt universitet spelar vi en aktiv roll i att driva och medverka i omställningen till ett hållbart samhälle. Här erbjuds du möjligheten att växa och utvecklas på en kreativ och dynamisk arbetsplats med goda arbetsvillkor och förmåner. Jämställdhet, mångfald och lika villkor är en kvalitetsfråga och en självklar del av KTH:s värdegrund som universitet och statlig myndighet.

ap:253637.body:
Docent-promovendus Duitse taal en cultuur / Lecturer-PhD candidate German language and culture

Vacaturenummer: 26-16921

Ben jij gepassioneerd door taalkunde én wil je jouw eigen promotieonderzoek uitvoeren terwijl je studenten inspireert? LUCL is op zoek naar een  docent-promovendus  op het gebied van de  Duitse taal en cultuur , met een specifieke focus op  Duitse taalkunde en taalverwerving.
Promoveer in een inspirerende internationale onderzoeksomgeving en combineer dit met het geven van stimulerend onderwijs. In deze rol combineer je 75% promotieonderzoek en 25% onderwijs:
Je doet taalkundig onderzoek dat uitmondt in een promotie. Dit onderzoek is vrij in te vullen zolang het een relatie heeft met de Duitse taal en aansluit bij één (of meer) van de  zes onderzoeksprogramma’s van LUCL .
Je geeft onderwijs in het Duits op het gebied van de Duitse taal en cultuur, met een specifieke focus op Duitse taalkunde en taalverwerving. Afhankelijk van jouw expertise kun je eventueel ook bijdragen aan onderwijs over Duitse cultuur en geschiedenis.

Wij zoeken

Een nieuwsgierige en gedreven academicus die graag kennis deelt. Daarnaast breng je mee:
Een succesvol afgeronde (Research) Master opleiding op het gebied van de taalkunde.
Bij voorkeur aantoonbare onderwijservaring, idealiter op het gebied van de Duitse taalkunde en/of taalverwerving.
Excellente actieve beheersing van het Duits (niveau C1/C2).
Voldoende actieve beheersing van het Nederlands (minimaal niveau B1).
Interesse in één of meer van de volgende taalkundige gebieden: computationele, beschrijvende, theoretische, sociolinguïstische, experimentele of vergelijkende Indo-Europese taalkunde (Zie ook  zes onderzoeksprogramma’s van LUCL)
Excellente communicatieve vaardigheden die je kunt inzetten om zowel studenten te inspireren als nieuwe studenten Duits te werven.

Wij bieden

Een 5-jarig traject leidend tot een voltooide dissertatie / PhD thesis (75% promotieonderzoek, 25% onderwijs):
Een dienstverband voor bepaalde tijd voor de periode van vijf jaar (volgens CAO NU artikel 2.2a).
Begeleiding door professionele staf met diepgaande vakexpertise en een hoog academisch niveau.
Een salaris volgens de CAO Nederlandse Universiteiten van € 3.706,- bruto per maand in het eerste jaar oplopend tot € 4.422,- bruto per maand in het laatste jaar.
Uitstekende arbeidsvoorwaarden met een flexibel arbeidsvoorwaardenkeuzemodel, 8% vakantietoeslag en 8,3% eindejaarsuitkering. Zie ook  www.werkenbij.leidenuniv.nl .
Een inspirerende en collegiale werkomgeving in hartje Leiden.

Startdatum is februari 2027  (of zo snel mogelijk daarna).

LUCL PhD community

Binnen LUCL is er een actieve en internationale PhD community van ruim 40 promovendi. Je ontmoet elkaar in gezamenlijke seminars, leesgroepen, peer feedbacksessies en sociale activiteiten. Hier is een sterke cultuur van samenwerking en onderlinge ondersteuning: promovendi wisselen expertise uit, organiseren zelf workshops en bouwen duurzame netwerken op binnen én buiten de taalkunde. Je staat er dus nooit alleen voor.

Over LUCL en de faculteit

LUCL staat bekend om zijn brede en diepgaande expertise in taalwetenschap. Wij bieden uitstekende onderzoeks- en onderwijsmogelijkheden in een breed scala aan talen van over de hele wereld. Onze missie is om taalvariatie en diversiteit te bestuderen vanuit verschillende theoretische perspectieven, om zo bij te dragen tot een beter begrip van allerlei talen, van vroeger tot nu. Samenwerking vindt plaats binnen onze overlappende onderzoeksprogramma’s en draagt bij aan excellent onderzoek op het gebied van vastgestelde universitaire thema’s zoals in ‘Talen, culturen en wereldbeeld’ en ‘AI voor mens, maatschappij en wetenschap’.
Het LUCL is één van de zeven instituten die vallen onder de Faculteit der Geesteswetenschappen. Met meer dan 120 taalkundigen is het een rijke onderzoeksomgeving die zich onderscheidt door het bevorderen van wetenschappelijke excellentie.

Diversiteit

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Informatie

Wil je meer weten? Neem dan contact op.
Inhoudelijke vragen: Jenny Audring ( [email protected] ).
Praktische vragen: Maarit van Gammeren ( [email protected] ).

Solliciteren

Solliciteren kan tot uiterlijk  8 november 2026  via ons online sollicitatiesysteem. Graag de volgende documenten bij de sollicitatie voegen:
Motivatiebrief
CV
Contactgegevens van twee referenten. Gelieve geen brieven in te sturen.
MA-scriptie.
Korte beschrijving van mogelijk promotie-onderzoek (max. 1 A4), inclusief potentiële begeleiders binnen LUCL.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Bij onderlinge afweging van kandidaten, geldt bij gelijke geschiktheid een voorkeur voor interne kandidaten, vrouwen, werknemers met een arbeidsbeperking en werknemers met een migratieachtergrond.

Je woont en bent officieel ingeschreven als inwoner van Nederland of bent bereid te verhuizen zodra je de functie aanvaardt.
Een pre-employment screening (referenties, diploma’s, VOG) kan onderdeel uitmaken van de selectieprocedure.

Docenten die Engelstalige vakken verzorgen beschikken over een Engels taalniveau dat minimaal overeenkomt met niveau C1.Van internationale docenten die in het Nederlands doceren wordt niveau C1 verwacht. Van andere medewerkers wordt minimaal een passieve kennis van het Nederlands verwacht.

De Universiteit Leiden verwacht dat docenten de Basiskwalificatie Onderwijs (BKO) halen. Als de nieuwe medewerker deze kwalificatie of het equivalent daarvan nog niet bezit, moet deze bereid zijn deze kwalificatie binnen twee jaar te behalen.

Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Mocht je ons toch cv’s toesturen dan kunnen daar geen rechten aan worden ontleend. #LI-Hybrid

ap:253649.body:
The International Max Planck Research School for Ultrafast Imaging and Structural Dynamics in Hamburg, Germany , offers a structured PhD program focusing on ultra-fast phenomena, X-ray physics and dynamical imaging in all areas of science, covering physics, chemistry and biology.
23 Interdisciplinary doctoral PhD projects in the fields of Ultrafast Science and Quantum Materials
Research
The program offers exciting research opportunities at ultra-intense electron and X-ray sources to directly observe atomic motions during primary events. The use of ultrafast imaging over the relevant length and time scales generates new levels of understanding of the interplay between structure and dynamics. Specific areas include the theoretical and experimental aspects of quantum materials and atomically resolved dynamics, fundamental light-matter interaction, accelerator-based light sources, coherent controlled molecular and solid-state dynamics, molecular imaging, extreme timescale spectroscopy, ultrafast optics and X-ray science.
Requirements
We seek applicants with an excellent academic background. You hold (or are about to complete) an MSc degree or equivalent in physics, chemistry or related areas. You need to be passionate about research in ultrafast phenomena and motivated to conduct rigorous scientific work over the full degree period.
We offer:
A range of PhD positions in these areas: open positions
State-of-the-art research facilities on an extensive science campus
Cross-disciplinary research in a vibrant, international scientific environment
First class supervision and mentorship by a team of internationally renowned experts
Outstanding training in your scientific subject and transferable skills (in English)
A 3-year employment contract based on the German federal pay agreement

Apply
Applications must be submitted via the online application portal . The application deadline is 6th November 2026 . PhD projects start in summer/​autumn 2027. In exceptional cases, it may be possible to start on the research project earlier. For any further questions or problems regarding the application process or the online system, please contact the IMPRS UFAST coordinator at [email protected] .

ap:253652.body:
Description du poste
La GSEM (Geneva School of Economics and Management) invite des candidatures pour un poste de professeur·e à plein temps en management. La personne retenue contribuera aux activités de recherche, d’enseignement et de rayonnement de la GSEM dans le domaine « Business and Society », entendu dans une acception large. Nous recherchons un·e chercheur·e dont les travaux portent sur les interactions entre les organisations et les enjeux sociétaux, et qui s’inscrivent solidement dans les disciplines fondamentales du management telles que le comportement organisationnel, la théorie des organisations et la stratégie.
La personne nommée devra être en mesure d’enseigner aux niveaux bachelor, master, doctorat et formation continue (executive education), d’encadrer des mémoires de master ainsi que des thèses de doctorat, et de contribuer au développement de l’Institut de Management. Les enseignements couvriront principalement des thématiques liées à « Business and Society », notamment la durabilité, les critères ESG, le management responsable et les relations avec les parties prenantes. Elle contribuera également à renforcer les liens de la Faculté avec l’écosystème genevois, notamment les organisations internationales, les ONG, les institutions publiques et les entreprises.
Titre et compétences exigés
Les candidat·es doivent démontrer un excellent dossier de recherche attesté par des publications dans des revues académiques de premier plan en management. Un programme de recherche établi portant sur les enjeux « Business and Society » tels que la durabilité, les critères ESG, le management responsable, les relations avec les parties prenantes ou des thématiques connexes, tout en restant solidement ancré dans les théories fondamentales du management, est indispensable. Nous accueillons favorablement les candidat·es mobilisant une large diversité de méthodes de recherche empirique. Un profil marqué en recherche quantitative constituerait un atout particulier pour compléter les expertises existantes au sein de l’Institut et soutenir la formation doctorale ainsi que l’encadrement de thèses.
Les candidat·es doivent faire preuve d’excellence dans l’enseignement et justifier d’une expérience dans des thématiques liées à « Business and Society ». Une expérience en formation continue (executive education), ou un fort potentiel de contribution à ce type de programmes, est hautement souhaitable. La capacité à enseigner en anglais est requise. La connaissance du français constitue un atout.
Entrée en fonction
1er août 2027 ou date à convenir.
Contact
Les dossiers de candidature doivent inclure les documents suivants : une lettre de motivation, un CV avec une liste de publications, une copie des diplômes, une liste de personne de référence qui pourront être contactés directement par la commission (des lettres de recommandation ne sont pas demandées pour le moment). Les dossiers doivent être exclusivement en ligne en cliquant sur le bouton ci-dessous ‘Postuler / Apply now’. Aucun dossier reçu par email ou par courrier ne sera admis. Le dernier délai pour le dépôt des candidatures est fixé au 30.11.2026, minuit, heure de Genève.
Informations complémentaires
Des renseignements complémentaires peuvent être obtenus auprès du Professeur Sebastian Raisch : [email protected]

Dans une perspective de parité, l'Université encourage les candidatures du sexe sous-représenté.

The European University Institute (EUI) offers four-year fully-funded PhD programmes in Economics , History , Law and Political and Social Sciences . Up to 130 scholarships are available for entry in September 2027, covering tuition and providing a monthly grant.
Our well-structured PhD programmes include closely supervised dissertation work, courses on methods and theory, topical workshops, as well as academic and professional development training.
Why choose the EUI?
Critical thinking and multidisciplinary approaches
EUI offers a unique environment where multidisciplinary collaboration is central. Our PhD programmes empower researchers to address pressing social challenges by combining diverse perspectives and expertise.
Social impact beyond academia
At the EUI, your research extends far beyond academic circles. We prepare scholars to engage with the world, engaging politics and society. Research at EUI is relevant, outward-looking, and designed to shape sustainable futures.
A community of peers and support
With top-tier faculty, structured supervision, and an inspiring environment, the EUI is dedicated to your success. You’ll collaborate with practitioners, access unparalleled resources, and enjoy continuous training, allowing you to thrive in your PhD journey.
Intellectual freedom and academic integrity
The EUI upholds high standards of academic freedom and ethical research. Here, scholars explore and defend their work confidently, contributing responsibly to European and global debates.
Research opportunities across Europe and beyond
Rooted in Europe, the EUI's vision is global. Whether exploring European history, international law, or global political issues, the institute provides opportunities to make European impact.
Access to an international network
Our alumni hold posts in academia (66%), international organisations (8%), the private sector (5%), other research institutions (4%), European Union (3%), law firms (3%),
central banks (3%), national administration/government (2%), museums/archives/libraries (1.5%)*.
*Alumni Surveys
Application deadline: 15 January 2027 (14:00 CET)
To find out more and to apply online before the 15 January deadline, please visit: www.eui.eu/phd
About the EUI
The European University Institute is an international postgraduate teaching and research institute. It offers advanced academic training for doctoral and postdoctoral researchers and fosters research in fields that are of particular interest for the development of Europe. The Institute is composed of four departments—Economics, History, Law, and Political and Social Sciences—; the Robert Schuman Centre for Advanced Studies; the Max Weber Programme for Postdoctoral Studies; the School of Transnational Governance; and the Historical Archives of the European Union.
Grants and tuition fees for PhD candidates are covered by the national grant-awarding authorities of our contracting states.

ap:253679.body:
BI Norwegian Business School’s Department of Communication and Culture and Department of Law and Governance invite applications for a four-year doctoral scholarship focusing on outsider innovation, early-warning signals and regulatory foresight for transformative technologies. The expected start date is 1 January 2027, or upon agreement.
Position details
Location: BI Norwegian Business School, Oslo, Norway
Position: One PhD candidate position, full time, fixed-term contract of 48 months
Doctoral programme: PhD specialisation in Communication at BI Norwegian Business School
Application deadline: 15 November 2026 at 23:59 CET
Expected start: 1 January 2027, or upon agreement
About REGULAIRE
The scholarship is part of REGULAIRE (Regulatory Learning for the Governance of Transformative Technologies), a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network funded by the European Union under Horizon Europe. Coordinated by Professor Urs Gasser at the Technical University of Munich, with Professor Sebastian Schwemer as principal investigator at BI, the network brings together 15 doctoral candidates at ten European universities.
REGULAIRE studies how regulation can learn to govern transformative technologies such as AI, quantum computing and neurotechnology. Its projects examine how regulators recognise emerging problems, test interventions, develop institutional capacities and share lessons across organisations and jurisdictions. You will join an international cohort with supervision across institutions, joint training and collaboration with regulators, standardisation bodies and international organisations.
The doctoral project
Open-source communities, civic technologists, small and medium-sized enterprises and marginalised user groups often notice the risks and possibilities of new technologies before regulators do. This doctoral project, “Outside-In Signals: Outsider Innovation as Foresight Infrastructure”, examines how these actors generate early insights, why institutions sometimes overlook them, and how their knowledge can inform regulatory foresight.
You will investigate where outsider innovators sit in networks and geographical settings, how signals emerge through sources such as issue trackers and incident reports, and how authorities assess their relevance. Possible approaches include case studies, interviews, document analysis and network analysis. The project also involves developing and testing routines through which authorities can receive, assess and escalate outsider inputs while preserving legality and proportionality.
The research is expected to produce a typology of outsider signals, a curated dataset and codebook, and tested procedures for translating signals into regulatory review. It will also develop guidance on maintaining channels through which outsider knowledge can inform ongoing foresight. The successful candidate will develop an independent PhD project within this theme and contribute to REGULAIRE’s interdisciplinary research agenda.
Research environment and supervision
You will be based in BI’s Department of Communication and Culture and also affiliated with the Department of Law and Governance. Communication and Culture is an international research environment working on communication technologies, online communities, digital transformation and the social legitimacy of technological change. Law and Governance contributes expertise in national and European regulation of markets and technology, digital governance and public policy.
You will also join BI’s Nordic Centre for Internet and Society (NCIS), an interdisciplinary research centre studying how emerging internet technologies affect working life and society.
Your main supervisor will be Professor Christian Fieseler (BI), with Professor Sebastian Schwemer as co-supervisor at BI and Sandra Cortesi at the Technical University of Munich as the international academic co-supervisor. A sectoral mentor will support the secondment.
You will meet your main supervisor at least monthly and the full supervisory team at least four times a year. Your progress and training will be recorded in a personal Career Development Plan.
Training and secondment
Network training includes three residential summer schools, covering regulatory learning and foresight at TUM, methods and analytics at BI, and academic writing and impact at the University of St. Gallen. You will also take part in methods workshops, monthly paper development seminars and annual network reviews. This training complements the coursework and other requirements of BI’s doctoral programme.
The project includes a planned three-month intersectoral secondment, providing opportunities to work with foresight practitioners on emerging technological signals and ways to bring outsider insights into regulatory decisions. The host, timing and detailed arrangements will be confirmed with the supervisory team.
Your work
Refine the research questions and design with the supervisory team.
Collect, manage and analyse research material using methods appropriate to the project.
Complete a doctoral thesis and related research publications, and communicate findings to academic and practitioner audiences.
Participate in local and network training, cohort activities, reviews and practitioner engagement, including the summer schools and planned secondment.
Contribute to teaching or other career-promoting duties as part of the four-year appointment.

Your profile
Applicants must hold, or complete by the start date, a relevant two-year master’s degree or comparable qualification that meets BI’s PhD entry requirements . The qualifying degree must include thesis work, normally 15–30 ECTS, and applicants must have a grade point average of B or higher, equivalent to 4 on BI’s five-point scale. An MBA does not qualify for admission.
Relevant backgrounds include communication and media studies, innovation studies, science and technology studies, information systems, sociology, political science, law, public administration, or related interdisciplinary fields.
An interest in outsider innovation, open-source communities, civic technology, or how regulators identify and assess emerging technological risks would be an advantage. Relevant experience may include foresight, digital governance, risk communication, interviews, case studies, document analysis, network analysis, or other qualitative and quantitative methods. You are not expected to have experience in all these areas.
We are looking for strong analytical and academic writing skills, the ability to work independently and systematically, and a willingness to collaborate across disciplines. Excellent written and spoken English and fulfilment of the MSCA eligibility conditions below are required.
Employment and support
The appointment is a full-time, four-year position based in Oslo. The annual salary is currently NOK 623,200 gross and will be adjusted in accordance with applicable regulations. The position normally offers membership in BI’s collective pension scheme. Twenty-five per cent of working time is allocated to teaching or other career-promoting duties; 36 research months are funded through REGULAIRE.
MSCA funding also provides support for mobility and, where applicable, family allowances under the grant rules. BI will confirm the applicable arrangements as part of the employment terms. You will have access to the network’s research, training and networking activities.
MSCA eligibility
Applicants may be of any nationality. On the first day of MSCA employment, the selected candidate must meet the following conditions:
Not hold a doctoral degree. Applicants who have successfully defended a doctoral thesis are ineligible even if the degree has not yet been formally awarded.
Not have resided or carried out their main activity, such as work or study, in Norway for more than 12 months during the preceding 36 months. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent in a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are excluded.
Be enrolled in, or meet the conditions for timely enrolment in, BI’s doctoral programme.

Appointment is conditional on documentary verification of these conditions and fulfilment of BI’s admission requirements. See the official MSCA Doctoral Networks guidance for further information.
How to apply
Submit your application through the “Send application” button on this vacancy’s page in BI’s electronic recruitment system. Please consult BI’s PhD application guidance and upload the following:
A cover letter explaining your motivation and relevant qualifications, identifying REGULAIRE DC03.
A CV, including publications and other relevant research activities, where applicable.
An original five-page project proposal addressing this doctoral project, including the research topic, proposed methods, schedule and relevant literature. Any use of generative AI to produce text must be clearly stated and cited.
Bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates and transcripts, with a Diploma Supplement or equivalent explanation of the study and grading system and eligibility for further study. Include other relevant certificates and transcripts.
At least two recommendation letters from relevant employers, professors or supervisors providing evidence of your research potential.
BI’s signed verification document .
Documentation of English proficiency, or an English test waiver application with supporting evidence, where required.
Certificates and the course approval form for previously completed doctoral courses, if you wish to request recognition of these courses.

Applicants still completing their master’s degree should upload their latest transcript and state their expected completion date. The qualifying degree must be completed before the appointment begins.
All application documents must be submitted through the electronic system, not by email. Documents received after the deadline will not be considered, except for the final master’s certificate where the degree is being completed shortly before the agreed start date. Applications cannot be revised after submission. Candidates may be asked for further information or invited to an interview.
English language requirements
BI normally accepts native English speakers, applicants with a qualifying master’s degree from a Nordic institution, and applicants whose qualifying master’s degree was taught in English as meeting its English-language requirement. Other applicants must normally provide TOEFL or IELTS results, or apply for a waiver.
BI’s published minimum is IELTS 6.5 or TOEFL iBT 90 on the 0–120 scale, with results from the preceding two years. Consult BI’s PhD entry requirements for current score requirements, accepted documentation and reporting instructions. TOEFL results should be sent directly to BI using institution code 0529; IELTS copies are accepted when the TRF number is visible. GMAT or GRE may be requested in particular cases; BI will inform applicants if required.
Contact
For questions about this doctoral project or the PhD specialisation in Communication, contact Professor Christian Fieseler at [email protected] .
For questions about REGULAIRE at BI, contact Professor Sebastian Schwemer at [email protected] .
For questions about admission requirements and the application process, contact BI’s PhD Administration at [email protected] . Further information about the network is available at REGULAIRE .
REGULAIRE is funded by the European Union under the Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions, Grant Agreement No. 101312218.

Regulation accumulates over time, but institutions’ capacity to revise or retire rules that no longer serve their purpose does not always keep pace. About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine.
Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in.
Your role
Determine the specific impact of Wnt signalling on C2C12 progenitors and differentiation
Develop dedicated BRET biosensors to measure intracellular protein-protein interactions in the Wnt pathway
Investigate the impact of developed peptidic ligands on Wnt/β-catenin signalling and differentiation in C2C12 cells
Measure: cellular differentiation, signalling responses and β-catenin localisation
Build: BRET biosensors for target engagement and molecular events
Integrate: cellular read-outs with ligand optimisation in the wider FlexCAT programme

β-catenin is a central regulator of cell differentiation and stemness. Aberrant Wnt/β-catenin activity can drive developmental defects and cancer. This project tests whether context-specific peptidic ligands targeting β-catenin can restore aberrant differentiation. Using C2C12 myoblasts, you will combine cellular differentiation assays, signalling and confocal localisation studies with dedicated BRET biosensors to measure intracellular protein-protein interactions and target engagement. The resulting mechanistic read-outs will feed back into iterative β-catenin ligand optimisation within FlexCAT.
Your profile
MSc in Biochemistry, Developmental Biology, Biophysical Chemistry or a related field, with excellent results, qualifying for doctoral admission
Good knowledge of molecular biochemistry, fluorescence microscopy and/or bioluminescence experiments applied to cell biology
Basic cell-culture skills; experience with cellular differentiation models is an asset
Strong project organisation, communication and collaborative skills
MSCA mobility rule: normally no more than 12 months of residence/main activity in the recruiting country during the 36 months before recruitment
Motivation for multidisciplinary international research, hands-on experimental work, secondment, publications, conferences and dissemination
Operational Language Requirements: Excellent knowledge of English is required

Academic Eligibility (Thesis) :

ap:253692.body:
Turn groundbreaking 3D integration technologies into a manufacturing-ready platform for next-generation semiconductor products.
Advanced packaging is reshaping how complex semiconductor systems are designed and manufactured. At IC-Link by imec, you will lead the integration of technologies such as silicon interposers, fine-pitch microbumps, redistribution layers, through-silicon vias and advanced bonding technologies into a coherent platform for prototyping and manufacturing.
You will work at the intersection of technology development, semiconductor manufacturing, design enablement and the global packaging supply chain. Your goal will be clear: make imec's originated advanced 3D integration technologies ready for reliable use by customers and manufacturing partners.
IC-Link by imec is imec's chip development and manufacturing services division. We help start-ups, universities, SMEs and established technology companies move from an innovative chip concept to a qualified, manufacturable product. Our services cover chip design, packaging, testing, qualification and supply chain management.
What you will do
As Advanced 3D Packaging Integration Lead, you will define and drive the technical roadmap for IC-Link imec’s 3D packaging platform, bringing advanced integration technologies from development into manufacturing-ready solutions.
More specifically, you will:
Lead the development and industrialization of imec's advanced 3D packaging platform in current and future semiconductor fabrication facilities.
Define and optimize integration flows for technologies such as silicon interposers, microbumps, redistribution layers, through-silicon vias, die-to-wafer bonding and wafer-to-wafer bonding.
Drive platform readiness through test vehicles, customer programs and continuous process improvements.
Ensure that process design kits and assembly design guidelines are developed and maintained to support successful platform adoption.
Align the platform with the broader manufacturing ecosystem, including fab, test and outsourced assembly and test partners.
Collaborate with experts across process integration, design, manufacturing, testing and reliability to resolve technical challenges and support industrialization.
Represent imec towards customers and partners by presenting the platform roadmap, benchmarking industry developments and supporting technology transfers to manufacturing partners.

What we do for you
We offer you the opportunity to join one of the world’s premier research centers in nanotechnology at its headquarters in Leuven, Belgium. With your talent, passion and expertise, you’ll become part of a team that makes the impossible possible. Together, we shape the technology that will determine the society of tomorrow.
We are committed to being an inclusive employer and proud of our open, multicultural, and informal working environment with ample possibilities to take initiative and show responsibility. We commit to supporting and guiding you in this process; not only with words but also with tangible actions. Through imec.academy, 'our corporate university', we actively invest in your development to further your technical and personal growth.
We are aware that your valuable contribution makes imec a top player in its field. Your energy and commitment are therefore appreciated by means of a market appropriate salary with many fringe benefits.
Who you are
You are an experienced semiconductor professional who combines deep technical expertise with the ability to guide multidisciplinary teams and engage confidently with customers and manufacturing partners.
To succeed in this role, you bring:
A master's degree or PhD in semiconductor engineering, microelectronics, materials science, electrical engineering or a related field.
More than 10 years of relevant experience in a semiconductor foundry, manufacturing or advanced packaging environment.
Strong experience with wafer-level 3D integration and advanced packaging process flows.
Practical knowledge of technologies such as redistribution layers, microbumps, silicon interposers, through-silicon vias, die-to-wafer bonding or wafer-to-wafer bonding.
The ability to discuss complex process and integration challenges with fab engineers, designers, test specialists and manufacturing partners.
Experience translating technology development into manufacturing requirements and roadmap decisions.
Strong stakeholder management and project leadership skills.
The confidence to represent imec in customer meetings and discussions with international semiconductor partners.
Excellent written and spoken English.

Experience working with outsourced semiconductor assembly and test partners is strongly valued. Familiarity with electronic design automation tools and the development or use of process design kits is considered an advantage.
You do not need to have experience with every technology listed above . What matters most is that you understand advanced semiconductor integration, can connect expertise across disciplines and know how to move a complex technology platform towards manufacturing.

Job description
Come join IMT Mines Alès, a prestigious “grande école” ranked among the top engineering schools both nationally and globally, located in Alès—a welcoming, livable city and the capital of the Cévennes region, where residents highly value the quality of life.
Founded in 1843, IMT Mines Alès currently has 1,400 students (including 250 international students) and 380 staff members. The school has three high-level scientific and technological research and teaching centers, working in the fields of materials and civil engineering (C2MA), the environment and risk management (CREER), and artificial intelligence and industrial and digital engineering (CERIS). It operates 12 technology platforms and has 1,600 partner companies. For more information: https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr
You will be affiliated with the Center for Research and Teaching in Environment and Risks (CREER) at IMT Mines Alès and the HSM research unit.
This work is part of the PREV’IA project, which focuses on understanding and forecasting water resources in the Pliocene-Quaternary aquifer of the Roussillon Plain and the Lez spring that supplies Montpellier with drinking water.
Your work will build upon an ongoing thesis within the UMR HSM (HYTAKE team), focusing on the sustainability of the karst water resource (Lez aquifer) supplying a Mediterranean metropolis (Montpellier) in the context of climate change.
Your mission:
Use emerging concepts in “Physics-Informed Machine Learning” (PIML) approaches to assess the potential benefits of synergy in hydrogeological modeling: (1) concept-based modeling on the one hand, and (2) neural networks informed by, or complemented with, physics on the other. The PIML (Physics Informed Machine Learning) approach is being developed along two lines: (i) Physics Informed Architecture (PIA): integration of physical knowledge into the model architecture (hidden layers); and (ii) Physics Informed Loss Function (PILF): combining physical modeling (differential equations) and black-box methods, merged into the cost function (regularization term). Both methods may be explored. The proposed models may be used to determine the evolution of certain hydrological variables in response to climate change.

Description de l'offre d'emploi
Venez rejoindre l'IMT Mines Alès, grande école de prestige qui se classe parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs sur le plan national et mondial et implantée à Alès, ville à taille humaine, capitale des Cévennes où la qualité de vie est fortement appréciée par ses habitants.
Créée en 1843, IMT Mines Alès compte à ce jour 1400 élèves (dont 250 étrangers) et 380 personnels. L’école dispose de 3 centres de recherche et d’enseignement de haut niveau scientifique et technologique, qui œuvrent dans les domaines des matériaux et du génie civil (C2MA), de l’environnement et des risques (CREER), de l’intelligence artificielle et du génie industriel et numérique (CERIS). Elle dispose de 12 plateformes technologiques et compte 1600 entreprises partenaires. Pour en savoir plus : https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr
Vous êtes rattaché(e) au Centre de Recherche et d’Enseignement en Environnement et Risques (CREER) de l'IMT Mines Alès et dans l'unité de recherche : HSM.
Ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet PREV’IA qui s’intéresse à la connaissance et à la prévision des ressources en eaux de la nappe plioquaternaire de la plaine de Roussillon, et de la source du Lez qui alimente Montpellier en eau potable.
Votre travail s’inscrira dans la continuité d’une thèse en cours au sein de l’UMR HSM (équipe HYTAKE), portant sur la durabilité de la ressource en eau karstique (aquifère du Lez) alimentant une métropole méditerranéenne (Montpellier) en contexte de changement climatique.
Votre mission :
Utiliser les concepts émergeants dans les approches de « Physics Informed Machine Learning » (PIML) pour évaluer les intérêts d’une synergie en modélisation hydrogéologique : (1) à base conceptuelle d’une part et (2) à base de réseaux de neurones informés, ou complémentés, par la physique. L’approche PIML (Physics Informed Machine Learning) est développée, avec deux courants : (i) les Physics Informed Architecture (PIA) : intégration de connaissances physiques dans l’architecture du modèle (couches cachées) ; et (ii) les Physics Informed Loss Function (PILF) : combinaison de modélisations physiques (équations différentielles) et boîte noire, fusionnées dans la fonction de coût (terme de régularisation). Les deux méthodes pourront être explorées. Les modèles proposés pourront être utilisés pour déterminer l’évolution de certaines grandeurs hydrologiques en réponse au changement climatique.

Description de l'offre d'emploi
IMT Atlantique , reconnue internationalement pour la qualité de sa recherche, est une école d’ingénieurs de premier plan sous la tutelle du ministère de l'industrie et du numérique, classée dans les trois principaux classements internationaux (THE, SHANGHAI, QS).
Le poste est ouvert sur le campus de Rennes au sein du département SRCD (Systèmes Réseaux, Cybersécurité et Droit du numérique) . Le département SRCD est composé de 24 enseignant.e.s-chercheurs.euses permanent.e.s, plus de 10 post-doctorant.e.s et ingénieur.e.s contractuel.le.s, et 30 doctorant.e.s. Ses domaines d'activité recouvrent tous les aspects de l'enseignement et de la recherche en systèmes et réseaux au sens large, en cybersécurité, et en droit et économie des activités numériques. Dans le cadre de ses activités de recherche, la personne recrutée rejoindra l’équipe SOTERN (Self Protecting the Future Internet) du département D2 du laboratoire IRISA (UMR CNRS 6074), l'un des plus grands laboratoires de recherche français (+ de 850 personnes) dans le domaine de l'informatique et des nouvelles technologies de l'information.
Enjeux et profil attendu sur le thématique de recherche
Deux enjeux majeurs présentent actuellement un impact conséquent sur la recherche et l’innovation en Cybersécurité. D’un côté, l’intelligence artificielle par ses développements récents et les attendus pour les années à venir décuple les possibilités offertes aux attaquants pour mettre en œuvre de nouvelles attaques, tout autant qu’aux structures défensives (type SOC par exemple) pour détecter, corréler et contrer des incidents de sécurité. D’un autre côté, les cibles des attaques évoluent et les architectures déployées dans les réseaux opérationnels (systèmes industriels, réseaux intra-véhiculaires, avionique, opérateurs d’importance vitale) nécessitent de nouveaux moyens de détection et protection face à une menace grandissante.
Le profil recherché pour ce poste s’inscrit ainsi dans la thématique de la sécurité des réseaux au sens large. Il sera plus spécifiquement recherché soit une expertise relative aux architectures, protocoles et algorithmes d’intelligence artificielle pour la sécurité des réseaux ou de l’IA (apprentissage fédéré, sécurité des architectures d’IA type Model Context Protocol (MCP), etc.), soit une expertise sur la sécurité des réseaux opérationnels (OT) quel qu’en soit le cadre applicatif.
Enjeux et profil attendu en enseignement
Positionnée sur 3 campus attractifs, IMT Atlantique affiche une forte dynamique internationale tout en restant à taille humaine. Dans ces différents cursus BAC+5 (formations d’ingénieurs et de masters-DNM), les étudiants sont confrontés, via des approches pédagogiques variées, à des situations-problèmes concrets. L’école a ainsi pour ambition de former de jeunes professionnels à fort potentiel, capables de mobiliser un large spectre de compétences en situation réelle, dans des environnements (production, recherche, création d’activité, etc.) et des domaines socio-économiques variés.
Impliqué tant en tronc commun que dans les parcours électifs, la personne recrutée contribuera aussi bien dans sa spécialité Cybersécurité que dans des activités transverses, interdisciplinaires ou en lien avec des entreprises : tutorat de projets / stages, soutenances, accompagnement, etc. La personne recrutée sera encouragée à contribuer, dans un esprit de collaboration, à l’évolution cohérente des programmes d’études, en proposant de nouveaux projets, programmes et méthodologies pédagogiques, particulièrement inspirés et soutenus par les exigences et les partenariats industriels. https://www.imt-atlantique.fr/fr/formation
En cohérence avec le profil de la personne candidate, il sera demandé de prendre en main les thématiques d’enseignement parmi les suivantes : IA et Cybersécurité (IA offensive, IA pour la protection des infrastructures, sécurité de l’IA), Sécurité des systèmes industriels, participation puis prise de responsabilité de l’organisation du CTF Hack’lantique, et plus largement une participation aux différents enseignements en Cybersécurité.
Responsabilité collective et implication dans le développement économique
En effet une attention particulière sera portée sur la capacité du candidat à s’impliquer dans la vie collective de l’école : contribuer, ou piloter des projets transverses (par exemple sur la transition écologique, prendre des responsabilités (programmes de formation, projets de recherche, équipes pédagogiques ou de recherche) ou participer à des instances : comité de l’enseignement, conseil d’école, comité social d’administration.
En outre dans un environnement de relations privilégiées avec de grands partenaires industriels nationaux et internationaux, ainsi qu’un réseau dense de PME, Start up, l’enseignant chercheur recruté contribuera au rayonnement de l’école et au développement économique, notamment au travers de la valorisation de ses travaux par le dépôt de brevet ou le transfert de technologies. Avec 257 enseignants-chercheurs permanents, 2450 étudiants dont 399 doctorants, IMT Atlantique produit chaque année 655 publications et lève 28.3M€ de fonds de recherche.

ap:253700.body:
Resilient Distributed ISAC for UAV Communication and Localization

This PhD project develops and experimentally validates resilient communication and localization methods for UAVs in dynamic, congested and adversarial electromagnetic environments, including 5G/6G systems. Research covers spectrum and spatial sensing, interference management, adaptive beamforming, distributed antenna arrays, synchronization, ISAC and AI-assisted signal processing. Algorithms will be evaluated with software-defined radios, antenna hardware and over-the-air field measurements.

The project will address the following key areas:
Unmanned Aerial Vehicle (UAV) communication systems must operate reliably in dynamic, congested and potentially adversarial electromagnetic environments. The increasing use of higher-frequency bands, 5G/6G technologies, distributed antenna systems, advanced beamforming and integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) creates new opportunities for improving link reliability, while introducing challenges related to propagation, blockage, interference, synchronization, hardware impairments and system integration.
The research aims to develop and experimentally validate methods for improving the resilience of UAV communication under realistic operating conditions. Resilience includes the ability to detect changing electromagnetic conditions, maintain communication and localization performance, adapt to interference or blockage, tolerate hardware and synchronization imperfections.
Potential research topics include spectrum and spatial sensing, interference and coexistence management, adaptive beamforming and distributed antenna arrays, synchronization and calibration, communication-assisted localization, ISAC, fault-tolerant communications, AI/ML-assisted signal processing, and resilient multi-UAV communication. The selection and emphasis of individual topics may evolve with technological developments and emerging research opportunities.
A particular emphasis will be placed on bridging theoretical and simulation-based research with practical implementation and reproducible measurement. Selected algorithms and architectures will be evaluated using software-defined radio, antenna/array hardware, over-the-air (OTA) and field measurements. The research will investigate how realistic propagation conditions and hardware imperfections affect resilience and how simulation and experimental models can be reconciled.
The expected outcome is a set of scientifically validated methods, models and evaluation methodologies for designing and assessing resilient UAV communication links

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
Undertake research for specific doctoral research project.
Present and publish research in both academic and non-academic audiences. Attend and participate in academic and non-academic conferences, events and seminars.
Full-time employment (40 hours per week), temporary contract for 3 years.
The above job descriptions are not exhaustive, the PhD candidate may be required to undertake other tasks, which are broadly in line with the above duties and responsibilities.

Applicants should fulfil the following requirements:
The candidate should hold a master’s degree (or equivalent) in telecommunication, electronics, or in a related field of electrical engineering.
Excellent command of written and spoken English.
Strong analytical thinking, teamwork, and communication skills (written and oral) are required.
Motivation to work in an interdisciplinary, innovation-driven research environment is essential.

The following experience is beneficial:
A strong foundation in communication engineering and signal processing.
Experience in publishing articles and technical reports.
Experience in writing flight test protocols and following them through.
Experience with experimental design and controlled testing of algorithms or systems.
Familiarity with modern drone communication technologies.
Ability to develop quantitative metrics for evaluating algorithm performance and operational limitations.

We offer:
Full-time employment.
Access to laboratory facilities and equipment for numerical, laboratory and flight testing.
Opportunity to work with UAV-based experimental platforms and relevant communication technologies.
Practical experience in designing, constructing and validating experimental test equipment.
Support for publishing scientific articles and presenting research results at conferences

Supervisors:
Main supervisor: Senior Lecturer Ivo Müürsepp, School of Information Technologies: Thomas Johann Seebeck Department of Electronics: Communication System Research Group
Co-Supervisor: Researcher Ahti Ainomäe, Metrosert AS

Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) is an international scientific community with approximately 9,000 students and 2,000 employees; it is one of the largest universities in Estonia, the leading EU country in digitalisation. The university's strengths are broad multidisciplinary study/research interests, a modern research environment, and strong collaboration with international educational and research institutions. TalTech is aiming to be an organisation leading the way to a sustainable digital future.
The Drone Technologies Unit of Metrosert AS is interested in the research of interference-resilient distributed array systems and reproducible OTA validation for reliable UAV links in electromagnetically congested environments, where interference from coexisting services is both unavoidable and potentially adversarial. The scientific core is distributed wireless communication/sensing systems (i.e. the concept of Integrated Sensing and Communication (ISAC)) such as UAV distributed arrays, hybrid ground-air arrays, and distributed Multiple-Input-Multiple-Output (MIMO) arrays for 5G/6G communications.

ap:253702.body:
Universal properties in double category theory

The objective of this position is to advance the understanding of universal properties in double category theory and to demonstrate applications in theoretical computer science. Topics may include loose universal properties, two-dimensional sketches, double-categorical enrichment, and formal category theory.

The project will address the following key areas:
Double categories provide a unified framework for the study of both functional and relational structure, jointly generalising the classical notions of 2-category and bicategory in two-dimensional category theory. Double category theory is becoming an increasingly useful tool in both mathematics and theoretical computer science, for instance in the development of two-dimensional methods for scientific modelling and in the study of systems theories. However, the general theory of double categories is still nascent, and there remain fundamental questions about the nature of double categories.
The goal of this project is to advance the theory of double categories and to demonstrate applications in theoretical computer science. Depending on the interests and background of the candidate, topics may include loose universal properties, two-dimensional sketches, double-categorical enrichment, and formal category theory. We envision the project to extend the existing theory of 2-categories and bicategories, as well as to develop entirely new methods in study of low-dimensional higher category theory.

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
The student’s primary responsibility is research on this PhD project.
The student may have to contribute to the teaching activities of the lab as a course assistant.

Applicants should fulfil the following requirements:
A strong knowledge of basic category theory and an interest in theoretical computer science. Applicants from under-represented and diverse backgrounds are particularly encouraged to apply.

The following experience is beneficial:
Experience in two-dimensional category theory is beneficial.

We offer:
We offer a fully funded PhD position for 48 months in a vibrant research environment. The gross salary is 2300 EUR/month, which ensures a good living standard in Estonia. The start date is negotiable.

Supervisors:
Main supervisor: Researcher Bryce James Clarke, School of Information Technologies: Department of Software Science: High-assurance Software Laboratory
Co-Supervisor: Researcher Nathanael Amariah Arkor, School of Information Technologies: Department of Software Science: High-assurance Software Laboratory

Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) is an international scientific community with approximately 9,000 students and 2,000 employees; it is one of the largest universities in Estonia, the leading EU country in digitalisation. The university's strengths are broad multidisciplinary study/research interests, a modern research environment, and strong collaboration with international educational and research institutions. TalTech is aiming to be an organisation leading the way to a sustainable digital future.
The Department of Software Science is a leading computer science department in Estonia. In particular, we are strong in programming language theory, logic, type theory, category theory. The relevant labs are the High-Assurance Software Laboratory, incl the Logic and Semantics Group , and the Lab for Compositional Systems and Methods . We have a number of PhD students working in these domains, we collaborate with many European centers, receive many visitors.
For information about the admission process, please visit the PhD Admission homepage

Applications can be submitted from 01.10.2026 to 10.11.2026

ap:253717.body:
THE POSITIONS
emlyon business school invites applications for the following full-time Faculty positions:
A full-time position in Supply Chain & Operations Management at Associate Level - Teaching-Oriented Profile
A full-time position in Applied Mathematics and Statistics at Associate / Full professor Level or Professor of Practice - Teaching-Oriented Profile
A full-time position in Finance at Associate / Full professor Level, hybrid teaching & research-oriented position
Full-time Faculty position in Organizational Behavior at Associate / Full professor Level - Teaching-Oriented Profile

Appointments are made at full Professor, Associate and Assistant level depending on research, teaching record and business experience.
All these positions are based in  France (Lyon - Paris)
Rank of appointment and salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience. Salary and conditions will be competitive with leading European Business Schools
Successful candidates are expected to start by  September 1, 2027.
We strongly encourage people of all backgrounds (gender, ethnic background, nationality) to apply.
The selected candidate is expected to  be based in Lyon or nearby area . emlyon business school has set-up a relocation policy to support the moving process.

THE SCHOOL
Founded in 1872, emlyon business school is one of the oldest business schools in Europe. It belongs to the top 1% of business schools worldwide recognized by the triple accreditation: EQUIS, AACSB, and AMBA.
emlyon business school welcomes 9,260 students from 130 nationalities across its three campuses in Lyon, Shanghai, and Paris. The School relies on a Faculty of 174 international professors and researchers, as well as a network of 220 academic partners, to deliver top-quality trainings recognized in the world’s best rankings. It boasts a community of 48,000 alumni.
As a Mission-driven company since 2021, emlyon business school cultivates the ability to drive change in resonance with the world by placing the hybridization of skills with social and environmental responsibility at the core of its training programs, supported by teaching methods that combine action and thinking. emlyon has endorsed the European Charter for researchers and is awarded HR excellence in research by the European Commission. The HR Strategy for Researchers (HRS4R) is available at the following link:  https://em-lyon.com/en/faculty-and-research/hr-strategy-for-researchers
THE ENVIRONMENT
emlyon  business school is at the center of a vibrant ecosystem of large universities with excellent research teams in engineering, computer science, natural sciences, social sciences, and the humanities (see:  https://www.lyoncampus.com/en/welcome/lyon-a-city-of-innovation )
Lyon is the second largest city in France, with a long entrepreneurship tradition and a solid digital industry.
Further information
About  emlyon  business school:  http://www.em-lyon.com/en/

THE APPLICATION SHOULD CONSIST OF
A cover letter including the motivation to join emlyon business school
An up-to-date curriculum vitae
A research statement
A teaching statement (with teaching evaluations, where available)
A list of papers under review or in progress
Two references/names with contact information

All application materials should be submitted in English. The application materials will not be returned.
Candidates are strongly encouraged to apply as soon as possible as review of applications will begin immediately.
Interested candidates should apply electronically through emlyon business school recruitment webpage:
HERE
RECRUITMENT PROCESS
emlyon business school complies with the Open, Transparent and Merit-based Recruitment principles as stated in the European Code of Conduct for the recruitment of researchers.
The selection committee is appointed by the Head of department and composed of three to eight professors, ensuring a balanced representation of gender, national origin, and professor grades.
Pre-selection step: the selection committee reviews all the applications to short-list the candidates who meet the most criteria as described in the candidate’s characteristics.
Short-listed candidates are invited to a recruitment day (held by videoconference in most cases) with:   a) a job talk presentation
b) one-on-one interviews with committee members.

Each permanent professor attending the job talk completes an assessment grid, and the results are aggregated to identify the top one and top two applicants. Finalists are interviewed by the Dean for Faculty & Research and/or the Associate Dean for Research. The final decision is communicated by the Dean for Faculty & Research.
