ap:253858.body:
About the FHSE
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Humanities, Education and Social Sciences (FHSE) at the University of Luxembourg brings together expertise from the humanities, linguistics, cognitive sciences, social and educational sciences.
People from across 20 disciplines are working within the Faculty . Along with the disciplinary approach a very ambitious interdisciplinary research culture has been developed. The faculty's research and teaching focuses on social, economic, political and educational issues with the common goal of contributing to an inclusive, open and resourceful society.
The research project PALATE (Participatory Actions for Lifestyle Adaptation & Transition Engagement) explores how participatory governance structures, food democracy initiatives and multi-stakeholder collaboration contribute to sustainable food-system transformation in Luxembourg. The project seeks to generate actionable knowledge for policymakers, practitioners and civil society while advancing scientific understanding of food sovereignty, food governance and sustainability transitions. It contributes to Social Readiness withing the overall Climate Nexus Framework, by examining food-related behavioural change and participatory transitions toward sustainable lifestyles.
Your role
Conduct an original PhD research project leading to a doctoral degree
Carry out literature reviews on food literacy, sustainable consumption and behavioural change
Design and implement qualitative and mixed-methods research
Conduct interviews, focus groups, participant observation and surveys
Analyse qualitative and quantitative datasets
Contribute to stakeholder workshops and co-creation activities
Publish scientific articles in peer-reviewed journals
Participate in doctoral training activities and the University's doctoral programme
Contribute to project reports, policy briefs and dissemination activities

Your profile
Master's degree in Sociology, Cultural Anthropology, Political Sciences, History and/or Geography in the field of food studies or related study areas
Experience in research project management and conduct, ideally in interdisciplinary contexts
In-depth knowledge of Luxembourg's foodscape, both of the existing interrelations and the cultural and socio-economic stakes, is a prerequisite
Previous research work on sustainable food practices and system is a plus
Experience and excellent skills in qualitative methods, e.g., individual and group interviews, oral history, ethnography, participant observation, focus groups, as well as good knowledge of quantitative methods - descriptive statistics
Interest in food studies, transformative research, agroecological and food system transition studies, practice theory, political ecology, theory of change, as well as governance, governmentality and policy coherence approaches
Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English is required

Academic Eligibility (Thesis):
Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover letter presenting your motivation for this doctoral thesis topic, and explaining how your qualifications and aspirations align with its academic focus
Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. In line with our values, the University of Luxembourg promotes an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are dedicated to upholding equality and respect for our employees and students.
General information:
Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract 36 Month
Work Hours: Full Time 40.0 Hours per Week
Location: Belval Campus
Internal Title: Doctoral Researcher
Job Reference: UOL08510

The yearly gross salary for every Doctoral researcher at the UL is EUR 44531 (full time).

ap:253860.body:
Are you a professional looking for your next challenges? Are you all about science and technology or passionate about business and people? Would you like to collaborate with superb colleagues who are top experts in their field? Do you want to work with fascinating projects in state-of-the-art facilities? VTT might be just the place for you.
VTT is one of the leading applied research organisations in Europe. What unites us are curiosity, a passion for learning, and a purpose: to solve the biggest challenges of our time and turn them into sustainable growth and well-being. Our cross-disciplinary community of over 2000 brilliant minds from 55+ different nationalities focus on creating impact through science-based innovation. VTT’s research, development and innovation activities are divided into two business areas in which we develop solutions for companies and society: Digital systems and Materials and energy. In addition, we have Customer operations, Digital transformation, Incubation and strategy, Finance and services, People and Culture and Communications and brand units. Get to know us further by exploring  VTT's tech & infra .
We're excited to explore opportunities together!
We aim to review open applications on a regular basis and as we open new positions. If we spot a potential opportunity for you, we will reach out to you to continue the discussion. If you are applying for research and science opportunities, you can investigate which of our research topics and areas speaks most to you  from VTT's Research Information Portal  or  from VTT's tech & infra . Once you have identified your specific area of interest, you can mention it in the application form to ease identifying new opportunities.
Submit an open application, and make an impact for a brighter future!
If you are a student looking for new opportunities, please  Join our student talent pool!
Opportunities in research and science:
We offer long-term positions and flexible career paths in top-level research. People tend to stay with us for over ten years, as you can advance to different roles and responsibilities within VTT. At VTT, researchers have the flexibility and independence to affect the content of their work. Combining cutting-edge academic research and applied customer projects keeps your career path interesting.
Digital technologies
We develop breakthrough digital technologies and systems to enable a safe, connected and resilient society. Digital systems business area includes the following research areas: Digital infrastructures, Physical AI, Flexible electronics and human sensing, Quantum, Microelectronics and photonics, Microfabrication, and National metrology institute VTT MIKES.
Materials and energy
We develop sustainable materials, processes and energy solutions to accelerate the green transition and the renewal of industries and society. Materials and energy business area includes the following research areas: Advanced bio-based materials, Materials intelligence, Regenerative living and transport, Nuclear energy, Energy, Industrial chemistry, and Industrial biotechnology and food.
Read more about our services: All VTT's services .
Opportunities in customer operations, digital transformation and other support functions:
Working as part of our enabling functions, you’ll get to use your professional expertise to help solve the greatest challenges of our time through science and innovation. You’ll get to do your part in driving this meaningful change through your professional skills.
We have a large pool of professionals supporting the execution of high-quality research. Our Customer operations unit employs professionals in sales, marketing, commercial excellence and customer partnerships. Our Digital transformation unit employs professionals who advance VTT’s digital transformation and accelerate the use of AI, data and digital solutions in research and business operations. In our support functions , including Incubation and strategy, Finance and services, People and culture, and Communications and brand, we employ professionals in areas such as strategy, business incubation, finance, legal services, procurement, human resources, communications, branding and administration.
With VTT, you’ll enjoy:
Science with an impact.  At VTT, we seek to solve significant societal challenges and drive a sustainable future through applied research and innovation. With us, you'll get to work on projects that make a concrete, positive impact on the world. Read more about our strategy,  Chain reaction for growth , and  our organisational culture  as we build the world’s most meaningful place to work.
An open culture of innovation.  We have over 80 years of experience in science-based innovation, a solid international reputation, and global networks. We work across disciplines and house all the cutting-edge sciences, from quantum computing to synthetic biology, under one roof. At VTT, you'll join a community of over 2000 multidisciplinary experts who foster a culture of trust, openness, and knowledge-sharing. Collaborating with amazing colleagues is a source of learning, inspiration, and fun.
Nordic work–life balance.  Working in Finland, the world's happiest country enables an excellent quality of life. At VTT, we make our people's well-being a strategic priority. We offer six weeks of paid vacation a year after one year of employment. Our benefits include comprehensive occupational healthcare and a range of well-being services, such as exercise, culture benefits, and hobby clubs. If you are an international talent searching for a new opportunity, read more about the benefits of living in Finland and VTT's support for relocation here .

Apply now and join our community of brilliant minds!
Please write a short summary your key expertise and the roles that you are interested in the fee description box, attach your CV and answer a few short/multiple choice questions to apply for our open opportunities. You can also attach a PDF of your LinkedIn profile* as your CV. (*Go to your personal LinkedIn profile -> Click More -> Save to PDF). If we see a potential match, we will contact you to continue the recruitment process.
We look forward to hearing from you!
First application date: 7 October 2026
VTT
VTT is a visionary research, development and innovation partner. We drive sustainable growth and tackle the biggest global challenges of our time and turn them into growth opportunities. We go beyond the obvious to help the society and companies to grow through technological innovations. We have 80 years of experience of top-level research and science-based results. VTT is at the sweet spot where innovation and business come together.
VTT – beyond the obvious.

ap:253866.body:
The Munich Centre for Quantum Science and Technology (MCQST) together with the  Munich Quantum Valley (MQV) gladly announce the open call for several fully funded PhD fellowships . The applications are accepted from October to January every year. We invite passionate and dedicated young professionals to seize this career opportunity and join us for their PhD in quantum science and technology.
About MCQST and MQV:
MCQST is a Cluster of Excellence funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG, Deutsche Forschungsgemeinschaft). More than 500 scientists from various disciplines work on different areas of quantum science and technology, from basic research to applications. The MCQST Doctoral Program builds upon the framework established by the International Max Planck Research School for Quantum Science and Technology (IMPRS-QST). The program offers structured supervision and mentoring, interdisciplinary training, scientific workshops, career-development activities, networking opportunities, and community events. Doctoral researchers can also access guidance and support throughout their PhD.
The  Munich Quantum Valley , on the other hand, is dedicated to advancing quantum science and quantum technologies in Bavaria, with a primary focus on developing competitive quantum computers and bringing quantum technology to industrial applications. MQV doctoral fellows selected through the open call will have the freedom to choose any research group involved in Quantum Science and Technology across Bavarian universities , ensuring a diverse and dynamic research experience. The doctoral fellows of Munich Quantum Valley have access to courses and events from other quantum programs and MQV-partners, including  IMPRS-QST and  MCQST programs in Munich.
Fields of Research:
The research fields covered by MCQST and MQV include but are not limited to:
Atomic physics and quantum optics
Solid-state physics and material science
Quantum information theory
Quantum many-body systems
Quantum-related fields of electrical engineering and computer science

Who Should Apply:
Candidates who have completed a Master’s degree (or equivalent) outside of Bavaria are eligible to apply . Persons who have completed their degree within Bavaria are welcome to contact research groups for doctoral research opportunities directly. We welcome applications from candidates whose qualifications are completed or will be completed before the start of the fellowship but not later than September of the following year.
Whether you're an aspiring physicist, engineer, or computer scientist , if you're committed to pushing the boundaries of quantum science and technology , we encourage you to apply. There are no tuition fees, and all PhD positions are fully funded for three years .
You can apply for one or both fellowships.  Applications for both fellowships will be considered in parallel by separate committees in Spring after the application round is closed.
Diversity and Inclusion:
Both MCQST and MQV programs are committed to recruiting exceptional students from diverse backgrounds and meeting them with openness and respect. We explicitly encourage candidates of all genders to apply and extend our welcome to students from all countries. We believe that diversity drives innovation, and we look forward to welcoming a cohort of students with unique perspectives.
Don’t miss the opportunity and apply to either MCQST, MQV, or both  to become part of a community at the forefront of quantum science and technology.
For more information and to apply, please visit our  application portal , as well as the  MCQST and  MQV websites.
Join us in Bavaria and let's shape the future together.

On behalf of
Prof. Ignacio Cirac & Prof. Jan von Delft
MQV and IMPRS Educational Team

ap:253872.body:
About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Law, Economics and Finance (FDEF) at the University of Luxembourg offers a unique academic and research environment.
Rooted in Luxembourg but with a European and international outlook, teaching and research benefit from the proximity of the European institutions, Luxembourg's leading international financial centre and its vibrant business community. Institutional and private sector partnerships, sponsored Chairs and a growing network of international partner universities make the FDEF a dynamic academic hub at the heart of Europe.
As part of the Luxembourg National Centre of Excellence in Research and Innovation in Financial Technologies (FTNCER) we look for two PhD students in financial law, with a focus on collective investment schemes, private assets and financial technologies.
Your role
The PhD students will be supervised by Assistant Professor Julia Sinnig and Professor Dirk Zetzsche with additional support from disciplinary experts in computer science, information systems management and/or finance. The doctoral researcher's main task will be to prepare a doctoral thesis. The topic of the PhD thesis relates to the FTNCER's "Lighthouse Project on Private Assets" and will be determined jointly by the PhD candidat.

Your profile
Master's degree in related field
Excellent academic credentials; candidates with excellent grades will be prioritised
Proven interest in financial law, for instance through master theses, publications, and/or internships at law firms
Ability to work in and interest in interdisciplinary work, with a focus on computer science, information systems management and finance
Operational Language Requirements: Both profiles require excellent command of English. One PhD profile additionally requires excellent command of French, while the other requires excellent command of German

Academic Eligibility (Thesis) :
Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover letter presenting your motivation for this doctoral thesis topic, and explaining how your qualifications and aspirations align with its academic focus
Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken
A detailed research proposal (2-4 pages) including a bibliography
Names, contact information and current position of 1 referee who can, upon request, provide an assessment of the application. Please indicate their relationship to you

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. In line with our values, the University of Luxembourg promotes an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are dedicated to upholding equality and respect for our employees and students.
General information:
Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract 36 Month
Work Hours: Full Time 40.0 Hours per Week
Location: Weicker Building
Internal Title: Doctoral Researcher
Job Reference: UOL08514

The yearly gross salary for every Doctoral researcher at the UL is EUR 44531 (full time).

ap:253875.body:
Escuela de Odontología. Facultad de Medicina. Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile
La Escuela de Odontología, invita a postular a un cargo académico de jornada completa en la Planta Ordinaria, categoría Profesor(a) Asistente o Profesor(a) Asociado(a), para incorporarse a una carrera académica con una sólida orientación hacia la investigación, la docencia y la gestión universitaria.
Se busca un(a) académico(a) con trayectoria destacada y proyección de liderazgo en investigación odontológica o en disciplinas afines de las ciencias biomédicas y de la salud, con capacidad demostrada para desarrollar investigación independiente y competitiva a nivel nacional e internacional. Se valorará especialmente la experiencia en obtención de financiamiento externo, producción científica de alto impacto y desarrollo de colaboraciones interdisciplinarias.
La persona seleccionada deberá contribuir al fortalecimiento de las actividades de pregrado y postgrado de la Escuela, así como participar activamente en iniciativas de gestión académica, vinculación con el medio y desarrollo institucional.
La Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile se encuentra entre las principales universidades de América Latina y promueve activamente la igualdad de oportunidades, la diversidad y la inclusión como principios fundamentales de su proyecto educativo y académico. En este contexto, se invita especialmente a postular a mujeres y personas pertenecientes a grupos históricamente subrepresentados en la academia.
RESPONSABILIDADES DEL CARGO
La persona seleccionada deberá:
Desarrollar una línea de investigación independiente, innovadora y de impacto internacional en odontología o áreas afines de las ciencias biomédicas y de la salud, que resulte en la generación de publicaciones de impacto indexadas en WoS o Scopus en la disciplina de odontología o en ciencias interdisciplinarias afines.
Generar y fortalecer redes de colaboración científica con investigadores nacionales e internacionales, promoviendo proyectos interdisciplinarios en conjunto con académicos de distintas unidades de la Universidad y centros de investigación externos.
Obtener financiamiento competitivo mediante la postulación y adjudicación de fondos de investigación nacionales e internacionales que contribuyan a la sustentabilidad y crecimiento de su programa de investigación.
Participar activamente en la formación de estudiantes de pregrado y postgrado, incluyendo la dirección de tesis.
Desarrollar actividades docentes de excelencia en programas de pregrado, especialidad, magíster y doctorado, incorporando metodologías innovadoras y evidencia científica actualizada.
Colaborar en el diseño, actualización y evaluación curricular de programas académicos de la Escuela de Odontología.
Participar en actividades de gestión académica y administrativa que contribuyan al desarrollo institucional de la Escuela y de la Facultad de Medicina.
Promover actividades de investigación, vinculación con el medio, transferencia de conocimiento y difusión científica dirigidas a la comunidad académica, profesional y la sociedad en general.
Contribuir al fortalecimiento de un ambiente académico inclusivo, colaborativo y de excelencia, alineado con la misión y los valores de la Universidad.

REQUISITOS PARA POSTULAR
Los(as) postulantes deberán cumplir con los siguientes requisitos:
Poseer título profesional de Cirujano Dentista o un título profesional y/o grado académico equivalente en áreas afines al desarrollo de investigación y docencia en odontología.
Poseer grado académico de Doctor (PhD) obtenido en una institución reconocida.
Demostrar experiencia en investigación científica, evidenciada mediante publicaciones en revistas indexadas (WoS), participación en proyectos competitivos y actividades de colaboración nacional e internacional.
Demostrar capacidad para desarrollar investigación independiente y competitiva, con proyección de liderazgo académico.
Mostrar interés y disposición para contribuir a actividades de gestión universitaria y desarrollo institucional.

DOCUMENTACIÓN REQUERIDA
Los(as) postulantes deberán presentar los siguientes 3 documentos para postular :
1. CURRICULUM VITAE (CV):
Este CV debe incluir:
Estudios.
Experiencia profesional y docente.
Publicaciones científicas.
Participación en proyectos de investigación.
Presentaciones en congresos nacionales e internacionales.
Actividades de gestión académica.
Premios, reconocimientos y distinciones.
Nombre y datos de contacto de al menos dos académicos(as) que puedan actuar como referentes.

2. CARTA DE INTENCIÓN
La carta debe incluir los siguientes apartados:
a. Plan de investigación: Descripción de la línea de investigación que el/la postulante proyecta desarrollar durante los próximos años, incluyendo su potencial articulación con líneas de investigación existentes en la Escuela de Odontología y en la Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile.
b. Plan de docencia: Descripción de los aportes que el/la postulante espera realizar en docencia de pregrado, especialidad, magíster y doctorado, incluyendo iniciativas de innovación educativa y formación de estudiantes e investigadores jóvenes.
c. Contribución a la gestión académica y desarrollo institucional:  Descripción de la experiencia previa y de las potenciales contribuciones a actividades de gestión universitaria, aseguramiento de la calidad, desarrollo curricular, internacionalización y vinculación con el medio.
3. LISTADO DE PUBLICACIONES CIENTÍFICAS WoS  (Documento en formato Word).
Este listado debe incluir todas las publicaciones WoS del postulante, con el listado de todos los autores del artículo y el código DOI. Las publicaciones que no cuenten con esta información no serán consideradas en la evaluación. Dentro de este listado de publicaciones, destaque con un asterísco sus dos artículos más relevantes, incluyendo una breve explicación que fundamente por que son especialmente importantes para la línea de investigación que desea desarrollar.  Se pueden incluir manuscritos enviados a publicación agregando esta información al documento. El nombre del postulante debe aparecer subrayado en la referencia.
Cada publicación debe seguir el siguiente formato (ejemplo):
Feher B , de Souza Oliveira EH, Mendes Duarte P, Werdich AA, Giannobile WV, Feres M. Machine learning-assisted prediction of clinical responses to periodontal treatment. J Periodontol. 2025 Nov;96(11):1199-1212. doi: 10.1002/JPER.24-0737. Epub 2025 Apr 20. PMID: 40254962; PMCID: PMC12671691.*
*Este artículo describe la metodología que quiero implementar en una línea de investigación donde se analice la respuesta al tratamiento periodontal utilizando AI. Esta metodología fue validada en este estudio y deseo implementar esta nueva tecnología en futuros proyectos. (EJEMPLO).
CRITERIOS DE SELECCIÓN
La evaluación de los antecedentes considerará los siguientes aspectos:
Calidad, impacto y proyección de la trayectoria académica y científica.
Liderazgo y productividad en investigación.
Potencial para liderar una línea de investigación innovadora y competitiva.
Capacidad para obtener financiamiento externo.
Experiencia y calidad de la docencia universitaria.
Potencial de integración y colaboración con las actividades académicas de la Escuela de Odontología.
Experiencia en gestión académica y liderazgo universitario.
Contribución al desarrollo de equipos interdisciplinarios y redes de colaboración científica.
Referencias académicas.

En igualdad de condiciones, se favorecerá la diversidad y la inclusión de acuerdo con las políticas institucionales de la Universidad.
DISPONIBILIDAD
La persona seleccionada deberá tener disponibilidad para incorporarse al cargo en marzo de 2027.
RECEPCIÓN DE POSTULACIONES
Las postulaciones deberán enviarse electrónicamente a la Secretaría de Dirección de la Escuela de Odontología de la Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile. Para postular debe enviar CV, carta de intención y listado de publicaciones en Word.
Fechas del concurso: 01 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026.
Las consultas sobre el concurso y documentos de postulación deben ser enviadas al email: [email protected]
CONSIDERACIONES PARA POSTULANTES EXTRANJEROS
Los(as) postulantes de nacionalidad extranjera que resulten seleccionados(as) deberán contar con la visa o autorización correspondiente que les permita incorporarse a la planta académica de la Pontificia Universidad Católica de Chile, de conformidad con la normativa migratoria vigente.

ap:253876.body:
Job description
The Challenge
Egypt’s horticulture sector operates under growing pressure from limited water availability, salinity, and rising competition over finite water resources. At the same time, the sector is economically important for food security, rural livelihoods, and export earnings, which means that improving water productivity is not only an environmental protection measure but also a strategic development and trade challenge.
These pressures call for better evidence on current and future water use, stronger metrics for identifying good performance, and more robust ways to link farm-level improvements to wider policy and investment decisions. They also raise questions about how private-sector actors can support and scale water-smart change, including through credible incentive and financing mechanisms.
The position
You will join the Water Footprint in Action programme, a multi-partner initiative funded by the Dutch Ministry of Foreign Affairs and focused on advancing water-smart agriculture in Egypt’s horticulture sector. The programme brings together three complementary lines of work: building a strong scientific and evidence base, strengthening advisory and knowledge systems, and supporting business innovation and investment in water-smart solutions. Within this wider setting, your PhD work will mainly sit in the research and knowledge component, while also helping connect scientific insights to shared knowledge resources, decision-support tools, stakeholder learning, and new financing approaches.
A preliminary research plan looks as follows.
First, you will develop and apply quantitative approaches to analyse the present and future water consumption (i.e., the water footprint) of Egypt’s horticulture sector. This includes crop modelling using our in-house ACEA model, designing climate and socio-economic scenarios, and linking analyses across scales to local intervention settings, national policy priorities, and trade dynamics.
Next, you will work on water footprint benchmarks and performance indicators. In this part of the PhD, you will compare different ways of defining good performance, for example by looking at producer performance based on Best Available Technology and Best Available Practice, and relate these to broader sustainability and efficiency indicators.
A third part of your research will focus on how water savings and other water-smart improvements can be measured in a way that is credible, transparent, and useful in practice. You will help develop a science-based method that can underpin incentive or finance mechanisms for improved water performance, working closely with project partners and engaging with wider debates around environmental credits and integrity.
You will be embedded in an international consortium and work closely with partners in the Netherlands and Egypt, including Egyptian water and agricultural research centres. The position includes intensive interaction with stakeholders, frequent visits to project locations and case-study sites in Egypt, and an active role in a broader knowledge exchange programme through joint research, data exchange, publications, and learning activities.
Your profile
You have a Master’s degree in a relevant field, such as water management, agricultural systems, or environmental science.
You have a strong quantitative profile, including experience with data analysis, modelling, programming, or computational research methods.
You are conceptually strong and able to translate complex sustainability questions into rigorous research designs, including scenario development and method design.
You are interested in water footprint assessment, water-smart agriculture, benchmarking, sustainability metrics, and environmental crediting approaches.
You enjoy collaborating with international academic and practice partners and can work effectively in a multi-stakeholder environment.
You exhibit high levels of self-motivated and have strong communication skills.
You are willing to travel and conduct regular project visits in Egypt in connection with research activities, partner collaboration, and case studies.
You are motivated to contribute both to high-quality academic research and to applied impact in an international, policy-relevant project setting.
Arabic language skills are a strong asset; being an Arabic speaker and having experience in the Egyptian context is beneficial.
You are available to start the position per 1 January 2027.

Our offer
We offer a full-time 4-year PhD-position, with excellent mentorship and a stimulating research environment.
We encourage high responsibility and independence, while collaborating with colleagues, researchers, other university staff and partners.
The gross monthly salary will be ranging from € 3.204,- (first year), increasing each year up to € 4.051,- in the fourth year. Salary and associated conditions are in accordance with the collective labour agreement for Dutch universities (CAO-NU).
You will have a minimum of 232 leave hours in case of full-time employment based on a formal workweek of 38 hours.
A full-time employment in practice means 40 hours a week, therefore resulting in 96 extra leave hours on an annual basis.
We offer excellent fringe benefits including a holiday allowance of 8% of the gross annual salary, an end-of-year bonus of 8.3%.
a solid pension scheme, healthcare benefits, free access to sport facilities and a family-friendly institution that offers parental leave (both paid and unpaid).

Information and application
For additional information regarding this position, you are welcome to contact dr.ir. Rick Hogeboom, [email protected] .
Please apply by uploading a
motivation letter (1 page)
your CV (max 3 pages)
a writing sample (max 1 page e.g., an Abstract of a publication or a one page summary of your master thesis) as well as relevant certificates

You can apply until 1 November 2026 using the link below. The application must not exceed 5 pages excluding certificates. The first (online) job interview will take place between 9-13 November 2026.
Screening is part of the procedure
About the organisation
At the Faculty of Engineering Technology (ET), we work on engineering for impact: developing smart, sustainable, human-centred and technological solutions for societal challenges. We connect fundamental education, research and practice across five core domains: Asset & Maintenance engineering, Intelligent Manufacturing Systems, Personalised Health Technology, Resilience Engineering, and Sustainable Production, Energy and Resources.
We work on education and research in mechanical engineering, civil engineering and industrial design engineering. Together, we learn by making, creating, and innovating, addressing challenges in a solution-oriented way. Quality, connection and inclusivity are the foundation of our culture.
In our open community, students, researchers and staff collaborate with industrial and societal partners. This enables us to develop insights, applications and solutions that add value to society.

ap:253880.body:
Teaser Text

The The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in South Africa. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities, considering that in South Africa colonial and apartheid legacies still influence patterns of access to coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economizing nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.

Project Description

The project investigates the impacts of economisation of seaweed as part of a global drive to develop ‘blue economy’ strategies. Seaweed harvesting and cultivation (as food, or fertilizer- and bioplastic ingredient) are increasing considerably and promoted as contributing to sustainable development. The project focuses on coastal communities in Scotland, which has developed a comprehensive blue economy strategy. Building on insights from political ecology and valuation studies and inspired by the multispecies turn in anthropology, this project aims to study local impacts of new forms of economisation of seaweed, and the possible contestations these may entail. It seeks to incorporate the ideas, interests, and knowledge from local groups who live from, in and with seaweed ecologies, examining how new versions of economisation affect local social relations, including the entanglements with non-humans these ecologies and economisations depend on. It does so by focusing on valuations of seaweed ecologies, based on an understanding of values as enacted through practices by all (human and non-human) stakeholders. The project employs a collaborative approach vis-à-vis research participants and a wider audience through a visual storytelling approach.

What you will do

You will work in a project team consisting of PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in South Africa. You will:

Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in South Africa. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.
Actively contribute to the output and dissemination of the research project, which includes collaborating with the other team members on academic and non-academic publications, science communication, and the organization of workshops, seminars and an exhibition.
Participate in relevant PhD-courses and masterclasses, organized in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Social Science and the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology. PhD-courses at Stellenbosch University, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in South Africa you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the Department of Sociology and Social Anthropology at Stellenbosch University.

Where you will work

The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences consists of five institutes: the Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, Education and Child Studies, Political Science, and Psychology. The faculty is home to approximately 7,000 students and 1,000 staff members. Our institutes are dedicated not only to education but also to groundbreaking research that expands our understanding of human behavior and societal structures. What makes our faculty unique is the diversity of research topics, the variety of teaching approaches, and the structure of professional support. This provides you with the opportunity to explore and develop your interests and expertise. For an introduction to our faculty, visit our website: Welcome to the Leiden Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences – Leiden University .

Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology (CADS)
Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology concentrates on 'global vulnerability and social resilience'. The institute has three main themes: diversity, sustainability, and digitalisation. CADS is dedicated to making a real-world impact, not just studying change, but also working with communities to promote positive change through education and research. We use a unique approach that blends qualitative, quantitative, audiovisual, and digital methods based on ethnographic fieldwork.

With our unique blend of interdisciplinary interests, comparative regional studies, and social science research methods, we emphasize our role in the extensive collaborative network within Leiden University. In both our research and education, we engage in extensive interdisciplinary and international networks.

The project team
The project team at Leiden University works closely together with colleagues at the University of Edinburgh, the Scottish Association for Marine Science, and Stellenbosch University. The PhD-students will be jointly supervised by Leiden University and Stellenbosch University, and Leiden University and the University of Edinburgh respectively. A project assistant will assist with training and dissemination activities.

What you bring

A Master’s degree in Anthropology, Sociology, Environmental Humanities or another relevant discipline within the social sciences or humanities.
Demonstrable excellent qualitative research skills and experience with ethnographic fieldwork.
Affinity with the topics of sustainability and environmental justice.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Strong command of English;
Knowledge of one of the other official languages of South Africa is a bonus.
Excellent social and organisational skills and the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

What we offer

Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University.

We also offer:
PHD: An employment contract for 38 hours per week as a PhD candidate, initially for a period of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for 3 years after a positive evaluation. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student);

A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;

Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;

Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.

Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;

A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone.

For more information about employment conditions, see  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value

Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

Want to apply or find out more?

If you want to apply straight away, click the application button.

As part of your application we ask you to submit:
A letter explaining your motivation to apply for a PhD-position, and more specifically for such a position within the project (maximum of 2 pages);
A curriculum vitae (CV) (maximum of 2 pages);
A copy of your Bachelor and Master degree with a course and grade list;
A summary of how you would design the ethnographic research in South Africa (maximum of 500 words);
The names and contact details of two referees who can be contacted to provide information on your qualifications and strengths (we are not asking for a referee report at this stage of the application procedure).

If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact prof. dr. Marja Spierenburg, project leader, at at +31715276699 or by email: [email protected] or dr. Miriam Waltz, project member, by email: [email protected] . You can apply until 7 November 2026;  applications will be processed immediately. Interviews will take place during the last week of November and the first week of December 2026.

To help us get to know each other better, we follow a number of steps in the application procedure. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

We believe mobility is very important. That is why we are also publishing this vacancy internally. In case of equal suitability, we will give priority to the internal candidate.
A pre-employment screening (references, diplomas, certificate of good conduct (VOG)) may be part of the selection procedure.

Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this. #LI-Hybrid

ap:253885.body:
Ben je een ervaren leidinggevende met affiniteit voor wetenschappelijke informatievoorziening? En weet je medewerkers te verbinden, te ontwikkelen en mee te nemen in verandering? Bij Universitaire Bibliotheken Leiden krijg je de kans om leiding te geven aan een veelzijdige afdeling waar specialistische kennis en innovatie samenkomen. Met technologische ontwikkelingen zoals AI en Linked Data liggen er volop kansen om de toekomst van de beschikbaarstelling van wetenschappelijke informatie vorm te geven.

Dit ga je doen

Als Afdelingshoofd Metadatadiensten & Acquisitie (MDA) geef je samen met een teamleider richting aan een afdeling van ongeveer 30 medewerkers. Je stuurt uitvoerende professionals, inhoudelijke specialisten en coördinatoren aan die zorgen voor het verwerven, verwerken en toegankelijk maken van wetenschappelijke informatiebronnen. Daarbij bewaak je de dagelijkse dienstverlening en neem je medewerkers mee in de ontwikkeling van processen en werkwijzen.
Concreet houd je je onder meer bezig met:
Leidinggeven & verbinden: direct aansturen en begeleiden van circa twintig medewerkers, met aandacht voor samenwerking, professionele ontwikkeling en duurzame inzetbaarheid.
Vernieuwen & verbeteren: signaleren van kansen voor innovatie en initiëren van verbeteringen in werkprocessen door de inzet van nieuwe technologie zoals AI en Linked Data, met draagvlak bij je medewerkers.
Organiseren & bewaken: waarborgen van de kwaliteit en continuïteit van processen rondom acquisitie, catalogisering en metadatabeheer, zodat wetenschappelijke publicaties goed vindbaar en toegankelijk zijn.
Licentiebeheer & contractonderhandelingen: verantwoordelijkheid dragen voor licentiebeheer, bijdragen aan (landelijke) contractonderhandelingen met uitgevers en leveranciers van wetenschappelijke informatiebronnen en complexe contractuele vraagstukken oplossen.
Adviseren & samenwerken: bijdragen aan de beleidsontwikkeling binnen de UBL en samenwerken met andere afdelingen, de universiteit en externe partners waaronder het LUMC.

Hier ga je werken

Je komt te werken binnen een toonaangevende wetenschappelijke bibliotheek met collecties van wereldformaat. Centraal staat het bieden van betrouwbare, duurzame en innovatieve diensten. We doen dit samen met andere partijen in binnen- en buitenland. Onze werkterreinen zijn breed en divers, zo ook onze klantgroepen, in het bijzonder studenten, docenten en onderzoekers. Voor hen verzorgen we de wetenschappelijke informatievoorziening als partner in kennis. Universitaire Bibliotheken Leiden (UBL) staat wereldwijd bekend om de bijzondere collecties, die naast hun rol voor onderwijs en onderzoek ook een belangrijke maatschappelijke en culturele functie hebben. Op onze bibliotheeklocaties bieden wij iedereen een prettige studie- en onderzoeksomgeving.  Online staan wij in contact met gebruikers van over de hele wereld. Onze medewerkers dragen hier samen, ieder vanuit hun eigen achtergrond, ervaring en talent aan bij. Kijk voor meer informatie over ons op de website van de UBL. https://www.bibliotheek.universiteitleiden.nl/ .

De afdeling MDA verzorgt het proces van de verwerking van aanzienlijke hoeveelheden elektronische en papieren (wetenschappelijke) informatiebronnen, vanaf de aanschaf, of het afsluiten van de licentie, tot het moment van beschikbaarstelling aan gebruikers. Ook ten behoeve van NIMAR, KITLV-Jakarta en LUMC worden informatiebronnen verwerkt en licenties beheerd. Daarnaast heeft MDA de verantwoordelijkheid voor het beleid, het beheer en grootschalige bewerking van metadata en de plaatsing van proefschriften en andere wetenschappelijke output van de Universiteit Leiden en het LUMC in het CRIS- en het repositorium.
Binnen MDA werken ongeveer 30 medewerkers, verdeeld over verschillende teams en specialismen zoals acquisitie, catalogisering, wetenschappelijke output en metadata. Je geeft rechtstreeks leiding aan circa 20 specialisten, uitvoerende en coördinerende medewerkers en werkt samen met een teamleider die verantwoordelijk is voor de overige medewerkers. Je werkt vanuit het Van Steenisgebouw op het Leiden Bio Science Park en rapporteert aan de divisiemanager Bibliotheekprocesondersteuning.
De afdeling staat de komende jaren voor een interessante ontwikkeling. Bestaande processen functioneren al lange tijd, terwijl nieuwe technologieën, waaronder AI, kansen bieden om het werk anders en slimmer te organiseren. Dat vraagt om een leidinggevende die bestaande expertise waardeert, medewerkers betrekt en tegelijkertijd vernieuwing stimuleert.

Dit breng je mee

In deze functie zoeken we iemand die zelfstandig aan de slag kan. Elke functie is anders dus er is in het begin aandacht voor inwerken. Mochten bepaalde werkzaamheden nieuw zijn voor je, dan kijken we samen wat je nodig hebt en stellen hiervoor een ontwikkelplan op.
Deze functie past bij jou als je je herkent in de volgende punten:
Een academische opleiding, bij voorkeur met een specialisatie op het gebied van informatiewetenschappen of een verwant onderwerp;
Minimaal drie jaar leidinggevende ervaring, binnen een kennisintensieve of informatiegerichte organisatie zoals een bibliotheek of uitgeverij;
Aantoonbare kennis van en ervaring met licentiebeheer en contractonderhandelingen;
Verbindend leiderschap met een voorbeeldfunctie voor medewerkers om hun persoonlijke en professionele kwaliteiten optimaal in te zetten en onderlinge samenwerkingen te versterken, binnen een divers team;
Affiniteit met metadatering, acquisitie en administratieve verwerking van publicaties; een visie op en kennis van ontwikkelingen en standaarden op die gebieden;
Analytisch vermogen, organisatiesensitiviteit, overtuigingskracht, sturen op resultaat;
Uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden en beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift.

Herken je jezelf volledig in dit profiel óf voldoe jij nog niet aan alle eisen maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren!

Dit bieden we je

We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een uitdagende maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
Een arbeidsovereenkomst voor de duur van één jaar met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband. De overeenkomst valt onder de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten;

Een salaris van maximaal € 7537,-- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (schaal 12);

Vakantietoeslag (8%), een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%) en een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het ABP;

Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.

Flexibele werkduur: standaard heb je minimaal 29 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime werkweek van 38 uur; je kunt daarnaast extra verlof opbouwen door bijvoorbeeld fulltime 40 uur per week te werken en zo 96 extra verlofuren op te bouwen óf door 96 verlofuren in te leveren en een werkweek van 36 uur te werken;

Ruime keuze in secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden; zo is het bespreekbaar om voor een sabbatical of betaald ouderschapsverlof te kiezen. Binnen ons keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden kunnen vrije dagen en/of salaris ingezet worden voor bijvoorbeeld een voordelig sportabonnement en fietsregeling;

Als de werkzaamheden het toelaten is hybride werken binnen Nederland mogelijk;

Een thuiswerkvergoeding (dag- en internetvergoeding) en aandacht voor goede werkplekken, daarnaast krijg je een laptop en een mobiele telefoon van de universiteit tot je beschikking.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier:  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Direct solliciteren? Klik dan op de sollicitatiebutton.

Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met Bas Vat, Divisiemanager Bibliotheekprocesondersteuning , [email protected] , tel. 071-5272884. Solliciteren kan tot en met maandag 2 november. De twee gespreksrondes vinden naar verwachting plaats in week 45/46 en week 47/48. De beoogde startdatum is 1 april 2027.Je ontvangt uiterlijk twee weken na de sluitingsdatum van de vacature een reactie op je sollicitatie.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Bij onderlinge afweging van kandidaten, geldt bij gelijke geschiktheid een voorkeur voor interne kandidaten, vrouwen, werknemers met een arbeidsbeperking en werknemers met een migratieachtergrond.

Een pre-employment screening (referenties, diploma’s) kan onderdeel uitmaken van de selectieprocedure.

Voor deze functie vragen wij bij indiensttreding om een Verklaring Omtrent Gedrag (VOG). Deze verklaring is verkrijgbaar bij de afdeling Burgerzaken van de gemeente waar je staat ingeschreven. De aanvraag verloopt via ons en de kosten hiervoor worden vergoed.

ap:253886.body:
Why apply?

This multidisciplinary project integrates electrochemistry, metal–organic framework-based materials, and membrane chemistry to develop the next generation of high-performance membranes and unlock new possibilities for advanced molecular separation and transport.

Can you design the membrane that powers the next generation of electrolysers?

Electrolysis and electrocatalysis have a key role to play in creating a more sustainable chemical industry. At the heart of these technologies are membranes that control the transport of protons and other species—but today’s proton exchange membranes rely heavily on PFAS-based materials such as Nafion®. We are looking for a PhD candidate to develop a new generation of high-performance, PFAS-free proton-conductive membranes. In this project, you will combine the unique properties of proton-conductive metal–organic frameworks (MOFs) with those of proton-conductive polymers to create innovative membrane materials. You will systematically investigate how molecular structure, composition, and membrane architecture determine proton transport and overall performance. Your research will span materials chemistry, membrane science, and electrochemistry. You will establish design principles for high-performance proton-conductive membranes and put your materials to the test in different electrolyser configurations. This is an opportunity to work at the interface of fundamental materials science and real-world energy technology, with the ambition to develop membrane materials that can help enable a cleaner and more sustainable chemical industry. The PhD students will be supervised by Dennis Hetterscheid (Leiden Institute of Chemistry).

What you bring

We are looking for an enthusiastic and motivated candidate who is excited to pursue an interdisciplinary PhD at the interface of electrochemistry, materials chemistry, and membrane science. The project combines electrochemistry, MOF synthesis and characterization, physical measurements, and electrolysis studies, offering the opportunity to develop expertise across multiple fields.
You hold an MSc degree in Physical Chemistry, Chemistry, Materials Science, or a related discipline, with a background in one or more of the following areas: electrochemistry, membrane chemistry, MOF synthesis, or materials characterization. Most importantly, you are curious, eager to learn, and motivated to work across disciplinary boundaries.
You will join a highly collaborative and international research team of PhD candidates, postdoctoral researchers, MSc students, and scientific staff. We collaborate extensively with research groups both locally and internationally, and work closely with industry partners to translate fundamental scientific discoveries into technologies with real-world societal impact.
We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can thrive. Our lab values diversity, accessibility, and inclusion in all their forms, and we strive to foster a safe and supportive workplace that encourages personal and professional growth, well-being, scientific integrity, and responsible research.
If you are excited by the opportunity to combine fundamental materials chemistry with electrochemical energy technologies and help develop the membranes of the future, we would love to hear from you.

Skills:
Hands-on experimental experience , with co-authorship of one or more scientific publications considered an advantage.
A strong interest in fundamental science and a genuine curiosity about understanding the principles underlying new materials and technologies.
High motivation for research , combined with a solid theoretical understanding of relevant scientific principles.
Strong organizational and time-management skills , with the ability to plan your work, work independently, and communicate your progress clearly.
Excellent written and spoken English .
A collaborative mindset and the ability to work effectively as part of a diverse, interdisciplinary team.

What we offer

Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organization is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.
You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organize through Healthy University.

The position will be for a maximum of 4 years, and the candidate is expected to complete a PhD thesis at the end of this period. A contribution to classroom teaching (maximum 10% of the time) will be part of the responsibilities of the candidate, as well as supervision of BSc and MSc research projects that contribute to the goals of this PhD project.
We offer a stimulating and interactive research environment, free use of all state-of-the-art facilities, and a competitive salary.

We also offer:
An employment contract for 12 months initially, to be extended for 3 more years upon satisfactory performance. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
A salary between € 3.204,- and  € 4.051,-  gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours - PhD student);
A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;
Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.
Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;
If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces.

For more information about employment conditions, see  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

Where you will work

Leiden University is one of Europe’s leading international research universities.
Thanks to its committed and inspired employees, the university enjoys a leading role in academic research and education. Every year, Leiden University scores very well in prominent rankings. This means that, to maintain our position, the bar is set very high. Regardless of the work you do at our university, you are always encouraged to broaden your horizons, develop your talents and reach your full potential.

Faculty of Science & Leiden Institute of Chemistry
The Faculty of Science at Leiden University is a world-class faculty where staff and students work together in a dynamic international environment. It is a faculty where personal and academic development are top priorities. Our people are committed to expand fundamental knowledge by curiosity and to look beyond the borders of their own discipline; their aim is to benefit science, and to contribute to addressing the major societal challenges of the future.

The research carried out at the Faculty of Science is very diverse, ranging from mathematics, information science, astronomy, physics, chemistry and bio-pharmaceutical sciences to biology and environmental sciences. The research activities are organized in eight institutes. These institutes offer eight bachelors’ and twelve master’s programmes. The faculty has grown strongly in recent years and now has more than 2,300 staff and over 5,000 students. We are located at the heart of Leiden’s Bio Science Park, one of Europe’s biggest science parks, where university and business life come together.

The research is embedded within the Leiden Institute of Chemistry, with its long-standing traditions of excellence in research. Apart from a state-of-the-art electrochemistry laboratory, and excellent synthesis facilities, preparation and measurement facilities, unconventional nanofabrication equipment and experimental setups to measure ion transport will be designed supported by outstanding mechanical and electronic workshops. We foster an international and collaborative atmosphere and have close ties to other institutes housed within our Faculty of Science and with many research groups within the Netherlands, and many prominent labs abroad.

What we value

Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. We strive to be an open community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to fully develop themselves. We consider an inclusive academic environment, where students and staff can share their experiences and viewpoints, to be essential for the development of talent.

Want to apply or find out more?

If you want to apply straight away, click the application button.
If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Dr. Dennis Hetterscheid, at [email protected] . You can apply until 20 November 2026; You will receive a response to your application no later than two weeks after the vacancy closing date.

Your application should include a motivation letter clearly indicating WHY you apply for this position and project and WHAT makes you a suitable candidate, an extensive CV, the courses you took and grades you obtained in your Master’s studies, and the names and contact details of at least two references.
You will receive a response to your application no later than two weeks after the vacancy closing date.
If you have any questions about the procedure, please contact our management- & office assistent Angelo Philippi ( [email protected] ).

To help us get to know each other better, we follow a number of steps in the application procedure. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

Teaser Tekst

De afdeling Moot Court van de Faculteit Rechtsgeleerdheid zoekt

Moot Court-videotrainers (student-assistenten)

Dit ga je doen

Kun jij goed studenten motiveren? Kun jij goed luisteren en feedback geven? Beschik jij over digitale vaardigheden en ben je handig met de camera? Voor het vak Moot Court Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid zoeken we enthousiaste en betrokken studenten voor de functie van student-assistent ten behoeve van de videotrainingen.

Het vak Moot Court Bachelor Rechtsgeleerdheid begint 26 februari 2027 en duurt tot en met 28 mei 2027 (week 8 tot en met week 21).

Hier ga je werken

De Faculteit der Rechtsgeleerdheid is gevestigd in Leiden en Den Haag en is met ruim 7000 studenten en ongeveer 600 medewerkers een van de grootste faculteiten van Nederland. De faculteit richt zich op innovatief multidisciplinair onderzoek en een steeds vernieuwend onderwijsaanbod aan de hand van maatschappelijke vraagstukken. Onze faculteit is groot genoeg om nationaal en internationaal het verschil te maken en klein genoeg om persoonlijk onderwijs te bieden. Zo leveren we dagelijks een bijdrage aan een veilige en duurzame wereld. Impact met recht! Zie voor meer informatie https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/rechtsgeleerdheid .

Dit breng je mee

Studenten die het vak Moot Court te Leiden of een vergelijkbaar pleitvaardighedenvak elders met goed gevolg hebben afgerond komen in aanmerking.
Van 15 t/m 17 februari 2027 vinden de Train-de-Trainers-dagen plaats. Je kunt alleen solliciteren als je deze drie dagen volledig beschikbaar bent (af en toe weg voor een werkgroep of college is geen probleem). Ook tijdens de pleitdagen van 25 mei t/m 27 mei 2027 wordt er vanzelfsprekend op je gerekend. Met tentamens in die periode wordt rekening gehouden.

Dit bieden we je

We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
De aanstelling is voor gemiddeld 6 uur in de week, gedurende een periode van 14 weken. Je ontvangt een aanstelling via JobMotion. Het salaris bedraagt tussen de €19,58 en €19,93 bruto per uur, afhankelijk van je studiejaar. Meer informatie over JobMotion: JobMotion - Universiteit Leiden .

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. We streven ernaar om een open gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Een inclusieve academische omgeving waarin studenten en medewerkers hun ervaringen en opvattingen kunnen delen, zien we als essentieel voor de ontwikkeling van talenten.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Direct solliciteren? Klik dan op de sollicitatiebutton. Je kunt uitsluitend solliciteren via ons online sollicitatiesysteem. Sollicitaties vergezeld van een motivatiebrief, cv met recente pasfoto en een gewaarmerkte cijferlijst (OIC) kunnen t/m 22 november 2026 ingezonden worden ter attentie van mw. prof. mr. C.G. Breedveld-de Voogd. De sollicitatiegesprekken staan begin januari 2027 gepland.

Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met het secretariaat van Moot Court: Saskia van der Werf en Liselotte Kleine, [email protected] . Solliciteren kan tot en met 22 november 2026. Je ontvangt uiterlijk twee weken na de sluitingsdatum van de vacature een reactie op je sollicitatie.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

ap:253897.body:
Die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft ( www.fraunhofer.de ) ist eine der weltweit führenden Organisationen für anwendungs­orientierte Forschung. 74 Institute entwickeln weg­weisende Technologien für unsere Wirt­schaft und Gesell­schaft – genauer: 30 000 Menschen aus Technik, Wissen­schaft, Ver­waltung und IT. Sie wissen: Wer zu Fraunhofer kommt, will und kann etwas verändern – für sich, für uns und die Märkte von heute und morgen.
Technologien für morgen gestalten: das ist unsere Mission am Fraunhofer-Institut für Optronik, Systemtechnik und Bildauswertung (IOSB). Wir erforschen, entwickeln und evaluieren neuartige Sichtsysteme und sorgen für den optimalen Einsatz und die Vernetzung von Sensoren, mit dem Ziel, die entstehenden Datenströme zu verarbeiten und auszuwerten. So unterstützen wir Menschen bei der Entscheidungsfindung, der Prozessoptimierung und der intelligenten Steuerung autonomer Systeme. Wo Forschung auf Praxis trifft, entsteht Veränderung – gestalten Sie mit uns die Zukunft der elektro-optischen Signaturbewertung und Tarntechnik!
Die Gruppe Signaturbewertung beschäftigt sich mit der Analyse, Bewertung und Reduzierung elektro-optischer Signaturen. Unsere Forschungsarbeiten fließen direkt in die Entwicklung und Bewertung moderner Tarn- und Schutztechnologien ein. Dabei arbeiten wir eng mit der Bundeswehr sowie nationalen und internationalen Partnern zusammen.
In dieser Position übernehmen Sie wissenschaftliche Verantwortung für anspruchsvolle Forschungsthemen und gestalten Forschungsprojekte von der ersten Idee bis zur Umsetzung aktiv mit. Neben der Forschung gehört auch die Leitung und Weiterentwicklung von Projekten zu Ihrem Aufgabenbereich. So tragen Sie dazu bei, zukünftige Technologien für sicherheitsrelevante Anwendungen mitzugestalten.
Hier sorgen Sie für Veränderung
Forschungsschwerpunkte
Vermessung und Analyse der Oberflächenreflektanz verschiedener Materialien
Durchführung von BRDF Vermessung
Einsatz von KI-gestützten Methoden zur Tarnbewertung
Bedienung und Auswertung von Lichfeldgeneratoren
Erarbeitung innovativer Tarnkonzepte
Planung und Durchführung von Feldkampagnen

Projektverantwortung
Planung, Koordination und Leitung von Forschungs- und Industrieprojekten
Erstellung von Anforderungsanalysen in Abstimmung mit Kunden und Kooperationspartnern

Forschungsstrategie und Kooperationen
Zusammenarbeit mit der Bundeswehr zur Entwicklung neuer Tarn- und Täuschkonzepte
Leitung von internationalen Forschungsgruppen bei NATO und EDA
Beobachtung des Marktumfeldes und strategische Ausrichtung der Forschungsgruppe
Aufbau von Kooperationen und Netzwerken für zukünftige Forschungsthemen

Hiermit bringen Sie sich ein
Ein abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Diplom oder Master) in Physik, Elektrotechnik, Optik oder vergleichbarer Fachrichtung – eine Promotion ist von Vorteil
Fundierte Kenntnisse und Erfahrung in Forschungsprojekten, Projektleitung und Akquise
Mehrjährige Berufserfahrung in Signaturanalyse, Tarntechnik oder verwandten Bereichen der elektro-optischen Forschung
Hohe Selbständigkeit, Zielorientierung und wissenschaftliche Arbeitsweise
Organisationsgeschick, Teamfähigkeit und exzellente Kommunikationsfähigkeiten
Sehr gute Deutschkenntnisse und gute Englischkenntnisse in Wort und Schrift
Kenntnisse verteidigungsrelevanter Themen sind wünschenswert

Was wir für Sie bereithalten
Eine abwechslungsreiche, spannende Tätigkeit an der Schnittstelle zwischen Wissenschaft und Wirtschaft, zwischen Gegenwart und Zukunft
Großen Freiraum zur wissenschaftlichen Entfaltung und zum selbstbestimmten Vorantreiben von Themen und Projekten
Eine exzellente technische Ausstattung
Motivierte Kolleg*innen, die sich durch ihre interdisziplinäre und internationale Zusammensetzung gegenseitig inspirieren
Individuelle Karrierepfade durch umfangreiche Fortbildungs- und Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten (z.B. Förder- und Entwicklungsprogramm »Fraunhofer TALENTA« für Wissenschaftlerinnen und weibliche Führungskräfte)
Optimale Bedingungen zur Vereinbarkeit von Beruf und Privatleben (flexible Arbeitszeiten, mobiles Arbeiten im Rahmen der Erfordernisse der Stelle, Kita-Platz-Kontingent in Karlsruhe etc.)
Eine Kantine sowie nahegelegene Einkaufsmöglichkeiten
Eine gute Anbindung an den ÖPNV sowie ein Zuschuss zum Deutschlandticket

Wir wertschätzen und fördern die Vielfalt der Kompetenzen unserer Mitarbeitenden und begrüßen daher alle Bewerbungen – unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht, Nationalität, ethnischer und sozialer Herkunft, Religion, Weltanschauung, Behinderung sowie sexueller Orientierung und Identität. Schwerbehinderte Menschen werden bei gleicher Eignung bevorzugt eingestellt. Unsere Aufgaben sind vielfältig und anpassbar – für Bewerber*innen mit Behinderung finden wir gemeinsam Lösungen, die ihre Fähigkeiten optimal fördern.
Die wöchentliche Arbeitszeit beträgt 39 Stunden. Die Stelle kann auch in Teilzeit besetzt werden. Die Stelle ist zunächst auf 2 Jahre befristet. Eine Verlängerung wird angestrebt. Anstellung, Vergütung und Sozialleistungen basieren auf dem Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD). Zusätzlich kann Fraunhofer leistungs- und erfolgsabhängige variable Vergütungsbestandteile gewähren.
Mit ihrer Fokussierung auf zukunftsrelevante Schlüsseltechnologien sowie auf die Verwertung der Ergebnisse in Wirtschaft und Industrie spielt die Fraunhofer-Gesellschaft eine zentrale Rolle im Innovationsprozess. Als Wegweiser und Impulsgeber für innovative Entwicklungen und wissenschaftliche Exzellenz wirkt sie mit an der Gestaltung unserer Gesellschaft und unserer Zukunft.
Bereit für Veränderung? Dann bewerben Sie sich jetzt, und machen Sie einen Unterschied! Nach Eingang Ihrer Online-Bewerbung erhalten Sie eine automatische Empfangsbestätigung. Dann melden wir uns schnellstmöglich und sagen Ihnen, wie es weitergeht.
Bei Fragen zur Stelle wenden Sie sich bitte an:
Dr. Karin Stein
Telefon: +49 7243 992-114
Fraunhofer-Institut für Optronik, Systemtechnik und Bildauswertung IOSB
www.iosb.fraunhofer.de
