ap:253900.body:
Doctoral Researcher in Pulse Electron Paramagnetic Resonance
The Spin Dynamics and Hyperpolarisation group is looking for a doctoral researcher, fully funded by a Starting Grant from the Swiss National Science Foundation (SNSF). The group explores ways to enhance the sensitivity of electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR, also known as electron spin resonance, ESR) by orders of magnitude. The project lies at the interface between method development and applied chemical spectroscopy.

Starting date: by mutual agreement. There is no deadline and the position will remain open until suitable candidates are found. Applications are considered as long as this advertisement is online.

Job description
The position involves working with a state-of-the-art pulse EPR spectrometer with arbitrary phase and amplitude control. The aim is to develop new pulse sequences with improved sensitivity and higher information content, and to apply them to challenging systems from inorganic chemistry and catalysis, as well as to organic radicals. Our group is also developing a new method based on optical hyperpolarisation, which will eventually be applied to the same systems.

The work will focus on the spectroscopic aspects, including experiments and spin-dynamics simulations. Depending on the candidate's background, it can also include chemical synthesis and catalysis, as well as quantum-chemical calculations.

The working language of the group is English.

Profile

The candidate must hold a Master's degree in (physical) chemistry or a related field by the start of the position. Interest in spin dynamics, magnetic resonance, and their applications to (in)organic chemistry is essential.

Research experience in an advanced magnetic resonance technique (EPR, solid-state NMR, or similar) is required.

A good understanding of the physics underlying magnetic resonance is expected.

In addition, the candidate should have:

the drive to take ownership of their project and push it forward

openness to collaborating with people from different backgrounds

We offer

An exciting project at the forefront of magnetic resonance method development

A position in a new research group with close collaboration and structured mentoring

Considerable freedom to pursue your own ideas and to develop both academically and personally

World-class infrastructure

Opportunities to initiate your own collaborations

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

CV

Motivation letter (max. one page) explaining your interest in magnetic resonance, spin dynamics, and science in general

Copies of available BSc/MSc diplomas or current transcripts

Contact details of two referees (please inform them that they might get contacted)

Further information about Institute for Molecular Physical Science can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Nino Wili ( [email protected] ) (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications by email, LinkedIn, etc. will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:253903.body:
Let’s shape the future - University of Antwerp
The University of Antwerp is a dynamic, forward-thinking, European university. We offer an innovative academic education to more than 20 000 students, conduct pioneering scientific research and play an important service-providing role in society. We are one of the largest, most international and most innovative employers in the region. With more than 6 000 employees from 100 different countries, we are helping to build tomorrow's world every day. Through top scientific research, we push back boundaries and set a course for the future – a future that you can help to shape.
The Department of Veterinary Sciences in the Faculty of Pharmaceutical, Biomedical and Veterinary Sciences is looking for a full-time (100%) doctoral scholarship holder in the field of endocrine disruptor-mediated neurotoxicity.
Position
You will become one of the 15 Doctoral Candidates in the NeXED Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions (MSCA) Doctoral Network. For more information about NeXED, see https://www.nexed.eu .
Your research will focus on the development of a cross-species approach to assessing impaired neurological function caused by endocrine disruptors. This will facilitate the use of NAMs such as cell-based methods and zebrafish embryos for raising concern on neurological effects in humans and non-target organisms. A draft AOP network linking different ED modalities to impaired neurological development is available, and will be used to investigate cross-species applicability of the pathways. Knowledge gaps will be identified, and addressed experimentally.
A short interdisciplinary secondment to the University of Milan, and an intersectoral secondment to the Belgian Federal Public Service Public Health will be part of your programme.
You will enroll in the University of Antwerp Doctoral School and comply with the local doctoral training requirements.
You will write project reports on a regular basis, and publish high-quality research results related to the research project in international conference proceedings and peer-reviewed scientific journals.
You will participate actively in the NeXED training, dissemination, communication and exploitation activities.
You will work on the preparation and defence of a doctoral thesis.
You will be expected to engage with and further support a limited number of teaching activities for the research group Veterinary Physiology and Biochemistry of the Department of Veterinary Sciences (e.g., by assisting in practical courses Biochemistry and supervising thesis students).

Profile
You hold a Master’s degree in one of the life sciences (Biomedical sciences, Biology, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical sciences,…) or you will have obtained it by the time you start work.
You have knowledge of (eco)toxicology.
A background in adverse outcome pathways and neurotoxicity, and experience in working with zebrafish embryos and cell-based methods are considered an asset.
Excellent proficiency in English is required.
You can work accurately and independently as well as within a multidisciplinary team.
You obtained a FELASA B/C certificate for animal research, or are willing to do so as soon as possible.
Your teaching competences are in line with the University of Antwerp’s educational vision .
Your research qualities are in line with the faculty and university research policies .
You act with attention to quality, integrity, creativity and cooperation.

Horizon Europe MSCA eligibility criteria
To be eligible as a Doctoral Candidate, applicants cannot already be in possession of a doctoral degree at the date of the recruitment. Researchers who have successfully defended their doctoral thesis but who have not yet formally been awarded the doctoral degree will not be considered eligible.
Mobility rule : Applicants can be of any nationality, but must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting host organisation for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before the recruitment date. Compulsory national service, short stays such as holidays, and time spent as part of a procedure for obtaining refugee status under the Geneva Convention are not taken into account. Important : note that the country of main activity is not only where you were physically based but also the country of the institution for which the main activity was performed, including remotely.

What we offer
The selected candidate will be employed full-time by University of Antwerp on the MSCA-DN project for a period of 24 months . In line with the University of Antwerp regulations and following a positive evaluation by the doctoral committee, additional funding to complete the doctoral degree is available for at least a further period of 12 months.
Doctoral candidates are offered a direct contract with equivalent benefits to an employment contract, including social security coverage, with a competitive remuneration based on the MSCA allowances in line with the MSCA WP 2023-2025 . The gross monthly amount at UAntwerpen corresponds to the amount for doctoral scholarship holders.
Funding is available for technical and personal skills training and participation in international research events.
The expected start date is January 2027 .
You will receive ecocheques, Internet-connectivity allowance, and a bicycle allowance or a full reimbursement of public transport costs for commuting.
As a doctoral researcher, you will have access to a wide and varied range of courses and an educational credit through the Antwerp Doctoral School .
You will do most of your work at Campus Drie Eiken in a dynamic and stimulating working environment.
Find out more about working at the University of Antwerp here .

Want to apply?
You can apply for this vacancy through the University of Antwerp’s online job application platform up to and including November 3, 2026 (23:59h CET). Click on the 'Apply' button and complete the online application form. Be sure to include (1) your academic CV, (2) a motivation letter, (3) list of reference persons including their contact details. Your CV should unambiguously demonstrate that you meet the MSCA eligibility criteria .
The selection committee will review all applications as soon as possible after the application deadline. Only pre-selected candidates will be invited to an interview with the selection committee. We will inform pre-selected candidates about the next steps in the selection procedure as soon as possible.
NeXED follows an open, transparent, merit-based, impartial and equitable recruitment procedure, with particular focus on fair gender representation and diversity. The recruitment aligns with the principles of the Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers and the European Charter for Researchers and follows pre-defined selection criteria.
If you have any questions about the online application form, please check the frequently asked questions or send an email to [email protected] . If you have any questions about the job itself, please contact Prof. Dries Knapen ( [email protected] ).

The University of Antwerp received the European Commission’s HR Excellence in Research Award for its HR policy. We are a sustainable, family-friendly organisation which invests in its employees’ growth. We encourage diversity  and attach great importance to an inclusive working environment and equal opportunities, regardless of gender identity, disability, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual orientation or age. We encourage people from diverse backgrounds and with diverse characteristics to apply.

ap:253913.body:
How do advanced composite materials perform after millions of load cycles in the demanding environment of an aeroengine? As a doctoral student in this international research collaboration, you will help answer that question through a combination of experimental testing, advanced simulations, and close interaction with leading researchers and industry experts. Your work will contribute to the development of future aerospace structures that are lighter, more efficient, and more reliable.
About us
The PhD position is placed at the Division of Computational Mechanics and Materials Engineering . We foster an inclusive, friendly, and helpful work environment to which we welcome you to contribute. Our activities integrate computational mechanics and advanced materials technology, combining multidisciplinary expertise to predict, understand, and elevate the performance of engineering materials and structures.
Within the project, you will be supported by an international team of experts in the area of mechanics of composites, combining academic excellence with industrial expertise and experience.
About the research project
The project aims to enable the deployment of advanced composite structures in aeroengines by developing reliable methods for predicting fatigue life of textile carbon fibre composites under thermomechanical tension-tension loading. Through combined experimental characterisation and development of an industrially applicable simulation framework, the project will support safe and efficient design of complex aerospace components.
More specifically, the project goals are to:
Characterise the fatigue properties and stiffness degradation of a relevant prototype textile reinforced composite material system under pure cyclic tension-tension loading.
Develop an industrially applicable and computationally efficient ply-level macroscale fatigue model that describes how damage evolves under varying load amplitudes and thermal conditions.
Combine the novel ply-level fatigue model with an existing state-of-the-art inter-laminar fatigue damage model into a complete fatigue life assessment framework.
Accelerate the computational efficiency of the framework by utilising novel cycle extrapolation techniques to represent the effect of fatigue loading over many cycles at a time.
Evaluate realistic but critical thermomechanical fatigue cycles through a combined experimental-simulation approach.
Enable industrial adoption of the proposed fatigue assessment framework into future design procedures at GKN Aerospace.

Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in  Applied Mechanics, Structural Engineering, Computational Engineering, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics or similar.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Documented experience (education/courses or thesis project with high grades) in continuum mechanics, advanced finite element method and the mechanics of fibre-reinforced polymers
Interest and high skills in programming and numerical methods

*for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
We also expect that you are analytical, ambitious, independent, and a strong team player that thrives through collaboration.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Documented knowledge in experimental testing.
Documented knowledge in aerospace applications and/or aeroengines.
Documented knowledge and experience in ANSYS or LS Dyna, including implementation of user subroutines (such as user materials or user elements)

What you will do
Characterise the thermoemechanical tension-tension fatigue behaviour of a prototype composite materials sytem with textile reinforcements.
Develop and implement a complete numerical framework to assess the tension-tension fatigue life of aeroengine components.
Develop your scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research through written scientific publications and oral presentations at international conferences.
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Solid and Structural Mechanics .
Teach on Chalmers' undergraduate level corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than   6 November 2026.
For questions, please contact:
Martin Fagerström
Professor
email: [email protected] , phone: +46 70 224 8731
We look forward to your application!
*** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position.  ***
Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society.
Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

ap:253917.body:
The European Synchrotron, the ESRF, is an international research centre based in Grenoble, France.
Through its innovative engineering, pioneering scientific vision and a strong commitment from its 700 staff members, the ESRF is recognised as one of the top research facilities worldwide. Its particle accelerator produces intense X-ray beams that are used by thousands of scientists each year for experiments in diverse fields such as biology, medicine, environmental sciences, cultural heritage, materials science, and physics.
Supported by 19 countries, the ESRF is an equal opportunity employer and encourages diversity.
As a PhD student at the ESRF, you will investigate grain growth in polycrystalline metals by 4D (3D + time) synchrotron diffraction imaging within the project 4DGG, funded by the French National Research Agency (ANR) and coordinated by the ESRF in partnership with the MATEIS laboratory at INSA Lyon (Wolfgang Ludwig) and CEMEF at Mines Paris, PSL University (Marc Bernacki). Classical models treat grain growth as curvature-driven boundary migration, yet 3D studies show that boundary velocity and curvature are often poorly correlated, pointing to contributions from elastic strain and dislocation substructures that remain to be measured directly in 3D during growth. You will use pink-beam topotomography, developed within the project at beamline ID03, in which rotating the sample about the diffraction vector of a selected grain keeps it in diffraction condition and enables time-resolved 3D imaging of grains and their boundaries during in situ annealing. Combined with dark-field X-ray microscopy (DFXM), 3DXRD and diffraction contrast tomography (DCT), these measurements will follow normal and abnormal grain growth in aluminium, iron and nickel, and provide quantitative input for full-field grain growth models. You will be enrolled in the École Doctorale de Physique at Université Grenoble Alpes (UGA) on a 3-year contract, with Can Yildirim (ESRF) as main supervisor.
Your responsibilities include:
Preparing polycrystalline aluminium, iron and nickel samples and selecting target grains by 3DXRD and DCT.
Designing and performing in situ high-temperature grain growth experiments at ID03 combining pink-beam topotomography, DFXM and 3DXRD/DCT.
Reconstructing and analysing the 4D datasets to quantify grain boundary velocity, curvature, misorientation and elastic strain, in close collaboration with INSA Lyon on topotomographic reconstruction.
Providing experimental input to the full-field simulations of grain growth performed at CEMEF, and comparing measured and simulated microstructure evolution.

Publishing the results, presenting at international conferences, and writing and defending a doctoral thesis at UGA.
You are enthusiastic about physical metallurgy and X-ray science, and motivated by experimental work at a large-scale research facility. You are curious and keen to learn new experimental and data analysis methods, and you enjoy working in a collaborative, international environment. To be considered for this position, you should have:
A Master's degree (or equivalent) in materials science, physics, physical metallurgy or a related field, obtained by the start of the contract and meeting the admission requirements of the UGA École Doctorale de Physique.
Knowledge of crystallography and diffraction.
An interest in physical metallurgy, in particular grain boundaries and grain growth.
A solid programming experience (for example Python or MATLAB) and an interest in image processing and data analysis.
Laboratory experience, for example from a Master's project or internship (sample preparation, EBSD or XRD), is welcome; prior synchrotron experience is an asset
Good communication skills and motivation to work in a multidisciplinary team.
Good command of English (working language at the ESRF).

Your shall be enrolled in UGA University / Doctoral School as a condition of your hiring.
Contract of two years renewable for one year.
Do you recognize yourself in this description? Apply now for your next professional adventure!What makes the ESRF experience unique...
Join an innovative international research institute, with a workforce from 38 different countries
Collaborate with global experts to advance science and address societal challenges
Come and live in a vibrant city, in the heart of the Alps, and Europe's Green Capital 2022
Enjoy a workplace designed to support your quality of life
Benefit from our competitive compensation and allowances package, including financial support for your relocation to Grenoble For further information on employment terms and conditions, please refer to "What we offer" section of our Careers page https://www.esrf.fr/Jobs The ESRF is an equal opportunity employer and encourages applications from disabled persons.

ap:253925.body:
Project

The proposed PhD project "Optimizing Digital Uptake: An Interdisciplinary Evaluation of Blended Micro-Certifications for Frontline Extension in Ethiopia" forms part of the VLIRUOS TEAM project EQUIP, in which Arba Minch University (AMU), KU Leuven and Arba Minch College of Teacher Education (AMCTE) collaborate to strengthen the professional practice of Health Extension Workers (HEWs) and Development Agents (DAs) in Southern Ethiopia through inclusive, low-bandwidth digital and blended learning. EQUIP will establish a Digital Learning Hub at Arba Minch University, co-create health and agriculture micro-certifications with the Gamo Zone bureau, and test offline-first learning approaches designed for remote and low-connectivity settings. Gender, location and other barriers to participation will be addressed through the PROGRESS-Plus equity framework and iterative design-based research.

The PhD candidate will lead an equity-adaptive design-based research program examining which combinations of instructional design, motivational design, low-bandwidth technology and field coaching produce meaningful learning and sustained changes in frontline practice. The PhD candidate will work across the health–agriculture–education nexus and will help translate evidence into institutional standards, micro-certification design, Continuing Professional Development (CPD) recognition and implementation guidance.

The final research questions and methods will be refined with the selected PhD candidate and supervisors, reviewed by the Scientific Quality Cell, and submitted for the required scientific, ethics and data-protection approvals. The approved project anticipates iterative prototyping, mixed-method evaluation, disaggregated learning analytics and field-based competency assessment across selected Gamo Zone woredas.

The main responsibilities of the candidate will be to

develop a rigorous doctoral proposal and equity-adaptive design-based research protocol

conduct literature review, stakeholder/needs assessment and baseline research

obtain and comply with ethics, informed-consent and data-protection approvals

coordinate iterative design, pilot, evaluation and redesign cycles for the health and agriculture micro-certification tracks

evaluate access, usability, learning, competency gain and application in frontline practice, with attention to gender and remote locations

work with HEWs, DAs, zonal supervisors/Field Coaches, AMU/AMCTE staff, technical teams and policy partners

integrate quantitative, qualitative and learning-analytics evidence

contribute scientifically to the project’s behavioral-change, credential-value, cost and sustainability questions

coordinate research linkages with four MSc projects and support MSc researchers (without replacing their supervisors)

produce timely progress reports, peer-reviewed manuscripts, conference contributions, policy/practice briefs, open research outputs where appropriate, and a doctoral thesis

contribute to the Digital Learning Hub, E-learning Champion training and project learning events

comply with AMU, KU Leuven and VLIRUOS research-integrity, safeguarding, financial, visibility and scholarship requirements

Profile

The applicant must

preferably be a permanent AMU academic staff member, appointment and continued institutional affiliation must be verifiable

hold a relevant master’s degree in Computer Science or related fields

meet the applicable academic admission requirements of AMU including NGAT and the agreed KU Leuven doctoral/visiting doctoral route

demonstrate research readiness through a strong master’s record, thesis/research experience and a feasible concept note

demonstrate aptitude and genuine interest in digital pedagogy, adult learning and inclusive low-bandwidth design

be able to conduct interdisciplinary mixed-method research and work respectfully with non-academic stakeholders and rural frontline workers

have a sufficient command of English for doctoral research and international collaboration, and be willing to provide any formal evidence or training required by the doctoral authorities

be available for the full doctoral trajectory and for the approved research stays in Belgium (6 months in Activity Year 1, 12 months in Activity Year 3 and 6 months in Activity Year 5, subject to admission, visa and mobility administration)

obtain a signed AMU/department commitment for meaningful study leave from normal academic/administrative duties, continued employment/salary and reintegration/retention during and after the doctorate

pass the eligibility (CGPA, Publication, interview and/or written) exam to be administered by the project as per the Grant and Collaborative Projects guidelines of AMU

be eligible for a VLIRUOS project scholarship, including the applicable institutional-affiliation and nationality requirements

Desirable Experience :

Design-based research, implementation research or program evaluation

Mixed-method study design, statistics and qualitative analysis

Adult learning, instructional design, e-learning, HCI/UX or educational technology

Working with health or agriculture extension systems and public-sector stakeholders

Affinity with gender, inclusion, PROGRESS-Plus or other equity analysis

Mobile/offline digital tools, LMS data or learning analytics

Research ethics, secure data management and reproducible research

Peer-reviewed publication, policy communication or supervision/mentoring

Project coordination and ability to deliver across disciplines and institutions

Note: No single applicant is expected to be an expert in every desirable area. The committee will assess research potential, thematic fit, learning ability and the strength of the complete profile.

Offer

Scholarship and Institutional Support

The selected scholar will remain an AMU staff member. AMU’s agreed employment, salary and study leave arrangements will apply while the scholar conducts research in Ethiopia.

During approved research stays in Belgium, the current budget provides a research scholarship allowance of EUR 1,900 per month, subject to the applicable VLIRUOS framework and final scholarship administration.

The approved project budget provides financing for a research stay of 24 months in Belgium spread across three mobilities and includes budgeted international travel. Scholarship and travel payments remain subject to admission, registration, visa, mobility and financial procedures.

Approved project research and fieldwork costs in Ethiopia will be covered according to the project work plan and financial rules. There is no separate local PhD stipend in the approved budget.

The scholarship allowance is a compensation for living costs during the approved stays in Belgium.

The researcher will receive joint scientific supervision from AMU and KU Leuven, access to the EQUIP research network and appropriate project facilities.

The application should include the following documents in order :
1. Cover page with name, AMU Faculty/department, Staff ID, contact details, and document checklist
2. Motivation letter, maximum two pages
3. Curriculum vitae, including education, employment, research, publications/outputs, methods/software, teaching, service, languages, and two referees
4. Concept note of 1,500-2,000 words excluding references and containing the
* Problem statement and relevance to EQUIP
* Proposed research questions
* Conceptual/design-based research approach
* Proposed quantitative and qualitative methods
* Gender, location, and inclusion considerations
* Ethics and data-protection considerations
* Expected scientific and practical outputs
* High-level four-to-five-year work plan aligned with the three stays in Belgium
5. Master’s and bachelor’s degree certificates and complete transcripts
6. Master’s thesis abstracts plus one sample publication
7. Evidence of current permanent AMU employment
8. Signed faculty/department/unit head letter confirming in-principle study leave, continued employment/salary, and reintegration
9. Available evidence of English proficiency
10. Signed declaration of accuracy, availability, conflicts of interest, and consent to process application data

The following selection procedure will be applicable :

Administrative eligibility screening against the mandatory criteria

Independent scoring of eligible written applications by the joint selection panel using the published criteria and as per AMU grant and collaborative projects guidelines

Shortlisted candidates complete a short research/methods exercise and give a structured presentation/interview online or at AMU

References, credentials, employment status and institutional-study leave feasibility are verified

The joint committee records a ranked recommendation. The Project Steering Committee endorses the final selection as required by the approved proposal; university admission remains with the competent academic authorities

Selection remains conditional on AMU and KU Leuven academic admission, the applicable scholarship/visa route and final institutional approvals

Disclaimer
AMU and KU Leuven are committed to a fair, transparent and inclusive call process. Female applicants and qualified staff from groups or locations under-represented in research leadership are strongly encouraged to apply. The same merit criteria will be applied to all candidates; where candidates are substantially equal, the project’s approved gender and inclusion commitments may be used as a documented tie-break in accordance with applicable policy.

Interested?

For more information please contact Dr. Mohammed Abebe, mail: [email protected] , Prof. dr. Wim Van Petegem, mail: [email protected] or Prof. dr. ir. Koen Eneman, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

ap:253926.body:
Do you want to contribute to ethnographic research into the politics of valuing seaweed in Scotland?

The Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, based within the Faculty of Social Sciences, is looking for an ambitious PhD-candidate to study the impacts of economization of seaweed as part of ‘blue economy’ strategies in Scotland. Research focuses on the impacts on coastal communities considering that in Scotland colonial legacies still influence patterns of unequal access to and use of coastal areas. You will work within the project ‘Entangled in seaweed: The politics of economising nature in Scotland and South Africa’ funded by an NWO Open Competition grant.

Project Description

The project investigates the impacts of economisation of seaweed as part of a global drive to develop ‘blue economy’ strategies. Seaweed harvesting and cultivation (as food, or fertilizer- and bioplastic ingredient) are increasing considerably and promoted as contributing to sustainable development. The project focuses on coastal communities in Scotland, which has developed a comprehensive blue economy strategy. Building on insights from political ecology and valuation studies and inspired by the multispecies turn in anthropology, this project aims to study local impacts of new forms of economisation of seaweed, and the possible contestations these may entail. It seeks to incorporate the ideas, interests, and knowledge from local groups who live from, in and with seaweed ecologies, examining how new versions of economisation affect local social relations, including the entanglements with non-humans these ecologies and economisations depend on. It does so by focusing on valuations of seaweed ecologies, based on an understanding of values as enacted through practices by all (human and non-human) stakeholders. The project employs a collaborative approach vis-à-vis research participants and a wider audience through a visual storytelling approach.

What you will do

You will work in a project team consisting of two PhD-candidates and researchers at Leiden University, collaborating with project partners in Scotland. You will:

Develop a research proposal in the context of the overall project theme, and conduct twelve months of ethnographic research in Scotland. An ethics review and contribution to the data management plan are included in the proposal development. Research includes historical document/policy analysis, participant observation, interviews, and the application of participatory visual storytelling methods.
Analyse research findings and write a dissertation that contributes to the objectives of the ‘Entangled with Seaweed’ project.
Actively contribute to the output and dissemination of the research project, which includes collaborating with the other team members on academic and non-academic publications, science communication, and the organisation of workshops, seminars and an exhibition.
Participate in relevant PhD-courses and masterclasses, organised in accordance with the guidelines of the Faculty of Social Science and the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology. PhD-courses at the University of Edinburgh, our partner in the project, can be included in the individual training and supervision plan as well.
Participate in the PhD programme and other academic activities of the Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology at Leiden University. During your stay in Scotland you will also be able to participate in the PhD-programme at the University of Edinburgh as well as academic activities organised by the Scottish Association for Marine Science (SAMS).

Where you will work

The Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences consists of five institutes: the Centre for Science and Technology Studies, Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology, Education and Child Studies, Political Science, and Psychology. The faculty is home to approximately 7,000 students and 1,000 staff members. Our institutes are dedicated not only to education but also to groundbreaking research that expands our understanding of human behavior and societal structures. What makes our faculty unique is the diversity of research topics, the variety of teaching approaches, and the structure of professional support. This provides you with the opportunity to explore and develop your interests and expertise. For an introduction to our faculty, visit our website: Welcome to the Leiden Faculty of Social and Behavioural Sciences – Leiden University .

Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology (CADS)
Leiden University's Institute of Cultural Anthropology and Development Sociology concentrates on 'global vulnerability and social resilience'. The institute has three main themes: diversity, sustainability, and digitalisation. CADS is dedicated to making a real-world impact, not just studying change, but also working with communities to promote positive change through education and research. We use a unique approach that blends qualitative, quantitative, audiovisual, and digital methods based on ethnographic fieldwork.
With our unique blend of interdisciplinary interests, comparative regional studies, and social science research methods, we emphasize our role in the extensive collaborative network within Leiden University. In both our research and education, we engage in extensive interdisciplinary and international networks.

The project team
The project team at Leiden University works closely together with colleagues at the University of Edinburgh, the Scottish Association for Marine Science, and Stellenbosch University. The PhD-students will be jointly supervised by Leiden University and Stellenbosch University, and Leiden University and the University of Edinburgh respectively. A project assistant will assist with training and dissemination activities.

What you bring

A Master’s degree in Anthropology, Sociology, Environmental Humanities, Science and Technology Studies, or another relevant discipline within the social sciences or humanities.
Demonstrable excellent qualitative research skills and experience with ethnographic fieldwork.
Affinity with the topics of sustainability and environmental justice.
Excellent oral and written communication skills.
Strong command of English;
Knowledge of one of the other official languages of Scotland (Scots, Scottish Gaelic) is a bonus.
Excellent social and organisational skills and the ability to work independently as well as in a team.

What we offer

Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University.

We also offer:
PHD: An employment contract for 38 hours per week as a PhD candidate, initially for a period of 1 year, with the possibility of extension for 3 years after a positive evaluation. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;
A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student);

A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;

Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;

Flexible working hours: as a standard, you are entitled to a minimum of 29 leave days on the basis of a full-time working week of 38 hours; you can also save for extra leave, for example by working 40 hours a week, and in this way accrue an extra 96 leave hours, or exchange 96 leave hours for a 36-hour week.

Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription and bicycle scheme;

If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;

A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop and a mobile telephone.

For more information about employment conditions, see  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value

Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research.

Want to apply or find out more?

If you want to apply straight away, click the application button.

As part of your application we ask you to submit:

ap:253941.body:
The Faculty of Law at the University of Lapland is recruiting one (1) Junior Researcher for the “Arctic Transitions, Energy and Climate Governance Horizons in the Far North” project.
The aim of the Arctic Transitions (AT) project is to critically examine how rapidly changing climatic conditions and a race to extract rare and valuable earth materials have made Arctic regions the focus of new extractive possibilities, as well as a laboratory for testing who controls these possibilities.
To meet this aim, the AT project is hiring a team to conduct comparative multidisciplinary research at locations across Arctic nations to explore:
How and why changing climatic conditions and new resource demands are shaping extraction activities, infrastructures, security configurations, and governance arrangements.
The impact of these activities and arrangements on the people and communities who live in these regions.
How and why energy security and energy transition narratives are being mobilised, by whom, and to what end.
How and why these activities, infrastructures, configurations and arrangements are connected to, and entangled with, international legal provisions and flows of capital.

This is an exciting and unique opportunity to be a core junior member of a cutting-edge research team, in an area of research that is fast-moving and of geopolitical significance.
It is a full-time, funded, 36-month research position, based in Rovaniemi (Finland), with the possibility of remote working. The prospective start date is August 2027.
Work tasks
The successful candidate will be a core member of the Arctic Transitions team. They will carry out independent research, and work in close collaboration with the project’s Principal Investigator (PI). In particular, the selected candidate will:
Conduct independent research under the supervision of the PI.
Complete the requirements for the successful completion of their PhD in the Faculty of Law.
Present research results at national and international conferences.
Contribute to the planning of an international conference to be hosted in Rovaniemi.
Contribute to AT project planning and project administration.
Participate in other duties related to the role assigned by the employer. Tasks in teaching may occur to a small extent.

Competence
Prospective candidates must:
Have a Master’s degree in law, policy, geography, economics, environmental studies, sociology, anthropology, science and technology studies, or related field.
Be proficient in reading, writing, and speaking English at an academic level.

Proficiency in reading, writing, and speaking Finnish will be considered a merit.
What we offer
An opportunity to work in a multidisciplinary research team.
An opportunity to conduct funded primary data collection (qualitative, quantitative, mixed method, etc.).
An opportunity to be a part of an international university community.
Modern work equipment and facilities.
A stable organisation to work in.
Opportunities for professional development.
Extensive occupational health services.
Sport, culture, and wellbeing benefits.

Application
Prospective candidates should submit their application via the University’s electronic application form below. Applications must include:
Cover letter (maximum 1 page)
Curriculum vitae (cv)
Research proposal (max. 2 pages, single spaced, 12-point font)

Research proposals should include:
The region and/or location of the proposed legal research.
The methodological approach to data collection and analysis.

Offer Description
Project: Preventable Harm: How Health System Failures Shape Climate-Demographic Inequality
Institution:  Center for Demographic Research (DEMO), UCLouvain,   Louvain-la-Neuve, Belgium
Position: Full-time doctoral researcher
Application deadline:16 November 2026 at 17:00 CET (Belgian time)
Interviews: Shortlisted candidates are expected to be interviewed in early December 2026
Expected starting date:  February 2027 (negotiable)
Contact: Prof. Risto Conte Keivabu – [email protected]
Position description
The full-time doctoral position in demography is situated at the intersection of population and environment and funded by an FSR project titled " Preventable Harm: How Health System Failures Shape Climate-Demographic Inequality ". The project emphasizes how climate change related environmental exposures affect population processes and inequalities, with particular attention to how health systems and institutional contexts shape vulnerability to environmental risks.
The doctoral research may address a broad range of questions concerning the demographic consequences of climate and environmental change, including effects on health and mortality, fertility, migration and other dimensions of population dynamics. Additionally, projects could engage with understanding inequalities across population groups, places and institutional settings with a focus on the role of health care access, quality and preparedness with the aim to inform relevant policies.
The doctoral researcher will have substantial scope to develop their own research questions within this broader agenda. The project will primarily use quantitative approaches and may combine demographic, administrative or survey data with spatially and temporally detailed information on climate and environmental exposures. Also, the candidate is welcome to pursue research on High-Income and/or Low-Middle-Income countries.
Profile
Applicants should hold, or expected to obtain before taking up the position, a Master's degree or equivalent in demography, sociology, population health, epidemiology, economics, geography, public policy, quantitative social science, statistics/data science, or another closely related field. Applicants must also meet UCLouvain's requirements for admission to doctoral studies for which further information is available at the link: https://uclouvain.be/fr/facultes/espo/conditions-dacces . Applicants still completing their master’s degree may apply provided they expect to meet the admission requirements before starting the doctoral position. Candidates that do not comply with these requirements cannot be considered.
We are particularly interested in candidates with:
•    strong quantitative research skills and an interest in demography, environment, climate change, social inequalities, health and population dynamics;
•    experience with statistical programming, particularly R, Stata or Python;
•    the ability to work independently as well as collaboratively;
•    strong written and spoken English.
Experience with administrative or health data, geospatial/environmental data, causal inference, longitudinal methods is an advantage but is not required. Knowledge of French is not required but preferable.
Candidates are encouraged to apply even if they do not meet every listed skill or area of experience, and applicants from a wide range of disciplinary and social backgrounds are very welcome.
Working conditions
The position is based at UCLouvain in Louvain-la-Neuve and is embedded in the Center for Demographic Research (DEMO). The doctoral researcher is expected to reside in Belgium and to participate actively in the scientific life of the research center, including seminars and collaborative activities and engage in an international research environment.
The position is full-time and funded through an FSR doctoral scholarship for an initial period of 24 months. Progress will be reviewed during the doctoral programme and follow-up funding for additional 24 months will be sought jointly by the candidate and supervisor through relevant funding schemes.
Remuneration and social benefits follow the applicable UCLouvain rules for doctoral scholarship holders.
How to apply
Applications must be submitted through this online form: https://surveys.uclouvain.be/index.php/911318  by 16 November 2026 at 17:00 Belgian time.
Please upload one PDF file containing the following documents, in this order:
1.     Motivation letter (maximum 2 pages), explaining your motivation for applying, your research interests and their fit with the project, and your relevant methodological and substantive experience. In case the Master degree is still ongoing please provide here an expected date of completion;
2.     Curriculum vitae  (maximum 2 pages);
3.     Bachelor's and Master's degree certificates and academic transcripts, as well as any other relevant academic records (if your Master's degree has not yet been completed, please provide a certificate of enrolment and your most recent academic transcript);
4.     Contact details of two academic referees (name, position, institution and email address). Reference letters are not required at this stage; referees may be contacted for shortlisted candidates;
5.     One example of academic or research-oriented written work, such as a Master's thesis, Bachelor's thesis, research paper, working paper or published article. If the document is long, a relevant chapter or excerpt is sufficient.

ap:253944.body:
Quantum computing devices are rapidly increasing in scale and complexity. However they are still very far away from the abstract ideal of a computer, and an important part of making them better is designing procedures that characterize errors and noise in an efficient and robust.  Do you enjoy working at the intersection between physics and computer science? Are you comfortable with mathematical work and interested in applying those skills in a practical setting? Then CWI invites you to apply for a PhD position where you will research testing and learning algorithms for fault-tolerant quantum computers in the context of the EQUATE ERC starting grant project, supervised by Dr. Jonas Helsen.
Job description
As part of your PhD project, you will develop and mathematically analyze new methods for extracting information from quantum computers, with a focus on testing and learning algorithms and their interactions with quantum error correction.
Possible research directions include (but are not limited to):
-Testing and learning under resource restrictions (specifically the “low-magic” setting)
-Testing and learning of QEC relevant properties such as membership of the Clifford hierarchy
-The interaction of (logical) noise with learning algorithms
You will:
- Research fault-tolerant quantum computing, developing new testing and learning algorithms and analyzing their properties.
- Work with colleagues on translating these theoretical algorithms to a more practical setting, perhaps even all the way down to real experiments.
- Publish and present your work in international conferences and journals.
- Be an active part of the local research groups at CWI and QuSoft.
Requirements
Candidates are required to have a Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Physics, Computer Science, Mathematics, or a related subject.
Preferable qualifications for candidates include proven research talent, an excellent command of English and good academic writing and presentation skills.
Furthermore, we ask for previously demonstrated interest in quantum computing, in the form of coursework, projects, or academic publications and a high motivation in pursuing academic research.

Terms and conditions
The terms of employment are in accordance with the Dutch Collective Labour Agreement for Research Centres ("CAO-onderzoeksinstellingen"). The initial labour agreement will be for a period of 18 months. After a positive evaluation, the agreement will be extended by 30 months. The gross monthly salary, for a PhD student on a full time basis, is € 3,115 during the first year and increases to €3,989 over the four year period. Employees are also entitled to a holiday allowance of 8% of the gross annual salary and a year-end bonus of 8.33%. CWI offers attractive working conditions, including flexible scheduling and help with housing for expat employees.
Please visit the CWI website for more information about our terms of employment’ , or go to the working pages of the NWO website
Information and application
All applications should include a detailed resume, motivation letter, list of your MSc courses and grades, copy of your Master’s thesis and preferably a list of publications and two references.
The deadline for the application is 10 December 2026. Evaluation of candidates will begin immediately, and will continue until the position is filled. We aim to start the project on the 1st of March 2027, however starting dates can be negotiated.
For more information about the vacancy, please contact Dr. Jonas Helsen, email:  [email protected] .
Diversity code
CWI strives to be a diverse and inclusive research institute. To achieve balanced representation in positions, we have been investing in a diverse and inclusive organization already since 2010, among others by prioritizing applications from women researchers. This approach has recently led to hiring a majority of women in Tenure Track positions.
CWI encourages a diverse workforce: we endeavour to develop talent and creativity by bringing people from different backgrounds and cultures together. We strongly encourage candidates with the appropriate qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, origin, sexual orientation or physical abilities.
About CWI
Centrum Wiskunde & Informatica (CWI) is the Dutch national research institute for mathematics and computer science and is part of the Institutes Organisation of the Dutch Research Council (NWO) . The mission of CWI is to conduct pioneering research in mathematics and computer science, generating new knowledge in these fields and conveying it to trade, industry, and society at large.
CWI is an internationally oriented institute, with 160 scientists from approximately 27 countries, an informal atmosphere and short lines of communication. We have an activity committee that organizes after-work activities and among others a women’s network.
CWI is located at Science Park Amsterdam, which is a major location of research in the physical sciences in The Netherlands, housing the sciences of the University of Amsterdam as well as several other national research institutes next to CWI.
About Research group
QuSoft is the Dutch research Center for Quantum Software that was launched in 2015. Its mission is to develop new communication protocols, algorithms, and applications for small and medium-sized prototypes as well as larger quantum computers. The researchers at QuSoft develop software and applications that exploit the extraordinary power of quantum computers based on their quantum mechanical properties such as superposition, interference and entanglement. To find more information about QuSoft and the Algorithms and Complexity group, please visit their webpages and watch their video.  https://www.cwi.nl/research/groups/algorithms-and-complexity   http://www.qusoft.org/

Doctoral Position in Risk-Based Inspection and Maintenance Planning of Tunnels
The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a doctoral student. This position focuses risk-based inspection and maintenance planning for tunnels, including probabilistic risk updating, Value of Information analysis, and intervention program optimisation. This position is part of an interdisciplinary SNSF project in collaboration with the Free University of Bozen-Bolzano, the Hagerbach Test Gallery, and the EuroTube Foundation.

The preferred starting date is 1 February 2027, although other dates are negotiable.

Project background
Tunnels are critical links in transport networks, and many Swiss road and rail tunnels are ageing while being subject to increasing traffic loads, climate-related stressors, and evolving safety requirements. Their maintenance involves two interdependent asset domains, namely structural elements, such as lining, portals, and drainage, and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing systems, such as ventilation, lighting, and fire detection. In current practice, these domains are managed largely in isolation, inspections remain heavily manual, and evidence from different campaigns, sensors, and specialists is fragmented across separate reports and databases. Interventions are therefore often planned using disjointed evidence and conservative heuristics, even where substantial data exist.

The project Predictive, Resilient, Integrated Systems for Management of Tunnel (PRISM-T), funded by the SNSF, addresses this challenge through an integrated digital twin workflow for tunnel maintenance decision support. Heterogeneous inspection and monitoring evidence is transformed into uncertainty-aware condition indicators, which are used to update risk, to assess whether additional information is worth collecting, and to derive executable intervention programs. Extended reality (XR) is used to validate decisions and to guide inspection and maintenance work on site.

The workflow is developed and validated in the Tunnel Digitalisation Centre of the Hagerbach Test Gallery in Flums, and its transferability is tested at the DemoTube facility of the EuroTube Foundation in Dübendorf. Regular field work at both sites and close collaboration with the partner team in Bolzano form an integral part of the doctoral research.

Within this project, the doctoral position addresses the decision layer of the workflow, in which maintenance decision processes are formalised and uncertainty-aware condition indicators, developed in a companion doctoral position, are used to update risk and to optimise intervention programs under realistic tunnel constraints.

Job description
The successful candidate will map and formalise current tunnel maintenance decision processes for the structural and mechanical, electrical, and plumbing domains through workshops and interviews with practitioners. On this basis, risk and consequence models based on Bayesian networks will be formulated, and incremental risk updating methods will be developed. A computationally tractable Value of Information analysis will be developed using approximation strategies, such as surrogate models and scenario reduction. Intervention program optimisation models accounting for sequencing, bundling, access windows, and resource constraints will be formulated and solved, with outputs traceable to the underlying evidence. The candidate will contribute to validation campaigns at the Hagerbach Test Gallery and the EuroTube Foundation.

Profile

A Master’s degree in civil engineering, operations research, industrial engineering, applied mathematics, or a related field

A strong background in probabilistic modelling, reliability and risk analysis, and mathematical optimisation

Very good programming skills, preferably in Python, and experience with optimisation solvers

Familiarity with infrastructure asset management, Bayesian networks, decision analysis, Value of Information analysis, or business process modelling would be considered an advantage

Willingness to carry out field work in underground environments and to collaborate within an interdisciplinary and international team

Proficiency in written and spoken English is required, and knowledge of German is regarded as an asset

The Chair of Infrastructure Management, led by Professor Dr. Bryan T. Adey within the Institute of Construction and Infrastructure Management of the Department of Civil, Environmental and Geomatic Engineering, has an opening for a doctoral student. Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder, Fakultet for kunstfag, er det ledig en til to 100% stillinger som doktorgradsstipendiat, tilknyttet Institutt for visuelle og sceniske fag, for en periode på tre år. Arbeidssted er Campus Kristiansand. Tiltredelse etter avtale med fakultetet.
Fakultet for kunstfag har ca. 530 studenter og 90 ansatte i vitenskapelige stillinger. Fakultetet består av Institutt for visuelle og sceniske fag, Institutt for klassisk musikk og musikkpedagogikk og Institutt for rytmisk musikk.
Fakultetet har forskningsmiljøer innen rytmisk musikk, klassisk musikk, musikkpedagogikk, visuell kunst og scenekunst, med to doktorgradsprogrammer, Ph.d.-program i kunstfag og ph.d.-program i kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid .
Denne stillingen knyttes til program for ph.d. i kunstfag.
Institutt for visuelle og sceniske fag tilbyr ph.d.-spesialisering i «Kunst i kontekst» (KiK), mastergrad i kunstfag, bachelorgrad i teater, skuespill og regi og en bachelorgrad i visuell kunst og formidling, i tillegg til flere årsstudier og en rekke emner innenfor lærerutdanningene. Instituttet anvender et bredt og åpent kunstbegrep, og studietilbudene kombinerer didaktisk, vitenskapelig og utøvende/skapende praksis.
Arbeidsoppgaver
Stillingen inngår i fakultetets forskningsplattform Kunst i kontekst .
Ph.d.-prosjektet skal gi et bidrag til forskningsfeltet innen visuell kunst. Tema for doktorgradsprosjektet skal være knyttet til kunstens rolle i utdanning og samfunn, og hvordan kunstpraksiser og kunstmøter erfares og tillegges betydning. Av særlig interesse er prosjekter som utforsker kunstens betydning og legitimering i skole, lærerutdanning, kulturinstitusjoner, Den kulturelle skolesekken eller på andre samfunnsarenaer. Det er ønskelig at prosjektet benytter praksisnære, kunstbaserte og/eller deltakende forskningstilnærminger. Det kan være aktuelt å knytte prosjektet til pågående eller framtidige eksternt finansierte forskningsprosjekter ved Fakultet for kunstfag.
Ph.d.-programmet i kunstfag åpner opp for to ulike avhandlingsformater; vitenskapelig avhandling og kombinert kunstnerisk vitenskapelig avhandling. Søkerne til stillingen skal opplyse i søknaden hvilket avhandlingsformat de ønsker å arbeide med. For nærmere opplysninger, se informasjon om programmets innhold og læringsutbytte.
Det er en forutsetning for ansettelse at fakultetet har veiledningskapasitet og infrastruktur som er nødvendig for å realisere ph.d.-prosjektet.
Basert på det ovenstående, inviterer vi aktuelle søkere til å utarbeide en prosjektbeskrivelse.

Mastergrad eller tilsvarende høyere utdanning innen visuelle kunstfag og/eller fagdidaktikk i kunst og håndverk, kunst, design og arkitektur. Om søkeren har en tverrestetisk mastergrad må fordypning innen visuelle kunstfag dokumenteres.
Den som ansettes må beherske norsk eller et annet skandinavisk språk, skriftlig og muntlig. Avhandlingen kan gjerne skrives på engelsk.
Gode engelskkunnskaper, både skriftlig og muntlig. Engelskkunnskapene kan bli nærmere vurdert under intervjuet

ap:253956.body:
Vill du vara med och bygga ett nytt internationellt kunskapsnav för forskning om undervisning och skolutveckling? Karlstads universitet och forskningsmiljön Research on Subject-specific Education (Rose) söker nu fyra internationellt framstående forskare till meriteringsanställningar inom ämnesdidaktik. Som biträdande lektor får du möjlighet att utveckla din egen forskning och samtidigt vara med och forma ett framväxande forskningsfält: ämnesdidaktisk skolutveckling.
Karlstads universitet och forskningsmiljön Research on Subject-specific Education, Rose, bedriver internationellt erkänd forskning inom ämnesdidaktik. Rose erbjuder nu fyra nya meriteringsanställningar inom ramen för en långsiktig satsning på forskning av högsta kvalitet.
Rose är ett centralt profilområde vid Karlstads universitet och samlar omkring 50 seniora och juniora forskare samt cirka 30 doktorander. Forskningsmiljön präglas av jämförande och tvärvetenskapliga perspektiv på undervisning, lärande och skolutveckling.
Tillsammans med Göteborgs universitet bygger Rose, inom ramen för en statlig satsning på excellens i skolan, ett ledande internationellt kunskapsnav: Centre for Teaching and Learning in Schools (CTL). Centret sammanför tre forskningsområden: ämnesdidaktik, kunskapsbedömning och lärandets villkor samt skolledarskap. Målet är att främja alla elevers kunskapsutveckling.
Totalt rekryteras åtta nya biträdande lektorer till centret, varav fyra till Karlstads universitet.
Var med och forma ett nytt forskningsfält
Som biträdande lektor blir du en del av en grupp om fyra forskare inom ämnesdidaktik. Tillsammans med ett dynamiskt och innovativt forskarteam får du möjlighet att utveckla ett nytt forskningsfält med fokus på hur forskning kan bidra till konkret utveckling av undervisning och skola.
Du kommer bland annat att utveckla och implementera undervisningsinnovationer med utgångspunkt i olika skolämnen. Anställningen är knuten till något av följande ämnen:
biologi
samhällskunskap
historia
engelska
matematik

En meriteringsanställning med möjlighet att växa som forskare
Vi söker internationellt erkända forskare med doktorsexamen och eventuellt postdoktoral erfarenhet, som vill utveckla sin självständighet som forskare och bidra till den fortsatta utvecklingen av ämnesdidaktisk forskning.
Anställningen som biträdande lektor är en meriteringsanställning där du får möjlighet att bygga vetenskapliga och pedagogiska meriter för att därefter uppfylla kraven för en tillsvidareanställning som universitetslektor för att sedan fortsätta utforska möjligheterna till vidare akademisk utveckling.
Se vidare Högskoleförordningen, 4 kap. samt i: Karlstads universitets anställningsordning .
En internationell och attraktiv arbetsplats
På Karlstads universitet möter du en livlig och internationell arbetsplats med studenter, medarbetare och besökare från hela världen. Vi erbjuder generösa semester- och friskvårdsförmåner samt en förmånlig tjänstepension.
Anställningen är på heltid och tidsbegränsad till fem år, med preliminär start den 1 mars 2027 eller enligt överenskommelse.
Läs mer och sök senast den 15 november:
Biträdande lektor i engelsk språk- eller litteraturdidaktik.
Biträdande lektor i samhällsvetenskapliga ämnenas didaktik.
Biträdande lektor i biologins didaktik/ naturvetenskapernas didaktik.
Biträdande lektor i matematikens didaktik.
Välkommen med din ansökan!

ap:253963.body:
We invite applications for two Doctoral positions in experimental quantum computing with superconducting circuits. You will work in the stimulating research environment of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology ( WACQT ), a 12-year initiative started in 2018 with the purpose of advancing Swedish academia and industry to the forefront of quantum technology. The core project of the centre is to build a quantum computer based on superconducting circuits. You will be part of the Quantum Computing group  in the Quantum Technology Laboratory (QTL) division of the Microtechnology and Nanoscience (MC2) department, working in a large team of PhDs, postdocs and researchers.
About us
The Department of Microtechnology and Nanoscience advances the frontiers in quantum technology, nanoscience, photonics and future electronic systems - for technical and societal development. Our cross-disciplinary approach gives interesting collaborations in academy, industry and society, and is a driving force for innovations, results and breakthroughs. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.
At the Quantum Technology Laboratory , we explore how quantum physics can unlock radically new ways of processing information - far beyond the limits of classical systems. Our research spans quantum computing, sensing, transduction, thermodynamics, and foundations, all aimed at harnessing the powerful behavior of light and matter at the quantum level. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.
About the research project
We are seeking Doctoral students to work on building the next generation of large-scale quantum processors based on superconducting circuits. To achieve this ambitious goal, we currently have projects related to:
• Development and optimization of nano-fabrication processes for superconducting devices
• Design and microwave simulation of quantum processors
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Physics, Applied Physics, Nanotechnology.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Experience in one or more of the following areas: superconducting circuits, experimental quantum computing, quantum optics, or a related field within experimental physics.
You are passionate about quantum technology and eager to contribute to its future development.
You thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy sharing knowledge, and take responsibility for your work.
You have a strong analytical mindset, pay attention to detail, and enjoy tackling complex challenges.
You are keen to contribute to the development of students through supervision and mentoring.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience in nanofabrication, microwave measurements, cryogenics, microwave simulations, experimental quantum computing

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of the Department of Microtechnology and Nanoscience
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing
The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours
Contribute to the development of next-generation superconducting quantum processors, working in one of the following research areas: Nanofabrication of superconducting quantum devices: Develop and optimize fabrication processes to improve device performance, reproducibility, and scalability. Investigate different materials and fabrication techniques to understand and mitigate sources of loss in superconducting circuits.
Design and simulation of quantum processors: Design superconducting circuits and perform electromagnetic and microwave simulations to optimize device performance and support the development of larger-scale quantum processors.

Work closely with experimentalists, theorists, and engineers in an interdisciplinary research environment, contributing to the development and testing of quantum hardware.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.
State which project you would prefer

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  5 November.
Interviews will be conducted on an ongoing basis during the recruitment process.
For questions, please contact:
Dr. Giovanna Tancredi
[email protected]
Links: WACQT , QTL
We look forward to your application!
*** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position.  ***
Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society.
Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

Fakultetet har forskningsmiljøer innen rytmisk musikk, klassisk musikk, musikkpedagogikk, visuell kunst og scenekunst, med to doktorgradsprogrammer, Ph.d.-program i kunstfag og ph.d.-program i kunstnerisk utviklingsarbeid .
