EPFL, the Swiss Federal Institute of Technology in Lausanne, is one of the most dynamic university campuses in Europe and ranks among the top 20 universities worldwide. The EPFL employs more than 6,500 people supporting the three main missions of the institutions: education, research and innovation. The EPFL campus offers an exceptional working environment at the heart of a community of more than 18,500 people, including over 14,000 students and 4,000 researchers from more than 120 different countries.
PhD Student Position in Numerical Modeling and Design of Plasmonic Crystals for Solar Energy
Mission
We are seeking a candidate with experience in numerical modeling of nanostructured materials to join our SNSF project “Coupled oscillations in plasmonic crystals”.
In this project, we focus on the effects of coupling of plasmonic oscillations in metallic micro-/nanostructures. It might be possible to achieve plasmonic crystals featuring broad frequency bands of extraordinary optical transmission (EOT) in the UV-VIS-NIR spectral range. The insights from this project will have considerable impact on the fields of photovoltaics, flat screens and flexible displays, as well as energy efficient OLED lighting, electrochromic devices and energy-efficient insulating glazing.
Research Group SCI-ENAC-AS: Nanotechnology for Solar Energy Conversion
Prof. Andreas Schüler
In our research group, we develop novel micro- and nanostructured smart materials for active and passive solar energy applications being integrated into the building envelope. We focus on thin films, because these allow covering a large surface area with a small quantity of raw material - and we focus on their electronic and optical properties, because these closely interrelated properties are most important for the use of solar energy.
https://www.epfl.ch/labs/sci-enac-as/
Main duties and responsibilities
As a PhD Student, you will be expected to:
Assume full responsibility for your PhD dissertation;
Perform research in close collaboration with other lab members and international collaborators;
Design and execute experiments;
Analyze and interpret experimental results;
Write scientific articles for publication in peer-reviewed journals;
Present at international conferences;
Contribute to teaching, coach Master students and provide basic administrative support.

Profile
An excellent Master’s-level degree in Physics, Optics, Micro-/Nanotechnology, Materials Science, Energy, or a related quantitative field
A strong background in several of the following fields: theory of light-matter interaction, computer simulations using the method of Finite Differences in the Time Domain (FDTD), determination of optical material constants by multiangle UV-VIS-NIR ellipsometry, and/or characterization by UV-VIS-NIR spectrophotometry
A sincere interest in micro-/nanostructures, electronic and optical material properties, plasmonics, and solar energy
Proficiency in English (French is a plus)
Strong motivation for academic research, critical thinking, independence, good self-management skills, and excellent team spirit
Interest in a career involving research and teaching is an asset

We offer
A stable position for up to 4 years in order to complete your PhD;
Term of employment: 1-year fixed-term contract (CDD), renewable for 4 years
An international research environment
Individual and intensive supervision of your PhD project
Financial support in accordance with EPFL doctoral student conditions
The opportunity to work on innovative materials in a laboratory with a cutting-edge equipment

Information
Your application should include:
CV
Motivation letter
Diplomas
Transcripts/grades from Bachelor’s and Master’s studies

If you are successful, you will need to enrol in one of the EPFL doctoral school programs in parallel. Please check this page for additional information. Please note that this is a separate application process necessary to be eligible to complete your PhD at EPFL. Potential doctoral program for this position: EDEY, EDCE, EDMX, EDPY
Expected start date : May 1st, 2027. An alternative start date may exceptionally be agreed upon by mutual agreement.
Application : Application deadline is November 30, 2026. Apply through the EPFL job opportunities webpage . Only applications submitted through the online platform are considered. Only shortlisted candidates will be contacted.
For any further information, please contact [email protected]

ap:254087.body:
Let’s shape the future - University of Antwerp
The University of Antwerp is a dynamic, forward-thinking, European university. We offer an innovative academic education to more than 20,000 students, conducting pioneering scientific research and playing an important service-providing role in society. We are one of the largest, most international and most innovative employers in the region. With more than 6,000 employees from 100 different countries, we are helping to build tomorrow's world every day. Through top scientific research, we push back boundaries and set a course for the future – a future that you can help to shape.
The research group Applied Electrochemistry and Catalysis ( ELCAT ) in the Faculty of Applied Engineering is looking for a full time (100%) doctoral scholarship holder in the field of redox flow batteries. Batteries will be crucial to transform our society to a sustainable one. As a PhD student you will therefore conduct research to understand how battery design, operating conditions and redox chemistry affect performance and study the influence on lifetime.
Within the research group ELCAT you will find yourself in an excellent research environment consisting of more than 40 researchers and equipped with state-of-the-art lab facilities and research equipment. The scope of ELCAT is situated in the field of electrochemistry and electrochemical engineering. Its scientific activities are related to the development of state-of-the-art electrochemical reactors and batteries, striving towards a green and sustainable industry and society.
Position
You will work actively on the preparation and defence of a PhD thesis in the field of redox flow batteries for renewable energy storage. To guarantee energy supply in the future and keep on incorporating windmills and solar panels in our energy mix, it is crucial that we can store electricity for moments when production levels are too low. Redox flow batteries stand out in the field of energy storage but their performance and cost can still be improved. In this, electrolyte composition and battery design are important and still need to be improved. You will study in a team of researchers the novel titanium-cerium redox chemistry and how it’s electrolyte formulation (e.g. type of acid) affect charge/discharge rate and stability. You will conduct experiments to test how battery design (e.g. flow field design, membrane, scale-up, stacking) with relation to the titanium-cerium electrolyte formulation affects performance (e.g. cross-over, power density, electrolyte precipitation).
You will publish scientific articles and/or patents related to your research.
You also assist in a limited number of teaching tasks and research support to aid in the good day-to-day functioning of the research group and the Faculty of Applied Engineering.

Profile
You hold a Master’s degree in chemical engineering, Master’s degree in applied engineering/industrial science: chemistry, Master’s degree in a related field or equivalent through experience or you will have obtained it by the time you start working.
You can demonstrate excellent study results.
You have a thorough understanding of mass transfer and reactor engineering
You are pro-active and have mind-set for scientific research.
You are enthusiast and highly motivated.
You can work safely in research laboratories, in particular regarding chemical substances.
Experience in performing experiments with electrochemical systems such as redox flow batteries is considered a plus.
You have a good knowledge of English language. You can communicate well, both in speaking and in writing. A C1 in English is considered a plus.
You are strong in planning and organizing; you can work independently.
Your teaching competences are in line with the University of Antwerp’s educational vision .
Your research qualities are in line with the faculty and university research policies .
You act with attention to quality, integrity, creativity and cooperation.
Recommendation letters are highly advised and considered an added value.

What we offer
We offer a doctoral scholarship for a period of one year. Following a positive evaluation, the scholarship can be renewed for a total of 4 years.
The planned start date is preferably 01 January 2027 or sooner.
Your monthly scholarship amount is calculated according to the scholarship amounts for doctoral scholarship holders on the pay scales for Contract Research Staff (Dutch: Bijzonder Academisch Personeel , BAP).
You will receive ecocheques, Internet-connectivity allowance and a bicycle allowance or a full reimbursement of public transport costs for commuting.
You will do most of your work at Campus Drie Eiken (Universiteitsplein 1, 2610 Wilrijk, Belgium) and Campus Groenenborger (Groenenborgerlaan 171, 2020 Antwerpen) in a dynamic and stimulating working environment.
Find out more about working at the University of Antwerp here .

Want to apply?
You can apply for this vacancy through the University of Antwerp’s online job application platform until November 12 th 2026 . Click on the 'Apply' button, complete the online application form and be sure to include the following attachments: a motivation letter and your academic CV.
The selection committee will review all of the applications as soon as possible after the application deadline. As soon as a decision has been made, we will inform you about the next steps in the selection procedure.
If you have any questions about the online application form, please check the frequently asked questions or send an email to [email protected] . If you have specific questions about the position, please contact Prof. Jonas Hereijgers ( [email protected] ). Applications need to be submitted through the online job application platform.

The University of Antwerp received the European Commission’s HR Excellence in Research Award for its HR policy. We are a sustainable, family-friendly organisation which invests in its employees’ growth. We encourage diversity  and attach great importance to an inclusive working environment and equal opportunities, regardless of gender identity, disability, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual orientation or age. We encourage people from diverse backgrounds and with diverse characteristics to apply.

ap:254090.body:
Introduction
Are you passionate about building an entanglement-based routing in quantum optical networks?
Join us to develop an innovative entanglement-based routing architecture and protocol, and set up an experimental testbed to route entangled photons in the presence of classical telecom traffic in multi-node quantum optical fiber networks.

Job Description
Efficient distribution and routing of entanglement are indispensable for quantum‑secure communication (e.g., advanced QKD networks), distributed quantum computing, quantum‑secure enterprise connectivity and quantum teleportation services across metropolitan or regional distances. However, unique features of quantum information, such as non-amplification, no-cloning, or measurement without altering the quantum states, make it difficult to re-use the architecture and protocols of classical telecom networks for quantum communication and networking. In contrast to classical optical signals, quantum states are extremely fragile and degrade rapidly due to loss, noise, and decoherence, especially over long distances. As a result, conventional telecom solutions such as optical amplification, regeneration, and routing cannot be directly applied to quantum networks. Nevertheless, recent advances in quantum state generation and measurement have opened new opportunities for developing quantum network architectures and protocols for routing and teleportation, a critical enabler for quantum networks.
In this PhD project, you will set up an experimental testbed for a multi-node quantum optical fiber network that enables entanglement generation and detection, frequency conversion, and entanglement routing of quantum-classical packets between nodes connected by optical switches. Additionally, you will investigate the coexistence of classical telecom traffic and quantum signals and the effects of impairments such as noise and crosstalk. The project will combine theoretical and simulation studies and validate them with experimental studies. The project will leverage KPN’s expertise to address real‑world constraints—including scalability, interoperability, reliability, and manageability—while developing the telecom‑grade quantum networks.
The PhD position is fully funded by our industry partner (KPN) in Smart Optical Networks Lab  (SONL) of the Electro-Optical Communication group. The research activity of SONL covers a wide range of topics, including network design and software control, reconfigurable interconnects for telecom, datacenters, AI clusters, and quantum networks, down to heterogeneous photonic integrated circuits and systems for enabling low-latency, fast network reconfiguration in real systems. Additionally, we focus on innovative solutions for switching and routing in secure quantum-optical networks. The ECO group covers a wide range of topics from the Photonic layer to the Application layer of the communication system, and we also play a key role in the  Casimir Institute  at TU/e, and within the PhotonDelta and QuantumDelta growth fund program. Besides research you will also contribute to education within our group and the Department of Electrical Engineering and mentor BSc and MSc students during their research projects.

Job Requirements
A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in (applied) physics, electrical engineering, or related subjects.
Solid background in fiber-optic communication, quantum optics, and networks.
Knowledge of programming languages such as Python.
Prior experience with setting up quantum optical communication and network experiments is an asset.
A background in Electronics/FPGA is a plus.
A research-oriented attitude.
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interested in collaborating with industrial partners.
Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.
Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process .
An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs.
A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme ) for international candidates.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .
Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .
The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field.

Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond.

The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed.

Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager Prof. Nicola Calabretta by email at [email protected] .
Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact [email protected] .
Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video .
Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page.

Application
We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a:
Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position.
Curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application.
Attach your bachelor's and master's theses and scientific papers, if any.

Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications.

We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled.

Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

As Equipment Integration Functional Analyst, you translate business requirements into software specifications for development of automation components controlling advanced semiconductor equipment units.
What you will do
IMEC performs world-leading research in nano-electronics, operating a diverse equipment set of most advanced semiconductor wafer processing models. To improve and further roll out our CIM application landscape, we have started the Smart Fab initiative in 2024. Smart Fab is not only about simplification of manual work, it also will deliver more insight into capacity utilization, as well as product quality. You will become part of this journey in a growing team, providing opportunities in an exciting environment.
As a member of our Smart Fab team, you will closely work with business analysts and software developers for our equipment integration solution. You will be supported by dedicated test engineers.
You will receive industry specific training and can rely on experienced teammates.
You perform the crucial task of analyzing how our equipment integration software platform can implement business requirements. The specifications to be passed on to internal and more often external developers can range from straightforward configuration to additional logic to be defined.
Some business requirements will result in equipment integration being dependent on related configuration or even features to be implemented in adjacent applications, especially the MES. You thus will gain sufficient knowledge about adjacent CIM applications to effectively collaborate with their business analysts and functional analysts.
You have an active role in test preparation and debugging. You will be supported by our PMO team during all phases of the software lifecycle.

What we do for you
We offer you the opportunity to join one of the world’s premier research centers in nanotechnology at its headquarters in Leuven, Belgium. With your talent, passion and expertise, you’ll become part of a team that makes the impossible possible. Together, we shape the technology that will define the society of tomorrow.
We are committed to being an inclusive employer and proud of our open, multicultural, and informal working environment with ample possibilities to take initiative and show responsibility. We commit to supporting and guiding you in this process; not only with words but also with tangible actions. Through imec.academy, 'our corporate university', we actively invest in your development to further your technical and personal growth.
We are aware that your valuable contribution makes imec a top player in its field. Your energy and commitment are therefore appreciated by means of a market appropriate salary with many fringe benefits.
Who you are
You have a master’s degree in engineering, exact sciences, or equal by experience.
You bring 5 years or more of experience in a complex manufacturing environment, characterized by demanding processes, high product mix, and delicate materials.
Prior experience in, or knowledge of, semiconductor manufacturing is a strong asset, preferably in a 300 mm Fab.
You have participated in a CIM project, understanding concepts like the automation pyramid and equipment state engines, as well as standards like OPC or SECS.
You have strong analytical skills and are solution oriented. You can challenge assumptions and question approaches.
You can work independently and in a team. You do work diligently and are dependable.
You feel comfortable in a complex environment.
Since you will be working in a highly international environment and will be maintaining a good contact with colleagues and co-workers from all over the world, fluency in English is essential.

ap:254099.body:
Doctoral Position in High Intensity Electron Sources for Future Accelerators
Our research group, based at the Paul Scherrer Institute (PSI), explores new technologies for future accelerator facilities. Through the development of new technologies and techniques, we develop high intensity particle sources, high gradient particle accelerators and beam diagnostics systems that measure beam qualities down to the sub-femtosecond regime. Our research combines beam/plasma physics, unique RF technologies and high-power lasers to realise the accelerators that exist within the Paul Scherrer Institute and reaching beyond with contributions to CERN’s future circular collider (FCC).

This Doctoral Position will be based at PSI Villigen but with teaching assistant duties at ETH Zurich.

Project background
The project involves developing electron sources for future accelerator facilities at PSI and the institute’s contributions to the FCC. A central shared challenge is shaping the electron beam as it is generated or shortly afterward. For the FCC, precise control of the laser profile in the RF photogun enables the flexible filling schemes needed for top-up operation. For X-ray free-electron lasers, like SwissFEL, transverse laser shaping and early RF compression are key to producing brighter electron beams. This PhD project will advance beam-shaping techniques for both applications.

Job description

Commission a new electron source test stand and demonstrate pulse-to-pulse modulation of bunch charge, beam size, and laser pulse energy relevant to the FCC-ee electron source concept

Compare laser-shaping techniques through beam measurements, build a prototype for photocathode operation, and investigate machine-learning/AI-based optimization to improve performance

Study photocathode and laser performance, including the lifetime of semiconductor photocathodes at bunch charges of up to 5 nC

Measure gains in beam brightness from both photocathode laser shaping and RF compression with applications to a SwissFEL upgrade (SwissFEL+)

Profile

Master’s degree (or equivalent) in physics, accelerator science, electrical engineering, photonics, or a closely related field

Strong interest in accelerator physics, electron sources and experimental work; experience with beam dynamics, lasers/optics, numerical modelling or scientific programming is an advantage

A practical, independent and analytical working style, combined with enthusiasm for interdisciplinary collaboration

Professional proficiency in English; knowledge of German is an asset

We offer
We are a dynamic, interdisciplinary research group committed to innovation and collaboration. As a Doctoral student with us, you will benefit from comprehensive on-the-job training alongside a wide range of personal and professional development opportunities. We are strongly committed to vocational training and to supporting your growth both as a scientist and as a professional.

We value work-life balance and offer modern employment conditions with on-site infrastructure designed to give you the flexibility to accommodate your personal interests and family commitments.

As part of our team, you will have access to:

A stimulating research environment combining fundamental beam physics, laser physics, and RF technology development, with hands-on practical experience in designing, commissioning, and operating particle accelerators

A broad range of transferable skills with applications in both academic research and industry

State-of-the-art instruments and fully operational accelerator facilities

Large-scale, multidisciplinary projects that build teamwork and collaboration competencies across a wide range of scientific and engineering interfaces

Enrollment in the ETH Doctoral Programme

Teaching and mentoring opportunities

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application in the format of a single, merged PDF document in the following order:

Cover letter detailing your research motivation, interests, and experience

Curriculum Vitae (CV)

Academic transcripts of all degrees in English (Bachelor's and Master's)

Three professional reference contacts, including an email and a direct phone number to reach them

A publication or thesis work sampling your academic reasoning and writing

Name the PDF with your last name and initials as well as the application date (for example, 20251110_DoeJane_application)

Further information about Paul Scherrer Institute Accelerator Center can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Thomas Lucas,  [email protected]   (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:254100.body:
Die Interkantonale Arbeitsgemeinschaft zur Betreuung anthropologischer Funde (IAG) hat als Verein das Ziel, die archäoanthropologischen Funde seiner Mitglieder gemeinsam zu lagern, zu erschliessen und wissenschaftlich zu erforschen. Mit rund 40'000 Skeletten aus 8000 Jahren gehört ihre Sammlung europaweit zu den grössten Beständen dieser Art. Mitglieder sind kantonale amtliche Fachstellen für Archäologie. Die Stelle ist der Integrativen Prähistorischen und Naturwissenschaftlichen Archäologie (IPNA) am Departement Umweltwissenschaften der Universität Basel angegliedert. Arbeitsort ist Bottmingen (BL).
Betreuung der anthropologischen Sammlung sowie Verantwortung für Depotverwaltung und Leihwesen
Übernahme, Inventarisierung, Datenbankerfassung und fachgerechte Einlagerung von anthropologischen Funden
Beratung und Unterstützung der Mitgliedskantone in anthropologischen Fach- und Forschungsfragen, bei Feldeinsätzen und strategischen Themen
Wissenschaftliche Auswertung ausgewählter Sammlungsbestände
Probenentnahmen
Begleitung von studentischen Praktika
Erarbeitung von Richtlinien für eine vertiefte, standardisierte Erfassung des Sammlungsmaterials, gemeinsam mit der lehrbeauftragten Person für Archäoanthropologie an der IPNA
Fachliche Vernetzung im In- und Ausland, Koordination von Forschungsprojekten sowie Repräsentation der Sammlung gegenüber Öffentlichkeit und Wissenschaft, in Absprache mit der IAG und der IPNA

Abgeschlossenes Hochschulstudium im Bereich der Archäoanthropologie/Humanosteologie, vorzugsweise mit Promotion
Umfangreiche Erfahrung in der Bearbeitung archäoanthropologischen Materials in all seinen Facetten (Körper- und Brandgräber, Kollektiv- und Mehrfachbestattungen, Morphologie, Osteometrie, Paläopathologie, Kenntnisse von Probenstrategien und Probenentnahmen für naturwissenschaftliche Untersuchungen)
Sichere Anwendung der gängigen morphologischen und metrischen Bestimmungsmethoden
Archäologische Felderfahrung, speziell in der Freilegung und Dokumentation von Gräbern
Erfahrung in der wissenschaftlichen Auswertung und Publikation archäologischer Grabfunde
Erfahrung in der Einwerbung von Drittmitteln, im Projektmanagement und in der Leitung von Projekten
Teamfähigkeit, vorausschauende Arbeitsweise, Dienstleistungsbereitschaft und ein sicherer Umgang mit Datenbanken
Gute Vernetzung und Engagement in der archäologischen Forschung der Schweiz und ihrem Umland
Führerausweis Kat. B

Eine vielfältige Tätigkeit zwischen Sammlungsmanagement, wissenschaftlicher Facharbeit und der Zusammenarbeit mit den Mitgliedskantonen der IAG
Anstellung gemäss der Personal- und Gehaltsordnung der Universität Basel

ap:254101.body:
Introduction
Are you an excellent teacher in operations management? Do you have the passion to teach a range of courses in the area of operations management that prepare students for a successful career? Do you like to develop education, with a focus on cases that show students the practical relevance of the content?

Job Description
We are looking for a University Teacher for the Operations, Planning, Accounting and Control (OPAC) group (between 0.5 and 1.0 FTE). The OPAC group is part of Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e)’s Industrial Engineering and Innovation Sciences Department, which has a worldwide reputation for high-quality research and excellent educational programs. The OPAC group helps stakeholders across sectors to make smart, informed decisions, thereby contributing to more efficiency, enhanced (environmental) sustainability, better use of resources and reduced costs.  The research of the group deals with the control of operational processes, which can be related to supply chains, manufacturing systems, high-tech equipment, distribution, transportation, warehousing, retail, and service processes such as equipment maintenance.
You will design and teach courses in the areas of operations management. You are especially interested in designing realistic cases that can be used in the courses and that show students the practical relevance of the things they learn. Courses are mainly to be taught in the Bachelor programs Industrial Engineering and the Master programs Operations Management and Logistics. Also students from other programs at TU/e, mostly Bachelor programs, may decide to follow these courses. You will also be involved in supervising bachelor end-projects and potentially guiding master thesis projects.

Job Requirements
We offer a stimulating and ambitious educational and research environment and are looking for candidates with the following qualifications:
You hold a Phd degree in the field of operations management, operations research, supply chain management, or a comparable domain.
You have the ability to teach and to design courses, shown by experience in teaching and positive evaluations of these teaching efforts.
You have good communication skills.
You have excellent proficiency (written and oral) in English.

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.
In addition, we offer you:
Salary in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale 10, ranging from €3,706 to €5,760 gross base salary per month (full-time).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
A favorable arrangement for more holidays or a sabbatical.
A selection model for additional fringe benefits.
Working hours in consultation for an optimal work-life balance.
An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care.
Unlimited access to the modern on campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
Scope for your talent with advancement prospects and excellent development opportunities such as mentoring, workshops and coaching.
Partially paid parental leave and reimbursement for commuting expenses, working from home and the internet.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .
Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .
The Industrial Engineering & Innovation Sciences (IE&IS) department combines disciplinary knowledge from the humanities, social sciences and technical sciences to solve the complex problems of industries and society. We collaboratively focus on and create responsible and effective innovations for the research themes: Humans and Technology, Supply Chain Management, Sustainability and Circularity, and Value of Data-Driven Intelligence.
Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more?
Please contact the hiring manager Zümbül Atan, Group Chair OPAC, [email protected] .
Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact Jolanda van der Sande, HR advisor [email protected] or +31 40 247 4979.
Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page .

Application
If you are interested, please use the ‘apply’ button to send us your CV and letter of application with your motivation and a description of your qualifications.
Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. Please note that incomplete applications may not be considered and could be rejected.
We look forward to receiving your application!

Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ap:254102.body:
Teaser Tekst

Binnen Leiden University College zijn wij op zoek naar een administratieve office assistant voor 2 dagen per week (0.4 fte) voor de periode januari (of zo spoedig mogelijk) tot en met juli 2027. Er is een kans op uitbreiding of verlenging. In deze functie heb je contact met studenten en werk je samen met andere collega's binnen de studentenadministratie. Je maakt deel uit van de ondersteunende staf van LUC.

Hier ga je werken

Het doel van de Faculteit Governance en Global Affairs (FGGA) is bijdragen aan de samenleving. Dit doet de faculteit met hoogwaardig interdisciplinair onderwijs en (nieuwe) wetenschappelijke kennis. Of het nu gaat om terrorisme, veiligheid, artificial intelligence of een bestuurlijke oplossing voor de woningcrisis, bij FGGA komen hedendaagse vraagstukken uitgebreid aan bod.

In hartje Den Haag, waar belangrijke beslissingen worden genomen, komen studenten en professionals samen om kennis en vaardigheden op te doen. Er wordt veel samengewerkt met universitaire en maatschappelijke partners, wat ervoor zorgt dat studenten de universiteit verlaten met een glimlach en alvast met één been in de toekomst, klaar om een substantiële bijdrage te leveren aan de maatschappij.

FGGA is één van de zeven faculteiten van de Universiteit Leiden. Deze jonge, ondernemende, vernieuwende en innovatieve organisatie heeft drie wetenschappelijke instituten, twee centers, ruim 3700 studenten en 425 medewerkers. Voor meer informatie over de faculteit klik hier .

Leiden University College The Hague (LUC) is het internationale Engelstalige Honours College van de Universiteit Leiden. Getalenteerde en gemotiveerde studenten van over de hele wereld komen speciaal naar Den Haag om deel te nemen aan het innovatieve Liberal Arts and Science-programma dat zich richt op de mondiale uitdagingen van vandaag. Het LUC kan al meer dan tien jaar rekenen op een plekje in de Keuzegids Universiteiten als best gewaardeerde University Colleges van Nederland. Het wetenschappelijke personeel, met diverse achtergronden en disciplines, heeft een passie voor lesgeven en onderwijs waarin de student centraal staat.

De administratieve office assistant is onderdeel van de support staf, een gezellig en multidisciplinair team dat onze studenten en staf van Leiden University College over de volle breedte ondersteunt.

Dit ga je doen

Het produceren van documenten voor studenten, zoals transcripts, brieven en verklaringen;
Helpen met de voorbereiding van de diploma uitreiking, vooral het doorvoeren van de studieplannen in uSis en het registreren en produceren van officiële (diploma) documenten;
Cijfers invoeren in uSis;
Het studiematerialen archief beheren;
Algemene administratieve processen ondersteunen, zoals het opcoeren van de studenten voor de vakken, het produceren van cijferlijsten, het ondersteunen van het vak evaluatieproces en het beantwoorden van vragen van studenten en staf over beleid, procuedures en IT systemen.

Dit breng je mee

In dit team zoeken we iemand die zelfstandig aan de slag kan. Uiteraard is er aandacht voor het inwerken. Deze functie past bij jou als je je herkent in de volgende punten:
HBO werk- en denkniveau

Minimaal 1 jaar relevante werkervaring, bij voorkeur binnen het hoger onderwijs

Ervaring met/kennis van de verschillende internationale onderwijssystemen

Ervaring met uSis of vergelijkare administratie systemen of processen

Uitstekende verbale en schriftelijke communicatieve vaardigheden in Nederlands en Engels

Accuraat en georganiseerd werken met oog voor procedures en details

Hands on mentaliteit en teamplayer

Interesse in het werken in een internationaal team

Herken je jezelf volledig in dit profiel óf voldoe jij niet aan alle eisen maar denk je wel dat dit de functie voor jou is? Dan nodigen wij je graag uit om te solliciteren!

Dit bieden we je

We streven ernaar om met elkaar een transparante, inclusieve werkomgeving te creëren, waarin iedereen zich welkom en gewaardeerd voelt. Onze organisatie is volop in beweging en met jouw ideeën voor verbetering en vernieuwing komen we verder. We besteden graag met jou aandacht aan je persoonlijke ontwikkeling.

Je kunt rekenen op een leuke maatschappelijk relevante baan binnen de wereld van onderwijs en onderzoek. De uitdagende en internationale werkomgeving van de universiteit bevindt zich op een steenworp afstand van de levendige Leidse binnenstad of in het bruisende stadscentrum in Den Haag. Ook hebben we – samen met jou – aandacht voor gezondheid en vitaliteit. Vanuit Healthy University organiseren we leuke activiteiten die hieraan bijdragen.

Daarnaast bieden we je:
Een tijdelijke arbeidsovereenkomst van 1 januari (of zsm) tot en met 31 juli 2027. De overeenkomst valt onder de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten;

Een salaris tussen 3202,- tot 4159,- bruto per maand bij een fulltime (38 uur) aanstelling (schaal 7);

Vakantietoeslag (8%), een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%) en een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het ABP;

Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.

Flexibele werkduur: standaard heb je minimaal 29 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime werkweek van 38 uur; je kunt daarnaast extra verlof opbouwen door bijvoorbeeld fulltime 40 uur per week te werken en zo 96 extra verlofuren op te bouwen óf door 96 verlofuren in te leveren en een werkweek van 36 uur te werken;

Ruime keuze in secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden; zo is het bespreekbaar om voor een sabbatical of betaald ouderschapsverlof te kiezen. Binnen ons keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden kunnen vrije dagen en/of salaris ingezet worden voor bijvoorbeeld een voordelig sportabonnement en fietsregeling;

Als de werkzaamheden het toelaten is hybride werken binnen Nederland mogelijk;

Een thuiswerkvergoeding (dag- en internetvergoeding) en aandacht voor goede werkplekken, daarnaast krijg je een laptop en een mobiele telefoon van de universiteit tot je beschikking.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier:  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. De Universiteit Leiden streeft ernaar om een inclusieve gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Onderwijs en onderzoek van hoge kwaliteit is inclusief.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Direct solliciteren? Klik dan op de sollicitatiebutton.
Graag vragen wij u om bij je sollicitatie de volgende aanvullende documenten in pdf-formaat te uploaden:
Motivatiebrief
CV

Wilt u eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met Mirjam van den Brand ( [email protected] ). Solliciteren kan tot 26 november. Je ontvangt uiterlijk 30 november een reactie op je sollicitatie.
Op maandag 7 december vindt de eerste ronde interviews plaats bij Leiden University College op het Anna van Buerenplein in Den Haag. Op donderdag 10 december volgt mogelijk een tweede ronde. Houd hier alsjeblieft vast rekening mee in je agenda.

Om elkaar goed te leren kennen, volgen we een aantal stappen in de sollicitatieprocedure. Meer informatie lees je hier: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden
Een pre-employment screening (referenties, diploma’s, VOG) maakt deel uit van de selectieprocedure.

Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze vacature wordt niet op prijs gesteld. Mocht je ons toch cv’s toesturen dan kunnen daar geen rechten aan worden ontleend.

ap:254104.body:
Teaser Tekst

Ben jij een ervaren projectleider en krijg jij energie van het opzetten en ondersteunen van onderwijsprogramma’s? Dan kun jij direct impact maken op de onderwijsvernieuwing van onze universiteit als projectleider Microcredentials

Dit ga je doen

Jouw rol richt zich op de uitrol van microcredentials binnen de universiteit vanuit de Npuls pilot. Je zorgt dat opleidingen en faculteiten dit collegejaar 2026-2027 in staat worden gesteld kwalitatief goede microcredentials te ontwikkelen en aan te bieden vanaf september 2027, dat het interne proces (van ontwerp tot uitgifte van de edubadge) soepel verloopt, en dat de juiste bestuurlijke kaders, mandaten en kwaliteitsborging zijn ingericht. Je bent in deze zes maanden hét aanspreekpunt binnen de instelling voor Npuls en het landelijke projectleidersnetwerk Microcredentials.
Resultaatgebieden en taken voor deze zes maanden zijn:
Prioriteren van kansrijke domeinen voor de universiteit, met name waar sprake is van aantoonbare arbeidsmarktvraag (bijvoorbeeld ICT, zorg, techniek, onderwijs).
Deze arbeidsmarktsignalen vertalen naar concrete voorstellen voor nieuwe of aan te passen microcredentials voor Universiteit Leiden.
Adviseren aan en ondersteunen van faculteiten en opleidingsteams bij het ontwerpen van deze microcredentials; studielast (SBU), leeruitkomsten, toetsing en de koppeling aan edubadges.
Monitoring en evaluatie opzetten (voortgang, deelnamecijfers, opbrengsten).
Adviseert de LLO- programmamanager en de LLO-katalysator Stuurgroep over governance, mandatering en de plek van microcredentials in de LLO-visie en het onderwijsbeleid van Universiteit Leiden.

Hier ga je werken

Binnen het landelijke programma Npuls werken hogescholen en universiteiten sinds 2021 samen aan de doorontwikkeling van microcredentials: kleinere, zelfstandig gecertificeerde onderwijseenheden waarmee lerenden aantoonbaar maken wat zij weten en kunnen. Het vervolgtraject ‘Samen doorbouwen aan microcredentials’ richt zich op verankering van microcredentials in het reguliere onderwijsaanbod, gebaseerd op het gezamenlijke kwaliteitskader van de Vereniging Hogescholen en Universiteiten van Nederland.
Onze universiteit heeft meegedaan aan deze pilot en zoekt een projectleider die de implementatie lokaal verder vormgeeft en verbindt: inhoudelijk, procesmatig én bestuurlijk, met scherp oog voor aansluiting op de arbeidsmarkt.

Dit breng je mee

Jouw profiel
Je beschikt over een HBO werk- en denkniveau aangevuld met ervaring als projectleider in het hoger onderwijs.
Aantoonbare affiniteit met en bij voorkeur ervaring met ICT/digitalisering in het onderwijs (bijvoorbeeld edubadges, onderwijslogistieke systemen, digitale certificering).
Kennis van of ervaring met Leven Lang Ontwikkelen, flexibilisering van onderwijs en/of microcredentials is een pré.

Benadert vraagstukken constructief en oplossingsgericht, met oog voor zowel kansen als praktische beperkingen.
Je kunt samenwerken met diverse belanghebbenden, beweegt je gemakkelijk op verschillende niveaus en hebt verbindende kwaliteiten.
Je beschikt over uitstekende mondelinge en schriftelijke vaardigheden in het Nederlands.

Meer informatie over LLO en de Universiteit Leiden is hier te vinden. https://www.medewerkers.universiteitleiden.nl/vr/leven-lang-ontwikkelen?cf=bestuursbureau-expertisecentra&cd=bestuursbureau

Dit bieden we je

Het betreft een tijdelijk dienstverband voor 0,6 fte voor het LLO-project voor de periode van zes maanden (start in overleg). De aanstelling vindt plaats conform de cao Nederlandse Universiteiten. Gezien de tijdelijkheid van de functie behoort een overeenkomst op basis van (interne)detachering of projectbasis zeker tot de mogelijkheden.
Het salaris bedraagt, afhankelijk van opleiding en werkervaring, minimaal € 3.706 en maximaal € 5.760 bruto per maand bij een fulltime aanstelling (schaal 10).
Daarnaast kent de Universiteit Leiden goede arbeidsvoorwaarden. Zo is er sprake van een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%), vakantietoeslag (8%), uitstekende opleidingsfaciliteiten, betaald ouderschapsverlof, sabbatical leave en de mogelijkheid om via een keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden op maat te kiezen. Alle informatie hierover kunt u nalezen op:  https://www.werkenbij.leidenuniv.nl .
Universiteit Leiden hecht groot belang aan diversiteit en verwelkomt daarom speciaal sollicitaties van mensen die nu in haar instelling ondervertegenwoordigd zijn.
Deze functie wordt intern en extern gepubliceerd, bij gelijke geschiktheid hebben interne kandidaten voorrang. Interne detachering behoort hierbij zeker tot de mogelijkheden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. De Universiteit Leiden streeft ernaar om een inclusieve gemeenschap te worden die alle studenten en medewerkers in staat stelt om zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd te voelen en zich volop te ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Onderwijs en onderzoek van hoge kwaliteit is inclusief.

Solliciteren of meer weten?

Solliciteren kan tot en met 12 november 2026. Wil je eerst nog meer informatie over de inhoud van deze functie? Neem contact op met Annet van der Helm, Programmamanager Lifelong Learning [email protected]
Je kunt uitsluitend solliciteren via ons online sollicitatiesysteem. Gebruik hiervoor de blauwe button bovenaan deze pagina. Sollicitaties voorzien van het vacaturenummer en vergezeld van een motivatiebrief en CV, kunnen worden gericht aan Annet van der Helm. We plannen gesprekken zodra we een geschikt sollicitatie ontvangen, dus wacht vooral niet te lang met solliciteren.
Acquisitie naar aanleiding van deze advertentie wordt niet op prijs gesteld.

ap:254105.body:
Teaser Text

PhD Researcher in “A Sociology of Post-Imperial Islamic Legal Culture: Insights from Central Asia, the Middle East, North Africa, and Southeast Asia” ( Minaret Project ), 1.0 FTE.

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) invites applications for one PhD Researcher (1.0 FTE, 4 years) from September/October 2027 – September/October 2031 to join the Minaret Project, a HORIZON Unit Grant-funded interdisciplinary and transnational research initiative, which examines the interconnection between law, religion and governance in post-imperial Muslim-majority societies to promote democracy and good governance.

The project brings together 11 universities with 15 PhD researchers across 3 work packages and 15 subprojects, with the applicant contributing to the subproject Neo-Imperialism and Constitutional Reform: The Global Dimension . This subproject examines to what extent international organizations and global governance actors act as neo-imperial forces shaping constitutional reform in North Africa and the Middle East.

It will explore how donor-driven “rule of law” and “good governance” programs are developed, interpreted, and implemented in countries such as Jordan, Lebanon, and Syria. Particular attention will be paid to how the legal frameworks promoted by international actors relate to the government practices in these countries, and in particular to those embedded in local traditions and religious values.

Drawing on policy-document analysis and elite interviews with a diverse range of actors -including international advisers, domestic policymakers, civil-society representatives, legal practitioners, religious scholars, and community leaders-, the study will investigate how transnational constitutional models are negotiated, adapted, resisted, or hybridized in practice. It will contribute to debates on postcolonial constitutionalism by examining the processes through which legal and governance norms circulate across borders, as well as the forms of influence, dependency, and agency that shape their adoption.

Ultimately, the project seeks to develop a nuanced account of how external interventions affect perceptions of legitimacy, legal pluralism, and sovereignty in transitional Muslim-majority societies.

What you will do

The PhD researcher will join the Leiden-based Minaret team, working closely with two senior-researchers and two external mentors (one academic and one non-academic, associated with the project). The position provides the opportunity to conduct original empirical research on the underlying structures of constitutional reform in said countries, while also contributing to public engagement and the collaborative life of the project. All PhD researchers are required to undertake two secondments abroad with the project’s associated partners, one academic and one non-academic, of between two and six months' duration. This will not only enhance research capabilities but also equip the PhD researcher for academic and non-academic roles.

Academic Research
Conduct socio-legal and policy analysis with key stakeholders in selected countries.
Write a doctoral dissertation and co-author academic publications based on qualitative research.
Contribute to the project’s comparative framework within the subproject; within the work package (Imperial Genealogies and Constitutional Formation) and between the work packages.

Communications & Engagement
Present research findings at events organized by the research project, such as 3 summer schools and 4 training events.
Willingness and ability to spend extended periods abroad for fieldwork and 2 secondments.
Help organize international workshops, conferences, and events with academic and civil society partners.
Contribute to project website and social media accounts.

Where you will work

The Faculty of Law is based in both Leiden and The Hague and, with over 7,000 students and approximately 600 staff members, is one of the largest law faculties in the Netherlands. The faculty is committed to innovative, multidisciplinary research and a constantly evolving curriculum that addresses key societal challenges. Our faculty is large enough to make an impact on both a national and international scale, yet small enough to offer a personal and engaging learning experience. In this way, we contribute every day to a safer and more sustainable world. Impact with law! For more information, please visit https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/law .

The Van Vollenhoven Institute for Law, Governance and Society (VVI) is part of the Leiden Law School. The VVI seeks to advance knowledge of the formation and functioning of legal systems in their social contexts, the impact of these systems on society and vice versa, their effectiveness in governance, and their contribution to development. The Institute adopts a socio-legal and global approach, doing research on law in the books and law in action in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Europe. VVI staff teaches several socio-legal thematic and regional courses for both Dutch and foreign exchange students. In addition, VVI provides PhD supervision, advisory services and training courses to policy makers and practitioners. For more information, see  www.vvi.leidenuniv.nl .

What you bring

In our team, we are looking for someone who can work independently while also contributing to a collaborative environment. Since every position is unique, we will devote careful attention to your onboarding. If some aspects of the work are new to you, we will identify what support you need and develop a tailored plan for your professional growth.

We do not expect candidates to already have all the qualifications listed below. Training will be provided in areas such as socio-legal studies, research methods, and the specificities of constitutional reform in the Middle East. That said, this position will be a good fit for you if you recognize yourself in many of the following:
A MSc or LLM in Anthropology, Political Science, Law, International Studies, International Relations, Development Studies, or a closely related field;
Demonstrated experience in conducting empirical research, ideally in the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria);
Experience working with (inter)national civil society actors;
Knowledge of constitutional reform, especially in relation to religion, democracy, and governance;
Familiarity with socio-legal literature and qualitative research methods;
Ability to work effectively as part of an interdisciplinary and international research team;
Familiarity with one of the project’s country contexts (Jordan, Lebanon, Syria) is an asset;
Knowledge of written and spoken Arabic is strongly recommended.

What we offer

Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.

You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world of education and research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre or the bustling city centre of The Hague. We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University.

We also offer:
An employment contract for the duration of four years. This contract falls under the CLA of Dutch Universities;

A salary between €3204 - €4051 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (PhD student);

A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;

Full reimbursement of public transport commuting costs for home-to-work travel;

For more information about employment conditions, see  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

What we value

Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research.

Want to apply or find out more?

If you want to apply straight away, click the application button. First, however, please review the information below to see whether your profile matches the requirements of the role.
Who can apply?
Please note that the MSCA mobility rule applies to this position , as MINARET is funded under the Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Networks programme. According to this rule, doctoral candidates must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in the country of the recruiting institution for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding their recruitment date.

If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Dr. Nadia Sonneveld, at [email protected] . You can apply until 31 January 2027;

To apply for this vacancy, please submit your application in English addressed to Dr. Nadia Sonneveld using the blue button at the top of this text. Interviews are scheduled in February-March 2027. Please include with your application the following:
A cover letter stating your motivation for this position;
A curriculum vitae;
Transcripts from your bachelors and masters degrees;
A major writing sample (i.e Master’s thesis, article, or other class paper);
Names of 2-3 academic references.

To help us get to know each other better, we follow a number of steps in the application procedure. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions

In choosing between candidates, in case of equal suitability, preference will be given to internal candidates, women, the occupationally disabled and employees with a migration background.

A pre-employment screening (references, diplomas, certificate of good conduct (VOG)) may be part of the selection procedure.

Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this. #LI-Hybrid

Post-doctoral Researcher: Agent-Based Modelling of Pleistocene Landscape Connectivity in Europe

The Department of World Archaeology, Faculty of Archaeology, Leiden University, is looking for a temporary Postdoctoral Researcher to investigate prehistoric landscape connectivity and human movement across Europe using agent-based modelling. The project is part of the NWO-VICI project Neandertal Legacy, awarded to Prof. dr. M.A. Soressi, which investigates the contacts and interactions between Neanderthals and early modern humans in Late Pleistocene Europe through an interdisciplinary archaeological approach. The successful candidate will implement the movement modelling framework developed by Coco & Iovita ( 2025 PLOS’one) to reconstruct the geography-driven movement architecture of Europe and adjacent regions during the Middle and Late Pleistocene. By simulating autonomous agents that make only local least-cost movement decisions, using Leiden University's ALICE High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster, the project will identify movement corridors, bottlenecks, and barriers that emerge solely from landscape structure. The central research question is: if hominins moved across Europe constrained primarily by palaeogeography, what large-scale patterns of movement and connectivity would naturally emerge? Predicted movement pathways will subsequently be compared with the archaeological record to evaluate how geography shaped patterns of human dispersal and landscape connectivity through time.

What you will do

Adapt the Coco & Iovita (2025) agent-based movement model to reconstruct prehistoric landscape connectivity across Europe.
Build and process palaeoenvironmental and geospatial datasets (including digital elevation models, palaeocoastlines, river networks and glacier extents) for multiple Middle and Late Pleistocene time slices using GIS and R.
Run computationally intensive agent-based simulations on Leiden University's ALICE High Performance Computing (HPC) cluster and analyse predicted movement corridors and connectivity patterns.
Compare predicted movement corridors and connectivity networks with archaeological datasets to evaluate the extent to which landscape structure alone explains observed patterns of prehistoric human dispersal.
Produce reproducible datasets and code, and contribute to one scientific publication and one scientific presentation.
Engage with the Faculty community through discussion meetings, journal clubs, and other events.

Where you will work

The future of the past begins at Leiden University. The Faculty of Archaeology is internationally leading for its research, home to a broad array of specializations and notable for its strong connection between teaching and research. Home to over 500 students in the multidisciplinary world of Archaeology, the Faculty, and its researchers from all areas of the archaeological field, determine the future of archaeological research. More information about our university and our faculty can be found at: https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/archaeology
The successful candidate will join the  Department of World Archaeology . They will be supervised by Prof. dr. M.A. Soressi and by Dr. E. Coco, Researcher at the Interdisciplinary Center for Archaeology and Evolution of Human Behaviour (ICArEHB) at the University of Algarve in Faro, Portugal.
They will work as a post-doctoral researcher for 0,7 to 1 fte (26,6 to 38 hours per week), maximaal 6 months, depending on the number of fte’s.

Working arrangements

The position can be carried out remotely. The postdoctoral researcher will work independently while maintaining regular contact with the project team through scheduled online meetings. Progress will be monitored through agreed milestones and deliverables to ensure timely completion of the project.
Expected deliverables:
Reproducible European palaeogeographic datasets for multiple Pleistocene time slices.
Connectivity maps identifying emergent movement corridors, bottlenecks and barriers.
Comparison of predicted corridors with archaeological site distributions.
Reproducible R code and documentation.
Draft manuscript suitable for submission to a peer-reviewed journal.

What you bring

We are looking for someone who can work independently while collaborating effectively with the project team. Given the short duration of the appointment, you should be able to quickly familiarise yourself with the project objectives and work towards clearly defined milestones. This position is a good fit for you if you recognise yourself in the following:
PhD degree completed by the time of appointment in Archaeology, Geography, Geosciences, Ecology, Computer Science, or a related discipline;
Experience with GIS, spatial analysis, and processing large raster and vector geospatial datasets.
Programming experience in R (preferred), or Python or another language suitable for spatial analysis and simulation.
Experience with agent-based modelling or spatial simulation is an advantage;
Ability to work independently, manage time effectively, and deliver project milestones within a short-term appointment;
Excellent written and spoken English and strong communication skills.

What we offer

Our goal is to work together to create a transparent and inclusive work environment in which everyone feels welcome and appreciated. Our organisation is always evolving and we need your ideas for improvement and innovation to take us further. We want to devote attention to your personal development.
You can count on an enjoyable job within the socially relevant world research. The University's challenging and international work environment is located just steps away from Leiden’s lively city centre . We also want to work with you to devote attention to your health and vitality, for example with the fun activities we organise through Healthy University.
The selected candidate will be appointed for up to a maximum of 6 months depending on the start date and the number of FTE. The project needs to be completed by July 2027;
A salary of a minimum of €4422 and a maximum of €5760 gross per month, based on a full-time appointment (38 hours) (scale 10 for post-doctoral researcher);
A holiday allowance (8%), an end-of-year bonus (8,3%), and an attractive pension scheme at ABP;
For a 38-hour week you have 232 vacation hours per year. If you work part-time, your vacation credit is proportional to your contracted hours;
Lots of options when it comes to secondary employment conditions; we can, for example, discuss options for a sabbatical or paid parental leave. Within our terms of employment individual choices model, you can exchange leave days and/or salary for benefits such as an advantageous sports subscription or bicycle scheme, and we also offer child-care options;
If your work allows it, hybrid working is possible within the Netherlands;
A home-working allowance (day and internet allowance) and attention for good workplaces. The University will also provide you with a laptop.

For more information about employment conditions, see  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/en/working-at/job-application-procedure-and-employment-conditions .

What we find important

Promoting an inclusive community is central to Leiden University’s values and vision. Leiden University aims to be an inclusive community in which all students and staff members feel valued and respected, and are able to develop to their full potential. Diversity in experiences and perspectives enriches our teaching and strengthens our research. High-quality education and research means inclusive education and research.

Want to apply or find out more?

If you want to apply straight away, click the application button.
If you would like more information about what the job entails, please contact Prof. dr. M.A Soressi at [email protected] . Applications will be processed as they arrive, and until the position is filled, and no later than 6th November 2026

For other matters, please contact Human Resources [email protected]
To help us get to know each other better, we follow a number of steps in the application procedure. For more information, see https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Please attach the following additional documents, stating the job number above:
Motivation letter, including your relevant interest and experience in the subject matter and a brief work plan outlining how you would structure the project, including the datasets you would prioritise, the modelling workflow, and the milestones you would aim to achieve during the appointment (max. 2.5 pages).
Curriculum vitae , including a list of publications
The names and addresses of two potential referees (no actual recommendation letters required at this stage).

Selected candidates will initially be invited for an online interview.
We believe mobility is very important. That is why we are also publishing this vacancy internally. In case of equal suitability, we will give priority to the internal candidate.
Acquisition in response to this vacancy is not appreciated. If you nevertheless choose to send us CVs, no rights can be derived from this. #LI-Hybrid

Medewerker studentenzaken

De Faculteit der Sociale Wetenschappen zoekt voor het Onderwijs Servicecentrum van de Faculteit der Sociale Wetenschappen per 1 december een Medewerker studentenzaken (0,8 - 1 fte)

Hier ga je werken

De Faculteit der Sociale Wetenschappen bestaat uit vijf instituten: Centrum voor Wetenschaps- en Technologiestudies, Culturele Antropologie en Ontwikkelingssociologie, Pedagogische Wetenschappen, Politieke Wetenschap en Psychologie. De faculteit heeft circa 7000 studenten en 1000 medewerkers. Binnen de instituten wordt niet alleen onderwijs gegeven, maar ook baanbrekend onderzoek verricht dat de grenzen van ons begrip van menselijk gedrag en maatschappelijke structuren verlegt. Wat onze faculteit uniek maakt is de diversiteit aan onderzoeksonderwerpen, de verschillende stijlen van onderwijs geven en de manier waarop de professionele ondersteuning is ingericht; dit biedt jou de mogelijkheid om jouw interesses en expertise te verkennen en te ontwikkelen. Bezoek onze website voor een impressie: welkom bij de Leidse Faculteit der Sociale Wetenschappen - Universiteit Leiden.

Het Onderwijs Servicecentrum (OSC) van de Faculteit der Sociale Wetenschappen (FSW) is het centrale aanspreekpunt op het gebied van onderwijsadministratie en -logistiek. Studenten kunnen er bijvoorbeeld terecht voor vragen over vakken, tentamens, roosters, studievoortgang, afstuderen en het studievoortgangssysteem uSis. Docenten worden onder andere ondersteund bij de organisatie van tentamens, cursus evaluaties en bij de invoer van studieresultaten.

Het OSC is gevestigd in het Agora-gebouw in Leiden en heeft daarnaast een kantoor in het Spui in Den Haag. Het team bestaat uit ongeveer 20 enthousiaste en betrokken collega’s die samen zorgen voor een goede dienstverlening aan studenten, docenten en opleidingen. Het is een prettig en collegiaal team waarin wordt samengewerkt, kennis wordt gedeeld en ruimte is om elkaar te helpen en van elkaar te leren.

Het OSC bestaat uit een frontoffice waar vragen aan de balie, per telefoon en per e-mail worden beantwoord en een backoffice waar taken plaatsvinden die gericht zijn op de organisatie van het onderwijs. Het OSC ondersteunt de instituten Culturele Antropologie en Ontwikkelingssociologie, Pedagogische Wetenschappen, Politieke Wetenschap en Psychologie.

Het OSC is op zoek naar een medewerker studentenzaken die fungeert als roosteraar/accountmedewerker binnen het cluster dat verantwoordelijk is voor de opleidingen van het Instituut Politieke Wetenschap. Standplaats voor deze functie is vooral Leiden en deels Den Haag.

Dit ga je doen

Roosteren van de onderwijsprogramma’s van de opleidingen van het Instituut Politieke Wetenschap (POWE).
Nauwe samenwerking en afstemming met de onderwijscoördinator bij POWE over rooster, vakinschrijvingen en benodigde capaciteit.
Contactpersoon voor medewerkers en commissies van POWE.
Aanspreekpunt voor docenten.
Op de hoogte blijven van de ontwikkelingen rondom de onderwijsprogramma’s van de opleidingen van POWE.
Voeren van de studenten- en studievoortgangadministratie.
Het beantwoorden van informatieverzoeken van studenten en docenten vooral per e-mail.
Administratieve ondersteuning bij de overige werkzaamheden van het OSC.

Dit breng je mee

De ideale kandidaat is een kwaliteit-, resultaat- en klantgerichte collega die graag in teamverband werkt en pro-actief het werk benadert en beschikt over:

HBO werk- en denkniveau.
Uitstekende kennis van Excel en Word.
Werkervaring in een soortgelijke functie.
Ervaring met studenteninformatiesysteem uSis is een pré.
Ervaring met roosterprogramma TermTime is een pré.
Affiniteit met softwareprogramma’s en je kunt deze snel eigen maken.
Flexibiliteit, daadkracht en het vermogen klanten rustig te benaderen als zich een probleem voordoet.
Het vermogen om goed te schakelen en gemakkelijk in te spelen op veranderende omstandigheden en daarbij beleid weet om te zetten naar uitvoering.
Het vermogen om knelpunten te analyseren en voorstellen te doen voor verbetering.
Een goede beheersing van de Nederlandse en Engelse taal in woord en geschrift.

Dit bieden we je

Een levendige werkomgeving met veel contacten in een gezellig team. Aanstelling vindt plaats conform de CAO Nederlandse Universiteiten, in eerste instantie voor de duur van een jaar met uitzicht op een vast dienstverband bij goed functioneren. Het salaris is afhankelijk van opleiding en ervaring en bedraagt minimaal € 3.537,-  en maximaal € 4.673,-  bruto per maand (salarisschaal 8).

Vakantietoeslag (8%), een eindejaarsuitkering (8,3%) en een aantrekkelijke pensioenregeling bij het ABP;

Volledige vergoeding van reiskosten met OV voor woon-werkreizen.

Flexibele werkduur: standaard heb je minimaal 29 vakantiedagen bij een fulltime werkweek van 38 uur; je kunt daarnaast extra verlof opbouwen door bijvoorbeeld fulltime 40 uur per week te werken en zo 96 extra verlofuren op te bouwen óf door 96 verlofuren in te leveren en een werkweek van 36 uur te werken;

Ruime keuze in secundaire arbeidsvoorwaarden; zo is het bespreekbaar om voor een sabbatical of betaald ouderschapsverlof te kiezen. Binnen ons keuzemodel arbeidsvoorwaarden kunnen vrije dagen en/of salaris ingezet worden voor bijvoorbeeld een voordelig sportabonnement en fietsregeling;

Als de werkzaamheden het toelaten is hybride werken binnen Nederland mogelijk;

Een thuiswerkvergoeding (dag- en internetvergoeding) en aandacht voor goede werkplekken, daarnaast krijg je een laptop en een mobiele telefoon van de universiteit tot je beschikking.

Meer informatie over arbeidsvoorwaarden lees je hier:  https://www.universiteitleiden.nl/werken-bij/sollicitatieprocedure-en-arbeidsvoorwaarden

Dit vinden wij belangrijk

Het bevorderen van een inclusieve gemeenschap staat centraal in de waarden en visie van de Universiteit Leiden. De Universiteit Leiden streeft ernaar om een inclusieve gemeenschap te zijn waar alle studenten en medewerkers zich gewaardeerd en gerespecteerd voelen en zich volop kunnen ontplooien. Diversiteit in ervaringen en perspectieven verrijkt ons onderwijs en versterkt ons onderzoek. Onderwijs en onderzoek van hoge kwaliteit is inclusief.
