ap:254112.body:
An der Helmut-Schmidt-Universität/Universität der Bundeswehr Hamburg (HSU/UniBw H), Fakultät für Maschinenbau und Bauingenieurwesen, Professur für Informatik im Maschinenbau (Herr Univ.-Prof. Dr. Niggemann), ist ab dem 01.01.2027 die Stelle einer/eines
Wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeiterin /
Wissenschaftlichen Mitarbeiters (m/w/d)
(Entgeltgruppe 13 Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst (TVöD);
39 Stunden wöchentlich)
befristet bis zum 31.12.2029 zu besetzen.
Forschungsschwerpunkt der Professur ist das Themenfeld „Künstliche Intelligenz und Maschinelles Lernen für Cyber-Physische Systeme“. In einem aktuellen Forschungsprojekt ist eine Stelle vakant, bei der die Forschung für die Bundeswehr im Bereich Künstlicher Intelligenz im Vordergrund steht. Neben der Forschung im Bereich von Algorithmen der Künstlichen Intelligenz (z.B. Neuronale Netze und Planungsalgorithmen) beinhaltet dies auch die Umsetzung der entwickelten Ansätze und die Unterstützung bei der Einführung in die Bundeswehr.
Aufgabengebiet:
Bearbeitung von Forschungsfragen auf dem o.g. Themenfeld sowie Entwicklung einer neuen Lösung mit wissenschaftlicher Systematik
Implementierung der entwickelten Lösung in Software sowie Anwendung auf Plattform-Äquivalenten und auf Live-Systemen im Feld
Beratung der Bundeswehr und verwandten Organisationen im Schwerpunktbereich der Professur
Arbeit an der Verallgemeinerung der entwickelten Lösung und Erschließung neuer Anwendungsmöglichkeiten und Forschungsthemen
Einarbeitung in Domäne-spezifisches Wissen
Möglichkeit zur wissenschaftlichen Weiterqualifikation (z. B. Promotion oder Habilitation)
Erledigung von Verwaltungsarbeiten allgemeiner Art sowie akademische Tätigkeiten in der akademischen Selbstverwaltung

Qualifikationserfordernisse:
Ein mit mindestens gutem Erfolg abgeschlossenes wissenschaftliches Hochschulstudium (Diplom [univ.] oder Master) der Fachrichtungen Informatik, Ingenieurwissenschaften oder einer vergleichbaren Fachrichtung
Kenntnisse in einer Programmiersprache (z.B. Python) und in Mathematik
Sie stimmen zu, an einer erweiterten Sicherheitsüberprüfung (SÜ2/SÜ3) teilzunehmen. Die erfolgreiche Sicherheitsüberprüfung der Stufe SÜ2 ist verpflichtend zur Besetzung der Stelle.

Darüber hinaus erwünscht:
Sie besitzen gute Sprachkenntnisse in Deutsch sowie gute Fremdsprachenkenntnisse in Englisch und sind bereit, diese durch Fortbildung auszubauen.
Ausgeprägtes Interesse an Künstlicher Intelligenz und Maschinellem Lernen sowie eine ausgeprägte Analysefähigkeit und Freude an der Konzeption neuer Lösungen
Verantwortungsbewusstsein, Teamfähigkeit sowie die Fähigkeit zum zielorientierten und selbständigen Arbeiten
Bereitschaft zur Durchführung von Dienstreisen innerhalb der Bundesrepublik Deutschland und gelegentlich im internationalen Umfeld
Gültige Fahrerlaubnis der Klasse B

Was für Sie zählt:
Vermögenswirksame Leistungen
Jahressonderzahlung
Betriebliche Altersversorgung
Flexible Arbeitszeiten
DeutschlandJobTicket mit Arbeitgeberzuschuss bei Vorliegen der notwendigen Voraussetzungen
Möglichkeit der Inanspruchnahme eines Kinderbetreuungsplatzes in einer campusnah gelegenen Kindertagesstätte bei Vorliegen der notwendigen Voraussetzungen
Sie profitieren von einer gezielten Personalentwicklung und einem umfangreichen Fort- und Ausbildungsangebot.
Kostengünstige Verpflegungsmöglichkeit in der Campus-Mensa mit drei Mahlzeiten pro Tag
Möglichkeit der Teilnahme am Corporate-Benefits-Programm
Sie haben die Möglichkeit, an Angeboten der betrieblichen Gesundheitsförderung teilzunehmen (Nähere Informationen finden Sie unter:  www.hsu-hh.de/bgm/ ).
Kostenfreie Parkmöglichkeiten auf dem Campus-Gelände
Möglichkeit zur Nutzung des bundeswehreigenen Carsharings (Nähere Informationen finden Sie unter:  www.bwcarsharing.de )

Auskünfte bei fachlichen Fragen erteilt Ihnen Herr Univ.-Prof. Dr. Niggemann, Tel.: 040/6541-2722 oder per E-Mail:  [email protected] .

ap:254114.body:
Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder, Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap er det ledig en 100 % stilling som doktorgradsstipendiat i helsevitenskap med fokus på sosial inkludering og likeverdig tilgang til digitale løsninger for helsefremming for en periode på tre år. Stillingen er organisatorisk knyttet til  Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap . Arbeidssted er for tiden Campus Grimstad. Tiltredelse etter avtale med fakultetet.
Fakultetet har fem institutter: Institutt for ernæring og folkehelse, Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap, Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, Institutt for psykososial helse og Institutt for psykologi.
Stillingen vil være knyttet til Centre for Personalized Digital Health Promotion,  DigiVita , et Senter for forskningsdrevet innovasjon (SFI) der Universitetet i Agder, ved Senter for e-helse, er partner. DigiVita er finansiert av Norges forskningsråd og ledes av Nasjonalt senter for e-helseforskning (NSE) og SINTEF.
Stipendiaten vil være tilknyttet  Senter for e-helse ved UiA. Det er utviklet en tematisk innramming (betenkning) for doktorgradsprosjektet som kan fås ved henvendelse til Elin Thygesen,  [email protected] .
Arbeidsoppgaver
DigiVita er organisert i flere forskningsområder hvor denne doktorgradsstillingen inngår i temaområdet Brukermedvirkning, inkludering og tilgjengelighet.  Doktorgradsprosjektet skal bidra med ny kunnskap om hvordan digitale løsninger for helsefremming kan utvikles, implementeres og tas i bruk på en måte som fremmer sosial inkludering og likeverdig tilgang til helsefremmende tjenester. Prosjektet må ha en praksisnær og deltakende forskningstilnærming med stor grad av brukerinvolvering.
Doktorgradsstipendiaten skal gjennomføre et doktorgradsprosjekt som tar utgangspunkt i den tematiske innrammingen (betenkningen) for prosjektet. Søkere bes derfor å skrive frem et forslag til prosjektplan basert på innrammingen for stillingen og som svarer til formålet med doktorgradsprosjektet. Doktorgradsstipendiaten vil i samarbeid med veilederteamet utarbeide en endelig prosjektplan ved prosjektstart.
Det er en forutsetning for tiltredelse at stipendiaten tas opp på  UiAs ph.d.-program ved Fakultet for Helse- og idrettsvitenskap med  spesialisering i helse- og sykepleievitenskap
Nødvendige kvalifikasjoner
Den som ansettes må ha:
Relevant mastergrad innen helse- sosialfag, eller andre fagområder som er relevante for arbeidsoppgavene i prosjektet, for eksempel: Andre helserelaterte utdanninger
Samfunnsvitenskap
Teknologi (f.eks. deltakende design, menneske-maskin interaksjon)

God skriftlig og muntlig formidlingsevne i norsk og engelsk

Årets kandidater/kandidater som er i avslutningsfasen av master kan også søke. Masteroppgaven må imidlertid være ferdigskrevet og levert for bedømming.
Ansettelsesvilkår for rekrutteringsstillinger fremgår av  Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven.
Ved vurdering av søkerne legges det vekt på oppnådde eksamensresultater, relevansen av faglig bakgrunn, eventuelle tidligere utviklingsarbeider og publiserte arbeider.
Arbeidsspråket ved Universitetet i Agder er norsk. Den som ansettes må beherske norsk eller et annet skandinavisk språk, skriftlig og muntlig. Det kreves gode kunnskaper i engelsk, skriftlig og muntlig.
Ønskede kvalifikasjoner
Erfaring fra forskning eller kjennskap til forskningsområdet relevant for utlysningen
Erfaring med forsknings-, innovasjons- eller utviklingsprosjekt
Faglige kvalifikasjoner, interesse og motivasjon innenfor det utlyste området
Vitenskapelige publikasjoner og faglig formidling
Erfaring fra helsefremmende arbeid
Gode kommunikasjonsferdigheter.
Erfaring med å jobbe i tverrfaglige team.
God skriftlig og muntlig formidlingsevne i et tredje språk i tillegg til norsk og engelsk.

Personlige egenskaper
Kunne arbeide målrettet, ryddig, konsentrert og selvstendig
Evne til å samarbeide
Analytiske evner
Skriftlig formidlingsevne
Gjennomføringsevne

Personlige egenskaper og egnethet for stillingen vil bli vektlagt.
Vi tilbyr
Faglig utvikling i en stor, spennende og samfunnsviktig organisasjon
Et godt, inkluderende og mangfoldig arbeidsmiljø
Moderne lokaliteter og et allsidig velferdstilbud
Medlemskap i  Statens pensjonskasse

Mer om Universitetet i Agder som arbeidsplass.
Stillingen lønnes etter Statens lønnsregulativ lønnsplan 17.515, kode 1017 stipendiat, kr. 550 800 brutto pr år. Fra lønnen går det lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.
Generell informasjon
UiA er et åpent og inkluderende universitet. Vi har tro på at mangfold beriker arbeidsplassen og gjør oss bedre. Vi oppfordrer derfor kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke uavhengig av kjønn, alder, kulturell bakgrunn, nedsatt funksjonsevne eller “hull i CV-en".
Den som ansettes, har rettigheter og plikter etter de retningslinjer som til enhver tid gjelder for stillingen. Ansettelse foretas av Ansettelsesutvalget for undervisnings- og forskerstillinger ved Universitetet i Agder.
Aktuelle kandidater vil bli innkalt til intervju. Det vil også bli innhentet referanser etter nærmere avtale med søkeren. Det kan bli foretatt  bakgrunnssjekk for å verifisere opplysninger som kommer frem av tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med søkerens samtykke, og ansettelse i stillingen forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette.
Mer om ansettelsesprosessen.
I henhold til offentlighetsloven § 25, 2.ledd kan søker be om ikke å bli oppført på den offentlige søkerlista. Universitetet kan likevel beslutte at navnet på søkeren skal offentliggjøres. Søker vil bli varslet i forkant ved eventuell offentliggjøring.
Søknad
Søknaden og nødvendige opplysninger om utdanning og erfaring (inkludert vitnemål og attester) sendes elektronisk, benytt linken " Søk stillingen ".
Følgende må lastes opp elektronisk:
Vitnemål med karakterer
Motivasjonsbrev for stillingen (maks én side/500 ord)
En refleksjon (maks tre sider, litteraturliste kommer i tillegg) som skisserer en mulig retning for forskningsprosjektet og metodiske tilnærminger innenfor forskningstemaene beskrevet ovenfor og i den tematiske innrammingen som kan fås ved henvendelse
Kopi av masteroppgave/hovedfagsoppgave. For søkere som ikke har fått vurdert masteroppgaven, så må dokumentasjon på fullført mastergrad fremlegges før tiltredelse. Vurderingen må tilfredsstille krav for opptak på UiAs ph.d. program.
Vitenskapelig arbeid og FoU-virksomhet, samt liste over disse

Søkeren har selv ansvar for å levere fullstendig dokumentasjon digitalt innen søknadsfristen. All dokumentasjon må foreligge på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk.
Søknadsfrist: 10. november 2026.
Kontaktinformasjon
For spørsmål om stillingen:
Hovedveileder, professor Elin Thygesen, tlf 91 57 15 15, e-post:  [email protected]
Instituttleder Dag Tomas Sagen Johannesen, tlf. 91 87 37 99, e-post:  [email protected]

For spørsmål om søknadsprosessen:
Personalrådgiver Daniel Øverdahl Perkis tlf. 98 05 42 99, e-post  [email protected]

Sammen om kunnskap
Når engasjerte mennesker samles om kunnskap, er alt mulig.
Universitetet i Agder kombinerer Sørlandets unike varme og nærhet med førsteklasses vitenskapelig, teknologisk og kunstnerisk kompetanse.
Vil du jobbe med oss for å skape bedre løsninger på våre felles utfordringer?
Om Universitetet i Agder (UiA)
Universitetet i Agder har over 1500 ansatte og nesten 14 000 studenter. Det gjør oss til en av Sørlandets største arbeidsplasser. Våre ansatte forsker, underviser og formidler kunnskap fra alle sine fagområder.
Universitetet holder til på to moderne campuser i Kristiansand og Grimstad.

ap:254121.body:
Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research?
As a research assistant, you will join the Perception Lab at the Department of Clinical Neuroscience, Karolinska Institutet. The group studies the neural basis of the human sense of smell using psychophysics, functional neuroimaging and electrophysiology. In this role, you will contribute to data collection in ongoing studies, with a focus on conducting EEG testing to understand how the human brain processes odours.
Your mission
You will do research in ongoing studies. Your tasks include conducting EEG testing and standardised olfactory psychophysical tests with research participants, assisting in the preparation and execution of neuroimaging (MRI) studies, and contributing to data management, documentation and the practical coordination of test sessions.
Your profile
To be eligible for employment as a research assistant, you must hold a bachelor’s degree in a subject that we consider relevant to the position. Fluency in spoken and written English is required. You are well-organized, meticulous, and able to work independently as well as in a team. As you will be in direct contact with research participants and patients, a high level of social and communication skills is required. Great emphasis will be placed on personal suitability.
Documented experience in the following is a strong advantage :
EEG recordings
EEG analysis
Programming in MATLAB and/or Python
Olfactory psychophysical testing
Working in a research environment (e.g. as a research assistant)

It is also an advantage if you have:
MR safety certification and experience operating an MRI scanner
Very good knowledge of Swedish

What do we offer?
A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is also a state university, which entitles you to several good benefits through our collective agreement. And you get to practice freely in our modern wellness facilities, where trained staff are on site.
Location: Solna
Read more about the Department of Clinical Neuroscience
Read more about the Perception Lab

Application
KI applies individual and differentiated salary setting in accordance with our collective agreements RALS and RALS-T.
The application is to be submitted through the Varbi recruitment system.In this recruitment, you will apply with your CV without a personal letter. Instead, you will answer some questions about why you are applying for the job in the application form.

ap:254122.body:
Vill du bidra till medicinsk forskning av toppkvalitet?
Som forskningsassistent kommer du att ingå i Perception Lab vid Institutionen för klinisk neurovetenskap, Karolinska Institutet. Gruppen studerar det mänskliga luktsinnets neurala grund med psykofysik, funktionell hjärnavbildning och elektrofysiologi. I rollen bidrar du till datainsamlingen i pågående studier, med fokus på att genomföra testning med EEG för att förstå hur den mänskliga hjärnan processar lukter.
Din roll
Du kommer att arbeta med forskning i pågående studier. I arbetsuppgifterna ingår att genomföra testning med EEG samt standardiserade luktpsykofysiska tester med försökspersoner, att assistera vid förberedelse och genomförande av hjärnavbildningsstudier (MR), samt att bidra till datahantering, dokumentation och praktisk samordning kring studietillfällen.
Vem är du?
Behörig att anställas som forskningsassistent är den som har kandidatexamen inom ett ämne som vi bedömer som relevant för anställningen. Att kunna engelska flytande i tal och skrift är ett krav.  Du är välorganiserad, noggrann och kan arbeta självständigt såväl som i team. Då du kommer vara i direkt kontakt med försökspersoner och patienter ställs höga krav på social kompetens och kommunikativ förmåga. Vi lägger stor vikt vid personlig lämplighet.
Det är starkt meriterande om du har dokumenterad erfarenhet av:
mätningar med EEG
EEG analyser
programmering med MATLAB och/eller Python
luktpsykofysisk testning
arbete i forskningsmiljö (t.ex. assistenttjänst)

Det är meriterande om du har:
MR-licens samt erfarenhet av att operera MR-kamera
mycket goda kunskaper i svenska

Vad erbjuder vi?
En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Vår vision är att driva utvecklingen av kunskap om livet och verka för en bättre hälsa för alla. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. Som universitet är Karolinska Institutet en statlig myndighet. Det gör att du får goda förmåner genom vårt kollektivavtal. Medarbetare på KI erbjuds också möjlighet till ett flexibelt arbetssätt. Det innebär att om den verksamhet du jobbar i tillåter, så kan du arbeta en del av din arbetstid på distans. Du får även träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar där utbildad personal finns på plats.

ap:254146.body:
Offer Description
In the frame of cancer treatment, chemotherapy is widely used, but it is impaired by resistance
development and by toxicity on healthy cells. New targeted therapies (tyrosine-kinase
inhibitors, ADC…) have led to the improvement of patient’s survival rates, but oncogenic targets
are not always well defined, and resistance may also occur, as do side-effects.
We recently developed a straightforward synthesis of new fused quinoline derivatives by means
of a photoactivation step. These compounds exhibit antiproliferative activity through an
innovative bioactivation pathway we have just patented.
Thanks to a grant from Inserm, we intend to exemplify these preliminary results through
numerous new promising chemical targets, some of which being patentable too.
Collaborations with two partners strongly support this project: 1) Computational chemistry
(LPCT UMR CNRS 7019, same location as L2CM) and 2) Biologic evaluation (CRCLille, UMR
1366 INSERM).

ABOUT GHENT UNIVERSITY
Ghent University is a world of its own. Employing more than 15.000 people, it is actively involved in education and research, management and administration, as well as technical and social service provision on a daily basis. It is one of the largest, most exciting employers in the area and offers great career opportunities.
With its 11 faculties and more than 85 departments offering state-of-the-art study programmes grounded in research in a wide range of academic fields, Ghent University is a logical choice for its staff and students.
YOUR JOB
Q-ForestLab (www.q-forestlab.ugent.be) is seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to work on the ERC project SPACETWIN: Digital twins for understanding forest disturbances and recovery from space.
Forests worldwide are undergoing large-scale and unprecedented changes in terms of structure and species composition due to anthropogenic disturbances, climate change, and other global change drivers. Climate, disturbances and forest structure are all closely linked: changes in climate can lead directly to physical changes in forest structure and vice versa or to an anticipated increase in forest disturbances. However, it is still uncertain how forest structure is impacted by disturbances (locally) and how we can detect and monitor various levels of disturbance regimes using spaceborne satellite data (globally).
This PhD position draws on the experience and resources from multiple projects such as SPACETWIN (ERC) and the Queensland Permanent Rainforest Plots (QPRP) Australia project (FWO). This project will focus on the impact of drought, fire, cyclone and logging disturbances across a range of tropical and temperate forest ecosystems. It will lead to a step-change in our ability to observe, quantify and understand forest disturbances and recovery by using time series of the most detailed structural and radiometric 3D forest models ever built: 'digital twin' forests. The project will draw upon Earth observation platforms spanning passive and active optical and microwave sensors.
Within your work, you will:
use 3D terrestrial laser scanning data to further develop the creation and implementation of digital twins of forests for optical and microwave radiative transfer modelling
explore the near-real time inversion of remote sensing of forest disturbances from satellites
use a library of digital twin forests to understand the monitoring of disturbances from satellites, applying this to important satellite missions quantifying forest structure such as ESA BIOMASS, NASA GEDI and future NASA EDGE and JAXA MOLI, with a particular focus on upscaling and uncertainties. We will use the extensive multi-scale lidar dataset of the Australian Wet Tropics as a case study. Fieldwork at these field sites may be required.

This PhD project will be promoted by prof. Kim Calders and co-supervised by dr. Niall Origo. You will interact regularly with Prof. Mathias Disney (University College London), who will act as an informal advisor.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
MSc degree (or equivalent) in a relevant field (Bioscience-Engineering, Remote Sensing, Surveying, Physics, Geosciences, Environmental Sciences, Computer Science, etc.)
Fluent in programming languages such as (at least one of) R, C++ or Python
Prior experience with satellite remote sensing (either optical or radar or both) and satellite data analysis
Prior experience with, or a solid understanding of, radiative transfer modelling within vegetation is preferred
Previous experience with (terrestrial) laser scanning and 3D modelling of forests is a plus, but not a requirement
A passion for nature and forests and a keen interest in forest ecology. You might also contribute to fieldwork to collect additional field data for this project
A good command of English, both written and oral.

WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
We offer a full-time position as a doctoral fellow, consisting of an initial period of 12 months, which, after a positive evaluation, will be extended to a total maximum of 48 months.
Your contract will start on January 1, 2027 at the earliest.
The fellowship amount is 100% of the net salary of an AAP member in equal family circumstances. The individual fellowship amount is determined by Team Personnel Administration based on family status and seniority. A grant that meets the conditions and criteria of the regulations for doctoral fellowships is considered free of personal income tax. Click here for more information about our salary scales.
All Ghent University staff members enjoy a number of benefits, such as a wide range of training and education opportunities, 36 days of holiday leave (on an annual basis for a full-time job) supplemented by annual fixed bridge days, bicycle allowance and eco vouchers. Click here for a complete overview of all the staff benefits.
The successful candidate will be based in Ghent.
Opportunities to present your work at scientific conferences.
Collaboration in a young and dynamic international scientific team. Life-work balance is important for us.
Please mention your favourite animal in your motivation letter so we can check that you at least read this vacancy in full.
About Q-ForestLab – www.q-forestlab.ugent.be Our lab is part of Ghent University in Belgium and studies vegetation dynamics, ecology, biogeochemistry, carbon and water cycling of terrestrial ecosystems. Q-ForestLab has a strong focus on forest ecosystems, but a broad interest in all types of terrestrial ecosystems, including tropical and temperate forests, drylands, peatlands and urban ecosystems. Our strength lies in a unique combination of methodologies, ranging from empirical in-situ observations and experiments, over 3D forest reconstructions, to process-based modelling and remote sensing.

ABOUT GHENT UNIVERSITY
Ghent University is an internationally renowned, open, pluralistic, and socially engaged university in Belgium. We strive to make science better and through that science, we also make the world better. Our credo is “Dare to Think”: we are a haven for courageous thinkers, including more than 50.000 students and 15.000 employees. As a caring and committed employer, our talent-driven HR policy is rewarded with the European “HR Excellence in Research” quality label.
RESEARCH PROJECT
Within the Faculty of Economics and Business Administration and the research group HRM, Strategy and Organization, Professor Gosia Kozusznik and Professor Greet Van Hoye are looking for a motivated PhD student to carry out a four-year research project on how human-robot teamwork is experienced in daily work, and under which conditions it supports worker well-being and performance.
Technology is rapidly transforming work. The integration of cobots within Industry 5.0 can enrich jobs, but it also brings psychological and organizational challenges, especially where robots work closely with people or replace them in hazardous settings. Both the popular press and academic work increasingly describe people and robots as teams. Yet existing research has mostly examined communication, coordination, and collaboration, and we know very little about the psychosocial processes that emerge when workers collaborate with robots every day: how they make sense of the robot as a colleague, how they cooperate in daily routines, and when tensions or conflicts arise. Understanding these processes, and the conditions under which collaboration with robots supports rather than undermines worker well-being and performance, is essential for designing healthier, more sustainable human-centered workplaces. To this end, multiple quantitative and qualitative research methods can be applied (e.g., experiment, questionnaire, interview, literature review).
YOUR TASKS
This position is primarily dedicated to carrying out the proposed research project, with the aim to write a doctoral dissertation consisting of academic articles that are publishable in international peer-reviewed journals.
You will present our research at international scientific conferences.
You will also reach out to experts and organizations in the field to discuss ideas, get feedback, collaborate on data collection, and translate our research findings into actionable advice.
You will provide some limited teaching support, such as guiding Master’s thesis students on a topic related to the research project.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You are almost or recently graduated with a Master’s degree relevant for the research project and including a research-based Master’s thesis. Final-year students are thus also encouraged to apply. Examples of relevant degrees are a (Research) Master in HRM/Organizational Behavior/Management/Business Economics/Communication or Work/Organizational/Social Psychology. For diplomas awarded outside the European Union, a certificate of equivalence (NARIC) must be submitted. The degree requirements need to be fulfilled at the start of your appointment.
You have performed well academically, as demonstrated by your study results (grades), Master’s thesis, and/or publications.
You are highly interested in the described research project and strongly motivated to obtain your PhD.
You possess good methodological and statistical skills, and are willing to develop those further. You have experience with SPSS or R.
You have good scientific writing and speaking skills, both in English and Dutch (surveys will be in both languages, writing will be mostly in English, contact with participants and organizations will be mostly in Dutch).
You are analytical, a problem-solver, and eager to learn.
You are conscientious, reliable, and quality-oriented. Your work is structured and consistent. You can keep a general oversight focusing on priorities but also have an eye for detail. You plan your work efficiently and can handle deadlines, both in the short and long term.
You take initiative and can work independently. You are open to feedback, which you proactively seek.
You have good social and communication skills, and work well within a team.
You are resilient and can cope with stress and setbacks.

WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
We offer a full-time, four-year position as a PhD student, enabling you to follow a doctoral training program and obtain a PhD in Business Economics. The contract starts with an initial period of 1 year, which, after a positive evaluation, will be extended by another 3 years.
Your contract will start on 1 February 2027 at the earliest, in consultation with you.
A monthly net wage of € 2.714. A grant that meets the conditions and criteria of the regulations for doctoral fellowships is considered free of personal income tax.
You will have the opportunity to work in a stimulating, dynamic, and open research environment “daring you to think”. Your (co-)supervisors have strong academic performance records, both in terms of publications and successful PhD’s. The research group houses many other PhD students allowing for ample social interactions and learning opportunities.
You will be able to conduct state-of-the art research on human-robot collaboration, a topic with great societal and practical relevance.
We offer many training and development opportunities, allowing you to further extend your methodological and statistical knowledge needed for the project, but also to acquire transferable skills supporting your further career (e.g., communication, project management).
We offer autonomy and flexibility, as well as multiple international experiences.
All Ghent University staff members enjoy a number of benefits, such as 36 days of holiday leave (on an annual basis for a full-time job) supplemented by annual fixed bridge days, bicycle allowance and eco vouchers.

INTERESTED?
Please send your application in a single pdf document to [email protected] by the 18th of November 2026 at the latest.
Your application should include:
A motivation letter and CV highlighting how you match the profile we look for.
Copy of your diploma (if already in your possession) and grade lists for each year in your study curriculum.
An English summary of your Master’s thesis (1-2 pages).
Two reference contacts, preferably including the (co-)supervisor of your Master’s thesis.

Candidates who are invited for the next selection round will be notified by the 30th of November 2026. On-site interviews will take place on the 16th and the 17th of December 2026 in Ghent.
As Ghent University maintains an equal opportunities and diversity policy, everyone is encouraged to apply for this position.
If you have any further questions about this vacancy, feel free to contact Professor Gosia Kozusznik ( [email protected] ). If you would like to talk to current PhD students of Prof Kozusznik and Van Hoye, you can reach out to Lucas Dierickx ( [email protected] ) or Julie Haspeslagh ( [email protected] ).

ap:254155.body:
Introduction
Do you enjoy bringing structure to complex projects and working with researchers in an innovative academic environment? Are you organized, communicative and curious about research and new technologies? Would you like to contribute to innovative research projects while developing your knowledge of research funding and project development? If so, we are looking for you.

Within the Project Development Office (PDO), you will help researchers navigate the different stages of a research project, from identifying funding opportunities and preparing grant proposals to facilitating a smooth transition towards project implementation. The PDO supports researchers throughout this process, ensuring that funding opportunities are identified, proposals are well prepared and projects can move smoothly from development to implementation.

We are looking for a proactive and organized Junior Project Development Officer to strengthen our research support team. In this role, you will support researchers, project coordinators and experienced Project Development Officers with grant preparation, project administration, consortium coordination and project management activities. You will help ensure that funding applications and research projects run smoothly by keeping track of deadlines, documentation, communication and administrative processes.

Job Description
As a Junior Advisor Research Funding, you support researchers and experienced Project Development Officers in the preparation and coordination of research proposals and projects. You help ensure that the practical, administrative and organizational aspects of funding applications are handled accurately and efficiently, keeping track of deadlines, documentation and communication.

A key part of your role is keeping track of the many moving parts involved in grant applications. You coordinate input from researchers and consortium partners, organize meetings, follow up on action points, monitor deadlines, perform compliance and completeness checks, and help set up applications in funding portals such as the European Commission Funding & Tenders Portal. You also maintain application records, project documentation and internal systems, and support communication activities where needed.

Once a project is awarded, you help ensure a smooth transition from proposal development to project implementation. You will support the administration and coordination of running research projects, for example by monitoring deadlines and deliverables, organizing meetings, supporting reporting and maintaining collaborative project environments such as SharePoint.

Within the Project Development Office of the Department of Biomedical Engineering, you will work closely with researchers, project coordinators and colleague Project Development Officer. You will be part of a team that supports innovative research throughout the project lifecycle. This role offers an opportunity to learn about research funding, project development and the research conducted within Biomedical Engineering, while contributing to the continuous improvement of research support processes.

Job Requirements
We are looking for a proactive and organized colleague who is eager to learn and interested in supporting innovative research. You bring:
A Bachelor's or Master's degree, preferably in Biomedical Engineering, a related field, or another relevant discipline.
Strong organizational and administrative skills, with an eye for detail and the ability to keep an overview of multiple tasks and deadlines.
Excellent communication skills in English, both written and verbal.
A proactive and hands-on approach: you take initiative, follow up on actions and make sure things keep moving.
The ability to work effectively with different stakeholders, including researchers, colleagues and external partners.
An interest in research, innovation and research funding, and the curiosity to learn how research projects are developed and funded.
Affinity with digital tools and new technologies, and an interest in exploring how AI and other tools can improve the way we work.

Experience with academic research, project management, research funding, or tools such as Microsoft Teams, SharePoint and online grant submission systems is a plus, but not required.

If you are concerned that you don’t meet all the requirements sufficiently, but the job does excite you, then be sure to respond, we would love to look at your profile.

Conditions of Employment
An exciting position within an international yet personal university. You are right in the middle of the students, on a green campus within walking distance of the central station. Besides beautiful architecture, you will find varied workplaces and excellent sports facilities.

We also offer you:
Salary in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , starting scale 8, ranging from €3.537 to €4.673. gross base salary per month (full-time), depending on your knowledge and experience.
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
A favorable arrangement for more holidays or a sabbatical.
A selection model for additional fringe benefits.
Working hours in consultation to support a healthy work-life balance, with the opportunity to work from home occasionally where the work allows.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
Scope for your talent with advancement prospects and excellent development opportunities such as mentoring, workshops and coaching.
Partially paid parental leave and reimbursement for commuting expenses, working from home and the internet.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
The Department of Biomedical Engineering offers top-level education and research in one of the most relevant and exciting scientific disciplines of the 21st century: engineering health. In combining engineering and life sciences, through challenge-based learning and a multidisciplinary approach in collaboration with hospitals, industry and others, the department addresses the great challenges of the future, striving to improve healthcare and society as a whole.

We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .

Our university is located in Braintport Eindhoven and part of a strong and diverse ecosystem of clinical centres, innovative SMEs and leading international companies. This close collaboration creates opportunities to connect research, technology and clinical practice, and to contribute to innovations that have a meaningful impact on society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .

Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to have more information about the position, please contact the hiring manager:  Steffie Hermans – Beijnsberger, [email protected] .

Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact Ivo Uitdenbogaart, Recruiter, [email protected] or +31 40 247 3299.

Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page.

Application
If you are interested, please use the ‘apply’ button to send us your CV and letter of application with your motivation and a description of your qualifications. Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications.

Screening of candidates begins as soon as applications are received and continues until the position is filled. Where applicable, internal candidates will be given priority over external candidates where they are equally suitable.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
Applications will be reviewed as soon as possible.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Important for non-EU applicants: Please be aware that for this position, specific residence permit requirements apply. If you are a non-EU national, you may not be eligible to legally work in this role under current Dutch immigration regulations. We strongly advise you to contact our Staff Immigration Team ( [email protected] ) before applying to check your eligibility and to receive further guidance.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ap:254156.body:
Following a grant of the Research Fund of the University of Leuven, an interdisciplinary research project “A New Model for the Edition of Ancient Philosophical Fragments” was launched in October 2025. In its present phase, the Faculty of Arts and the Faculty of Philosophy seek to hire a doctoral student who will prepare a PhD dissertation in (Ancient) History.

Website unit

Project

The project intends to develop a new model for editions of fragments, making use of the possibilities of digital editions. By ‘fragments’ we mean instances of incomplete text reuse. The goal is not exclusively to reconstruct what would otherwise be lost, but to map text reuse as a whole. Fragments are not treated as chunks of text extracted from source texts but as a demarcation of the relevant data in the latter plus a set of annotations with metadata and comments. A new, complex digital annotation scheme will allow for overlapping and mixed categorizations, document editorial decisions, and signal uncertainty. Texts in which concepts, doctrines, and arguments are central demand special treatment. They require philosophical and historical analyses of source context and of the reused text.

Currently three editions from the history of Platonism serve as test cases for the premises of the project. One of those texts is Damascius’ Vita Isidori, preserved in excerpts and fragments compiled by Photius and the Suda.

Candidates can apply for a full-time, four-year fellowship for the study of Damascius’ Vita Isidori, focusing on Photius’ methodology in compiling the excerpts, on the genre of Damascius’ work (biography/historiography of the Platonic school), the relationship between the different sets of excerpts (including the possibility of finding further as yet unidentified excerpts in Suda), the possibility of reconstructing the text, and especially the prosopography of the persons named in Damascius’ text and the history of the Platonic schools described in that work. The PhD student will also contribute to the annotation of, and the commentary on, the online edition of the Vita Isidori. The PhD thesis, supervised by an ancient historian and a historian of philosophy, is supposed to lead to a doctorate in History.

Profile

Selected candidates will have a broad, solid competence in ancient Greek, and preferably also in late ancient philosophy. They should also have the ability to combine historical, philological and philosophical methodologies in an interdisciplinary fashion. Candidates demonstrating relevant experience with Digital Humanities will have an asset. Applications from candidates with an excellent graduate degree (typically M.A.) in Classics are especially welcome, and candidates with an excellent degree in related disciplines (e.g. Ancient History, Philosophy) are also strongly invited to apply, providing that they have the necessary competence in Greek. Candidates are expected to be able to write and speak English on an academic level and to read relevant secondary literature in French, German, and Italian.

Candidates are, in addition, willing to perform a limited number of administrative and teaching tasks that the university expects of doctoral students.

Offer

• This fellowship provides the opportunity to participate in an enthusiastic research group within the context of a dynamic, internationally-oriented academic environment possessing unrivalled library resources.

• We are offering a 4-year full-time doctoral position. Initially, a 1-year contract will be offered. Following a positive evaluation, the contract will be extended for 3 years.

• You will be paid as a doctoral researcher (100%). From a legal standpoint, it is therefore necessary to reside in Belgium.

Interested?

To apply please submit:

• Your CV with detailed information about your academic performance in your bachelor’s and master’s programs (diploma supplement)

• A cover letter explaining why you are the best candidate for this project in this research unit (max. 2 pages)

• A writing sample in the form of a research-based text you have written (e.g., a scientific article, your master’s thesis)

• a letter of recommendation by a person related to a research institution

Preselected candidates will be invited for an interview by 16 November 2026, which will take place in the week of 30 November 2026 (in English).

Starting date: 1 February 2027 (or as soon thereafter as possible)

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Stefan Schorn, mail: [email protected] or Prof. dr. Gerd Van Riel, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

Oulun yliopisto on monitieteinen, kansainvälisesti toimiva tiedeyliopisto, jonka noin 4000 työntekijää tuottavat korkeatasoiseen tutkimukseen pohjautuvaa uutta tietoa ja antavat tutkimukseen perustuvaa opetusta kestävämmän, älykkäämmän ja inhimillisemmän maailman rakentamiseksi. Oulun yliopistoyhteisössä toimii kaikkiaan noin 19   000 henkilöä. Pohjoisen tiedeyhteisömme toiminta on globaalisti vaikuttavaa ja luo edellytyksiä innovaatioiden syntymiselle. Kaikkea tutkimus-, opetus- ja työyhteisötoimintaamme ohjaavat yliopistomme arvot sekä eettiset periaatteet.
Haemme nyt Oulun yliopiston kauppakorkeakouluun
Yliopisto-opettajaa
toistaiseksi voimassaolevaan työsuhteeseen kehittämään digitaalista opetusta, tutkinto-ohjelmien verkkokurssitarjontaa sekä jatkuvan oppimisen koulutustarjontaa.
Oulun yliopiston kauppakorkeakoulu on AACSB-akkreditoitu kauppakorkeakoulu ja yksi Oulun yliopiston kahdeksasta tiedekunnasta. Meillä opiskelee noin 1500 opiskelijaa ja työskentelee 130 henkilökunnan jäsentä. Kauppakorkeakoulu luo asiantuntijuutta nopeasti muuttuvien globaalien liiketoimintahaasteiden tarpeisiin, ja sen tavoitteena on rakentaa kestävämpää, älykkäämpää ja inhimillisempää maailmaa.
Työtehtävät

Verkkokurssien ja MOOC-opintojaksojen pedagoginen suunnittelu, kehittäminen ja koordinointi
Jatkuvan oppimisen koulutustarjonnan kehittäminen yhteistyössä koulutusohjelmien ja oppiaineiden kanssa
Opetusvastuu KTK-tutkinnon MOOC-toteutuksilla
Opetuksen suunnitteluun, kehittämiseen ja arviointiin liittyvät muut tehtävät
Omaopettajatehtävät ja opiskelijoiden ohjaus
Digitaalisten oppimisratkaisujen ja oppimisanalytiikan kehittäminen ja käyttöönotto osana opetusta
MOOC-tuotantoprosessien koordinointi ja laadunvarmistus kauppatieteiden opetusportfoliossa

Tuen asiantuntevalta ja innostuneelta tiedekuntayhteisöltä, jossa pääset kehittymään ja jakamaan asiantuntemustasi.
Liikunta-, kulttuuri- ja hyvinvointietuja (ePassi). Lue lisää muista työsuhde-eduistamme .

ap:254163.body:
Empa  and Eawag , two world-leading research institutes within the ETH Domain, are bundling their expertise to address one of the key questions of our times: How can demonstrated, but underutilized, climate change adaptation and mitigation technologies (like NetZero construction, resilient urban water systems, renewable energy, etc.) be scaled up and mainstreamed to reach their full transformative potential? To tackle this question, we established the Climate Solutions Hub (CSH) , a new collaboration platform in which scholars from our two institutes and the ETH Domain more broadly are collaborating with partners from industry, the public sector, and civil society to analyze and support the scaling of innovative climate solutions.
The Hub’s co-leadership is composed of two representatives, one from each institution, with backgrounds in social sciences and engineering sciences respectively. We are now opening the position that should represent Empa and the domain of engineering, materials, natural and building sciences.

Co-Lead of the Climate Solutions Hub (a, 50%)
Your main tasks will include
Development and implementation of the strategy of the Climate Solutions Hub
Liaison with the research community at Empa and Eawag, across the ETH Domain, and beyond
Managing high-level stakeholder networks in academia, as well as the private and public sector
Project and funding acquisition
Representing the Hub towards our directorates and scientific/impact Advisory Boards
Managing the CSH team with three research groups and support staff
Responsibility for personnel and budget

Your profile
You are a team-oriented and forward-thinking person with a strong interest in implementing science-based measures addressing climate mitigation and adaptation. You have experience with leading and managing projects at the interface of social sciences, engineering, and natural sciences and in close collaboration with stakeholders. You are well-connected in the ETH Domain and with practice partners and have a strong interest in developing the Hub concept further and establishing it within broader ETH Domain strategies.
Your qualifications include
Experience in leading or substantially shaping inter- and transdisciplinary research projects  and communicating key results to broad, non-scientific audiences
Institutional judgement . Experience in operating within and across research organisations - effectively and constructively navigating diverging cultures, department politics, or directorate priorities.
PhD in engineering, materials, building sciences, or related fields
Familiarity with Empa, the ETH Domain, and its broader research and innovation ecosystem.
Working proficiency in English and German ; knowledge of other official languages in Switzerland is a plus. An existing network in Swiss construction, energy or infrastructure sectors - including at cantonal and municipal levels and/or with industry partners is a plus.
Clear vision for developing an open and inclusive team culture
A track record of raising third-party funding for collaborative, multi-partner projects is a plus.
Experience in working in co-leadership arrangements is a plus.

Our offer
We offer a purposeful leadership role within a unique and dynamic research environment that bundles the expertise of multiple ETH Domain Institutes. You will have the opportunity to guide and perform high-level research with direct impact in practice and play a key role in developing a highly innovative research initiative. We foster a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities. Our commitment is documented in our Diversity Action Plan and refers to specific goals, which are implemented and further developed on a regular basis.

You don't meet every single requirement? We are aware that particularly women and individuals from minority backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. However, we also value motivation, commitment and a willingness to learn. If you see yourself in this role, we would love to receive your qualified application, even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements.

We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal until 25 November 2026 . Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.

ap:254165.body:
Introduction
Data centers are the backbone of the digital economy, but their exponential growth in energy consumption-driven by AI and machine learning workloads-demands transformative solutions. The next-generation of data centers will be based on Solid-State Transformer, which enables energy distribution with higher efficiency, grid-friendly data center operation and etc.
This PhD position offers a unique opportunity to work at the intersection of power electronics, control systems, and grid integration, with direct collaboration with Delta Energy System GmbH, a global leader in power conversion for data centers. Your research will focus on power electronics converters for SST, focusing on the DC-DC stage.
Job Description
As a PhD candidate in the Electromechanics and Power Electronics (EPE) group at TU/e, you will with solid-state transformers (SST) for datacenter, focusing on the DC-DC stage. Your research will address the critical challenges of power density, efficiency, and grid stability in modern data centers, focusing on the converter design and advanced control/modulation strategies to achieve high performance and high controllability. Additionally, the design should be validate with experimental results. Your work will directly contribute to the sustainability of AI infrastructure by enabling data centers to efficiently integrate renewable energy sources, support grid stability, and reduce their carbon footprint. With access to cutting-edge tools and industrial collaboration, you will have the opportunity to shape the future of power electronics for data centers.
Job Requirements
A master's degree (or equivalent university degree) in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, Control Systems, or a related field.
A research-oriented attitude with strong analytical and problem-solving skills.
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team and interest in collaborating with industrial partners.
Motivated to develop your teaching skills and coach students.

Based on our candidate assessment, the following skills are valuable:
Required:
Demonstrated knowledge in power converter topologies (e.g., DC-DC, AC-DC, multilevel converters).
Familiarity with control theory (e.g., classical control, state-space methods, model predictive control).
Experience with simulation tools (MATLAB/Simulink, PLECS, or similar).
Understanding of grid integration challenges (e.g., power quality, stability, renewable energy interfacing).

Advantageous:
Hands-on experience with prototyping and experimental validation of power converters.
Affinity with embedded systems (DSP, FPGA) for real-time control implementation.

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.

Introduction
Are you a graduate in exact sciences, engineering or econometrics, passionate about using data and AI to improve people's lives?Eindhoven University of Technology is looking for a PhD candidate to develop innovative data-driven solutions that predict and optimise the impact of housing improvements on children's health and wellbeing.
Job Description
Millions of children, even in high-income countries, are born and grow up in homes with poor insulation, inadequate heating, or insufficient ventilation, affecting their health and development. While housing upgrades are often motivated by sustainability and affordability goals, we focus on their potential benefits for future generations. How does inadequate housing during pregnancy and early childhood affect children's health and development? Which housing upgrades offer the greatest benefits? And how can behavioural modelling, big data and AI help shape healthier, more equitable homes? These are the questions your PhD research will tackle.
You will join an interdisciplinary team of researchers and practitioners, working at the intersection of housing, public health, climate adaptation, and social equity. Combining medical and behavioural insights, large-scale data analysis, computer vision and advanced statistical methods, you will be tranforming complex unstructured housing and health data into predictive models. The results will feed into a digital tool to predict and optimise the impact of housing upgrades across different scenarios, helping housing providers and municipalities create healthier, more resilient homes for families.
This research is part of the NWO-funded research programme Homes for Upcoming Generations, which brings together social scientists, medical doctors, building engineers and industry partners.
As a PhD candidate, you will be part of the TU/e's internationally renowned Urban Systems and Real Estate group (Department of the Built Environment), conducting cutting-edge research at the intersection of urban systems, real estate, data science, and smart technologies. The four-year program combines advanced training with impactful research, offering strong support for professional development through courses, seminars, and international conferences. You will collaborate closely with scientific partners at Erasmus Medical Centre, Erasmus University Rotterdam, VU University Amsterdam, as well as societal partners including housing providers, municipalities and engineering bureaus.

ap:254167.body:
How Do Genetics and Diet Influence Trout Cardiac and Cellular Morphology?

Join the Laboratory of Systems Biology at TalTech for a four-year Ph.D. investigating how genetics and diet influence rainbow trout heart and cardiomyocyte morphology. Using experimental approaches, you will help identify factors underlying cardiac abnormalities in farmed fish and contribute to guidelines for improving fish robustness.

The project will address the following key areas:
Farmed salmonid fish commonly exhibit cardiac abnormalities, including unusual ventricular shapes and tissue lesions. These changes may compromise blood flow and limit cardiac performance, but the relative contributions of genetic background and feed composition remain unclear. This project aims to determine how these factors influence cardiac morphology in rainbow trout and to provide evidence for guidelines that support the production of more robust farmed fish.
The research will examine morphology at both the whole-heart and cardiomyocyte levels. Histology, immunocytochemistry, microscopy, and quantitative image analysis will be used to assess structural differences between experimental groups. The project will relate observations across these scales to develop a clearer understanding of how genetics and diet shape cardiac structure.
The student will work closely with a second Ph.D. student investigating cardiac performance and metabolism in the same fish cohorts. Together, the projects will connect structural observations with functional measurements. The work will involve independent experimental planning coordinated with other laboratory members, data analysis, and communication of findings through scientific publications and conference presentations. Training in project-specific methods will be provided, building on the successful applicant's existing experimental background.

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
Plan and conduct experiments independently, coordinating schedules and shared resources with other laboratory members.
Assess whole-heart and cardiomyocyte morphology using histology, immunocytochemistry, microscopy, and image analysis.
Analyse and interpret experimental data in collaboration with the student studying cardiac performance and metabolism.
Prepare scientific publications and present findings at conferences.
Contribute to the supervision of students.
Assist with routine fish husbandry, including a few hours on assigned weekends through a shared rota. This is a supporting responsibility rather than the main focus of the project.

Applicants should fulfil the following requirements:
Hold an M.Sc. degree in biology or a related discipline.
Have practical experience in experimental biological research, gained through a thesis, research project, or laboratory work.
Demonstrate English proficiency at C1 or C2 level.
Be able to plan and organise work independently while coordinating effectively with colleagues.
Show motivation to develop new experimental skills and conduct doctoral research.
Be willing to work with live fish and participate in the animal-care rota.

The following experience is beneficial:
Cardiac morphology, comparative anatomy, or cell biology.
Histology and tissue preparation.
Immunocytochemistry or related antibody-based imaging methods.
Microscopy and quantitative image analysis.
Statistical analysis of experimental data.
Animal handling or fish husbandry.

Experience in all of these areas is not required.
We offer:
A four-year Ph.D. position with a minimum gross monthly salary of EUR 2,300 throughout the four years.
Training in the experimental and analytical methods needed for the project.
Opportunities to participate in scientific conferences and present research findings.
An interdisciplinary research environment bringing together expertise in biology and physics.
Close collaboration with a fellow Ph.D. student working on complementary measurements in the same fish cohorts.

Supervisors:
Main supervisor: Tenured Full Professor Marko Vendelin, School of Science: Department of Cybernetics: Laboratory of Systems Biology
Co-Supervisor: Assistant Professor Martin Laasmaa, School of Science: Department of Cybernetics: Laboratory of Systems Biology

ap:254169.body:
Experimental Development of Sorption-Enhanced Gasification with Calcium Looping for Hydrogen-rich Gas Production

This PhD project will develop and validate sorption-enhanced gasification with calcium looping (SEG-CaL) using biomass, residues and calcium-rich materials. It will assess how feedstock, sorbent, and operating conditions affect gas composition, H₂ production, CO₂ capture, stability and scale-up. The work combines characterisation, TGA, batch gasification and pilot testing. The project is co-funded by the European Union and the Estonian Ministry of Education and Research TEM-TA205.

The project will address the following key areas:
SEG-CaL integrates biomass (BM) and residue gasification with in-situ CO₂ capture: a calcium-based sorbent captures CO₂ and forms CaCO₃. This interaction can improve H2 content, but it also introduces technical questions related to sorbent reactivity, ash interactions, heat transfer, circulation, etc. The PhD research novelty lies in the integrated Lab-to-pilot investigation of SEG-CaL using locally available BM, residues and calcium-rich circular resources. The PhD will evaluate secondary materials as sorbents and determine how their interactions with feedstock ash and gasification products affect CO₂ capture, H2-rich gas formation, carbon conversion and cyclic stability. Pilot-scale validation will be used to verify laboratory findings, identify practical limitations and generate data for environmental, techno-economic and industrial assessment.
The research will address the following questions:
How do the composition, mineralogy and morphology of locally available calcium-rich materials influence carbonation capacity, cyclic stability and interaction with BM and residue-derived ash?
Which laboratory-scale measurements and material-performance indicators can reliably predict sorbent behaviour and process performance during pilot-scale operation?
How do feedstock properties and operating conditions govern the coupling between gasification, in-situ CO2 capture and H2-rich gas formation?

And test the following hypotheses:
Selected local calcium-rich materials can provide effective CO2 capture while supporting gasification of representative BM and residue streams.
In-situ CO2 removal can shift the gasification chemistry towards higher H2 production and improved carbon conversion under suitable operating conditions.
The interaction between sorbent properties, feedstock ash and operating conditions is a major determinant of cyclic stability and pilot-scale performance and can be described using laboratory-to-pilot correlations.

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
Select, prepare and characterise representative biomass, residue, ash-derived and calcium-rich sorbent materials.
Perform thermogravimetric and complementary laboratory experiments to determine gasification, carbonation, calcination and sorbent-cycling behaviour.
Investigate the effects of feedstock composition, ash constituents and sorbent properties on gasification reactions and CO2 capture.
Plan and conduct batch-scale gasification experiments under selected temperature, steam and sorbent conditions.
Measure and evaluate syngas composition, hydrogen production, CO2 capture, carbon conversion and relevant process-performance indicators.
Assess sorbent stability, deactivation, attrition, agglomeration, fouling and other material or operational limitations relevant to scale-up.
Contribute to the design, modification, commissioning and safe operation of the integrated fluidised-bed combustion-pyrolysis pilot facility.
Conduct pilot validation campaigns and compare pilot observations with laboratory results and process-model predictions.
Collaborate with researchers, doctoral students, technical staff and project partners.
Publish research results in peer-reviewed journals and present findings at international conferences.
Contribute to the supervision of BSc and MSc students, and willingness to assist in teaching where appropriate.

Applicants should fulfil the following requirements:
A master's degree in chemical engineering, energy technology, process engineering, environmental engineering, materials science, chemistry, mechanical engineering or another closely related subject.
Proven experience in fluidized bed processes, high-temperature experimental research, particularly combustion or gasification.
A clear interest in biomass and residue conversion, gasification, CO2 capture, calcium or chemical looping, hydrogen production or related energy technologies.
Ability to plan experiments, analyse results critically and document research in a reproducible manner.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently and as part of a multidisciplinary research team.
Good written and spoken English, at least B2 level according to the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.
Additional general requirements can be found at the TalTech PhD admission homepage .

Applicants should submit:
A cover letter outlining the applicant's motivation and relevant experience.
A CV, including education, research experience, technical skills and a list of publications, where applicable.
A short research plan describing the proposed research strategy, experimental approach and expected contribution to the SEG-CaL project.
Proposed titles and brief outlines of at least three potential scientific publications arising from the research.
Previous work, such as a master's thesis, scientific articles, technical reports or conference contributions, demonstrating relevant research experience.

The following experience is beneficial:
Practical experience in thermochemical processes, such as gasification, pyrolysis, combustion, chemical/calcium looping, or another high-temperature reactor research.
Experience with thermogravimetric analysis and the interpretation of reaction kinetics or cyclic sorbent behaviour.
Experience with biomass, waste-derived materials, ash chemistry or calcium-based sorbents.
Experience with gas analysis, including gas chromatography, infrared gas analysis or comparable methods.
Experience operating laboratory or pilot-scale equipment and working safely with high temperatures, steam and reactive gases.
Technical report writing, scientific publication, conference presentation and collaboration in an international research environment.

We offer:

A doctoral research position in the Department of Energy Technology at Tallinn University of Technology, connected to the Tem-TA205 project.

ap:254170.body:
When the Mundane Becomes Transformational. Everyday self-provisioning practices as form of prefiguration for a degrowth future

The PhD research examines the transformative potential of alternative self-provision practices (e.g. food self-provisioning, sharing, repair and DIY) as pathways to degrowth. It explores how everyday practices can be system-changing (e.g. prefiguration, prosumption, quiet sustainability) and under what conditions they support economic transformation “from below”, drawing on qualitative research on alternative/ecological economies, degrowth and sustainability.

The project will address the following key areas:
While alternative self-provision practices, incl. food self-provisioning, foraging, informal sharing economy practices, repair and DIY, have hitherto remained largely invisible in mainstream economic thinking (Pungas 2023), they have recently gained increasing attention in the research on quiet sustainability (Smith and Jehlicka 2013, Sovova et al. 2025), prefiguration (Siddharth et al. 2026) and degrowth (Spanier et al. 2024). Yet evidence on whether and under what conditions such seemingly mundane everyday practices can contribute to transformative change remains fragmented (cf Forno and Wahlen 2022). Some research has questioned their political and transformative potential (e.g. Goodman et al. 2012), while other studies have highlighted pathways from individual practices towards collective forms of action, such as local food solidarity networks and community-based FSP initiatives (Forno et al, 2015; Guidi and Andretta, 2015; Smith and Jehlicka 2013, Sovova et al. 2025). Tapping into this gap, this PhD project sets out to explore the transformative potential of alternative self-provision practices for a degrowth future .
The thesis should address questions such as:
If and how can mundane and quiet practices be seen as part of a degrowth future or “nowtopia”? Do practitioners see them as such, why/why not? (in other words, is a prefigurative mindset needed for prefigurative change)
Which practices and quiet sustainability niches exist in Estonia, how do they emerge and which are their development paths?
What are the motives, barriers / enablers and potential pathways from seemingly mundane everyday self-provisioning practices toward broader economic and business transformation (e.g. degrowth and sustainability management, doughnut, diverse, degrowth economies)? (in other words, systemic scaling of quiet small-scale practices)

Responsibilities and (foreseen) tasks:
The selected PhD candidate will be granted independence regarding the choice of theoretical framing, research philosophy, and methodological emphasis, while working within the broader framework outlined above. The project is expected to involve mixed-method qualitative research. The PhD candidate should already have learned, or be willing to learn, one or more research methodologies and methods such as qualitative interviewing, case-study analysis, participatory observation and fieldwork, as well as qualitative research analysis.
The PhD candidate’s work is expected to engage with several empirical components, including:
Mapping of existing mundane self-provisioning practices in Estonia , and former research studying these (e.g. foraging, dacha gardening, informal food (exchange) networks, organic non-profit farms/semi-self-sufficiency farms, repair, DIY)
Multiple case studies with self-provisioning practitioners to understand their pathways, practices, networks and relation to the conventional (market-based) system and transformative impact/intention
Exploration with self-provision practitioners and dis-/enabling system stake-holders about the possible pathways from prefiguration to system change
Analysis of findings from a system transformation / degrowth (or other suitable alternative economy and management) perspective

The candidate’s main task will be to prepare a doctoral thesis under the supervision of Ass. Prof. Bianka Plüschke-Altof. The candidate is also expected to engage in small-scale teaching, contribute to topic-related project proposals, and actively participate in the department’s academic life.

The candidate is expected to have:
a master’s degree in social sciences (e.g. sociology, human geography, economics), management, anthropology, or a related field
a clear interest in the topic
excellent command of English and Estonian
strong and demonstrable writing and analytical skills
capacity to work both as an independent researcher and part of a research team
capacity and willingness to contribute to teaching and organisational tasks

The candidate must submit a research plan (5 pages) for the topic , including a preliminary overview of relevant literature and an overall research design. The candidate may expand on the listed research questions and tasks and propose specific theoretical lenses and methods to be used.

The following experience is beneficial:
working knowledge of qualitative research methods
familiarity with mixed-method designs or willingness to learn
knowledge of topics such as prefiguration, quiet sustainability, alternative economic practices, system transformation, degrowth
experience in fieldwork and participatory research

We offer
4-year funded PhD position at Taltech’s School of Business and Governance, with a large portfolio of ongoing pan-European and national research projects;
Enrolment in the doctoral study program “Business, Economics and Governance”
Potential for high-impact research and active involvement in research projects of the assigned research group;
Opportunities for conference visits, research stays and networking with leading universities and research centres;
All PhD positions are guaranteed a gross income of at least 2300 EUR and Estonian national health insurance.

Supervisors:
Main supervisor: Assistant Professor Bianka Plüschke-Altof, School of Business and Governance: Department of Business Administration: Sustainable Value Chain Management Unit

Tallinn University of Technology (TalTech) is an international scientific community with approximately 9,000 students and 2,000 employees; it is one of the largest universities in Estonia, the leading EU country in digitalisation. The university's strengths are broad multidisciplinary study/research interests, a modern research environment, and strong collaboration with international educational and research institutions. TalTech is aiming to be an organisation leading the way to a sustainable digital future.
TalTech School of Business and Governance is the leading provider of higher education in the fields of economics, business administration, law and public administration in the Baltic States. Our faculty includes internationally recognised top scientists and outstanding practitioners not only from Estonia but also from abroad (34% international faculty members from 33 countries). About 23% of international students from over 60 countries confirm the attractiveness of the School in international education. The research carried out at the  Department of Business Administration deals with various aspects of business – entrepreneurship, sustainability, knowledge and technology transfer, operations and strategic management, digitalization, marketing, supply chain management, accounting and performance management. The department is highly internationalised. Its staff have been involved in a multitude of international research projects with the EU (INTERREG, COST, Horizon Europe etc).
