ap:254171.body:
DIFFER: Science for future energy
At the Dutch Institute for Fundamental Energy Research (DIFFER) we work on a future in which clean energy will be available to everybody, anywhere in the world. DIFFER’s mission is to perform leading fundamental research on materials, processes, and systems for a global sustainable energy infrastructure.
Our research focuses on two major energy themes: fusion energy as a clean, safe and sustainable energy source and chemical energy. We work in close partnership with (inter)national academia and industry. DIFFER is one of the ten research institutes of the Dutch Research Council (NWO).
Within our institute physicists, chemists, engineers, and other specialists work together in multidisciplinary teams to accelerate the transition to a sustainable society. DIFFER’s workforce is currently composed of ~160 scientists (of which 60 guests and interns), supported by ~40 technicians and ~40 support staff members.
The global nature of the energy challenge is apparent from the international representation of our employees, who originate from over 30 different countries. To strengthen our commitment to diversity, we formed a task force to design, implement, and monitor diversity and gender equality initiatives.
Differ is looking for a PhD candidate in Nitrogen Valorization in High Temperature Proton and Oxygen Ion Conducting Electrochemical Cells
Sustainable ammonia production is an important challenge in the transition towards a climate-neutral chemical industry. Conventional ammonia synthesis is highly energy intensive and relies predominantly on fossil-derived hydrogen. Electrochemical routes offer the possibility to produce ammonia using renewable electricity while enabling new, decentralized production concepts.
This PhD project will focus on the development of advanced materials, electrodes, and membrane-electrode assemblies for high-temperature electrochemical ammonia synthesis using solid oxide and protonic ceramic electrochemical cells (SOC and PCC technologies). The research will address the electrochemical conversion of nitrogen- and NOx-containing streams towards NH3.
The project will combine catalyst and electrode development with ceramic-cell fabrication, electrochemical testing, product analysis, and advanced materials characterization. Different catalyst integration strategies, including infiltration and exsolution, will be investigated to improve activity, selectivity, and long-term stability. Particular attention will be given to electrode–electrolyte interfaces, reaction mechanisms, and degradation under realistic operating conditions.
This PhD position is part of HyNITROGEN ( https://groenvermogennl.org/en/nieuws/e20-3-million-for-hynitrogen-consortium-research-into-sustainable-nitrogen-chemistry ) a large national research program within GroenvermogenNL that brings together more than 40 academic and industrial partners to develop sustainable production routes for ammonia and other nitrogen-based chemicals using renewable hydrogen and green electricity.
Position and requirements
About the group
The work will be carried out in the Catalytic and Electrochemical Processes for Energy Applications (CEPEA) group at DIFFER. The research of the group focuses on electrochemical membrane reactors for sustainable fuel production and the electrification of the chemical industry. Our activities span the full chain from functional materials and electrodes to membrane-electrode assemblies and laboratory-scale electrochemical reactors, with the overarching goal of developing scalable technologies.
Responsibilities and tasks
The research is highly interdisciplinary and combines materials science, catalysis, electrochemistry, and ceramic electrochemical-cell engineering. The successful candidate will contribute to:
Development and evaluation of catalytic electrodes for high-temperature electrochemical ammonia synthesis.
Fabrication, assembly, and testing of SOEC/SOFC and/or PCEC/PCFC cells.

Integration of electrocatalysts into porous ceramic electrodes using approaches such as infiltration, impregnation, and exsolution.

Electrochemical characterization using polarization measurements, electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS), and complementary techniques.

Investigation of electrode kinetics, interfacial resistances, mass transport, and degradation mechanisms.

Operation of ceramic electrochemical cells at temperatures typically between 400 and 800 °C and, where relevant, under elevated pressure.

Gas-phase analysis of reaction products using GC, QMS/MS, and FTIR.

Physico-structural characterization of materials and electrodes using techniques such as XRD, XPS, SEM/EDX, and TEM.

Correlation of material and electrode properties with electrochemical performance, selectivity, and durability.

Long-term durability experiments and post-test degradation analysis.

Preparation of scientific publications and presentations at international conferences.

Supervision and support of BSc and MSc students.

Contribution to the collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment at DIFFER and within the project consortium.

Job requirements
We are particularly interested in candidates with a background in electrochemistry, material science and catalysis.
You should have:
A Master's degree, or equivalent, in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Chemistry, Applied Physics, Energy Engineering, Electrochemistry, or a closely related discipline.

Practical research experience with SOFC/SOEC, PCFC/PCEC, or closely related ceramic electrochemical-cell technologies.

Experience with the fabrication, assembly, or electrochemical testing of ceramic electrochemical cells is strongly preferred.

Familiarity with ceramic electrolytes, porous electrodes, mixed ionic-electronic conductors, or electrode/electrolyte interfaces is highly desirable.

Experience with electrochemical characterization techniques, particularly EIS and polarization measurements, is considered a strong advantage.

Experience with high-temperature experimental setups, gas handling, fuel-cell/electrolyser test stations, or product analysis by GC, QMS/MS, or FTIR is an advantage.

Knowledge of electrocatalysis, heterogeneous catalysis, infiltration, exsolution, or ceramic-material synthesis will be regarded as an additional asset.

Strong analytical skills, initiative, and creativity.

A genuine curiosity for science and motivation to pursue high-level experimental research.

Excellent written and oral communication skills in English.

Ability to work effectively in a collaborative, international, and multidisciplinary environment with a positive team spirit.

Candidates with hands-on experience in SOFC/SOEC or PCFC/PCEC research are particularly encouraged to apply.
Terms and conditions
This position is for 1 FTE, will be for a period of 4 years and is graded in pay scale PhD; the gross monthly salary starts with €3.115,- in the first year and increases to €3.989,- in the fourth year of your employment. he salary is supplemented with a holiday allowance of 8% and an end-of year bonus of 8.33%.The position will be based at DIFFER ( www.differ.nl ) and the working location will be at TU Eindhoven. When fulfilling a position at DIFFER, you will have an employee status at NWO. You can participate in all the employee benefits NWO offers. We have a number of regulations that support employees in finding a good work-life balance. At DIFFER we believe that a workforce diverse in gender, age and cultural background is key to performing excellent research. We therefore strongly encourage everyone to apply. More information on working at NWO can be found at the NWO website ( https://www.nwo-i.nl/en/working-at-nwo-i/jobsatnwoi/ ).
Information and application
Further information about the vacancy is available through Dr. M. N. Tsampas, e-mail:  [email protected] , and via the CEPEA website at  www.differ.nl/research/cepea .
Application
We invite you to submit a complete application using the apply button. The application should include:
A motivation letter describing your interest in the position and, in particular, your previous experience with ceramic electrochemical cells, or closely related technologies.

A curriculum vitae, including contact details of at least two references.

A list of BSc and MSc courses and grades.

We look forward to receiving your application and will start screening applications as soon as they are received. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled.
Closing date
The vacancy will close on Sunday, November 29.
Closing date
November 29, 2026

Om stillingen
Vil du være med på å utvikle kunnskap for å møte framtidas sosialfaglige utfordringer?
Stillingen er treårig, men dersom stipendiaten som ansettes har relevant bakgrunn for våre undervisningsbehov, kan ansettelsesperioden utvides til fire år med 25% karrierefremmende arbeid. Tiltredelse i stillingen forutsetter opptak på doktorgradsprogrammet i samfunnsvitenskap, studieretning for sosialt arbeid og sosialpolitikk.
Institutt for sosialfag har sosialt arbeid og eldre som en av fem tematiske satsingsområdene i sin instituttstrategi for perioden 2025-2030. Den demografiske utviklingen viser at det innen 2030 vil være flere over 67 år enn barn i Norge. Dette er en utvikling som utfordrer alle deler av velferdsstaten.
Den delen av livsløpet som kan kalles alderdommen inkluderer personer fra 60 år til godt over 100 år. Kjente utfordringer for eldre og gamle personer er tap av roller og funksjoner, samt tap av funksjonsnivå. Sosial ulikhet og ulik evne til å ta i bruk tjenester, teknologiske og digitale virkemidler påvirker i stor grad omfanget av utfordringer.
Instituttet vil ha et særlig søkelys på de sosiale og relasjonelle sidene ved aldring, alderdom og eldreomsorg. Det vil være viktig for instituttet å utvikle kunnskap om eldres menneskeverd, frigjøring og myndiggjøring, og hvordan den ivaretas i eldreomsorgen. Herunder er vi opptatt av hvordan teknologiske løsninger, deriblant KI, kan brukes på måter som styrker, ikke erstatter, det menneskelige og relasjonelle aspektet ved eldreomsorg. Vi er også opptatt av konsekvenser av den politiske målsettingen om at alle skal bo lengst mulig hjemme, og hvilke forhold som kan påvirke disse konsekvensene.
For en nærmere beskrivelse av satsingen, se  Strategi 2025 – 2030 for Institutt for sosialfag - OsloMet .
Vi forventer at du i prosjektbeskrivelsen beskriver hvordan prosjektet knytter seg til instituttstrategien.
Kvalifikasjonskrav
Du må ha:
utdanning innen sosialfag på hovedfags- eller mastergradsnivå (120 studiepoeng) eller tilsvarende innen øvrige samfunnsvitenskapelige disipliner. Du må ha B eller bedre på masteroppgaven og gjennomsnittskarakter tilsvarende B eller bedre på mastergraden.
gode kvalifikasjoner innenfor forskningsmetoder
god skriftlig og muntlig fremstillingsevne på norsk/skandinavisk og engelsk
kapasitet til å arbeide selvstendig, planmessig og målrettet
gode samarbeidsevner
faglig engasjement
gode analytiske ferdigheter

Det er en fordel at du har:
relevant erfaring fra forsknings- og utviklingsarbeid
relevant praksiserfaring fra en eller flere velferdstjenester
sosialfag i fagkretsen

Det er viktig for OsloMet å gjenspeile befolkningen i vår region og vi ønsker alle kvalifiserte søkere velkommen. Vi arbeider aktivt med å utvikle oss videre som en inkluderende arbeidsplass og for å tilrettelegge arbeidsplassen dersom du har behov for det. Har du perioder i livet hvor du ikke har vært i arbeid, utdanning eller opplæring er du også velkommen til å søke hos oss.
Vilkår:
opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet i doktorgradsprogrammet i samfunnsvitenskap, studieretning for sosialt arbeid og sosialpolitikk er et vilkår for tiltredelse i stilling som stipendiat.
endelig plan for forskerutdanning skal være godkjent og avtalefestet senest tre måneder etter tiltredelse.

Søkeren skal sende inn fullstendig prosjektbeskrivelse med søknaden. Prosjektet må være innenfor temaene i utlysningen og forholde seg til den faglige innretningen for doktorgradsprogrammet i sosialt arbeid og sosialpolitikk.
Prosjektbeskrivelsen skal være på maks 10 sider og skrives på skandinavisk språk eller engelsk, og skal inneholde
problemstilling(er), teoretisk forankring og metodisk tilnærming
beskrivelse av kunnskapsbehov og avhandlingens bidrag til forskningen i feltet
plan for gjennomføring av doktorgradsstudiet, inkludert tidsplan
eventuelt planlagt opphold ved et relevant utenlandsk universitet
referanseliste

I vurderingen av søkere vil det bli lagt særlig vekt på grunnleggende kvalifikasjoner (karakterer, faglige kvalifikasjoner og tidligere erfaring) og innsendt prosjektbeskrivelse. Beskrivelsen må være på et faglig nivå som gjør det sannsynlig at prosjektet vil føre frem til doktorgrad innen en treårsperiode.
Sakkyndig utvalg
Som søker vil du bli vurdert av et sakkyndig utvalg.
Vi benytter et elektronisk rekrutteringssystem. Innen søknadsfristen må du sammen med søknaden laste opp følgende dokumenter:
CV, attester og vitnemål
prosjektbeskrivelse skrevet på skandinavisk språk eller engelsk (maks 10 sider inkl. referanseliste)
hovedoppgave eller masteroppgave
eventuelle andre vitenskapelige arbeider
liste over eventuelle publikasjoner og presentasjoner ved internasjonale seminarer/konferanser

Søknader som sendes inn uten vedleggene som er nevnt ovenfor vil ikke bli vurdert.
Vitnemål, attester og publikasjoner må være på engelsk eller et skandinavisk språk. Oversettelser må være autorisert. Du må fremvise originaler ved et eventuelt intervju. OsloMet gjennomfører kontroll av dokumenter, slik at du som kandidat skal få en reell evaluering og rettferdig konkurranse.
Dersom vi får mer enn 20 kvalifiserte søkere til stillingen, vil det bli etablert en presilingskomite for å sile ut de mest kvalifiserte søkerne før sakkyndig utvalg vurderer søkerne.

OsloMet søker deg som trives med å automatisere og modernisere driften av Windows-servere, og som ønsker å bidra til gode teknologiske veivalg for fremtiden.

bidra til stabil, sikker og effektiv drift av Windows-servere

erfaring med drift av Windows Server i hybride miljøer (lokalt og i sky)

Inkludering og mangfold styrker vår evne til å løse OsloMets samfunnsoppdrag. Derfor ønsker vi medarbeidere med ulike kompetanser, livserfaringer og perspektiver velkommen. Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder, Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap er det ledig en 100 % stilling som doktorgradsstipendiat i helsevitenskap med fokus på sosial inkludering og likeverdig tilgang til digitale løsninger for helsefremming for en periode på tre år. Stillingen er organisatorisk knyttet til  Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap . Arbeidssted er for tiden Campus Grimstad. Tiltredelse etter avtale med fakultetet.
Fakultetet har fem institutter: Institutt for ernæring og folkehelse, Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap, Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, Institutt for psykososial helse og Institutt for psykologi.
Stillingen vil være knyttet til Centre for Personalized Digital Health Promotion,  DigiVita , et Senter for forskningsdrevet innovasjon (SFI) der Universitetet i Agder, ved Senter for e-helse, er partner. DigiVita er finansiert av Norges forskningsråd og ledes av Nasjonalt senter for e-helseforskning (NSE) og SINTEF.
Stipendiaten vil være tilknyttet  Senter for e-helse ved UiA. Det er utviklet en tematisk innramming (betenkning) for doktorgradsprosjektet som kan fås ved henvendelse til Elin Thygesen,  [email protected] .
Arbeidsoppgaver
DigiVita er organisert i flere forskningsområder hvor denne doktorgradsstillingen inngår i temaområdet Brukermedvirkning, inkludering og tilgjengelighet.  Doktorgradsprosjektet skal bidra med ny kunnskap om hvordan digitale løsninger for helsefremming kan utvikles, implementeres og tas i bruk på en måte som fremmer sosial inkludering og likeverdig tilgang til helsefremmende tjenester. Prosjektet må ha en praksisnær og deltakende forskningstilnærming med stor grad av brukerinvolvering.
Doktorgradsstipendiaten skal gjennomføre et doktorgradsprosjekt som tar utgangspunkt i den tematiske innrammingen (betenkningen) for prosjektet. Søkere bes derfor å skrive frem et forslag til prosjektplan basert på innrammingen for stillingen og som svarer til formålet med doktorgradsprosjektet. Doktorgradsstipendiaten vil i samarbeid med veilederteamet utarbeide en endelig prosjektplan ved prosjektstart.
Det er en forutsetning for tiltredelse at stipendiaten tas opp på  UiAs ph.d.-program ved Fakultet for Helse- og idrettsvitenskap med  spesialisering i helse- og sykepleievitenskap

Relevant mastergrad innen helse- sosialfag, eller andre fagområder som er relevante for arbeidsoppgavene i prosjektet, for eksempel: Andre helserelaterte utdanninger

About the Project
PhD Position: Control Capacity of Active Matter Using Activity Landscapes
The Molecular Nanophotonics Group at Leipzig University, led by Prof. Dr. Frank Cichos, invites applications for a doctoral researcher position in a joint ISF-DFG project with the group of Prof. Dr. Yael Roichman at Tel Aviv University. Our group pioneered “photon nudging”, the feedback control of light-driven microswimmers, and has since combined it with reinforcement learning, physical reservoir computing and programmable hydrodynamics.
Start Date: January 1, 2027 (or earliest possible date)
Research Focus: How many collective degrees of freedom of an active system can we actually control, and at what energetic cost? You will help to build a quantitative framework for controlling active matter with light, bridging stochastic thermodynamics and control theory. The project combines:
Self-thermophoretic Janus microswimmers driven by dynamic laser landscapes (Cichos group, Leipzig)
Light-powered bristle robots on a programmable LED arena (Roichman group, Tel Aviv University)
A shared theoretical framework built on fundamental thermodynamic limits

Comparing microswimmers with robots will reveal which limits of control are universal, from single particles to swarms, with applications from microswimmer transport to energy-efficient swarm robotics.
What You Will Do
Design and run experiments with light-driven Janus microswimmers, shaping activity landscapes in real time with a spatial light modulator
Fabricate microfluidic chips and measure the energy that drives the particles
Track hundreds of interacting particles with machine-learning methods and test fundamental thermodynamic bounds on control
Work closely with the Tel Aviv team through monthly joint meetings
Present findings at international conferences and co-author publications in high-impact journals

Qualifications
Master's degree in Physics or Physical Chemistry with excellent academic standing
Solid background in soft matter, statistical or non-equilibrium physics, and a keen interest in connecting experiment with theory
Hands-on experience in optics, video microscopy, particle tracking and/or microfluidics
Programming experience for data analysis and experiment automation (Python preferred; machine-learning experience is a plus)
Excellent English and enjoyment of interdisciplinary teamwork

What We Offer
State-of-the-art laser and microscopy setups for real-time, light-driven control of active particles
Research stays in the Roichman lab in Tel Aviv and a binational team working on shared protocols and joint publications
The chance to help shape a new research direction at the interface of active matter, stochastic thermodynamics and control
Support for international conference travel
Professional development opportunities including teaching experience and transferable skills training
Vibrant research community in a culturally rich and affordable European city

Application Process
Please submit the following documents and information to [email protected]   by 16 November 2026:
Cover letter (max. 1 page) outlining your interest in the project, relevant skills and career goals
CV/resume including any publications or conference presentations
Academic transcripts (bachelor’s and master’s degrees)
Names and contact information of at least two academic references

About Leipzig University
Founded in 1409, Leipzig University is one of Germany's leading research institutions with a strong international focus.
For more information about our research:  https://www.uni-leipzig.de/~mona Partner group in Tel Aviv:   https://www.roichmanlab.sites.tau.ac.il/
We are committed to increasing diversity in STEM and strongly encourage applications from qualified candidates of all backgrounds.

Research and Teaching Assistant
The newly established Chair of Global Security, held by Prof. Annette Idler, is part of the Department of Humanities, Social and Political Sciences (D-GESS) at ETH Zurich. The Chair examines global security, especially in relation to armed conflicts, the global illicit economy, transitions from war to peace, and the interconnections between local conflict dynamics and global shifts in order and power. Its mixed-methods research programme integrates macro-level theory with detailed, contextualised fieldwork across world regions, combines qualitative, quantitative, and computational approaches, and bridges the social sciences with complexity science and other disciplines. The Chair’s international research group engages closely with international organisations, governments, and civil society. From 2029, Prof. Idler will additionally assume the Directorship of the Center for Security Studies (CSS) at ETH Zurich.

The Chair holder, Prof. Annette Idler, is seeking to appoint, as soon as possible or by agreement, a research and teaching assistant (100%).

Job description
You will prepare the Chair’s courses each semester, manage the online learning environment for the Chair’s courses and help with grading. You may be asked to represent the Chair on the departmental Teaching Committee. You will also support Prof. Idler with research for teaching and research projects – including literature and background research, data collection and management, editorial support and preparing presentations – and maintain the Chair’s teaching records.

Profile

You hold a Master’s degree in Political Science, International Relations or a related discipline, with specialist knowledge of international politics and global security, and are familiar with the relevant research institutes and publication outlets. You have an excellent command of written and spoken English; knowledge of German is an advantage. Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research methods, a high degree of independence and very good IT skills round off your profile.

This position is an ideal entry point after completing a university degree and is fixed-term for about two years. You can look forward to varied and challenging work in a stimulating and motivating environment at a world-leading university. You will work closely with Prof. Idler, gain insight into teaching and research at a newly established chair at ETH Zurich and engage with a wide range of global security issues. There is also scope to develop a small independent research project of your own, for example towards a PhD proposal.

We offer

Ihr Beruf mit Wirkung: Werden Sie Teil der ETH Zürich, die nicht nur Ihre berufliche Entwicklung unterstützt, sondern auch aktiv zu positiven Veränderungen in der Gesellschaft beiträgt

Es erwarten Sie zahlreiche Vergünstigungen , wie z.B. ÖV-Abonnemente und Car Sharing, ein breites Sportangebot des ASVZ , Kinderbetreuung sowie attraktive Vorsorgeleistungen

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability

ap:254196.body:
À propos de nous
L’Ecole nationale supérieure des Mines de Paris (MINES Paris) est une des plus prestigieuses écoles d’ingénieurs en France et la première école par son volume de recherche orientée vers l’industrie. L’école des Mines de Paris forme des ingénieurs généralistes via une expérience pédagogique innovante et pluridisciplinaire, dans laquelle sciences de l’ingénieur et sciences humaines et sociales sont étroitement liées. Cette double culture est renforcée encore par son appartenance à l’Université PSL, qui se positionne dans le top 50 des classements internationaux, et qui constitue une véritable opportunité d’enrichissement des parcours.
Mines Paris est un établissement public à caractère scientifique, culturel et professionnel (EPSCP), placé sous la tutelle du ministère de l’économie, des finances et de la souveraineté industrielle et numérique.

Mission
Votre environnement : Les plateformes autonomes, et notamment les drones, s'appuient sur des informations provenant de systèmes GNSS, de centrales inertielles et de différents capteurs de navigation et de dynamique. Dans un environnement électromagnétique perturbé, ces informations peuvent être dégradées ou perdre leur cohérence. Les conséquences peuvent se propager à la chaîne de navigation et de commande et se traduire par des modifications du comportement dynamique de la plateforme.
Le projet vise à développer une nouvelle génération de systèmes embarqués autonomes capables de maintenir leur intégrité fonctionnelle dans des environnements perturbés (leurrage, brouillage, GNSS-denied). Le moteur AKHEROS repose sur des réseaux bayésiens dynamiques non-stationnaires (NS-DBN) embarqués, capables de détecter en temps réel les incongruités comportementales du système de navigation avec une empreinte mémoire ultra-réduite (~150 Ko), déployés sur hardware souverain. L'enjeu du post-doctorat est d'exploiter ces modifications comportementales pour détecter et caractériser en temps réel les anomalies affectant un système autonome, sans nécessairement disposer d'un modèle précis de l'ensemble des perturbations. Le poste, hébergé à Mines Paris – ITN et conduit en lien étroit avec AKHEROS, se situe à la charnière entre cette IA embarquée de détection et la commande de la plateforme : fermer la boucle perception → décision → actionnement, en couplant la détection d'anomalies aux asservissements qui assurent le maintien de trajectoire en conditions dégradées.
Votre challenge et vos missions :
·     Concevoir et valider le couplage détection ↔ asservissement : intégration du signal de détection dans les boucles de commande des actionneurs.
·     De la modélisation à la validation expérimentale : modélisation → génération de scénarios perturbés → apprentissage du comportement nominal → détection d'anomalies → caractérisation → réduction/optimisation du modèle → validation expérimentale.
·     Les méthodes seront d'abord évaluées sur des données simulées et des bancs instrumentés, puis confrontées à des données expérimentales issues de plateformes drones.
·     Développer les logiques de repli et de reconfiguration de navigation en environnement GNSS-denied.
·     Participer aux livrables scientifiques et à la stratégie de propriété intellectuelle (dépôt de brevet).
·     Les résultats pourront donner lieu à des publications dans des conférences et revues internationales en automatique, robotique et IA.

Profil
Parlons de vous !...
Doctorat en robotique, automatique / systèmes embarqués, ou IA embarquée (soutenu ou en cours de soutenance).
Pour ce poste, les principales compétences recherchées sont :
Savoirs et savoir-faire :
• Maîtrise de l'IA embarquée / edge AI ; une familiarité avec les modèles probabilistes ou bayésiens constitue un atout déterminant.
• Compétences en asservissement et commande d'actionneurs en robotique mobile ou aérienne.
• Programmation embarquée temps réel (C / C++) ; maîtrise de Python, notions de HDL / FPGA, développement pour RTOS appréciées.
• Intérêt marqué pour les drones / UAV, la navigation inertielle et le GNSS.
• Autonomie, goût de l'expérimentation matérielle, aptitude au travail en consortium.
• Une expérience en IA embarquée, systèmes temps réel ou réduction/optimisation de modèles d'apprentissage sera particulièrement appréciée.
Savoir-être :
• Pratique du travail en équipe
• Esprit collaboratif
…Et de nous ! Travailler à Mines Paris, c’est aussi :
·       Rejoindre une institution prestigieuse et chargée d’histoire
·       Être acteur de la transition numérique et de la transition vers la neutralité carbone pour faire face à l’urgence climatique
·       Appartenir à un établissement de l’Université PSL, 33ème au classement mondial de Shanghai
Mines Paris - PSL s’engage à soutenir et promouvoir l’égalité, la diversité et l’inclusion via un processus de recrutement ouvert et transparent.
Mines Paris - PSL s'engage également dans l'insertion professionnelle et au développement de carrière des personnes en situation de handicap.

The IB is currently seeking an experienced individual to take on the role of Deputy Examiner Responsible (DER)  for its Basque A: Literature  course.
The International Baccalaureate® (IB) is a non-profit educational foundation offering four programmes of international education that develop the intellectual, personal, emotional and social skills needed to live, learn and work in a rapidly globalizing world. We strive to develop students who will build a better world through intercultural understanding and respect.
One of the characteristics of the IB's Diploma Programme is that students are required to study, as one of six subjects that constitute the diploma, one of three ‘Language A’ courses, each designed to develop high social, aesthetic and cultural literacy, as well as communication skills. The language A: literature course introduces students to the analysis of literary texts. It is the course through which the IB’s policy of mother-tongue entitlement is delivered. The course is automatically available in 55 languages and available by special request and may be studied in any language with a sufficiently developed written literature.
The duties of DER include the setting and marking of examinations and determining final grades of students.
Outline information about this role, as well as the application form and recruitment policy can be found at:  IB Deputy Examiner Responsible - International Baccalaureate®
Please note that this position is part-time, involves no relocation, and is usually undertaken in addition to existing work commitments.
You must:
have a degree or equivalent in the subject (or a related subject) for which you are applying,
have a minimum of one year’s experience teaching the subject (or a related subject) for which they are applying to students of: 16 to 18 years of age (DP)

be native speaker/fluent in English and Kurdish in order to write reports and mark students’ written and spoken responses.

ap:254216.body:
Do you want to help create the next generation of sustainable 3D products from pulp fibres? In this Doctoral project, you will combine materials science, mechanics and multiscale characterisation to establish predictive design rules for transforming fibres into advanced products. You will contribute to research with the potential to replace fossil-based plastics with sustainable alternatives.
About us
The Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering pushes the knowledge of chemistry and chemical engineering forward in a broad field of research and education. We offer an international environment, with scientific areas ranging from fundamental chemistry, health and medical technology, materials science, renewable energy, to chemical engineering processing, material recycling, nuclear chemistry, theory and modelling.
The Division of Applied Chemistry
We primarily focus on applied research, that is, research aimed at addressing societal challenges and that is ready for implementation either immediately or in the near future. Examples of application areas include fossil-free fuels and energy systems, electronic devices, health and technology, the utilisation of fibres and forest-based materials, and various forms of catalysis.
About the research project
Can pulp fibres be engineered into complex 3D products that rival conventional plastics?
This Doctoral project aims to transform fibre-based manufacturing from trial-and-error development to predictive design. You will combine experiments, mechanical analysis and multiscale material characterisation to uncover how fibre properties govern deformability, damage, spring-back and shape retention in 3D forming processes.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (120 credits) or an equivalent degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Fibre and Polymer Technology, Wood Technology, Engineering Physics, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology or a related field.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
Documented experience from experimental research, thesis work, or industrial projects related to materials, mechanics, manufacturing, polymers, fibre-based materials, or modelling.
Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex experimental data
Ability to collaborate effectively and communicate clearly in multidisciplinary and international environments.

The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience with fibre-based materials, polymers, paper, packaging, or other sustainable material systems.
Experience in experimental materials characterisation, mechanical testing, microscopy, image analysis, or related analytical techniques.
Experience with data analysis, modelling, finite element methods, or programming (e.g. Python, MATLAB, or similar tools).
Experience working in interdisciplinary teams and communicating scientific results in written reports or presentations.

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Chalmers graduate education system and actively participate in the research environment of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a Vinnova Competence Centre bringing together academia and industry.
Conduct research aimed at understanding how fibre properties, material structure and processing conditions influence the formability of lignocellulosic materials into complex three-dimensional products. You will combine experimental studies, multiscale characterisation and data analysis to develop predictive design principles for fibre-based manufacturing.
Develop your own scientific ideas and communicate research results through publications in international journals, presentations at conferences, and interactions with industrial partners.
Collaborate with researchers from Chalmers, KTH and industrial partners within FibRe, contributing to the development of sustainable alternatives to fossil-based plastics.
The position generally includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or other departmental duties corresponding to up to 20% of full-time employment.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
The successful candidate will be employed by Chalmers University of Technology and enrolled in the doctoral education programme upon admission.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.
The doctoral student will be part of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a VINNOVA Competence Centre involving close collaboration with academic and industrial partners and Area of Advance Production .

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  November 20
For questions, please contact:
Prof. Anette Larsson
[email protected]
We look forward to your application!
*** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position.  ***
Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society.
Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.
Chalmers University of Technology conducts research and education in engineering sciences, architecture, mathematical sciences, natural and nautical sciences, working in close collaboration with industry and society. The strategy for scientific excellence focuses on our eight Areas of Advance; Built Environment, Energy, Information & Communication Technology, Life Science, Materials Science, Nanoscience & Nanotechnology, Production and Transport. The aim is to make an active contribution to a sustainable future using the basic sciences as a foundation and innovation and entrepreneurship as the central driving forces. Chalmers has around 11,000 students and 3,000 employees. New knowledge and improved technology have characterised Chalmers since its foundation in 1829, completely in accordance with the will of William Chalmers and his motto: Avancez!

ap:254218.body:
Referensnummer ORU 2.1.1-06037/2026
Örebro universitet söker en doktorand till utbildning på forskarnivå till doktorsexamen i psykologi vid Institutionen för beteende-, social och rättsvetenskap med preliminär utbildningsstart i januari 2027.
Projektbeskrivning
Ämnet psykologi vid Örebro universitet ingår tillsammans med kriminologi, socialt arbete och rättsvetenskap i Institutionen för beteende-, social- och rättsvetenskap (BSR). Vid BSR finns en unik kombination av huvudområden i form av psykologi, kriminologi, socialt arbete och rättsvetenskap som möjliggör samarbeten över ämnesgränserna, möten och utbyte av kompetens samt goda möjligheter för tvärvetenskapliga forskningsprojekt. Vid BSR erbjuds fristående kurser och utbildningsprogram på grund-, avancerad och forskarutbildningsnivå.
Forskningen i psykologi vid Örebro universitet fokuserar främst på utvecklingspsykologi (till exempel barn och ungdomars levnadsförhållanden, samt åldrande och kognition) och klinisk psykologi/hälsopsykologi (till exempel psykologisk prevention och behandling, långvarig smärta och andra kroniska hälsotillstånd, sömn).
Vi söker en doktorand med nyfikenhet och intresse för psykologi med inriktning mot klinisk psykologi. Som doktorand kommer du att vara en central del i ett forskningsprojekt inom enheten för psykologi med fokus på ilskerelaterad problematik och känsloreglering. Projektets övergripande mål är att identifiera fysiologiska och psykologiska mekanismer samt vidareutveckla känsloregleringsfokuserade behandlingar för detta problemområde. Projektet finansieras av Vetenskapsrådet och leds av professor Hugo Hesser. Projektet sker inom ramen för ett större forskningssamarbete mellan Karolinska Institutet, Stanford University (USA) och Örebro universitet.
Du kommer att arbeta i en mångsidig och tvärvetenskaplig forskningsmiljö där experimentell psykologi, hälsopsykologi och klinisk psykologi förenas. Doktorandprojektet inbegriper forskning gällande kopplingen mellan känsloreglering och problematisk ilska samt om, och hur, riktad träning i att reglera känslor kan minska ilskerelaterad problematik, i synnerhet undantryckt ilska. Metoder som kommer att användas inkluderar experimentella laborationsstudier, survey-/enkätstudier samt kliniska behandlingsstudier.
Dina huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter kommer att innefatta att under handledning, och i samarbete med övriga forskare i projektet, planera studier, rekrytera studiedeltagare och analysera data. Du förväntas även aktivt bidra till spridningen av forskningsresultat via vetenskapliga publikationer och muntliga presentationer på svenska och engelska.
Utbildningen och anställningen
Forskarutbildningen består av kurser och ett självständigt forskningsarbete som du presenterar i en doktorsavhandling. Utbildningen avses avslutas med doktorsexamen. Utbildningen omfattar 240 högskolepoäng, vilket motsvarar fyra års studier på heltid. I anställningen kan det komma att ingå undervisning, administration och annan forskning än det egna avhandlingsarbetet med högst 20 procent av heltid. Tillägg till utbildningstid och finansiering med motsvarande tid kommer i sådant fall att göras.
Vår ambition är att din utbildning på forskarnivå ska vara stimulerande och kännas meningsfull från början och ända fram till din doktorsexamen. Att du som doktorand får en bra introduktion underlättar starten på dina studier och ger dig en god grund att bygga din forskarutbildning på. Som doktorand vid Örebro universitet erbjuds du en särskilt anpassad seminarieserie med allt från utbildningsregler och karriär till stöd i din studiesituation och doktorandmingel.
Till utbildningsplatsen är knuten en doktorandanställning på heltid under utbildningstiden. I regelhandboken kan du läsa mer om doktorandanställning samt om studier och anställning på deltid. Ingångslönen för doktorandanställning är för närvarande 32 300 kr per månad. Lönerevision pågår och nya doktorandlöner kommer att fastställas från 1 oktober 2026.
Behörighet och urval
För att bli antagen till utbildning på forskarnivå krävs att den sökande har grundläggande behörighet och särskild behörighet samt bedöms ha sådan förmåga som i övrigt behövs för att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen. De fullständiga behörighetskraven finns i antagningsordningen samt i bilaga 2 till den allmänna studieplanen i psykologi .
Grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå har den som har:
avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå,
fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå, eller
på något annat sätt inom eller utom landet förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.

Särskild behörighet för att bli antagen till utbildning på forskarnivå i ämnet har den som i sin högskoleutbildning har godkänt betyg på kurser om minst 90 högskolepoäng, inklusive självständigt arbete för kandidatexamen, i psykologi. Särskild behörighet har även den som inom eller utom landet har förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.
I övrigt sker bedömning av om sökanden har sådan förmåga som behövs för att tillgodogöra sig utbildningen skall göras utifrån sökandens utbildning och annan tidigare verksamhet samt de uppsatser och andra självständiga arbeten av vetenskaplig karaktär som sökanden har åberopat.
Specifika färdigheter och erfarenheter
Egna forskningserfarenheter inom något av psykologins delområden är meriterande, i synnerhet om forskningen bedrivits inom för projektet relevanta områden med fokus på exempelvis känsloreglering, ilska eller psykologisk behandlingsforskning. Eftersom projektet inbegriper kliniska behandlingsstudier är det särskilt meriterande om den sökande har examen som psykolog och har såväl teoretiska kunskaper som kliniska erfarenheter av psykologisk behandling, i synnerhet av kognitiv beteendeterapi och/eller emotionsfokuserad behandling. Därtill bör den sökande ha goda kunskaper i experimentell forskningsdesign och avancerad statistik. Den sökande skall ha mycket god förmåga att uttrycka sig i tal och skrift på svenska och mycket goda kunskaper i engelska är även ett krav. Därutöver värderas också förmågan att arbeta självständigt med god struktur och organisation, samt samarbetsförmågan.
Information
Ytterligare information om utbildningen och anställningen ges av professor Hugo Hesser, [email protected]

ap:254219.body:
Join our interdisciplinary team at the Methodology of Educational Science Research Group (CMPO) and the Center for Contextual Psychiatry (CCP) at KU Leuven, one of Europe’s most renowned research universities. The CMPO, part of the Faculty of Psychology and Educational Sciences, is internationally recognized for its expertise in advanced statistical modeling and research methodology, encompassing both quantitative and qualitative approaches. Prof. Ginette Lafit leads innovative work to advance quantitative methods in ESM study design and drives methodological innovation in intensive longitudinal research. The CCP, housed within the Department of Neurosciences in the School of Medicine, is an internationally leading research center specializing in Experience Sampling Methodology (ESM) in mental health research. Under the leadership of Prof. Inez Myin-Germeys, the CCP brings together a vibrant group of 25 researchers from diverse backgrounds and is widely recognized for its expertise in designing, implementing, and analyzing experimental studies and clinical trials. You will join the eMotion project, an ambitious long-term research initiative dedicated to developing new interventions for the negative symptoms of psychosis. As a PhD student, you will play a central role in developing a statistical framework for optimizing the design of Ecological Momentary Interventions (EMIs) using Micro-Randomized Trials (MRTs).

Website unit

Project

This research program uses Virtual Reality (VR) and the Experience Sampling Method (ESM) to examine the approach-avoidance mechanisms underlying amotivation, a core negative symptom of psychosis. A major advancement of the project is developing tailored interventions that combine EMIs with VR technology. As a PhD student, you will play a pivotal role in advancing statistical methodologies to optimize EMI design through MRTs, enhance EMI effectiveness by incorporating data from VR-based tasks, and develop rigorous measures to evaluate the clinical impact of the EMI-VR intervention framework.

Your Responsibilities:

Apply quantitative methods to analyze ESM data, including time series analysis and multilevel modeling techniques.

Develop novel quantitative methods to construct EMIs and advance the EMI-VR integration using MRTs.

Write papers for publication in international peer-reviewed journals.

Collaborate closely with researchers across three research lines: (i) ESM methodology, statistics, and meta-science, (ii) Person-environment interactions in psychosis, and (iii) Development, efficacy testing, and implementation of Digital Mobile Mental Health.

This position is part of eMotion, a recently funded, large-scale research program aimed at creating new treatments for negative symptoms—among the most challenging aspects of psychiatric care. You will join a dynamic, interdisciplinary team of clinical psychologists, experimental psychologists, psychiatrists, and statisticians in an environment that fosters collaboration and scientific excellence.

Profile

The candidate holds a master’s degree in psychology or a related discipline (e.g., Mental Health, Psychiatry, Social or Health Sciences) and has demonstrated a strong interest in research. Solid experience with quantitative research methods and strong statistical skills are essential. Prior experience with, or knowledge of, the Experience Sampling Method is highly desirable. The candidate should be committed to open‑science practices and possess excellent written and spoken English skills (C1 proficiency level).

Offer

A contract for one year will be offered, which is renewable for another three years after a positive evaluation. Salaries for PhD students are competitive by international standards. The starting date is flexible, but no later than the first of March 2027.

Interested?

For this application, the following information will be considered:

Cover Letter (describing your motivation, research career goals, skills, and experience)

CV

Diploma and transcripts of records (BSc and MSc)

Contact details of at least two reference persons

Other information for consideration (e.g., a list of publications if applicable)

Please use the university’s job portal when applying for this position.

For more information, please contact prof. Ginette Lafit ( [email protected] ).

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

ap:254220.body:
The University of Oulu is a multidisciplinary, international research university, with about 4000 employees who produce new knowledge based on high-standards research and provide research based education to build a more sustainable, smarter, and more humane world. The University of Oulu community has about 19,000 people in total. Our northern scientific community operates globally and creates conditions for the emergence of innovations. The University of Oulu is ranked in the top 3% of the world’s universities. All our research, education, and community activities are guided by our university’s values and ethical principles.
We are currently looking for a
Doctoral Researcher in Educational Technology
to join research projects focusing on Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI), teacher education, and teachers’ professional development at the Faculty of Education and Psychology at the University of Oulu, Finland.
The position is connected to two research projects: INTEGRATE – Training Teachers to Integrate EU Matters through GenAI-Supported Pedagogy and The Power of Teachers' Online Mentorship for AI Partnership (Power T/A) .
The INTEGRATE project, funded by the Erasmus+ Programme under the Jean Monnet Teacher Training action, aims to empower pre-service and in-service teachers to integrate EU topics and values into everyday teaching through GenAI-supported pedagogy. The project develops and implements teacher education courses, online professional development modules, instructional materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities.
The Power T/A project, funded by the Research Council of Finland, explores the integration of AI-based technologies into teacher mentorship and instructional activities. The project focuses on how AI technologies can support teachers’ professional development, particularly through online mentorship, and how teachers can develop the knowledge and skills needed for meaningful AI integration in education.
About the job
As a doctoral researcher, you will:
Conduct doctoral research within the INTEGRATE (75%) and Power T/A (25%) projects, with a focus on GenAI, teacher education, and teachers’ professional learning.
Contribute to the development, implementation, and evaluation of GenAI-supported teacher education and professional development activities .
Participate in the development and implementation of courses, online professional development modules, case-based learning materials, and GenAI-supported teaching activities for teachers.
Collect and analyse qualitative and quantitative research data related to the implementation and evaluation of project activities.
Contribute to scientific publications and other research outputs arising from the projects. Collaborate with teachers, teacher educators, researchers, and national and international project partners.
Present research findings at scientific conferences and contribute to the dissemination of project results.

In this role, you will become part of a dynamic and supportive research environment focusing on educational technology, teacher education, and the pedagogically meaningful and responsible use of artificial intelligence.
Qualifications
To succeed in the position, we expect from you:
A Master’s degree in education, educational technology, educational psychology, or another relevant discipline.
A strong interest in research on Generative AI, educational technology, teacher education, and EU matters and values.
Proficiency in qualitative and/or quantitative research methods and the ability to apply these methods in educational research.
Good IT and data analysis skills and an interest in using digital and AI-based tools in educational research.
Fluent written and spoken English. Ability to work both independently and collaboratively in multidisciplinary and international research environments.
Please see also the requirements of the University of Oulu Gradduate school

Additional merits considered an advantage
Familiarity with the Finnish K–12 education system and/or teacher education . Experience working with pre-service or in-service teachers .
Experience in teaching, teacher education, professional development, or instructional design . Experience or demonstrated interest in AI/GenAI-supported teaching and learning .
Experience with qualitative and/or quantitative research data collection and analysis. Familiarity with technology-enhanced learning environments.
Finnish language skills (not required but considered as an advantage).

What we offer?
The support of an experienced and enthusiastic project team of  where you can share your expertise and grow as an expert.
Wellness benefit ePassi covering sport, culture and well-being. Read more about other staff benefits.
Development and career options of the big organization.
Work that matters and a workplace that promotes flexibility and work-life balance. Read more about working with us .
Our  Buddy Programme and  Spouse Network support you and close-ones in settling into Oulu.
We have a HR Excellence in Research -quality label which is a recognition awarded by the European Commission for the development of researchers’ working conditions and careers.
Finland is one of the most livable countries in the world, with a high quality of life, safety, excellent education system, and competitive economy. Read more about living in Oulu .

Salary
The position is fixed-term for three years as soon as possible or starting from January 2027.
The salary will be based on the levels 2-4 of the demand level chart for teaching and research staff of Finnish universities. In addition, a salary component based on personal work performance will be paid (maximum of 50% of the job-specific component). Starting gross salary will be approx. 2300-2600 € per month (before taxes). A trial period of 6 months is applied in the position.
How to apply?
Interested? If yes, please apply by 15.11.2026 (23:59 Finnish local time) through our recruitment system.
The application should be written in English and include the following:
Cover letter
CV following the guidelines of the Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity
Certificates/Diplomas
Contact information of two persons available for recommendation

The eligible applicants fitting best in the profile expected for the position will be invited to an on-site or remote interview. All applicants will be notified during the selection process. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, such as people of different ages, genders and lingual, cultural or minority groups.
Contact Information
If you have any further questions, please contact D r. Ismail Celik, Faculty of Education and Psychology, [email protected] , +358 503284505

Description de l'offre d'emploi
Venez rejoindre l'IMT Mines Alès, grande école de prestige qui se classe parmi les meilleures écoles d’ingénieurs sur le plan national et mondial et implantée à Alès, ville à taille humaine, capitale des Cévennes où la qualité de vie est fortement appréciée par ses habitants.
Créée en 1843, IMT Mines Alès compte à ce jour 1400 élèves (dont 250 étrangers) et 380 personnels. L’école dispose de 3 centres de recherche et d’enseignement de haut niveau scientifique et technologique, qui œuvrent dans les domaines des matériaux et du génie civil (C2MA), de l’environnement et des risques (CREER), de l’intelligence artificielle et du génie industriel et numérique (CERIS). Elle dispose de 12 plateformes technologiques et compte 1600 entreprises partenaires. Pour en savoir plus : https://www.imt-mines-ales.fr
Vous êtes rattaché(e) au Centre de Recherche et d’Enseignement en Environnement et Risques (CREER) de l'IMT Mines Alès et dans l'unité de recherche : HSM.
Ce travail s’inscrit dans le cadre du projet AMI CMA 3MRBAT qui porte sur l’évaluation environnementale de différents scénarios du cycle de vie des batteries lithium-ion, avec pour objectif de mieux comprendre les principaux « hot spot » des batteries.
Vos missions :
Vous vous appuierez sur l’expertise des partenaires de 3MRBAT, et sur les données techniques des principaux projets industriels qui sont en débat Public au niveau de la France et sur la littérature scientifique existante. Un soin particulier sera apporté au niveau de l’impact sur les ressources en eau, l’ensemble des activités de cette filière nécessitant de grands volumes d’eau.
Vous contribuerez au développement des enseignements d'IMT Mines Alès dans le cadre du Mastère Spécialisé PRINEC.
Vous participerez à la conception et à la mise en place d'un module de formation interactif sur le cycle de vie des batteries, afin de mettre en évidence l’influence des différents scénarios d’approvisionnement, de fabrication, d’utilisation et de fin de vie sur les impacts environnementaux. Vous préparerez les supports pédagogiques et assurerez les enseignements associés.
Vous participerez à la valorisation scientifique des travaux réalisés dans le cadre du projet.

ap:254224.body:
Do you want to contribute to better health for all?
To be a doctoral student means to devote oneself to a research project under supervision of experienced researchers and following an individual study plan. For a doctoral degree, the equivalent of four years of full-time doctoral education is required.
The research group
The doctoral position is based in the Arroyo Mühr Research Group, part of the Center for Cervical Cancer Elimination at the Department of Clinical Science, Intervention and Technology (CLINTEC), Karolinska Institutet. The group is led by Associate Professor (Docent) Sara Arroyo Mühr and combines molecular biology, bioinformatics and epidemiology to investigate HPV and cancer. We use clinical samples and health registry data to understand cancer development and improve prevention and early detection. The doctoral student will work in an interdisciplinary environment with national and international collaborations.
The doctoral student project and the duties of the doctoral student
The doctoral project is part of the ERC-funded ESCAPE-HPV research programme and focuses on molecular characterisation of HPV-negative cervical cancer. Almost all cervical cancers are caused by human papillomavirus (HPV), which forms the basis for prevention through HPV vaccination and HPV-based screening. Nevertheless, HPV is not detected in a small proportion of tumours. These cancers may escape current HPV-based prevention strategies, and greater understanding of their origins and how they can be detected and prevented is therefore needed.
The aim is to investigate the biological mechanisms underlying these tumours and identify molecular characteristics that may contribute to improved diagnosis and prevention. The project combines laboratory work with analyses of genomic, transcriptomic and epigenetic data, as well as clinical and registry data.
Duties include:
Identifying relevant cancer cases in health registries, and compiling and quality-checking clinical and registry data.
Contributing to ethics applications and documentation for the use of biological samples and associated data.
Collaborating with national and international partners on access to, transfer of, and management of samples and data.
Processing biological samples, extracting DNA and RNA, and carrying out quantification and quality control.
Performing molecular analyses, including PCR, qPCR and HPV genotyping, and preparing sequencing libraries.
Conducting bioinformatic analyses of sequencing data and other molecular data.
Developing and applying reproducible scripts in R and/or Python for data processing, quality control, statistical analysis and visualisation.
Analysing and integrating molecular results with clinical and registry data.
Documenting methods and results, contributing to scientific publications and presenting research at seminars and conferences.

Both laboratory work and computational analyses are central parts of the doctoral project. The work involves samples and data from Sweden and international collaborators. The doctoral student will receive supervision and methodological training within the research group and gradually develop independence in planning, conducting and interpreting the research.
What do we offer?
A creative and inspiring environment full of expertise and curiosity. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is a state university, which entitles to several benefits such as extended holiday and generous occupational pension. Employees also have access to our modern gym for free and receive reimbursements for medical care.
Eligibility requirements for doctoral education
In order to participate in the selection for a doctoral position, you must meet the following general (A) and specific (B) eligibility requirements at latest by the application deadline.
It is your responsibility to certify eligibility by following the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education.
A) General eligibility requirement
You meet the general eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you:

have been awarded a second-cycle/advanced/master qualification (i.e. master degree) or have satisfied the requirements for courses comprising at least 240 credits of which at least 60 credits were awarded in the advanced/second-cycle/master level, or have acquired substantially equivalent knowledge in some other way in Sweden or abroad.*
Follow the instructions on the web page Entry requirements (eligibility) for doctoral education.
*If you claim equivalent knowledge, follow the instructions on the web page Assessing equivalent knowledge for general eligibility for doctoral education.
B) Specific eligibility requirement

You meet the specific eligibility requirement for doctoral/third-cycle/PhD education if you:
- Show proficiency in English equivalent to the course English B/English 6 at Swedish upper secondary school.
Follow the instructions on the web page English language requirements for doctoral education.
Verification of your documents
Karolinska Institutet checks the authenticity of your documents. Karolinska Institutet reserves the right to revoke admission if supporting documents are discovered to be fraudulent. Submission of false documents is a violation of Swedish law and is considered grounds for legal action.
Skills and personal qualities
We are looking for a motivated and curious candidate with a strong interest in cancer research who enjoys combining laboratory work and bioinformatics. You collaborate well, communicate clearly and contribute actively to the research group. You take initiative, think creatively and are open to trying new approaches to solve scientific and practical problems. You can prioritise tasks and work efficiently in a fast-paced research environment while maintaining accuracy and quality. You can plan and organise your work, take responsibility for agreed tasks and move them forward with increasing independence. When problems arise, you investigate potential causes, propose solutions and seek support when needed.
Requirements
Relevant educational background in molecular biology, biomedicine, biotechnology, bioinformatics, or a related field.
Practical experience in molecular biology laboratory work, including accurate pipetting and handling of DNA and/or RNA samples.
Basic experience with sequencing-based methods and bioinformatic analysis of biological data.
Good oral and written communication skills in English.

Meritorious qualifications
Experience in DNA/RNA extraction, PCR, qPCR, and nucleic acid quality control.
Experience in sequencing library preparation or working with next-generation sequencing (NGS) platforms.
Experience in the analysis of genomic, transcriptomic, or epigenetic data.
Experience in programming and data analysis using R and/or Python.
Knowledge of cancer biology, virology, or HPV-related research.
Experience working with tumour samples, FFPE material, or health registries.
Experience in scientific research and presentation of research findings.
Co-authorship of scientific publications relevant to the project's research area.
Experience presenting research findings through oral or poster presentations at scientific conferences.

Terms and conditions
The doctoral student will be employed on a doctoral studentship maximum 4 years full-time.
Location: Flemingsberg
Application process
Submit your application and supporting documents through the Varbi recruitment system. Use the button in the top right corner and follow the instructions.
Your application should contain the following documents. We prefer that your application is written in English, but you can also apply in Swedish:
- A personal letter and a curriculum vitae
- Degree projects and previous publications, if any
- Any other documentation showing the desirable skills and personal qualities described above
- Documents certifying your general eligibility (see A above)
- Documents certifying your specific eligibility (see B above)
Selection
A selection will be made among eligible applicants on the basis of the ability to benefit from doctoral education. The qualifications of the applicants will be evaluated on an overall basis.
Karolinska Institutet uses the following bases of assessment:
- Documented subject knowledge of relevance to the area of research
- Analytical skill
- Other documented knowledge or experience that may be relevant to doctoral studies in the subject.
All applicants will be informed when the recruitment is completed.

ap:254225.body:
Vill du bidra till en bättre hälsa för alla?
Att vara doktorand innebär att vara antagen till en utbildning på forskarnivå (forskarutbildning) där man följer en individuell studieplan. En doktorand ägnar sig åt ett forskningsprojekt under handledning, kompletterat med kurser och andra lärandeaktiviteter. För en doktorsexamen krävs motsvarande fyra års utbildning på forskarnivå på heltid.
Forskargruppen
Doktorandtjänsten är placerad i forskargruppen Arroyo Mühr, som är en del av Centrum för eliminering av livmoderhalscancer vid institutionen för klinisk vetenskap, intervention och teknik (CLINTEC), Karolinska Institutet. Gruppen leds av docent Sara Arroyo Mühr och kombinerar molekylärbiologi, bioinformatik och epidemiologi för att studera HPV och cancer. Vi arbetar med kliniska prover och data från hälsoregister för att förstå cancerutveckling och förbättra prevention och tidig upptäckt. Doktoranden kommer att arbeta i en tvärvetenskaplig miljö med nationella och internationella samarbeten.
Doktorandprojektet och doktorandens uppgifter
Doktorandprojektet ingår i det ERC-finansierade forskningsprogrammet ESCAPE-HPV och fokuserar på molekylär karakterisering av HPV-negativ livmoderhalscancer. Nästan all livmoderhalscancer orsakas av humant papillomvirus (HPV), vilket ligger till grund för prevention genom HPV-vaccination och HPV-baserad screening. Trots detta påvisas inte HPV i en mindre andel av tumörerna. Dessa cancerfall kan undgå dagens HPV-baserade preventionsstrategier, och det behövs därför ökad kunskap om hur de uppstår och hur de kan upptäckas och förebyggas.
Målet är att undersöka de biologiska mekanismerna bakom dessa tumörer och identifiera molekylära kännetecken som kan bidra till förbättrad diagnostik och prevention. Projektet kombinerar laboratoriearbete med analys av genomiska, transkriptomiska och epigenetiska data samt kliniska data och registerdata.
Arbetsuppgifterna omfattar:
Identifiera relevanta cancerfall i hälsoregister samt sammanställa och kvalitetskontrollera kliniska data och registerdata.
Medverka i utarbetandet av etikansökningar och dokumentation för användning av biologiska prover och tillhörande data.
Samarbeta med nationella och internationella partners kring tillgång till, överföring och hantering av prover och data.
Bearbeta biologiska prover, extrahera DNA och RNA samt utföra kvantifiering och kvalitetskontroll.
Utföra molekylärbiologiska analyser, inklusive PCR, qPCR och HPV-genotypning, samt förbereda sekvenseringsbibliotek.
Genomföra bioinformatiska analyser av sekvenseringsdata och andra molekylära data.
Utveckla och tillämpa reproducerbara skript i R och/eller Python för databearbetning, kvalitetskontroll, statistisk analys och visualisering.
Analysera och integrera molekylära resultat med kliniska data och registerdata.
Dokumentera metoder och resultat, bidra till vetenskapliga publikationer och presentera arbetet vid seminarier och konferenser.

Både laboratoriearbete och datorbaserad analys är centrala delar av doktorandprojektet. Arbetet omfattar prover och data från Sverige och internationella samarbetspartners. Doktoranden får handledning och metodutbildning av forskargruppen och utvecklar successivt självständighet i att planera, genomföra och tolka forskningsarbetet.
Vad erbjuder vi?
En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. På KI får du träffa forskare med olika forskningsinriktningar som jobbar tillsammans. Det är det gränsöverskridande samarbetet som bidrar till KI:s världsledande position inom forskning. Som doktorand erbjuds du ett individuellt forskningsprojekt, en välutbildad handledare, ett stort utbud av valbara kurser och möjligheten att arbeta i en framgångsrik forskargrupp. Karolinska Institutet har samarbeten med framstående universitet över hela världen, vilket ger möjlighet till internationella utbyten. Som anställd doktorand får du en avtalsenlig lön, du får träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar och du får ersättning för läkarvård.
Behörighetskrav för utbildning på forskarnivå
För att delta i urvalet till en doktorandplats måste du styrka både det grundläggande (A) och det särskilda (B) behörighetskravet innan ansökningsperioden stänger.
Det är ditt ansvar som sökande att styrka din behörighet genom att följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå.
A) Grundläggande behörighetskrav
Du uppfyller det grundläggande behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du:
har avlagt en examen på avancerad nivå (magister- eller masterexamen), eller
har fullgjort kursfordringar om minst 240 högskolepoäng, varav minst 60 högskolepoäng på avancerad nivå,  eller
har på annat sätt förvärvat i huvudsak motsvarande kunskaper.*

Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan  Behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå .
*Om du anser dig ha motsvarande kunskaper ska du följa instruktionerna på webbsidan Bedömning av motsvarande kunskaper för grundläggande behörighet till utbildning på forskarnivå.
B) Särskilt behörighetskrav
Du uppfyller det särskilda behörighetskravet för utbildning på forskarnivå om du:
- Intygar kunskaper i engelska (motsvarande Engelska B/Engelska 6 vid gymnasiet med godkänt betyg).
Följ instruktionerna på webbsidan  English language requirements for doctoral education.
Kontroll av dokument Karolinska Institutet gör kontroll av dokumenten för att upptäcka förfalskningar. Karolinska Institutet förbehåller sig rätten att återkalla antagningsbeslut om förfalskningar eller oriktigheter påvisas. Inlämnande av falska handlingar är ett brott mot svensk lag och anses vara grund för rättsliga åtgärder.
Färdigheter och personliga egenskaper
Vi söker en engagerad och nyfiken person med ett starkt intresse för cancerforskning, som trivs med att kombinera laboratoriearbete och bioinformatik. Du har god samarbetsförmåga, kommunicerar tydligt och bidrar aktivt till gruppens arbete. Du tar initiativ, tänker kreativt och är öppen för att pröva nya angreppssätt för att lösa vetenskapliga och praktiska problem. Du kan prioritera mellan olika uppgifter och arbeta effektivt i en forskningsmiljö med högt tempo, samtidigt som du är noggrann och värnar om arbetets kvalitet. Du kan planera och organisera ditt arbete, ta ansvar för överenskomna uppgifter och driva dem framåt med successivt ökad självständighet. När problem uppstår undersöker du möjliga orsaker, föreslår lösningar och söker stöd vid behov.
Krav
Relevant utbildningsbakgrund inom molekylärbiologi, biomedicin, bioteknik, bioinformatik eller närliggande område.

Praktisk erfarenhet av molekylärbiologiskt laboratoriearbete, inklusive noggrann pipettering och hantering av DNA- och/eller RNA-prover.

Grundläggande erfarenhet av sekvenseringsbaserade metoder och bioinformatisk analys av biologiska data.

God förmåga att kommunicera muntligt och skriftligt på engelska.

Meriterande
Erfarenhet av DNA-/RNA-extraktion, PCR, qPCR och kvalitetskontroll av nukleinsyror.

Erfarenhet av beredning av sekvenseringsbibliotek eller arbete med NGS-plattformar.

Erfarenhet av analys av genomiska, transkriptomiska eller epigenetiska data.

Erfarenhet av programmering och dataanalys i R och/eller Python.

Kunskaper inom cancerbiologi, virologi eller HPV-relaterad forskning.

Erfarenhet av arbete med tumörprover, FFPE-material eller hälsoregister.

Erfarenhet av vetenskaplig forskning och presentation av forskningsresultat.

Medförfattarskap i vetenskapliga publikationer relevanta för projektets forskningsområde.

Erfarenhet av att presentera forskningsresultat muntligt eller som poster vid vetenskapliga konferenser.

Villkor
Doktorandplatsen innebär en anställning som doktorand under maximalt 4 år på heltid.

Ansökan
Du söker doktorandplatsen i rekryteringsverktyget Varbi. Använd knappen uppe till höger och följ anvisningarna. Vi ser gärna att din ansökan är skriven på engelska, men det går också bra att ansöka på svenska.
Din ansökan ska innehålla dessa dokument:
- Ett personligt brev och curriculum vitae
- Eventuella examensarbeten och publikationer
- Andra dokument som styrker de ovan efterfrågade färdigheter och egenskaper
- Dokument som styrker det grundläggande behörighetskravet (se A ovan)
- Dokument som styrker det särskilda behörighetskravet (se B ovan)
Urval
Urval bland behöriga sökande görs med hänsyn till deras förmåga att tillgodogöra sig forskarutbildning. En samlad bedömning av de sökandes meriter och lämplighet kommer att göras.
Följande bedömningsgrunder tillämpas vid Karolinska Institutet:
- Dokumenterade ämneskunskaper av betydelse för forskningsområdet
- Analytisk skicklighet
- Övriga dokumenterade kunskaper/erfarenheter som kan ha betydelse för aktuell forskarutbildning
Alla sökanden kommer att få information när rekryteringen är slutförd.

KI tillämpar en lönestege vid lönesättning av doktorander.
