About LISCO-BIOMED

The KU Leuven Institute for Single Cell Omics (LISCO) is a leading Cell Center in the world. Within LISCO, a dedicated innovation, translation and service platform in biomedicine, termed LISCO-BIOMED, brings together internationally recognised expertise in single-cell and spatial multi-omics, and integrates capabilities across single-cell sequencing, advanced imaging, bioinformatics, artificial intelligence, automation, microfluidics, molecular and cellular biology, disease modelling and clinical pathology.

This interdisciplinary environment enables us to bridge discovery science, technology development and clinical translation. We collaborate with academic, clinical and industry partners to address complex translational research questions by combining advanced technologies with methodological innovation, disease biology and scientific interpretation. Our capabilities span the workflow from sample preparation and assay development through data generation, computational analysis, biological interpretation and advanced modelling. Access to specialised pathology expertise at UZ Leuven further enables tissue context and clinically relevant interpretation to be integrated into projects.

LISCO-BIOMED has established a strong industry portfolio of more than 10 pharmaceutical and biotechnology partners, ranging from global pharma leaders to emerging biotech innovators. Leveraging its advanced multi-omics capabilities, LISCO-BIOMED supports industry R&D across the drug development pipeline, from early discovery through clinical development and lifecycle management. To further strengthen its position as a strategic scientific partner for industry, we are seeking an experienced commercial professional to lead the development and growth of LISCO-BIOMED’s industry services portfolio and associated partnerships. The role therefore combines business development, strategic account management, commercial negotiation and partnership development, with responsibility for industry relationships from first engagement through contracting and into follow-on business.

Website unit

Responsibilities

Business development and market engagement

Develop relationships and commercial opportunities across pharmaceutical, biotechnology, diagnostics, and other relevant life-science organisations, with a primary focus on pharma and biotech.

Build and manage a qualified pipeline aligned with LISCO-BIOMED’s scientific strengths and strategic priorities, and develop relationships with key scientific, business and decision-making stakeholders.

Identify market needs and emerging opportunities, represent LISCO-BIOMED at relevant partnering events and industry forums, and bring market and customer insights into portfolio and commercial strategy.

Commercial leadership and deal execution

Qualify and prioritise opportunities based on scientific fit, strategic value and commercial potential, and translate partner needs into compelling propositions together with the relevant scientific and technical experts.

Coordinate proposals and quotations based on the agreed scientific scope, project effort, cost structure and commercial framework.

Define pricing and commercial positioning within agreed margin and pricing parameters and lead commercial negotiations within the defined mandate.

Coordinate contracting with KU Leuven Research & Development (LRD) and the relevant compliance and project functions through to signature and implementation.

Building winning teams and partnerships

Build opportunity-driven multidisciplinary teams, bringing together the most relevant principal investigators, scientists, technology platforms and specialist expertise across LISCO-BIOMED, combining technological capabilities with disease biology, pathology, clinical and computational expertise to develop differentiated solutions for industry partners.

Connect LISCO-BIOMED with complementary capabilities across UZ Leuven, other KU Leuven translational platforms and the broader KU Leuven research and innovation ecosystem where this strengthens the proposition.

Coordinate the internal team during the commercial phase, bringing the right expertise into the discussion at the right stage while maintaining a clear and coherent interface towards the partner.

Work with IOF Innovation Managers, LRD and relevant scientific teams when an opportunity extends beyond standard service delivery into collaborative research, consultancy, licensing, co-development or a broader strategic partnership.

Strategic account development

Retain commercial ownership of partner relationships throughout project delivery while day-to-day execution is managed by the relevant project team.

Develop account plans, understand programmes and decision structures within key accounts, and identify opportunities to expand collaborations across programmes, therapeutic areas, research teams and business units.

Manage the commercial aspects of scope changes, additional work and follow-on opportunities, and convert successful initial engagements into repeat business and longer-term strategic relationships, including master service agreements and preferred-partner arrangements where relevant.

Commercial performance and professionalisation

Take accountability for agreed commercial objectives, including pipeline development, revenue, margin, conversion, account growth and follow-on business. In the first year, the emphasis will be on building and converting a qualified pipeline, securing initial and follow-on industry agreements, and establishing a robust commercial operating model. Revenue and margin objectives will scale as the portfolio matures

Maintain reliable pipeline, forecasting and commercial reporting, supported by disciplined use of CRM and appropriate commercial tools.

Contribute to the continued professionalisation of LISCO-BIOMED’s industry-facing activities, including clear commercial workflows, decision points and handovers across scientific, project, finance, compliance and LRD interfaces.

Reporting and key interfaces

The role reports to the LISCO-BIOMED leadership, comprising the Director and the six LISCO-BIOMED Principal Investigators. This LISCO-BIOMED leadership sets the overall strategy, scientific priorities and commercial framework; within this framework, the role has substantial autonomy and accountability for business development, strategic account management, commercial positioning, pricing within agreed parameters and commercial negotiations. Your direct line manager is Prof. Thierry Voet, Director of LISCO-BIOMED. Key interfaces include LISCO-BIOMED’s scientific teams, IOF Innovation Managers, KU Leuven Research & Development (LRD), and the relevant project management, finance, legal, compliance and communications functions. The Industry Partnerships Lead will maintain a direct interface with the LISCO-BIOMED Industrial Advisory Board, including through an annual review of commercial performance, market developments and the strategic evolution of LISCO-BIOMED’s industry-facing portfolio.

Profile

We are looking for an experienced commercial professional from the life-science sector who combines strong business-development capabilities with the scientific understanding to engage credibly with R&D organisations.

At least seven years of relevant experience in business development, strategic or key account management, or a comparable commercial role within pharma, biotech, diagnostics, CROs, scientific services or life-science technology.

A demonstrated track record of originating and developing opportunities and progressing them through commercial negotiation to signed agreements.

Experience working towards commercial targets and accountability for revenue, margin, pipeline development and account growth.

Strong commercial judgement in opportunity qualification, pricing, negotiation and account development.

A life-science background (MSc or PhD preferred) and sufficient scientific literacy to engage credibly with discovery, preclinical, translational and clinical R&D teams and to translate complex scientific capabilities into compelling propositions.

Familiarity with how pharma and biotech buy external R&D services: master service agreements, preferred-vendor onboarding and procurement cycles.

The ability to build and coordinate multidisciplinary teams and progress opportunities across organisational boundaries without relying on formal authority.

A proactive, results-oriented and collaborative working style, with excellent written and spoken English. Knowledge of Dutch is a strong asset for working across KU Leuven, UZ Leuven and LRD.

Experience in scientific services, CRO services or technology-platform business development; knowledge of single-cell and spatial (multi)omic technologies; experience with universities or academic medical centres; and an established network within the European pharmaceutical and biotechnology sector are considered strong assets.

Offer

We offer a senior and highly visible role at the interface of leading biomedical research, clinical expertise and industry. You will play a central role in shaping the further development of LISCO-BIOMED’s industry activities, with substantial autonomy and direct access to LISCO-BIOMED’s scientific leadership and the broader KU Leuven and UZ Leuven innovation ecosystem.

The position is full-time (100% FTE, a different working percentage can be discussed), based in Leuven, with an intended start date of early February 2027.

Salary category: Scientific Staff Member (BAP)

Contract type and duration: one-year fixed-term contract, with a realistic prospect of extension.

Interested?

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Thierry Voet, mail: [email protected] or Mrs. Shinjini Mukherjee, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Humanities, Education and Social Sciences (FHSE) at the University of Luxembourg brings together expertise from the humanities, linguistics, cognitive sciences, social and educational sciences.
People from across 20 disciplines are working within the Faculty . Along with the disciplinary approach a very ambitious interdisciplinary research culture has been developed. The faculty's research and teaching focuses on social, economic, political and educational issues with the common goal of contributing to an inclusive, open and resourceful society.
The doctoral student will be a member of the Institute of Teaching and Learning, within the Department of Education and Social Work. The person will be part of a dynamic organisational context of a growing, globally connected research university.
Your role
Develop a thesis in Educational sciences under the supervision of Prof. Dr. Thierry Geoffre ( https://www.uni.lu/fhse-en/people/thierry-geoffre/ ) on topics related to the languages of literacy in the Luxembourgish primary school context (mostly French, German) and grammatical error correction (GEC) systems. GEC has emerged as a cornerstone of AI-supported language learning, offering automated feedback previously available only through human instruction. GEC systems are designed to automatically detect and correct grammatical, syntactic, and lexical errors in learners' writing (Yuan, 2017). For multilingual and non-native speakers, this real-time, personalised feedback can significantly accelerate language development by supporting independent learning and revision. Given the highly multilingual context in Luxembourg, and the ambition of inclusive school, proposing a GEC system to K-12 students, especially primary school students, in languages of literacy would be an innovation of high interest
Collaborate actively with an interdisciplinary PhD committee composed of Computer scientists and linguists
Produce high‑quality research articles together with researchers involved in the project
Assist the supervisor with day‑to‑day management, the organisation of research activities and the preparation of learning data
Contribute to teaching and mentoring Bachelor students

Your profile
Master's degree in educational sciences or computer science, with a focus on inclusive, multilingual education. Experience in at least one of the following areas is required
Interest in inclusive language education and K-12 education issues and ambition to advance one of the aforementioned subject areas
The possibility of a joint supervision arrangement between Education and Computer Science could be explored
Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English and good working knowledge of French is required

Academic Eligibility (Thesis) :
Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover letter presenting your motivation for this doctoral thesis topic, and explaining how your qualifications and aspirations align with its academic focus
Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. In line with our values, the University of Luxembourg promotes an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are dedicated to upholding equality and respect for our employees and students.
General information:
Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract 36 Month
Work Hours: Full Time 40.0 Hours per Week
Location: Belval Campus
Internal Title: Doctoral Researcher
Job Reference: UOL08541

The yearly gross salary for every Doctoral researcher at the UL is EUR 44531 (full time).

ap:254229.body:
The German Institute of Human Nutrition Potsdam-Rehbruecke (DIfE) is a member of the Leibniz Association. The institute’s mission is to conduct experimental and clinical research in the field of nutrition and health, with the aim of understanding the molecular basis of nutrition-dependent diseases and of developing new strategies for treatment and prevention (Website: https://www.dife.de/en/ ).
The Department of Molecular Metabolism and Precision Nutrition investigates hormonal and molecular mechanisms involved in the nutritional regulation of the human metabolism. Currently, the focus of the department lies on the role of the circadian clock in metabolic regulation by nutrition. The department is looking for a
Doctoral Student (m/f/div)
starting on January 1st, 2027 .
The successful candidate will contribute to a human study involving the metabolic phenotyping of participants with and without type 2 diabetes. This project aims to investigate the relationship between daily dietary patterns and 24-hour glucose fluctuations in healthy individuals and participants with prediabetes or type 2 diabetes. Among other objectives, the study aims to identify the individual lifestyle-related, metabolic, and molecular factors that predict metabolic responses to diet.
Tasks:
Support of study coordination, study participant’s examination, and processing of blood and adipose tissue samples
Analysis of dietary protocols and questionnaires
Biochemical and molecular analysis of biosamples
Analysis of digital 24-hour glucose, nutrition, and activity data
Analysis of multimodal study data using machine learning algorithms
Preparation of publications
Presentation of research results (colloquia, conference contributions)

Requirements and skills:
M.Sc. degree / Diploma in in nutritional sciences, molecular biology, biochemistry, or another biological / medical field
Additional qualification in bioinformatics, digital health, or a similar field is preferred
Experience in planning and conducting human studies and nutritional data analysis
Proficiency in programming languages such as R or Python
Experience in molecular biology lab work and bioinformatic analysis of omics data (e.g., transcriptome and lipidome data)
High motivation and ability to work in interdisciplinary collaboration and in a diverse research environment
Very high level of written and spoken English and German

We offer:
Intensive scientific support, close collaboration with cooperating institutions and enrolment in a local PhD program
Excellent technical equipment, a wide range of experimental methods, and a dynamic and interactive research environment
Salary will be paid in accordance with TV-L, level 13 (65%)
Opportunities for targeted further education and professional development
Family-friendly working conditions (certificate “audit berufundfamilie”)
Supporting of mobility with a jobticket for using the public transport
Easy accessibility by public transport or car (including free parking)
30 days of vacation
Participation in the benefits program for employees (“corporate benefits”)

The advertised position is available for three years subject to the approval of third-party funding.
We promote the employment of people with severe disabilities and are committed to equal opportunities for them. Applicants with severe disabilities will be given preferential consideration if they have the same qualifications.
Contact:
Please send your documents (cover letter explaining your motivation, CV, copies of degrees / certificates, and references) with reference number 2026_W13_AP   as a single PDF file before November 8th, 2026 , via e-mail to [email protected] .
For further information please do not hesitate to contact:
Prof. Dr. Olga Ramich
Head of the Department Molecular Metabolism and Precision Nutrition
E-Mail: [email protected]
We process your application documents for the purpose of carrying out the application procedure in accordance with Art. 6 para. 1 lit. b) GDPR, Art. 88 GDPR. For more information on the collection, processing, and use of personal data by the German Institute of Human Nutrition as part of the application process and your rights under data protection law, please contact the Department of Human Resources and Social Services ( [email protected] ).

Descrizione dell'attività di ricerca:
FIBERLoop è un progetto di ricerca industriale dedicato al recupero e alla valorizzazione delle fibre minerali artificiali (MMVF), in particolare lana di vetro e lana di roccia, provenienti da rifiuti da costruzione. Il progetto mira a trasformarle in materiali secondari di maggior valore, utilizzabili come componenti cementizi supplementari (SCM), attraverso pretrattamento meccanico, trattamento idrotermale, biodegradazione delle resine fenoliche, micronizzazione e caratterizzazione, fino alla validazione in prodotti cementizi. Il contrattista UNIBZ dovrà avvalersi di microbiologia applicata e biodegradazione di matrici complesse, selezionare e caratterizzare consorzi microbici, progettare e ottimizzare prove sperimentali, analizzare processi biologici e idrotermali, procedere all'elaborazione dei dati e alle attività di scale -up. Dovrà collaborare in contesti interdisciplinari e curare la documentazione scientifica delle attività di ricerca.

Beschreibung der Forschungstätigkeit:
FIBERLoop ist ein industrielles Forschungsprojekt zur Rückgewinnung und Verwertung künstlicher Mineralfasern (MMMF), insbesondere Glas- und Steinwolle, aus Bauabfällen. Ziel ist ihre Umwandlung in höherwertige Sekundärmaterialien für den Einsatz als sekundäre zementäre Zusatzstoffe (SCM), durch mechanische Vorbehandlung, hydrothermale Behandlung, biologischen Abbau phenolischer Harze, Mikronisierung und Charakterisierung sowie die Validierung in zementgebundenen Produkten. Der/die UNIBZ-Forschungsvertragnehmer/in wird angewandte Mikrobiologie und Biodegradation komplexer Matrizen verwenden, mikrobielle Konsortien auswählen und charakterisieren, experimentelle Versuche planen und optimieren, biologische und hydrothermale Prozesse analysieren, Daten auswerten und Scale-up-Aktivitäten durchführen. Darüber hinaus soll er/sie in interdisziplinären Kontexten zusammenarbeiten und die wissenschaftliche Dokumentation der Forschungsaktivitäten übernehmen.

Description of the research activity:
FIBERLoop is an industrial research project focused on the recovery and valorisation of man-made mineral fibres (MMMF), particularly glass wool and rock wool, from construction waste. The project aims to transform them into higher-value secondary materials for use as Supplementary Cementitious Materials (SCM), through mechanical pre-treatment, hydrothermal treatment, biodegradation of phenolic resins, micronisation and characterisation, followed by validation in cementitious products. The UNIBZ research contractor shall make use of applied microbiology and the biodegradation of complex matrices, select and characterise microbial consortia, design and optimise experimental tests, analyse biological and hydrothermal processes, process data and carry out scale-up activities. The research contractor should also collaborate in interdisciplinary contexts and be responsible for the scientific documentation of the research activities.

ap:254246.body:
Student Research Assistant in Bridge Monitoring, Computer Vision & Data Science
The Chair of Structural Mechanics & Monitoring , led by Prof. Eleni Chatzi, conducts research at the intersection of structural engineering, sensing, data science, and artificial intelligence for infrastructure monitoring.

We are looking for a Student Research Assistant with a background in structural engineering, signal processing, data science, computer vision, or related fields to support our ongoing SwissBWIM project. The project combines bridge structural monitoring and traffic monitoring data to identify vehicle loads and assess the structural condition and performance of highway bridges.

Project background
Our project, “SWISS-BWIM: Multi-functional bridge loads and condition assessment,” develops robust and cost-efficient methods for bridge load identification and condition assessment based on the Bridge Weigh-in-Motion (B-WIM) concept.

B-WIM uses sensors installed directly on bridges to estimate the loads of passing vehicles from the bridge response they induce. The same monitoring data can also provide information on structural behaviour and condition. By combining identified traffic loads with structural response, the project aims to derive performance indicators such as dynamic amplification factors, response envelopes, and load-response relationships, and ultimately support the identification of abnormal behaviour and potential damage.

We have completed monitoring-system installations on several highway bridges in Switzerland and are continuously collecting large-scale, multi-modal datasets, including bridge acceleration, strain and displacement measurements, environmental data, and traffic videos.

The Student Research Assistant will work with an analysis framework which has been developed by our Chair to process and integrate these datasets. Depending on background and interest, there will also be opportunities to develop and test new methods for traffic-load identification, computer-vision-based traffic monitoring, and structural health monitoring under the supervision of experienced researchers

Job description
The main tasks include:

Multi-modal data preprocessing: synchronising measurements from different sensing systems, identifying and cleaning faulty data, and improving data organisation and storage.

Traffic video analysis: applying deep-learning-based computer vision methods for vehicle detection and tracking; manually labelling data and fine-tuning models where needed; and using camera calibration and geometric transformation to determine vehicle locations and trajectories on the bridge.

Bridge Weigh-in-Motion analysis: fusing vehicle trajectories with bridge acceleration, strain and displacement measurements to estimate traffic loads.

Structural monitoring: analysing structural and environmental measurements to extract key performance indicators and investigate changes in bridge behaviour and structural condition.

Integrated condition assessment: combining identified traffic loads with structural response indicators to support more comprehensive assessment of bridge performance and condition.

Please note that the methods required to complete most of the tasks above have already been developed by our Chair. Depending on the candidate’s background and interests, there will also be opportunities to develop and test new methods.

Profile
We are looking for a motivated student who can contribute to several of the areas above. Ideally, you:

Are currently enrolled at a university in Zurich or the nearby area.

Have a background in civil/structural engineering, mechanical engineering, data science, computer science, or a related field.

Have experience or strong interest in two or more of the following:

bridge engineering, structural dynamics, or system identification;

sensing systems and signal processing;

data analysis and machine learning;

computer vision, particularly object detection, tracking, or localisation.

Are familiar with Python programming. Experience with MATLAB and Linux is an advantage.

Can dedicate 15 hours per week to the project.

Enjoy working on real-world engineering problems and developing practical, data-driven solutions.

Are proficient in English. The working language of our group is English.

Please note that you are not expected to have prior experience in all of the areas listed above . We particularly welcome applicants who have a strong foundation in two or more of them and are motivated to learn the others.

We offer

Salary in accordance with ETH Zurich’s standard rates for student assistants.

Access to sufficient computational resources, including CPU and GPU computing on Euler, ETH Zurich's high-performance computing cluster.

A workplace in our offices on the ETH Zurich Hönggerberg campus.

Hands-on experience with real-world bridge monitoring systems and large-scale multi-modal datasets.

Close supervision and the opportunity to work at the intersection of structural engineering, sensing, computer vision, and data science.

A collaborative and international research environment within the Chair of Structural Mechanics & Monitoring.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application, by 31 October, 2026 , with the following documents:

CV

Cover letter

Further information about our research group can be found on the website of the Chair of Structural Mechanics & Monitoring. Questions regarding the position can be directed to Dr. Xudong Jian, [email protected] (no application).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

ap:254247.body:
Achtergrond
Het onderzoek zal worden uitgevoerd in de onderzoeksgroep  Centrum voor Statistiek (CenStat) binnen het Data Science Institute (DSI)  van de Universiteit Hasselt.
Jouw promotor zal Prof. dr. Thomas Neyens zijn, jouw co-promotor dr. Maxime Fajgenblat.
Als doctoraatsstudent zal je samenwerken met ecologen en met partners zoals Natuurpunt Studie, het Instituut voor Natuur- en Bosonderzoek (INBO) en andere stakeholders als Dragonfly Conservation Europe.
Het Data Science Instituut (opgericht in 2019) brengt meer dan 150 onderzoekers samen die werkzaam zijn binnen het brede veld van data science, verspreid over faculteiten en onderzoeksgroepen aan de Universiteit Hasselt. DSI's belangrijkste doelstelling is het faciliteren van de data-gedreven toekomst. We zetten ons in voor data-gerelateerde uitdagingen, fundamentele innovaties en toepasbare oplossingen. Voor meer informatie: https://www.uhasselt.be/dsi

Functie-inhoud
Natuurliefhebbers en burgerwetenschappers registreren via portalen zoals Waarnemingen.be en iNaturalist miljoenen waarnemingen van planten en dieren. Die gegevens worden niet volgens een vast protocol verzameld: waar, wanneer en hoe intensief er gezocht wordt, verschilt sterk, en niet elke aanwezige soort wordt ook gezien.

In dit project ontwikkel je Bayesiaanse hiërarchische modellen die hiermee rekening houden, zoals site-occupancy-modellen met imperfecte detectie en spatio-temporele modellen, en gebruik je ze om ecologische vragen te beantwoorden. Voorbeelden zijn:

hoe zijn vlindergemeenschappen in Vlaanderen veranderd over de voorbije 125 jaar;

hoe verschuiven de verspreidingsgebieden van insecten in Europa onder invloed van klimaatverandering;

op welke ruimtelijke en temporele schaal beïnvloedt landgebruik het voorkomen van soorten;

hoe kan het herstel van Natura 2000-gebieden opgevolgd worden met bestaande waarnemingen?

Als doctoraatsstudent op dit project voer je onderzoek uit in het domein van de biostatistiek, meer bepaald ecologische statistiek. Welke onderdelen jouw doctoraat vormen, wordt in overleg bepaald. Je bouwt de modellen in Stan en R en test ze met simulatiestudies. Je publiceert jouw resultaten in wetenschappelijke tijdschriften, stelt jouw werk voor op nationale en internationale congressen en bouwt een (inter)nationaal netwerk uit.
Tenslotte zal je in beperkte mate bijdragen aan de onderwijstaken van de vakgroep Wiskunde-Statistiek (bijvoorbeeld werkzittingen begeleiden, examens voorbereiden en verbeteren, studenten begeleiden bij hun masterproef).

De positie wordt gefinancierd vanuit een onderzoeksproject. We verwachten dat de je een aanvraag indient voor een persoonlijk doctoraatsmandaat (bv. een FWO-aspirantenmandaat), met volledige ondersteuning van het promotorenteam.

Profiel
Je beschikt over een masterdiploma in (Bio-)Statistiek of Data science (of gelijkwaardig) of Kwantitatieve Biologie. Ecologen met een sterke kwantitatieve achtergrond worden ook aangemoedigd om te solliciteren.
Je hebt interesse in ecologie en biodiversiteit, ervaring met het onderzoeksthema is een meerwaarde.
Je kan programmeren in R (of Python/Julia). Ervaring met Bayesiaanse statistiek (bijvoorbeeld Stan) is een pluspunt.

Je hebt een goede kennis van het Engels.
Je hebt sterke communicatieve vaardigheden, zowel schriftelijk als mondeling.

Je hebt uitstekende studieresultaten.
Je werkt graag in een multidisciplinaire omgeving en je kan goed in teamverband werken.

Aanbod
Je wordt aangesteld en verloond als Doctoraatsbursaal .
We bieden jou een doctoraatsbeurs aan voor twee jaar. Dit kan verlengd worden met twee jaar na een positieve tussentijdse evaluatie door de doctoraatscommissie.
Startdatum: bij voorkeur januari 2027.

Selectieprocedure
Je kan enkel online solliciteren en dit tot en met 16 november 2026 .
De selectieprocedure bestaat uit een voorselectie op sollicitatiedossier en een interview.

Meer info
Prof. dr. Thomas NEYENS, +32-11-268300, [email protected]

Voor vragen over de selectieprocedure, mail je naar [email protected] .

ap:254248.body:
Background
The research will be performed in the research group Center for Statistics (CenStat) within the Data Science Institute (DSI) at Hasselt University.
Your supervisor will be Prof. dr. Thomas Neyens and your co-supervior dr. Maxime Fajgenblat.
As a PhD student, you will work with ecologists and with partners such as Natuurpunt Studie, the Research Institute for Nature and Forest (INBO) and other stakeholders like Dragonfly Conservation Europe.
The Data Science Institute (established in 2019) brings together more than 150 researchers working in the broad field of data science, spread across faculties and research groups at Hasselt University. DSI's primary objective is to facilitate a data-driven future. We are committed to addressing data-related challenges, fundamental innovations, and applicable solutions. For more information, please visit: https://www.uhasselt.be/dsi

Job content
Through online portals such as Observation.org and iNaturalist, naturalists and citizen scientists record millions of observations of plants and animals. These data are not collected according to a fixed protocol: where, when and how intensively people search varies widely, and not every species that is present is also seen.
In this project you will develop Bayesian hierarchical models that account for this, such as site-occupancy models with imperfect detection and spatio-temporal models, and use them to answer ecological questions. Examples are:

how have butterfly communities in Flanders changed over the past 125 years;

how are the ranges of insects in Europe shifting under climate change;

at which spatial and temporal scale does land use affect where species occur;

how can the restoration of Natura 2000 sites be monitored with existing observations?

As a PhD student, you will conduct research in the field of biostatistics, more specifically ecological statistics. Which parts make up your PhD will be decided together. You will build the models in Stan and R and test them with simulation studies. You will publish your results in scientific journals, present your work at national and international conferences and build an (inter)national network.
Finally, you will contribute to a limited extent to the teaching tasks of the Mathematics-Statistics department (for example, supervising exercise sessions, preparing and grading exams, and supervising students with their master’s thesis).

The position is funded by a research project. We expect you to apply for personal PhD funding (e.g. an FWO fellowship), with full support from the supervisory team.

Profile
You hold a master's degree in (Bio-)Statistics or Data science (or equivalent) or Quantitative Biology. Ecologists with a strong quantitative background are also encouraged to apply.
You are interested in ecology and biodiversity, previous experience with the research topic is an asset.
You can program in R (or Python/Julia). Experience with Bayesian statistics (for example Stan) is a plus.
You have a good command of English.
You have strong communication skills, both written and oral.
You have excellent study results.

You enjoy working in a multidisciplinary environment and you can work well in teams.

Offer
You will be appointed and paid as PhD student .
We offer you a doctoral fellowship for two years. This can be extended by two years after a positive mid-term evaluation by the doctoral committee.
Start date: ideally January 2027.

Selection procedure
You can only apply online up to and including 16 November 2026 .
The selection procedure consists of a preselection based on application file and an interview.

Further information
Prof. dr. Thomas NEYENS, +32-11-268300, [email protected]

For questions about the selection procedure, please email [email protected] .

ap:254253.body:
De groep Wetenschap & Technologie van KU Leuven Campus Kulak verzorgt het onderwijs in een brede waaier van bacheloropleidingen wetenschappen, met doorstroomopties naar ingenieurswetenschappen, bio-ingenieurswetenschappen, en farmacie.

Binnen de doorstroomoptie ingenieurswetenschappen zoeken we een gemotiveerde praktijkassistent om enerzijds integratie van AI in het curriculum te ondersteunen en anderzijds de interactie tussen het (lokale) bedrijfsleven en de opleiding te versterken. Dit laatste kan gebeuren door bedrijfsvragen te gebruiken in de vakken probleemoplossen en ontwerpen, bedrijfsbezoeken te organiseren, en connecties uit te bouwen die studenten toelaten om op eigen initiatief vakantiewerk te doen met relevantie tot hun opleiding.

Website van de eenheid

Functie

Je biedt op Campus Kulak Kortrijk ondersteuning en begeleiding bij oefenzittingen, practica en projectwerk binnen de doorstroomoptie ingenieurswetenschappen.

Je begeleidt en ondersteunt studenten bij het uitvoeren van projecten binnen het vak probleemoplossen en ontwerpen.

Je werkt mee aan de ontwikkeling en verdere uitbouw van interacties met het bedrijfsleven binnen de opleiding, met het oog op integratie van concrete vraagstukken in zowel het theoretische als het praktische deel van het curriculum.

Je werkt mee aan de ontwikkeling en integratie van artificiële intelligentie in het curriculum op een verantwoorde en ondersteunende manier.

Je houdt je technisch-wetenschappelijke expertise en je studiemateriaal up-to-date, onder andere door betrokkenheid bij de docententeams van Campus Kulak Kortrijk en die van de Faculteit Ingenieurswetenschappen.

Je werkt campusoverschrijdend binnen de Faculteit Wetenschappen en werkt samen met collega’s die een vergelijkbare opdracht hebben.

Je biedt ondersteuning bij het beheer en het onderhoud van de labo-infrastructuur en haar inzet voor studentenprojecten. Je werkt hiervoor nauw samen met andere collega’s van Campus Kulak Kortrijk.

Je werkt actief mee aan PR- en rekruteringsactiviteiten (workshops voor studenten secundair onderwijs, infodagen, etc.) en onderhoudt contacten met bedrijven in het kader van je didactische opdrachten, dienstverleningsactiviteiten en organisatie van bedrijfsbezoeken.

Profiel

Je beschikt over een diploma van master in de (industriële) ingenieurswetenschappen, toegepaste fysica, of een diploma dat hiermee equivalent is.

Ervaring in het hoger academisch onderwijs in het domein van de ingenieurswetenschappen of toegepaste fysica is een plus.

Je bent communicatief (Nederlands en Engels) en sociaal vaardig.

Je hebt een sterke interesse in het begeleiden van studenten.

Je bent technisch aangelegd, leergierig en gemotiveerd om je technisch-wetenschappelijke en onderwijskundige kennis voortdurend te verbeteren.

Je werkt nauwkeurig en kan zowel zelfstandig werken als in teamverband.

Je kan een netwerk van bedrijfscontacten onderhouden en verder uitbouwen.

Aanbod

Wij voorzien een 60% aanstelling (eventueel mogelijk tot verhoging bij onderlinge overeenkomst) als praktijkassistent voor de duur van één jaar, met mogelijkheid van verlenging tot 2031 na positieve evaluatie. Aan deze functie is een salaris in barema 43 gekoppeld.

Wij bieden een uitdagende en gevarieerde functie binnen een dynamische universitaire omgeving. Je krijgt de kans om actief mee te bouwen aan innovatieve opleidingen, samen te werken met een enthousiast team van collega’s en een betekenisvolle bijdrage te leveren aan de opleiding van toekomstige biowetenschappers.

Daarnaast bieden we ruimte voor initiatief, professionele ontwikkeling en verdere vorming binnen onderwijsinnovatie, educatieve technologie en studentenbegeleiding.

Interesse?

Meer informatie is te verkrijgen bij prof. dr. ir. Wim Thielemans, mail: [email protected] of prof. dr. David Dudal, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven wil een inclusieve, respectvolle en sociaal veilige gemeenschap zijn. Wij omarmen diversiteit tussen individuen en groepen als een meerwaarde. Open dialoog en verschillen in perspectief zijn noodzakelijk in een ambitieuze onderzoeks- en onderwijsomgeving. In ons streven naar gelijke kansen erkennen wij de gevolgen van historische ongelijkheden. Wij aanvaarden geen enkele vorm van discriminatie op basis van, onder meer, geslacht, genderidentiteit en -expressie, seksuele oriëntatie, leeftijd, etnische of nationale afkomst, huidskleur, levensbeschouwelijke overtuiging, neurodivergentie, arbeidshandicap, gezondheid, of socio-economische status. Bij vragen over toegankelijkheid of aangeboden ondersteuning helpen we je graag op dit e-mailadres .

ap:254257.body:
Introduction
Are you eager to shape the next generation of chips using atomically thin materials? In this PhD position, you will develop 2D nanomaterials and devices for more energy-efficient sensing and computing. The project will be undertaken within the NanoComputing Research Lab in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology (TU/e), at the heart of Europe’s leading semiconductor region.

Job Description
In this PhD position, you will investigate 2D materials as a platform for next-generation sensing and computing devices. You will develop growth recipes for 2D materials and fabricate and characterize devices that could contribute to emerging energy efficient brain-inspired computing hardware.
What you'll contribute to
Specifically, you will:
develop metal-organic chemical vapour deposition (MOCVD) growth recipes for large-area 2D materials, such as MoS₂ and WSe₂, with controlled defect densities;
optimize transfer processes to integrate the grown 2D materials onto target device substrates, enabling heterogeneous integration;
develop scalable fabrication processes in the TU/e cleanroom (NanoLab@TU/e) for device arrays, including sensors and transistors;
engineer metal–semiconductor and dielectric interfaces to improve device performance;
characterize materials and devices, and work with circuit designers to link material properties to device and circuit performance;
publish your results in leading journals and present them at international conferences;
supervise Bachelor’s and Master’s student projects.

Your research environment
You will join the NanoComputing Research Lab ( NanoComputing Research Lab ), in the Integrated Circuits group of the Department of Electrical Engineering at TU/e. You will be supervised by Dr. Abhishek Singh Dahiya (project leader) and Prof. Aida Todri-Sanial. You will have access to TU/e’s state-of-the-art cleanroom and characterization facilities.
What we're looking for
A master’s degree in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field, with a solid foundation in semiconductor materials and device physics, and prior experience in the growth of nanomaterials (preferably 2D materials using CVD), nanofabrication processes such as atomic layer deposition, lithography, etching etc., and 2D material transfer process.

Job Requirements
A master’s degree (or an equivalent university degree) in electrical engineering, nanotechnology, or a related field.
A research-oriented attitude.
Ability to work in an interdisciplinary team.
Motivated to develop your teaching skills and mentor bachelor/master’s students.
Fluent in spoken and written English (C1 level).

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process .
An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs.
A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme ) for international candidates.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .
Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .

The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field.

Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The Electrical Engineering department takes its inspiration from contacts with high-tech industry in the direct surrounding region and beyond.

The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed.

Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager Dr Abhishek Singh Dahiya, Assistant Professor, [email protected] .
Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact [email protected] .
Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video .
Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page.

Application
We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a:
Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and qualifications for the position.
Curriculum vitae, including a list of your publications and the contact information of three references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application.

Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications.

We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled.

Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) at the University of Luxembourg contributes multidisciplinary expertise in the fields of Mathematics, Physics, Engineering, Computer Science, Life Sciences and Medicine.
Through its dual mission of teaching and research, the FSTM seeks to generate and disseminate knowledge and train new generations of responsible citizens in order to better understand, explain and advance society and the environment we live in.
The DoE develops solutions to engineering problems by combining theoretical, experimental, computational and data-driven approaches. The DoE applies a 360° holistic vision and expertise, promotes an interdisciplinary and integrated research approach, and serves Luxembourg by forming the next generation of engineers, by supporting policy making and by catalysing industrial innovation through consolidated national and international collaborations, enabling the testing and implementation of new approaches and development of innovative products.
PFAROS is a pioneering European initiative aimed at accelerating the replacement of harmful per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS) in the pharmaceutical and medical technology sectors. In line with EU priorities for public health, environmental protection, and industrial development, PFAROS is developing safe, scalable alternatives designed to meet regulatory requirements, bringing healthcare innovation and sustainability together.
The mission of PFAROS is to replace PFAS in medical and pharmaceutical applications through a multidisciplinary approach. It combines validated alternatives, advanced degradation and disposal technologies, and data science to guide substitution decisions and inform policy development.
Your role
Within PFAROS, the University of Luxembourg team will help address three key questions:
Does hospital wastewater contribute to PFAS pollution, and to what extent?
Can functionalized membranes effectively concentrate PFAS and reduce their levels in wastewater?
Which technologies are suitable for subsequently destroying the concentrated PFAS?

To investigate these questions, laboratory-scale and full-scale trials will be conducted under real-world conditions. The PhD student will work on this project and contribute to the technical reports, disseminating the results in conferences, seminars and scientific articles. The candidate will attend doctoral school courses and network training, contributing to education activities to a certain extent. They should finalize the work with a doctoral degree in engineering science.
Your profile
Master's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or an equivalent degree in engineering
Advanced competence in laboratory and analytical work is necessary
Capability to examine large data sets
Operational Language Requirements: Very good command of English is required. Good working knowledge of German or French is an asset

Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .

A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

We are seeking a highly motivated PhD candidate to join the IAS Audacity project AI4TECS, which investigates how advanced artificial intelligence (AI) techniques can enable real‑time identification and treatment of emerging contaminants (ECs). AI4TECS aims to develop the first AI‑powered system that integrates real‑time EC identification using non-target high resolution mass spectrometry (HRMS) data, toxicity prediction, and transformation modelling into an early‑warning monitoring framework.
Your role
Conducting excellent collaborative research within the project AI4TECS. The person will pursue three core research directions: Developing a foundation model capable of identifying ECs directly from complex LC‑HRMS data
Designing hierarchical graph‑based models to predict toxicity under uncertainty by linking molecular‑level and system‑level knowledge
Advancing causal inference methods to predict transformation products (TPs) under varying treatment conditions

Writing a doctoral dissertation in computer science
Publishing research findings in leading international conferences and high‑impact journals in AI, machine learning, and environmental sciences
Presenting results at scientific meetings, workshops, and project events, contributing to the visibility and impact of the AI4TECS project
Potential participation in teaching activities

The PhD candidate will join an interdisciplinary project team with expertise spanning environmental chemistry, AI, and water‑treatment engineering. Collaboration is central to the project's design. Throughout the project, the candidate will work closely with a second doctoral researcher to be recruited within the Environmental Cheminformatics Group (ECI) at LCSB. The ECI PhD candidate will perform prioritized Non-Targeted Assessment (pNTA) across diverse water matrices and case studies, while the AI4Science PhD (this position) will develop machine‑learning models that learn from and build upon these pNTA results.

The successful candidate will be employed at the Department of Computer Science of the University of Luxembourg (UL) and have access to high-performance computing (HPC) resources suitable for large-scale machine-learning and foundation-model experiments. They will be supervised by Prof. Dr. Jun Pang and Dr. Zhiqiang Zhong.

ap:254272.body:
Scientific Assistant in Real-Time Generative Models and Computer Models
The Biomedical Image Computing Group develops algorithmic solutions to enable automatic interpretation and forming of biomedical images, aiming to increase efficiency and accuracy in clinical practice and research.

Project background
The enhancement of endoscopic videos is a critical yet complex task. These videos are integral to various clinical interventions, where the clarity of imaging data is essential for procedural success. Due to challenging imaging conditions, the quality of endoscopic videos can be significantly compromised by a range of artifacts. This project seeks to develop the next generation of enhancement algorithms tailored for endoscopic videos, with a focus on applications in real-time interventions. Development efforts will prioritize both enhancement quality and computational efficiency, particularly with respect to latency.

The successful candidate will join the BMIC team at ETH Zurich and also be part of the Computer Vision Lab (CVL). The project is conducted in collaboration with an industrial implementation partner, who will provide support with hardware and software integration.

The position is open immediately and initially limited to 8 months.

Job description
This position involves the implementation, optimization, and deployment of deep-learning image-enhancement models for real-time operation. Rather than focusing primarily on model training, the successful candidate will work on translating existing and new architectures into efficient real-time processing pipelines connected directly to an industrial camera system. Typical tasks will include profiling and optimizing models for low-latency inference, implementing and adapting neural-network architectures with real-time constraints in mind, integrating camera acquisition and preprocessing pipelines, and contributing to project deliverables and scientific manuscript preparation.

Profile

MSc degree in computer science, machine learning, medical image computing, or a related field.

Familiarity with neural-network-based image processing pipelines.

Excellent programming skills and experience with Python.

Experience implementing and validating neural-network architectures using PyTorch.

Demonstrable experience with model deployment/acceleration (PyTorch, ONNX, TensorRT, CUDA/C++, etc.), profiling tools, and camera/sensor integration is a plus.

We offer

Your job with impact: Become part of ETH Zurich, which not only supports your professional development, but also actively contributes to positive change in society

You can expect numerous benefits , such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ , childcare and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.

CV

Recommendation Letter (if available)

Further information about Biomedical Image Computing can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Julio Jose Silva Rodríguez, [email protected] (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

ap:254273.body:
Do you want to contribute to top quality medical research?
The department of clinical science and education, Södersjukhuset (KI SÖS), is characterized by medical research that is closely integrated with clinical practice. Our location at one of Stockholm's major emergency hospitals provides excellent opportunities to investigate clinically relevant research questions through collaboration between researchers and healthcare professionals. The department is now looking for a statistician to join Gianluigi Savarese’s research group.
Here, you will have the opportunity to work in an interdisciplinary academic environment, develop your expertise, and contribute to research that has the potential to improve healthcare.
Your mission
As a statistician, you will be part of the heart failure and arrhythmia research group. The group focuses on heart failure, arrhythmias, and related cardiovascular diseases. We use large clinical registries, linked national health data registries, electronic health records, and clinical trials to study patient outcomes, treatment effectiveness, the implementation of evidence-based care, and the epidemiology of these diseases.
Working closely with clinical researchers, doctoral students, and international collaborators, you will contribute to the entire research process, from study design to scientific publication.
Your responsibilities will include:
Develop study designs and statistical analysis plans in collaboration with the research group.
Apply for access to data from quality registries and administrative registers.
Process, manage, and validate large datasets, including data from the Swedish heart failure registry (RiksSvikt/SwedeHF) linked to other national registers.
Independently conduct statistical analyses, including survival analysis, longitudinal modelling, competing risk analysis, propensity score methods, methods for handling missing data, machine learning and AI, as well as target trial emulation using the clone-censor-weight approach.
Contribute to scientific manuscripts and research grant applications.
Provide statistical guidance and support to doctoral students and other researchers, and ensure well-documented and reproducible analytical workflows.
Serve as the point of contact between the research group and KI's IT department to coordinate the management and resolution of IT-related issues concerning research servers, virtual machines, and associated IT infrastructure.
Participate in all activities of the research group.

Additional responsibilities may be assigned depending on the development of the research group and your expertise. Your profile
We are looking for a candidate with a master's degree in statistics, biostatistics, epidemiology, or a related quantitative field. You have extensive and documented experience in applying for access to data from quality registries and administrative registers, as well as in extracting, managing, and analyzing large registry-based datasets and data from electronic health records. Your expertise includes pharmacoepidemiology, studies of treatment effectiveness and safety, survival analysis, longitudinal analyses, and the application of machine learning and artificial intelligence. A good understanding of the Swedish healthcare system is required to ensure the correct interpretation of extracted data. Furthermore, you have good proficiency in both R and Stata.
As a person, you are structured and detail-oriented, with the ability to work independently. You enjoy sharing your expertise and are able to provide guidance and support to doctoral students and other researchers in a clear and pedagogical manner. You have strong collaboration skills, are flexible, and are able to adapt to varying needs and priorities within a large international research group. What do we offer?
A creative and inspiring environment with wide-ranging expertise and interests. Karolinska Institutet is one of the world's leading medical universities. Our vision is to pursue the development of knowledge about life and to promote a better health for all. At Karolinska Institutet, we conduct successful medical research and hold the largest range of medical education in Sweden. Karolinska Institutet is also a state university, which entitles you to several good benefits through our collective agreement. And you get to practice freely in our modern wellness facilities, where trained staff are on site.

ap:254274.body:
Vill du bidra till att förbättra människors hälsa?
Institutionen för klinisk forskning och utbildning, Södersjukhuset (KI SÖS) är en institution som kännetecknas av medicinsk forskning nära integrerad med den kliniska vardagen. Vår placering vid ett av Stockholms stora akutsjukhus ger möjlighet att undersöka kliniskt relevanta frågeställningar genom samarbete mellan forskare och hälso- och sjukvårdspersonal. Institutionen söker nu en statistiker som kommer att arbeta i Gianluigi Savareses forskargrupp.
Här får du möjligheten att arbeta i en tvärvetenskaplig akademisk miljö, utveckla din kompetens och bidra till forskning som kan förbättra vården.
Din roll
Som statistiker kommer du att tillhöra forskargruppen för hjärtsvikt och arytmi. Gruppen fokuserar på hjärtsvikt, arytmier och relaterade hjärt-kärlsjukdomar. Vi använder stora kliniska register, länkade nationella hälsodataregister, elektroniska patientjournaler och kliniska prövningar för patientutfall, behandlingseffektivitet, implementering av evidensbaserad vård och sjukdomarnas epidemiologi.
I nära samarbete med kliniska forskare, doktorander och internationella samarbetspartners kommer du bidra till hela forskningsprocessen, från studiedesign till vetenskaplig publicering.
Dina arbetsuppgifter kommer bestå av att:
Utveckla studiedesigner och statistiska analysplaner i samarbete med forskargruppen.
Ansöka om tillgång till data från kvalitetsregister och administrativa register.
Bearbeta, hantera och validera stora datamängder, inklusive data från det svenska hjärtsviktsregistret (RiksSvikt/SwedeHF) länkade till andra nationella register.
Självständigt genomföra statistiska analyser, inklusive överlevnadsanalys, longitudinell modellering, analys av konkurrerande risker, propensity score-metoder, metoder för hantering av saknade data, maskinlärning och AI samt emulering av kliniska prövningar med metoden clone-censor-weight.
Bidra till vetenskapliga manuskript och forskningsansökningar.
Ge statistisk vägledning och stöd till doktorander och andra forskare samt säkerställa väldokumenterade och reproducerbara analysflöden.
Fungera som kontaktperson mellan forskargruppen och KI:s IT-avdelning för att samordna hantering och lösning av IT-frågor som rör forskningsservrar, virtuella maskiner och tillhörande IT-infrastruktur.
Delta i forskargruppens samtliga aktiviteter.

Andra arbetsuppgifter kan tillkomma beroende på forskargruppens utveckling och din kompetens.
Vem är du?
Vi söker dig som har en masterexamen i statistik, biostatistik, epidemiologi eller ett närliggande kvantitativt ämnesområde. Du har omfattande och dokumenterad erfarenhet av att ansöka om tillgång till data från kvalitetsregister och administrativa register samt av att extrahera, hantera och analysera stora registerdatamängder och data från elektroniska patientjournaler. Din kompetens omfattar farmakoepidemiologi, studier av behandlingseffektivitet och säkerhet, överlevnadsanalys, longitudinella analyser samt tillämpning av maskininlärning och artificiell intelligens. God förståelse för det svenska hälso- och sjukvårdssystemet krävs för att kunna tolka extraherade data korrekt. Vidare har du goda kunskaper i både R och Stata.
Som person är du strukturerad, noggrann och har förmåga att arbeta självständigt. Du tycker om att dela med dig av din kompetens och kan på ett pedagogiskt sätt ge vägledning och stöd till doktorander och andra forskare. Du har en god samarbetsförmåga, är flexibel och har förmåga att anpassa dig till varierande behov och prioriteringar i en stor internationell forskargrupp.
Vad erbjuder vi?
En kreativ, internationell och inspirerande miljö fylld av kompetens och nyfikenhet. Karolinska Institutet är ett av världens ledande medicinska universitet. Vår vision är att driva utvecklingen av kunskap om livet och verka för en bättre hälsa för alla. Här bedriver vi framgångsrik medicinsk forskning och har det största utbudet av medicinska utbildningar i Sverige. Som universitet är Karolinska Institutet en statlig myndighet. Det gör att du får goda förmåner genom vårt kollektivavtal. Medarbetare på KI erbjuds också möjlighet till ett flexibelt arbetssätt. Det innebär att om den verksamhet du jobbar i tillåter, så kan du arbeta en del av din arbetstid på distans. Du får även träna fritt i våra moderna friskvårdsanläggningar där utbildad personal finns på plats.

ap:254278.body:
About the SnT
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The  Interdisciplinary Centre for Security, Reliability and Trust ( SnT ) at the University of Luxembourg is a leading international research and innovation centre in secure, reliable and trustworthy ICT systems and services.
We play an instrumental role in Europe by fueling innovation through research partnerships with industry, boosting R&D investments leading to economic growth, and attracting highly qualified talent. We look for researchers from diverse academic backgrounds to contribute to our projects in areas such as: Network Security, Information Assurance, Model-driven Security, Cloud Computing, Cryptography, Satellite Systems, Vehicular Networks, and ICT Services & Applications.
Your role
SnT is looking for a Research Data Steward to lead the organisational Research Data Management (RDM) development and shape the RDM support landscape within the organisation. The role will support the implementation and continuous improvement of RDM practices within SnT at the University of Luxembourg. The role is responsible for providing strategic oversight of Research Data Management (RDM) at the institutional level, including designing and evolving the RDM support strategy and contributing to the development and implementation of RDM policies. In parallel, the role delivers direct, hands‑on RDM support to researchers across the research data life cycle, ensuring alignment with institutional policies, FAIR data principles, and Open Science standards.
The successful candidate will collaborate closely with internal and external stakeholders to strengthen and harmonise RDM workflows, provide expert guidance on daily data management practices and long‑term preservation, contribute to the development of sustainable and maintainable data management procedures, and actively participate in organisational and national communities and initiatives to ensure alignment with emerging best practices, standards, and strategic priorities.
Key responsibilities:
Implement and promote the institutional RDM policy, supporting researchers' understanding of and alignment with its requirements
Design, develop, and deliver RDM training, guidance materials, and awareness activities tailored to the diverse needs of research groups
Advise researchers on RDM best practices throughout the research data life cycle, including planning, documentation, storage, sharing, and long-term preservation
Raise awareness of FAIR data principles and Open Science practices across the Centre
Support and improve the preparation, review, and maintenance of Data Management Plans (DMPs) from initial drafting through funder submission and periodic updates
Assist researchers in selecting and using appropriate repositories to ensure data accessibility and long-term preservation
Standardise research data storage by identifying ad-hoc or non-institutional storage practices, establishing clear storage guidelines, and facilitating the adoption of secure institutional storage solutions
Identify researchers' needs related to RDM, proactively identify gaps in current RDM support, and provide evidence-based recommendations to the SnT management team
Contribute to the enhancement of SnT's RDM procedures, workflows, and service offerings to ensure effective organisational support

Your profile
MSc in a relevant field, such as information science, library science, data management, or a research discipline aligned with SnT's priority domains, combined with expertise in data-intensive research
2-5 years of relevant experience in data stewardship, research support, research data management, or a similar role
Strong understanding of the research lifecycle, RDM best practices, the FAIR data principles, and leading data governance frameworks
Familiarity with funder and institutional RDM requirements (e.g., FNR, Horizon Europe)
Familiarity with GDPR and its application to research data, with the ability to recognise when to consult specialists
Familiarity with data security measures (e.g., encryption, access restrictions, anonymisation/pseudonymisation) sufficient to support storage standardisation responsibilities
Understanding of ethical aspects of RDM, including informed consent and ethical approval processes
Demonstrated ability to design and deliver training or information sessions for varied audiences
Possessing one or more of the following competencies is a strong asset: Knowledge of and experience with relevant domain-specific metadata standards
Knowledge of legal aspects of RDM, including intellectual property rights and data licensing relevant to sharing and reusing research data
Skills in reproducible research and Open Science practices

Cooperative and collaborative team member; able to support colleagues and contribute to shared goals
Excellent command of English is required

We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover letter

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
The University of Luxembourg is committed to achieving gender parity among its staff. Should candidates present equivalent profiles, preference will be given to female candidates in all departments where gender parity is not yet achieved.
The University of Luxembourg embraces inclusion and diversity as key values. We are fully committed to removing any discriminatory barrier related to gender, and not only, in recruitment and career progression of our staff.
