Om stillingen
Institutt for informasjonsteknologi ved Fakultet for teknologi, kunst og design har en ledig åremålsstilling som stipendiat innen pålitelig KI med verifikasjon av kunnskap. Nåværende arbeidssted for stillingen er på campus Pilestredet i Oslo. I forbindelse med etableringen av ny campus på Lillestrøm kan det bli aktuelt med endring av arbeidssted på et senere tidspunkt.
Benjamin A. Ward

Dine ansvarsområder og arbeidsoppgaver vil være å
Dette prosjektet er banebrytende i utviklingen av et nevro-symbolsk KI-rammeverk som adresserer den kritiske «hallusinasjons»-barrieren i generativ KI (GenAI). Per i dag fungerer GenAI-modeller som probabilistiske «svarte bokser» som ofte produserer plausible, men faktisk feilaktig informasjon uten kildehenvisning. Dette utgjør uakseptable risikoer, særlig i høyrisiko-domener som for eksempel utdanning, trafikksikkerhet og fornybar energi.
For å håndtere dette utvikler prosjektet et generaliserbart nevro-symbolsk verifikasjonsrammeverk, med mål om systematisk å transformere GenAI til etterprøvbare, verifiserbare og sosialt ansvarlige systemer for høy-risiko- og datafattige domener. Prosjektet undersøker hybride rammeverk hvor GenAI fungerer som semantiske tolkningsmoduler, mens symbolske logikkmoduler — som resonerer over strukturerte grafer eller regler — fungerer som faktasjekkere.
Stipendiaten vil utføre følgende oppgaver:
rammeverk design og implementering
utvikling av resonneringsalgoritmer og validering.

Det primære bruksområdet bygger på en KI-forsterket nettplattform for nord-samisk språklæring. Doktorgradsprosjektet vil utvikle en modulær verifikasjonsmotor integrerti plattformen for å sikre at KI-generert innhold er språklig korrekt og kulturelt passende. To tilleggstilfeller kan velges for å teste generaliserbarheten til det foreslåtte rammeverket: autonom kjøring og informasjonsmodellering for bærekraft.
Det forventes at PhD prosjektet involverer akademisk samarbeid med Karlsruhe Institute of Technology (KIT, Germany).
Stillingen lyses ut som 3 år med 100% forskning, eller 4 år med 75% forskning og 25% annet karrierefremmende arbeid. Det er et mål at kandidaten skal fullføre PhD-programmet/-graden innenfor den besluttede tidsrammen. Beslutningen om 3- eller 4- årigstilling vil bli diskutert som en del av intervjuene i ansettelsesprosessen.
Som stipendiat ved OsloMet har du mulighet til å søke om stipend for lengre forskningsopphold i utlandet.
Kvalifikasjonskrav
Mastergrad/hovedfag innen informatikk, matematikk, ingeniørfag eller tilsvarende relaterte fagdisipliner. Graden må normalt inneholde 120 studiepoeng (ECTS). Søkere med mastergrad bestående av mindre enn 120 ECTS må innen søknadsfristen dokumentere at graden kvalifiserer til opptak til doktorgradsstudier i landet hvor mastergraden ble tatt.
En faglig profil som passer forskningsgruppens og instituttets behov.
For ansettelse i stillingen stilles normalt følgende karakterkrav: Minimum gjennomsnittskarakter B på emner som inngår i mastergraden.
Minimum karakter B på masteroppgave/hovedoppgave.
Minimum gjennomsnittskarakter C på emnene som inngår i bachelorgraden. Dersom du har en integrert mastergradsutdanning regnes karakterene fra de tre første normerte studieårene.
Unntak fra karakterkravene er oppgitt på doktorgradsprogrammets nettside ( Ingeniørvitenskap - OsloMet ).

Gode engelskkunnskaper, muntlig og skriftlig( Språkkrav for ansatte ved OsloMet )

Godkjent opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet for ingeniørvitenskap ( Ingeniørvitenskap - OsloMet ) ved Fakultet for teknologi, kunst og design er en forutsetning for stillingen. Det må søkes om opptak til doktorgradsprogrammet innen 3 måneder etter tiltredelsesdato.
Generelle kriterier for ansettelse som stipendiat fremgår av forskriften ( Forskrift til universitets- og høyskoleloven- Lovdata ).
Det vil være en fordel om du har
dokumentert sterk kompetanse innen programmering, for eksempel Python.
gode analytiske evner og matematisk grunnlag, med en stor interesse for å anvende formell logikk på generative modeller.
kjennskap til kunnskapsrepresentasjon (f.eks. kunnskapsgrafer og semantiske teknologier); formell resonnering er en fordel.

Personlige egenskaper
selvmotivert og målrettet
sterk motivasjon for å gjennomføre et doktorgradsløp.
god gjennomføringsevne
evne til å samarbeideogjobbe selvstendig
gode analytiske ferdigheter
gode kreative ferdigheter og evne til nytenkning

Personlig egnethet vil bli vektlagt.
Det er viktig for OsloMet å gjenspeile befolkningen i vår region og vi ønsker alle kvalifiserte søkere velkommen. Vi arbeider aktivt med å utvikle oss videre som en inkluderende arbeidsplass og for å tilrettelegge arbeidsplassen dersom du har behov for det. Har du perioder i livet hvor du ikke har vært i arbeid, utdanning eller opplæring er du også velkommen til å søke hos oss.
Vi tilbyr
interessante arbeidsoppgaver ved Norges tredje største universitet
deltakelse i forskningsgruppe og et kreativt og inspirerende fagmiljø
muligheter til faglig utvikling
gode velferdsordninger og et bredt spekter av tilbud av aktiviteter innen kultur og sport
låne- og pensjonsbetingelser i Statens pensjonskasse

Søknadsprosess
Vil du søke på stillingen må du søke via vårt rekrutteringssystem.
Innen søknadsfristen må du laste opp følgende dokumenter:
søknadsbrev som beskriver din motivasjon for å søke stillingen
CV, attester og alle sider av vitnemålfor bachelor- og mastergrad. Utenlandsk utdanning bør være godkjent på forhånd, og godkjenningsbrev må isåfall vedlegges. Informasjon finnes via lenken: Godkjenning av utenlandsk utdanning – jobb i Norge | HK-dir

Vi behandler kun søknader sendt via vårt elektroniske rekrutteringssystem og alle dokumenter må lastes opp for at din søknad skal behandles.Dokumentene må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Oversettelser må være autorisert og du må påregne å fremvise originaler ved et eventuelt intervju.OsloMet gjennomfører kontroll av dokumenter, slik at du som kandidat skal få en reell evaluering og rettferdig konkurranse. Ufullstendige søknader vil ikke bli tatt til vurdering.
For aktuelle stillinger gjennomfører OsloMet bakgrunnssjekk av søkere i samarbeid med en ekstern leverandør, for å verifisere opplysninger som fremgårav tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med kandidatens samtykke, og ansettelse i disse stillingene forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette.
Ønsker du nærmere informasjon om stillingen kan du kontakte:
Førsteamanuensis Baifan Zhou, email: [email protected]
Gruppeleder Ellen Sethov, email: [email protected]
For spørsmål av administrativ karakter kontakt [email protected]

Informasjon til deg som søker
Inkludering og mangfold styrker vår evne til å løse OsloMets samfunnsoppdrag. Derfor ønsker vi medarbeidere med ulike kompetanser, livserfaringer og perspektiver velkommen. Vi arbeider kontinuerlig for å være en inkluderende arbeidsplass, og gjennom dialog tilrettelegger vi for medarbeidere som har behov for det.
Opplysninger om deg som søker kan publiseres på den offentlige søkerlisten selv om har bedt om at søknaden behandles konfidensielt. Hvis det skjer, vil du bli varslet om det før publiseringen.
Ansettelsen blir gjennomført etter prinsippene i statsansatteloven og lovverk som regulerer eksport av kunnskap, teknologi og tjenester. Søkere som er i konflikt med dette regelverket vil ikke anses kvalifisert for stillingen.
OsloMet er Charter & Code -sertifisert av EU-kommisjonen med rett til å bruke logoen HR Excellence in Research (HRS4R) og er medlem i nettverket EURAXESS , som bidrar til gode arbeidsvilkår for mobile forskere.
OsloMet har sluttet seg til prinsippene og forpliktet institusjonen til å følge anbefalingene i DORA-erklæringen (sfdora.org) (The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment).
Besøk OsloMet på LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram
Om oss
OsloMet - storbyuniversitetet er Norges tredje største universitet med 23 000 studenter og over 2600 ansatte. Vi har campus i Oslo Sentrum og på Romerike. OsloMet leverer forskning og utdanning med høy relevans for arbeidslivet, velferdsstaten og storbyregionen.
I over 200 år har OsloMet – storbyuniversitetet bidratt til å bygge kunnskap og kompetanse for det norske velferdssamfunnet. I dag er OsloMet et moderne og urbant universitet som er kjent for sine store og solide fagmiljøer innenfor lærerutdanning, helse- og sosialfag, samfunnsforskning, design og teknologifag.
Fakultet for teknologi, kunst og design (TKD) utgjør et sterkt og mangfoldig faglig miljø med tydelig internasjonalt preg. Arbeidet gjøres i en profesjonell organisasjon som er ledende i å ta i bruk ny teknologi og nye løsninger, og er langt fremme på tverrfaglig og eksternt samarbeid. Fakultet for teknologi, kunst og design er i sterk vekst og vi rekrutterer høyt kvalifiserte medarbeidere fra hele verden.
Fakultet TKD har om lag 4 000 studenter og 400 ansatte, og holder til i Pilestredet i Oslo sentrum og på Kjeller utenfor Lillestrøm. Fakultetet utfører forskning og tilbyr utdanning på bachelor-, master- og doktorgradsnivå innen teknologi, kunst og design.

ap:254367.body:
We are looking for a research assistant in biomedicine for a temporary position in the research environment Cardiovascular Research Centre (CVRC) at the Department of Medical Sciences.
Background
The Cardiovascular Research Centre (CVRC) is an active research environment that conducts translational research in the cardiovascular field at Örebro University and Örebro University Hospital/Region Örebro County. The environment is a platform that brings together research on molecular vascular biology, systemic inflammation in cardiovascular diseases and thrombosis research in close collaboration with local, national and international academic actors and private companies in the field. The goal of the research is to identify new mechanisms, risk factors and treatment principles for better and more effective diagnosis, treatment and prevention of cardiovascular and blood diseases.
The project is part of an established 4-year Knowledge Foundation-funded project on new drug candidates for cardiovascular disease and breast cancer.
Duties and responsibilities
The duties include work with cell and molecular biology studies of regulatory pathways that affect inflammation and immune response in vascular cells and platelets in collaboration with academic partners and companies. Work with leukocytes or cell cultures with leukocyte-like cancer cells may also be considered.
In addition to research, some teaching/supervision comprising a maximum of 20% within the framework of the department's education can also be carried out, which is why merits from teaching are also meritorious.
You should be able to work independently and we are looking for someone who is meticulous, aware of goals and quality standards and who can work quality-consciously and responsibly. Great emphasis is placed on your personal qualities where good collaboration skills with a flexible approach are of great importance.
Experience from studies at an advanced level or higher is a merit.
Qualifications
As a general assessment basis, the applicant must be able to demonstrate such personal qualities as are required to perform the duties described above. A Bachelor's degree in biomedicine or related fields is a requirement.
You should have documented practical experience in cell biology molecular biology techniques, such as cell culture, isolation of nucleic acids, real-time PCR and Western blotting. Experience in quantitative, immunological techniques, such as ELISA, is also important. The researcher is expected to be able to perform statistical calculations and independently summarize and present scientific data in publications and other types of scientific presentations. Theoretical and practical knowledge in inflammation in cardiovascular diseases is desirable. Good oral and written communication skills in English are a requirement.
Information
The employment is 100% from 2027-01-18 to 2027-07-18, with the possibility of extension. Örebro University applies individual salary setting.
For further information about the position, please contact Head of Unit Simon Athlin 070-265 88 80, e-mail: [email protected] and Karin H Franzén 019-30 14 08, e-mail: [email protected] .
Application
You make your application on our website by clicking on the "Apply" button.
A complete application must include the following electronic documents:
A cover letter
CV with relevant description of overall competence
Copies of relevant grades/certificates proving eligibility and requirements
Degree project
Any scientific publications

Only documents written in Swedish, English, Norwegian and Danish can be assessed. More information for applicants can be found on our Job vacancies page:  https://www.oru.se/jobba-hos-oss/lediga-jobb/information-for-dig-som-sokande-och-sakkunnig/
The last day to apply is 2026-12-01. Welcome with your application!
After the application deadline, no supplementary information can be made electronically. We do not ask for contact with advertisers and staffing agencies in the recruitment process.
According to the National Archives' regulations, we must archive a batch of application documents excluding publications for two years after the appointment decision has gained legal force.

Vi söker en forskningsassistent i biomedicin för tidsbegränsad anställning i forskningsmiljön Cardiovascular Research Centre (CVRC) vid Institutionen för medicinska vetenskaper.
Bakgrund
Cardiovascular Research Centre (CVRC) är en aktiv forskningsmiljö som bedriver translationell forskning inom det kardiovaskulära området vid Örebro Universitet och Universitetssjukhuset i Örebro/Region Örebro Län. Miljön är en plattform som samlar forskning kring molekylär kärlbiologi, systemisk inflammation vid kardiovaskulära sjukdomar och trombosforskning i nära samarbete med lokala, nationella och internationella akademiska aktörer och privata företag inom området. Målet för forskningen är att identifiera nya mekanismer, riskfaktorer och behandlingsprinciper för bättre och effektivare diagnos, behandling och prevention av hjärt-kärl och blodsjukdomar.
Projektet är en del av ett etablerat 4-årigt KK-stiftelsefinansierat projekt om nya läkemedelskandidater mot hjärt-kärlsjukdom och bröstcancer.
Arbetsuppgifter
I arbetsuppgifterna ingår bland annat arbete med cell- och molekylärbiologiska studier av regleringsvägar som påverkar inflammation och immunrespons i vaskulära celler och trombocyter i samarbete med akademiska partners och företag. Arbete med leukocyter eller cellkulturer med leukocyt-liknande cancerceller kan också komma i fråga.
Utöver forskning kan även viss undervisning/handledning omfattande maximalt 20% inom ramen för institutionens utbildningar genomföras, varför meriter från undervisning också är meriterande.
Du skall kunna arbeta självständigt och vi söker dig som är noggrann, medveten om mål och kvalitetsstandard och som kan arbeta kvalitetsmedvetet och ansvarstagande. Stor vikt läggs vid dina personliga egenskaper där god samarbetsförmåga med ett flexibelt förhållningssätt är av stor vikt.
Erfarenhet från studier på avancerad nivå eller högre är meriterande.
Kvalifikationer
Som allmän bedömningsgrund gäller att den sökande kan uppvisa sådana personliga egenskaper som krävs för att fullgöra de aktuella arbetsuppgifterna som beskrivs ovan. Kandidatexamen i biomedicin eller näraliggande områden är ett krav.
Du ska ha dokumenterad praktisk erfarenhet av cellbiologiska molekylärbiologiska tekniker, så som cellodling, isolering av nukleinsyror, realtids-PCR och Western blotting. Även erfarenhet av kvantitativa, immunologiska tekniker, såsom ELISA, är av vikt. Forskaren förväntas kunna genomföra statistiska beräkningar och självständigt sammanfatta och presentera vetenskapliga data i publikationer och andra typer av vetenskapliga presentationer. Teoretisk och praktisk kunskap inom inflammation vid kardiovaskulära sjukdomar är önskvärt. God muntlig och skriftlig kommunikationsförmåga på engelska är ett krav.
Information
Anställningen är 100 % från 2027-01-18 till 2027-07-18, med eventuell möjlighet till förlängning. Örebro universitet tillämpar individuell lönesättning.
Närmare upplysningar om anställningen lämnas av Enhetschef Simon Athlin 070-265 88 80 e-post: [email protected] samt Karin H Franzén 019-30 14 08, e-post: [email protected] .
Ansökan
Du gör din ansökan på vår hemsida genom att klicka på knappen "Ansök".
En komplett ansökan ska innehålla följande elektroniska dokument:
Ett personligt brev

Kopior av relevanta betyg/intyg som styrker behörighet och krav
Examensarbete
Eventuella vetenskapliga publikationer

Endast handlingar skrivna på svenska, engelska, norska och danska kan bedömas. Mer information för dig som sökande hittar du på vår Lediga-jobb-sida:  https://www.oru.se/jobba-hos-oss/lediga-jobb/information-for-dig-som-sokande-och-sakkunnig/

ap:254371.body:
About the position
A fixed-term 100 % position as a PhD Research Fellow in Civil and Structural Engineering, is available at the University of Agder, Faculty of Engineering and Science . The position is affiliated with the Department of Engineering Sciences and is offered for a period of three years. The position is located at Campus Grimstad. The starting date is agreed with the Faculty.
The Department of Engineering Sciences has more than 120 employees in scientific positions and more than 1500 students at all levels. A wide range of research activities is conducted across the department’s research groups: Mechatronics, Renewable Energy, Civil Engineering, and Industrial Economy. Interdisciplinary projects within the department or with other research groups are also welcome.
This position will be affiliated with the Civil Engineering section. The department has extensive international collaboration and works closely with industrial partners and public-sector organisations in the region. These collaborations provide valuable opportunities for both teaching and research. Our partners contribute assignments, expertise and resources.
Project background
The position is associated with a recently awarded EU project, HelioSea. The project aims to develop innovative interconnected floating solar arrays for offshore sites. The project will assess innovative concepts under various environmental conditions, investigate systems integration and the co-location of different marine renewable energy devices, and conduct techno-economic analyses.
Responsibilities
The PhD research fellow will conduct research on the design and analysis of multibody floating solar systems under offshore environmental conditions. Such systems are typically characterised by lightweight floats with mechanical connectors and mooring systems.
The work will involve analytical modelling and numerical analysis of multibody hydrodynamics. Structural analysis may also be included, depending on the research focus. The candidate is expected to work collaboratively in an international research environment.
The research will include preparing and submitting research reports, publishing high-quality scientific articles, and participating in dissemination activities at the European level.
Required qualifications
Applicants must hold a master’s degree in Marine Technology, Mechanical Engineering, Civil Engineering, or a closely related field. Applicants must have their master’s thesis approved by the application deadline.
Applicants are expected to have in-depth knowledge of several of the following subjects:
Marine hydrodynamics
Structural Dynamics
Physics-based simulations of marine structures
Stochastic analysis methods
Design optimization

As a general rule, the following should normally apply:
The average grade for courses included in the bachelor's degree (or equivalent) should be C (or equivalent) or higher.
The average grade for all courses (including the dissertation) in the master’s degree should be B (or equivalent) or higher. The master's dissertation (or equivalent) should have the grade B (or equivalent) or higher.
Competence in English is a requirement for all applicants to the PhD programme. International candidates that are not exempt from the English language requirements pursuant to the guidelines of the Norwegian Agency for Quality Assurance in Education (NOKUT), must document this through one of the following tests with the stated results or better:  TOEFL - Test of English as a Foreign Language with a minimum score of 600 for the Paperbased Test (PBT), or 92 for the Internetbased Test (iBT)
IELTS - International English Language Testing System, with the result of 6.5

Criteria for positions as PhD Research Fellow (in Norwegian).
Desired qualifications
Research experience and a record of scientific publications
Strong analytical and programming skills
Research or work experience related to offshore structures

Personal qualities
The assessment will place emphasis on personal suitability, teamwork skills and relevant practical experience. Research fellows are expected to contribute to the active research community at the University. The position requires the ability to work independently towards defined goals, maintain focus and pay attention to detail.

We offer
Professional development in a large, exciting and socially important organisation
A positive, inclusive and diverse working environment
Modern facilities and comprehensive welfare schemes
Membership in the  Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund

More about  working at UiA .
The position is remunerated according to the State Salary Scale, salary plan 17.515, code 1017 PhD Research Fellow, NOK 550 800 gross salary per year. A compulsory pension contribution to the Norwegian Public Service Pension Fund will be deducted from the salary according to current statutory provisions.
General information
UiA is an open and inclusive university. We believe that diversity enriches the workplace and makes us better. We, therefore, encourage qualified candidates to apply for the position independent of gender, age, cultural background, disability or an incomplete CV.
Women are strongly encouraged to apply for the position.
The successful applicant will have rights and obligations in accordance with the current regulations for the position, and organisational changes and changes in the duties and responsibilities of the position must be expected. The engagement is to be made in accordance with the regulations in force concerning the acts relating to  Control of Export of Strategic Goods, Services and Technology .
Appointment is made by the University of Agder’s Appointments Committee for Teaching and Research Positions. A  background check  may be conducted to verify information that appears in available documents. Background checks are always done with the applicant's consent, and employment in the position requires an approved background check. Relevant applicants will receive further information.
Short-listed applicants will be invited for interview. With the applicant’s permission, UiA will also conduct a reference check before appointment. Read more about the  employment process .
In accordance with the Freedom of Information Act § 25 (2), applicants may request that they are not identified in the open list of applicants. The University, however, reserves the right to publish the names of applicants. Applicants will be advised of the University’s intention to exercise this right.
Application
Applications, including documentation of education and experience (such as diplomas and certificates), must be submitted electronically via the link “ Apply for this job ”.
The following documentation must be uploaded electronically:
Academic transcripts showing grades from bachelor’s and master’s degree programmes
A CV detailing education and work experience
Up to 10 academic articles or R&D projects that the candidate wishes to emphasise in the assessment process
A brief project description related to the research topic described above.  (maximum two pages) The project description should outline proposed research questions, methods and relevance to floating solar arrays.

The applicant is fully responsible for submitting complete digital documentation by the application deadline. All documentation must be available in a Scandinavian language or English.
Application deadline: 0 1.12.26.

ap:254377.body:
The Department of Biological and Environmental Science  is seeking to recruit a Doctoral Researcher in Evolutionary Biology  starting 4 January 2027, or as soon as possible after that for a fixed-term of three years. The fixed-term position is for completing doctoral studies.
The interactions between different evolutionary forces, including natural and sexual selection, are key to understanding the evolution of biological diversity over space and time. To increase understanding of the dynamic interplay between natural and sexual selection in driving diversification of natural populations at contemporary timescales, we are looking for a PhD candidate with a keen interest in evolutionary questions. The candidate will have freedom to develop their research in this broader context, with the freshwater isopod  Asellus aquaticus –  an emergent model - as an empirical model system. The species is sexually dimorphic, has extended maternal care and hosts a variable microbiome, providing ample opportunities to investigate different sources of variation in fitness. For candidates with theoretical background in evolutionary biology/ecology, empirical work can be combined with conceptual work.
The Doctoral Researcher will join an international academic community at the Department of Biological and Environmental Science , which houses broad expertise in evolutionary theory, ecological and environmental research as well as molecular, experimental and digital tools.
Who should apply
The main focus of the PhD researcher will be in research, but the candidate is expected also to contribute to some undergraduate student mentoring and teaching as part of their doctoral training. Some basic funding is available to cover research costs. The candidate is expected to apply for supplemental funding in case of major research costs (depending on the type of methods of research the candidate is interested in pursuing).
Who are we looking for
The candidate is expected to have a strong basis in evolutionary biology/evolutionary ecology
The ideal candidate should have some experience in experimental research, as well as strong statistical skills.
The candidate should be independent and work well in a team, as well as be willing to engage in a thriving scientific community.

The tasks of a Doctoral Researcher focus on research aiming at the completion of a doctoral thesis, doctoral studies, assisting teaching tasks, and other related tasks to these. The duties, qualification requirements, and the language skills of Doctoral Researchers are stipulated by  the University of Jyväskylä Regulations and language skills guidelines  (Doctoral Students). A good command of English is required. A trial period of six months will be used in the beginning of the employment.
The eligible candidate has, or is about to obtain, a suitable Master's degree. In addition, the Doctoral Researcher must have a permission for post-graduate studies at the University of Jyväskylä. After selection, the selected person must apply for postgraduate study rights through  a separate application  procedure from the Faculty of Mathematics and Science.
What we offer
Come to Jyväskylä, Finland, and join our vibrant and inspiring community!
At the University of Jyväskylä, you will be a valued member of our community with a unique opportunity to contribute to international research. You will become part of our international and multidisciplinary community that prioritizes the wellbeing of each individual. Our lively campus provides excellent opportunities for maintaining an active and healthy lifestyle.
Finland, named the world’s happiest country for consecutive years since 2018, offers a high standard of living with free education (also in English), affordable childcare, generous family benefits, and comprehensive healthcare. Work–life balance is highly valued in Finland, and employees enjoy four to six weeks of annual holiday. Jyväskylä is located in central Finland, just three hours by train from the capital Helsinki. Part of the Finnish Lakeland, the city offers easy access to nature and a range of outdoor, sports and exercise activities. As a major centre of education with a large student population, it also features a vibrant cultural scene. For more information about the University of Jyväskylä, the city of Jyväskylä, and living in Finland, see the  University's International Staff Guide .
Salaries are based on job demands and employees’ performance following the Finnish University Salary System. The salary for a Doctoral Researcher is determined based on the task-specific demand level 2–4 for teaching and research staff. The starting salary will be approximately EUR 2500 per month (gross income). A holiday bonus is paid to all employees. With progress of thesis work, the salary will be revised in accordance with the Collective Agreement of Finnish Education Employers. If you are relocating from abroad, we will support your move to Jyväskylä and Finland.
We offer good working conditions for researchers and promote the principles of HR Excellence in Research,  HRS4R . The Human Resources Strategy for Researchers (HRS4R) is based on the values of the European Charter for Researchers & The Code of Conduct for the Recruitment of Researchers (Charter & Code). JYU is committed to fairness, consistency and transparency in selection decisions, and undertakes  the recommendations for the responsible evaluation of a researcher in Finland . JYU has signed  the DORA Declaration . By signing the agreement, JYU is committed to complying with the  CoARA principles.
How to apply?
The application documents that should be included in English and in PDF format:
A Curriculum vitae, composed according to good scientific practice and considering the template for researcher´s curriculum vitae by  The Finnish Advisory Board on Research Integrity .
A short and informal motivation/cover letter (max 2 pages), including your research interests, career goals and previous experience and merits in relation to the qualifications for this position.
Degree certificate (highest degree).

We look forward to receiving your application in our recruitment system by  15 November 2026.
For further information, please write to Associate Professor Jussi Lehtonen, [email protected] and Professor Katja Räsänen,  [email protected]  who will be the supervisors of the PhD student.
Our application process is transparent, professional and international. We communicate openly with the applicants throughout the recruitment process. We value equality and diversity in our work community and encourage qualified applicants to apply for this position.

Department of Biological and Environmental Science

Good science, good life! The Department of Biological and Environmental Science is an international and multidisciplinary research community conducting impactful research to improve understanding of biodiversity, the environment and biological systems, from the molecular and cellular levels to biological communities and ecosystems. Our research strengths include evolutionary biology, natural resources and the environment, and biological nanoscience. We work closely with partners in academia, the public sector, and industry. Our research is supported by high-quality, versatile infrastructure on the Ylistönrinne campus, including the modern laboratories and experimental facilities in the Ambiotica building and in the Nanoscience Center. Field and laboratory teaching are central to our curriculum. By combining theory with practical experience, we prepare students to address real-world challenges. The  Konnevesi research station  provides opportunities for large scale ecologically relevant experiments and field studies, as well as a location for workshops and field courses in a natural setting. The department has approximately 200 staff members and 450 students. Together, they form an international and supportive community that brings together research, education and societal impact.

Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitos hakee väitöskirjatutkijaa, evoluutiobiologia , 4.1.2027   alkaen tai mahdollisimman pian sen jälkeen kolmen vuoden määräajaksi. Määräaikaisuuden syy on jatkokoulutus tohtoriksi.
Väitöskirjatutkija liittyy kansainväliseen tutkijayhteisöön bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitoksella, jolla on laajaa asiantuntemusta evoluutioteoriasta, ekologisesta ja ympäristötutkimuksesta sekä molekyyli-, kokeellisista ja digitaalisista työkaluista. Katso tarkemmat tiedot englanninkielisestä hakuilmoituksesta .
Etsimämme henkilö
Väitöskirjatutkijan tehtävät painottuvat väitöskirjaan tähtäävään tutkimukseen, jatkokoulutukseen, avustaviin opetustehtäviin sekä niihin liittyviin muihin tehtäviin. Väitöskirjatutkijan tehtävistä, kelpoisuusvaatimuksista ja kielitaidosta määrätään  yliopiston johtosäännössä ja kielitaito ohjeistuksissa  (tohtorikoulutettava). Tehtävissä edellytetään hyvää englannin kielen suullista ja kirjallista taitoa jatko-opinto-oikeudelle asetettujen vaatimusten mukaisesti. Tehtävää täytettäessä käytetään kuuden kuukauden koeaikaa.
Väitöskirjatutkijalta edellytetään ylempi korkeakoulututkinto ja jatkotutkinnon opiskeluoikeus Jyväskylän yliopistoon. Mikäli tehtävään valitulla hakijalla ei ole ennestään jatko-opinto-oikeutta, sitä on haettava hakuajat huomioiden  erillisellä hakemuksella  Matemaattis-luonnontieteellisestä tiedekunnasta. Tehtävää voivat hakea myös opintojen loppuvaiheessa olevat opiskelijat, joiden maisterin tutkinto on hakuvaiheessa vielä kesken.
Tarjoamme
Tule osaksi innostavaa ja lämminhenkistä yhteisöämme!
Jyväskylän yliopistossa olet arvostettu yliopistoyhteisön jäsen. Teemme merkityksellistä työtä ja vaalimme sivistystä. Monitieteisessä yliopistossamme saat mahdollisuuden vaikuttaa kansainväliseen tutkimukseen ja laadukkaaseen akateemiseen koulutukseen. Meille jokaisen hyvinvointi on tärkeää, ja tarjoamme kampuksella sekä sen läheisyydessä erinomaiset puitteet aktiiviseen ja hyvinvoivaan elämäntapaan.
Palkkaus perustuu tehtävien vaativuuteen ja henkilökohtaiseen työstä suoriutumiseen yliopistojen palkkausjärjestelmän mukaisesti. Väitöskirjatutkijan tehtäväkohtainen palkanosa määräytyy opetus- ja tutkimushenkilöstön tehtävien vaativuustason 2–4 mukaan. Palkkasi työsuhteen alussa on noin 2500 euroa kuukaudessa. Väitöskirjatyön edistyessä palkkaa tarkistetaan yliopistojen työehtosopimuksen mukaisesti.
Tarjoamme hyvät työolosuhteet tutkijoille ja noudatamme Tutkijanuran ja -aseman kehittämisen ( HRS4R ) periaatteita. Human Resources Strategy for Researchers (HRS4R) -työ perustuu Euroopan komission julkaisemaan Tutkijoiden eurooppalaisen peruskirjan arvoihin ja säännöstöön tutkijoiden työhönotosta (englanninkielinen lyhenne Charter & Code). Jyväskylän yliopisto on sitoutunut tasapuolisuuteen, johdonmukaisuuteen ja läpinäkyvyyteen valintapäätöksissä ja noudattaa vastuullisen tutkijanarvioinnin kansallisia suosituksia . Jyväskylän yliopisto on sitoutunut vastuullisen tutkijanarvioinnin DORA-julistukseen ja noudattamaan CoARA -periaatteita.
Hakeminen
Hakemuksiin tulee liittää pdf-muodossa:
Ansioluettelo (CV), joka laaditaan hyvää tieteellistä käytäntöä noudattaen sekä ottaen huomioon mahdollisuuksien mukaan ansioluettelomalli (ks.  TENK:n ohje ).
Lyhyt vapaamuotoinen hakemuskirje (enintään 2 sivua) sisältäen tutkimusintressisi, uratavoitteesi ja aiemman kokemuksesi sekä ansiosi suhteessa tämän tehtävän pätevyyteen.
Tutkintotodistus (korkein tutkinto).

Odotamme hakemustasi rekrytointijärjestelmäämme viimeistään 15.11.2026 .
Lisätietoja antavat apulaisprofessori Jussi Lehtonen, [email protected] ja professori Katja Räsänen, [email protected] , jotka toimivat tohtoriopiskelijan ohjaajina.
Hakemusprosessimme on läpinäkyvä, ammattimainen ja kansainvälinen. Tiedotamme hakijoita avoimesti prosessin edistymisestä sen eri vaiheissa. Arvostamme tasa-arvoa ja monimuotoisuutta työyhteisössämme ja kannustamme kelpoisuuden täyttäviä hakijoita hakemaan tehtäviä.

Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitos

Hyvää tiedettä, hyvää elämää! Bio- ja ympäristötieteiden laitos on kansainvälinen ja monitieteinen tutkimusyhteisö, jossa tehdään vaikuttavaa tutkimusta luonnon monimuotoisuuden, ympäristön ja biologisten systeemien ymmärtämiseksi molekyyli- ja solutasolta aina eliöyhteisöihin ja ekosysteemeihin. Tutkimuksen vahvuusalueisiin kuuluvat evoluutiobiologia, luonnonvarojen ja ympäristön tutkimus sekä biologinen nanotiede, ja työtä tehdään tiiviissä yhteistyössä akateemisten, julkisen sektorin ja yrityskumppaneiden kanssa. Tutkimusta tukevat korkeatasoiset ja monipuoliset infrastruktuurit Ylistönrinteen kampuksella, kuten Ambiotica-rakennuksen modernit laboratorio- ja koetilat sekä Nanotiedekeskuksen yhteydessä toimivat huipputason tutkimuslaitteistot. Kenttä- ja laboratorio-opetus ovat keskeinen osa opetustamme. Opetuksemme yhdistää teorian käytännön kokemuksiin ja valmistaa opiskelijat suoraan todellisen maailman haasteisiin.  Konneveden tutkimusasema tarjoaa mahdollisuuksia laajamittaisiin, ekologisesti merkityksellisiin kokeisiin ja kenttätutkimuksiin sekä tilat työpajoille ja kenttäkursseille luonnonkauniissa ympäristössä. Laitoksella työskentelee noin 200 asiantuntijaa ja opiskelee noin 450 opiskelijaa kansainvälisessä ja kannustavassa ilmapiirissä, jossa yhdistyvät tutkimus, opetus ja yhteiskunnallinen vaikuttavuus.

ap:254380.body:
Introduction
Are you inspired to push the limits of polymeric materials for lighter and smarter defense platforms? Join us to develop a new generation of 3D-printed composite panels that shield electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact.

Job Description
We are offering 2 PhD positions within project VALOR, an ambitious, interdisciplinary collaboration between academia, industry and government partners. The project aims to develop a new generation of lightweight composite panels that both shield sensitive electronics from electromagnetic threats and withstand impact events, helping to make defense platforms safer and more resilient.
Naval ships, drones and military vehicles increasingly depend on electronic radar, communication and navigation systems that must be protected against electromagnetic interference and radar detection . Today, this is mostly done with metals, which block practically all wave power with only a thin layer. However, they add weight, corrode, and reflect electromagnetic waves, making platforms easier to detect. Project VALOR tackles this challenge by merging two fields that have so far been developed separately: absorption-based electromagnetic shielding and impact-resistant sandwich structures . By combining 3D-printed architected nanocomposite materials with predictive modelling into one integrated design strategy, the project will construct a design framework for panels that are able to both carry loads and absorb electromagnetic waves, with a performance that can be tailored to specific (defense) applications.
Your role
We are recruiting two PhD candidates who will work as a team throughout the project, i.e. from material screening to design and testing of larger scale panel demonstrators. Both candidates will conduct a combination of experimental and numerical work and collaborate closely with industrial partners within the consortium. More specifically:
PhD 1 focuses on mechanics and manufacturing : 3D printing nanocomposite lattice materials, fabricating composite facesheets, conducting mechanical tests, constructing and validating mechanical finite element models.

PhD 2 focuses on electromagnetic testing and design : formulating polymer nanocomposite materials and characterizing their electromagnetic behaviour, designing and testing absorbing architected nanocomposite structures, conducting electromagnetic shielding simulations.

Your team and network
You will join the Processing and Performance of Materials section in the Department of Mechanical Engineering at TU/e. The group has around 20 PhD and post-doctoral researchers working on how processing, structure and properties connect in polymers and polymer-based composite materials. The group is known for its integrated experimental-numerical approach to tailor the performance of these materials. You will have access to state-of-the-art computational facilities and laboratories dedicated to rheology, polymer processing (incl. additive manufacturing) and mechanical testing. You will be supervised by Frederik Van Loock (project leader), Ruth Cardinaels and Tom Engels.

Job Requirements
PhD 1 – Mechanics and manufacturing
We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications:
A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Mechanical Engineering with a specialization in mechanics of materials / solid mechanics .
A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling.
Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners.
A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature.
Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level).
Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: mechanical characterization of polymer-based materials, finite element simulations of mechanical behaviour of polymer-based materials, 3D printing of polymers, polymer and composite processing .

PhD 2 – Electromagnetic testing and design

We are looking for a highly motivated and ambitious researcher with the following qualifications:
A master’s degree (or equivalent) with excellent grades in Engineering (Mechanical or Electrical), Materials Science or Applied Physics, with a specialization in materials .
A strong interest in combining experimental work with numerical modelling.
Enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary team and with industrial and defense partners.
A research-oriented mindset: critical thinking is your second nature.
Good communication skills and fluency in English, both spoken and written (C1 level).
Experience with one or more of the following areas is a plus: electromagnetic characterization of polymer-based materials (e.g. vector network analysis, waveguide measurements), electromagnetic simulations (e.g. full-wave finite element modelling), 3D printing and processing of polymers.

Why Join?
Work within the multidisciplinary Processing and Performance of Materials group
Work at the forefront of advanced materials research in collaboration with industry leaders.
Combine material formulation, characterization, and computation in a multidisciplinary team.
Get trained to use cutting-edge experimental and numerical simulation facilities.
Contribute to the development of advanced multi-functional and 3D printed composite panels that make defense platforms more safe and resilient.
Work in an international working environment and present your work at international conferences.

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.

Introduction
Are you interested in the communication networks behind modern AI systems? Would you like to combine mathematical modeling with experiments on programmable network hardware to make AI infrastructure faster and more energy-efficient? In this PhD project, you will develop models and orchestration methods for the networks that connect GPUs during large language model inference. Are you our next PhD candidate in high-performance AI networking?

Job Description
Your research challenge
Large language models rely on powerful computing infrastructure to generate responses. When inference is distributed across multiple GPUs, these devices must continuously exchange intermediate results. Network congestion and communication overhead can therefore limit performance and increase energy consumption, even when substantial computing resources are available.
In the project Communication-Optimized Inference in Large Language Models (COIL) , you will investigate how analytical network models can support the design and operation of AI clusters. The project combines network performance modeling, optimization, and experimental research, giving you the opportunity to connect mathematical foundations with practical challenges in AI infrastructure.
You will develop fast, composable analytical models using Network Calculus, a mathematical framework for analyzing communication networks. These models will capture interactions between inference traffic, network architecture, and mechanisms such as flow control and congestion feedback. They will provide bounds on communication latency and buffer requirements, complemented by energy estimates based on measurement-calibrated power models.
Building on these models, you will explore how architectural choices—including network topology, link bandwidth, and parallelization strategies—affect performance and energy consumption. You will develop tools that help cluster designers evaluate promising configurations efficiently.
You will also investigate how the models can guide runtime decisions, such as workload placement, prioritization, routing, or resource reservation. A focused prototype will demonstrate how model-informed decisions can improve the operation of an existing network.
Experimental validation will be an integral part of your research. You will use measurements from AI infrastructure and conduct reproducible experiments on programmable networking testbeds. Technologies of interest include Ethernet-based AI networks, emerging Ultra Ethernet mechanisms, P4-programmable switches, and SmartNICs. Finally, you will evaluate the results from the testbeds on real AI infrastructure in collaboration with our partner SURF .
Through this combination of theory, software development, and experimentation, you will contribute to more responsive and energy-efficient AI infrastructure. The project also offers opportunities to share your findings with networking standardization communities and to release research tools and experimental results openly.
An interdisciplinary and international environment
You will conduct your research under the main supervision of Prof. Lisa Maile who leads the Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) lab. NoMaD is part of the Electronic Systems group in the Department of Electrical Engineering at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your supervision will also include partners from the Advanced Models by Open Research and Engineering (AMOR/e) Lab of Computer Science and the Model-Based Design Lab from Electrical Engineering.
The position is funded through the EuroTech programme, which promotes research collaboration between leading technical universities across Europe. As part of this project, you will collaborate closely with Prof. Georg Carle and his research group on Network Architectures and Services at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) . As part of this collaboration, you will spend six-month in Munich with the group at TUM , where you will gain hands-on experience with programmable network hardware and reproducible experimental infrastructure.

Job Requirements
Essential qualifications
A master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Applied Mathematics, or a closely related field.
A strong mathematical background, demonstrated by excellent performance in mathematically rigorous courses, additional mathematics electives, a mathematics minor or specialization, or substantial mathematical work in a thesis or research project.
Good programming skills and an interest in developing research software and experimental tools.
Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, initiative, and creativity.
An interest in high-performance networking and AI infrastructure, and motivation to apply mathematical methods to computer networks and distributed systems.
A strong team spirit and enthusiasm for working in an international, collaborative, and socially engaging environment.
Excellent oral and written communication skills in English.
Willingness to spend at least six months at the Technical University of Munich (TUM) as part of the project.

Desirable qualifications
A solid foundation in computer networks or distributed systems.
Experience with Network Calculus, network simulation, mathematical optimization, or GPU communication.
Experience with programmable networking technologies, such as P4 or SmartNICs.

Selection procedure
Interviews and a scientific presentation will be part of the selection procedure.

A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

The Network Modeling and Design (NoMaD) Lab develops mathematical models, tools, and protocols for reliable and efficient communication networks. Its research connects formal analysis with practical implementation, covering technologies such as Time-Sensitive Networking, Ultra Ethernet, and beyond-5G networks. Applications range from connected vehicles and industrial automation to large-scale AI infrastructure. By combining analytical methods with simulation and hardware experiments, the lab translates theoretical insights into practical network designs and resource-management solutions.
NoMaD is part of the ES group , which develops methods for designing electronic, embedded, and cyber-physical systems with predictable performance, timing, reliability, and energy consumption. With about 12 full-time and 5 part-time professors and ~45 post-docs, PhDs, and EngD students, the group’s expertise spans model-driven engineering, system architectures, software, and digital circuits. This provides an interdisciplinary environment for your research, connecting network modeling and optimization with broader challenges in computing and system design.
The mission of the Department of Electrical Engineering is to acquire, share and transfer knowledge and understanding in the whole field of Electrical Engineering through education, research and valorization. We work towards a ‘Smart Sustainable Society’, a ‘Connected World’, and a healthy humanity (‘Care & Cure’). Activities share an application-oriented character, a high degree of complexity and a large synergy between multiple facets of the field.

Research is carried out into the applications of electromagnetic phenomena in all forms of energy conversion, telecommunication and electrical signal processing. Existing and new electrical components and systems are analyzed, designed and built. The department is innovative and has international ambitions and partnerships. The result is a challenging and inspiring setting in which socially relevant issues are addressed.

The University of Eastern Finland is inviting applications for a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) position in the field of Finite Element Technology for Smooth Problems at the Department of Technical Physics on the Kuopio Campus. The position will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 January 2027 (or as agreed).
Please find more information below and submit your application by 16 November 2026.
Role and salary
We are seeking a motivated Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) to work on the development and application of advanced computational methods with a particular focus on finite element technologies for complex continuum and multiphysics problems. The research will combine methodological development, numerical implementation and applications to challenging problems in computational engineering. The research project will be supervised by Assistant Professor Adam Sky from the Department of Technical Physics at the University of Eastern Finland together with Dr. Michael Neunteufel from the Johann Radon Institute for Computational and Applied Mathematics (RICAM) in Linz, Austria.
As our new Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), your responsibilities will include the development, mathematical analysis and numerical implementation of finite element methods, as well as the preparation and publication of scientific results. The position may also include a limited amount of teaching-related duties (max. 5% of total working hours), such as developing exercise materials and supervising exercise sessions. The Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) will also be expected to participate in scientific exchange through conferences, research visits and collaboration with the participating research groups and institutes.
The main duty of the Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) is to conduct research for their doctoral dissertation and to complete postgraduate studies.
The position will be filled for a fixed term of three years as from 1 January 2027 (or as agreed). The position will be filled for a fixed term due to the Doctoral Researcher’s (PhD Student’s) own doctoral dissertation work and studies. A trial period is applied to all new members of the staff.
The salary of the position is determined in accordance with the salary system for Finnish universities. The salary comprises two components: a job-related salary element and a personal salary element. For a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), the job-related salary element is based on levels 2–4 of the job requirement level chart for teaching and research staff depending on the stage of the applicant’s doctoral research and postgraduate studies. The personal salary element is 6–50% of the job-related salary element. At the beginning of the employment, the total salary will be approximately EUR 2,710–2,845 /month.
Our requirements and expectations
We require you to
be eligible for postgraduate studies; i.e., to hold a Master’s degree in computational physics and engineering, mathematics, scientific computing, mechanical engineering or a related field, awarded by a university or by a university of applied sciences, or to have completed an applicable study programme abroad which in the awarding country gives eligibility for corresponding postgraduate education
meet the student admission criteria for the LUMETO doctoral programme ( Doctoral Programme in Science, Forestry and Technology, website )
have a good command of written and spoken English.

Students in the final stages of their Master’s degree may also apply, provided that they complete their degree and deliver a copy of their degree certificate to the faculty by 30 November 2026.
Applicants who do not yet have the right to pursue postgraduate studies at the University of Eastern Finland are not required to apply for study rights at the application stage. If the applicant is selected for the position and applies for postgraduate study rights, the selection will be conditional until the right to pursue postgraduate studies in the faculty’s doctoral programme has been granted. The application for postgraduate study rights is submitted through the Studyinfo (Opintopolku) service.
Other requirements
a strong foundation in mathematics and continuum physics
experience in scientific programming, preferably in Python.

Experience in the following areas will be considered an advantage
finite element methods
tensor calculus
continuum mechanics
generalised continuum theories
scientific computing
programming in C++, C or Rust.

Your benefits
You will have access to the university’s staff benefits, including
the opportunity for flexible multi-location work
extensive occupational health care
a broad selection of staff training
staff discount on lunch in our campus restaurants, as well as on a range of other services
affordable sports services.

Please read more in the  Work at UEF section on our website .
You will have an opportunity to work in meaningful as part of our international, creative, participatory and inclusive academic community.
Enjoy your life in Finland! Known for its cleanliness, welfare know-how, modern technology and superb education system, Finland is an exotic and safe country to work in. Please visit the  Life in Finland section on our website  to learn more.
How to apply?
Submit your application by using our electronic application form no later than 16 November 2026 by 23:59 (midnight) Finnish time (UTC+2).
Please note that you must include the following appendices in your application
CV (Template for CV, TENK web page)
copies of your academic degree certificates / diplomas, and copies of certificates / diplomas relating to your language proficiency, if not indicated in the academic degree certificates/diplomas
a transcript of records
a motivation letter (max. 1 page) in which you describe your interest in the position, your background, as well as your career aspirations and your motivation for engaging in doctoral-level research
if available (not a pre-requisite), a list of publications ( Instructions, Research Council of Finland, website )
other documents to demonstrate your merits for the position.

If your degree certificate is not in English, Finnish, or Swedish, you must provide official English translations of your degree certificate documents. All translations must be issued by the awarding educational institution or an authorized translator. Each page of the official translation must bear the translator's stamp and/or signature. Official translations must be accurate translations of the original documents. Translations made by the applicants themselves will not be accepted.
Questions?
For further information on the position, please contact Assistant Professor Adam Sky, e-mail: [email protected] .
For further information on the application procedure, please contact HR Specialist Iiris Korhonen, e-mail: [email protected] , tel. +358 29 445 8161 or HR Specialist Noora Hämäläinen, e-mail: [email protected] , tel. +358 29 445 8302.

Role and salary
The demand for minerals required for energy transition and digitalisation is expanding mining faster than our ability to understand its impacts. MINE-THE-GAP (website) , funded by the European Research Council (ERC), combines satellite imagery, mining data reports, and AI to map mining activities and their impacts worldwide and provide the information needed for more transparent and sustainable mining. We are seeking three motivated Doctoral Researchers (PhD Students) to join the project, each leading their own thesis on mapping different aspects of mining. As part of the MINE-THE-GAP team, you will, as a Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student), have the opportunity to apply your data science and programming skills to a global sustainability challenge and to become an expert in handling large Earth observation datasets and scalable AI.
We offer three Doctoral Researcher (PhD Student) positions in a research group with strong international visibility. You will receive hands-on training in the processing of large Earth observation and spatial datasets, as well as in scalable AI methods, developing highly sought-after skills for careers in academia, industry, government, and non-governmental organizations. The position provides opportunities for international collaboration and research visits abroad through an extensive network of partner institutions, including the German Aerospace Center (DLR), GFZ Helmholtz Centre for Geosciences, Monash University Indonesia, and the University of Melbourne. You will benefit from close supervision, mentoring, and a supportive team environment, along with dedicated funding for conference participation, workshops, and scientific publications.

mining land use: semantic segmentation of satellite images to map mining areas (e.g., open pits, waste rock piles, tailings dams)
mining waste: predicting terrain height changes from radar and optical satellite image time series to estimate mining waste
minerals and commodities: image classification with multispectral and hyperspectral data to identify the minerals and commodities of mining sites.

Within your chosen research topic, you will build, train, and validate scalable deep learning and computer vision models using large, multi-modal Earth observation data (e.g., Sentinel-1 radar, Sentinel-2 multispectral, LiDAR, hyperspectral). You will work closely with the principal investigator, Victor Maus, postdoctoral researchers, and international collaborators, publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to open science.

ap:254389.body:
Are you excited to push the boundaries of artificial intelligence in nuclear technology? Join us as a doctoral student to explore the advanced frontier of AI-driven nuclear safeguards and enhance global nuclear safety and security.
About us
The Reactor Physics, Modelling and Safety group at Chalmers develops advanced methods for modelling, simulation, monitoring and safety analysis of current and next-generation nuclear reactors. Combining expertise in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear safeguards, diagnostic techniques and machine learning applied to nuclear technology, the group conducts both fundamental and applied research in collaboration with national and international partners across academia and industry. We are part of the Division of Subatomic, High Energy and Plasma Physics , at the Department of Physics and Astronomy , offering a dynamic and stimulating working environment.
About the research project
Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models are powerful tools for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. However, their architectural and optimization complexity renders them black boxes, posing a challenge when making critical decisions, such as classifying SNF as either consistent or inconsistent with declared information. In this doctoral research, you will investigate an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to enable transparency in ANN models and their predictions for SNF inspection, bridging high-performing machine learning with transparent nuclear verification.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or equivalent.
You have strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
You have background/experience in at least one of the following areas: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Explainable AI, Reactor Physics, Nuclear Safeguards.
You have a solid background in computational methods and strong programming skills (e.g., in Python).
You thrive in a collaborative environment and take responsibility for your work.
You have a strong analytical mindset and enjoy complex challenges.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
What you will do
Conduct doctoral research focused on exploring, testing, and evaluating an Explainable AI (XAI) framework for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection.
Integrate various XAI methods and study semantic layers to aggregate predictions into actionable explanations for safeguards inspectors.
Leverage XAI insights to guide ANN model architectures, optimize training strategies, and strengthen model robustness.
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate research results through peer-reviewed journal publications and conference presentations.
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Nuclear Engineering .
The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  November 23, 2026
For questions, please contact:
Paolo Vinai
Associate Professor
[email protected]
We look forward to your application!

ap:254392.body:
Doctoral Student in Environmental Bioengineering
The Environmental Microfluidics Group of Prof. Roman Stocker in the Institute of Environmental Engineering is seeking a dynamic and motivated doctoral student with an engineering background for a project on how bacterial chemotaxis accelerates plasmid transfer, including the spread of antibiotic resistance. The position is funded by a recently awarded SNSF grant, and the project is a joint effort with Prof. Jonasz Slomka at the University of Warsaw. This position will be based in the laboratory of Prof. Roman Stocker.

Project background
Bacterial conjugation, the contact-dependent transfer of plasmids between cells, speeds up bacterial evolution and is a major route for the spread of antibiotic resistance in the environment, which in turn poses a global health threat. Aquatic environments are full of microscale chemical hotspots, such as the nutrient-rich 'phycosphere' around phytoplankton and sinking marine particles, and chemotactic bacteria are known to find and accumulate rapidly at these locations. This project will test the hypothesis that this accumulation enhances plasmid spreading in the environment, contributing to a cutting-edge view of the role of antibiotic resistance in nature.

The project seeks to study when, where and how strongly this enhancement operates across different chemical hotspots, fluid flows and bacterial strains, and what it means for the spread of antibiotic resistance among aquatic bacteria.

Job description
This is a primarily experimental PhD at the interface of engineering and microbiology. The student will:

Design, build and characterize new instrumentation to couple existing chemotaxis assays to controlled shear systems. This includes mechanical design, 3D printing, control systems and integration with a fluorescence microscope.

Run chemotaxis and conjugation experiments with bacterial donors and recipients of plasmids and a range of chemoattractants, with the opportunity to learn and use advanced techniques such as flow cytometry and plate-reader-based plasmid transfer quantification.

Image and track fluorescently labeled bacteria and chemical plumes in shear flow, and analyze the data with quantitative image- and data-analysis pipelines.

Test clinically relevant bacteria and freshwater (e.g. lake) bacteria, to assess the potential for chemotaxis-driven spread of resistance in the environment.

Contribute data to mathematical models of plasmid spread.

Profile
We are looking for a hands-on, skilled and curious engineer who loves to build new tools and is interested in using them to answer fundamental scientific questions. Ideal candidates hold an MSc degree in bioengineering, mechanical engineering, mechatronics, electrical engineering, environmental engineering, physics or a related discipline, and have some (not necessarily all) of the following skills:

Practical experience in prototyping and manufacturing, for example CAD, 3D printing, machining (strongly preferred).

Experience with control systems and instrumentation, for example motor control, sensors, microcontrollers, and automation or data-acquisition code (Python, MATLAB, LabVIEW or similar) (preferred).

Openness to gain experience in the microbiology laboratory: bacterial cultures, sterile technique, plate readers and flow cytometry.

Familiarity with microscopy, image analysis, fluid mechanics or microfluidics (beneficial but not necessary).

Fluency in English (oral and written), enthusiasm for working in an interdisciplinary and international team, and the drive to pursue scientific excellence (required).

You will be guided by Prof. Roman Stocker and by members of his lab with extensive experience in microbiology, experimental techniques and environmental processes. You will have the opportunity to work in a cutting-edge, fast-paced research environment, interact with researchers from many different disciplines (engineers, physicists, microbiologists, oceanographers, chemists, mathematicians), gain technical experience across diverse research approaches and interact with world-class collaborators.

We offer
ETH Zurich is a family-friendly employer with excellent working conditions. You can look forward to an exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application by December 15th, 2026, including the following documents:

Curriculum vitae

Cover letter (max one page, including brief motivation, research interests and possible start date)

Full transcript from undergraduate studies (both Bachelor and Masters, including grades)

Copy of Master’s or Bachelor’s thesis (PDF)

At least two reference letters

Further information about The Stocker Lab can be found on our Website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr Stefano Ugolini, [email protected] (no applications).

Applications will be reviewed as they are received.

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.
