ap:254400.body:
Introduction
Are you fascinated by how molecular-scale interactions determine the real-world performance of functional materials? In this PhD project, you will study a new class of materials that find application in future technologies ranging from neuromorphic computing and bioelectronics to energy storage. Are you ready to help unravel the inner workings of these fascinating materials by investigating them during operation?

Job Description
Your research
In your PhD project, you will uncover how intermolecular interactions and supramolecular morphology govern the functionality of organic mixed ionic-electronic conductors (OMIECs). Bridging the fields of OMIECs and supramolecular chemistry, you will investigate these relationships through in-depth operando characterization.
OMIECs are soft materials that conduct both electrons and ions, highly promising for applications ranging from energy storage and solar fuels to bioelectronics and neuromorphic computing. However, electrons, ions, solvent and the molecular structure all reorganize during operation, making it difficult to disentangle how molecular-scale interactions ultimately determine macroscopic function.
You will develop characterization methods and experimental setups to probe intermolecular interactions as OMIECs operate. Spectroelectrochemistry will be a key tool; developing operando cells, setups, and experiments that enable you to discern dynamic spectral signatures of molecular packing. By following changes in supramolecular organization during electrochemical doping, your work will reveal how doping affects supramolecular organization.
You will also determine how supramolecular packing governs doping efficiency and dynamics, linking morphology to device-relevant properties, by studying varied samples of available supramolecular building blocks. These fundamental insights will provide a supramolecular knob for tuning material functionality, thereby introducing new ways to control material behavior.
The key outcome of your research is a mechanistic framework describing the bidirectional interplay between OMIEC doping and supramolecular interactions. Building on this framework, you will ultimately design switchable supramolecular OMIEC systems in collaboration with other researchers, targeting applications in in-material computing. Beyond these systems, your fundamental insights will contribute to the general development of next-generation computing and adaptive bioelectronics.
Your environment and support
As a member of the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group at the Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry, you will conduct your research under the supervision of Prof. Tom van der Pol. Your project is highly interdisciplinary, with opportunities to collaborate with researchers across the department. You will become part of a broad and vibrant scientific community, including the Institute for Complex Molecular Systems.
At TU/e and within the Optoelectronic Mixed Conductors group, curiosity-driven research and personal development go hand in hand. You will have the freedom to pursue ambitious scientific questions while receiving the guidance and support needed to develop your own ideas and expertise. Your supervisory team will support you in developing the skills, confidence, and scientific perspective needed to uncover the mechanisms that govern OMIECs and to shape your own path as a researcher.

Job Requirements
We are looking for an enthusiastic self-motivated researcher who holds an MSc degree in chemistry, physics, material science, or equivalent .
Experience with functional material characterization is essential, and spectroscopy or electrochemistry is preferred.
Prior experience with organic semiconductors, supramolecular chemistry, or operando characterization is highly valued.
You possess strong analytical and problem-solving skills and enjoy hands-on experimental research.
You are curious, creative, and eager to develop new experiments, setups, knowledge, and skills.
You enjoy working in an interdisciplinary team and you actively seek opportunities to collaborate.
You are motivated to contribute to teaching and supervision of students.
You are excellent in spoken and written English.

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process .
An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs.
A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme ) for international candidates.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .

Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .
The Department of Chemical Engineering and Chemistry bridges science and engineering to create sustainable solutions for society. By combining expertise in molecules, materials, and processes, we drive innovations that address global challenges in energy, circularity, health and future technology. Through world-class research, interdisciplinary collaboration, and strong industry partnerships, we educate engineers and scientists who turn scientific discoveries into technologies with lasting societal impact. Together, we create chemistry for a better world.

PhD Student Position (f/m/x) in “Quantum Hall calorimetry of quantum materials“
Institute of Physics II | Bocquillon Working Group
We are one of the largest and oldest universities in Europe and one of the most important employers in our region. Our broad range of subjects, the dynamic development of our main research areas and our central location in Cologne make us attractive for students and researchers from around the world. We offer a wide range of career opportunities in science, technology, and administration.

One PhD Student position is available in the group of Professor Erwann Bocquillon, which specializes in the quantum transport of quantum materials
(https://ph2.uni-koeln.de/en/research-groups/bocquillon).
YOUR TASKS
This PhD project will develop a new ultra-sensitive quantum calorimeter to explore how heat flows through exotic quantum materials. By combining layered crystals with quantum Hall devices, the researcher will be able to probe elusive states of matter with unprecedented precision—starting with alpha-RuCl3, a leading candidate for hosting Majorana-like particles and a quantum spin liquid. The project offers an opportunity to build new cutting-edge techniques in collaboration with partners at the University of Tokyo (Japan), while tackling some exciting open questions in condensed-matter physics.

YOUR PROFILE
The candidate should possess an excellent academic record and hold a Masters in Physics, preferably with a major in Quantum Physics or Condensed Matter Physics. Research experience in one or several of the following fields will be appreciated: cryogenic systems, quantum transport measurements, nano-fabrication and cleanroom techniques
An excellent command of English, as well as high motivation, commitment, good communication skills and team spirit are expected.

WE OFFER
An exciting research project at the forefront of research on quantum matter
A diverse working environment with equal opportunities
Support in balancing work and family life
Extensive advanced training opportunities
Occupational health management offers
Flexible working time models

The University of Cologne promotes equal opportunities and diversity. Women will be considered preferentially in accordance with the Equal Opportunities Act of North Rhine-Westphalia (Landesgleichstellungsgesetz – LGG NRW). We also expressly welcome applications from all suitable candidates regardless of their gender, nationality, ethnic and social origin, religion, disability, age, sexual orientation and identity.

ap:254402.body:
Itec is een onderzoeksgroep aan de KU Leuven en imec, het Vlaamse hightech onderzoeks- en innovatiecentrum voor nano-elektronica en digitale technologieën. Op de campus van de KU Leuven in Kortrijk voert de groep interdisciplinair onderzoek uit dat gericht is op het ontwerp, de ontwikkeling en de evaluatie van gepersonaliseerde digitale oplossingen. De belangrijkste toepassingsdomeinen van itec zijn onderwijs, training en gezondheidszorg.

Binnen verschillende nationale en Europese onderzoeks- en innovatieprojecten rond digitale gezondheid, AI in de gezondheidszorg, gezondheidsdata en innovatieve gezondheidstechnologieën zoeken we een projectmanager die ervoor zorgt dat projecten efficiënt worden georganiseerd, stakeholders betrokken blijven en projectdoelstellingen succesvol worden gerealiseerd. De functie combineert projectmanagement met stakeholdermanagement en valorisatie binnen het domein Smart Healthcare.

Website van de eenheid

Functie

Als projectmanager Healthcare Technology neem je een coördinerende, verbindende en vertegenwoordigde rol op binnen een portfolio van onderzoeks- en innovatieprojecten.

Je bewaakt de voortgang van projecten, ondersteunt samenwerking tussen partners en zorgt ervoor dat projectdoelstellingen tijdig en kwalitatief worden gerealiseerd. Daarnaast bouw je actief mee aan het Smart Healthcare-ecosysteem van itec door duurzame relaties uit te bouwen met zorgactoren, innovatiekansen te identificeren en de maatschappelijke impact van onderzoeksresultaten te versterken.

Projectcoördinatie

Coördineren van nationale en Europese onderzoeks- en innovatieprojecten binnen het domein van digitale gezondheid en gezondheidstechnologie.

Bewaken van planning, budgetten, deadlines en rapporteringsverplichtingen.

Organiseren en opvolgen van projectvergaderingen en consortiumactiviteiten.

Faciliteren van samenwerking tussen onderzoekers, zorgorganisaties, bedrijven, beleidsactoren en andere stakeholders.

Ondersteunen van onderzoekers en projectpartners bij de realisatie van projectdoelstellingen, en aanvragen bij ethische commissies.

Stakeholdermanagement en ecosysteemontwikkeling

Bouwen en onderhouden van strategische relaties met zorgorganisaties, ziekenhuizen, zorgverstrekkers, bedrijven en beleidsactoren om onderzoeksnoden, maatschappelijke uitdagingen en innovatie-opportuniteiten te identificeren.

Afstemmen met de portfolio managers die verantwoordelijk zijn voor projectverwerving en business development binnen het team om projectkansen en samenwerkingsmogelijkheden te detecteren en verder te ontwikkelen.

Fungeren als aanspreekpunt voor externe stakeholders binnen het domein Smart Healthcare en bijdragen aan duurzame samenwerkingsverbanden.

Positioneren van itec als een betrouwbare en zichtbare partner binnen het gezondheidszorgecosysteem.

Vertegenwoordigen van de onderzoeksgroep binnen het imec-netwerk voor het domein Healthcare en bewaken van de aansluiting tussen de onderzoeks- en innovatiestrategie van itec en de bredere imec-roadmaps.

Ondersteunen van de uitbouw van strategische samenwerkingen en bijdragen aan de verwerving van nieuwe onderzoeks- en innovatieprojecten.

Kwaliteitsbewaking en rapportering

Opstellen en opvolgen van projectrapporten en andere projectdocumentatie.

Bewaken van de kwaliteit van projectresultaten en deliverables.

Identificeren van risico's en proactief voorstellen van oplossingen.

Disseminatie, valorisatie en projectontwikkeling

Ondersteunen van communicatie-, disseminatie- en valorisatieactiviteiten.

Organiseren van workshops, studiedagen en netwerkevenementen.

Stimuleren van de valorisatie van onderzoeksresultaten door bruggen te slaan tussen onderzoek, praktijk en markt.

Identificeren van opportuniteiten voor implementatie, opschaling en dienstverlening gebaseerd op onderzoeksresultaten.

Bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van nieuwe onderzoeks- en innovatievoorstellen binnen het domein Smart Healthcare.

Profiel

Je hebt een masterdiploma, bij voorkeur met affiniteit voor gezondheidszorg, gezondheidstechnologie, innovatie of digitale transformatie.

Je hebt ervaring met projectmanagement, bij voorkeur binnen gezondheidszorg-, innovatie- of onderzoeksprojecten.

Je bent sterk in plannen, organiseren en het bewaken van deadlines.

Je communiceert vlot met diverse stakeholders en bouwt gemakkelijk professionele relaties op.

Je bent sterk in netwerking en onderhoudt op een natuurlijke manier relaties met zorgactoren, bedrijven en beleidsmakers.

Je kan meerdere projecten gelijktijdig opvolgen en behoudt overzicht in complexe trajecten.

Je werkt zelfstandig, neemt initiatief en hebt een sterk verantwoordelijkheidsgevoel.

Je hebt affiniteit met digitale gezondheid, gezondheidstechnologie, AI in de gezondheidszorg, gezondheidsdata of digitale zorgoplossingen.

Je hebt interesse in valorisatie, innovatie-ecosystemen en de maatschappelijke implementatie van onderzoeksresultaten.

Ervaring met Europese of nationale onderzoeks- en innovatieprojecten is een pluspunt.

Ervaring met programmeren, data-analyse of de technische ontwikkeling van digitale toepassingen wordt als een pluspunt beschouwd.

Je beschikt over uitstekende communicatieve vaardigheden in het Nederlands en Engels, zowel mondeling als schriftelijk.

Aanbod

Een voltijdse aanstelling voor één jaar als wetenschappelijk medewerker in Barema 43, met mogelijkheid tot verlenging mits positieve evaluatie en beschikbare financiering. Een deeltijdse aanstelling is bespreekbaar.

Een uitdagende functie binnen een sterk interdisciplinair onderzoeks- en innovatienetwerk van KU Leuven en imec.

Werkplek op campus Kulak Kortrijk, met mogelijkheden tot flexibel en hybride werken.

De kans om samen te werken met onderzoekers, zorgorganisaties, ziekenhuizen, bedrijven, beleidsmakers en innovatieve HealthTech-organisaties.

Een afwisselende functie met een hoge mate van autonomie en maatschappelijke impact.

Een stimulerende, internationale en multidisciplinaire werkomgeving.

De mogelijkheid om een actieve rol te spelen in de verdere uitbouw van het Smart Healthcare-ecosysteem van itec en imec.

Als wetenschappelijk medewerker krijg je alle kansen om je professionele carrière vooruit te helpen door literatuur te bestuderen, seminaries en workshops bij te wonen en in contact te komen met vooraanstaande onderzoekers uit verschillende disciplines.

Naast een competitief salaris biedt KU Leuven verschillende extra voordelen, waaronder een hospitalisatieverzekering, ecocheques, vergoeding van vervoerskosten met het openbaar vervoer, voordelige maaltijden en een KU Leuven-fiets.

Interesse?

Meer informatie is te verkrijgen bij prof. dr. Celine Vens, mail: [email protected] of mevrouw Ine Windey, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven wil een inclusieve, respectvolle en sociaal veilige gemeenschap zijn. Wij omarmen diversiteit tussen individuen en groepen als een meerwaarde. Open dialoog en verschillen in perspectief zijn noodzakelijk in een ambitieuze onderzoeks- en onderwijsomgeving. In ons streven naar gelijke kansen erkennen wij de gevolgen van historische ongelijkheden. Wij aanvaarden geen enkele vorm van discriminatie op basis van, onder meer, geslacht, genderidentiteit en -expressie, seksuele oriëntatie, leeftijd, etnische of nationale afkomst, huidskleur, levensbeschouwelijke overtuiging, neurodivergentie, arbeidshandicap, gezondheid, of socio-economische status. Bij vragen over toegankelijkheid of aangeboden ondersteuning helpen we je graag op dit e-mailadres .

ap:254407.body:
Join us at Chalmers University of Technology to pioneer the next generation of batteries through advanced 3D printing and additive manufacturing. Be part of an innovative research team (4 Professors in battery, additive manufacturing, sustainable product design, and AI) exploring new ways to manufacture batteries with greater design flexibility, improved performance, and more sustainable production.
About us
At the Department of Mechanical Engineering , we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world.
The Division of Materials and Manufacture conducts research across the full value chain, from materials design and processing to advanced manufacturing and characterisation, with a strong emphasis on metallic systems. We combine interdisciplinary expertise with close industry collaboration to develop sustainable materials and manufacturing technologies.
About the research project
What if you could 3D-print a battery? This doctoral project explores advanced additive manufacturing technologies to develop new approaches for battery fabrication, enabling greater design flexibility and new possibilities for integrating battery materials and structures. You will investigate how materials, printing processes and electrode design can be combined to create functional battery components and demonstrate their potential in next-generation energy storage. The research aims to advance innovative and more sustainable battery manufacturing.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in materials science, mechanical engineering, materials mechanics, chemical engineering, materials chemistry, physics, or production engineering
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English
Experience (one of the following) in metal and ceramic additive manufacturing (AM), battery electrode processing, slurry preparation, 3D printing

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Experience in battery manufacturing, additive manufacturing, 3D printing

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Materials Science
Work with the research project as described above
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing
The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions (Licentiate) are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment, with the possibility to teach up to 20%.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  22nd of November, 2026
For questions, please contact:
Jinhua Sun (Associate Professor), [email protected] or Eduard Hryha (Professor), [email protected]
We look forward to your application!
*** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position.  ***
Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society.
Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

ap:254408.body:
The  Berlin School of Economics  offers career development programs in economics, accounting, finance and management at the PhD and Postdoc levels in a single and unique structure. Nine major institutions active in economics research in the Berlin-Brandenburg area cooperate within the Berlin School of Economics: European University Viadrina Frankfurt (Oder), Freie Universität Berlin, Humboldt-Universität zu Berlin, Technische Universität Berlin, University of Potsdam, ESMT Berlin, Hertie School, ROCKWOOL Foundation Berlin Institute for the Economy and the Future of Work (RFBerlin) and WZB Berlin Social Science Center. Together they are pooling their efforts in the education of young researchers in economics.
The Berlin School of Economics is welcoming applications for the new cohort of its PhD Program  starting in October 2027.
General structure of the curriculum
The  Berlin School of Economics PhD Program  provides outstanding doctoral students with a vibrant, intensively networked research community. The program develops the students’ talents in a unique combination of a high-level, academic research environment together with applied, policy-oriented research opportunities. Students receive state-of-the-art coursework training and can select from a wide array of specializations for their doctoral research.
The Berlin School of Economics PhD Program offers four different  PhD tracks : PhD in Economics, PhD in Accounting, PhD in Finance, and PhD in Management. All tracks share the same structure and general curriculum, and allow for numerous specializations.
The curriculum is divided in a qualification and a dissertation phase. During the  qualification phase  of the program (about three semesters), students acquire methodological and research-oriented training in  mandatory and elective courses in economic theory, applied economics, business studies (accounting, finance, management), econometrics, and economic policy. Students define their research area and find supervisory support from two supervisors. They write research proposals that are discussed with faculty members individually and in seminars in order to provide early feedback on the scientific potential of research ideas. This is a central part of the Berlin School of Economics PhD Program, in which the students have full flexibility in the choice of their research topics and of the supervisors. During this phase, students are funded through stipends that allow for this flexibility. A minimum of 90 ECTS credits have to be obtained in order to finish the qualification phase of the program.
During the subsequent  dissertation phase  of the program (about three to four years), students write their doctoral thesis while having the opportunity to apply their knowledge in the professional research environment that is provided at the research institutions participating in the Berlin School of Economics. During this phase, students are typically employed at the research institution their supervisor is affiliated with. The PhD will be awarded by the Berlin School of Economics institution one of the student’s supervisors is affiliated with.
Graduates of the Berlin School of Economics PhD Program are excellently prepared for positions in academia as well as for policy-related institutions and organizations, which has been documented by a list of outstanding  placements .
Application Requirements
Applicants should have a Master’s degree in economics or business studies. Applicants from related fields (such as industrial engineering, statistics, or quantitative social sciences) may also fulfill the admission requirements if they have a sufficient background in economics or business studies.
Applicants with a Bachelor’s degree are eligible to apply for the program if they also apply for a Master’s program offering a fast track option.
Applicants whose native language is not English are asked to demonstrate their English language proficiency, unless they hold a degree from a university in an English-speaking country or can document at least one year of studies at an English-speaking university. Sufficient evidence of a good command of English can be demonstrated with a high score in the “Test of English as a Foreign Language” (TOEFL) or the “International English Language Testing System” (IELTS). Providing TOEFL or IELTS scores is highly recommended but not mandatory.
All applicants are asked to provide GRE General Test scores with their application. Providing GRE General Test scores is highly recommended but not mandatory.
How to Apply:
Applications for an intake into the Berlin School of Economics PhD Program in October 2027 will be accepted until January 15, 2027 , and can only be submitted via the Berlin School of Economics Application Portal.
All information on the application for the Berlin School of Economics PhD Program can be found on the  official website .
Contact information
Berlin School of Economics Office
Vita Ozolina / Admissions Officer
Email:  [email protected]
Telephone: +49 (0)30 2093 99413

Degree You hold a Master's degree (preferably) in Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or an equivalent degree. The degree requirements must be met by the date of appointment.
Occupancy rate 100%
Vacancy type Research staff
ABOUT GHENT UNIVERSITY
Ghent University is a world of its own. Employing more than 15.000 people, it is actively involved in education and research, management and administration, as well as technical and social service provision on a daily basis. It is one of the largest, most exciting employers in the area and offers great career opportunities.
With its 11 faculties and more than 85 departments offering state-of-the-art study programmes grounded in research in a wide range of academic fields, Ghent University is a logical choice for its staff and students.
Image Processing and Interpretation (IPI, http://ipi.ugent.be) is an imec research group at Ghent University. IPI consists of 40 researchers and conducts state-of-the-art research in digital image and video processing for a wide range of applications, including real-time image and video processing and machine learning. This encompasses application domains such as industrial inspection, (ultra) high-definition video enhancement, smart multi-camera networks, computer vision, sensor fusion, and (medical) imaging.
This project is in close collaboration with the Radiation Physics research group at the Center for X-ray Tomography (UGCT, http://www.ugct.ugent.be). This group conducts research on micro-CT, an imaging technique for examining materials and objects at high resolution in 3D.
YOUR TASKS
This vacancy concerns a PhD-level research position within an ambitious project on the reconstruction of micro-CT using machine learning in the form of implicit neural representations (INRs).
The goal is to improve traditional computed tomography by avoiding computational bottlenecks by directly reconstructing and analyzing raw μCT data into a compressed neural form, rather than via the intermediate step of traditional discrete voxel grids.
You will conduct fundamental and applied research at the intersection of linear algebra, inverse problems, signal processing, and machine learning.
The position requires close collaboration with experts in both image processing and imaging physics, as well as with researchers in computational mathematics and applied AI. In addition to the collaboration within Ghent University, there is also a collaboration with the Centrum Wiskunde en Informatica (CWI, http://www.cwi.nl), a research institution in Amsterdam specializing in computational mathematics.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You hold a Master's degree (preferably) in Engineering, Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or an equivalent degree. The degree requirements must be met by the date of appointment.
A strong interest in signal processing, inverse problems, and mathematics is essential for success in this position, in addition to expertise in machine learning.
Familiarity with (medical) image reconstruction (tomography) or computational imaging is highly desirable.
Knowledge of and experience with machine learning is also a plus. You will design, implement, and validate novel algorithms, and benchmark them against state-of-the-art reconstruction pipelines.
Strong programming skills (e.g., Python/C++ and GPU-based computing) and proficiency with modern machine learning frameworks are required.
We seek a motivated researcher eager to push the boundaries of dynamic imaging through the research and development of mathematically grounded, computation-efficient methods.
As an academic, you represent your work at international conferences, and you display a positive, critical attitude towards improving the current state-of-the-art in the field.

WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
We offer a full-time position as a doctoral fellow, consisting of an initial period of 12 months, which - after a positive evaluation, will be extended to a total maximum of 48 months.
Your contract will start on 01/12/2026 at the earliest.
The fellowship amount is 100% of the net salary of an AAP member in equal family circumstances. The individual fellowship amount is determined by Team Personnel Administration based on family status and seniority. A grant that meets the conditions and criteria of the regulations for doctoral fellowships is considered free of personal income tax. Click here for more information about our salary scales
All Ghent University staff members enjoy a number of benefits, such as a wide range of training and education opportunities, 36 days of holiday leave (on an annual basis for a full-time job) supplemented by annual fixed bridge days, bicycle allowance and eco vouchers. Click here for a complete overview of all the staff benefits.

INTERESTED?
Send your cv, copy of your diploma (if already in your possession) and a motivation letter to [email protected] .
We do not accept late applications.
As Ghent University maintains an equal opportunities and diversity policy, everyone is encouraged to apply for this position.
For more information about this vacancy, please contact prof. Jan Aelterman ( [email protected] ,)

ap:254410.body:
Three Doctoral Positions in History and Theory of Urban Design and Architecture
The Chair of the History and Theory of Urban Design (Prof. Dr. Tom Avermaete) at the Institute for the History and Theory of Architecture (gta), ETH Zürich, is looking for three doctoral candidates within the ERC Advanced Grant Project “Co-opolis: Another Architectural History of the European City (1890–1990).” The positions are expected to start in March 2027 and are fully funded for four years.

Project background
The ERC Project explores how third-sector actors, such as cooperatives, mutual aid societies, associations, and other collective institutions, co-produced the city following precise values and collectivist agendas centred on the shared provision, usage, and maintenance of built resources, resulting in housing and civic structures (e.g., people’s palaces, cultural centres) that complemented and shaped the urban spaces produced by the state and the market. To this end, the project compares selected examples from Sweden, France, and Switzerland from 1890 to 1990 to examine how the ideologies and practices of third-sector actors influenced the built environment within the evolving frameworks of European welfare states. The project seeks to demonstrate the contribution of collective initiatives to the making of contemporary European cities and to assess the lessons they can offer for current challenges such as affordable housing, social inclusion, and sustainable urban development.

Job description
The three PhD candidates within the “Co-opolis” project will investigate the conditions of emergence, spatial characteristics, and endurance of architectural and urban projects at the intersection of welfare regimes and third-sector collective actors in France, Sweden, and Switzerland over the project’s timeframe. Each candidate will focus on one of these countries, examining how housing projects and civic infrastructures developed through the initiatives of third-sector actors within different welfare regimes.

Specifically, the candidates will:

Focus on the line of enquiry previously described, producing research on the case studies as well as bringing their own original ideas to the topic. For this reason, we ask potential candidates to include a short description of a possible research direction with the application documents.

Complete the PhD dissertation within the given timeframe (March 2027–March 2031).

Contribute to the activities and outputs of the overall ERC project, such as workshops, seminars, authoring articles, presenting their research at international conferences, and contributing to the project’s website.

Actively engage with the courses and seminars of the PhD programme at the gta Institute, as well as in the academic activities of the Chair of the History and Theory of Urban Design, including participation in research discussions and occasional contributions to teaching activities, such as critiques, reviews, and examinations.

Profile

We are looking for passionate candidates with an MSc degree in Architecture, History of Art, Social History, or closely related fields in the humanities, to be completed by the start of the position.

Previous experience in publishing, as well as archival and historical research, is welcome.

The working language is English.

Candidates must also be proficient in the language relevant to their selected case-study country: French (France), German plus French and/or Italian (Switzerland), or Swedish (Sweden)

We offer
The successful candidates will join a stimulating and international research environment at the Chair of the History and Theory of Urban Design and Institute for the History and Theory of Architecture (gta), benefiting from close collaboration, structured mentoring, and opportunities to strengthen academic networks through conference participation, training, and teaching activities.

The positions are fully funded according to ETH Zürich doctoral salary conditions.

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

Motivation letter

CV

Short description of possible research direction (max. 1 page)

Two reference contacts

Further information about the Chair of the History and Theory of Urban Design can be found at our website  and repository . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Dr. Elettra Carnelli,  [email protected]  (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

Applications will be accepted until 22 November 2026. For selected candidates, interviews will take place online on 17 December 2026.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:254411.body:
As a joint venture of the University of Basel and the University Hospitals Basel, the Department of Biomedicine (DBM) brings together basic and clinical scientists to advance the understanding of health and disease.
We are home to more than 67 research groups and over 800 employees across six locations in the heart of Basel. Our collaborative and international environment fosters innovation, excellence, and impactful research.
The Developmental Genetics led by Prof. Aimée Zuniga, is looking for a Research Assistant/Technician.
Join our community and help shape the future of biomedicine.
The Research Assistant will join the Developmental Genetics Research Group, which investigates the signalling interactions and molecular mechanisms controlling embryonic development. Our research uses genetically engineered mouse models, mouse models of human diseases, and organoid systems to investigate the gene regulatory networks that control normal organ development and the alterations resulting in congenital disorders. We combine these experimental models with state-of-the-art genetic and molecular technologies, genome-wide approaches, and advanced 3D confocal imaging techniques.
Applicants must have completed an apprenticeship as molecular biology research technician (Laborant:in) and/or hold a BSc/MSc in molecular biology and excellent skills in molecular biology. Prior expertise in using mouse models and/or transcriptome/analysis (immunofluorescence cells/frozen embryo sections, protein biochemistry etc) will be an asset for the position. Applicants with certification for animal experimentation (LTK1 or FELASA certification) and experience in using mouse models will be given preference. Good knowledge of (spoken) English is important as this is the working language.
We offer a stimulating discovery research environment in an internationally renowned research team at the University of Basel. The group is located in one of the flagship Research Institutes at the Department of Biomedicine with state-of-the-art research facilities and excellent training and career development opportunities.
For more information, please go to:
https://www.devgenbasel.com/
The University of Basel is an equal opportunity employer that offers competitive salaries.
Application

Please submit a letter of motivation, CV, copies of the relevant diplomas, degrees and certifications, brief summary of research and technology expertise, and the names and email addresses of minimally two referees.
The position is available from January 1, 2027 or as agreed.

Introduction
Are you organized, proactive, and ready for the next step in your career, finding satisfaction in providing essential support to a board and office? Then we’d love to have you on our team!

Job Description
The department of Mathematics & Computer Science (M&CS) is looking for a Management Assistant for the Board secretariat. As a Management Assistant for the Board Secretariat, you will play a critical role in supporting the smooth functioning of the board and office operations within the department. You will act as the primary point of contact for board members and take on various responsibilities to ensure effective coordination and communication. Your duties will require a high level of organization, discretion, and proactivity.

You will perform the following duties:
You will be part of the M&CS board secretariat and provide secretarial support especially to the managing director, the other department board members, and the departmental office (HR, finance, facility services, policy, communication, PDO) and appointment committees (BACs). You work accurately and remain calm under pressure.
You organize meetings with internal and external participants, managing complex calendars and ensuring everyone receives the right documents on time.
You provide full secretarial support for BACs: agenda management, preparing and distributing papers, taking minutes in English, archiving files, and following up on action points.
You provide practical support such as arranging room reservations, catering, ordering flowers and gifts.
Planning and organizing social events for the department and office, such as the end-of-year drink and department event.
Organizing the secretarial meetings. Additionally organizing the Secretary’s Day, scheduling informal coffee moments, and sharing relevant information with other secretaries.
You handle internal communication by sending out department mailings (Board Business, facility updates, newsletters, information from the board) and by keeping the department mailbox and several mailing lists up to date.
You take care of administrative and financial processes, such as preparing and processing purchase orders, reimbursements, and travel requests, as well as handling incoming calls and correspondence in a professional and friendly manner.
You provide practical support in facility and housing matters, including furniture requests, and liaise with Facility Services.
You act as a backup for the colleague board secretaries to ensure continuity of service.

Job Requirements
We are looking for an enthusiastic, committed and independent team player who recognizes himself in the following points:
Secretarial or administrative education and thinking level at least HBO level and have relevant work experience at board level;
You are accurate, representative, discrete, reliable and communicative;
Organizational and supportive, stress-resistant and solution-oriented, think along and shift gears quickly;
Extensive experience working with MS Office (calendar management via Outlook, Word, PowerPoint, SharePoint, Excel);
Affinity with and knowledge of the primary target groups: (TU/e) students and scientists;
You communicate effectively in both fluent (business) English and Dutch, orally and in writing;
You are able to build positive relationships with the board and management, colleagues and relations at all levels of the organization;
You are a team player with a presentable approach and a hospitality mentality; working in an occasionally hectic office environment energizes you;
You are a proactive and enthusiastic person, willing to take initiative. You feel comfortable in an administrative and international environment and know how to prioritize under pressure;
You do not get stressed by a hectic environment where ad hoc appointments and activities frequently take place;
You enjoy working with different stakeholders;
You are open to new developments and changes and make recommendations for improving the further professionalization of our management support organization.

If you are concerned that you don’t meet all the requirements sufficiently, but the job does excite you, then be sure to respond, we would love to look at your profile.

Conditions of Employment
An exciting position within an international yet personal university. You are right in the middle of the students, on a green campus within walking distance of the central station. Besides beautiful architecture, you will find varied workplaces and excellent sports facilities.

We also offer you:
Salary in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale 8, ranging from €3,537 to €4,673 gross base salary per month (full-time), depending on your knowledge and experience.
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
A favorable arrangement for more holidays or a sabbatical.
A selection model for additional fringe benefits.
Working hours in consultation for an optimal work-life balance.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
Scope for your talent with advancement prospects and excellent development opportunities such as mentoring, workshops and coaching.
Partially paid parental leave and reimbursement for commuting expenses, working from home and the internet.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!

About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .
Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .
As one of the largest and most dynamic academic communities in the Netherlands, the department Mathematics and Computer Science (M&CS) brings together more than 140 scientific staff, over 250 PhD and EngD candidates, and more than 3000 students. We collaborate closely with leading industrial partners in the Brainport Eindhoven region and with universities across the globe—creating a uniquely fertile environment for both fundamental breakthroughs and applied innovation.
Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to have more information about the position, please contact the hiring manager: Manon van Leeuwen, Departmental Secretariat M&CS, [email protected] @tue.nl or +31 40 247 2750.
Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact HR Services at [email protected] .
Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page.

Application
If you are interested, please use the ‘apply’ button to send us your CV and letter of application with your motivation and a description of your qualifications. Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications.
Screening of candidates begins as soon as applications are received and continues until the position is filled. Where applicable, internal candidates will be given priority over external candidates where they are equally suitable.

We look forward to receiving your application!

Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Important for non-EU applicants: Please be aware that for this position, specific residence permit requirements apply. If you are a non-EU national, you may not be eligible to legally work in this role under current Dutch immigration regulations. We strongly advise you to contact our Staff Immigration Team ( [email protected] ) before applying to check your eligibility and to receive further guidance.
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

ap:254414.body:
Dit doctoraatsproject maakt deel uit van een multidisciplinaire samenwerking tussen de onderzoeksgroep Livestock Technology, onder leiding van prof. Ben Aernouts, en de onderzoeksgroep Insect Production and Processing, onder leiding van prof. Jeroen De Smet, op de KU Leuven-campus in Geel.

Beide onderzoeksgroepen brengen complementaire expertise samen op het vlak van insectenbiologie, insectenproductie en -verwerking, sensortechnologie en data-analyse.

De onderzoeksgroep Insect Production and Processing bestudeert biologische en biochemische uitdagingen binnen de industriële insectenwaardeketen, van insectveiligheid en productie tot verwerking en het gebruik van insectgebaseerde producten. Binnen het domein van precisieveehouderij (precision livestock farming, PLF) ontwikkelt de onderzoeksgroep Livestock Technology innovatieve sensortechnologieën en data-analysemethoden om diergedrag, gezondheid en productieprestaties automatisch te beoordelen.

Door deze expertisegebieden te combineren, willen beide onderzoeksgroepen betere methoden ontwikkelen om insectengedrag te meten en te interpreteren, en om te begrijpen hoe kweekomstandigheden de biologie en productie van insecten beïnvloeden.

KU Leuven is een onderzoeksintensieve universiteit met een sterke internationale oriëntatie. De campus in Geel ligt in een groene, landelijke omgeving en werkt nauw samen met onderzoeksinstellingen, bedrijven en insectenkwekerijen.

Project

De productie van insecten wint aan belang als een manier om organische reststromen om te zetten in waardevolle grondstoffen voor voeding en diervoeder. Larven van de zwarte soldatenvlieg (BSF, Hermetia illucens ) zijn bijzonder veelbelovend omdat ze uiteenlopende organische materialen kunnen omzetten in nutriëntenrijke biomassa die eiwitten en vetten bevat.

Een succesvolle insectenproductie vereist echter een beter inzicht in de manier waarop kweekomstandigheden de biologie, het gedrag en de productieprestaties van insecten beïnvloeden. Hoe reageren larven op veranderingen in hun omgeving? Kunnen gedragspatronen ons helpen om hun reacties op uitdagende omstandigheden beter te begrijpen en mogelijkheden te identificeren om kweekstrategieën te verbeteren?

Dit doctoraatsproject maakt deel uit van EntoBOOST , een project dat wordt gefinancierd door het Fonds Wetenschappelijk Onderzoek – Vlaanderen (FWO). EntoBOOST brengt onderzoekers samen van KU Leuven, Universiteit Gent, Universiteit Antwerpen, de Università degli Studi dell'Insubria in Italië, Inagro en Thomas More. Het project wil onze kennis van de fysiologie, biologie en het gedrag van insecten verdiepen om kweekstrategieën te verbeteren en de productie van veilige, hoogwaardige insectgebaseerde producten met gewenste biologische en nutritionele eigenschappen te ondersteunen.

Binnen dit project zal je een centrale onderzoeksvraag behandelen: Hoe reageren larven van de zwarte soldatenvlieg gedragsmatig op verschillende kweekomstandigheden, en hoe hangen deze reacties samen met larvale groei, overleving en productieprestaties?

Om deze vraag te onderzoeken, bestudeer je het gedrag van larven met behulp van een geavanceerd cameragebaseerd sensorplatform dat binnen het onderzoeksteam al werd ontwikkeld en operationeel is. Het platform combineert hogeresolutie-RGB-beeldvorming, zichtbare en nabij-infrarode multispectrale beeldvorming en thermografie.

Deze metingen worden aangevuld met monitoring van gasemissies, waaronder koolstofdioxide, ammoniak, lachgas en methaan, en met conventionele kweekparameters zoals larvale groei en overleving, substraatvochtigheid, pH en samenstelling van het substraat.

Jouw rol

Je werkt samen met een doctoraatsstudent met een ingenieursachtergrond, die de sensorhardware en computer vision-algoritmen verder ontwikkelt om bewegings- en gedragsinformatie uit de camerabeelden te halen.

Jouw belangrijkste focus ligt op het biologische onderzoek: onderzoeksvragen vertalen naar experimenten, gedragsgegevens analyseren en de resultaten interpreteren in relatie tot omgevingsomstandigheden, larvale fysiologie en productieprestaties.

Je neemt verantwoordelijkheid voor de biologische onderzoeksvragen en de statistische analyse. Tegelijk werk je nauw samen met het engineeringteam om te begrijpen hoe de sensorgegevens worden gegenereerd en hoe ze kunnen worden ingezet om biologische onderzoeksvragen te beantwoorden. Ervaring met computer vision is niet vereist; nieuwsgierigheid naar de technologie en bereidheid om bij te leren zijn belangrijk.

Wat ga je doen?

Experimenten ontwerpen en uitvoeren: kweekexperimenten ontwikkelen en uitvoeren om te onderzoeken hoe verschillende omgevingsomstandigheden en stressgerelateerde factoren het gedrag en de productieprestaties van larven beïnvloeden.

Gedragsgegevens analyseren: samenwerken met het engineeringteam om betekenisvolle gedragskenmerken uit cameragebaseerde sensorgegevens te halen en tijdreeksgegevens van gedrag te analyseren.

Gedrag koppelen aan productie: statistische modellen gebruiken om verbanden te onderzoeken tussen gedragspatronen, omgevingsomstandigheden, groei en overleving.

Fysiologische reacties onderzoeken: samenwerken met onderzoekers van de Universiteit Antwerpen om gedragswaarnemingen te koppelen aan metabole merkers die verband houden met stress.

Onderzoeksresultaten communiceren: resultaten publiceren in internationale peer-reviewed wetenschappelijke tijdschriften en presenteren op wetenschappelijke congressen, en zo bijdragen aan de verdere ontwikkeling van precisie-insectenkweek.

Je krijgt ondersteuning van KU Leuven-experts in insectenproductie en -verwerking en in sensortechnologie. De experimenten vinden plaats in de SymBIOnt Insect Pilot Plant van KU Leuven en Thomas More in Geel, en in de insectenkweekfaciliteiten van Inagro.

In het Toxicologisch Centrum van de Universiteit Antwerpen werkt een collega-doctoraatsstudent aan de ontwikkeling en validatie van een metabolomicsplatform om biomarkers te identificeren die verband houden met stress bij larven van de zwarte soldatenvlieg. Door jouw gedragsstudie met dit onderzoek te combineren, help je een vollediger beeld te krijgen van de biologische reacties van larven op uitdagende kweekomstandigheden.

Op langere termijn kan een beter inzicht in deze reacties helpen om mogelijkheden te identificeren om kweekstrategieën te optimaliseren, de productie-efficiëntie te verbeteren en bij te dragen aan productiesystemen die ook meer rekening houden met insectenwelzijn.

Profiel

We zoeken een nieuwsgierige en gemotiveerde doctoraatskandidaat die graag biologische onderzoeksvragen onderzoekt, met gegevens werkt en samenwerkt met onderzoekers uit verschillende disciplines.

Je:

Hebt een masterdiploma in de biologie, biosciences, bio-ingenieurswetenschappen, dierwetenschappen of een gelijkwaardige opleiding. Kandidaten met een masterdiploma in data science en een sterke interesse in biologie worden eveneens aangemoedigd om te solliciteren.

Hebt een sterke interesse in diergedrag (ethologie), insectenbiologie en de relatie tussen omgevingsomstandigheden en biologische reacties.

Wilt onderzoeken hoe kweekomstandigheden het gedrag, de fysiologie en de productieprestaties van larven beïnvloeden.

Werkt graag met gegevens en bent gemotiveerd om verantwoordelijkheid te nemen voor de statistische analyse en interpretatie van je experimenten.

Bent geïnteresseerd in de manier waarop sensortechnologie en data-analyse biologisch onderzoek kunnen bevorderen, en bent bereid om samen met het engineeringteam de basisprincipes van computer vision te leren.

Beschikt over een kritische, analytische, creatieve en innovatieve ingesteldheid.

Beschikt over goede mondelinge en schriftelijke communicatievaardigheden in het Engels.

Werkt graag in een internationale, multidisciplinaire onderzoeksomgeving en werkt vlot samen met onderzoekers met uiteenlopende achtergronden.

De volgende ervaring is een pluspunt, maar geen vereiste:

Ervaring met insectenkweek of entomologisch onderzoek, bij voorkeur met larven van de zwarte soldatenvlieg.

Ervaring met het ontwerpen en uitvoeren van gedrags- of dierexperimenten.

Ervaring met statistische analyses, waaronder mixed-effectsmodellen, multivariate analyses of tijdreeksanalyses.

Ervaring met wetenschappelijke dataverwerking met R, Python, MATLAB of gelijkwaardige software.

Ervaring met computer vision en machine learning.

Voorwaarde voor toelating: Om in aanmerking te komen voor deze functie, moet je beschikken over een masterdiploma met minstens onderscheiding, behaald aan een universiteit binnen de Europese Economische Ruimte (EER) in de afgelopen drie jaar.

Aanbod

We bieden een voltijdse doctoraatspositie van vier jaar met een competitief salaris, met een zo snel mogelijke startdatum.

Je komt terecht in een multidisciplinair onderzoeksproject met een operationeel sensorplatform en toegang tot insectenkweekfaciliteiten op pilootschaal. Hierdoor kan je vanaf het begin focussen op biologische onderzoeksvragen, terwijl je nauw samenwerkt met onderzoekers in engineering, insectenbiologie en metabolomics.

Je mag rekenen op:

Praktijkgericht onderzoek: experimenten ontwerpen en uitvoeren met behulp van gespecialiseerde insectenkweek- en sensorfaciliteiten.

Interdisciplinaire samenwerking: nauw samenwerken met biologen, ingenieurs en collega-onderzoekers van verschillende onderzoeksinstellingen.

Wetenschappelijke ontwikkeling: begeleiding en opleiding krijgen om je onderzoeksvaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen en je doctoraat succesvol af te ronden.

Internationale ervaring: je onderzoek presenteren op congressen, wetenschappelijke publicaties schrijven en een professioneel netwerk uitbouwen.

Doctoraatsopleiding: deelnemen aan de Arenberg Doctoral School van KU Leuven, die een uitgebreid opleidingsaanbod in wetenschappelijke en overdraagbare vaardigheden biedt.

Je maakt deel uit van een jong, dynamisch en multidisciplinair team dat je tijdens je doctoraat ondersteunt. Je hoofdwerkplek is de KU Leuven-campus in Geel. Kennis van het Nederlands is niet vereist.

Website 'Insect Production and Processing' onderzoeksgroep
Website 'Livestock Technology' onderzoeksgroep

Interesse?

Voor meer informatie over deze functie kan je contact opnemen met Prof. Ben Aernouts, mail: [email protected] of Mr. Maximilian Hoffmann, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven wil een inclusieve, respectvolle en sociaal veilige gemeenschap zijn. Wij omarmen diversiteit tussen individuen en groepen als een meerwaarde. Open dialoog en verschillen in perspectief zijn noodzakelijk in een ambitieuze onderzoeks- en onderwijsomgeving. In ons streven naar gelijke kansen erkennen wij de gevolgen van historische ongelijkheden. Wij aanvaarden geen enkele vorm van discriminatie op basis van, onder meer, geslacht, genderidentiteit en -expressie, seksuele oriëntatie, leeftijd, etnische of nationale afkomst, huidskleur, levensbeschouwelijke overtuiging, neurodivergentie, arbeidshandicap, gezondheid, of socio-economische status. Bij vragen over toegankelijkheid of aangeboden ondersteuning helpen we je graag op dit e-mailadres .

ap:254415.body:
This PhD position is part of a multidisciplinary collaboration between the Livestock Technology group, led by Prof. Ben Aernouts, and the Research Group for Insect Production and Processing, led by Prof. Jeroen De Smet, at KU Leuven campus Geel.

The two groups bring together complementary expertise in insect biology, production and processing, sensor technology and data analysis.

The Research Group for Insect Production and Processing investigates biological and biochemical challenges across the industrial insect value chain, from insect safety and production to processing and the use of insect-based products. Within the field of precision livestock farming (PLF), the Livestock Technology group develops innovative sensor technologies and data-analysis methods for automatically assessing animal behaviour, health and production performance.

By combining these areas of expertise, the two groups aim to develop better ways of measuring and interpreting insect behaviour and understanding how rearing conditions influence insect biology and production.

KU Leuven is a research-intensive university with a strong international orientation. Its campus in Geel offers a green, rural setting and close connections with research institutes, industry and insect-production facilities.

Project

Insect production is gaining importance as a way to convert organic side streams into valuable resources for food and feed. Black soldier fly (BSF, Hermetia illucens ) larvae are particularly promising because of their ability to transform a wide range of organic materials into nutrient-rich biomass containing proteins and fats.

However, successful insect production requires a better understanding of how rearing conditions influence insect biology, behaviour and production performance. How do larvae respond to environmental variation? Can behavioural patterns help us understand their responses to challenging conditions and identify opportunities to improve rearing strategies?

This PhD position is part of EntoBOOST , a project funded by the Research Foundation – Flanders (FWO). EntoBOOST brings together researchers from KU Leuven, Ghent University, the University of Antwerp, the University of Insubria in Italy, Inagro and Thomas More. The project aims to deepen our understanding of insect physiology, biology and behaviour to improve rearing strategies and support the production of safe, high-quality insect-based products with desirable biological and nutritional properties.

Your PhD will address a central question within the project: How do black soldier fly larvae respond behaviourally to different rearing conditions, and how are these responses related to larval growth, survival and production performance?

To investigate this, you will study larval behaviour using an advanced camera-based sensor platform already developed and operational within the research team. The platform combines high-resolution RGB imaging, visible and near-infrared multispectral imaging, and thermal imaging. These measurements will be complemented by gas-emission monitoring, including carbon dioxide, ammonia, nitrous oxide and methane, and by conventional rearing parameters such as larval growth and survival, substrate humidity, pH and composition.

Your role

You will work alongside a PhD researcher with an engineering background who continues to develop the sensor hardware and computer-vision algorithms used to extract movement and behavioural information from the images.

Your primary focus will be the biological research: translating research questions into experiments, analysing behavioural data and interpreting the results in relation to environmental conditions, larval physiology and production performance.

You will take ownership of the biological questions and statistical analysis while working closely with the engineering team to understand how sensor data are generated and how they can be used to answer those questions. Previous experience with computer vision is not required; curiosity about the technology and a willingness to learn are what matter.

What will you do?

Design and conduct experiments: develop and implement rearing experiments to investigate how different environmental and stress-linked conditions affect larval behaviour and production performance.

Analyse behavioural data: work with the engineering team to extract meaningful behavioural features from camera-based sensor data and analyse behavioural time series.

Connect behaviour to production: use statistical modelling to investigate relationships between behavioural patterns, environmental conditions, growth and survival.

Investigate physiological responses: collaborate with researchers at the University of Antwerp to link behavioural observations to metabolic markers associated with stress.

Communicate your findings: publish your results in international peer-reviewed journals and present your research at scientific conferences, contributing to the development of precision insect farming.

You will be supported by KU Leuven experts in insect production and processing and livestock technology. Experiments will take place at the SymBIOnt Insect Pilot Plant of KU Leuven and Thomas More in Geel, as well as at Inagro's insect-rearing facilities.

At the Toxicological Centre of the University of Antwerp, a fellow PhD researcher is developing and validating a metabolomics platform to identify biomarkers associated with stress in black soldier fly larvae. By combining your behavioural research with this work, you will help build a more comprehensive understanding of the biological responses of larvae to challenging rearing conditions.

Ultimately, a better understanding of these responses can help identify opportunities to optimize rearing strategies, improve production efficiency and, in the longer term, contribute to production systems that better account for insect welfare.

Profile

We are looking for a curious and motivated PhD candidate who enjoys asking biological questions, working with data and collaborating across disciplines.

You:

Hold a Master's degree in biology, biosciences, bioscience engineering, animal sciences or an equivalent field. Candidates with a Master's degree in data science and a strong interest in biology are also encouraged to apply.

Have a strong interest in animal behaviour (ethology), insect biology and the relationship between environmental conditions and biological responses.

Are eager to investigate how rearing conditions influence larval behaviour, physiology and production performance.

Enjoy working with data and are motivated to take responsibility for the statistical analysis and interpretation of your experiments.

Are interested in how sensor technology and data analysis can advance biological research, and are willing to learn the basic principles of computer vision in collaboration with the engineering team.

Have a critical, analytical, creative and innovative mindset.

Have good written and oral communication skills in English.

Enjoy working in an international, multidisciplinary research environment and collaborating with researchers from different backgrounds.

The following experience is an advantage, but not a requirement:

Insect rearing or entomological research, particularly involving black soldier fly larvae.

Designing and conducting behavioural or animal experiments.

Statistical analysis, including mixed-effects models, multivariate analysis or time-series analysis.

Scientific data processing using R, Python, MATLAB or equivalent software.

Experience with computer vision and machine learning.

Eligibility condition: To be eligible for this position, you must hold a Master's degree with at least distinction, obtained within the last three years at a university in the European Economic Area (EEA).

Offer

We offer a full-time PhD position with a competitive salary for four years, starting as soon as possible.

You will join a multidisciplinary research project with an operational sensor platform and access to pilot-scale insect-rearing facilities. This allows you to focus on biological research questions from the start, while benefiting from close collaboration with researchers in engineering, insect biology and metabolomics.

You can expect:

Hands-on research: design and conduct experiments using dedicated insect-rearing and sensor facilities.

Interdisciplinary collaboration: work closely with biologists, engineers and fellow researchers across several research institutions.

Scientific development: receive guidance and training to develop your research skills and complete your PhD.

International exposure: present your work at conferences, publish scientific papers and build your professional network.

Doctoral training: enrol in KU Leuven's Arenberg Doctoral School, which offers a broad programme in scientific and transferable skills.

You will work in a young, dynamic and multidisciplinary team that will support you throughout your doctoral research. Your main workplace will be KU Leuven campus Geel. Knowledge of Dutch is not required.

ap:254429.body:
Materials science and technology are our passion. With our cutting-edge research, Empa's around 1,100 employees make essential contributions to the well-being of society for a future worth living. Empa is a research institution of the ETH Domain.
The Laboratory for Acoustics/Noise Control is an international team of scientists and engineers active in the fields of vibroacoustics, environmental acoustics, and psychoacoustics. The diverse research topics rely on extensive numerical models and a broad range of experimental equipment for noise and vibration measurements.

Mechanical waves and vibrations are traditionally controlled using linear devices with fixed properties. In this PhD project, the student will explore a new generation of nonlinear resonators whose dynamic behaviour changes with vibration amplitude, enabling functionalities that are not achievable with conventional designs. The research will combine mechanical modelling, finite-element simulations, prototype development, and experimental testing. The goal is to develop efficient models and design rules for nonlinear metamaterials capable of adaptive vibration isolation, frequency conversion, and non-reciprocal wave propagation. The successful candidate will work within a collaborative Swiss-French project involving Empa, ETH Zurich, and LAUM.

PhD position in the field of nonlinear vibrational metamaterials
Your tasks
As doctoral candidate within this project you will work on highly nonlinear building blocks for vibrational metamaterials. Specific tasks to achieve the challenging results include
Develop analytical and numerical models for strongly nonlinear resonators exhibiting nonlinear stiffness, damping, and inertia effects.
Design, simulate, and optimize novel resonator concepts based on inertia amplification, bilinear stiffness, and multi-degree-of-freedom dynamics.
Manufacture and experimentally characterize resonator prototypes using vibration testing, laser vibrometry, and modal analysis techniques.
Investigate nonlinear phenomena such as internal resonances, frequency conversion, bifurcations, and nonlinear energy transfer.
Create reduced-order models and efficient simulation tools for the design of nonlinear metamaterials and wave-control devices.
Disseminate research results through publications in leading journals, presentations at international conferences, and collaboration with project partners at ETH Zurich and the Université du Mans.

Your profile
If you recognize yourself in the story below, then you have the profile that fits the project and the research group:  I have a master degree in engineering, physics or mathematics performed above average in comparison to my peers.
I am proficient in written and spoken English.
During my courses or prior professional activities, I have gathered some experience with at least one of the following: structural and/or nonlinear dynamics, numerical modelling techniques (finite element method), or experimental methods in acoustics. I have a profound interest for these topics.
As a researcher I perform research in a structured and scientifically sound manner. I read technical papers, understand the nuances between different theories and implement and improve methodologies myself.
In frequent reporting, varying between weekly to monthly, I show the results that I have obtained and I give a well-founded interpretation of those results. I iterate on my work and my approach based on the feedback of my supervisors which steer the direction of my research.
It's important for me to work as an active team member and I am eager to share my results to inspire and being inspired by my colleagues.
During my PhD I want to grow towards more independence, e.g. representing the research group on project meetings and conferences. I see these events as an occasion to disseminate my work to an audience of international experts and research colleagues, and to learn about the larger context of my research and the research project.

Our offer
We offer a fully funded 4-year PhD position at Empa. The candidate will also be enrolled as a PhD student at the ETH Zürich, co-supervised by Dr. Paolo Tiso. The core of the PhD project will be conducted at Empa with at least one research secondment in Le Mans and intense collaboration with the Chair in Nonlinear Dynamics at ETHZ. Besides ample occasions to develop yourself in a scientific and/or industrial direction offered by the research group, further doctoral training for PhD candidates is provided in the framework of the Doctoral School .
Starting date is February 2027 or upon mutual agreement.

You stay in a vibrant environment centrally in Europe. Empa has its main campus in Dübendorf, located close to Zürich and 20 minutes by tram from Zurich International Airport. Zurich is one of the cities with the highest quality of life worldwide, welcoming to non-German speaking people and with ample opportunities for social, cultural, and outdoor activities.

We foster a culture of inclusion and respect. We welcome all people who are interested in innovative, sustainable and meaningful activities. Our commitment is documented in our Diversity Action Plan and refers to specific goals, which are implemented and further developed on a regular basis.
You don't meet every single requirement? We are aware that particularly women and individuals from minority backgrounds often hesitate to apply unless they meet every requirement. However, we also value motivation, commitment and a willingness to learn. If you see yourself in this role, we would love to receive your qualified application, even if you don't meet 100% of the requirements.
We look forward to receiving your complete online application including a letter of motivation, CV, certificates, diplomas and contact details of two reference persons. Please submit these exclusively via our job portal. Applications by e-mail and by post will not be considered.
