ap:254456.body:
1 - Werken bij de VUB
De Vrije Universiteit Brussel staat al meer dan 50 jaar voor vrijheid, gelijk(waardig)heid en verbondenheid , en dat leeft sterk op onze campussen bij zowel studenten als personeel.
Bij de VUB vind je een diverse verzameling aan persoonlijkheden: innovators pur sang, maar vooral mensen die 100% hun authentieke zelf zijn . Met zo’n 4.000 medewerkers zijn we de grootste Nederlandstalige werkgever, in de privésector, in Brussel ; een internationale stad waarmee we ons maar al te graag verbinden en waar(rond) onze 4 campussen gelegen zijn.
Voeg daarbij ons beginsel van vrij onderzoek - waarin zelfreflectie, een kritische houding en een open, creatieve geest rond wetenschappelijke en maatschappelijke vraagstukken centraal staan - en je hebt een universiteit die fundamenteel grensverleggend en pionierend is op het vlak van onderwijs en onderzoek. Kortom: de VUB ten voeten uit .
De VUB is bovendien lid van EUTOPIA , een alliantie van gelijkgestemde Europese universiteiten, allen klaar om zichzelf opnieuw uit te vinden.
2 - Functie
Momenteel zijn we voor de Onderzoeksbursalen van de  Faculteit Ingenieurswetenschappen , vakgroep Toegepaste mechanica , onderzoeksgroep Thermodynamics and Fluid Mechanics  op zoek naar een doctoraatsbursaal .
Meer concreet zal je takenpakket, ter voorbereiding van een doctoraat , er als volgt uitzien:
Wij bieden een voltijdse doctoraatspositie aan in het kader van het ERC Starting Grant-project “Energising the future with clean plasma-based technologies” (ESCAPADE, proposal number 101302707). Plasma-assisted combustion (PAC) biedt veelbelovende perspectieven voor een schonere en efficiëntere verbranding van duurzame brandstoffen. De verdere industriële toepassing wordt echter beperkt door het ontbreken van voorspellende computermodellen die de complexe interacties tussen plasmaontladingen, chemische reacties en vlamdynamica nauwkeurig kunnen beschrijven.
ESCAPADE pakt deze uitdaging aan door een innovatief multiphysics-simulatiekader te ontwikkelen dat modellering op basis van eerste principes combineert met machine learning, reduced-order technieken en computational fluid dynamics (CFD). Het project zal een nieuwe generatie voorspellende tools opleveren voor het ontwerp en de optimalisatie van verbrandingssystemen met lage emissies die werken op zowel duurzame als conventionele brandstoffen.
De onderzoeksgroep FLOW van de VUB beschikt over uitgebreide expertise in zowel fundamenteel als toegepast onderzoek naar de modellering van thermo-fluid systemen, met toepassingen in de luchtvaart (aerodynamica, flow control), ruimtevaart (atmosferische terugkeer, ruimtevaartplasma's) en energie (windenergie, bio-energie, waterstof, warmtenetten en verbranding). Sinds 2021 werkt FLOW samen met de ATM-onderzoeksgroep van de ULB binnen de gezamenlijke onderzoeksgroep BRITE (Brussels Institute for Thermal-fluid Systems and clean Energy, https://brite-research.be).
Plasma-assisted combustion combineert plasmaontladingen met verbrandingsprocessen om ontsteking, vlamstabiliteit en emissies van verontreinigende stoffen te verbeteren voor duurzame brandstoffen. Hoewel gedetailleerde state-to-state plasmaverbrandingsmodellen een ongeziene beschrijving bieden van de onderliggende fysica, blijft hun rekenkost te hoog voor multidimensionale simulaties en industriële toepassingen.
Dit doctoraatsproject heeft als doel de volgende generatie computationele tools voor plasma-assisted combustion te ontwikkelen door gedetailleerde state-to-state kinetische modellering, mechanismereductie en physics-informed machine learning te combineren. De onderzoeker zal bijdragen aan de ontwikkeling van geavanceerde simulatiecodes die plasmaontladingen, chemie en verbrandingsprocessen expliciet kunnen modelleren over een breed scala aan operationele omstandigheden.
Een centraal doel van het project is de ontwikkeling van nieuwe reductiemethodologieën voor omvangrijke state-to-state kinetische mechanismen met honderden tot duizenden soorten en reacties. Voortbouwend op recente ontwikkelingen zoals plasma-directed relation graph-technieken (P-DRGEP), principal component analysis en machine-learninggebaseerde lumping-strategieën, zal de doctoraatsstudent reduced-order modellen met hoge nauwkeurigheid ontwikkelen die de essentiële plasma-verbrandingsinteracties behouden en tegelijk de rekenkost aanzienlijk verminderen.
De ontwikkelde methodologieën zullen worden geïntegreerd in intern ontwikkelde plasma-assisted combustion solvers en gevalideerd aan de hand van experimentele benchmarkdatasets die worden aangeleverd door toonaangevende internationale projectpartners. Bijzondere aandacht gaat uit naar ammoniak- en waterstofverbrandingssystemen, die worden beschouwd als veelbelovende koolstofvrije brandstoffen voor toekomstige energie- en voortstuwingssystemen.
De resulterende gereduceerde modellen zullen de rechtstreekse integratie van gedetailleerde plasmachemie mogelijk maken binnen geavanceerde CFD-omgevingen, waaronder DNS- en LES-simulaties van realistische verbrandingssystemen.
Referenties:
-Rekkas-Ventiris, G., Giuntini, L., Sabia, P., Sorrentino, G., & Bellemans, A. (2026). Numerical investigation of plasma-assisted MILD combustion of ammonia using a hybrid modeling approach. Fuel , 406 , 136751.
-Rekkas-Ventiris, G., Gomez, A. D., Deak, N., Kincaid, N., Pepiot, P., Bisetti, F., & Bellemans, A. (2024). A novel machine learning based lumping approach for the reduction of large kinetic mechanisms for plasma-assisted combustion applications. Combustion and Flame , 260 , 113252.

Voor deze functie zal onze Brussels Humanities, Sciences & Engineering Campus (Elsene) je thuisbasis worden.
3 - Profiel
Wat verwachten wij van jou?
Je bent in het bezit van een Master in de Ingenieurswetenschappen, Toegepaste Wiskunde, Fysica, Computational Science of een verwante discipline;

Je hebt een sterke achtergrond in numerieke methoden en wetenschappelijk programmeren;
Je beschikt over uitstekende programmeervaardigheden (Python, Fortran en/of C++);
Je bent geïnteresseerd in chemische kinetiek, plasmafysica, verbranding, reduced-order modellering en machine learning;
Je ervaring met CFD-, DNS- en/of LES-methodologieën is een pluspunt;
Je ervaring met technieken voor kinetische mechanismereductie, data-driven modellering of high-performance computing is een pluspunt;
Je beschikt over uitstekende schriftelijke en mondelinge kennis van het Engels;
Je hebt sterke analytische vaardigheden en het vermogen om zowel zelfstandig als binnen een internationaal onderzoeksteam te werken.

Je hebt geen werkzaamheden verricht in het kader van een mandaat als assistent bezoldigd ten laste van de werkingsmiddelen, gedurende meer dan 12 maanden (gecumuleerd).

Als (niet-)EER-onderdaan dien je te voldoen aan de voorwaarden voor het verkrijgen van een rechtsgeldige vergunning voor VUB, en dien je te voldoen aan de VUB verblijfsvoorwaarden. Meer info vind je hier .

VUB wil een weerspiegeling zijn van de maatschappij waar ieders talent wordt gewaardeerd, ongeacht het gender, geslacht, leeftijd, religie, huidskleur, migratieachtergrond, functiebeperking en de neurodiversiteit.
4 - Aanbod
Word jij onze nieuwe collega?
Dan bieden we je een voltijdse doctoraatsbeurs aan, voor de duur van  12 maanden (verlengbaar tot max. 48 maanden, mits positieve evaluatie van de doctoraatswerkzaamheden), met voorziene startdatum 01/02/2027.
Je ontvangt een beursbedrag gekoppeld aan een van de barema’s die door de overheid worden vastgelegd.
OPGELET: De effectieve uitwerking van de doctoraatsbeurs is onderworpen aan de opschortende voorwaarde van jouw inschrijving als doctoraatsstudent aan de universiteit.
Bij de VUB garanderen we een open, betrokken en diverse werkplek en bieden we je kansen om je carrière (verder) uit te bouwen.
Daarnaast geniet je van voordelen als:
Uitgebreide thuiswerkmogelijkheden , een telewerkvergoeding van 50 euro per maand OF een internetvergoeding van 20 euro per maand;
Een open informele werkomgeving met aandacht voor je work-life balance , een uitzonderlijke verlofregeling met 35 verlofdagen (bij voltijdse tewerkstelling), sluiting tussen Kerstmis en Nieuwjaar, en 3 extra verlofdagen;
Een kosteloze hospitalisatieverzekering ;
Maximale terugbetaling van woon-werkverkeer met het openbaar vervoer en/of een fietsvergoeding;
Gevarieerde maaltijden in onze campusrestaurants aan een aantrekkelijk tarief;
Voordelige sportmogelijkheden , een gamma aan kortingen via Benefits@Work (in allerlei winkels, op vluchten, in tankstations, pretparken...) en Ecocheques ;
Kinderdagverblijf vlak bij de campus, korting op vakantiekampen ;
De ruimte om je job-inhoud mee te vormen en voortdurend bij te leren via onze VUB-leerplatformen en opleidingen;
En tot slot: toffe collega's met een gezonde drive.

5 - Geïnteresseerd?
Spreekt deze functie je aan?
Stel je dan kandidaat, ten laatste op 15/11/2026 ,  via jobs.vub.be , en laad volgende documenten op:
je motivatiebrief;
je curriculum vitae;
je diploma’s (niet van toepassing voor VUB-alumni).

Ons sollicitatieproces ziet er als volgt uit (onder voorbehoud van wijzigingen):
stap 1: een eerste selectie op basis van je sollicitatiedossier;
stap 2: een job-interview.

Heb je vragen over deze functie? Contacteer dan Prof. Aurélie Bellemans via [email protected] .
Wil je graag weten hoe het is om te werken bij de VUB? Ga dan naar jobs.vub.be , en ontdek alles over o.a. onze campussen, voordelen, strategische doelen en collega’s.
Wil je meer info over EUTOPIA? Ga dan naar eutopia-university.eu , en kom meer te weten over ons Europees netwerk van universiteiten.

ap:254458.body:
Om stillingen
Er du strukturert, serviceinnstilt og engasjert i studentenes studiehverdag? Så er det deg vi ser etter.
På Fakultet for helsevitenskap ved Seksjon for studieadministrasjon og internasjonalisering, er det ledig en fast 100% stilling som førstekonsulent/seniorkonsulent.
Seksjonen har ansvar for utvikling og forvaltning av studieadministrative regelverk og rutiner. Vi arbeider med studentforvaltning, rapportering, eksamensadministrasjon, internasjonalisering og brukerstøtte for studieadministrative systemer.
Seksjonen består av tre studieadministrative kontorer og denne stillingen er tilknyttet studieadministrativt kontor på Campus Kjeller som består av 15 ansatte.
Vi søker deg som er god i møte med studenter, som er nøyaktig og effektiv er god på digitale systemer, og som ønsker å være en god støttespiller for de vitenskapelig ansatte.
Hos oss blir du en del av et faglig sterkt og inkluderende arbeidsmiljø med engasjerte kolleger som samarbeider tett om å utvikle og levere gode tjenester til studenter og fagmiljøer.
Stillingen er ledig fra dags dato og arbeidsstedet er Campus Kjeller.
Arbeidsoppgaver og ansvarsområder
saksbehandling av studentsaker og forvaltning av studieprogram, eksempelvis behandle søknader om permisjon, tilrettelegging, klagebehandling og saker knyttet til fusk
utføre studieadministrative oppgaver i forbindelse med eksamensgjennomføringer
veiledning, rådgiving og informasjonsarbeid for studenter
andre studieadministrative oppgaver

Oppgavene vil variere over tid, og du må være innstilt på at du kan få andre oppgaver innenfor seksjonens ansvarsområde.
Kvalifikasjonskrav
utdanning fra høgskole/universitet på minimum bachelornivå. Meget god og relevant praksis kan kompensere for kravet til formell utdanning.
god skriftlig og muntlig fremstillingsevne i norsk og engelsk
relevant studieadministrativ erfaring
god kjennskap til lovverk tilknyttet UH-sektoren
erfaring med saksbehandling fra offentlig sektor eller tilsvarende

Det vil være en fordel om du har
god digital kunnskap
du kjenner til og har relevant erfaring med et eller flere av våre systemer og saksbehandlerverktøy (timeplanleggingssystem TP, studentsystemet FS, Public 360 og læringsplattformen Canvas eller tilsvarende systemer)

Personlige egenskaper
gode kommunikasjons- og samarbeidsevner
god vurderingsevneevne til å finne løsninger og tenke nytt
evne til å prioritere og håndtere ulike arbeidsoppgaver
nøyaktig, strukturert, effektiv og serviceinnstilt
gode kommunikasjons- og samarbeidsevner

Personlig egnethet vil bli vektlagt.
Det er viktig for OsloMet å gjenspeile befolkningen i vår region og vi ønsker alle kvalifiserte søkere velkommen. Vi arbeider aktivt med å utvikle oss videre som en inkluderende arbeidsplass og for å tilrettelegge arbeidsplassen dersom du har behov for det. Har du perioder i livet hvor du ikke har vært i arbeid, utdanning eller opplæring er du også velkommen til å søke hos oss.
Vi kan tilby deg
spennende jobb på Norges tredje største og mest urbane universitet
varierte arbeidsoppgaver med muligheter for faglig utvikling
et godt arbeidsmiljø som er preget av samarbeid og engasjement
en arbeidsplass i utvikling
låne- og pensjonsbetingelser i Statens Pensjonskasse
fleksibel arbeidstid og gode velferdsordninger

Stillingen lønnes, i henhold til Hovedtariffavtalene i staten og OsloMets lønnspolitikk i stillingskode 1408 førstekonsulent, kroner 517000 - 600000 evnt. 1363 seniorkonsulent kr. 546000 - 662000 per år. For spesielt kvalifiserte søkere kan høyere lønn vurderes. Fra lønnen trekkes 2 % pensjonsinnskudd til Statens pensjonskasse (SPK).
Søknadsprosess
Vil du søke på stillingen må du søke via vårt rekrutteringssystem.
Innen søknadsfristen må du laste opp følgende dokumenter:
søknadsbrev
CV, attester og alle sider av vitnemål
gjerne kontaktinformasjon til to referanser

Vi behandler kun søknader sendt via vårt elektroniske rekrutteringssystem og alle dokumenter, attester og alle sider av vitnemål må lastes opp for at din søknad skal behandles. Dokumentene må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Oversettelser må være autorisert og du må påregne å fremvise originaler ved et eventuelt intervju. OsloMet gjennomfører kontroll av dokumenter, slik at du som kandidat skal få en reell evaluering og rettferdig konkurranse. Ufullstendige søknader vil ikke bli tatt til vurdering.
For aktuelle stillinger gjennomfører OsloMet bakgrunnssjekk av søkere i samarbeid med en ekstern leverandør, for å verifisere opplysninger som fremgår av tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med kandidatens samtykke, og ansettelse i disse stillingene forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette.
Andre opplysninger
Ønsker du nærmere informasjon om stillingen kan du kontakte
konstorsjef Kristine Sandaker, tlf: 67236244, e-post: [email protected]
for spørsmål av administrativ karakter, kontakt HR rådgiver Hanne Christensen Eckholm på e-post: [email protected]

Informasjon til deg som søker
Inkludering og mangfold styrker vår evne til å løse OsloMets samfunnsoppdrag. Derfor ønsker vi medarbeidere med ulike kompetanser, livserfaringer og perspektiver velkommen. Vi arbeider kontinuerlig for å være en inkluderende arbeidsplass, og gjennom dialog tilrettelegger vi for medarbeidere som har behov for det.
Opplysninger om deg som søker kan publiseres på den offentlige søkerlisten selv om har bedt om at søknaden behandles konfidensielt. Hvis det skjer, vil du bli varslet om det før publiseringen.
Ansettelsen blir gjennomført etter prinsippene i statsansatteloven og lovverk som regulerer eksport av kunnskap, teknologi og tjenester. Søkere som er i konflikt med dette regelverket vil ikke anses kvalifisert for stillingen.
OsloMet er Charter & Code -sertifisert av EU-kommisjonen med rett til å bruke logoen HR Excellence in Research (HRS4R) og er medlem i nettverket EURAXESS , som bidrar til gode arbeidsvilkår for mobile forskere.
OsloMet har sluttet seg til prinsippene og forpliktet institusjonen til å følge anbefalingene i DORA-erklæringen (sfdora.org) (The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment).
Besøk OsloMet på LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram
OsloMet - storbyuniversitetet
OsloMet - storbyuniversitetet er Norges tredje største universitet med 23 000 studenter og over 2600 ansatte. Vi har campus i Oslo Sentrum og på Romerike. OsloMet leverer forskning og utdanning med høy relevans for arbeidslivet, velferdsstaten og storbyregionen.
I over 200 år har OsloMet – storbyuniversitetet bidratt til å bygge kunnskap og kompetanse for det norske velferdssamfunnet. I dag er OsloMet et moderne og urbant universitet som er kjent for sine store og solide fagmiljøer innenfor lærerutdanning, helse- og sosialfag, samfunnsforskning, design og teknologifag.

ap:254462.body:
Arbetsuppgifter
Inom avdelningen driver vi ett stort antal forskningsprojekt i nära samverkan med samhällsaktörer. Målet är att skapa värde av hälsodata på samhälls-, individ- och vårdnivå. Dataharmonisering, kunskapsgrafer, visualisering och deltagande metoder är centrala kompetenser för att utveckla meningsfulla projekt.
Avdelningen har många studenter, och vi söker en forskare som kan bygga framgångsrika samarbeten mellan samhällsaktörernas behov och studenternas samlade kompetens. Vi ser utbildning i nära koppling till forskning som en viktig modell för att skapa genomslag.
Kvalifikationer
Krav
Avlagd doktorsexamen eller utländsk examen som bedöms motsvara en doktorsexamen.
Du har vetenskaplig skicklighet inom datavetenskap inom hälsoområdet eller närliggande ämne.
Du har erfarenhet av att driva forskningsprojekt i samverkan med samhälsaktörer, framförallt inom offentlig sektor kring hälsofrågor.
Du kan driva och utveckla projekt kring hälsodata och är mycket erfaren i hantering av kunskapsgrafer, molntjänster och kubernetes miljöer.
Du har ett pedagogiskt förhållningssätt samt pedagogiska förmågor för att kunna inkludera (master) studenter i dina projekt.
Du är självständigt, och kan samverka med en bred rad olika roller för att åstadkomma genomslag med forskningen.

Meriterande
Bekantskap med svenska öppna datakällor inom offentlig verksamhet med vård och omsorg är meriterande.
Kunskap om mångfalds- och likabehandlingsfrågor med särskild fokus på jämställdhet

Vi kommer lägga stor vikt vid personliga egenskaper.
Bli en del av KTH
KTH formar framtiden genom utbildning, forskning och innovation. Som ett ledande internationellt tekniskt universitet spelar vi en aktiv roll i att driva och medverka i omställningen till ett hållbart samhälle. Här erbjuds du möjligheten att växa och utvecklas på en kreativ och dynamisk arbetsplats med goda arbetsvillkor och förmåner. Jämställdhet, mångfald och lika villkor är en kvalitetsfråga och en självklar del av KTH:s värdegrund som universitet och statlig myndighet.
Läs mer om våra förmåner och hur det är att arbeta och utvecklas på KTH .
Fackliga representanter
Kontaktuppgifter till   fackliga representanter .
Ansökan
Du ansöker via KTH:s rekryteringssystem. Du som sökande har huvudansvaret för att din ansökan är komplett när den skickas in.
Ansökan ska innehålla:
CV inklusive relevant yrkeserfarenhet och kunskap.
Kopia av examensbevis och betyg från dina tidigare universitetsstudier. Översättningar till engelska eller svenska om de ursprungliga dokumenten inte utfärdas på något av dessa språk.
Kortfattad redogörelse för varför du vill bedriva forskning, dina akademiska intressen och hur de relaterar till dina tidigare studier och framtida mål. max 2 sidor lång.

Ansökan ska vara KTH tillhanda senast sista ansökningsdagen vid midnatt, CET/CEST (CentralEuropean Time/Central European Summer Time).
Om anställningen
Anställningen gäller tidsbegränsat enligt avtal - i upp till 12 mån, med tillträde enligt överenskommelse.
Övrigt
För information om behandling av personuppgifter i samband med rekrytering.
Det kan förekomma att en anställning hos KTH är placerad i säkerhetsklass. Om så är fallet för just denna anställning görs en säkerhetsprövning av sökande i enlighet med säkerhetsskyddslagen (2018:585) efter samtycke. I dessa fall är en förutsättning för anställning att sökande blir godkänd efter säkerhetsprövning.
Vi undanber oss direktkontakt med bemannings- och rekryteringsföretag samt försäljare av platsannonser.

Arbetsuppgifter
Du kommer att arbeta som forskningsingenjör inom gruppen för kvantmaterial och bistå gruppens medlemmar i arbetet med att utveckla de experimentuppställningar som gruppen driver. ap:254469.body:
De doctoraatsstudent(e) wordt tewerkgesteld aan de KU Leuven, Departement Aard- en Omgevingswetenschappen, Afdeling Bodem- en Waterbeheer, in het SPIRAL-lab onder leiding van prof. Jean-Thomas Cornelis. De groep onderzoekt hoe bodemprocessen op microschaal de eigenschappen van ecosystemen op macroschaal bepalen, met focus op bodem–plant- terugkoppelingen, biogeochemische kringlopen en de weerstand, veerkracht en het herstel van ecosystemen. We werken in uiteenlopende bodems en eco-culturele contexten en hechten belang aan multidisciplinair, collaboratief en respectvol onderzoek.

SPIRAL staat voor Soil Genesis and Plant Interactions: Reciprocal feedbacks Across Landscapes. De groep werd opgericht aan de University of British Columbia (Canada) als het SoilRes3 Lab, en prof. Cornelis is net naar de KU Leuven overgestapt; meer over het onderzoek en de filosofie van de groep lees je op

Website van de eenheid

Project

Stikstof beperkt de plantenproductiviteit in veel terrestrische ecosystemen. Vrijlevende (asymbiotische) stikstoffixeerders in de rhizosfeer kunnen een aanzienlijke hoeveelheid stikstof leveren, zonder symbiose of kunstmest. Stikstoffixatie kost echter veel energie, en het enzym nitrogenase heeft molybdeen (Mo) nodig als cofactor, een sporenelement dat in bodems vaak slecht beschikbaar is.

Dit project test het idee dat de manier waarop planten dit proces actief kunnen sturen via hun wortelexsudaten sterk afhangt van bodemvormende processen. We veronderstellen dat de stoichiometrie tussen bodem en plant invloed heeft op (1) de vrijstelling door wortels van makkelijk afbreekbare koolhydraten die vrijlevende N-fixeerders van energie voorzien, en (2) carboxylaten (bv. citraat, malaat, oxalaat) die aan bodemmineralen gebonden Mo mobiliseren en beschikbaar maken voor nitrogenase. Samen kunnen deze mechanismen een positieve terugkoppeling vormen: meer ondergrondse plantenkoolstof voedt vrijlevende N- fixeerders en levert tegelijk het Mo dat de enzymatische fabriek nodig heeft. De bodemwatertoestand stuurt naar verwachting elke stap van deze kringloop.

Door wortelexsudatie, Mo-biogeochemie en microbiële N-fixatie aan elkaar te koppelen, wil het project begrijpen hoe planten en bodems samen de stikstofinput in terrestrische ecosystemen regelen, met toepassingen voor duurzame landbouw en ecosysteemherstel.

Als doctoraatsonderzoeker bestudeer je de interacties tussen plant, bodem, water en micro-organismen die vrijlevende N-fixatie in de rhizosfeer bepalen. Concreet zal je:

Wortelexsudatie (koolhydraten en carboxylaten) kwantificeren onder contrasterende bodem- en watercondities, met rhizoboxen, mesocosmen en/of veldproeven

Vrijlevende N-fixatie meten (bv. 15N2-incubaties, acetyleenreductietest) en koppelen aan de abundantie en activiteit van diazotrofen (bv. nifH-genmerkers)

Onderzoeken hoe carboxylaten Mo (en het daarmee geassocieerde Fe) uit bodemmineralen mobiliseren, met batchexperimenten, bodemfractionering en geavanceerde (isotopen)geochemische methoden

Nagaan hoe bodemvocht en droog–nat-cycli de exsudatie, de Mo-beschikbaarheid en de N-fixatie beïnvloeden

Deze resultaten integreren in een conceptueel en/of kwantitatief model van de positieve terugkoppeling tussen plant en bodem

Je resultaten publiceren in internationale tijdschriften, voorstellen op congressen en meewerken aan de begeleiding van masterstudenten

Profiel

Vereist

Een masterdiploma Bio-ingenieurswetenschappen, Bodemkunde, Milieuwetenschappen, Aardwetenschappen, Biologie, Chemie of een verwante richting

Een sterke achtergrond in bodemkunde en biogeochemie

Een sterke interesse in bodem–plant–water-interacties en terugkoppelingen in terrestrische ecosystemen Enthousiasme voor labo- en experimenteel werk

Goede schriftelijke en mondelinge kennis van het Engels

Nieuwsgierigheid, kritisch denkvermogen en het vermogen om zowel zelfstandig als in team te werken

Pluspunten

Ervaring met plantenproeven, rhizosfeerbemonstering of het verzamelen van wortelexsudaten

Ervaring met chemische bodemanalyses (bv. ICP-MS, chromatografie) of stabiele isotopen

Vertrouwdheid met bodemmicrobiologie

Vaardigheden in data-analyse (bv. R of Python)

Voldoe je niet aan alle punten? Solliciteer toch. Vaardigheden kan je leren, en we waarderen nieuwsgierigheid en motivatie evenveel als ervaring.

Aanbod

We bieden een competitieve voltijdse doctoraatsbeurs voor 1 jaar (verlengbaar met nog 3 jaar), volgens de doctoraatsbarema's van de KU Leuven.

Begeleiding door prof. Jean-Thomas Cornelis

Een stimulerende, internationale en multidisciplinaire onderzoeksomgeving met toegang tot moderne labo-infrastructuur Een flexibele werkorganisatie die ruimte laat voor creativiteit en nieuwe ideeën

Kansen voor opleiding, deelname aan congressen en internationale samenwerking Lidmaatschap van de Doctoral School van de KU Leuven en haar opleidingsprogramma

De KU Leuven biedt bijkomende voordelen zoals een hospitalisatieverzekering, openbaar vervoer aan verminderd tarief, gratis fietsgebruik, toegang tot de universitaire sportfaciliteiten en kinderopvang, en nog meer. Interesse?

We moedigen je van harte aan om huidige en vroegere leden van de groep te contacteren over onze onderzoeksomgeving.

ap:254470.body:
The PhD candidate will be based at KU Leuven, Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences, Division of Soil and Water Management, in the SPIRAL lab led by Prof. Jean-Thomas Cornelis. The group studies how microscale soil processes drive macroscale ecosystem properties, with a focus on soil–plant feedbacks, biogeochemical cycles and ecosystem resistance, resilience and restoration. We work across diverse soils and eco-cultural contexts, and we value multi-disciplinary, collaborative and respectful science.

SPIRAL stands for Soil Genesis and Plant Interactions: Reciprocal feedbacks Across Landscapes. The group was founded at the University of British Columbia (Canada) as the SoilRes3 Lab and Prof. Cornelis has just moved to KU Leuven; read more about their research and philosophy at

Website unit

Project

Nitrogen limits plant productivity in many terrestrial ecosystems. Free-living (asymbiotic) nitrogen fixers in the rhizosphere can supply a significant amount of nitrogen, without relying on symbiosis or synthetic fertiliser. However, nitrogen fixation is energetically very costly, and the nitrogenase enzyme needs molybdenum (Mo) as a co-factor, a trace element that is often poorly available in soils.

This project tests the idea that the way plants can actively steer this process through their root exudates is highly dependent on soil-forming processes. We hypothesise that soil-plant stoichiometry influences (1) the root release of easily degradable carbohydrates that fuel free-living N fixers as an energy source, and (2) carboxylates (e.g. citrate, malate, oxalate) that mobilise Mo bound to soil minerals and make it available for nitrogenase. Together, these mechanisms may create a positive feedback loop: more belowground plant carbon fuel free-living N fixers while supplying Mo needed for the enzymatic factory. Soil water conditions are expected to modulate each step of this loop.

By linking root exudation, Mo biogeochemistry and microbial N fixation, the project aims to understand how plants and soils co-regulate nitrogen inputs to terrestrial ecosystems, with implications for sustainable agriculture and ecosystem restoration.

As a PhD researcher, you will investigate the plant–soil–water–microbe interactions that control free-living N fixation in the rhizosphere. More specifically, you will:

Quantify root exudation (carbohydrates and carboxylates) under contrasting soil and water conditions, using rhizoboxes, mesocosms and/or field experiments

Measure free-living N fixation rates (e.g. 15N2 incubations, acetylene reduction assay) and link them to the abundance and activity of diazotrophs (e.g. nifH gene markers)

Study how carboxylates mobilise Mo (and associated Fe) from soil minerals, using batch experiments, soil fractionation and advanced (isotope) geochemical tools

Investigate how soil moisture and drying–rewetting cycles affect exudation, Mo availability and N fixation

Integrate these results into a conceptual and/or quantitative model of the plant–soil positive feedback loop

Publish your results in international journals, present them at conferences, and contribute to the supervision of master’s students

Profile

Required

A master’s degree in Bioscience Engineering, Soil Science, Environmental Sciences, Earth Sciences, Biology, Chemistry or a related field

A strong background in soil science and biogeochemistry

A strong interest in soil–plant–water interactions and feedbacks in terrestrial ecosystems

Enthusiasm for laboratory and experimental work

Good written and spoken English

Curiosity, critical thinking, and the ability to work both independently and in a team

Assets

Experience with plant growth experiments, rhizosphere sampling or root exudate collection

Experience with soil chemical analyses (e.g. ICP-MS, chromatography) or stable isotopes

Familiarity with soil microbiology

Skills in data analysis (e.g. R or Python)

You don’t tick every box? Please apply anyway. Skills can be learned, and we value curiosity and motivation as much as experience.

Offer

We offer a competitive full-time PhD scholarship for 1 year (renewable for another 3 years) in accordance with KU Leuven's doctoral salary scale.

Supervision by Prof. Jean-Thomas Cornelis

A stimulating, international and multi-disciplinary research environment, with access to state-of-the-art laboratory facilities

Flexible work organisation that leaves room for creativity and new ideas

Opportunities for training, conference participation and international collaboration

Membership of the KU Leuven Doctoral School and its training programme

KU Leuven offers additional benefits in terms of health insurance, public transport at reduced rates, free bicycle use, access to university sports facilities, childcare opportunities – among others. You can find more information on working conditions at KU Leuven on the below-mentioned website.

Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences
Division of Soil & Water Management
Working conditions at KU Leuven
Arenberg Doctoral School

Interested?

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Jean-Thomas Cornelis, mail: [email protected] .

We warmly encourage you to reach out to current and former lab members to hear about our research environment.

Please include a CV, a motivation letter (max. 1 page), transcripts of your bachelor’s and master’s degrees, and the contact details of two referees.

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

Het Leuven Centre for Public Law onder de Onderzoekseenheid Publiekrecht bestaat uit een dynamische mengeling van academische onderzoekers en gerespecteerde praktijkexperten uit zowel de magistratuur, de advocatuur als diverse instellingen. Expertise binnen het Belgische publiekrecht wordt gecombineerd met een internationale en interdisciplinaire visie en netwerk. Wij willen een onderzoeks- en onderwijsomgeving creëren die zowel wetenschappelijk gegrond als praktisch georiënteerd is, en dit vanuit een uitgesproken maatschappelijke verantwoordelijkheidszin.

Functie

Je zal onderwijs(assistentie) verlenen binnen de werking van de onderzoekseenheid voor opleidingsonderdelen die raken aan het omgevingsrecht (milieurecht en ruimtelijk bestuursrecht) in ruime zin.

Tot jouw takenpakket behoort eerst en vooral het begeleiden van masterproeven, zowel reguliere Master en LL.M. masterproeven als potentieel ook Engage masterproeven.

Je bezit een diploma van master in de rechten (of gelijkwaardig).

Je hebt een bijzondere belangstelling voor het omgevingsrecht, en bent momenteel actief of beschikt over voorbije praktijkervaring binnen dit rechtsgebied.

Om stillingen
Ved Universitetet i Agder er det ledig fast 100 % stilling som studierådgiver ved Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap . Stillingen er knyttet til fakultetsadministrasjonen og hovedarbeidssted er Campus Kristiansand. Det må påregnes arbeidsdager ved begge campus.  Tiltredelsesdato avtales med fakultetet.
Fakultet for helse- og idrettsvitenskap har ca. 250 ansatte, hvorav 28 er tilknyttet fakultetsadministrasjonen, og er lokalisert i Kristiansand og Grimstad. Fakultetet har fem institutter; Institutt for helse- og sykepleievitenskap, Institutt for ernæring og folkehelse, Institutt for idrettsvitenskap og kroppsøving, Institutt for psykososial helse og Institutt for psykologi. Instituttene har alle utdanning innen sine fagområder på bachelor, master og ph.d.-nivå og tilbyr en rekke etter- og videreutdanninger.

Mer om UiA som arbeidsplass .
Stillingen er plassert i Statens lønnsregulativ lønnsplan 90.500, kode 1434 rådgiver kr. 640 000 – 700 000 brutto pr. år. For spesielt godt kvalifiserte søkere kan høyere lønn vurderes. Fra lønnen går det lovfestet innskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.
Generell informasjon
UiA er et åpent og inkluderende universitet. Vi har tro på at mangfold beriker arbeidsplassen og gjør oss bedre. Vi oppfordrer derfor kvalifiserte kandidater til å søke uavhengig av kjønn, alder, kulturell bakgrunn, nedsatt funksjonsevne eller “hull i CV-en".
Menn oppfordres spesielt til å søke stillingen.
Den som ansettes har rettigheter og plikter etter de retningslinjer som gjelder for tekniske og administrative stillinger ved Universitetet i Agder, og må påregne endringer i organisering og oppgaver. Ansettelse foretas av Ansettelsesrådet for tekniske-/administrative stillinger ved Universitetet i Agder.
Det vil bli innhentet referanser for aktuelle kandidater etter nærmere avtale med søkeren. Det kan bli foretatt  bakgrunnssjekk  for å verifisere opplysninger som kommer frem av tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med søkerens samtykke, og ansettelse i stillingen forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette.
Mer om  ansettelsesprosessen.
I henhold til offentlighetsloven § 25, 2.ledd kan søker be om ikke å bli oppført på den offentlige søkerlista. Universitetet kan likevel beslutte at navnet på kandidaten skal offentliggjøres. Søker vil i forkant av eventuell offentliggjøring bli varslet.

ap:254473.body:
Om stillingen
Ønsker du en spennende jobb innen personvern? Fakultet for helsevitenskap, OsloMet
Rådgiver/seniorrådgiver innen personvern, 1-årig vikariat
I forbindelse med at en av våre ansatte skal ut i svangerskapspermisjon, har vi ledig et vikariat som personvernkontakt med arbeidsoppgaver innen personvern og informasjonssikkerhet. Stillingen er tilknyttet Fakultetets stab og rapporterer til fakultetsdirektør som nærmeste leder.
Som personvernkontakt vil du bistå personvernombudet og personvernansvarlig ved OsloMet, i tillegg til behandlingsansvarlige ved fakultetet med kontroll og overholdelse av personvernregelverket. I denne rollen vil du ha ansvar for å planlegge, koordinere og følge opp personvernkrav i arbeidsprosesser, behandlinger og prosjekter der personvern og informasjonssikkerhet er sentrale elementer. Sentralt i rollen er evnen til å kunne arbeide selvstendig og strukturert, i tett samarbeid med fakultetets fagmiljøer, herunder administrative og vitenskapelige miljøer. Du vil inngå i fakultetets nettverk for personvernkontakter, og vil også delta i flere nettverk sammen med andre personvernkontakter og andre faglige samarbeidspartnere ved OsloMet.
Arbeidsoppgaver og ansvarsområder
rådgivning, veiledning og saksbehandling i spørsmål om personvern
følge opp fakultetets rutiner og planer innen personvern
delta i nettverk for fakultetets personvernkontakter innen utdanning/administrasjon, og forskning
legge til rette for og bidra til kartlegginger som ROS-vurderinger og personvernkonsekvensvurderinger (DPIA), samt dokumentere og vedlikeholde protokoll over behandlingsaktiviteter
bidra ved utarbeidelse og inngåelse av databehandleravtaler og oppfølging av disse, samt avtaler om felles behandlingsansvar
vurdering av overføring til tredjeland, samt bistå ved inngåelse av SCC-avtaler
internkontroll (egenkontroll og rapportering)
bidra ved gjennomføring av opplæring og bevisstgjøring av ansatte

Oppgavene i stillingen vil til en viss grad kunne tilpasses kandidatens kompetanse innen fagområdet, i samråd med fakultetsdirektør.
OsloMet

Kvalifikasjonskrav
relevant høyere utdanning på minimum bachelornivå, eks. forvaltningsinformatikk, juss og informatikk (fortrinnsvis for seniorrådgiver)
kompetanse innen personvern/GDPR og informasjonssikkerhet
evne til å uttrykke deg godt skriftlig og muntlig på norsk og i engelsk
god IKT- og systemforståelse

Det vil være en fordel om du har
relevant mastergrad
erfaring fra arbeid med personvern, gjerne i større virksomheter
kjennskap til universitets- og høgskolesektoren

Personlige egenskaper
er analytisk og evner å sette deg inn i store mengder informasjon
er løsningsorientert, har god organisasjonsforståelse
jobber selvstendig, er ansvarsfull og serviceinnstilt
har gode samarbeidsevner og evne til å skape tillit og forklare sammenhenger på en enkel og pedagogisk måte

Personlig egnethet tillegges stor vekt.
Meget god og relevant praksis kan kompensere for kravet om formell utdanning i stilling som rådgiver.
Det er viktig for OsloMet å gjenspeile befolkningen i vår region og vi ønsker alle kvalifiserte søkere velkommen. Nyutdannede er også velkomne til å søke. Vi arbeider aktivt med å utvikle oss videre som en inkluderende arbeidsplass og for å tilrettelegge arbeidsplassen dersom du har behov for det. Har du perioder i livet hvor du ikke har vært i arbeid, utdanning eller opplæring er du også velkommen til å søke hos oss.
Vi kan tilby deg
spennende jobb på Norges tredje største og mest urbane universitet
arbeidsmiljø preget av behjelpelige og inkluderende kollegaer
stor grad av frihet under ansvar
låne- og pensjonsbetingelser i Statens Pensjonskasse
fleksibel arbeidstid og gode velferdsordninger
Stillingen er ledig fra 1. februar 2027 og har en varighet på ett år. Oppstart etter nærmere avtale

Stillingen lønnes i henhold til Hovedtariffavtalene i staten og OsloMets lønnspolitikk i stillingskode 1434 rådgiver kr 573 000 – 708 000 / 1364 seniorrådgiver kr 641 000–923 000. Fra lønnen trekkes 2 % pensjonsinnskudd til Statens pensjonskasse.
OsloMet

Søknadsprosess
Vil du søke på stillingen må du søke via vårt rekrutteringssystem.
Innen søknadsfristen må du laste opp følgende dokumenter:
søknadsbrev
CV, attester og alle sider av vitnemål
gjerne kontaktinformasjon til to referanser

Vi behandler kun søknader sendt via vårt elektroniske rekrutteringssystem og alle dokumenter, attester og alle sider av vitnemål må lastes opp for at din søknad skal behandles. Dokumentene må være på et skandinavisk språk eller engelsk. Oversettelser må være autorisert og du må påregne å fremvise originaler ved et eventuelt intervju. OsloMet gjennomfører kontroll av dokumenter, slik at du som kandidat skal få en reell evaluering og rettferdig konkurranse. Ufullstendige søknader vil ikke bli tatt til vurdering.
For aktuelle stillinger gjennomfører OsloMet bakgrunnssjekk av søkere i samarbeid med en ekstern leverandør, for å verifisere opplysninger som fremgår av tilgjengelige dokumenter. Bakgrunnssjekk skjer alltid med kandidatens samtykke, og ansettelse i disse stillingene forutsetter godkjent bakgrunnssjekk. Aktuelle søkere vil motta nærmere informasjon om dette.
Ønsker du nærmere informasjon om stillingen kan du kontakte:
Seniorrådgiver personavern Katarina Andreassen Håkstad, tlf 67236906, e.post: [email protected]
Fung. fakultetsdirektør Anne Blikra; tlf 91805657, e.post: [email protected]
For administrative spørsmål: rådgiver HR Kate Olsen, [email protected]

Søknadsfrist: 8. november
Ref: 26/20089
Informasjon til deg som søker
Inkludering og mangfold styrker vår evne til å løse OsloMets samfunnsoppdrag. Derfor ønsker vi medarbeidere med ulike kompetanser, livserfaringer og perspektiver velkommen. Vi arbeider kontinuerlig for å være en inkluderende arbeidsplass, og gjennom dialog tilrettelegger vi for medarbeidere som har behov for det.
Opplysninger om deg som søker kan publiseres på den offentlige søkerlisten selv om har bedt om at søknaden behandles konfidensielt. Hvis det skjer, vil du bli varslet om det før publiseringen.
Ansettelsen blir gjennomført etter prinsippene i statsansatteloven og lovverk som regulerer eksport av kunnskap, teknologi og tjenester. Søkere som er i konflikt med dette regelverket vil ikke anses kvalifisert for stillingen.
OsloMet er Charter & Code -sertifisert av EU-kommisjonen med rett til å bruke logoen HR Excellence in Research (HRS4R) og er medlem i nettverket EURAXESS , som bidrar til gode arbeidsvilkår for mobile forskere.
OsloMet har sluttet seg til prinsippene og forpliktet institusjonen til å følge anbefalingene i DORA-erklæringen (sfdora.org) (The San Francisco Declaration on Research Assessment).
Besøk OsloMet på LinkedIn , Facebook , Instagram
OsloMet - storbyuniversitetet
OsloMet - storbyuniversitetet er Norges tredje største universitet med 23 000 studenter og over 2600 ansatte. Vi har campus i Oslo Sentrum og på Romerike. OsloMet leverer forskning og utdanning med høy relevans for arbeidslivet, velferdsstaten og storbyregionen.
I over 200 år har OsloMet – storbyuniversitetet bidratt til å bygge kunnskap og kompetanse for det norske velferdssamfunnet. I dag er OsloMet et moderne og urbant universitet som er kjent for sine store og solide fagmiljøer innenfor lærerutdanning, helse- og sosialfag, samfunnsforskning, design og teknologifag.

ap:254474.body:
Faculty of Engineering, Faculty of Social Science
Appointment Type and Rank : Assistant or Associate Professor, Probationary (Tenure-Track)
Number of Positions: 1
Posting Date:  October 21, 2026
Closing Date to Apply:  November 20, 2026
Anticipated Start Date:  No later than July 1, 2027
Position Profile:
The Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program is a one-time federal initiative that supports the recruitment of internationally based early-career researchers to Canadian institutions. This Emerging Leader position primarily aligns with Canada’s strategic priority in  Environment, climate resilience, and the Arctic . The Emerging Leader award  is valued at $100,000 annually for up to six years, with the possibility of extension for a further six years.
Applications are invited from exceptional candidates for the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leader position in Resilience of Infrastructure and Communities in a Changing Climate at Western University, with an anticipated start date no later than July 1, 2027. The Emerging Leaders award is awarded for a six-year term, renewable once, contingent on confirmation of the early-career researcher's academic progress and the transformational, translational impact of their research. The program is administered by the  Tri-agency Institutional Programs Secretariat   (TIPS) . The successful applicant will also receive a probationary (tenure-track) appointment within the Faculty of Engineering and/or the Faculty of Social Science at the rank of Assistant or Associate Professor, commensurate with their qualifications, experience, and record of performance in teaching and research.
The successful candidate will advance infrastructure and community resilience to severe weather and climate shocks. This emerging leader will work closely with a cohort of four research chairs and will contribute to a vibrant collaborative network of interdisciplinary researchers working in the broader area of multi-hazard risk and resilience, housed primarily in the Canadian Severe Storms Laboratory at Western, the Faculty of Engineering, the Faculty of Social Science, and the Faculty of Science.
Background
Canadians are increasingly affected by the compounding effects of climate change, including more frequent and severe storms, flooding, wildfires, and heat waves. These hazards are causing acute and chronic disruptions to critical infrastructure and the essential services on which communities depend. They are disrupting people’s lives, businesses, and economic opportunities, and doing so in an unequal fashion across socioeconomic and racial/ethnic groups as well as place of residence. The changing patterns of climate and weather extremes mean that Canadian society will face difficult choices about investments in adaptation: to what extent do we fortify infrastructure, and how do we optimize equitable recovery? There is a clear need for engineering solutions and policy approaches that strengthen community resilience and support informed, equitable decision-making.
This research theme is closely aligned with the strategic priority area of the Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair in Climate Risk and Resilience Analytics. In keeping with the requirements of the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program, the successful candidate’s research program must align with the same strategic priority area identified in the Chair’s application:  Environment, climate resilience, and the Arctic . An Emerging Leader recruited in this area will offer strong opportunities for collaboration with the Chair, with complementary expertise focused on strengthening the resilience of infrastructure systems and the communities that rely on them, an essential component of the broader Chair’s proposed program to enhance climate resilience at the community scale.
Eligibility
In keeping with the requirements of the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program, applicants must be early-career researchers who were working and residing outside Canada on July 3, 2026 — date when the associated Eddie Goldenberg Research Chair in Climate Risk and Resilience Analytics award formally accepted his position. Applicants may apply from any current location and can be Canadian or of other nationalities.
As of the same date (July 3, 2026), candidates must also be within five years of the start date of their first research-related appointment (i.e., an appointment with the autonomy to conduct research independently), less any eligible delays in research. Candidates are encouraged to describe in their application how career interruptions and personal circumstances have affected their career. Please note delays due to eligible leaves (e.g., parental leave, chronic illness) will be credited at twice the time taken; however, professional leaves (e.g., training, sabbatical, administrative) are not considered an eligible delay.
Academic Expectations:
Research/Impact:
We seek a candidate with a demonstrated record of excellence in contributing innovative insights and measurable impact on infrastructure resilience and adaptation and/or community response and resilience to severe weather. A defining feature of the Emerging Leader’s research program will be strong interdisciplinary collaboration and impactful engagement to ensure research is grounded in real-world need and rapidly translated into impact.
The successful candidate will work at the interface of engineering and social science to address the infrastructure and societal dimensions of climate adaptation and resilience, working in one or more of the following areas of interest:
Vulnerability and risk assessment : evaluating how infrastructure systems and communities are exposed to severe-weather or climate-related disruptions, and how that exposure varies across place, socioeconomic status, and race/ethnicity.
Resilient and equitable infrastructure : designing, monitoring, and managing infrastructure to withstand and recover from severe weather and climate shocks, while examining how social inequality shapes both the process and outcomes of that resilience, including who has access to its benefits and protections, and who bears the greatest costs when it fails.
Data, analytics, and decision-making under uncertainty : using data analytics and artificial intelligence, alongside quantitative or mixed-methods empirical research, to predict resilience and identify adaptation strategies, including where and for whom those strategies work.
Policy, place, and adaptive capacity:  analyzing how public policies, the spatial distribution of resources, social ties, and place-based governance shape the capacity of neighbourhoods, communities and nations to prepare for, respond to, and recover from climate-related shocks, with attention to housing, essential services, and community well-being among marginalized populations.

Teaching/Mentoring:
The successful candidate will be expected to teach undergraduate and graduate courses in the Faculty of Engineering and/or the Faculty of Social Science and to supervise graduate students.
Service/Leadership:
The successful applicant will be expected to participate in other educational and professional activities including administrative duties within the Department, the Faculty and the University.
Qualifications or Experience and Skills Required:
The successful applicant will have completed a PhD degree in an engineering discipline (e.g., civil, environmental, or a related field), a social science discipline (e.g., geography, economics, political science, sociology, or public policy), or in a closely related field (e.g, urban planning, disaster risk management, data science). The PhD is a requirement of Western University and not of the Canada Impact+ Emerging Leaders program. The successful candidate will demonstrate a trajectory of research excellence that points to the prospect of becoming a leader in their field. This should include evidence of high-quality scholarly output that demonstrates independent research potential, leading to peer-assessed publications and the securing of external research funding. Evidence of effective teaching at the university level is required through a teaching statement highlighting previous experience that can include leading successful workshops or seminars, student mentorship, delivering conference presentations or posters, or experience as a teaching assistant or course instructor. Evidence of effective teaching at the university level will also be considered, as the successful candidate will be expected to teach a diversity of introductory, fundamental, or advanced undergraduate and graduate courses.
Individuals from any relevant discipline are welcome to apply, with the understanding that collaboration across traditional boundaries is required.
Compensation Details : Salary range for this position is $130,000 - $180,000. Salary will be commensurate with qualifications and experience.
Affirmation Policy Statement
Western, like many postsecondary institutions in Canada, is moving beyond sole reliance upon Indigenous self-identification in its hiring processes. This is to safeguard against the use of incorrect, incomplete, or misleading information in circumstances where a candidate has declared Indigenous citizenship or membership. Candidates who are invited for an interview or who are short-listed, and who have made a declaration of Indigenous citizenship or membership for material advantage at Western, including where required or preferred for the position, will be asked to have their declaration of Indigenous citizenship or membership affirmed through a relational accountability process, led by the Office of Indigenous Initiatives (OII), that is consistent with Indigenous ways of knowing, being, and doing. Please contact the OII directly for details on the affirmation processes:   https://indigenous.uwo.ca/. The policy can be viewed at:  POLICY 1.58 - Affirming Declarations of Indigenous Citizenship or Membership at Western   University .
The Faculties:
The Faculty of Engineering at Western is home to internationally recognized research programs spanning engineering disciplines, with strength in wind engineering and multi-hazard risk. The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering, which is administering this search, is consistently ranked among the leading civil engineering programs in Canada and worldwide, with recognized expertise in environmental, geotechnical, structural, transportation, and wind engineering. The Department’s research is supported by unique facilities and centres, including the Boundary Layer Wind Tunnel Laboratory, the Wind Engineering, Energy and Environment (WindEEE) Research Institute, the Canadian Severe Storms Laboratory, the Institute for Catastrophic Loss Reduction, and the Geotechnical Research Centre.
The Faculty of Social Science is one of the largest and most diverse social science faculties in Canada. It includes eight core departments: Anthropology, Economics, Geography and Environment, History, the DAN Department of Management and Organizational Studies, Political Science, Psychology, and Sociology. Researchers regularly work across disciplines on shared questions, such as how public policies and place shape opportunity and inequality, and how communities prepare for and recover from disruption. Interdisciplinary research centres support this work, including the Centre for Urban Policy and Local Governance, the Centre for Research in Social Inequality, and the Centre for Climate Change, Sustainable Livelihoods and Health. These centres connect scholars to shared expertise, diverse methods, and partnerships with governments and community organizations. Together, they make the Faculty a leading environment for place-based, community-engaged social science research that informs policy and improves lives in Canada and beyond. ( https://www.ssc.uwo.ca/research/research_centres_and_groups/index.html ).
The University:

The Department of Mathematics at Radboud University is seeking an outstanding and highly motivated PhD candidate to work on a PhD project in homotopy theory.
The PhD position will be under the supervision of Dr Magdalena Kedziorek and is part of the NWO-XL project 'Symmetry on the Interface of Topology and Higher Algebra'. The position has a light teaching load (10%). You will be working on equivariant stable homotopy theory and contribute to the research on commutativity in this setting. You will be encouraged to participate in relevant conferences, workshops and seminars, and to communicate your findings through publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate .
At Radboud University, I can fully focus on expanding my expertise while learning from my peers and mentors.Noemí Segura-Solé
PhD candidate in Microbial Ecology
Read Noemí's story
Does this sound like you?
You hold a Master's degree in Mathematics (or an equivalent degree) completed before the start date.
You have a strong background in algebraic topology or a related area.
You have excellent writing and communication skills.

What we offer you
We will give you a temporary employment contract (1.0 FTE) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract).
You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 in the fourth year ( salary scale P ).
You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus.
You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20.

Additional employment conditions
Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. In addition, you receive a 34% discount on the sports and cultural activities at Radboud University as an employee. And, of course, we offer a good pension plan. We also give you plenty of room and responsibility to develop your talents and realise your ambitions. Therefore, we provide various training and development schemes.
Where you will be working
Algebraic topology is one of the research areas of the Department of Mathematics at Radboud University. The field is represented by Dr. Magdalena Kedziorek and Dr. Steffen Sagave .
The department has a friendly and welcoming atmosphere with researchers in related areas including algebraic and arithmetic geometry, differential geometry, operator algebras and representation theory. There is a good balance of senior and junior staff, as well as of Dutch and international researchers, and there are regular research seminars and informal events throughout the year. Moreover, the algebraic topologists at Radboud University are part of a larger network of Dutch algebraic topologists who regularly interact and meet for seminars and other events. The Mathematics Department has more than 20 PhD candidates, several of whom work in algebraic topology and related areas.
Faculty of Science
The Faculty of Science (FNWI), part of Radboud University, engages in groundbreaking research and excellent education. In doing so, we push the boundaries of scientific knowledge and pass that knowledge on to the next generation.
We seek solutions to major societal challenges, such as cybercrime and climate change and work on major scientific challenges, such as those in the quantum world. At the same time, we prepare our students for careers both within and outside the scientific field.
Currently, more than 1,300 colleagues contribute to research and education, some as researchers and lecturers, others as technical and administrative support officers. The faculty has a strong international character with staff from more than 70 countries. Together, we work in an informal, accessible and welcoming environment, with attention and space for personal and professional development for all.
Radboud University
At Radboud University, we aim to make an impact through our work. We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. We advocate for an inclusive community and welcome employees with diverse backgrounds, cultures, and perspectives.
If you want to learn more about working at Radboud University, follow our Instagram account and read stories from our colleagues.

Is this the job for you?
You can apply only via the button below. Address your letter of application to Magdalena Kedziorek. We look forward to receiving your application. We ask you to include following documents with your application:
Your CV.
Your cover letter.
A transcript of records for your Bachelor's and Master's studies.
A copy of your Master's thesis, if already completed. If it is not completed, a short summary of your Master's thesis (up to 1 page).
A name and an email address of at least one academic reference, preferably your Master project supervisor.

The first interviews will take place during the week of 30 November 2026 (online). Any second interview will take place during the week of 7 December 2026. You will preferably start your employment on 1 February 2027.
We can imagine you're curious about our  application procedure . It describes what you can expect during the application procedure and how we handle your personal data and internal and external candidates.

Are you an enthusiastic young scientist with a Master's degree in a neuroscience-related field? And would you like to figure out how plasticity at multiple synapses is coordinated within dendrites? Then you have a part to play as a PhD candidate in our research team. Put your ideas to the test at our green campus and push your boundaries in an internationally friendly environment.
Synaptic plasticity is considered to be the foundation of brain adaptation and learning. Multiple signalling pathways have been identified that are underlying synaptic plasticity of single synapses, depending on induction protocol and cell type. However, linking these molecular pathways to behavioural adaptation and learning turned out to be difficult. Under physiological conditions in vivo, multiple synapses will be activated simultaneously and plasticity pathways will inherently interfere.
In this PhD project, we will use a combination of single cell electrophysiology, advanced microscopy techniques and novel biosensors to examine molecular pathways underlying multisynaptic plasticity in dendrites of hippocampal CA1 neurons in brain slices.
Research in the Wierenga lab focuses on the formation and plasticity of inhibitory synapses and the interactions between inhibitory and excitatory synapses within dendrites. In this project, you will use two-photon glutamate uncaging in hippocampal slices to induce synaptic plasticity at multiple spines and you will exploit novel biosensors to study interactions between molecular pathways within the dendrite. Furthermore, you will explore how these interactions are affected by neuromodulators. Pilot experiments with four spine stimulation have shown that large calcium signals emerge within the dendritic shaft that continue even after the stimulation has ended, and that there are at least two modes of spine growth that seem to be regulated independently.
The research has the following objectives:
To determine how calcium release from internal stores contributes to dendritic calcium signals.
To investigate how PKA and PKC activity interacts with calcium signals.
To assess if these interactions can explain the two modes of spine growth.
To examine when and where molecular signalling molecules (aka retrograde messengers) are produced.

Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.

Where you will be working
Our research team is a diverse team of international scientists broadly interested in the role of inhibitory synapses in the brain at the molecular, cellular and systems levels. We use a combination of two-photon microscopy, electrophysiology and molecular techniques to study formation and plasticity of inhibitory synapses in organotypic and acute brain slices from mice. We are particularly interested in the interactions between excitatory and inhibitory synapses within dendrites during synaptic plasticity, in brain development and in neurodevelopmental and neurodegenerative diseases.
The Wierenga lab is embedded within the Donders Centre for Neuroscience (DCN) at the Faculty of Science of Radboud University (Nijmegen, Netherlands). DCN is part of the world-renowned Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition and Behaviour, a world-class interfaculty neuroscience institute with a lively and interactive culture housing more than 800 researchers devoted to understanding the mechanistic underpinnings of the brain.
Excellent, state-of-the-art research facilities are available for the broad range of neuroscience research that is being conducted at the Donders Institute. The Donders Institute has been assessed by an international evaluation committee as 'excellent' and recognised as a 'very stimulating environment for top researchers, as well as for young talent'. The Donders Institute fosters a collaborative, multidisciplinary and supportive research environment with a diverse international staff. English is the lingua franca at the Institute.
Faculty of Science
The Faculty of Science (FNWI), part of Radboud University, engages in groundbreaking research and excellent education. In doing so, we push the boundaries of scientific knowledge and pass that knowledge on to the next generation.
We seek solutions to major societal challenges, such as cybercrime and climate change and work on major scientific challenges, such as those in the quantum world. At the same time, we prepare our students for careers both within and outside the scientific field.
Currently, more than 1,300 colleagues contribute to research and education, some as researchers and lecturers, others as technical and administrative support officers. The faculty has a strong international character with staff from more than 70 countries. Together, we work in an informal, accessible and welcoming environment, with attention and space for personal and professional development for all.
Radboud University

We achieve this by conducting groundbreaking research, providing high-quality education, offering excellent support, and fostering collaborations within and outside the university. In doing so, we contribute indispensably to a healthy, free world with equal opportunities for all. To accomplish this, we need even more colleagues who, based on their expertise, are willing to search for answers. In this PhD position, you will develop integrated and innovative biodiversity monitoring and data analysis techniques to aid in the decision-making of businesses within the dairy sector for the benefit of biodiversity.
Biodiversity recovery is essential to sustain resilient food systems, robust businesses and healthy societies. A transition to a more nature-inclusive dairy sector in the Netherlands would be pivotal to biodiversity recovery, because of its influence in shaping landscapes through land use and management, and because of its socio-economic relevance.
To properly assess the suitability and effectiveness of key performance indicators and the effects of management practices on local biodiversity, it is crucial to monitor, for example, breeding birds, bats, insect communities and soil life (depending on the KPI).
By adapting and developing biomonitoring techniques programmes at dairy farms that are in line with long-running or recently developed monitoring schemes, you will utilise the full potential of datasets and methods to quantify biodiversity gains resulting from nature-inclusive farming as well as the potential for further biodiversity recovery. Novel instruments such as DIOPSIS smart insect cameras, LED buckets and bat loggers generate huge amounts of biodiversity data from across the Netherlands and can be used to detect and identify biodiversity automatically.
National schemes like the breeding bird monitoring project, the butterfly monitoring scheme and the dragon fly monitoring scheme (standardised and coordinated by NGOs such as Sovon and Dutch Butterfly Conservation, and powered by thousands of citizen scientists) generate standardised long-term trends based on thousands of plots around the country. You will design novel, integrated analyses to quantify the effects on biodiversity from existing and new data while accounting for factors such as observers' bias, weather and surrounding landscape configuration.
In this project you will:
Bring coherence across the diverse monitoring systems and KPI developed so far and adapt sets of KPI's suited to peat soils.
Document the relationships between different nature-inclusive measures taken by heterogeneous farm types, and the different aspects of biodiversity and ecosystem services considered. The precise type of monitoring and the number and locations of monitoring points will be decided in collaboration with stakeholders.
Further develop effective and integrated monitoring to guide decision-making in businesses and develop reward schemes.

Your teaching load may be up to 10% of your working time.
Would you like to learn more about what it’s like to pursue a PhD at Radboud University? Visit the page about working as a PhD candidate .

You have an affinity for, and proven experience with, computer programming, statistical modelling and large datasets, and you know how to perform qualitative analyses based on quantitative data.
You have an understanding of field work in practice, have a passion for biodiversity and are keen to absorb and share knowledge with others.
You are a team player, eager to work on a truly interdisciplinary project.

We will give you a temporary employment contract (0.8 FTE 5- year contract - 1.0 FTE 4- year contract) of 1.5 years, after which your performance will be evaluated. If the evaluation is positive, your contract will be extended by 2.5 years (4-year contract) or 3.5 years (5-year contract).
You will receive a starting salary of €3,204 gross per month based on a 38-hour working week, which will increase to €4,051 from the fourth year onwards ( salary scale P ).
You will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8,3% end-of-year bonus.
You will receive extra days off. With full-time employment, you can choose between 30 or 41 days of annual leave instead of the statutory 20.

Work and science require good employment practices. Radboud University's primary and secondary employment conditions reflect this. You can make arrangements for the best possible work-life balance with flexible working hours, various leave arrangements and working from home. You are also able to compose part of your employment conditions yourself. For example, exchange income for extra leave days and receive a reimbursement for your sports membership. The Department of Ecology at Radboud University is a dynamic, collaborative and interdisciplinary team. We are a young and ambitious group of ecologists committed to preserving and promoting biodiversity and ecosystem health. Our department brings together aquatic and terrestrial ecologists who focus on plants, animals and microorganisms and their interactions in a changing world. We are dedicated to conducting timely and innovative research that addresses both scientific and societal challenges. Your research will be integrated into ongoing studies in biodiversity research and applied ecology, with opportunities to collaborate with colleagues across departments. Dr Eelke Jongejans will be one of the two main supervisors for the project.
The Radboud Institute for Biological and Environmental Sciences (RIBES) is committed to equality of opportunity, fairness and inclusivity, striving to be a place where everyone feels respected and valued, and creativity and innovation are fostered and encouraged. We welcome applications from individuals of all genders, ethnicities, sexual orientations, abilities and backgrounds, and particularly encourage those from underrepresented groups to apply.
SoortenNL is an umbrella for organisations that collect and interpret biodiversity data from surveys and large monitoring schemes carried out by citizen scientists. It is both a social network and an information landscape. Dr Sander Turnhout of SoortenNL will be the co-supervisor of this project.
In this interdisciplinary research project (DECISION: Dairy and Ecology: Co-Innovating buSIness Operations for Nature) you will closely collaborate with three other PhD candidates and a postdoctoral researcher working in animal sciences and social sciences at Wageningen University and Erasmus University. The research consortium also includes agribusinesses, financial businesses, farmer associations and governmental organisations.

ap:254482.body:
Doctoral Position in Environmental Microbiology
The Environmental Microbiology group led by Prof. Marie Schölmerich at the Department of Environmental Systems Science, ETH Zurich, invites applications for a fully funded 4 year Doctoral Position. Our group explores the fascinating world of anaerobic microbiology from the global to the microscopic scale. This project investigates the physiology and bioenergetics of alkaliphilic methanogenic archaea.

Project background
The National Centre of Competence in Research NCCR Genesis is a research infrastructure project funded by SNSF focussing on exploring the emergence of life in the Universe. This interdisciplinary research infrastructure brings together physicists, earth and planetary scientists, chemists and biologists to understand the conditions and the mechanisms that enable life to emerge. Developing reliable methods to detect reliable traces of life (biosignatures) – whether through remote sensing or direct onsite measurements – requires significant innovation. These challenges demand close collaboration across physics, biology, chemistry and the earth sciences. NCCR Genesis does not aim to provide answers in all fields, but to drive innovative research and achieve decisive progress.

Details on NCCR Genesis are available on its website .

NCCR Genesis is deeply committed to equality, diversity and inclusion. Our aim is to cultivate a respectful and fair work culture with equal access to professional development and support for all. We strongly encourage applications from under-represented groups.

Job description

Alkaline environments such as soda lakes and serpentinising vents are candidate sites for the emergence of life on Earth and potential habitats on ocean worlds like Enceladus

Methanogenic archaea are the main biological source of the greenhouse gas methane

Some methanogenic archaea can thrive under alkaliphilic conditions where conventional energy conservation reaches its limits

This Doctoral project seeks to investigate what limits the growth of alkaliphilic methanogens, how they conserve energy and acquire carbon at high pH, and which signatures distinguish their methane from abiotic methane

The work combines anaerobic cultivation, physiology and biochemistry

Profile

MSc (or equivalent) in microbiology, environmental sciences or a related field

Experience in anaerobic cultivation and/or protein biochemistry is an advantage

Curiosity about fundamental questions and enthusiasm for experimental work and excellent communication skills in English

We offer

Opportunities to engage in cutting-edge research with the potential for high impact in the field of environmental microbiology

Encouraging and collaborative research environment

A Doctoral Position in a national, interdisciplinary network linking microbiology with geochemistry, planetary science and origin-of-life research

Training in anaerobic microbiology, bioenergetics, and omics

A fundamental research question with direct relevance to astrobiology and the methane cycle

Support for career goals through conference travel and workshops

Exciting working environment, cultural diversity and attractive offers and benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

Cover letter

CV including publication list

Diploma and Transcript of Records

Contact details of two references

Further information about the Environmental Microbiology Group in the Department of Environmental Systems Sciences can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position should be directed to Prof. Marie Schölmerich, [email protected]  (no applications).

Please note that we exclusively accept applications submitted through our online application portal. Applications via email or postal services will not be considered.

The deadline for applications is 1 December 2026.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.
