ap:254520.body:
The Leuven Institute of Criminology (LINC) was founded in 2007. It currently groups about 70 professors, researchers and assistants involved in criminological research and teaching. LINC forms part of the Faculty of Law and Criminology, KU Leuven.

Website unit

Project

Your main assignment will be to conduct doctoral research in the field of serious and organised crime.

In particular, it concerns empirical research into organised crime in a local, national and international perspective, with a particular focus on the organisations, networks and criminal activities involved. The concrete topic will be determined in mutual consultation.

The research will mainly use qualitative research methods and will mainly be carried out in Belgium.

In addition to the main assignment, the researcher will also provide limited assistance with teaching (e.g. supervision of master's theses, helping with improvement of tasks or examinations and with examination supervision) or with other research projects within the research team.

Profile

You have a master's degree in criminology. Master's degrees in other humanities (e.g. political science or sociology) will be considered provided that you have a clear and demonstrable work or research experience within the criminological domain.

You obtained an excellent study curriculum (at least one (great) distinction).

You have a strong interest in the actors, networks and activities within organised crime and in the way in which these phenomena develop and manifest themselves in local, national and international contexts.

You are already partly familiar with the criminological literature on organized crime.

You have demonstrable knowledge of qualitative and possibly quantitative methods of empirical scientific research. Preferably, you already have experience with qualitative data collection, such as conducting interviews, conducting focus groups or other forms of fieldwork.

You have excellent scientific writing skills and preferably already have one or more (international, peer-reviewed) scientific publications as a (co-)author.

You have the necessary didactic qualities.

You like to work together and function smoothly in a team.

You have strong organisational skills and can plan and coordinate research activities independently.

You have excellent oral and written skills in Dutch and English.

Offer

We offer an appointment as a full-time PhD researcher. The mandate is initially for one year, but is renewable.

Vacatures Leuvens Instituut voor Criminologie (LINC)

Interested?

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Letizia Paoli, mail: [email protected] .

KU Leuven strives for an inclusive, respectful and socially safe environment. We embrace diversity among individuals and groups as an asset. Open dialogue and differences in perspective are essential for an ambitious research and educational environment. In our commitment to equal opportunity, we recognize the consequences of historical inequalities. We do not accept any form of discrimination based on, but not limited to, gender identity and expression, sexual orientation, age, ethnic or national background, skin colour, religious and philosophical diversity, neurodivergence, employment disability, health, or socioeconomic status. For questions about accessibility or support offered, we are happy to assist you at this email address.

ap:254521.body:
How can artificial intelligence help predict equipment degradation and enable smarter maintenance decisions?
At Chalmers University of Technology, you will explore this question by developing AI-powered methods for assessing and predicting the health of industrial assets. We are looking for a Doctoral student to become part of our team at the Division of Production Systems  in the Department of Mechanical Engineering . Please join our innovative team and contribute to exciting research on Production systems, AI-supported condition assessment, and maintenance decision-making in a collaborative and dynamic environment.
About us
The Division of Production Systems works with the sustainability and competitiveness of industrial production systems. The research area is system-oriented and requires knowledge about both the system as a whole and its separate components, for example humans, automation, and processes. The research highlights the different stages of a production system’s life cycle, i.e. planning, design, commissioning, operation, maintenance and reuse. Methods and research findings are generic, with applications within various industries, such as automotive, aerospace, processing and mining industries.
The people in the division form an internationally diverse, gender-balanced, and inclusive team of more than 30 cross-disciplinary researchers and support staff. Our strong international collaborative networks and advanced research infrastructure, Stena Industry Innovation Lab, make us a competitive international actor.
The Production Systems Division is part of Chalmers largest unit, the Department of Mechanical Engineering , where we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. The department is highly ranked internationally. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world.
About the research project
The research will develop and evaluate AI-powered Asset Health Index models that combine heterogeneous condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge into transparent indicators of asset condition and degradation. The work will investigate how artificial intelligence can strengthen model development, support prognostics and Remaining Useful Life estimation, and turn complex data into useful information for maintenance and asset-management decisions. Through close academic and industrial collaboration, the project will validate the models in a real-world pilot environment, with emphasis on general methods for condition assessment, risk analysis, maintenance prioritisation, and lifecycle-oriented decision support for complex technical assets.
Who we are looking for
The following requirements are mandatory:
To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Automation, Data Science, Computer Science, or another relevant field.
Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.
You should have a strong interest in maintenance, asset management, data-driven engineering, artificial intelligence, or prognostics and health management.
A strong candidate is highly motivated, self-driven and curious, with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative research environment.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
The following experience will strengthen your application:
Prior expertise and experience in Asset Health Index (AHI)
Data analysis, machine learning, statistical modelling, or optimisation
Maintenance engineering, reliability, condition monitoring, prognostics, or asset management
Working with heterogeneous industrial data, including structured and unstructured information
Programming and development of decision-support or simulation models
Academic or industrial collaboration in multidisciplinary environments

What you will do
Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Product and Production Development  ( Product and production development | Chalmers )
Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing
Develop and validate Asset Health Index models by combining condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge
Explore AI-supported methods for prognostics, Remaining Useful Life estimation, transparent model interpretation, and maintenance decision support
Implement, test, and demonstrate models and decision-support concepts together with other researchers and industry participants in laboratory and real-world pilot environments
The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Contract terms
The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.
The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.
A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).
Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer
As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.
A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .
Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.
If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.
Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .
Application procedure
The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.
CV
Personal letter
A brief introduction about yourself.
A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.
Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.
A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.
Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.
We welcome your application no later than  November 30th, 2026.
For questions, please contact:
Johan Stahre
Professor of Production Systems, Division manager
[email protected]
Anders Skoogh
Professor of Maintenance Engineering
[email protected]
We look forward to your application!
*** Chalmers declines to consider all offers of further announcement publishing or other types of support for the recruiting process in connection with this position.  ***
Chalmers University of Technology in Gothenburg conducts research and education in technology and natural sciences at a high international level. The university has 3100 employees and 10,000 students, and offers education in engineering, science, shipping and architecture. With scientific excellence as a basis, Chalmers promotes knowledge and technical solutions for a sustainable world. Through global commitment and entrepreneurship, we foster an innovative spirit, in close collaboration with wider society.
Chalmers was founded in 1829 and has the same motto today as it did then: Avancez – forward.

ap:254522.body:
Doctoral Student in Magnetic Resonance for the Study of Granular Systems
ETH Zurich is one of the leading universities worldwide and renowned for its excellence in education, fundamental and applied research, and technology transfer. At the Institute for Biomedical Engineering, one research focus is on nuclear magnetic resonance. The team of Prof. Klaas Prüssmann drives innovation in magnetic resonance from physical and mathematical principles all the way to novel imaging, sensing, and tracking technology. In close collaboration with academic and industrial partners, we pursue applications in the biomedical realm, process engineering, and materials science. One recent focus of interest is on the use of magnetic resonance for particle tracking in granular systems. We are looking for a Physicist or Engineer to join us on this frontier as a Doctoral Student.

Project background
Granular systems are ubiquitous in nature and of fundamental importance to industry, from food and pharma to material conversion. However, despite their widespread occurence and use, many important phenomena such as the transition between flowing and solid states, mixing, segregation, or surface instabilities, are poorly understood. Magnetic resonance has proven a powerful means of studying granular physics, permitting both dynamic imaging and, newly, the tracking of particle swarms. The focus is now on further expanding the tracking strategies and, in the applied realm, on exploring the role of the shape of particles and how granular dynamics change when particles are soft and deform upon stress.

The project is a shared effort with ETH colleagues in process engineering and encompasses two Doctoral Student positions, one each at the Institute for Biomedical Engineering (Prof. Prüssmann) and the Laboratory of Energy Science and Engineering (Prof. Müller). The two Doctoral Researchers will benefit from immersion in both environments and are foreseen to collaborate closely.

Job description
The objective of the Doctoral Student hired by the Institute for Biomedical Engineering is to advance magnetic resonance technology and methods towards the study of granular systems made up of arbitrarily shaped and soft particles. This will include work on principles of particle tracking and imaging, creation of new methods, implementation on magnetic resonance equipment, all the way to  experimental exploration and use in granular systems.

The collaborative effort with the partner Doctoral Student will particularly target the fabrication of tailored and soft particles, applied studies in granular systems science, and the creation of experimental setups to this end.

Doctoral Position: Development of an Organ-on-chip platform
The Bioanalytics Group at ETH Zürich in Basel (Switzerland) is developing so-called lab-on-chip technology (or microfluidic technology) for applications across the life sciences and biomedicine. Our interdisciplinary approach includes the design and manufacturing of miniaturized platforms and their optimization for biochemical assays and analytical procedures. To strengthen our team, we are offering a Doctoral Position for developing an organ-on-chip model system.

Project background
Organ-on-chip systems, also known as microphysiological systems, are promising platforms for investigating disease development and evaluating potential treatments. Their miniaturized design enables the reproducible and controlled formation of human tissues with specific functions, as well as the parallelized study of biological processes.

In the Bioanalytics Group, we are developing vascularized tissue models to investigate how cells, cell-secreted molecules, and drugs cross the endothelial barrier to reach surrounding tissues and how compounds translocate from tissue into the blood stream.

As part of a project focused on understanding the mechanisms underlying cancer metastasis, we are looking for a motivated Doctoral student interested in experimental research at the interface of engineering and biology.

Job description

Design and manufacture a microfluidic platform

Develop, optimize and test biological assays

Perform imaging (time-lapse microscopy), data analysis and interpretation

ap:254524.body:
Doctoral Position in Groundwater Microbial and Viral Ecology and Environmental Bioinformatics
The Geomitigation of Greenhouse Gases group at ETH Zürich is actively recruiting a highly motivated and curious Doctoral candidate with a strong interest in environmental microbiology, biogeochemical cycling, and bioinformatics. The position is part of a newly funded SNSF interdisciplinary project investigating how microbial and viral communities influence carbon cycling in groundwater systems. The project brings together microbial and viral ecology, environmental genomics, and hydrogeochemistry to better understand how biological processes influence the fate of carbon in the subsurface.

Project background
Groundwater represents an important but poorly understood component of the global carbon cycle. While water-rock interactions strongly influence groundwater chemistry, microbial communities actively transform carbon through diverse metabolic pathways, and viruses may further regulate these processes through infection and metabolic reprogramming. However, how microbial and viral communities respond to changes in groundwater age and geochemistry, and how these interactions influence carbon cycling, remains largely unknown.

In this project, you will investigate microbial and viral diversity, metabolic activity, and evolutionary adaptation across groundwater age gradients. By combining metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, and viral metagenomics with hydrogeochemical measurements, you will explore how microbial metabolism and virus-host interactions influence carbon cycling in the subsurface.

Job description

Analyze large-scale environmental metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and viral sequencing datasets to investigate microbial and viral diversity, activity, and function in groundwater systems

Characterize microbial metabolic potential and activity, with a particular focus on pathways involved in carbon cycling and their responses to environmental conditions

Investigate microbial and viral community dynamics, virus-host interactions, and evolutionary adaptation across groundwater age and geochemical gradients

Integrate environmental multi-omics datasets with hydrogeochemical measurements to better understand the biological processes influencing subsurface carbon cycling

Perform DNA and RNA extractions from environmental samples and contribute to complementary laboratory analyses, including microbial cell abundance and activity measurements using flow cytometry and microscopy

Synthesize research findings into scientific manuscripts and present results at international conferences and workshops

Collaborate closely with the Principal Investigator, project partner, another Doctoral student working on groundwater hydrogeochemistry, and other group members while contributing to a supportive and communicative research environment

Profile
We are looking for a candidate who is curious, independent, and motivated by questions at the intersection of microbial ecology, evolution, and environmental biogeochemistry. You enjoy working with large biological datasets and are excited about using computational approaches to understand how microorganisms and viruses interact with their environments.

An MSc degree in microbiology, microbial ecology, bioinformatics, computational biology, geobiology, or a closely related discipline

Previous hands-on experience with metagenomic data analysis or closely related environmental bioinformatics approaches

Experience working in Linux/Unix command-line environments and familiarity with computational biology workflows

Experience with at least one programming or scripting language, such as Python, R or Bash

A strong understanding of microbial ecology, physiology, and/or metabolism

Excellent analytical and problem-solving skills, including the ability to work with complex biological datasets

Creativity, curiosity, and motivation to explore new research questions and computational approaches

Ability to work both independently and as part of a collaborative interdisciplinary team

Excellent spoken and written English

Experience with genome-resolved metagenomics, metatranscriptomics, comparative genomics, or high-performance computing is particularly advantageous. Previous experience with DNA and/or RNA extraction from environmental samples is also desirable. A background in groundwater microbiology, environmental geochemistry, or biogeochemical cycling is beneficial but not required.

We offer

A collaborative research environment: You will join an enthusiastic, inclusive, and highly collaborative research group where high quality research, open discussion, and creative scientific thinking are strongly valued. You will benefit from a dynamic departmental setting with broad expertise, excellent research infrastructure, and opportunities for interdisciplinary exchange

Mentorship and career development: You will receive direct mentorship from the PI and specialized guidance in environmental bioinformatics, microbial ecology, and viral ecology from the project's scientific partner,

Mentorship and career development: You will participate in the broader academic community through publications and presentations at scientific conferences

Mentorship and career development:  Additional development opportunities are available through teaching assistantships, ETH doctoral courses, and transferable-skills training

Access to extensive multi-omics datasets and computational resources : You will work with large-scale groundwater metagenomic, metatranscriptomic, and viral sequencing datasets and you will have access to ETH Zürich's computational infrastructure and resources for environmental bioinformatics, providing opportunities to develop and apply advanced computational approaches to important questions in microbial ecology and biogeochemistry

A supportive and inclusive workspace: We are committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and constructive working environment

A supportive and inclusive workspace:  Flexible working arrangements can be discussed where compatible with laboratory and project responsibilities

Employment conditions and benefits: We offer a fully funded 48-month Doctoral Position, with that, you can expect numerous benefits, such as public transport season tickets and car sharing, a wide range of sports offered by the ASVZ, childcare, and attractive pension benefits

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.

Cover letter describing your motivation and research interests (max. 2 pages)

Curriculum Vitae (max. 2 pages)

Bachelors' and Master's transcripts

Master Diploma (digital copy)

We will get in touch with you after 2 - 3 weeks following the submission deadline.

Bepaal mee de toekomst – Universiteit Antwerpen
De Universiteit Antwerpen is een dynamische, toekomstgerichte Europese universiteit. We bieden vernieuwend academisch onderwijs aan meer dan 20000 studenten, verrichten baanbrekend wetenschappelijk onderzoek en spelen een belangrijke dienstverlenende rol in de maatschappij. We zijn een van de grootste, meest internationale en innovatieve werkgevers van de regio. Met meer dan 6000 medewerkers uit 100 verschillende landen bouwen we dagelijks aan de wereld van morgen. Door wetenschappelijk toponderzoek verleggen we grenzen en geven we de richting aan. De richting van de toekomst. En die kan jij mee bepalen.
Het Departement Politieke Wetenschappen van de Faculteit Sociale Wetenschappen heeft de volgende deeltijdse vacature:
Zelfstandig academisch personeel Internationale Politiek (20%)
Functie
Je maakt deel uit van het Zelfstandig Academisch Personeel (ZAP) en je draagt bij aan de drie kerntaken van de Universiteit Antwerpen: onderwijs, onderzoek en dienstverlening. Ook organiserende en leidinggevende taken kunnen tot je opdracht behoren.
Onderwijs
Je verstrekt kwalitatief hoogstaand onderwijs in het Departement Politieke Wetenschappen.
Het opleidingsonderdeel dat je zal doceren is “Leeronderzoek Politieke Wetenschappen”, een verplicht opleidingsonderdeel dat in het Nederlands wordt aangeboden. In deze cursus voeren studenten een politiek-wetenschappelijk onderzoeksproject uit. Dit omvat het definiëren van een politiek-wetenschappelijke onderzoeksvraag, het formuleren van theoretisch afgeleide verwachtingen, het identificeren en toepassen van een geschikte onderzoeksmethode en het uitvoeren van het empirische onderzoek. Verder zal je ook een methodeseminarie doceren binnen de masteropleidingen van het Departement Politieke Wetenschappen.
Je werkt mee aan de ontwikkeling van activerende, studentgecentreerde en competentiegerichte opleidingsonderdelen en studieprogramma’s.
Je begeleidt studenten bij bachelor- en masterproeven in het Departement Politieke Wetenschappen.

Onderzoek
Je bouwt zelfstandig wetenschappelijk onderzoek uit in het domein Internationale Politiek.
Je verwerft en beheert (inter)nationale onderzoeksfinanciering.
Je publiceert in internationale tijdschriften en vakliteratuur in het domein Internationale Politiek.
Je bouwt een internationaal wetenschappelijk netwerk uit.
Je begeleidt doctoraatsstudenten en postdoctorale onderzoekers.

Dienstverlening
Je neemt interne en externe opdrachten van wetenschappelijke en maatschappelijke dienstverlening op. Je neemt onder meer deel aan studentenwerving, raden en commissies, populaire wetenschapscommunicatie, … .

Organisatie en leiderschap
Je neemt coördinerende verantwoordelijkheden op het vlak van onderwijs, onderzoek en/of dienstverlening op en je bouwt mee aan het beleid.
Je geeft op een motiverende, coachende wijze leiding. Daarbij heb je aandacht voor het groeiproces en de ontwikkeling van je medewerkers.

Profiel
Je behaalde een doctoraat op proefschrift in het domein Internationale Politiek.
Jouw onderzoekskwaliteiten sluiten aan bij het facultaire en universitaire onderzoeksbeleid . Je hebt een uitstekend onderzoeksdossier in de Internationale Politiek, met name in het deeldomein Historical International Relations. Je uitmuntendheid blijkt uit internationale publicaties van hoog niveau en het verkrijgen van zeer competitieve wetenschappelijke financiering. je behaalde een ERC-beurs die je in Antwerpen zal uitvoeren.
Jouw onderwijscompetenties sluiten aan bij de onderwijsvisie van de Universiteit Antwerpen. Je bent gemotiveerd om je didactische vaardigheden verder te ontwikkelen via de aangeboden professionaliseringsmogelijkheden .
Je doceert in het Nederlands. De beheersing van het Nederlands op ERK-niveau C1 (taalcertificaat of diploma secundair, bachelor, master of doctoraat) is vereist. Je toont leiderschapspotentieel en je geeft blijk van organisatievermogen.
Je gaat kwaliteitsgericht, integer, creatief en samenwerkingsgericht te werk.

Aanbod
We bieden een deeltijdse aanstelling als ZAP-lid voor een periode van drie jaar. De aanstelling is hernieuwbaar na positieve evaluatie. De graad van je aanstelling (docent, hoofddocent, hoogleraar of gewoon hoogleraar) bepalen we op basis van je professionele ervaring en academische kwalificaties.
Jouw brutomaandwedde wordt berekend volgens de barema’s voor het Zelfstandig Academisch Personeel en pro rata berekend op basis van het tewerkstellingspercentage.
Je krijgt ecocheques, internet-connectiviteitsvergoeding en een fietsvergoeding of volledige terugbetaling van je woon-werkverkeer met het openbaar vervoer.
De voorziene startdatum is 1 januari 2027 of zo spoedig mogelijk nadien.
Je werkt grotendeels op de Stadscampus, in een dynamische en stimulerende werkomgeving.
Lees hier meer over werken bij de Universiteit Antwerpen en ontdek alle andere voordelen .

Solliciteren?
Je kan tot en met 18 november 2026 voor deze vacature solliciteren via het online sollicitatieplatform van de Universiteit Antwerpen. Klik op de knop ‘Solliciteren’ en vervolledig het online sollicitatieformulier. Voeg volgende bijlages toe: je motivatiebrief;
de ingevulde sollicitatiebijlage voor ZAP
je academisch cv

De selectiecommissie bekijkt zo snel mogelijk na de sollicitatiedeadline alle sollicitaties. Zodra er een beslissing genomen is, brengen we je op de hoogte. Als je na de preselectie nog steeds in aanmerking komt, word je geïnformeerd over de eventuele volgende stap(pen) in de selectieprocedure.
Bij vragen over het online sollicitatieformulier kan je de Frequently Asked Questions raadplegen of mailen naar [email protected] . Bij inhoudelijke vragen over de functie kan je contact opnemen met prof. Wouter Van Dooren ( [email protected] ) of prof. Jorg Kustermans, ( [email protected] ).

De Europese Commissie bekroonde het HR-beleid van de Universiteit Antwerpen met de ‘ HR Excellence in Research Award ’. We zijn een duurzame, gezinsvriendelijke organisatie die maximaal in de groei van medewerkers investeert. We stimuleren diversiteit  en hechten veel belang aan een inclusieve werkomgeving met gelijke kansen - ongeacht gender, functiebeperking, afkomst, levensbeschouwing, seksuele oriëntatie of leeftijd. Wij moedigen mensen met een diverse achtergrond en diverse eigenschappen aan om te solliciteren.

Let’s shape the future - University of Antwerp
The University of Antwerp is a dynamic, forward-thinking, European university. We offer an innovative academic education to more than 20 000 students, conduct pioneering scientific research and play an important service-providing role in society. We are one of the largest, most international and most innovative employers in the region. With more than 6 000 employees from 100 different countries, we are helping to build tomorrow's world every day. Through top scientific research, we push back boundaries and set a course for the future – a future that you can help to shape.
The Department of Veterinary Sciences in the Faculty of Pharmaceutical, Biomedical and Veterinary Sciences is looking for a full-time (100%)
doctoral scholarship holder in the field of comparative perinatal gastroenterology
Position
You will actively work on the preparation and defence of a PhD thesis in the field of Comparative Perinatal Gastroenterology investigating sex-related differences in a piglet model. You will draw up a research plan and corresponding research methods in consultation with your supervisor(s) and undertake the necessary administration for a smooth PhD process.
You will conduct the research efficiently and to an appropriate standard, possibly abroad, and compete for funding for general or specific costs.
You will report progress to your supervisor(s) and committees and present your research at scientific conferences.
You will defend your thesis publicly and publish in the scientific press.

You will make a supporting, scientific contribution to existing research projects or lines of research within beyond your own doctoral research.
You will compete for internal or external predoctoral funding.
In addition to project-based research, you will also be responsible for a limited range of support tasks related to teaching and/or research management within the Comparative Perinatal Development group.

Profile
You hold a master degree in Life Sciences (Biology, Biomedical Sciences, Applied Biological Sciences, Pharmaceutical Sciences, Veterinary Sciences, Zoology, …) or you will have obtained it by the time of appointment.
You hold a personal license to work with laboratory animals (Functions ABC for rodents or Categorie C).
You can provide evidence of good study results.
You have a good knowledge of Dutch and English, both oral and written.
Your teaching competences are in line with the University of Antwerp’s educational vision .
Your research qualities are in line with the faculty and university research policies .
You act with attention to quality, integrity, creativity and cooperation.
You are prepared to apply for external financed personal research grants (e.g. FWO).
You stand for open and honest communication.

What we offer
We offer a doctoral scholarship for a period of one year. Following a positive evaluation, the scholarship can be renewed for another period of 1 year, up until a maximum of 4 years in total.
We offer the opportunity to take part in academic activities within the scope of your work, as well as the opportunity to further develop yourself through training and education.
The planned start date is 1 st February 2027 or as soon as possible after that date.
Your monthly scholarship amount is calculated according to the scholarship amounts for doctoral scholarship holders.
You will receive ecocheques, Internet-connectivity allowance, and a bicycle allowance or a full reimbursement of public transport costs for commuting.
As a doctoral researcher, you will have access to a wide and varied range of courses and an educational credit through the Antwerp Doctoral School .
You will do most of your work at Campus Drie Eiken in a dynamic and stimulating working environment.
Find out more about working at the University of Antwerp here .

Want to apply?
You can apply for this vacancy through the University of Antwerp’s online job application platform up to and including 30 th November 2026 (by midnight Brussels time). Click on the 'Apply' button and complete the online application form. Be sure to include the following attachments: a motivation letter
your academic CV
a summary of your master thesis
contact details of 1 professional referee
These documents are required and must be included. If one or more documents are missing, your application will be declared inadmissible.

The selection committee reviews all applications as soon as possible after the application deadline. As soon as a decision is made, we will notify you. If you are still eligible after the pre-selection, you will be informed about the possible next step(s) in the selection procedure.
If you have any questions about the online application form, please check the frequently asked questions or send an email to [email protected] . If you have any questions about the job itself, please contact Prof. Dr. Chris Van Ginneken ( [email protected] ) or Dr. Sara Prims ( [email protected] )

The University of Antwerp received the European Commission’s HR Excellence in Research Award for its HR policy. We are a sustainable, family-friendly organisation which invests in its employees’ growth. We encourage diversity  and attach great importance to an inclusive working environment and equal opportunities, regardless of gender identity, disability, race, ethnicity, religion or belief, sexual orientation or age. We encourage people from diverse backgrounds and with diverse characteristics to apply.

ap:254532.body:
Introduction
Are you excited about designing digital innovations for sustainable healthcare and eager to support Dutch care organizations in reducing medication waste while ensuring safe and compliant care? Join us as a PhD candidate on the NWO project REMARK.
Job Description
Healthcare organizations are under increasing pressure to become more sustainable while continuing to deliver safe, high-quality, and compliant care. Circular care pathways offer opportunities to reduce waste and improve resource utilization, but they also introduce new challenges. Healthcare organizations need to track resources across organizational boundaries, ensure compliance with regulations and quality standards, and monitor increasingly complex processes involving multiple stakeholders.
Existing healthcare information systems provide only limited support for monitoring circular processes and demonstrating compliance throughout the care pathway. As healthcare systems transition from linear to circular models, new methods are needed to continuously monitor processes, detect deviations, assess compliance risks, and provide actionable insights to healthcare professionals and managers.
In this PhD project, you will investigate how process-aware information systems can support the monitoring and governance of circular care pathways. You will develop novel methods that use event data and healthcare process information to provide visibility into the execution of care pathways and identify opportunities for improving compliance, transparency, and sustainability. A central goal is to understand how organizations can continuously monitor circular healthcare processes and ensure that circular interventions remain safe and compliant with regulatory requirements.
You will become member of the Information Systems group within the Department of Industrial Engineering & Innovation Sciences at Eindhoven University of Technology. Your work is embedded in the NWO KIC funded REMARK project, in which a multidisciplinary consortium investigates how circular healthcare pathways can be designed and implemented in practice. For this project, you will collaborate with researchers from multiple universities, Dutch healthcare organizations and industry partners, giving you a unique opportunity to achieve both scientific and societal impact.
Job Requirements
You hold a master’s degree in Information Systems or a closely related field such as Computer Science, Industrial Engineering, or Innovation Science
You have a research-oriented attitude and have interest in Healthcare and Design Science Research.
You have interest in working with conceptual and process modelling approaches (e.g., BPMN, CMMN, DMN, goal modelling) as well as data-driven process analysis; prior experience is a plus.
You have the ability to collaborate in an interdisciplinary team involving academic and industrial partners.
You have the ability to translate research outcomes into practical tools and insights for stakeholders.
You are proactive, independent, and organized, with the ability to contribute to research management activities and coordinate tasks with partners and experts across the consortium
You are motivated to contribute to teaching and student supervision.
You have a strong publication ambition, targeting high-quality peer-reviewed journals and conferences in Information Systems and related fields, and motivation to participate in dissemination activities targeting healthcare stakeholders
You are fluent in spoken and written Dutch and English (C1 level).

Conditions of Employment
A meaningful job in a dynamic and ambitious university, in an interdisciplinary setting and within an international network. You will work on a beautiful, green campus within walking distance of the central train station.

In addition, we offer you:
Full-time employment for four years, with an intermediate assessment after nine months. You will spend a minimum of 10% of your four-year employment on teaching tasks, with a maximum of 15% per year of your employment.
Salary and benefits (such as a pension scheme, paid pregnancy and maternity leave, partially paid parental leave) in accordance with the Collective Labour Agreement for Dutch Universities , scale P (min. € 3,204 - max. € 4,051 gross base salary per month (full-time)).
In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.
Generous leave options: a standard 29 days (based on a 38 hour working week) per year that you can increase to 41 days by working two hours more per week (flexible working hours). This is prorated if you work part-time.
As a TU/e employee, you participate in the ABP pension scheme, providing retirement pension and pension benefits for surviving dependents and occupational disability. TU/e pays 70% of the pension premium, while employees contribute the remaining 30%.
High-quality training programs and other support to grow into a self-aware, autonomous scientific researcher. At TU/e we challenge you to take charge of your own learning process .
An excellent technical infrastructure, and on-campus children's day care.
Unlimited access to the modern on‑campus TU/e Student Sports Center at an exceptionally affordable rate.
We support your wellbeing with free 24/7 access to OpenUp, providing you and your family with mental health support, expert guidance, and online training.
An allowance for commuting, working from home and internet costs.
A Staff Immigration Team and a tax compensation scheme (the Expat Scheme ) for international candidates.

On our website you can discover even more information about our conditions of employment . Build on your career at TU/e!
About us
We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset. We work in an open and collaborative way with high-tech industries to tackle complex societal challenges. Our responsible and respectful approach ensures impact — today and in the future. TU/e is home to over 13,000 students and more than 7,000 staff, forming a diverse and vibrant academic community. Discover what Light Up means to TU/e in our short company video .
Our university is located in Brainport Eindhoven — a world‑leading tech region with more than 7,000 high‑tech companies and strong R&D activity. Known for breakthroughs in AI, photonics, semiconductors and advanced manufacturing, Brainport is a place where technology serves people and society. Learn more about the Brainport region here .
Information
Do you recognize yourself in this profile and would you like to know more? Please contact the hiring manager dr.ir. Rik Eshuis, [email protected] .
Visit our website for more information about the application process . You can also contact HR services via [email protected] .
Curious to hear more about what it’s like as a PhD candidate at TU/e? Please view the video .
Are you inspired and would like to know more about working at TU/e? Please visit our career page.
Application
We invite you to submit a complete application by using the apply button. The application should include a:
Cover letter in which you describe your motivation and explain why you would fit well the position.
List of courses you have taken in your Master and Bachelor programs (including grades).
Master thesis and/or peer reviewed articles authored by you.
Curriculum vitae, including the contact information of two references. Kindly note that we may reach out to references at any stage of the recruitment process. We recommend notifying your references upon submitting your application.
Results of a recent English language test, or other evidence of your English language capabilities, if applicable. In case of a non-Dutch applicant, results of a recent Dutch language test should be included.

Ensure that you submit all the requested application documents. We give priority to complete applications.

We look forward to receiving your application and will screen it as soon as possible. The vacancy will remain open until the position is filled.
Please note
You can apply online. We will not process applications sent by email and/or post.
A pre-employment screening (e.g. knowledge security check) can be part of the selection procedure. For more information on the knowledge security check, please consult the National Knowledge Security Guidelines .
Please do not contact us for unsolicited services.

KU Leuven is een onderzoeksintensieve, internationaal georiënteerde universiteit die zowel fundamenteel als toegepast wetenschappelijk onderzoek uitvoert. Zij is sterk inter- en multidisciplinair gericht en streeft naar internationale excellentie. De Faculteit en de onderzoekseenheden werken hiervoor actief samen met onderzoekspartners in binnen- en buitenland.

De Faculteit Rechtsgeleerdheid en Criminologische Wetenschappen van de Groep Humane Wetenschappen van KU Leuven heeft een deeltijdse vacature voor een aanstelling als gastdocent voor het opleidingsonderdeel ‘Vreemdelingenrecht’ (5%) in het domein van het vreemdelingen- en migratierecht.

In een maatschappelijke context van toenemende diversiteit wenst de Faculteit het domein van vreemdelingen- en migratierecht een nieuwe impuls te geven, zowel inzake onderwijs, als onderzoek en dienstverlening. Daarbij staan een transversale benadering en interdisciplinaire openheid centraal. Het onderwijs zal daarom de nationaliteits- en verblijfswetgeving behandelen, maar eveneens privaat- en sociaalrechtelijke thema’s in verband met migratie in het algemeen. Het zal bijzondere aandacht besteden aan specifieke categorieën van vreemdelingen en migranten, in het bijzonder de meest kwetsbaren (bijvoorbeeld niet-begeleide minderjarigen, vreemdelingen zonder of met een precaire verblijfsstatus). Tevens wordt de band gelegd met het integratiebeleid en de actuele uitdagingen in een diverse samenleving.

De Faculteit Rechtsgeleerdheid en Criminologische Wetenschappen heeft een sterke nationale en internationale reputatie inzake onderwijs, onderzoek en dienstverlening. Zij streeft op elk van deze vlakken leiderschap na op nationaal, Europees en internationaal niveau. Daarbij wenst de Faculteit zich te onderscheiden door het academische karakter van haar werkzaamheden en het besef van de grote maatschappelijke rol van dat domein. De techniciteit van het rechtsdomein is daarom te overstijgen met originaliteit in onderzoek, aandacht voor waarden, bewustzijn voor de interactie van de rechtsregels in een meergelaagde rechtsorde, intra- en interdisciplinariteit.

Website van de eenheid

Functie

Onderwijs

De opdracht van de kandidaat omvat het verzorgen van het nationale luik binnen het opleidingsonderdeel Vreemdelingenrecht (in het Nederlands) binnen de master rechten, Campus Leuven en de begeleiding van masterproeven in het domein van het vreemdelingen- en migratierecht. Het nationale luik van het opleidingsonderdeel Vreemdelingenrecht beoogt om de studenten vertrouwd te maken met de institutionele verdeling van bevoegdheden op het vlak van migratie en integratie en de belangrijkste actoren op het terrein van het vreemdelingenrecht, met de voornaamste migratie- en verblijfsmogelijkheden (studiemigratie, arbeidsmigratie, gezinshereniging en verblijf om humanitaire redenen), inbegrepen de beroepsmogelijkheden tegen negatieve beslissingen, en, ten slotte, met de meest relevante juridische instrumenten op het vlak van migratiehandhaving en integratie.

Het onderwijs moet beantwoorden aan de eisen die aan academische opleidingen worden gesteld wat niveau, oriëntatie en academisch gehalte betreft. Het sluit aan bij het onderwijsconcept van KU Leuven; in het bijzonder is het onderzoeksgebaseerd en -georiënteerd. Engagement voor de kwaliteit van de opleiding als geheel wordt als vanzelfsprekend beschouwd.

Onderzoek

Het behoort tot de opdracht van de kandidaat om in nauwe samenwerking met andere onderzoekers van de Faculteit, wetenschappelijk onderzoek te verrichten over het vreemdelingen- en migratierecht. Van de kandidaat wordt verwacht dat zij/hij initiatieven tot het bekomen en uitvoeren van onderzoeksprojecten, zowel Vlaams, nationaal als Europees, ontplooit en doctoraten (mee) kan begeleiden. Van de kandidaat wordt gevraagd dat hij/zij een visie op onderzoek en een voorstel voor een duidelijke onderzoekslijn in het vreemdelingen- en migratierecht toevoegt aan het sollicitatiedossier.

Dienstverlening

De aangestelde kandidaat zal ook taken van wetenschappelijke en andere dienstverlening opnemen. Van de kandidaat wordt verwacht dat zij/hij bereid is om mee te werken aan de universitaire en facultaire dienstverlening. De kandidaat staat tevens ter beschikking van de overheid, samenleving en media voor wetenschappelijke dienstverlening en duiding.

Profiel

U heeft een doctoraat in de rechten behaald en u hebt relevante praktijkervaring.

U beschikt over een gedegen visie op, en de bekwaamheid tot, het verzorgen van academisch hoogstaand onderzoeksgebaseerd onderwijs en uitstekende didactische vaardigheden.

Onderwijservaring is een plusunt.

U beschikt over aantoonbare organisatorische, sociale en professionele vaardigheden en leidinggevende capaciteiten om zich collegiaal en flexibel in teamverband in te schakelen.

Aanbod

Wij bieden u een deeltijdse tewerkstelling (5%) aan in een intellectueel uitdagende omgeving.

U wordt aangesteld als gastdocent voor een periode van 1 jaar, verlengbaar.

De aanstelling start op 1 september 2027.

Interesse?

Er wordt verwacht dat u aan het sollicitatiedossier toevoegt:
- een motivatiebrief (max. 2 pagina’s);
- een uitgebreid cv met publicatielijst;
- een beschrijving van uw visie op academisch onderwijs;
- onderwijsevaluaties waarover u beschikt;
- informatie over uw studieresultaten (behaalde graden, rankings, ...).

Contactpersonen bij vragen over de inhoud van deze functie of vacature zijn:
Prof. dr. Koen Lemmens, voorzitter Onderzoekseenheid Publiekrecht, [email protected] ;
Prof. dr. Wouter Devroe, decaan, [email protected]

ap:254540.body:
Work Activities
AI-assisted discovery of chiral perovskite (quantum) emitters. You will leverage an AI-assisted materials optimization robot being developed at AMOLF as a route to rapid, closed-loop synthesis and characterization across large perovskite parameter spaces. You will optimize directly for figures of merit such as chirality, emission wavelength, brightness, and stability. Because optical excitation of perovskites can move atoms around, sculpting the optical field in time and space can enable programmable optical functions. By conducting approximately 1 million optical experiments in parallel using a spatial light modulator and hyperspectral camera, you will explore chemical and processing landscapes in days that would otherwise take a student a lifetime to cover systematically. Special attention will be paid to 2D and related low-dimensional perovskites, with the aim to understand if intrinsically strong material chirality is a necessary condition for reaching strong programmable chirality.
Materials discovery in non-trivial optical environments. Building on the first thrust, you will introduce a new paradigm in optoelectronic device design: to synthesize and screen perovskite emitters directly on substrates that already provide a structured optical response. In a material that can be sculpted by the optical field, this provides the opportunity for a self-optimizing response – the local optical field imprints a symmetry on the material, which then amplifies the light-matter coupling. In the conventional workflow, one first finds a material with good intrinsic properties and only then designs the surrounding cavity, resonance, or metasurface. You will reverse that order, replacing an optically inert glass slide by a substrate with a designed resonance arising from refractive-index structuring (optical metasurface). Thin perovskite films spun onto such a substrate will respond most strongly when their emission (absorption) spectrum aligns with the photonic resonance. Likewise, if the figure of merit is chirality and the substrate itself has chiral optical response, one can search for materials whose intrinsic emission (absorption) couples most effectively to that environment. In this way, the optical structure of the substrate transforms the material on top into exactly what it needs for maximal performance. Such exploration offers tantalizing opportunities to study the impact of local versus nonlocal optical resonances in the context of material optimization. How does the spatial extent of the photonic resonance affect the material symmetry? Does the optical field profile induce spatially varying chiral properties in the perovskite? Understanding the coupling between photonic environment and material crystallization poses completely new opportunities in material synthesis for advanced photonic integration and technologies.
Qualifications
You have a Msc degree in physics, chemistry, materials science, engineering or another scientific discipline. You have an analytical mind with the ability to think about a problem and come up with logical and creative solutions. You can work independently and also enjoy collaborating in a team. You enjoy actively engaging others to learn new concepts and experimental methods. You are eager to give and receive feedback and see it as an opportunity for personal and professional growth. You have excellent communication skills in English. You are responsible, reliable and dedicated while caring about the well-being of yourself and your colleagues. You value and cherish diversity of background, opinion and ability and see a team as more than the sum of its parts.
Work environment
This is a collaborative project between AMOLF and the University of Amsterdam. Your contract and host group will be the Nanoscale Solar Cells group led by Erik Garnett at AMOLF amolf.nl/research-groups/nanoscale-solar-cells but you will also work part time at the Van der Waals-Zeeman institute of the University of Amsterdam iop.uva.nl/wzi/wzi.html with professors Sander Mann mannlab.nl and Jorik van de Groep vandegroeplab.com in the department of physics. These institutes are located next to each other in the Amsterdam Science Park. This collaborative position opens up many experimental and theoretical tools and facilities needed for the project including the AI-assisted automated synthesis and characterization robot, the AMOLF nanolab www.amolf.nl/nanolab , ultrafast, chiral and single photon microscopes and full-wave numerical simulations and analytical models. We share a vibrant, inclusive and collaborative work culture that welcomes scientists and engineers with diverse backgrounds and skills. There is a very active staff association organizing regular social activities throughout the year to enrich the work experience and community. There is excellent support staff to help with the more technical and administrative parts of the project.
Working conditions
The working atmosphere at the institute is largely determined by young, enthusiastic, mostly foreign employees. Communication is informal and runs through short lines of communication.
The position is intended as full-time (40 hours / week, 12 months / year) appointment in the service of the Netherlands Foundation of Scientific Research Institutes (NWO-I) for the duration of four years
The starting salary is 3.115 Euro’s gross per month and a range of employment benefits .
After successful completion of the PhD research a PhD degree will be granted at a Dutch University.
Several courses are offered, specially developed for PhD-students.
AMOLF assists any new foreign PhD-student with housing and visa applications and compensates their transport costs and furnishing expenses.

More information?
For further information about the position or specific questions, please contact Erik Garnett: [email protected]
Application
You can respond to this vacancy online via the button below. Please apply by submitting a CV and cover letter explaining why you want this specific PhD position, what you can contribute and what you would like to learn. We will start evaluating applications on December 1st and will continue until the position is filled.
Online screening may be part of the selection.
Diversity code
AMOLF is highly committed to an inclusive and diverse work environment: we want to develop talent and creativity by bringing together people from different backgrounds and cultures. We recruit and select on the basis of competencies and talents. We strongly encourage anyone with the right qualifications to apply for the vacancy, regardless of age, gender, origin, sexual orientation or physical ability.
AMOLF has won the NNV Diversity Award 2022, which is awarded every two years by the Netherlands Physical Society for demonstrating the most successful implementation of equality, diversity and inclusion (EDI).
Commercial activities in response to this ad are not appreciated.

ap:254541.body:
Doctoral Positions in Exoplanet Atmosphere Characterisation and the Search for Life
We are looking for one or two Doctoral Students to work on the atmospheric characterisation of temperate terrestrial exoplanets and the search for life within the Exoplanets and Habitability Group led by Prof. Sascha P. Quanz at ETH Zurich. The positions is closely connected to the ETH-led LIFE space mission . LIFE is a space-based mid-infrared nulling interferometer to directly detect and spectroscopically characterise dozens of temperate terrestrial exoplanets around nearby stars. The successful candidates will join the LIFE Science Team and work closely with researchers and students at ETH Zurich and across the wider LIFE collaboration.

Project background
A central goal of LIFE is to characterise the atmospheres of temperate terrestrial exoplanets and ultimately assess their habitability and possible signs of life. Understanding which atmospheric properties can be robustly inferred from mid-infrared observations is also essential for translating LIFE's science goals into science requirements and corresponding instrument-performance requirements.

Our group has developed the atmospheric retrieval framework pyRetLIFE and has so far investigated mainly Earth-like planets and classical atmospheric biosignature gases. An important next step is to broaden this work towards the diversity of potentially habitable and inhabited worlds: different atmospheric compositions and climates, non-Earth-like biospheres, non-standard biosignatures, and the abiotic scenarios against which potential signs of life need to be interpreted.

Possible research directions for the successful Doctoral students include

The modelling and characterisation of non-Earth-like atmospheres and biospheres, using physically motivated atmospheric models and retrievals to understand which properties and potential biosignatures future missions like LIFE can robustly constrain

The exploration of alternative inference approaches, including machine learning and AI, for atmospheric characterisation and the interpretation of potential signs of life, this could include investigating where such methods provide additional information compared with conventional retrievals, and assessing their robustness, interpretability and sensitivity to modelling assumptions

Job description

Develop and pursue research on the characterisation of temperate terrestrial exoplanet atmospheres and the search for signs of life in the context of the LIFE mission

Investigate atmospheric scenarios beyond modern Earth analogues; this may include non-Earth-like biospheres, non-standard biosignatures and/or relevant abiotic alternatives

Use and further develop atmospheric retrieval and/or complementary modelling and inference approaches

Explore, where relevant, ML/AI approaches for atmospheric inference and interpretation

Investigate the robustness and limitations of atmospheric characterisation methods and compare complementary approaches where scientifically useful

In close collaboration with the LIFE Science Team and LIFE Instrument Science Team, translate atmospheric characterisation results into science requirements and related instrument-performance requirements for LIFE

Contribute new scientific ideas to the development of the LIFE science case and interact with the broader LIFE collaboration

Profile

Master's degree (or equivalent degree) in astrophysics, planetary science, atmospheric science, physics or a closely related field, completed by the start date

Strong interest in exoplanet science, atmospheres, habitability, biosignatures and the search for life

Experience in one or more of the following is welcome, but not required: atmospheric modelling, atmospheric retrievals, radiative transfer, photochemical or climate modelling, statistical inference, machine-learning/AI methods, or related numerical approaches

Strong scientific programming skills, preferably in Python; experience with AI and machine learning tools is an asset

Ability and interest to work in a team and across disciplinary boundaries

Ability to interact with the broader exoplanet, atmospheric science and astrobiology communities

Scientific curiosity, independence and a collaborative approach to research

Very good command of English (spoken and written)

We offer

A collaborative and interdisciplinary research environment within the Exoplanets and Habitability Group and the LIFE Space Mission team at ETH Zurich, with close links to the international LIFE collaboration

A fully funded four-year Doctoral Position with competitive salary and benefits according to ETH regulations, including support for conference travel, computing and career development

Working, teaching and research at ETH Zurich We value diversity and sustainability
In line with our values , ETH Zurich encourages an inclusive culture. We promote equality of opportunity, value diversity and nurture a working and learning environment in which the rights and dignity of all our staff and students are respected. Visit our Equal Opportunities and Diversity website to find out how we ensure a fair and open environment that allows everyone to grow and flourish. Sustainability is a core value for us – we are consistently working towards a climate-neutral future .
Curious? So are we.
We look forward to receiving your online application with the following documents:

CV

University transcripts and, if already available, diploma

A statement of research interests (max. 2 pages), indicating which of the research directions described above you would be particularly interested in pursuing.

Names and contact details of three referees

The application deadline is November 25, 2026. The start date is flexible, but we envision to start in spring / early summer 2027.

Further information about the group can be found on our website . Questions regarding the position and informal enquiries are welcome and should be directed to Prof. Sascha P. Quanz,  [email protected] . Please note that applications must be submitted exclusively through our online application portal; applications sent by email or post will not be considered.

We would like to point out that the pre-selection is carried out by the responsible recruiters and not by artificial intelligence.

About ETH Zürich
ETH Zurich is one of the world’s leading universities specialising in
science and technology. We are renowned for our excellent education,
cutting-edge fundamental research and direct transfer of new knowledge
into society. Over 30,000 people from more than 120 countries find our
university to be a place that promotes independent thinking and an
environment that inspires excellence. Located in the heart of Europe,
yet forging connections all over the world, we work together to
develop solutions for the global challenges of today and tomorrow.

ap:254546.body:
The Manufacturing Metrology research group of the KU Leuven Department of Mechanical Engineering investigates, develops, optimises and implements measurement solutions for manufacturing quality control. Our expertise covers surface and 3D coordinate metrology using tactile and optical probes as well as X-ray Computed Tomography (XCT). We target Industry 4.0 readiness of measurement solutions by increasing speed, reducing measurement errors, and establishing traceability to realise in-line and in-process capabilities that intelligently feedback inspection results for first-time-right and zero-waste manufacturing. We put our expertise and state-of-the-art equipment at the disposal of manufacturing companies to address complex metrology challenges and to improve manufacturing process understanding and performance.

Website unit

Responsibilities

X-ray computed tomography (XCT) is a non-destructive volumetric imaging technology that can image both external and internal structures of parts. The technology has been increasingly used for industrial applications. However, the cost and time consumed to conduct XCT scans are significant for industrial use in the uptake of the technology. Hence, most XCTs are used for research rather than for production purposes.

Recent developments have demonstrated the potential of using XCT to assess the quality of battery cells. However, there is currently no guidance on how to perform dimensional evaluation for such specialised applications, and the impact of systematic influence factors and measurement errors remains largely unknown. This project aims to develop a robust data analysis workflow that converts XCT measurement outputs into reliable, interpretable quality metrics.

As part of this project, you will join a supportive team of research scientists working together to advance battery quality evaluation using XCT. You’ll have the chance to learn new skills, contribute your own ideas, and grow your expertise while shaping your future career path.

Profile

Candidate must:

Hold a Master's degree in Maths, Computer Science, Physics, Engineering, or the equivalent.

Has distinction in Master degree.

Be knowledgeable in areas such as statistical analysis, imaging processing and analysis, machine learning

Experience in X-ray computed tomography or instrument calibration is considered an asset.

Other general requirement:

Has a scientific curiosity and interest in research.

Has strong mathematical and computational skills.

Has strong analytical and problem-solving skills.

Has the necessary skills to design and implement experiments, undertake computational tasks, and analyse measurement results.

Has adequate English communication skills and can present results competently and comprehensively in research team meetings, conferences and peer-reviewed journal papers.

Is flexible and has good time management skills.

Can work independently and have good interactions with the co/supervisors and peers.

Frequently report the progress of the conducted research to the co/supervisors.

Is willing to help organise workshops and other events.

Is willing to engage in teaching assignments.

Is willing to travel nationally or internationally to visit collaborators to conduct work.

Offer

The opportunity to pursue a PhD degree that is fully supported for 4 years.

The project can start immediately following the completion of recruitment.

Interested?

The applicant should provide the following information in the application:

·       An academic CV

·       Bachelor degree (Bachelor specification, University + Country, Year obtained), score

·       Master degree (Master specification, University + Country, Year obtained), Master thesis if any (Title, Year, Supervisor), score

·       A one-paragraph (maximum one page) statement explaining the motivation for applying for this PhD position.

·       Two academic references

For more information please contact Prof. dr. Wenjuan Sun, mail: [email protected] or dr. Maryam Ramezani, mail: [email protected] .

ap:254552.body:
In the Science, Engineering and Technology Group of KU Leuven, Faculty of Engineering Science, Department of Electrical Engineering (ESAT), there is a full-time academic vacancy in the field of analogue computing at microwave frequencies, in Leuven (Campus Arenberg).

We are looking for internationally oriented candidates with an excellent research record. Candidates have recently been awarded an ERC grant in this area and are willing to perform their research at KU Leuven. Candidates also have educational competence in the field of electrical engineering, with emphasis on electromagnetics in the broad sense.

Your research will be based in the ESAT Department, within the WAVECORE division at the Arenberg campus. This division boasts excellent research infrastructure, an extensive international network, industry connections, a steady stream of talented PhD students, and a supportive working environment.

You will contribute to the teaching activities of the Faculty of Engineering Science. KU Leuven is committed to a culture of quality and is highly rated by independent evaluation committees. Thanks to our (inter)national network, industry ties, and KU Leuven’s professional organizational network, we ensure innovation and quality assurance in our education.

Website unit

Duties

Research

You develop a research programme in the field of analogue computing at microwave frequencies.

Your work will be carried out within the division WaveCore of the Department of Electrical Engineering and in the Faculty of Engineering Science, in the Science, Engineering and Technology Group of KU Leuven.

Your research activities focus on both theoretical and experimental aspects regarding new architectures for analog computing at microwave frequencies and in telecommunications.

You set up collaborations within and outside of the department.

You publish at the highest scientific level, acquire resources for research, develop international collaborations, and supervise PhDs at an international level.

Teaching

You ensure high-quality education within the area of electrical engineering, with special attention on courses related to electromagnetics.

You contribute actively to the overall excellence of the Master in Electrical Engineering.

You also contribute to the pedagogic project of the faculty and university through the supervision of master theses and as a promoter of PhD students.

You develop your teachings in accordance with KU Leuven’s vision on activating and researched-based education and make use of the possibilities for the educationalist professionalization offered by the faculty and the university.

Service

Besides your responsibilities for research and teaching, you are willing to provide service to the community and the department and faculty, depending on requirements and interests.

Profile

You have a PhD in electrical engineering.

You have a strong research profile. The quality of your research is proven by publications in prominent journals and through international research experience.

You have demonstrable qualities related to academic education. Teaching experience is an advantage.

You possess organisational skills and have a cooperative attitude. You also possess leadership capacities within a university context.

The official administrative language of KU Leuven is Dutch. If, upon recruitment, you have no or insufficient knowledge of Dutch, then KU Leuven provides language training to enable you to participate in (board)meetings. You must achieve CEFR level B2 within five years of the start of your appointment.

Afterwards, you must acquire the required knowledge of Dutch [or English] at CEFR level C1 in order to become a course leader in Dutch [or English]. KU Leuven also provides training to help you achieve this level.

In order to fulfil the three core missions of your assignment (teaching, research, and academic and social service), the university expects you to eventually develop proficiency in both English and Dutch to CEFR level C1.

Offer

We are offering a full-time employment in an intellectually challenging environment. KU Leuven is a research-intensive, internationally oriented university that carries out both fundamental and applied scientific research. Our university is highly inter- and multidisciplinarily focused and strives for international excellence. In this regard we actively work together with research partners in Belgium and abroad and provide our students with an academic education that is based on high-quality scientific research.

You will be working at KU Leuven’s Arenberg campus nearby Leuven, a historic yet dynamic and vibrant city in the centre of Belgium, with a 25-minute train journey to Brussels, the capital of the European Union, and approximately two hours’ journey to Paris, London and Amsterdam.

KU Leuven offers hybrid working possibilities for a balanced combination of on-campus work and remote working.

Depending on your record and qualifications, you will be appointed to one of the grades of the senior academic staff: assistant professor, associate professor, professor or full professor.

To facilitate your academic integration and research at the start of your career, a start-up funding of 110,000 euro is also provided. The department also provides funding for a four-year PhD project, along with 5.000 euro in operating funds.

KU Leuven is well equipped to welcome international professors and their families and offers practical support in areas such as immigration and administrative matters, accommodation, childcare, learning Dutch, and more.

Interested?

For more information on the contents of the job, please contact:

o Prof. dr. ir. Vincent Rijmen, Chair of the department of Electrical Engineering, tel.: +32 16 321968, mail: [email protected]

o Prof. Dr. Ir. Dominique Schreurs, Vice-chair of Wavecore research group, tel.: +32 16 32 18 21, e-mail: [email protected]

You can apply exclusively via our online application system. If you encounter any problems when applying online, please contact: [email protected] .

Please include the following documents with your application (further information can be found on the KU Leuven job site):

- a biosketch indicating your added value as an academic in relation to the core tasks of research, teaching and service provision throughout your career to date and in relation to your future activities (maximum 2 pages);

- a file with your five most important publications or realisations;

- a detailed CV (including a full list of publications and, where applicable, a portfolio of your architectural projects/ADRO);

- a research plan focusing on the development of your research line and associated research team, with an emphasis on collaboration with the colleague-researchers within the employing entity (maximum 4 pages);

- your vision on academic education and how you translate this vision into practice (maximum 2 pages);

- your contribution to service activities (internal representation in boards and councils, contributions to society through outreach and science communication) (maximum 1 page);

- your vision on leadership and how you apply this vision in practice in your managerial role and responsibilities (maximum 1 page).

We ask that all documents be submitted in English.

KU Leuven places great importance on research integrity  and ethical conduct and will therefore ask you to sign a research integrity statement upon appointment.

ABOUT GHENT UNIVERSITY
Ghent University is a world of its own. Employing more than 15,000 people, it is actively involved in education and research, management and administration, as well as technical and social service provision on a daily basis. It is one of the largest, most exciting employers in the area and offers great career opportunities. With its 11 faculties and more than 80 departments offering state-of-the-art study programmes grounded in research in a wide range of academic fields, Ghent University is a logical choice for its staff and students.
YOUR TASKS
You will contribute to research projects focusing on medical terminologies, international classification systems and semantic interoperability of health data.
The position is situated at the intersection of health informatics, medical terminologies, ontologies and artificial intelligence. You will contribute to the development of methods and tools that enable semantic mapping and interoperability between SNOMED-CT and international classification systems such as ICPC-3, ICF, ICHI and other WHO classifications. The overall goal is to improve the interoperability, secondary use and analysis of health data in both clinical practice and research settings.
WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You hold a Master’s degree in one of the domains of Health Sciences, Medicine, Health Informatics, Computer Science, Informatics, or an equivalent qualification
You have a strong interest in scientific research related to medical information standards and medical terminologies
You possess strong analytical skills and work in a precise and structured manner
You are able to work both independently and as part of a multidisciplinary team
You have excellent written and spoken communication skills in English
The following knowledge and experience are considered strong assets:   Medical terminologies and classification systems (e.g. SNOMED-CT, ICPC-3, ICF, ICHI, …)
Semantic interoperability in healthcare
Ontologies, knowledge representation and Semantic Web technologies
Relevant programming languages and technical skills required for the execution of project tasks

Experience with WHO classifications and participation in (inter)national terminology projects is considered an advantage

INTERESTED?
Apply  online through the e-recruitment system   before the application deadline  (see above). We do not accept late applications or applications that are not submitted through the online system.
Your application must include the following documents:
In the field  ‘CV’ : your CV and a transcript of your academic record (merged into one pdf file)
In the field  ‘Cover letter’ : your application letter in pdf format
In the field  ‘Diploma’ : a transcript of the required degree (if already in your possession). If you have a foreign diploma in a language other than our national languages (Dutch, French or German) or English, please add a translation in one of the mentioned languages.

Note that the maximum file size for each field is 10 MB.
As Ghent University maintains an equal opportunities and diversity policy, everyone is encouraged to apply for this position.

MORE INFORMATION
