ABOUT GHENT UNIVERSITY
Ghent University is an internationally oriented research university with approximately 50,000 students, 15,500 employees, and nearly 5,000 doctoral researchers. Its doctoral researchers benefit from high-quality supervision, state-of-the-art research infrastructure, comprehensive doctoral training, and an international and multidisciplinary research community. Through its Dare to Think philosophy, the university encourages scientific curiosity, innovation, academic independence, and the development of critical and independent researchers.
You will join the Center for Microsystems Technology (CMST), an imec-associated research laboratory within the Department of Electronics and Information Systems (ELIS) of the Faculty of Engineering and Architecture. CMST conducts research on smart microsystem design and integration across technology platforms that include smart power, advanced packaging, and microsystem integration. The position therefore offers a highly relevant environment for interdisciplinary research combining GaN technology, integrated-circuit design, and power electronics.
This doctoral position is offered within BESCAPE (Boosting Europe’s Space Competitiveness through Advanced Power Electronics), a Horizon Europe Marie Skłodowska-Curie Actions Doctoral Network Joint Doctorate developed with the European Space Agency and leading European space companies. BESCAPE addresses power conversion, advanced control, and power-distribution challenges for future human space-exploration missions. Ghent University offers one fully funded doctoral position in this international research and training network, in close collaboration with imec and the University of Oviedo.
YOUR TASKS
As a doctoral researcher, you will:
Study state-of-the-art point-of-load (PoL) converter architectures and integrated-circuit solutions for space applications, identifying their main limitations and opportunities for further integration.
Explore and develop new circuit and system-level design solutions for highly integrated PoL converters.
Design and develop an all-GaN integrated circuit using one of imec’s low-voltage GaN technologies, targeting a stand-alone PoL voltage regulator for space applications.
Investigate the project’s Level 4 integration concept, with monolithic implementation of the closed-loop control and key circuit blocks, including the reference-voltage generator, error amplifier, comparator, sawtooth generator, and on-chip local supply-voltage generator.
Develop health-monitoring, protection, and reliability concepts, including temperature monitoring, short-circuit detection, and on-chip redundancy for critical circuit blocks.
Closely collaborate with researchers at CMST, imec, and the University of Oviedo, combining expertise in integrated-circuit design, GaN technology, and power-converter design.
Undertake research secondments at imec and the University of Oviedo as part of the BESCAPE Joint Doctorate programme.
Disseminate your research results through scientific publications and presentations at international conferences.
Contribute to the research activities of the group and assist with a limited number of educational tasks.

WHAT WE ARE LOOKING FOR
You hold a master’s degree in electronic engineering, electrical engineering, or a closely related discipline.
You have a solid background in electronic systems and circuit design, with a good understanding of analogue electronics and the design and operation of electronic circuits.
You have good knowledge of power electronics and power-converter topologies, including the principles of DC-DC conversion, switching converters, and their control.
You have a good understanding of semiconductor devices and their application in electronic and power-conversion circuits.
You have experience with circuit modelling and simulation and are familiar with relevant simulation and programming environments, such as SPICE, MATLAB/Simulink, or Python.
Experience in analogue and/or mixed-signal IC design is a strong asset. Experience with an IC process design kit (PDK), including schematic design, circuit simulation, layout, DRC, LVS, and parasitic extraction (PEX), is highly valued.
Experience with Cadence design tools or equivalent IC design environments is an asset.
Hands-on experience with PCB design, embedded electronics, laboratory measurement setups, or electrical characterization is considered an advantage.
You are highly motivated to conduct independent scientific research, explore new circuit and system concepts, and publish your results at leading international conferences and in peer-reviewed journals.
You have strong analytical and problem-solving skills, a critical and creative mindset, and the ability to work effectively in an international and collaborative research environment.
You have excellent spoken and written English communication skills.

Eligibility requirements: At the recruitment date, you must not hold a doctoral degree and must not have resided in or carried out your main activity in Belgium for more than 12 months during the 36 months immediately preceding recruitment. You must also meet the doctoral admission requirements of Ghent University and the University of Oviedo.
WHAT WE CAN OFFER YOU
A fully funded, full-time doctoral position, initially offered for 12 months and, following a positive evaluation, in principle extended for an additional 36 months, resulting in a total maximum duration of 48 months, within the BESCAPE Horizon Europe MSCA Doctoral Network Joint Doctorate (Grant Agreement No. 101312786). The estimated start date is between May and October 2027.
A joint doctoral degree awarded by Ghent University and the University of Oviedo.
An international training programme with leading universities, the European Space Agency, European space companies, and imec, including secondments, BESCAPE summer schools, and specialised training events.
A full employment contract and social-security coverage under Belgian legislation.
An MSCA funding package comprising living and mobility allowances and, where applicable, a family allowance. The indicated gross annual amount before employer and employee contributions is EUR 56,640 per year, plus a family allowance of EUR 7,920 per year where applicable.
A workplace at the Center for Microsystems Technology (CMST), an imec-associated research laboratory within ELIS at Ghent University in Ghent-Zwijnaarde. Two planned research secondments: three months at imec in Leuven and six months at the University of Oviedo in Spain.

INTERESTED?
Submit your application by email to [email protected] no later than 15 December 2026. Use “Application BESCAPE PhD position DC6” as the subject line and include:
a detailed CV in Europass format;
bachelor’s and master’s academic certificates and transcripts, including examinations and grades;
a copy of a valid passport or European identity card; and
contact details of two academic referees.

Documents must be submitted in English or accompanied by an English translation. Additional documentation may be requested during the selection process.

As a joint venture of the University of Basel and the University Hospitals Basel, the Department of Biomedicine (DBM) brings together basic and clinical scientists to advance the understanding of health and disease. We are home to more than 67 research groups and over 800 employees across six locations in the heart of Basel. Our collaborative and international environment fosters innovation, excellence, and impactful research. The Blood Cancer Biology and Immunotherapy group, led by Prof. Petya Apostolova ( www.apostolovalab.com ), is looking for a highly motivated research assistant/laboratory technician (70-100%) to support our ongoing work on understanding how metabolites shape anti-leukemia immunity and the leukemic microenvironment.

Start date: 1. February 2027 or upon agreement.
Duration: 1 year, with possibility of extension and long-term perspective.

Join our community and help shape the future of biomedicine.
The successful candidate will support the research group and individual scientists with lab maintenance,experimental work, and biobanking.

Your responsibilities will include: Laboratory maintenance
Preparation of common lab reagents
Biobanking of human blood and bone marrow samples including documentation
Technical support of PhD students and postdocs, including with cell culture and animal experiments

Experimental approaches in our group include in vivo leukemia and allogeneic hematopoietic stem celltransplantation models, liquid chromatography-mass spectrometry metabolomics and lipidomics, functionalgenomics and CRISPR screens, spectral flow cytometry, cell sorting, bulk, single-cell and spatialtranscriptomics, and functional immune and metabolic assays. The successful candidate will have theopportunity to learn and independently apply several of these techniques.
Research environment
The Apostolova Lab is based at the Department of Biomedicine, University of Basel, in a highly interactiveenvironment spanning cancer biology, immunology, genomics, metabolism, and translational medicine. Ourgroup combines mechanistic leukemia models with metabolism, immunology, and multi-omics to understandhow leukemia cells adapt to therapeutic pressure and interact with the immune system. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to join a young and dynamic group conducting high-levelresearch in hematology. The candidate will receive direct support from the lab manager and other scientists toset their mark in the lab and will be actively involved in the lab projects, providing multiple opportunities fortraining in flow cytometry, molecular biology, metabolism assays, and in vivo experimentation. Mentorship andrespect for human values, including diversity, equity, and inclusiveness, are driving forces of our group.
Training as a molecular biology research technician (lab technician) or M.Sc. (or equivalent) in biological sciences or related fields
Proficient in basic lab techniques (cell culture, working in sterile conditions, PCR)
Previous experience with processing human blood samples, animal work, molecular biology, flow cytometry, or metabolism assays will be advantageous
Willingness to work with animal models
Interest in hematology, tumor immunology, and metabolism
Excellent communication skills (English mandatory, German advantageous) and the ability to work collaboratively in an interdisciplinary team

A stimulating, interdisciplinary research environment focused on the role of metabolism in leukemia and the leukemia-immune crosstalk
A dynamic and international team with a strong culture of collaboration and mutual support
Opportunities for development of technical skills
Close interaction with neighboring labs in hematology, cancer immunology, oncology, and metabolism
Strong mentorship, including career development support
Competitive academic environment at the University of Basel

The Atmospheric Sciences group at the Department of Environmental Sciences, University of Basel, Switzerland, is looking for a PhD student candidate. One of our research projects focuses on novel photocatalytic processes for CO2 reduction. Our approach involved the production of metal and metal oxide nanoparticles via the aerosol phase (as opposed to liquid phase synthesis method usually applied). Aerosol-phase nanoparticle synthesis is completely solvent-free and allows to generate particles down to 1 nm in diameter and to modify particle properties such as crystal structure, doping and mixing to adjust and optimise photocatalytic processes.
A PhD studentship is available to generate metal nanoparticles with various composition in the gas phase and to thoroughly characterize them with various analytical techniques such as Transmission Electron Microscopy (TEM), X-ray Photoelectron Spectroscopy (XPS), X-ray diffraction (XRD) and optical methods such as UV-Vis and IR (see for example: Gfeller et al., Aerosol Res., 3, 351–369, 2025). In addition, the particles will be characterized by their photocatalytic activity. In addition, structural and compositional aspects of the nanoparticles will be optimized. The focus of the photocatalytic process will be on CO2 reduction in CO, methane and other products but also other reactions might be investigated with our novel nanoparticle generation methodology using chromatography and mass spectrometry techniques.
An academic qualification (master's degree) in chemistry, physics, environmental sciences, or a related field is mandatory
Experience in catalysis and/or surface science is highly favourable
A very good level of English (spoken and written)
Excellent communication skills and a willingness to collaborate with other team members are essential
Strong self-motivation, perseverance, and a creative way of problem solving
Ability to work independently

A fully funded PhD position (4 years) in the Atmospheric Sciences research group at the Department of Environmental Sciences at the University of Basel, Switzerland.
A motivated, interdisciplinary team that will support your ideas, research and career in a stimulating, welcoming and multicultural environment.
A well-equipped, modern lab at a top research university. University of Basel has an international reputation of outstanding achievements in research and teaching. It offers excellent support to PhD students in the early stage of their career and for their career advancement.
Salary and social benefits are provided according to Swiss standards and University of Basel rules ( https://www.unibas.ch/en/Working-at-the-University-of-Basel/Salary-Insurance.html ).

Application / Contact
Please submit your complete application documents, including a letter stating your motivation, experience and skills, a CV, and contact details of two references via our online recruiting platform
For further information please contact Prof. Dr. Markus Kalberer ( [email protected] ).
Applications will be reviewed from 1st December 2026, but the advert will remain open until the position is filled. Starting date is subject to agreement
You can find out more about us at https://duw.unibas.ch/en/research-groups/atmospheric-sciences/

ap:254669.body:
Department of Biomedical Engineering (DBE), University of Basel
Group: Analytics & Informatics for Child Health (AICH) in collaboration with University Children's Hospital Basel (UKBB)
Starting date: November 2026 or upon agreement
Duration: 4 years

About Us

The Analytics & Informatics for Child Health (AICH) group develops AI/ML methods, digital tools, and secure data pipelines to advance pediatric healthcare. We work at the intersection of clinical medicine, machine learning, and data-intensive research, collaborating closely with hospitals, clinical IT teams, and research partners at the University of Basel.

The Project

Preterm birth affects around 14 million infants each year and is a major risk factor for lifelong respiratory disease. Current definitions of bronchopulmonary dysplasia (BPD) are categorical and predict long-term outcomes poorly. Robust early-life markers to identify infants at the highest risk of prematurity-associated lung disease (PLD) are lacking.

This project uses the Basel-Bern Infant Lung Development (BILD) cohort, which combines infant lung function, breath metabolomics, urine oxidative stress markers, clinical history, high-resolution air pollution exposure, and longitudinal lung function follow-up into adolescence. The goal is a continuous, physiology-based risk stratification framework to replace categorical BPD definitions, and to inform a respiratory follow-up program for preterm children in Switzerland.

The PhD student will lead the machine learning component: integrating clinical, physiological, environmental, and biomarker data to identify early-life signatures, aetiotypes, and treatable traits of PLD, with external validation in cohorts from Italy and Australia.
Develop and apply multimodal ML methods to integrate clinical, breath metabolomics, biomarker, lung function, and environmental exposure data.
Model lung function trajectories from infancy to adolescence, with a focus on moderate-to-late preterm children.
Perform external validation with different cohorts and assess generalisability.
Publish in ML and clinical/respiratory venues; present at international conferences.
Work closely with clinicians, epidemiologists, and exposure scientists; contribute to reproducible, well-documented code.

MSc in Computer Science, Data Science, Statistics, Biomedical Engineering, or a related field.
Solid programming skills in Python; fluency with ML frameworks (PyTorch, scikit-learn) and statistical modelling.
You are curious about how early life shapes lifelong health, and motivated to build ML that clinicians will actually use.
Experience with tabular or longitudinal data, missing data, and model validation. Experience with small-sample or clinical/epidemiological data is a strong plus.
Interest in interpretable ML, clustering/phenotyping, or time-series/trajectory modelling.
Interest in clinical research and respiratory or pediatric health; no medical background required.
Rigour, independence, and the ability to communicate with non-technical collaborators.
Fluent in English (spoken and written). German is an advantage but not required.

A PhD at the interface of machine learning, clinical medicine, and environmental health, with direct translational impact.
Access to a unique longitudinal birth cohort spanning infancy to adolescence, plus international validation cohorts.
Close supervision and collaboration with clinical and technical experts.
Access to state-of-the-art HPC infrastructure.
Enrolment in the Graduate School Medical and Health Sciences (GMHS) , with training and conference opportunities.
Supportive team culture and employment conditions in accordance with the University of Basel.

ap:254672.body:
About us
The University of Luxembourg is an international research university with a distinctly multilingual and interdisciplinary character.
The Faculty of Humanities, Education and Social Sciences (FHSE) at the University of Luxembourg brings together expertise from the humanities, linguistics, cognitive sciences, social and educational sciences.
People from across 20 disciplines are working within the Faculty . Along with the disciplinary approach a very ambitious interdisciplinary research culture has been developed. The faculty's research and teaching focuses on social, economic, political and educational issues with the common goal of contributing to an inclusive, open and resourceful society.
The position is hosted within the Professorship of Health and Social Intervention at the University of Luxembourg. The PhD candidate will develop a research project in the field of sexuality and gender.
Your role
Develop and conduct an independent PhD research project
Collaborate with the research team and wider networks
Contribute to a limited amount of teaching and student supervision
Support the organisation of academic activities
Participate in doctoral training and skills development

Possible topics include:
Queer Disability Studies and intersections of embodiment, disability, and sexuality
Queer Sexualities, deviance, and processes of social normativity
History of sexualities in the tension between regulation and emancipation, e.g. Satanic Panic
History of psychiatry with a focus on sexuality, normativity, and pathologisation

The position is also open to related topics that explore intersections of race, gender, and/or medical history. The chair's research focuses on the analysis and critical evaluation of interventions and discourses that shape bodies, sexualities, and social norms.

For further information about this role, please contact Professor Christiane CARRI ()
Your profile
Master's degree (or equivalent) in sociology, gender studies, history, social work/social policy, anthropology, psychology or a closely related discipline
Strong academic record and demonstrated interest in sexuality, gender and/or queer studies
Familiarity with at least one of the advertised thematic fields
Proven ability to engage with critical and theoretical literature, e.g. queer theory, disability studies, feminist theory, history of sexuality, critical race studies
Operational Language Requirements: Excellent command of English is required. Good working knowledge of French and German would be considered an asset

Academic Eligibility (Thesis) :
Applicants must demonstrate at least B2-level proficiency in the language of their thesis. For details and accepted certificates, please visit the Application for admission - Doctoral Candidates .
We offer
A modern, dynamic university with a personal and inclusive atmosphere. Multilingual and international character. Staff coming from more than 90 countries. Member of The Guild of European Research Intensive Universities
An exceptional research environment, supported by skilled staff and high-quality equipment. Strong links to professional sectors and the Luxembourg labour market. A unique urban campus with excellent infrastructure
A partner for society and industry. Cooperation with European institutions, innovative companies, the Financial Centre and a wide range of non-academic partners including ministries, local governments, associations, and NGOs

How to apply
Applications should include:
Curriculum Vitae
Cover letter presenting your motivation for this doctoral thesis topic, and explaining how your qualifications and aspirations align with its academic focus
Transcript of all modules and results from university-level courses taken
Names, contact information and current position of 3 referees who can, upon request, provide an assessment of the application. Please indicate their relationship to you

Early application is highly encouraged, as the applications will be processed upon reception. Please apply ONLINE formally through the HR system. Applications by Email will not be considered.
All qualified individuals are encouraged to apply. In line with our values, the University of Luxembourg promotes an inclusive culture. We encourage applications from individuals of all backgrounds and are dedicated to upholding equality and respect for our employees and students.
General information:
Contract Type: Fixed Term Contract 36 Month
Work Hours: Full Time 40.0 Hours per Week
Location: Belval Campus
Internal Title: Doctoral Researcher
Job Reference: UOL08567

The yearly gross salary for every Doctoral researcher at the UL is EUR 44531 (full time).

Application deadline: 04/01/2027 12:00 PM
Start date: 01/10/2027
Job description
The Department of Molecular Biology (DBM) at the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) is inviting applications for a full-time academic position within its multidisciplinary research and teaching department.
Area of Research
The successful candidate will investigate the molecular and cellular mechanisms governing microorganism biology and/or immune system function, using cutting-edge experimental or interdisciplinary approaches.
We particularly encourage curiosity-driven basic research projects aimed at deepening our understanding of biological processes, regardless of their immediate clinical or translational applications.
Research areas of interest include, but are not limited to:
Fundamental Microbiology
Microbial physiology and metabolism
Microbial genetics, regulation of gene expression, and genome evolution
Molecular mechanisms underlying microbial adaptation and stress responses

Fundamental Immunology
Regulation, differentiation, and ontogeny of immune cells
Transcriptional, epigenetic, and metabolic control of immune responses
Fundamental mechanisms of inflammation, tolerance, and immunopathology

At the Interface of Microbiology and Immunology
Molecular mechanisms underlying host-microorganism interactions
Reciprocal adaptation of hosts and microorganisms in physiological and pathological contexts
Organization and dynamics of host-microorganism ecosystems

Applications from scientists working with diverse experimental models and employing innovative approaches in molecular and cellular biology, genetics, functional genomics, biochemistry, computational biology, systems biology, or multi-omics technologies are strongly encouraged.
The successful candidate will join the Department of Molecular Biology at the Brussels South Charleroi Biopark, a highly dynamic life sciences environment:  https://biopark.be/en . The BioPark is home to three academic research institutes and provides state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, as well as a thriving network of more than 100 companies in the life sciences sector. This environment offers opportunities for interdisciplinary collaboration with experts in nucleic acid biology, microbiology, immunology, virology, parasitology, and cell and developmental biology.
The successful candidate will benefit from a particularly stimulating scientific environment for developing research at the interface of immunology and microbiology. The department hosts complementary research groups specializing in immunology, microbiology, virology, parasitology, genetics, and nucleic acid biology. Research projects fostering synergies across these disciplines will be particularly encouraged.
Educational and scientific goals :
The successful candidate will demonstrate strong motivation and proven skills in teaching and mentoring. They will contribute to teaching activities across a broad range of contemporary topics in biochemistry and molecular and cellular biology at both Bachelor’s and Master’s levels, delivering both fundamental and specialized courses. They will also be expected to supervise undergraduate and graduate students, as well as postdoctoral researchers.
For candidates who are not proficient in French, a temporary period of French-language training, during which teaching may be conducted in English, may be granted for a maximum of three years. By the end of this period, the candidate must be able to teach in French.
The successful candidate will lead an independent and competitive research programme as a principal investigator (PI) and secure external funding to support it, including European and regional grants and funding schemes such as the ERC, Wel-RI, and FNRS.
Courses covered at the time of recruitment :
BIOL-Y-331  Host-Pathogen Interactions
5 ECTS (Lectures: 14 hours; Tutorials: 24 hours; Practical laboratory sessions: 24 hours; Independent study: 30 hours)
Teaching load: Lectures: 14 hours; Tutorials: 24 hours; Independent study: 30 hours.
BIOL-F-104 / BIOL-F-105 / CHIM-F-208  Molecular Basis of Life
10 ECTS (Lectures: 64 hours; Tutorials: 20 hours; Practical laboratory sessions: 12 hours)
Teaching load: Lectures: 14 hours (shared across the Biology, Bioengineering, and Chemistry programmes).
BIOL-F-303 Molecular Biology Laboratory
5 ECTS (Practical laboratory sessions: 48 hours)
Teaching load: Practical laboratory sessions: 48 hours.

Qualifications required :
PhD Degree (with doctoral thesis) in biological or biomedical sciences, medicine, pharmaceutical sciences, or a related discipline.
Skills required
Applicants should have at least 4 years of research experience at the time of their recruitment.
Post-doctoral experience and an excellent scientific record are a plus.
Demonstrated ability to conduct original, high-quality research commensurate with your career stage.
Exchange periods outside of the applicants’ home institution (during or after their PhD) will be taken into consideration when evaluating applications.
Applicants who do not speak French (level C1) may be granted a period of adaptation, but they must be able to teach in French at the end of the third year following their appointment.
Teaching experience will be taken into consideration and viewed favorably.

Interested ?
For more information, please contact Prof. Stanislas Goriely or Laurence Van Melderen  (E-mail:  [email protected] ,   [email protected] ).
Your application will consist of a Curriculum Vitae (if you wish, a standard CV can be downloaded from the website: https:  //www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/emplois-academiques-et-scientifiques-cv-type) and a document completed using the template available at this URL address
https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/1e-applic-form-acad-tps-plein-docx .
This template structures your application by including the following elements:
an application letter
a 7,000-character report (4 pages) presenting the applicant’s research activities and a research project, including how these will integrate into ULB’s research teams
a teaching dossier including a 7,000-character report (4 pages) on the applicant's previous teaching activities and a teaching project for the first five years in this position; these must be relevant to the faculty and to the teaching profiles for the programmes to which the applicant is to contribute
a note on the applicant's international achievements and projects (no more than 4 pages)
the names and e-mail addresses of five referees (respecting the gender balance) who may be contacted by those in charge of evaluating applications.  These referees should not have conflicts of interest because of family or emotional ties.

Incomplete applications or applications that do not use the template provided will not be examined by the selection committee.
The appointment to the academic staff of ULB is made at ”Chargé de Cours” level. As of their appointment, members of academic staff are authorised to use the honorary title of ”Professeur”.
Where to go to apply?
Click here:  https://jobs.ulb.be/job-invite/2091/?isInternalUser=true
For any connection problems or questions about our application, consult our FAQ :  e-recrut-mode-d-emploi-candidat-en-_1734942996246-pdf
N.B.: SAP complies with European and U.S. regulations and, as a result, does not allow access to its application from the following countries/regions: Crimea, Sevastopol, the Donetsk People’s Republic (DNR) / Luhansk People’s Republic (LNR), areas not controlled by the Ukrainian government in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia, and Belarus.
Therefore, candidates applying from these countries – and only from these countries – can submit their CV and application to this address:  [email protected]
Equal opportunities policy
ULB's personnel management policy is geared towards diversity and equal opportunities.
We recruit candidates on the basis of their skills, irrespective of age, gender, sexual orientation, origin, nationality, beliefs, disability, etc.
Would you like to be provided with reasonable accommodation in the selection procedure because of a disability, disorder, or illness?  Please contact Marie Botty, the person in charge of diversity aspects for the academic and scientific staff ( [email protected] ) . Be assured of the confidentiality of this information.
More details on the ULB gender and diversity policy are available at  Diversity at ULB - ULB .
You will find all the regulations relating to academic careers on our site at  http://www.ulb.ac.be/emploi/academique.html .

Référence : 2027/A020
Date limite du dépôt des candidatures :  04/01/2027 à midi
Date d’entrée en fonction prévue le : 01/10/2027
Descriptif du poste
Le Département de Biologie Moléculaire (DBM) de l’Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) ouvre un poste académique à temps plein au sein de son département de recherche et d’enseignement pluridisciplinaire.
Domaine de recherche
La ou le candidat·e recruté.e étudiera les mécanismes moléculaires et cellulaires qui régissent la biologie des microorganismes et/ou le fonctionnement du système immunitaire, en s'appuyant sur des approches expérimentales de pointe ou interdisciplinaires. Nous encourageons particulièrement les projets de recherche fondamentale, guidés par la curiosité scientifique, visant à approfondir notre compréhension des processus biologiques, indépendamment de leurs applications cliniques ou translationnelles immédiates.
Les domaines de recherche envisagés comprennent notamment, mais sans s'y limiter :
Microbiologie fondamentale
Physiologie et métabolisme des microorganismes
Génétique microbienne, régulation de l'expression génique et évolution des génomes
Mécanismes moléculaires de l'adaptation des microorganismes et des réponses aux stress

Immunologie fondamentale
Régulation, différenciation et ontogénie des cellules immunitaires
Contrôle transcriptionnel, épigénétique et métabolique des réponses immunitaires
Mécanismes fondamentaux de l'inflammation, de la tolérance et de l'immunopathologie

À l'interface de la microbiologie et de l'immunologie
Mécanismes moléculaires des interactions hôte-microorganismes
Adaptation réciproque de l'hôte et des microorganismes dans les contextes physiologiques et pathologiques
Organisation et dynamique des écosystèmes hôte-microorganismes

Les candidatures de scientifiques travaillant sur divers modèles expérimentaux et utilisant des approches innovantes en biologie moléculaire et cellulaire, génétique, génomique fonctionnelle, biochimie ou biologie computationnelle, biologie des systèmes et technologies multi-omiques sont vivement encouragées.
La ou le candidat·e rejoindra le Département de Biologie Moléculaire au sein du Brussels South Charleroi Biopark, un environnement très dynamique dédié aux sciences de la vie : https://biopark.be/en . Le BioPark abrite trois instituts de recherche académique et offre des infrastructures de laboratoire à la pointe de la technologie, ainsi qu’un réseau florissant de plus de 100 entreprises du secteur des sciences de la vie. Dans ce cadre, le candidat pourra collaborer de manière interdisciplinaire, en travaillant avec des experts en biologie des acides nucléiques, microbiologie, immunologie, virologie, parasitologie, ainsi qu’en biologie cellulaire et du développement.
La ou le candidat·e bénéficiera d'un environnement scientifique particulièrement propice au développement de recherches à l'interface entre immunologie et microbiologie, grâce à la présence au sein du département de groupes de recherche complémentaires couvrant l'immunologie, la microbiologie, la virologie, la parasitologie, la génétique et la biologie des acides nucléiques. Les projets favorisant les synergies entre ces disciplines seront particulièrement encouragés.
Objectifs pédagogiques et scientifiques
La ou le candidat·e devra faire preuve d’une forte motivation et de solides compétences en matière d’enseignement et d’encadrement. Il contribuera aux activités pédagogiques dans un large éventail de domaines modernes de la biochimie, de la biologie moléculaire et cellulaire, dans les programmes de Bachelier et de Master, en assurant à la fois des cours fondamentaux et des cours spécialisés. L’encadrement d’étudiants de premier et deuxième cycles ainsi que de chercheurs postdoctoraux est également attendu. Pour les candidats ne maîtrisant pas le français, une période temporaire d’apprentissage du français et d’enseignement en anglais pourra être accordée pour une durée maximale de trois ans, après quoi le candidat devra être en mesure d’enseigner en français.
Le candidat devra diriger un programme de recherche indépendant (principal investigator) et compétitif et assurer son financement par des subventions externes (fonds européens et régionaux, par exemple ERC, Wel-RI, FNRS, etc.).
Cours repris dans la charge au moment du recrutement :
BIOL-Y-331 Interactions hôte-pathogènes
5 ECTS (Cours magistral : 14h, Exercices dirigés : 24h, Travaux pratiques : 24h, Travaux personnels : 30h)
Charge : Cours magistral : 14h, Exercices dirigés : 24h, Travaux personnels : 30h.
BIOL-F-104/BIOL-F-105/CHIM-F-208 Bases Moléculaires du vivant
10 ECTS (Cours magistral : 64h,  Exercices dirigés : 20h, Travaux pratiques : 12 h)
Charge : Cours magistral : 14h (partagé par les sections Biologie/Bioingénieur/Chimie)
BIOL-F-303 Laboratoires de biologie moléculaire
5 ECTS (Travaux pratiques : 48h)
Charge : Travaux pratiques : 48h

Titre requis
Docteur à thèse en sciences biologiques ou biomédicales, médecine ou sciences pharmaceutiques, ou disciplines apparentées.
Compétences requises
Vous avez une ancienneté scientifique de 4 années minimum au moment de l’engagement.
Vous pouvez faire état d’une expérience post-doctorale et d’un excellent dossier scientifique.
Vous avez démontré votre capacité à mener des recherches originales de grande qualité, en adéquation avec votre niveau de carrière.
Si vous avez effectué une mobilité en dehors de l’institution où a été réalisé votre doctorat (durant la période doctorale ou après), ce sera pris en compte lors de l’évaluation de votre dossier.
Si vous ne parlez pas couramment la langue française (niveau C1), une période d’adaptation peut vous être accordée, mais vous devrez être capable d’enseigner en français à la fin de la troisième année suivant votre nomination.
L’expérience d’enseignement sera prise en compte et valorisée.

Intéressé·e ?
Des renseignements complémentaires peuvent être obtenus auprès des Prof. Stanislas Goriely et Laurence Van Melderen (courriel :  [email protected] , [email protected] ).
Votre dossier de candidature sera composé d’un Curriculum vitae ( si vous le souhaitez un CV type peut être téléchargé via le site internet :  https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/emplois-academiques-et-scientifiques-cv-type   ) et d’un document complété à l’aide du template disponible à cette adresse URL  https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/1f-dossier-de-candidature-acad-tps-plein-docx ).
Ce canevas structure votre dossier de candidature en reprenant les éléments suivants :
une lettre de motivation
un rapport de 7000 signes (ou 4 pages) environ sur les activités de recherche et un projet de recherche, en ce compris l’insertion envisagée au sein des équipes de recherche de l’ULB
un dossier d’enseignement comprenant un rapport de 7000 signes (ou 4 pages) environ sur les activités d’enseignement antérieures et un projet d’enseignement pour les 5 premières années du mandat, qui s’intègre de manière cohérente dans la vision de l’entité de rattachement et dans les profils d’enseignements des filières de formation auxquelles le candidat devra contribuer
une note sur les réalisations et projets internationaux (4 pages maximum)
les noms et adresses mail de contact de cinq personnes de référence susceptibles d’être contactées par les organes chargés d’évaluer les dossiers, en veillant à l’équilibre des genres.  Ces personnes ne peuvent être en conflit d’intérêt en raison de liens familiaux ou affectifs.

Les dossiers incomplets ou les dossiers n'utilisant pas le canevas mis à votre disposition ne seront pas examinés par la commission de sélection.
La nomination, dans le cadre académique de I’ULB, se fait au rang de chargé de cours.  Dès leur nomination, les membres du corps académique sont autorisé·e·s à porter, à titre honorifique, le qualificatif de professeur·e.
Où se rendre pour postuler ?
Cliquez ici : https://jobs.ulb.be/job-invite/2091/?isInternalUser=true
Pour tout problème de connexion ou question à propos de notre application, consultez notre FAQ : e-recrut-mode-d-emploi-candidat-fr-_1734942952302-pdf
N.B. : SAP respecte des directives européennes et états-uniennes, et en conséquence, n’autorise pas les accès à son application à partir des pays/ régions suivants : La Crimée, Sébastopol, République populaire de Donetsk (DNR) / République populaire de Louhansk (LNR), Les zones non contrôlées par le gouvernement ukrainien dans les oblasts de Kherson et Zaporijia, Cuba, l’Iran, La Corée du Nord, la Syrie, la Russie et la Biélorussie.
Dès lors, les candidats qui postulent au départ de ces pays – et uniquement au départ de ces pays – peuvent envoyer leur curriculum vitae et leur dossier de candidature à cette adresse :  [email protected]
Politique d’égalité des chances
La politique de gestion du personnel de l’ULB est axée sur la diversité et l’égalité des chances.
Nous recrutons les candidat·es en fonction de leurs compétences, indépendamment de leur âge, leur genre, leur orientation sexuelle, leur origine, leur nationalité, leurs convictions, leur handicap, etc.
Vous souhaitez bénéficier d’aménagements raisonnables dans le cadre de la procédure de sélection en raison d’un handicap, d’un trouble ou d’une maladie ? N’hésitez pas à prendre contact avec Marie Botty ( [email protected] ) notre personne de contact en charge des aspects de diversité pour le personnel enseignant et scientifique. Soyez assuré·e de la confidentialité de cette information.
Plus de détails sur les politiques de genre et de diversité sont disponibles sur  https://www.ulb.be/fr/l-ulb-s-engage/diversites .
Vous trouverez l’ensemble des dispositions relatives aux carrières du corps académique sur notre site à l’adresse  http://www.ulb.ac.be/emploi/academique.html .

Job description
The Department of Molecular Biology (DBM) of the Faculty of Sciences at the Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) is seeking to recruit a full-time academic staff member to join a multidisciplinary research and teaching environment.
Research area
Candidates with an internationally recognized scientific track record and an innovative research program in animal developmental biology are encouraged to apply. Priority will be given to candidates whose research activities align with the department's research interests and have the potential to strengthen its existing areas of expertise, particularly in the developmental biology of the nervous or cardiovascular systems.
The successful candidate will join the Department of Molecular Biology at the Brussels South Charleroi Biopark, a highly dynamic environment dedicated to life sciences:  https://biopark.be/en . The Biopark hosts three academic research institutes and offers state-of-the-art laboratory facilities, together with a thriving network of more than 100 companies in the life sciences sector. Within this environment, the successful candidate will have opportunities to develop interdisciplinary collaborations with experts in cell and developmental biology, nucleic acid biology, microbiology, immunology, virology, and parasitology.
Teaching and research responsibilities
The successful candidate is expected to demonstrate strong motivation and solid skills in teaching and supervision. They will contribute to teaching activities primarily focused on developmental biology at both Bachelor's and Master's levels, delivering both fundamental and specialized courses. Supervision of undergraduate and Master's students, as well as postdoctoral researchers, is also expected.
For candidates who are not proficient in French, a transitional period of up to three years may be granted to learn French and teach in English. By the end of this period, the successful candidate must be able to teach in French.
The successful candidate will be expected to lead a competitive research program and secure external funding through European and regional funding schemes (e.g., ERC, Wel-RI, FNRS, etc.).

Additional elective teaching:
BMOL-F-4008 – Practical Classes in Molecular Biology : 5 ECTS, Master's Year 1, 48 hours of practical classes, elective course.

Qualifications required :
PhD in Biological or Biomedical Sciences, Medicine, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related discipline.
Skills required
You must have at least four years of postdoctoral research experience at the time of appointment.
You must demonstrate postdoctoral research experience and an excellent scientific track record.
You must have demonstrated the ability to conduct original, high-quality research appropriate to your career stage.
Research mobility outside the institution where you obtained your PhD, either during or after your doctoral studies, will be taken into account when evaluating your application.
If you are not fluent in French (C1 level), an adaptation period may be granted. However, you must be able to teach in French by the end of the third year following your appointment.
Previous teaching experience will be considered an asset.

Descriptif du poste
Le Département de Biologie Moléculaire (DBM) de la Faculté des Science de l’Université libre de Bruxelles (ULB) recrute un académique à temps plein pour rejoindre un environnement de recherche et d’enseignement pluridisciplinaire.
Domaine de recherche :
Les candidats possédant un parcours scientifique internationalement reconnu et un programme de recherche innovant en biologie développementale animale sont invités à postuler. La priorité sera donnée aux candidats dont les activités de recherche s’intègrent dans les thématiques du département et sont susceptibles d’en renforcer les axes existants, en particulier dans les domaines de la biologie du développement du système nerveux ou cardiovasculaire.
Le candidat rejoindra le Département de Biologie Moléculaire au sein du Brussels South Charleroi Biopark, un environnement très dynamique dédié aux sciences de la vie : https://biopark.be/en . Le BioPark abrite trois instituts de recherche académique et offre des infrastructures de laboratoire à la pointe de la technologie, ainsi qu’un réseau florissant de plus de 100 entreprises du secteur des sciences de la vie. Dans ce cadre, le candidat aura l’opportunité de développer des collaborations interdisciplinaires avec des experts en biologie cellulaire et du développement, biologie des acides nucléiques, microbiologie, immunologie, virologie et parasitologie.
Objectifs pédagogiques et scientifiques :
Le candidat devra faire preuve d’une forte motivation et de solides compétences en matière d’enseignement et d’encadrement. Il contribuera aux activités pédagogiques principalement centrées sur la biologie du développement, dans les programmes de Bachelier et de Master, en assurant à la fois des cours fondamentaux et des cours spécialisés. L’encadrement d’étudiants de premier et deuxième cycles ainsi que de chercheurs postdoctoraux est également attendu. Pour les candidats ne maîtrisant pas le français, une période temporaire d’apprentissage du français et d’enseignement en anglais pourra être accordée pour une durée maximale de trois ans, après quoi le candidat devra être en mesure d’enseigner en français.
Le candidat devra diriger un programme de recherche compétitif et assurer son financement par des subventions externes (fonds européens et régionaux, par exemple ERC, Wel-RI, FNRS, etc.).
Cours repris dans la charge au moment du recrutement :
BIOL-F-318 – Histophysiologie et développement animal : 5 ECTS (partim), BA3, 18 h de cours théorique, co-titulaire.
BIOL-F-320 – Travaux pratiques d’histopathologie et développement animal : 5 ECTS (partim), BA3, 24 h de travaux pratiques, cours à option, coordinateur.
S-BIOG-935 – Biologie du développement ( correspond aux deux intitulés précédents dupliqués sur le site de Charleroi ): 5 ECTS, BA3, cours et travaux pratiques, coordinateur.
S-BIOG-914 – Embryologie humaine : 5 ECTS (partim), BA1–BA2, 12 h de cours et 8 h de travaux pratiques, partim, coordinateur.
BMOL-F-419 – Neurosciences et biologie cardiovasculaire : 5 ECTS (partim), Master 1, 12 h de cours et séminaires, cours à option, co-titulaire.

Enseignement optionnel :
BMOL-F-4008 – Travaux pratiques de biologie moléculaire : 5 ECTS, Master 1, 48 h de travaux pratiques, TP à option.

Titre requis
Docteur à thèse en sciences biologiques ou biomédicales, médecine ou sciences pharmaceutiques, ou disciplines apparentées.
Compétences requises
Vous avez une ancienneté scientifique de 4 années minimum (postdoctoral) au moment de l’engagement.
Vous pouvez faire état d’une expérience post-doctorale et d’un excellent dossier scientifique.
Vous avez démontré votre capacité à mener des recherches originales de grande qualité, en adéquation avec votre niveau de carrière.
Si vous avez effectué une mobilité en dehors de l’institution où a été réalisé votre doctorat (durant la période doctorale ou après), cela sera pris en compte lors de l’évaluation de votre dossier.
Si vous ne parlez pas couramment la langue française (niveau C1), une période d’adaptation peut vous être accordée, mais vous devrez être capable d’enseigner en français à la fin de la troisième année suivant votre nomination.
L’expérience d’enseignement sera prise en compte et valorisée.

Intéressé·e ?
Des renseignements complémentaires peuvent être obtenus auprès du Prof. Maud Martin (courriel :  [email protected] ).
Votre dossier de candidature sera composé d’un Curriculum vitae ( si vous le souhaitez un CV type peut être téléchargé via le site internet :  https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/emplois-academiques-et-scientifiques-cv-type   ) et d’un document complété à l’aide du template disponible à cette adresse URL  https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/1f-dossier-de-candidature-acad-tps-plein-docx ).
Ce canevas structure votre dossier de candidature en reprenant les éléments suivants :
une lettre de motivation
un rapport de 7000 signes (ou 4 pages) environ sur les activités de recherche et un projet de recherche, en ce compris l’insertion envisagée au sein des équipes de recherche de l’ULB
un dossier d’enseignement comprenant un rapport de 7000 signes (ou 4 pages) environ sur les activités d’enseignement antérieures et un projet d’enseignement pour les 5 premières années du mandat, qui s’intègre de manière cohérente dans la vision de l’entité de rattachement et dans les profils d’enseignements des filières de formation auxquelles le candidat devra contribuer
une note sur les réalisations et projets internationaux (4 pages maximum)
les noms et adresses mail de contact de cinq personnes de référence susceptibles d’être contactées par les organes chargés d’évaluer les dossiers, en veillant à l’équilibre des genres.  Ces personnes ne peuvent être en conflit d’intérêt en raison de liens familiaux ou affectifs.

Les dossiers incomplets ou les dossiers n'utilisant pas le canevas mis à votre disposition ne seront pas examinés par la commission de sélection.
La nomination, dans le cadre académique de I’ULB, se fait au rang de chargé de cours.  Dès leur nomination, les membres du corps académique sont autorisé·e·s à porter, à titre honorifique, le qualificatif de professeur·e.
Où se rendre pour postuler ?

N.B. : SAP respecte des directives européennes et états-uniennes, et en conséquence, n’autorise pas les accès à son application à partir des pays/ régions suivants : La Crimée, Sébastopol, République populaire de Donetsk (DNR) / République populaire de Louhansk (LNR), Les zones non contrôlées par le gouvernement ukrainien dans les oblasts de Kherson et Zaporijia, Cuba, l’Iran, La Corée du Nord, la Syrie, la Russie et la Biélorussie.
Dès lors, les candidats qui postulent au départ de ces pays – et uniquement au départ de ces pays – peuvent envoyer leur curriculum vitae et leur dossier de candidature à cette adresse :  [email protected]

La politique de gestion du personnel de l’ULB est axée sur la diversité et l’égalité des chances.

Soyez assuré·e de la confidentialité de cette information.
Plus de détails sur les politiques de genre et de diversité sont disponibles sur  https://www.ulb.be/fr/l-ulb-s-engage/diversites .

Job description
Context of the vacant position
This position is integrated within the Department of Organismal Biology (DBO), which is responsible for the Bachelor's programme in Biological Sciences and the Master's programme in Organismal Biology and Ecology. In terms of research, the DBO includes eight research units located across three campuses (Solbosch, Plaine and Gosselies):
• Evolutionary Biology and Ecology (EBE), Solbosch Campus, 8 professors
• Marine Biology (BIOMAR), Solbosch Campus, 1 professor
• Molecular Biology and Evolution (MBE), Solbosch Campus, 1 professor
• Plant Biotechnology (LBV), Gosselies Campus, 1 professor
• Plant Ecology and Biogeochemistry (EVB), Plaine Campus, 3 professors
• Social Ecology (USE), Plaine Campus, 2 professors
• Systems Ecology and Resource Management (SERM), Plaine Campus, 2 professors
• ULB Herbarium (BRLU), jointly managed by staff from EVB, EBE and SERM, Plaine Campus
The Department also includes approximately fifty researchers and nine laboratory technicians.
Animal behaviour research has been a historic strength of the DBO for more than 50 years.
Area of Research
Behavioural Ecology
In particular (non-exhaustive list):
Chemical and sensory ecology (perception, communication, signalling)
Behavioural evolution
Sexual selection and reproductive strategies
Social behaviour and cooperation
Conflict, dominance and social hierarchies
Behavioural genetics
Interspecific interactions
Behavioural plasticity and adaptive strategies
Responses to stress and environmental change
Conservation behavioural ecology
Behavioural modelling and theoretical approaches

An interdisciplinary dimension will be considered an asset.
Duties
Research
Develop an original and competitive research programme in behavioural ecology.
Publish regularly in international peer-reviewed scientific journals.
Obtain national and international research funding.
Supervise PhD students and postdoctoral researchers.
Participate in interdisciplinary collaborations both within and outside the university.

Teaching
Contribute to teaching within the Organismal Biology and Ecology curriculum, including in courses devoted to animal behaviour.
Contribute to teaching at both undergraduate (bachelor's) and graduate (master's) levels.
Supervise master's theses.
Contribute to educational innovation and to the supervision of practical and field-based courses.

Service to the Community
Participate in the administrative and collective activities of the Department and Faculty.
Contribute to the university's scientific outreach and visibility (seminars, conferences, science communication).

Long-term planning of these activities (over at least 10 years) is expected.
Courses Included in the Teaching Load at the Time of Recruitment
Bachelor Level
• BIOL-F-103: BIOL-F103: Bases de la biologie des organismes (10 ECTS; contribution to lectures: 15h).
Timeline: from academic year 2027-2028.
• BIOL-F-304: Evolution et diversité des arthropodes et des vertébrés (5 ECTS; contribution to lectures: 24h).
Timeline: from academic year 2028-2029.
Master Level
• BIOL-F-446: Animal Behaviour (15 ECTS; contribution to lectures: 30h).
Timeline: gradually during the first three years.
• BIOL-F-449: Biodiversity and Conservation - Terrestrial and Aquatic Ecosystems (15 ECTS; contribution to field excursions: 40h).
Timeline: gradually during the first three years.
• New master's course in the candidate's area of expertise.
Timeline: from academic year 2029-2030.
This teaching load may evolve with the needs of the Department.
Qualifications required
PhD in Biological Sciences in the broadest sense (including biology, bioengineering, biosciences, agronomy, life sciences and earth sciences).
Skills required
A minimum of four years of scientific seniority at the time of appointment.
Postdoctoral experience, mobility outside the institution where the PhD was obtained, and an excellent scientific record will be essential selection criteria.
International research experience will be considered an asset.
Ability to teach in French.
Strong organisational and leadership skills, adaptability and flexibility, ease of interaction in a multicultural environment, autonomy, ability to work collaboratively, and initiative.

Interested?
Further information may be obtained from:
Prof. Jean-Christophe de Biseau
E-mail: [email protected]
or
Ms Catherine Buess
E-mail: [email protected]
Your application will consist of a Curriculum Vitae (if you wish, a standard CV can be downloaded from the website: https:  //www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/emplois-academiques-et-scientifiques-cv-type) and a document completed using the template available at this URL address
https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/1e-applic-form-acad-tps-plein-docx .
This template structures the application around the following components:
An application letter.
A research document of approximately 7,000 characters (or 4 pages), including a report of previous research activities and a research project, and including the proposed integration within ULB research teams.
A teaching document of approximately 7,000 characters (or 4 pages), including a report of previous teaching activities and a teaching project for the first five years of the mandate, coherently integrated into the vision of the host entity and the educational profiles of the programmes to which the candidate will contribute.
A statement on international achievements and projects (maximum 4 pages).
Names and e-mail addresses of five referees who may be contacted by the committees responsible for evaluating applications, with attention paid to gender balance. These referees must not be in a conflict of interest due to family or personal relationships.

Incomplete applications, or applications not using the provided template, will not be considered by the selection committee.
The appointment to the academic staff of ULB is made at ”Chargé de Cours” level. As of their appointment, members of academic staff are authorised to use the honorary title of ”Professeur”.
Where to go to apply?

Therefore, candidates applying from these countries – and only from these countries – can submit their CV and application to this address:  [email protected]
Equal opportunities policy
ULB's personnel management policy is geared towards diversity and equal opportunities.

Job description
The Tourism unit within the Department of Geosciences, Environment and Society of the Faculty of Sciences (Université libre de Bruxelles) is opening a full-time academic position (100% Professorship) in the form of a Chair entitled ‘ Régulations, tourisme et société’ [i.e., Regulation within Tourism Systems & Society]. The starting contract is 3 years. After the first 3-year period, an evaluation of the scientific and teaching activities will be carried out. Following a positive evaluation, the position will become tenured.
The Chair in ‘Régulations, tourisme et société’ is part of the research activities of the Brussels Centre for Tourism Studies (BCTS). The BCTS is specialised in the study of issues relating to tourism as a social phenomenon as well as a set of economic activities . It brings together a number of researchers and scholars who study tourism from various perspectives, including mono-, multi- and interdisciplinary approaches. They carry out both fundamental and applied research on a wide range of tourism practices, stakeholders and destinations. Institutionally the BTCS is part of the ‘Institut de Gestion de l’Environnement et d’Aménagement du Territoire’ (IGEAT), and has recently joined the USET research hub together with four other research units. Within this hub the BTCS fosters research synergies on issues relating to socio-environmental transformations in urban spaces.
In response to the pressing social and ecological challenges facing contemporary societies, both the educational programme and research at the BCTS have taken over the past five years a more pronounced focus on the dynamics of transformation and adaptation within tourism systems. To find out more about the BTCS, please visit the website  https://bcts.sciences.ulb.be/fr-1
It is within this framework that the chairholder will develop their research and teaching, focusing on regulation in tourism systems. This area of research has not yet been investigated by the BCTS.
Description of the Chair in  ‘Régulations, tourisme et Société’
Area of Research  :
The selected candidate will be expected to carry out empirical research that examines in depth modes/forms of regulation within tourism systems, the processes and dynamics underpinning them, as well as their recent and future development. The notion of ‘regulation’ is understood in a broad sense here. It refers to the adjustment of a variety of movements or actions based on previously defined rules or standards, and their effects or outcomes within tourism systems. This encompasses the different models of governance (i.e., as decision-making systems of processes, functions, structures, rules, norms…), as well as all mechanisms designed to influence tourism systems.
With this scope the selected candidate will explore how tourism stakeholders take into account and attempt to influence current and future sociotechnical trajectories. Examples of these trajectories include—though this list is by no means exhaustive—the financialisation of tourism, digitalisation and AI-isation, de- and re-intermediation, individualisation, and the strong growth in tourism mobilities. Particular attention will be attributed to the relationships between the modes and forms of regulation and the social and/or ecological challenges affecting contemporary societies.
The candidate will also need to demonstrate strong skills in research methodologies.
Educational and scientific goals:
The selected candidate will be expected to design, lead and/or contribute to research projects within the Chair’s field (see above). As part of this, he or she will, amongst other things, work to forge research synergies at departmental level, within USET, at ULB and internationally. The selected candidate will be expected to disseminate their research, combining scientific communication with public outreach. He or she will also be involved in supervising, supporting and/or assessing doctoral theses.
The selected candidate will make an active and creative contribution to the Master’s programme in ‘sciences et gestion du tourisme’ (i.e., tourism analyse and management; 120 ECTS) as well as to the related supplementary course programme. Active learning methods are promoted on the Master’s programme. Expectations will be commensurate with the candidate’s career stage, and will reach a teaching load of at least 120 hours (see below for an overview of the teaching load at the time of recruitment). Additionally, the selected candidate will supervise Master’s theses in tourism studies and management, and will be part of the evaluation panel of other theses. He or she will also be expected to play a full part in other initiatives relating to the Master’s, including the enhancement of the curriculum and of the teaching approaches, as well as the development of partner networks.
In the near future, the selected candidate will be expected to take on one or more roles within the wider scientific community and at the ULB. These roles include, amongst others:
-  reviewing papers submitted for publication in various scientific journals;
- (co-)organising scientific conferences;
- coordinating the teaching quality committee for the Master’s;
- heading the BCTS or the teaching unit;
- playing an active part in the DGES council, for example as secretary (drafting meeting minutes).
In the more distant future, these roles may be expanded to include the vice-chair and chair of the DGES council, participation in working groups or faculty or university committees, etc.
Courses covered at the time of recruitment :
TOUR-F-433 Tourisme et régulations (Cours magistral : 24h, Travaux pratiques : 6h, Séminaires : 12h)
TOUR-F-434 Data Analysis Applied to Research and Management (en cotitularisation; Cours magistral: 24h, Travaux pratiques : 12h, Projet: 12h)
TOUR-F-436 Gouvernance et dynamiques collectives dans un monde en mutations (en cotitularisation ; Cours magistral : 18h ; Travaux pratiques : 18h).
TOUR-F_431 Principes et pratiques de l’analyse critique (en cotitularisation ; Cours magistral : 6h ; Travaux pratiques : 12h ; Séminaire : 6h).
Other courses, including one on social-cultural dynamics in tourism, will be added later to reach a teaching load of at least 120 hours.

The language of instruction – French and/or English – is a matter for discussion. Proficiency in French is, however, essential to ensure high-quality academic support for students.
Qualifications required :
PhD Degree (with doctoral thesis) in:
Tourism studies or Tourism/hospitality Managament
Sociology
Anthropology
Political Sciences
Geography
Business engineering or Management

Skills required
In addition to holding a PhD in one of the above-mentioned fields, applicants should have sound and in-depth knowledge of, and research experience in, issues relating to regulation modes within tourism systems.
The applicant should have sound knowledge of, and possibly research experience in, the social phenomena and/or issues associated with tourism.
Experience in applying a systems approach to research topics is a must.
Sound knowledge of, and experience in applying or teaching, quantitative and qualitative research methods in the social sciences.
Applicants should have at least 4 years of research experience (PhD included) at the time of their recruitment.
Post-doctoral experience (i.e., research experience after completing one’s PhD) and a robust scientific record are a plus.
You must be able to teach and take part in meetings in French.
Moreover,
Exchange periods outside of the applicants’ home institution (during or after their PhD) will be taken into consideration when evaluating applications.
A genuine interest in urban issues will be highly valued (e.g., previous studies, research experience, publications, etc.).

Interested ?
For more information, please contact Ms Isabelle Cloquet (email :  [email protected] ).
Your application will consist of a Curriculum Vitae (if you wish, a standard CV can be downloaded from the website: https:  //www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/emplois-academiques-et-scientifiques-cv-type) and a document completed using the template available at this URL address
https://www.ulb.be/fr/documents-officiels/1e-applic-form-acad-tps-plein-docx .
This template structures your application by including the following elements:
an application letter
a 7,000-character report (4 pages) presenting the applicant’s research activities and a research project, including how these will integrate into ULB’s research teams
a teaching dossier including a 7,000-character report (4 pages) on the applicant's previous teaching activities and a teaching project for the first five years in this position; these must be relevant to the faculty and to the teaching profiles for the programmes to which the applicant is to contribute
a note on the applicant's international achievements and projects (no more than 4 pages)
the names and e-mail addresses of five referees (respecting the gender balance) who may be contacted by those in charge of evaluating applications.  These referees should not have conflicts of interest because of family or emotional ties.

Incomplete applications or applications that do not use the template provided will not be examined by the selection committee.
The appointment to the academic staff of ULB is made at ”Chargé de Cours” level. As of their appointment, members of academic staff are authorised to use the honorary title of ”Professeur”.
Where to go to apply?
Click here:  https://jobs.ulb.be/job-invite/2096/?isInternalUser=true
For any connection problems or questions about our application, consult our FAQ :  e-recrut-mode-d-emploi-candidat-en-_1734942996246-pdf
N.B.: SAP complies with European and U.S. regulations and, as a result, does not allow access to its application from the following countries/regions: Crimea, Sevastopol, the Donetsk People’s Republic (DNR) / Luhansk People’s Republic (LNR), areas not controlled by the Ukrainian government in the Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Syria, Russia, and Belarus.
Therefore, candidates applying from these countries – and only from these countries – can submit their CV and application to this address:  [email protected]
Equal opportunities policy
ULB's personnel management policy is geared towards diversity and equal opportunities.
We recruit candidates on the basis of their skills, irrespective of age, gender, sexual orientation, origin, nationality, beliefs, disability, etc.
Would you like to be provided with reasonable accommodation in the selection procedure because of a disability, disorder, or illness?  Please contact Marie Botty, the person in charge of diversity aspects for the academic and scientific staff ( [email protected] ) . Be assured of the confidentiality of this information.
More details on the ULB gender and diversity policy are available at  Diversity at ULB - ULB .
You will find all the regulations relating to academic careers on our site at  http://www.ulb.ac.be/emploi/academique.html .
