Oversee contractor-led tool installations for the Málaga cleanroom (Fab 5) project, with a focus on safety and conformity with imec’s standards and guidelines.
What you will do
For the Málaga Fab 5 project, tool installations will be performed by the contractor. imec’s role focuses on safety oversight and validating that the installations conform to imec’s required standards and guidelines. That’s where you come in. Onboarding and training will take place in Leuven, Belgium until mid-2028, after which the position location will transfer to Málaga, Spain.
As Project Lead, your role combines contractor oversight, safety follow-up and installation conformity validation on behalf of imec.
The contractor is responsible for installation execution and day-to-day coordination of the installation works. You will monitor progress, review safety and quality matters, and coordinate interfaces with imec stakeholders, keeping a clear distinction between contractor execution and imec oversight.
Your focus is to validate conformity with imec’s installation standards, guidelines and safety requirements. You will review contractor deliverables and installation evidence, follow up deviations and corrective actions, and support installation acceptance by imec rather than directly managing execution.
You will:
Oversee contractor-led installations and coordinate interfaces with imec
Review contractor schedules and monitor progress against agreed milestones
Flag scope deviations and their impact on timelines, budgets and priorities
Validate installation conformity with imec’s standards and guidelines through reviews, inspections and supporting records
Provide safety oversight and follow up contractor actions on safety and quality findings
Keep internal stakeholders and external partners informed
Escalate risks and non-conformities, track corrective actions and review evidence for installation acceptance

What we do for you
We offer you the opportunity to join one of the world’s premier research centers in nanotechnology at its headquarters in Leuven, Belgium. With your talent, passion and expertise, you’ll become part of a team that makes the impossible possible. Together, we shape the technology that will define the society of tomorrow.
We are committed to being an inclusive employer and proud of our open, multicultural, and informal working environment with ample possibilities to take initiative and show responsibility. We commit to supporting and guiding you in this process; not only with words but also with tangible actions. Through imec.academy, 'our corporate university', we actively invest in your development to further your technical and personal growth.
We are aware that your valuable contribution makes imec a top player in its field. Your energy and commitment are therefore appreciated by means of a market appropriate salary with many fringe benefits.
Who you are
You have a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering or Electromechanical Engineering.
You have at least 5 years of relevant technical experience.
You have experience overseeing contractor-led technical projects and reviewing installations against defined standards and guidelines.
You communicate openly and proactively with both internal customers and external partners about the status of ongoing work, and you escalate issues promptly when needed.
You adapt easily to changes and time pressure and combine a practical mindset with a strong focus on safety, quality and conformity.
You are fluent in English and Spanish.

L’Institut de Géographie de l’Université de Neuchâtel met au concours un poste d’
Assistant.e doctorant.e à 75%
Entrée en fonction : 1er février 2027
Cahier des charges
Participation au cours « Adaptations aux changements climatiques » (MA).
Participation aux « Travaux Pratiques d’Introduction à la Géographie humaine » (BA).
Participation au cours interdisciplinaire « Changements climatiques et société » (BA).
Participation au cours « Géographies publiques » (MA).
Tâches d’assistanat pour l’institut (suivi des échanges Erasmus, organisation des rencontres scientifiques).
Expertises d’examens.
Suivi de mémoires de MA.
Réalisation d’une thèse de doctorat, sous la direction du Prof. Chahan Kropf (en français ou en anglais), au sein du groupe  Climat, Sociétés et Écosystèmes . Le sujet de thèse sera développé en discussion avec le ou la candidat·e retenu·e, en fonction de ses intérêts, de ses compétences et de ses propositions de recherche. Il devra s’inscrire à l’interface entre climat, société et écosystèmes, en combinant idéalement des approches issues des sciences sociales et naturelles (par exemple, l’étude des institutions en lien avec des analyses quantitatives). Deux pistes sont proposées à titre indicatif : Mobilité, société et limites planétaires :  dans quelle mesure une société organisée autour de l’automobile peut-elle être compatible avec les limites planétaires et les besoins sociaux ? Quelles implications cela a-t-il pour l’avenir de nos modes de vie, de nos infrastructures et de nos structures sociales ?
Sociétés et événements météorologiques extrêmes :  comment les sociétés ont-elles été façonnées par leur histoire d’exposition aux événements météorologiques extrêmes, et que nous apprend cette relation sur leur avenir dans un contexte de changement climatique rapide ?

Ces deux pistes ne sont pas exhaustives. Des propositions de recherche différentes, explorant les relations entre sociétés humaines, environnement et changements globaux, sont également les bienvenues.
Profil
Titulaire d’un master universitaire dans une discipline pertinente pour les relations entre climat, société et environnement, notamment en géographie humaine ou physique, sciences sociales (sociologie, anthropologie, sciences politiques, économie, etc.), sciences naturelles (climatologie, écologie, physique, etc.), sciences de l’environnement, dévelopment durable, urbanisme ou ingénierie, obtenu au plus tard à l’automne 2026. Les parcours atypiques et interdisciplinaires sont également encouragés.
Ouverture à des parcours académiques variés.  Nous attachons davantage d’importance à la curiosité, à la motivation et à la capacité de développer une approche originale qu’à l’appartenance à une discipline particulière. Une expérience préalable de recherche interdisciplinaire constitue un atout, mais n’est pas indispensable et peut être acquise durant la thèse.
Intérêt à contribuer au développement d’un nouveau groupe de recherche.  Envie de participer activement à sa dynamique collective, de réfléchir à ses modes de fonctionnement, de développer des collaborations et de contribuer à un environnement de travail stimulant, ouvert et bienveillant, guidé par deux principes :  « Eile mit Weile »  (avancer avec réflexion, sans précipitation) et  « Tough on science, kind to people »  (être exigeant sur la qualité scientifique, tout en restant bienveillant envers les personnes).
Intérêt marqué pour les approches interdisciplinaires et transdisciplinaires.  Envie de collaborer avec des personnes issues de différentes disciplines, de comprendre leurs perspectives, leurs méthodes, leurs cultures scientifiques et leurs objectifs, et de construire des ponts entre ces approches pour faire émerger de nouvelles connaissances. Cet intérêt s’étend également aux échanges avec des acteurs hors du monde académique, notamment les ONG, les administrations publiques et le secteur privé.
Curiosité intellectuelle, esprit critique et goût pour l’exploration de nouvelles questions de recherche.  Nous recherchons une personne capable de prendre des initiatives, de développer ses propres idées et de travailler de manière autonome. Le poste offre une grande liberté académique, accompagnée d’un encadrement scientifique engagé, flexible et adapté aux besoins individuels. Une attention particulière est portée au développement des idées et initiatives personnelles, à l’exploration de nouvelles pistes et à l’accompagnement de chaque doctorant·e dans la construction de son propre parcours scientifique et professionnel.
Intérêt pour une recherche ayant un impact au-delà du monde académique.  Les activités du groupe visent à produire des connaissances scientifiques rigoureuses, mais aussi à favoriser leur utilisation concrète dans la société, notamment à travers le développement de logiciels open source largement utilisés (p. ex. CLIMADA), la rédaction de policy briefs et de publications pertinentes pour les politiques publiques, ainsi que la collaboration avec des acteurs de terrain et des décideurs. Nous recherchons une personne intéressée par cette articulation entre recherche fondamentale, applications concrètes et impact sociétal.
Compétences linguistiques :  bonne maîtrise du français et de l’anglais. Une amélioration du français durant les premiers mois est possible si nécessaire.

Conditions d'engagement
Durée du contrat : une année, renouvelable 3 fois (éventuellement 4).
Salaire (1e année) : 55’503 CHF brut à 75%.
50% du temps de travail est consacré à la recherche personnelle (thèse).
Lieu de travail : Institut de Géographie, Faculté des lettres et sciences humaines, Université de Neuchâtel.

Veuillez adresser vos offres par e-mail à  [email protected]  jusqu'au  30.11.2026  avec informations suivantes en un document joint: lettre de motivation, CV, thèse / mémoire de Master et copies du dernier diplôme, coordonnées (y compris adresses email) de 2 références académiques.
Les entretiens avec les candidat.e.s retenu.e.s auront lieu le  07.12.2026.

About us

The Department of Electrical Engineering at Chalmers University of Technology invites applications for one doctoral student position in the Antenna Systems group , within the Division of Communications, Antennas and Optical Networks.

The Division of Communications, Antennas and Optical Networks conducts research in wireless and optical technologies for communication and sensing, including radar and positioning, with activities ranging from antenna systems and signal processing to communication theory, optical networks, security, machine learning, and future-generation wireless systems. The division comprises three research groups: Antenna Systems , Communication Systems , and Optical Networks .

The Antenna Systems group works with antenna technologies for wireless communication and sensor systems, with applications in telecommunications, radar, transport, astronomy, space sciences, and other emerging technology areas. The group’s research addresses antenna systems over a wide frequency range and includes electronics-integrated antenna technologies, holistic antenna-system design, and over-the-air test methods for future wireless systems. The group has access to advanced antenna measurement infrastructure at Chalmers, including facilities for characterising passive and active antenna systems for 5G, 6G, and beyond.

About the research project

Future 6G wireless communication systems must deliver higher performance while operating under strict constraints on energy consumption and spectrum availability. Many candidate frequency bands for 6G are already used by services such as satellite communications, radar, radio astronomy, fixed terrestrial links, and unlicensed wireless access systems. This creates a strong need for antenna systems that can support efficient spectrum sharing at the physical layer.

This doctoral project is part of the SSF-funded Sweden–Taiwan collaborative research project Antenna Systems for 6G Wireless Networks . The project focuses on adaptive, interference-resilient antenna systems for 6G operation in the centimetre-wave frequency range, including the 6–24 GHz range often discussed as FR3. The central scientific idea is that future spectrum sharing cannot rely only on higher-layer coordination or static RF filtering. Instead, the antenna system itself must actively control how electromagnetic energy is radiated in both space and frequency.

The doctoral student will contribute to the development of adaptive, interference-resilient antenna design  for energy-efficient and scalable spectrum sharing. The work will combine antenna hardware design, hybrid analogue–digital beamforming, and over-the-air experimental validation. The research will be carried out in close collaboration with Swedish and Taiwanese academic partners, as well as with industrial stakeholders connected to future wireless infrastructure, RF systems, and non-terrestrial networks.

The position is placed at Chalmers, in the Antenna Systems group. The recruiting manager and main supervisor will be Professor Marianna Ivashina . The project will also involve collaboration with researchers in active electronics design and communication sustems.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a doctoral student, you must have a master’s level degree corresponding to at least 240 higher education credits, or equivalent qualifications, in Electrical Engineering , Applied Physics / Engineering Physics , or another closely related field. The degree must be completed by the starting date of the employment.

You should have documented knowledge from completed courses and/or thesis work in:

antenna theory, antenna engineering, or electromagnetic field theory,

microwave electronics, RF systems, or microwave engineering,

mathematical modelling and numerical analysis relevant to electrical engineering or applied physics.

You should also have:

strong written and verbal communication skills in English,

good analytical ability and motivation for independent research,

the ability to work in an international and interdisciplinary research environment,

experience with programming or technical computing, for example in MATLAB, Python, or similar tools.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

It is meritorious if you have taken courses or carried out project work in:

electromagnetic and circuit simulation tools such as CST, HFSS, ADS, or similar,

RF measurements, antenna measurements,

hardware-oriented prototyping or modeling involving RF front ends, software-defined radio, or RFSoC platforms,

signal processing.

A master’s thesis in antennas, microwave engineering, RF systems, wireless communication, signal processing for antenna systems, or a closely related area is a strong advantage.

We value personal qualities such as curiosity, accuracy, creativity, independence, and the ability to collaborate across disciplinary and cultural boundaries.

What you will do

Your major responsibility will be to pursue doctoral studies and conduct research within the SSF Sweden–Taiwan collaborative project on antenna systems for 6G wireless networks.

The work will include:

developing and analysing adaptive antenna arrays for shared-spectrum 6G operation,

studying hybrid analogue–digital beamforming methods for interference suppression, integrated communication and sensing,

investigating how hardware constraints such as mutual coupling, finite phase resolution of beamforming electronics, calibration errors, and RF impairments affect achievable performance,

contributing to joint spatial–spectral optimisation of antenna systems, including the interaction with and co-design with active electronics, and beamforming,

supporting system-level proof-of-concept development and over-the-air validation,

collaborating with Swedish and Taiwanese academic partners and industrial stakeholders,

presenting results at international conferences and publishing in leading scientific journals,

taking courses at advanced and doctoral level as part of the graduate education,

contributing to teaching or other departmental duties, normally up to 20% of working time.

The project will include international collaboration and may involve research visits, joint workshops, and travel to project partners in Taiwan.

Contract terms

The doctoral student position is fully funded from the start.

The position is a full-time, fixed-term employment.

The doctoral programme corresponds to four years of full-time research studies. Departmental duties, such as teaching, may account for up to 20% of working time and can extend the employment period up to five years. Chalmers states that doctoral positions are full-time, fixed-term positions generally limited to a maximum of five years, and that teaching or other departmental duties may account for a maximum of 20% of working hours.

Salary follows Chalmers’ current salary agreement for doctoral students (35,725 SEK per month, valid from May 1, 2026)

Doctoral studies require physical presence at Chalmers throughout the study period. A valid residence permit must be in place by the start date where applicable.

What we offer

As a doctoral student at Chalmers, you will be employed by the university and will have access to Chalmers’ employee benefits. You will join a dynamic, international research environment in Gothenburg, with strong links to both academic research and industry.

Chalmers actively works to improve equality, diversity, and inclusion, and welcomes applicants with different backgrounds and experiences. If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.

Read more about   working at Chalmers   and our  benefits  for employees.

Application procedure

The application should be written in English and attached as PDF files. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. The recruitment system does not support Zip files.

The application should include:

CV

Include education, previous employment, research experience, technical skills, publications if any, and other relevant merits.

Personal letter

Include a brief introduction of yourself, your research interests, and a motivation for why you are interested in this doctoral position.

Degree certificates and transcripts

Include bachelor’s and master’s degree certificates, if available, together with official transcripts.

Thesis and other scientific work

Attach your bachelor’s and/or master’s thesis, if available. You may also attach publications, technical reports, or other relevant written work.

References

Contact details for references may be requested later in the recruitment process.

Use the application button at the foot of the vacancy page to reach the application form. The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered.

We welcome your application no later than 14 November 2026.

For questions, please contact

Professor Marianna Ivashina

Recruiting manager

Antenna Systems group, Division of Communications, Antennas and Optical Networks

Department of Electrical Engineering, Chalmers University of Technology

Email: marianna.ivashina@chalmers.se

Phone: +46 31 772 18 12

We look forward to your application!

Quantum computers promise capabilities far beyond today's computers, but only if we can reliably protect quantum information from errors. Quantum error correction (QEC) is therefore one of the central challenges on the path toward large-scale quantum computing.

In this PhD project, you will investigate how machine learning can enable faster, more scalable QEC decoding . The goal is to develop new learning-based methods that combine strong decoding performance with the very low latency and hardware constraints required in practical quantum systems.

The position is part of QuBriC , the first European Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network dedicated entirely to QEC. You will join an international cohort of doctoral researchers and collaborate with leading academic and industrial partners, including research visits at Duke University  and IQM Quantum Computers . The PhD position is fully funded for 4 years (plus possible extension based on teaching and department duties). We offer some of the highest salaries for PhD students in Europe, full social benefits and health insurance, no tuition fees for PhD studies, financial support for relocation, and more, see below for details.

The expected starting date is early 2027.

About us

At the Department of Electrical Engineering  at Chalmers, you will join an international research environment with strong expertise in machine learning, information and coding theory, signal processing, and quantum systems. Our research combines fundamental methods with algorithm development, with close connections to both academic and industrial partners. Our working language is English.

You will be part of a research group working at the intersection of machine learning, error-correcting codes, and quantum information . The group brings together complementary expertise in coding and information theory, modern machine learning, iterative and message-passing algorithms, and quantum systems.

You will further be part of QuBriC , a large European research and training network bringing together 16 academic institutions and 7 industrial partners across 11 countries. You will join a cohort of 15 doctoral candidates based in Europe's leading QEC groups, and you will meet them regularly at network-wide training schools, workshops and conferences, giving you access to expertise well beyond your immediate research group.

About the research project

Decoding is one of the major computational challenges in quantum error correction. A useful decoder must infer the most likely errors from incomplete and noisy measurements, while operating within extremely tight latency and hardware constraints.

In this project, you will explore whether modern machine-learning (ML) methods can provide new solutions to this problem. Possible research directions include:

designing ML-based decoders for leading quantum error-correcting code families, including surface and quantum LDPC codes;

developing algorithms that combine ideas from ML, coding theory, and conventional message-passing decoders;

using learning approaches and related data-driven methods to discover new decoding strategies or even new code structures;

jointly optimizing quantum codes and their decoders for realistic noise models and hardware constraints; and

studying how ML decoders generalize across code sizes, noise conditions, and hardware platforms.

The exact direction of the project can be shaped according to your background and research interests. We are particularly interested in fundamental ideas that can ultimately lead to practical algorithms rather than simply applying existing neural-network architectures.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in electrical engineering, computer science, applied mathematics, physics, or a closely related field

Strong background and excellent course grades in at least one of the following subjects: coding/information theory, digital communications, quantum information processing, quantum computing

Strong mathematics and programming skills (e.g., Python, Matlab, or similar)

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Ability to work independently as well as collaboratively in an international research environment

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Experience in deep learning and probabilistic machine learning

Experience in optimization and message-passing algorithms

Previous experience in research, publication, and teaching

Swedish language skills are not required for this position. If you are interested in learning Swedish, our department offers Swedish language courses free of charge.

MSCA Eligibility

Because this position is funded through a Marie Skłodowska-Curie Doctoral Network, additional eligibility requirements apply. In particular:

Candidates must not already hold a doctoral degree at the date of recruitment

Mobility rule: the candidate must not have resided or carried out their main activity (work, studies, etc.) in Sweden for more than 12 months in the 36 months immediately before their recruitment date

What you will do

Your main responsibility will be to conduct high-quality research within the project and progressively develop your own research ideas. You will develop algorithms and software, perform numerical experiments and theoretical analysis, and communicate your results through publications and presentations at leading international conferences and journals. You will also take courses at an advanced level within the graduate school of Electrical Engineering .

You will collaborate extensively with researchers within QuBriC and participate in the network's research, training, and dissemination activities.

The position also includes teaching at the undergraduate and Master's level and other departmental duties, corresponding to up to 20% full time.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

The indicative gross starting salary (excluding employer social security contributions and before income tax) is approximately 35,725 SEK per month.

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer

As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers   and our  benefits  for employees.

A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .

Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . Chalmers is an equal opportunity employer committed to diversity, inclusion, and gender balance. We evaluate all applicants on merit, regardless of gender, ethnic origin, religion, age, sexual orientation, or disability. We welcome applications from candidates of all backgrounds and underrepresented groups.

If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.

Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .

Application procedure

The application should be written in English and attached as PDF files (not Word or Zip), as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.  Do not send applications by email.

Do you want to contribute to impactful research in the data-driven Food and Health field?   Join our team as a Doctoral student at the Division of Food and Nutrition Science, Department of Life Sciences.

About us

The Department of Life Sciences conducts research, innovation, and education to enable a biobased society and improve human health. We explore how biological systems, and innovative technologies can be used to convert biomass into valuable products. We use advanced computational technologies to discover how biomolecules and organisms function and interact. We pioneer new methods for prediction, prevention, diagnostics and treatment of diseases.

The Division of Food and Nutrition Science addresses major societal challenges related to sustainable food production, nutrition and health. We conduct research, innovation, education and dissemination with the aim to provide new knowledge and solutions for a sustainable planet and healthy humans.

About the research project

This doctoral position is an opportunity to work at the intersection of nutrition, multi-omics, and precision health in a strong technical and natural sciences environment well connected with clinial enviromnets in Gothenburg and internationlly. You will join a dynamic, international academic community that values scientific excellence, innovation, and sustainable development. The role is designed for a curious, skilled and motivated person who wants to build a research career and contribute to better understanding how nutrition shapes human health at a molecular level.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in chemometry, bioinformatics, food and nutrition science, biotechnology, engineering or similar

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Experience in computational metabolomics and microbiome research

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Experience in large scale OMICs-data handling and statistical analysis

Documented programming skills and excellent R user.

Previous experience from scientific data generation, analysis and publishing

Hands on skills in metabolomics and multi-modal data integration

What you will do

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Bioscience  ( Bioscience | Chalmers  )

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing

The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Data management and programming support to other graduate students in the environment.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer

As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers   and our  benefits  for employees.

A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .

Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

Chalmers is dedicated to improving gender balance and actively works with equality projects, such as the GENIE Initiative for gender equality and excellence . We celebrate diversity and consider equality and inclusion as fundamental aspects of all our activities.

If Swedish is not your native language, Chalmers offers Swedish courses to help you settle in.

Find more general information about doctoral studies at Chalmers here .

Application procedure

The application should be written in English and attached as PDF-files, as below. Maximum size for each file is 40 MB. Please note that the system does not support Zip files.

CV

Personal letter

A brief introduction about yourself.

A brief motivation as to why you are interested in this position.

Bachelor’s and, if available, master’s thesis together with the transcripts.

Use the button at the foot of the page to reach the application form.

A background check may be conducted as part of the application process.

Please note: The applicant is responsible for ensuring that the application is complete. Incomplete applications and applications sent by email will not be considered. Contact details to references will be requested after the interview.

We welcome your application no later than  11 November, 2026.

For questions, please contact:

Rikard Landberg
Professor, Head of Division of Food and Nutrition Science
rikard.landberg@chalmers.se

We look forward to your application!

chalmers:15115.body:
Chalmers University of Technology is seeking to recruit an outstanding individual to serve as Director of Onsala Space Observatory (OSO) and lead the Observatory’s continued development as a world-class research infrastructure.

About us

Chalmers University of Technology strives for academic excellence while addressing the challenges and needs of society and industry. We offer a creative and dynamic environment for research, education, innovation and applied science.

Chalmers University of Technology hosts Onsala Space Observatory (OSO), Sweden’s national infrastructure for radio astronomy and space geodesy. OSO has a strong link to the Division of Astronomy and Plasma Physics and its broad astronomy research environment. The observatory is also a key part of Chalmers’ wider research and innovation ecosystem, benefiting from strong synergies with complementary infrastructures, such as Myfab for micro- and nanofabrication, Chalmers e-Commons for research data and computing, and the National Academic Infrastructure for Supercomputing in Sweden (NAISS).

OSO supports internationally leading research through advanced facilities and instrumentation in radio astronomy and space geodesy. OSO is also a key partner in major international collaborations, including ALMA, SKAO, EVN, JIV-ERIC and LOFAR ERIC, and is a leading station within the International VLBI Service for Geodesy and Astrometry (IVS). OSO is operated by Chalmers University of Technology with financial support from the Swedish Research Council (VR) and Lantmäteriet (the National Land Survey of Sweden). OSO employs around 50 researchers and research support staff, as part of the Department of Physics and Astronomy.

The Role

As Director of OSO, you will have a central leadership role with overall responsibility for the strategic, scientific and technical activities of the observatory. The role includes responsibility for staff, operations and budgets, as well as developing the organisation and competencies
needed to ensure high-quality operations and strengthen OSO’s long-term scientific development, both nationally and internationally.

An important part of the role is to continue to foster an engaging and attractive environment for employees, researchers and collaboration partners, and contribute to Chalmers’ long-term vision and ambition to be a leading technical university in Europe.

The Director will represent OSO nationally and internationally, with an ambition to further strengthen its scientific profile, secure long-term funding, and develop strategic partnerships with universities, research infrastructures and other stakeholders. The Director will also play a key role in strengthening and developing OSO’s international collaborations.

Working closely with scientific, technical and administrative staff, the Director will lead the continued development of the Observatory’s facilities and research-supporting technologies in radio astronomy and space geodesy.

The Director reports to the Head of the Department of Physics and Astronomy at Chalmers University of Technology, as well as to the international OSO Steering Committee. We will provide appropriate support to enable the Director to successfully fulfil the responsibilities of the role.

Qualifications

The successful candidate should have:

Academic qualifications at the level of Professor in astronomy, with an internationally recognised scientific track record.

A broad understanding of the international landscape in radio astronomy, astrophysics and space geodesy.

Experience in leading and developing research infrastructures, research groups and/or laboratories, preferably in an international environment.

Experience in managing personnel, budgets and operations in a complex scientific or technical organisation.

Experience in developing international collaborations.

Experience with advanced observational facilities, large-scale instrumentation or research infrastructures.

Personal Characteristics

We seek an inspiring and strategic leader who can set clear priorities, delegate effectively and enable others to take responsibility, while building trust and fostering a collaborative, high-performing environment. The successful candidate will combine sound judgement, operational effectiveness and financial responsibility with a strong strategic vision for the observatory and the ability to drive its operational development.

Strong analytical, communication and intercultural skills are essential, together with the ability to build and maintain productive relationships with staff, university leadership, funding agencies and international partners.

Employment terms

The position as Director can be structured in one of two ways: either as a full-time permanent position as Director, or as a permanent faculty position with a fixed-term assignment as Director. The latter option requires an academic review for candidates who do not already hold a faculty position at Chalmers, where the role as Director would then be combined with individual research or teaching up to 20% of full time.

The Director recruitment follows Chalmers’ guidelines for leadership appointments and are carried out by a recruitment committee. The final decision is made by the President.

The position is based at Onsala Space Observatory, in Sweden.
Start date by agreement.

What we offer

Chalmers offers a cultivating and inspiring work environment in the coastal city of  Gothenburg . This position offers a unique opportunity to lead a nationally important research infrastructure with strong international visibility and influence. The successful candidate will play a leading role in shaping the future of Swedish radio astronomy and space geodesy while contributing to major international scientific collaborations.

Chalmers and OSO provide a dynamic, international and inclusive work environment characterised by openness, collaboration, sustainability and scientific excellence. Equality and diversity are substantial foundations in all activities at Chalmers.

Application procedure

This recruitment process is being conducted in collaboration with Perrett Laver.

Please note that all application materials must be submitted via the advertisement published by Perrett Laver.

Please click here to access the advertisement on the Perrett Laver website.

CV

Personal letter

Other documents (optional): e.g. copies of completed education

References will be requested should you proceed in the recruitment process.

Interviews
Interviews are planned for 10 December, and possible the 16th of December 2026. We kindly ask you to reserve this date for a potential interview.
If you are unavailable during this period, please indicate this in your application.

As part of the recruitment process, a background check will be conducted on the final candidate.

Nominations
In parallel with this announcement, there is an opportunity to nominate candidates for the position.

Please include the nominee’s contact details and a brief motivation explaining why you consider the person suitable for the role. Nominations should be submitted no later than 6 November to HR Partner Madelene Olsson,
email: madelene.olsson@chalmers.se .

For external applicants:
If you are an external candidate and intend to conduct research and/or teaching alongside your assignment as Director, you will also be evaluated for a faculty position by Chalmers' Faculty Appointment Committee during this recruitment process. The purpose of the review is to ensure that you meet the requirements for a faculty position according to Chalmers Appointment Regulations for Teaching and Research Faculty . If you proceed in the recruitment process, you will be asked to supplement with teaching and research merits/documents, please see below.

Pedagogical qualifications:
• Please compile a pedagogical portfolio to describe your pedagogical and educational qualifications using the format specified in the Pedagogical Portfolio instructions .
• Please append certificates for completed courses in pedagogical training and any other documents described in the pedagogical portfolio instructions.

Other documents:
• Documents verifying awards and recognitions stated in your CV, and other documents relevant to support your application.
• Copies of a maximum of five relevant publications that cannot be accessed via your ORCID, Scopus ID or ResearcherID.

Application deadline: November 17, 2026

For questions, please contact:
Mattias Marklund, Head of Department
mattias.marklund@chalmers.se

Madelene Olsson, HR Partner
madelene.olsson@chalmers.se

Dr Valia Sakkoula, Perrett Laver
Valia.Sakkoula@perrettlaver.com

We look forward to your application!

How do advanced composite materials perform after millions of load cycles in the demanding environment of an aeroengine? As a doctoral student in this international research collaboration, you will help answer that question through a combination of experimental testing, advanced simulations, and close interaction with leading researchers and industry experts. Your work will contribute to the development of future aerospace structures that are lighter, more efficient, and more reliable.

About us

The PhD position is placed at the Division of Computational Mechanics and Materials Engineering . We foster an inclusive, friendly, and helpful work environment to which we welcome you to contribute. Our activities integrate computational mechanics and advanced materials technology, combining multidisciplinary expertise to predict, understand, and elevate the performance of engineering materials and structures.

Within the project, you will be supported by an international team of experts in the area of mechanics of composites, combining academic excellence with industrial expertise and experience.

About the research project

The project aims to enable the deployment of advanced composite structures in aeroengines by developing reliable methods for predicting fatigue life of textile carbon fibre composites under thermomechanical tension-tension loading. Through combined experimental characterisation and development of an industrially applicable simulation framework, the project will support safe and efficient design of complex aerospace components.

More specifically, the project goals are to:

Characterise the fatigue properties and stiffness degradation of a relevant prototype textile reinforced composite material system under pure cyclic tension-tension loading.

Develop an industrially applicable and computationally efficient ply-level macroscale fatigue model that describes how damage evolves under varying load amplitudes and thermal conditions.

Combine the novel ply-level fatigue model with an existing state-of-the-art inter-laminar fatigue damage model into a complete fatigue life assessment framework.

Accelerate the computational efficiency of the framework by utilising novel cycle extrapolation techniques to represent the effect of fatigue loading over many cycles at a time.

Evaluate realistic but critical thermomechanical fatigue cycles through a combined experimental-simulation approach.

Enable industrial adoption of the proposed fatigue assessment framework into future design procedures at GKN Aerospace.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in  Applied Mechanics, Structural Engineering, Computational Engineering, Engineering Mathematics, Engineering Physics or similar.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Documented experience (education/courses or thesis project with high grades) in continuum mechanics, advanced finite element method and the mechanics of fibre-reinforced polymers

Interest and high skills in programming and numerical methods

*for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

We also expect that you are analytical, ambitious, independent, and a strong team player that thrives through collaboration.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Documented knowledge in experimental testing.

Documented knowledge in aerospace applications and/or aeroengines.

Documented knowledge and experience in ANSYS or LS Dyna, including implementation of user subroutines (such as user materials or user elements)

What you will do

Characterise the thermoemechanical tension-tension fatigue behaviour of a prototype composite materials sytem with textile reinforcements.

Develop and implement a complete numerical framework to assess the tension-tension fatigue life of aeroengine components.

Develop your scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research through written scientific publications and oral presentations at international conferences.

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Solid and Structural Mechanics .

Teach on Chalmers' undergraduate level corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

We invite applications for two Doctoral positions in experimental quantum computing with superconducting circuits. You will work in the stimulating research environment of the Wallenberg Centre for Quantum Technology ( WACQT ), a 12-year initiative started in 2018 with the purpose of advancing Swedish academia and industry to the forefront of quantum technology. The core project of the centre is to build a quantum computer based on superconducting circuits. You will be part of the Quantum Computing group  in the Quantum Technology Laboratory (QTL) division of the Microtechnology and Nanoscience (MC2) department, working in a large team of PhDs, postdocs and researchers.

About us

The Department of Microtechnology and Nanoscience advances the frontiers in quantum technology, nanoscience, photonics and future electronic systems - for technical and societal development. Our cross-disciplinary approach gives interesting collaborations in academy, industry and society, and is a driving force for innovations, results and breakthroughs. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.

At the Quantum Technology Laboratory , we explore how quantum physics can unlock radically new ways of processing information - far beyond the limits of classical systems. Our research spans quantum computing, sensing, transduction, thermodynamics, and foundations, all aimed at harnessing the powerful behavior of light and matter at the quantum level. We offer a vibrant, international research environment and direct access to world-class nanofabrication facilities.

About the research project

We are seeking Doctoral students to work on building the next generation of large-scale quantum processors based on superconducting circuits. To achieve this ambitious goal, we currently have projects related to:

• Development and optimization of nano-fabrication processes for superconducting devices
• Design and microwave simulation of quantum processors

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Physics, Applied Physics, Nanotechnology.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Experience in one or more of the following areas: superconducting circuits, experimental quantum computing, quantum optics, or a related field within experimental physics.

You are passionate about quantum technology and eager to contribute to its future development.

You thrive in a collaborative environment, enjoy sharing knowledge, and take responsibility for your work.

You have a strong analytical mindset, pay attention to detail, and enjoy tackling complex challenges.

You are keen to contribute to the development of students through supervision and mentoring.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Experience in nanofabrication, microwave measurements, cryogenics, microwave simulations, experimental quantum computing

What you will do

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of the Department of Microtechnology and Nanoscience

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing

The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Contribute to the development of next-generation superconducting quantum processors, working in one of the following research areas:

Nanofabrication of superconducting quantum devices: Develop and optimize fabrication processes to improve device performance, reproducibility, and scalability. Investigate different materials and fabrication techniques to understand and mitigate sources of loss in superconducting circuits.

Design and simulation of quantum processors: Design superconducting circuits and perform electromagnetic and microwave simulations to optimize device performance and support the development of larger-scale quantum processors.

Work closely with experimentalists, theorists, and engineers in an interdisciplinary research environment, contributing to the development and testing of quantum hardware.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

What we offer

As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers   and our  benefits  for employees.

A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .

Read more about Sweden’s generous parental leave, subsidized day care, free schools, healthcare etc at Move To Gothenburg.

chalmers:15122.body:
Can a battery cathode be made from phosphorus recovered from municipal wastewater? Join us at Chalmers University of Technology to investigate how recovered phosphorus can be converted into battery-grade lithium iron phosphate (LFP), working hands-on along the entire chain from waste-derived powder to tested battery cells.

About us

You will join Daniel Weber’s research group at the Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering , with co-supervision from Martina Petranikova’s hydrometallurgy group within the same department. You will work alongside doctoral students and postdocs with experience from previous research projects, providing a collaborative environment for developing your experimental skills.

Our research facilities include furnaces with various atmospheres, stirred tank reactors and a spray dryer for precursor synthesis, an Ar glovebox, PXRD (housed at Chalmers Materials Analysis Laboratory ), TGA-DSC, Raman and IR spectroscopy, ICP and XRF, a laser diffraction particle size analyzer, and a battery assembly line with cell testing equipment.

Large-format pouch cells of the most promising materials will be built and tested in collaboration with a partner university in Germany. Through the project's industrial advisory board and potential research stay, you will have opportunities to engage directly with industrial partners and gain insight into how your research results can be applied in practice.

About the research project

The PHOS4CELL project investigates whether phosphorus recovered from municipal wastewater can be converted into battery-grade lithium iron phosphate (LFP). You will study how impurities in recovered phosphorus affect battery capacity and cycle life, which contaminants can be tolerated and which must be removed. By synthesizing, characterizing and testing LFP from different phosphorus sources, you will explore how recycled materials can contribute to a more sustainable battery value chain.

The four-year project is funded by the Swedish Energy Agency within the program Sustainable battery value chain (Hållbar batterivärdekedja). It brings together researchers from Chalmers, Polestar and industrial partners across the LFP value chain. The project may also include a research stay at a European LFP cathode producer.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master's degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, Metallurgy or a closely related field.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

Documented hands-on experience from a materials chemistry laboratory, including inorganic powder synthesis, and/or hydrometallurgical processing of materials.

Ability to independently plan and conduct laboratory experiments, identify and resolve experimental problems, and maintain accurate and systematic documentation of results.

Good communication and collaboration skills, including the ability to work with researchers and engineers from different disciplines and industrial partners.

A curious and analytical approach to experimental research, with a willingness to investigate and understand unexpected results.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Solid-state or wet-chemical synthesis of inorganic functional materials, particularly phosphates, iron compounds or battery cathode materials.

Experience with reduction of Fe(III) under hydrogen or carbothermal conditions.

Powder X-ray diffraction and Rietveld refinement (e.g. TOPAS, GSAS-II or FullProf), including quantitative phase analysis.

Experience controlling particle size and morphology through precipitation, milling, spray drying or similar methods.

Proficiency in Swedish, as the project involves regular interaction with Swedish industrial partners.

Experience working with or for industry, or in research projects involving industrial partners.

Familiarity with Matlab, Python or similar programming languages for data analysis and visualization, and with statistical or data-driven experimental design.

What you will do

Synthesize LFP cathode materials from waste-derived phosphorus and commercial reference reagents, incl. calcination, milling, reduction under hydrogen or carbothermal conditions, and carbon coating.

Purify and characterize secondary phosphorus feedstocks and intermediates using hydrometallurgical methods, in collaboration with the Petranikova group, and quantify impurities using techniques such as XRF, ICP, TOC and CHNS analysis.

Characterize material structure, composition and morphology using powder X-ray diffraction with Rietveld refinement, particle size analysis, electron microscopy and thermal analysis.

Investigate particle engineering through precipitation and spray drying to achieve particle sizes and tap densities relevant to industrial applications.

Assemble and test half and full coin cells, and relate their electrochemical performance to material composition, impurity profiles and particle properties.

Take courses at an advanced level within the relevant graduate school at Chalmers. Read more about our graduate schools .

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing.

The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Collaborate with industrial partners through advisory board meetings, sample exchanges and discussions of technical specifications, with the possibility of an industrial research stay.

Publish research results in peer-reviewed journals, present findings at national and international conferences, and contribute to the supervision of bachelor's and master's students.

chalmers:15124.body:
Join us as a research engineer and play a key role in supporting world-class research in materials science. Working closely with students, researchers, and advanced laboratory equipment, you will contribute to the development of materials and manufacturing technologies for a more sustainable future.

Information about the division

The Division of Materials and Manufacture at the Department of Mechanical Engineering (ME) conducts research and teaching in the areas of materials science and manufacturing technology. The activities range from materials design and coating development to additive manufacturing and the development of cutting processes. The work is mainly experimental and includes advanced microscopy and surface technology with links to theory. The division is responsible for the mechanical workshop and coordinates its experimental activities with the division of Computational Mechanics and Engineering Materials, whose activities in the Materials Manufacturing Lab are focused on mechanical testing and polymer processing. The two divisions share the need for advanced experimental support when it comes to computers and equipment.

Job description

As a research engineer, you will support Master's students, doctoral students, postdoctoral researchers, and staff by providing operational and technical support for laboratory equipment and related systems.

The role includes maintenance support for advanced research instruments, contact with suppliers and service organisations, purchasing consumables and electronic devices, and assisting with invoicing for external users. You will also contribute to ensuring compliance with applicable work environment legislation within your areas of responsibility.

Contract terms

Temporary employment, for a maximum period of one year.

Qualifications

As a research engineer, you will support the operation and maintenance of advanced characterization equipment. This includes troubleshooting technical issues and coordinating with suppliers' service organizations when needed.

To qualify for the position, you should have:

a university degree, or equivalent qualifications, in a relevant technical field,

knowledge of electrics, electrical installations, or digital electronics,

the ability to troubleshoot and resolve technical problems,

good communication skills in both Swedish and English.

It is meritorious if you have:

knowledge of mechanics, compressed air systems, cooling systems, and gases,

experience from materials science or laboratory environments,

experience supporting computers and electronic devices.

As many issues arise unexpectedly, you enjoy solving technical challenges and supporting students and researchers in their daily work. The position offers a varied workday with a wide range of responsibilities.

What we offer

Chalmers provides a cultivating and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of  Gothenburg .
Read more about  working at Chalmers  and our  benefits  for employees.

Chalmers aims to actively improve our gender balance. We work broadly with equality projects, for example the GENIE Initiative on gender equality for excellence . Equality and diversity are substantial foundations in all activities at Chalmers.

Vill du arbeta nära forskning, utbildning och nyttiggörande i en varierad roll där din servicekänsla gör skillnad? Som avdelningsadministratör vid Chalmers institution för miljö- och energivetenskaper får du en central roll med många kontaktytor och kvalificerade arbetsuppgifter. Du blir en del av institutionens nybildade verksamhetsstöd och får möjlighet att tillsammans med dina kollegor utveckla arbetssätt och forma ett verksamhetsstöd av högsta klass.

Information om institutionen och avdelningen

Institutionen för miljö- och energivetenskaper (ENV) bedriver verksamhet inom miljö- och energiområdet med starka kopplingar till tvärvetenskaplig forskning och samverkan med samhälle, industri och akademi, både nationellt och internationellt.

Du blir en del av institutionens nybildade verksamhetsstöd som arbetar nära och ger stöd till forskning och utbildning. Verksamhetsstödet består av administratörer, ekonomer, ett centrum (SLC) och en administrativ chef. Både institutionen och verksamhetsstödet befinner sig i en etablerings- och utvecklingsfas där gemensamma arbetssätt behöver utvecklas, tydliggöras och förankras i organisationen.

Beskrivning av tjänsten

Som avdelningsadministratör ger du kvalificerat administrativt stöd till avdelningschef, enhetschef, medarbetare och gäster. Rollen är bred och varierad med många kontaktytor och ett nära samarbete med chefer, ekonomer, administratörer och andra stödfunktioner, såväl inom institutionen som inom Chalmers centrala verksamhetsstöd.

I dina huvudsakliga arbetsuppgifter ingår att:

ge personaladministrativt stöd i samarbete med chefer och HR, exempelvis vid anställningar, förlängningar och avslut

ge administrativt och praktiskt stöd till nyanställda och gäster, bland annat vid introduktion, behörigheter samt rese- och hotellbokningar

hantera inköp och enklare ekonomiadministration, exempelvis kontering av fakturor, arvodesräkningar och inventering

hantera praktiska lokalfrågor såsom felanmälningar, fördelning av arbetsplatser och beställningar

ge administrativt stöd vid avdelningens möten, konferenser och andra arrangemang samt hantera övrig löpande administration

En viktig del av uppdraget är forskarutbildningsadministration för hela institutionen, ett ansvar som du delar med en annan administratör. I nära samarbete med viceprefekt för forskarutbildning och studierektorer ansvarar du för administrativa processer under doktorandernas utbildning, från antagning och registrering i Ladok till uppföljning av individuella studieplaner och administration i samband med licentiatseminarier och disputationer. Du ger även löpande stöd till doktorander och handledare i administrativa frågor.

Utöver den löpande administrationen har du en aktiv roll i att förbättra och vidareutveckla rutiner och arbetssätt, särskilt inom forskarutbildningen. Du identifierar förbättringsbehov, föreslår lösningar och bidrar till att dokumentera, införa och följa upp gemensamma arbetssätt. Du deltar även i relevanta administrativa nätverk och bidrar till kunskapsdelning, samarbete och ett välfungerande stöd inom institutionen. På sikt kan även viss administration inom grundutbildningen komma att ingå i tjänsten.

Anställningsform

Tillsvidareanställning på heltid med önskat tillträde i januari eller enligt överenskommelse.
Provanställnig kan komma att tillämpas.

Kvalifikationer

Vi söker dig som har minst gymnasieutbildning och flerårig erfarenhet av kvalificerat administrativt arbete. Du har hög servicekänsla, god förmåga att kommunicera på svenska och engelska i både tal och skrift samt god digital kompetens. Du är nyfiken på nya arbetssätt och har lätt för att sätta dig in i nya administrativa system och processer.

Det är meriterande om du har:

relevant eftergymnasial utbildning, exempelvis inom administration, eller arbetslivserfarenhet som vi bedömer likvärdig

erfarenhet av forskarutbildningsadministration eller annan högskoleadministration

erfarenhet av personaladministration, inköp och enklare ekonomiadministration

erfarenhet av administrativa system, exempelvis Ladok, Primula, Proceedo eller motsvarande

erfarenhet av förbättringsarbete och av att utveckla och införa administrativa rutiner

erfarenhet av att använda digitalisering och AI som stöd i administrativa processer

Personliga egenskaper

För att lyckas i rollen behöver du vara självständig, strukturerad och kvalitetsmedveten. Du har en god förmåga att planera, prioritera och hantera flera parallella arbetsuppgifter, även när förutsättningarna snabbt förändras. Du arbetar noggrant, har hög integritet och trivs med att kombinera löpande administration med utvecklingsarbete.

Som person är du serviceinriktad, flexibel och initiativtagande. Du samarbetar väl med andra, trivs med många kontaktytor och har lätt för att bygga goda relationer. Du är lyhörd för verksamhetens behov och bidrar med ett lösningsorienterat förhållningssätt till ett professionellt och välfungerande administrativt stöd.

Vi lägger stor vikt vid personlig lämplighet.

Att arbeta på Chalmers

Chalmers värdeord – öppenhet, respekt, delaktighet, mångfald och kvalitet – genomsyrar vår syn på arbetsmiljö och medarbetarskap. Vi erbjuder en stimulerande arbetsplats i en akademisk miljö, där studenter och medarbetare drivs av att skapa värde för en hållbar framtid.

Våra förmåner för anställda omfattar bland annat:

Flexibilitet att arbeta på distans med hänsyn till verksamhetens behov.

Semester upp till sju veckor per år.

Kollektivavtal med föräldralön, sjukpenningtillägg, ersättning för läkemedelskostnader, löneväxling, pension, inarbetade dagar samt flextid.

Friskvårdsbidrag samt en friskvårdstimma varje vecka under betald arbetstid.

Här kan du läsa mer om våra förmåner och hur det är att arbeta på Chalmers .

Ansökningsförfarande

Ansökan ska vara märkt med namn och dokumenten sparas som PDF-filer enligt nedan:

CV

Personligt brev

1–2 sidor

Övrigt (valfritt)

Eventuella intyg, betyg etc.

Bakgrundskontroll kan komma att genomföras som en del av rekryteringsprocessen.

Sista ansökningsdag:  8 november, urval kommer att genomföras löpande under ansökningsperioden.

Vid frågor, vänligen kontakta:

Camilla Kolm, administrativ chef
camilla.kolm@chalmers.se

Madelene Olsson, HR-partner
madelene.olsson@chalmers.se

Välkommen med din ansökan!

Chalmers undanber sig alla erbjudanden om ytterligare jobbannonsering eller rekryteringsstöd i samband med denna rekrytering.

Universitetet har 3 100 anställda, 10 000 studenter och utbildar ingenjörer, arkitekter och sjöbefäl. Med vetenskaplig excellens som grund utvecklar Chalmers kompetens och tekniska lösningar för en hållbar värld. Genom globalt engagemang och entreprenörsanda skapar vi innovationskraft, i nära samarbete med övriga samhället.

Chalmers grundades 1829 och har än idag samma motto: Avancez – framåt.

Do you want to help create the next generation of sustainable 3D products from pulp fibres? In this Doctoral project, you will combine materials science, mechanics and multiscale characterisation to establish predictive design rules for transforming fibres into advanced products. You will contribute to research with the potential to replace fossil-based plastics with sustainable alternatives.

About us

The Department of Chemistry and Chemical Engineering pushes the knowledge of chemistry and chemical engineering forward in a broad field of research and education. We offer an international environment, with scientific areas ranging from fundamental chemistry, health and medical technology, materials science, renewable energy, to chemical engineering processing, material recycling, nuclear chemistry, theory and modelling.

The Division of Applied Chemistry
We primarily focus on applied research, that is, research aimed at addressing societal challenges and that is ready for implementation either immediately or in the near future. Examples of application areas include fossil-free fuels and energy systems, electronic devices, health and technology, the utilisation of fibres and forest-based materials, and various forms of catalysis.

About the research project

Can pulp fibres be engineered into complex 3D products that rival conventional plastics?

This Doctoral project aims to transform fibre-based manufacturing from trial-and-error development to predictive design. You will combine experiments, mechanical analysis and multiscale material characterisation to uncover how fibre properties govern deformability, damage, spring-back and shape retention in 3D forming processes.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree (120 credits) or an equivalent degree in Materials Science, Mechanical Engineering, Fibre and Polymer Technology, Wood Technology, Engineering Physics, Chemical Engineering, Pharmaceutical Technology or a related field.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

Documented experience from experimental research, thesis work, or industrial projects related to materials, mechanics, manufacturing, polymers, fibre-based materials, or modelling.

Demonstrated ability to analyse and interpret complex experimental data

Ability to collaborate effectively and communicate clearly in multidisciplinary and international environments.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Experience with fibre-based materials, polymers, paper, packaging, or other sustainable material systems.

Experience in experimental materials characterisation, mechanical testing, microscopy, image analysis, or related analytical techniques.

Experience with data analysis, modelling, finite element methods, or programming (e.g. Python, MATLAB, or similar tools).

Experience working in interdisciplinary teams and communicating scientific results in written reports or presentations.

What you will do

Take courses at an advanced level within the Chalmers graduate education system and actively participate in the research environment of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a Vinnova Competence Centre bringing together academia and industry.

Conduct research aimed at understanding how fibre properties, material structure and processing conditions influence the formability of lignocellulosic materials into complex three-dimensional products. You will combine experimental studies, multiscale characterisation and data analysis to develop predictive design principles for fibre-based manufacturing.

Develop your own scientific ideas and communicate research results through publications in international journals, presentations at conferences, and interactions with industrial partners.

Collaborate with researchers from Chalmers, KTH and industrial partners within FibRe, contributing to the development of sustainable alternatives to fossil-based plastics.

The position generally includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or other departmental duties corresponding to up to 20% of full-time employment.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

The successful candidate will be employed by Chalmers University of Technology and enrolled in the doctoral education programme upon admission.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

The doctoral student will be part of the FibRe Centre for Lignocellulose-based Thermoplastics , a VINNOVA Competence Centre involving close collaboration with academic and industrial partners and Area of Advance Production .

What we offer

As a Doctoral student at Chalmers, you are an employee and enjoy all employee benefits. Read more about   working at Chalmers   and our  benefits  for employees.

A dynamic and inspiring working environment in the coastal city of Gothenburg .

Are you excited to push the boundaries of artificial intelligence in nuclear technology? Join us as a doctoral student to explore the advanced frontier of AI-driven nuclear safeguards and enhance global nuclear safety and security.

About us

The Reactor Physics, Modelling and Safety group at Chalmers develops advanced methods for modelling, simulation, monitoring and safety analysis of current and next-generation nuclear reactors. Combining expertise in reactor physics, thermal-hydraulics, nuclear safeguards, diagnostic techniques and machine learning applied to nuclear technology, the group conducts both fundamental and applied research in collaboration with national and international partners across academia and industry. We are part of the Division of Subatomic, High Energy and Plasma Physics , at the Department of Physics and Astronomy , offering a dynamic and stimulating working environment.

About the research project

Artificial Neural Network (ANN) models are powerful tools for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection. However, their architectural and optimization complexity renders them black boxes, posing a challenge when making critical decisions, such as classifying SNF as either consistent or inconsistent with declared information. In this doctoral research, you will investigate an Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) framework to enable transparency in ANN models and their predictions for SNF inspection, bridging high-performing machine learning with transparent nuclear verification.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Physics, Mathematics, Computer Science, or equivalent.

You have strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

You have background/experience in at least one of the following areas: Machine Learning, Deep Learning, Explainable AI, Reactor Physics, Nuclear Safeguards.

You have a solid background in computational methods and strong programming skills (e.g., in Python).

You thrive in a collaborative environment and take responsibility for your work.

You have a strong analytical mindset and enjoy complex challenges.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

What you will do

Conduct doctoral research focused on exploring, testing, and evaluating an Explainable AI (XAI) framework for Spent Nuclear Fuel (SNF) safeguards inspection.

Integrate various XAI methods and study semantic layers to aggregate predictions into actionable explanations for safeguards inspectors.

Leverage XAI insights to guide ANN model architectures, optimize training strategies, and strengthen model robustness.

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate research results through peer-reviewed journal publications and conference presentations.

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Nuclear Engineering .

The position generally also includes teaching at Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours.

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

Join us at Chalmers University of Technology to pioneer the next generation of batteries through advanced 3D printing and additive manufacturing. Be part of an innovative research team (4 Professors in battery, additive manufacturing, sustainable product design, and AI) exploring new ways to manufacture batteries with greater design flexibility, improved performance, and more sustainable production.

About us

At the Department of Mechanical Engineering , we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world.

The Division of Materials and Manufacture conducts research across the full value chain, from materials design and processing to advanced manufacturing and characterisation, with a strong emphasis on metallic systems. We combine interdisciplinary expertise with close industry collaboration to develop sustainable materials and manufacturing technologies.

About the research project

What if you could 3D-print a battery? This doctoral project explores advanced additive manufacturing technologies to develop new approaches for battery fabrication, enabling greater design flexibility and new possibilities for integrating battery materials and structures. You will investigate how materials, printing processes and electrode design can be combined to create functional battery components and demonstrate their potential in next-generation energy storage. The research aims to advance innovative and more sustainable battery manufacturing.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.
