chalmers:15151.body:
We are looking for a Doctoral student to conduct groundbreaking research on novel perovskite redox materials for hydrogen production. The project is multidisciplinary, and you will collaborate with leading researchers with extensive and internationally recognized expertise within a pan-European consortium aiming to demonstrate the technology at pilot scale.

About us

You will be employed at the Division of Energy Technology , which is part of the Department of Environmental and Energy Sciences . The Division of Energy Technology has approximately 80 employees, including around 30 doctoral students. We conduct research and offer education primarily in the fields of energy technology and energy systems. Our research focuses on biomass combustion and gasification, carbon dioxide mitigation technologies, high-temperature processes, energy transition, and sustainable energy systems. A considerable part of our research is experimental, and to support this work we have developed and maintain unique research facilities, including the Chalmers research boiler/gasifier and several chemical-looping pilot reactors. We also conduct systems-level research projects involving in-depth studies of energy conversion processes. Our research areas are characterized by a strong demand for new, efficient, and environmentally sustainable technologies, rapid changes in the political and economic landscape, and an urgent need to bring existing solutions into practical implementation. The current doctoral student position is collaborative in nature and also involves activities conducted at the Division of Chemical Physics and the Division of Energy and Materials.

About the research project

The announced positions are part of the project “Enabling Negative Emissions with Hydrogen Production by Advanced Chemical Looping (ENHANCE)”, a major collaborative project involving ten partners and funded through the Clean Energy Transition Partnership (CETP), a large EU-supported research initiative. The aim is to develop novel perovskite oxides with thermochemical properties suitable for hydrogen production from biogenic resources with inherent CO 2 capture. You will use advanced characterization and evaluation techniques, data mining, and generative machine learning models to establish an active learning framework for identifying materials with the required properties. Promising candidates will be synthesized, characterized, and evaluated in the laboratory. Your work will help establish the concept as a viable technology for the sustainable and efficient production of hydrogen. Subsequently, project partners will implement the materials in small- and medium-scale pilot units.

Who we are looking for

By the starting date, the applicant should have a MSc degree corresponding to at least 240 ECTS credits in a subject relevant for the project content (e.g. chemistry, physics, chemical engineering, engineering physics, material science, energy engineering, or alike).

The position requires excellent verbal and written communication skills in English.

Experience with machine learning algorithms and coding for material applications is highly meritorious.

Experience of work in chemistry lab environment (e.g. material synthesis, material characterization), or experience in ab-initio and DFT calculations of solid materials, are both meritorious.

What you will do

Your primary responsibility as a doctoral student is to pursue your own research studies. This includes developing your own scientific concepts and communicating the results of your research verbally and in writing. You are expected to write scientific articles, a mid-term licentiate thesis and defend your doctoral thesis in five years. The position also includes teaching in Chalmers' undergraduate programs and departmental duties, corresponding to a maximum of 20 % of the working time in total. You will also take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Energy, Environment and Systems ( Energy, Environment and Systems | Chalmers ).

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years. However, you are expected to teach in Chalmers' undergraduate programmes and perform other departmental duties corresponding to a maximum of 20% of your working time, which extend the period of employment to up to five years.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

chalmers:15155.body:
How can artificial intelligence help predict equipment degradation and enable smarter maintenance decisions?

At Chalmers University of Technology, you will explore this question by developing AI-powered methods for assessing and predicting the health of industrial assets. We are looking for a Doctoral student to become part of our team at the Division of Production Systems  in the Department of Mechanical Engineering . Please join our innovative team and contribute to exciting research on Production systems, AI-supported condition assessment, and maintenance decision-making in a collaborative and dynamic environment.

About us

The Division of Production Systems works with the sustainability and competitiveness of industrial production systems. The research area is system-oriented and requires knowledge about both the system as a whole and its separate components, for example humans, automation, and processes. The research highlights the different stages of a production system’s life cycle, i.e. planning, design, commissioning, operation, maintenance and reuse. Methods and research findings are generic, with applications within various industries, such as automotive, aerospace, processing and mining industries.

The people in the division form an internationally diverse, gender-balanced, and inclusive team of more than 30 cross-disciplinary researchers and support staff. Our strong international collaborative networks and advanced research infrastructure, Stena Industry Innovation Lab, make us a competitive international actor.

The Production Systems Division is part of Chalmers largest unit, the Department of Mechanical Engineering , where we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. The department is highly ranked internationally. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world.

About the research project

The research will develop and evaluate AI-powered Asset Health Index models that combine heterogeneous condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge into transparent indicators of asset condition and degradation. The work will investigate how artificial intelligence can strengthen model development, support prognostics and Remaining Useful Life estimation, and turn complex data into useful information for maintenance and asset-management decisions. Through close academic and industrial collaboration, the project will validate the models in a real-world pilot environment, with emphasis on general methods for condition assessment, risk analysis, maintenance prioritisation, and lifecycle-oriented decision support for complex technical assets.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Mechanical Engineering, Production Engineering, Industrial Engineering, Automation, Data Science, Computer Science, or another relevant field.

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English.

You should have a strong interest in maintenance, asset management, data-driven engineering, artificial intelligence, or prognostics and health management.

A strong candidate is highly motivated, self-driven and curious, with excellent problem-solving skills and the ability to work independently while contributing effectively to a collaborative research environment.

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Prior expertise and experience in Asset Health Index (AHI)

Data analysis, machine learning, statistical modelling, or optimisation

Maintenance engineering, reliability, condition monitoring, prognostics, or asset management

Working with heterogeneous industrial data, including structured and unstructured information

Programming and development of decision-support or simulation models

Academic or industrial collaboration in multidisciplinary environments

What you will do

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate school of Product and Production Development  ( Product and production development | Chalmers )

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing

Develop and validate Asset Health Index models by combining condition data, maintenance information, operational data, and expert knowledge

Explore AI-supported methods for prognostics, Remaining Useful Life estimation, transparent model interpretation, and maintenance decision support

Implement, test, and demonstrate models and decision-support concepts together with other researchers and industry participants in laboratory and real-world pilot environments

The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Contract terms

The Doctoral student positions are fully funded from start.

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

A starting salary of 35,725 SEK per month (valid from May 1, 2026).

Doctoral studies require physical presence throughout the entire study period. A valid residence permit must be presented by the study start date; otherwise the admission may be withdrawn.

Join a world-leading research environment at the Chalmers Security and Privacy Lab and help shape the future of web, software, and AI security. As a doctoral student, you will contribute to cutting-edge cybersecurity research while working closely with internationally recognized researchers. This position offers an excellent opportunity to develop as an independent researcher and make an impact on secure and trustworthy digital systems.

Software is often the root cause of vulnerabilities in modern computing systems. We develop principled concepts and mechanisms to ensure robust security and privacy for software. You will be supervised by Prof. Andrei Sabelfeld (Wallenberg Scholar and recipient of awards from ERC, SSF, VR, WASP, Google, Amazon, Facebook, and OpenAI, as well as the Chalmers Doctoral Supervisor of the Year award).

About us

The Department of Computer Science and Engineering , a joint department of Chalmers and the University of Gothenburg, spans the breadth of computing disciplines. Our internationally visible research, strong industry links and diverse environment create a collaborative setting where ideas grow into real impact.

At the division of Computing Science , we advance secure and trustworthy software and systems, spanning foundations, programming languages, tools and practical methods that help shape dependable digital infrastructures.

About the research project

You will contribute to one of our research projects on Web and Emerging Applications Security. Our research tracks include:
•  Web application crawling and security scanning ( Black Widow , Black Ostrich , and Spider-Scents )
•  Security and privacy of browser extensions ( FakeX and CodeX )
•  JavaScript server-side sandboxing ( SandTrap )
•  Data minimization in Trigger-Action Platforms ( minTAP and LazyTAP )
•  Security and privacy of agentic and AI-integrated systems (ongoing research area)

Promotional video of our research on securing web applications

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, or a closely related field

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Documented research interest and/or achievements in cybersecurity and/or privacy

Ability to work independently and analytically to solve complex research problems

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

A Master's thesis or research-oriented project in language-based security, web security, or systems security

Experience with program analysis, formal methods, or AI/LLM-based systems

Publications, open-source security tools, or participation in security competitions (CTFs) and bug bounty programs

What you will do

Take courses at an advanced level within the Graduate School of Computer Science and Engineering

Develop your own scientific concepts and communicate the results of your research verbally and in writing

The position generally also includes teaching on Chalmers' undergraduate level or performing other duties corresponding to 20 percent of working hours

Conduct research within one of the tracks above

Design, implement, and evaluate security analysis tools and prototypes, such as crawlers, scanners, sandboxes, data minimizers, and extension analyzers

Publish and present results at cybersecurity venues

Contract terms

The position is a fixed-term appointment of four years, with the possibility to teach up to 20%, which extends the position up to five years.

Join our research team at the Division of Materials and Manufacture, Chalmers University of Technology, and contribute to the development of next-generation solid-state batteries. Through close collaboration with Fraunhofer (Germany), RISE (Sweden) and Swedish industrial partners, you will investigate polymer-based solid-state electrolyte synthesis, materials engineering, and advanced electrode processing, with a strong focus on scalable battery manufacturing.

About us

At the Department of Mechanical Engineering , we unite the power of technology, people, and society to drive the transition toward a sustainable future. Through research, education, and collaboration, we create solutions that connect materials to mobility, ideas to impact – shaping a resilient and sustainable world.

The Division of Materials and Manufacture conducts research across the full value chain, from materials design and processing to advanced manufacturing and characterisation, with a strong emphasis on metallic systems. We combine interdisciplinary expertise with close industry collaboration to develop sustainable materials and manufacturing technologies.

About the research project

Our research group at Chalmers focuses on advanced materials development, electrode processing and battery manufacturing, and is part of Sweden’s strong and growing battery research and innovation ecosystem. The project aims to advance the development and manufacturing of next-generation solid-state batteries through innovative electrolyte materials and electrode processing strategies.

The research will combine materials synthesis, polymer science and processing technologies to understand and improve the properties, interfaces and manufacturability of solid-state battery components. The Doctoral student will work in an interdisciplinary and collaborative environment, involving Chalmers, Fraunhofer, RISE and Swedish industrial partners, with a focus on bridging materials research and practical battery manufacturing.

The Doctoral student will undertake a research exchange at Fraunhofer for a minimum of six months, providing an opportunity to work in an international research environment and strengthen the collaboration.

Who we are looking for

The following requirements are mandatory:

To qualify as a Doctoral student, you must have a Master's degree ( masterexamen ) of 120 credits or a Master’s degree ( magisterexamen ) of 60 credits* in materials science, chemical engineering, materials mechanics, polymer chemistry, materials chemistry, physics, or production engineering

Strong written and verbal communication skills in English

Experience in lithium-ion batteries and/or solid-state electrolyte battery

* for students with an education earned outside of Sweden, a 4-year Bachelor’s degree is accepted.

The following experience will strengthen your application:

Experience in solid-state electrolytes, lithium-ion batteries, electrode processing, battery manufacturing, battery binder development.

Project description
Third-cycle subject: Information and Communication Technologies
We invite applications for doctoral student positions with the Networked Systems Security (NSS) lab at EECS/CLS. We are looking for highly motivated individuals to pursue a PhD in security and privacy. The positions involve activities leading to original research and results in peer-reviewed publications. The research topics can relate with any of the NSS group areas ( https://www.eecs.kth.se/nss ).
The NSS group designs and builds trustworthy networked systems, with a research agenda covering a gamut of security and privacy problems and results that got significant attention by the research community. NSS introduced a new security curriculum at KTH. Candidates with experimental/systems or theoretical profiles and research interests in any aspect of security and privacy are welcome to apply.
Supervision: Professor Panagiotis ‘Panos’ Papadimitratos  is proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge

In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.
show solid background in several of the following: computer security, privacy preserving or enhancing technologies, mobile computing, networking, Internet security, wireless communications, distributed algorithms and systems, programming languages, performance analysis, operating systems, simulation techniques and tools, software engineering, system and network programming, applied cryptography, information theory.

Candidates with strong experimental, systems or theoretical profiles and research interests in all aspects of security and privacy are encouraged to apply. Applicants should have strong interest in several of the following: design, analysis, verification, implementation, or empirical evaluation of secure networked systems. Of primary interest are security and resilience of positioning/localization, including global navigation satellite systems.
In addition, candidates need to demonstrate readiness and willingness to contribute to our research and work in an international research team.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with many employee benefits and monthly salary according to KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement . Read more about Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden .
Union representatives
Contact information for   union representatives.
Doctoral Student’s network (Students’ union on KTH Royal Institute of Technology)
Contact information for   PhD chapter .
To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled language requirements (see above) . Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be certified .
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge.
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (Maximum 2 pages long)
Representative publications or technical reports. For longer documents, please provide a summary (abstract) and a web link to the full text.
Recommendation letters: Please include detailed contact information for at least two (2) references.

Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).
Other information
For information about processing of personal data in the recruitment process.
It may be the case that a position at KTH is classified as a security-sensitive role in accordance with the Protective Security Act (2018:585). If this applies to the specific position, a security clearance will be conducted for the applicant in accordance with the same law with the applicant's consent. In such cases, a prerequisite for employment is that the applicant is approved following the security clearance.
We firmly decline all contact with staffing and recruitment agencies and job ad salespersons.
Disclaimer: In case of discrepancy between the Swedish original and the English translation of the job announcement, the Swedish version takes precedence.

Join us at KTH

kth:955894.body:
Technical Student for KTH Innovation Makerspace – Help Startups Go from Idea to Prototype!
KTH Innovation is one of Europe’s leading startup hubs. Each year, we help hundreds of students and researchers explore ideas and launch startups. Our alumni include Blykalla, Airmee, TERASi, SuperAnnotate and Flox, as well as founders behind ventures such as Lovable and Neko Health.
An important part of our work is supporting teams developing physical products. That’s where you come in!
Your Role
We are looking for a student with an interest in, and experience from design and product development who wants a flexible part-time job alongside their studies. You will apply your technical skills, develop your prototyping expertise and gain insight into how startups and early-stage technologies evolve.
As a student assistant, you will support teams developing physical products, helping them move from ideas to functional prototypes in the KTH Innovation Makerspace.
Your responsibilities include:
Providing hands-on and digital support with CAD, 3D printing, laser cutting, basic electronics and prototype fabrication. You will particularly help others use 3D printers effectively and safely.
Guiding teams in defining what to test, choosing prototyping methods, planning iterations and evaluating results. Teams remain responsible for their own product development.
Introducing teams to the makerspace, its tools and equipment, and helping maintain welcoming, well-organized routines and workflows.

You will also contribute to events, study visits and administrative tasks. You will join the KTH Innovation student assistant team and collaborate with KTH's central makerspace, other makerspaces at KTH and student associations working with hardware.
The position is 30%, with flexible working hours to accommodate your studies. Some evening events are included.
Read more about KTH Innovation
Qualifications
Required - what is actually needed in the role
Admission to a first-, second- or third-cycle programme at a Swedish university.
Good spoken and written English as it is needed in daily work.
Practical knowledge of CAD software.
Experience using 3D printers.

Personal Attributes
We value inclusion, openness and diversity. You should enjoy helping people with different backgrounds and levels of experience feel welcome and confident in exploring their ideas.
You enjoy collaborating with and helping others.
You are solution-oriented and can troubleshoot practical technical problems independently.
You communicate technical concepts clearly and adapt your guidance to different levels of knowledge.
You take responsibility, show initiative and work independently.
You contribute to a welcoming environment where everyone feels comfortable asking questions, experimenting and learning.

Meriting- desirable, but not all are expected
At least one year of studies remaining at KTH.
Experience in physical product prototyping and product development.
Practical experience building hardware and/or software solutions.
Experience with makerspace equipment and manufacturing methods, such as laser cutting, casting, vacuum forming or 3D scanning.
Experience from student associations or other organizations connected to hardware and/or startups.
Knowledge of electronics.
Swedish language skills as it fascilitates daily work.

kth:970256.body:
Project description
Third-cycle subject: Electrical Engineering
Autonomous systems are increasingly deployed alongside humans to carry out complex coordinated tasks. In these settings, autonomous systems must handle strict spatial and temporal constraints while adapting in real time to supervisory commands, unexpected obstacles, and environmental disturbances. Enabling trustworthy human–robot collaboration calls for new mathematical foundations and computational tools that unify decision-making, planning, and control.
We are seeking an exceptional doctoral student to conduct research at the intersection of game theory and control for multi-agent autonomous systems. The position is part of the Digital Futures project Human-in-the-Loop Autonomy via Hybrid Games .  The work will span both mathematical foundations of hybrid games and the design of computationally tractable controllers for deployment on real robotic platforms.
The research will address:
Hybrid dynamic games under temporal logic task specifications;
Game-theoretic modelling of human–robot interaction;
Experimental validation on multi-robot and underwater robotic platforms;

Supervision: Assistant Prof. Giuseppe Belgioioso and Prof. Dimos Dimarogonas are proposed to supervise the doctoral student. Decisions are made on admission
Admission requirements
To be admitted to postgraduate education (Chapter 7, 39 § Swedish Higher Education Ordinance), the applicant must have basic eligibility in accordance with either of the following:
passed a second cycle degree (for example a master's degree), or
completed course requirements of at least 240 higher education credits, of which at least 60 second-cycle higher education credits, or
acquired, in some other way within or outside the country, substantially equivalent knowledge

In addition to the above, there is also a mandatory requirement for English equivalent to English B/6.
Selection
In order to succeed as a doctoral student at KTH you need to be goal oriented and persevering in your work. During the selection process, candidates will be assessed upon their ability to:
independently pursue his or her work
collaborate with others,
have a professional approach and
analyze and work with complex issues.

A strong background in optimization and automatic control is required. Familiarity with game theory, hybrid systems, MPC, or formal methods will be advantageous. Proficiency in programming, and any prior hands-on experience with robotic platforms, will also be beneficial.
Selected candidates must be able to provide contact information to at least one academic or professional reference. The candidate must be able to demonstrate high motivation for doctoral studies.
After the qualification requirements, great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
Target degree: Doctoral degree
Information regarding admission and employment
Only those admitted to postgraduate education may be employed as a doctoral student. The total length of employment may not be longer than what corresponds to full-time doctoral education in four years' time. An employed doctoral student can, to a limited extent (maximum 20%), perform certain tasks within their role, e.g. training and administration. A new position as a doctoral student is for a maximum of one year, and then the employment may be renewed for a maximum of two years at a time.
As a doctoral student, you are entitled to a workplace with many employee benefits and monthly salary according to KTH’s Doctoral student salary agreement . Read more about Doctoral studies (PhD) | KTH | Sweden .

To apply for the position
Apply for the position and admission through KTH's recruitment system. It is the applicant’s responsibility to ensure that the application is complete in accordance with the instructions in the advertisement.
Applications must include the following elements:
Copies of diplomas and grades from previous university studies and certificates of fulfilled language requirements (see above) . Translations into English or Swedish if the original document is not issued in one of these languages.Copies of originals must be certified .
CV including your relevant professional experience and knowledge. (max 2 pages).
Application letter with a brief description of why you want to pursue research studies, about what your academic interests are and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. (max 1 page).
Representative publications or reports (e.g., master thesis).
Name of at least one academic or professional reference.

Applications must be received at the last closing date at midnight, CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

Job description
KTH is establishing a new Makerspace, which is scheduled to open in February 2027. We are looking for a student assistant to support the development of activities within the Makerspace. The Makerspace is a place where students can develop their skills through hands-on work with tools and machinery. This may involve woodwork, 3D printing, prototype design using various materials, and electronics. The role involves tasks such as:
planning and running workshops for the space’s users
collaborating with teachers to integrate the use of the space into educational programmes
producing training materials and manuals on how to use the space

You may also be expected to manage technical equipment and software within the facility, maintain materials and equipment, and help with procurement.
Qualifications
Requirements
You should be admitted to first or second-level cycle education at a  Swedish university
Experience in organizing peer groups, student organizations, or volunteer teams.
Ability to create structured schedules, rosters, and event workflows.
You should be fluent in Swedish and English, for day-to-day work.

Preferred qualifications
Student at KTH
Ability to translate technical processes into clear, written instructions for non-technical users.
Experience in liaising with faculty and administration to identify curriculum needs.

Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.
